title: Design and experimental verification of target-oriented spraying system incorporating camera pitch angle
abstract: Accurate positioning is a critical step in enabling target-oriented spraying for cabbage. Poor positioning accuracy is caused by real-time changes in camera pitch angle during sprayer operation. In this paper, a cabbage positioning error correction method was proposed, which integrates real-time camera orientation information. A high-precision real-time positioning model was developed under dynamic conditions to achieve accurate cabbage objects during target-oriented spraying. The optimized YOLO v8n model was utilized to detect cabbage targets in images in real-time. The graph cut algorithm was applied to segment cabbages within the bounding boxes, extracting edge regions. Depth distance information for these edge regions was obtained by combining RGB and depth images. The imaging characteristics of the D455 depth camera under varying illumination and pixel positionings were investigated. The distribution patterns of positioning errors at different imaging angles were analyzed, and a real-time camera orientation-based error correction model was constructed. Positioning accuracy improved significantly with real-time camera pitch angle correction, particularly at larger orientation angles. Field tests showed that the average front-end error YB is 2.8 cm, and the average rear-end error YF is 3.4 cm. Compared with the target-oriented spaying system that does not fuse camera pitch angle information, the errors are reduced by 6.0 and 4.2 cm, respectively. When the sprayer sprayed the target at a speed of 1 m/s. The proposed real-time cabbage positioning method provides an algorithmic foundation for target-oriented spraying in leafy cabbage.

title: A multi-class deep learning segmentation approach for automated analysis of axial and lateral roots in barley plants
abstract: Accurate segmentation and analysis of root images from soil-grown plants are critical for advancing our understanding of root growth and plasticity under varying environmental conditions. Most approaches typically rely on binary segmentation of the entire root system architecture (RSA), which limits their ability to capture the hierarchical complexity of root structures, including axial and lateral roots. To address this, our study evaluated five convolutional neural network (CNN) architectures for multi-class (i.e. axial/lateral) segmentation of 2D root images from barley plants grown in rhizoboxes: (i) U-Net, (ii) U-Net with Atrous Spatial Pyramid Pooling (UnetASPP), (iii) U-Net with Attention Block (UnetAtt), (iv) DeepLabV3+ with MobileNetV2 (DLMB), and (v) DeepLabV3+ with ResNet-50 (DLR50). Among these, the DLR50 model achieved the highest segmentation accuracy, particularly for distinguishing lateral roots within complex RSA structures. Furthermore, analysis of root traits derived from the segmented images confirmed that DLR50 produced the most reliable estimations of phenotypic traits compared to ground truth measurements. These findings highlight the strong potential of advanced multi-class CNN models—especially DLR50—for detailed and quantitative analysis of soil-root systems, providing new insights into root responses to environmental conditions. • Evaluated five CNN models for multi-class segmentation of 2D root images, distinguishing axial and lateral roots. • DLR50 (DeepLabV3+ with ResNet-50) outperformed all models in accurately segmenting complex root structures. • Improved trait prediction accuracy using DLR50-segmented images compared to ground truth data. • Enables fine-grained analysis of root plasticity in response to environmental changes.

title: Depth-OC-SORT-based multi-object tracking of cattle in real-world farming scenarios
abstract: Dairy cattle breeds are important in livestock farming, providing humans with nutrient-rich dairy products. In dairy farming, cattle tracking can provide essential data for early disease detection, feeding optimisation, welfare improvement, and breeding management. However, dairy farms often feature complex backgrounds, fences, and cattle-to-cattle occlusions, which often lead to frequent false detections and identity (ID) loss during tracking (typically 10–20 times per minute). This study proposes a multi-target cattle tracking method based on depth observation-centric simple online and real-time tracking (Depth-OC-SORT). This method introduces depth information tailored to the physical characteristics of cows to improve the OC-SORT algorithm, which comprises two branches: object detection and object tracking. In the object detection branch, YOLO11 is used as the base model to obtain basic detection boxes. A geometry-aware false positive suppression algorithm during post-processing eliminates the erroneous bounding boxes, thereby improving detection precision in cases of overlapping cattle. In the object tracking branch, an improved OC-SORT algorithm is introduced to innovatively integrate the depth information obtained from Depth Anything V2 (a monocular depth estimation model), to transform two-dimensional positional data into three-dimensional spatial data and enhance cattle distinguishability. Additionally, the Kalman filter is optimised for real-time parameter self-correction, dynamically adjusting parameters through adaptive weighting based on confidence scores to adapt to the rapid morphological changes in cattle motion patterns such as turns, thereby improving tracking accuracy. In experiments conducted on a self-built cattle tracking dataset, the proposed method achieved a MOTA of 71.298, a HOTA of 54.026, and IDF1 of 75.386. These represent improvements of 2.5 %, 4.99 %, and 9.349 %, respectively, over those of leading 2D baseline methods. In comparative experiments, the proposed method significantly outperformed existing algorithms such as bag of tricks (BoT)-SORT and ByteTrack, effectively enabling accurate cattle detection and tracking by providing strong technical support for precision dairy farming. The code will be released at: https://github.com/Elite35P/Depth-OC-SORT.

title: Measuring shade use of dairy cattle at pasture with an on-cow light sensor: a case study
abstract: Grazing cows need access to shade to shield against heat stress. However, the conditions that provide cows with optimal shade access and use (e.g. no competition for access to shade) are still unknown. Continuous monitoring of shade use by grazing cattle could help to understand how and when cows use shade resources. The aim of this study was to validate a method for continuously recording the use of natural shade by grazing cows. We tested a light sensor attached to the dairy cows to measure their shade use. The study used seven dairy cows equipped with a light sensor (HOBO® Pendant® MX2202 temperature/light data logger) attached to their backs (on the transverse processes of the lumbar vertebrae). Live behavioral observations of shade use and cow posture were recorded from June to September (between 9 am and 6 pm). Based on the behavioral observation data, we determined thresholds in lux to discriminate between cows in shade and cows in sun on a randomly-generated training dataset representing 15% of the initial dataset. This process was repeated 100 times, generating 100 thresholds and threshold performances. Data loss due to sensor loss or battery discharge was 9%, which is acceptable. The thresholds ranged from 15688 to 40556 lx: sensitivity ranged from 92.0% to 99.8% and specificity ranged from 88.7% to 99.9%, showing that the performances were robust to threshold variation within this range. This study demonstrates that an efficient threshold to discriminate cows in shade from cows in the sun can be determined via a relatively short (about 12h) series of live observations. As performances seem to be slightly lower for lying cows than for standing cows (mean false-positive rate is 7.4% for lying cows versus 1.8% for standing cows), future studies should consider the posture factor.

title: Visible light image-based methods for age determination in Moso bamboo
abstract: Accurately determining the age of Moso bamboo and establishing a reasonable age structure for bamboo forests are essential prerequisites for the scientific management and productivity maximization of Moso bamboo forests. Visible light images offer the advantages of low acquisition cost and abundant information. These images reveal significant phenotypic differences in Moso bamboo of varying ages, allowing for the use of such images in age determination. However, the phenotypic recognition of Moso bamboo is often influenced by environmental conditions, leading to variations in image brightness and high similarity in the features of Moso bamboo across different age groups, thereby reducing age determination accuracy. This study analyzes the phenotypic characteristics of Moso bamboo at different ages and their susceptibility to brightness variations, proposing a novel age determination method using visible light images. The YOLO target detection model and the Segment Anything Model (SAM) are employed to extract Moso bamboo regions from images. Phenotypic features under abnormal brightness are corrected using four image enhancement techniques. Subsequently, various age models, constructed using different backbone networks and loss functions, are compared and analyzed to identify the optimal combination for Moso bamboo age determination. The best image enhancement method and model were selected to discriminate the age of Moso bamboo. The results show that brightness significantly affects the phenotypic characteristics of Moso bamboo in the images. In this study, adaptive histogram equalization was used to enhance the images, and an age determination model was built using ResNet-101 with Focal Loss and Label Smoothing Regularization (LSR). The accuracy of age determination for Moso bamboo reached 88.6 %, representing a 10.5 % improvement over the baseline model’s accuracy of 78.1 %.

title: CRODNet: Cascaded learning network for contactless top-view cattle rotated object detection
abstract: Cattle recognition and monitoring are critical components of precision livestock farming. However, most existing recognition methods require manual labor and inevitably involve direct contact with cattle, which may cause stress responses in animals. To address these issues, our research focuses on top-view images, with the data acquisition process being contactless. To meet the data requirements for recognition and improve data quality for enhanced recognition accuracy, we partition the overall goal into three sub-tasks, object detection, keypoint detection and image alignment, and designed cattle rotated object detection network (CRODNet) to address them. In the object detection stage, given the inherent characteristics of large body and long rectangular shape, we implemented a pruned multi-head network for rapid cattle pre-selection, ensuring that each image contains a cattle to meet the recognition data requirements. For keypoint detection, we leveraged pre-selection prior and adopted a parallel network architecture with multiple resolutions to extract critical physiological structure features, which are regressed to the cattle’s physiological keypoints that include information on body shape and posture. Finally, in the image alignment task, we fully leverage the relationship between the cattle’s biological posture and skeletal keypoints from an overhead perspective, modeling a rotation strategy to ensure that cattle with various postures achieve maximum vertical alignment. Experimental results demonstrate that our model achieves a 70% reduction in the number of parameters and 50% decrease in floating point operations (FLOPs), while outperforming other bottom-up approaches by at least 3% in Average Precision (AP). This approach enhances the quality of the pre-selected image and improves the accuracy of the downstream recognition task by at least 2%. These advances are expected to promote the development of precision livestock farming.

title: Efficient and lightweight model for detecting juvenile fish feeding behavior using feed pellet key point analysis
abstract: Feeding fish based on their feeding behavior and intensity facilitates their healthy growth and improves aquaculture efficiency. Current methods assess feeding intensity and behavior based on feeding sounds and splashes. However, evaluating the feeding behavior of juvenile fish is difficult because of their slow feeding rate and small size. This paper presents an improved YOLOv8-feed key points in the fish feeding behavior model (YOLOv8-FB), based on YOLOv8n-pose, to detect juvenile fish feeding behavior effectively. YOLOv8-FB combines target detection and key point recognition; it replaces the bottleneck in C2f with the feed pellets edge information extraction module stem (FPEIEMStem) block, resulting in C2f-FPEIEM. Additionally, the global-to-local spatial aggregation (GLSA) module is integrated into a bi-directional feature pyramid network (BiFPN) to replace the original path aggregation network as a neck network, enhancing feature fusion. FPEIEMStem block leverages a SobelConv branch for edge information extraction and a convolutional branch for spatial information extraction, enabling efficient feature learning that incorporates rich edge and spatial information. Experimental results reveal that YOLOv8-FB achieves a mean average precision of 94.8 % for detecting juvenile fish feeding behavior, reduces the number of parameters by 37.1 %, and has a model complexity of 6.9 GFLOPs. Moreover, a short-term starvation test demonstrated increased feeding activity among juvenile fish, reflected in a higher frequency of contact with feed pellets. YOLOv8-FB has excellent detection performance, effectively addressing juvenile fish feeding behavior detection.

title: Dual-branch frequency-domain fusion for RGB-D tree trunks instance segmentation
abstract: Tree trunk instance segmentation is a crucial task in vision-based perception systems for forestry robots, enabling precise autonomous navigation in complex forest environments. However, existing RGB-only methods struggle to achieve adequate accuracy due to challenges such as uneven illumination and occlusions. To overcome these limitations, we propose TrunkInst, a dual-branch, frequency-domain fusion RGB-D network for tree trunk instance segmentation. TrunkInst employs a Frequency-Domain Decomposition Gate Fusion (FDGF) module that decomposes and selectively fuses RGB and depth features in the frequency domain, enhancing segmentation accuracy by suppressing noise and preserving important details. The Multi-Head Dynamic Upsampling (MDU) module generates higher-quality upsampled feature maps by learning multiple offset groups, improving the resolution of small tree trunks. Finally, a Transformer decoder, using cross-modal queries between RGB features and fused representations, mitigates the negative effects of degraded depth maps. We also propose the Trunk-Depths dataset, which includes 1,326 finely annotated RGB-depth image pairs for tree-trunk instance segmentation. On this dataset, TrunkInst achieves a mean Average Precision (mAP) of 52.8%, with 85.3% AP at IoU=0.5 and 54.4% AP at IoU=0.75—improvements of +2.6%, +1.4%, and +4.6% over an RGB baseline, respectively. Further experiments on the public COME15K and NYU-Depth-V2 datasets demonstrate the generality and robustness of the model. TrunkInst also delivers real-time inference at 45 fps, achieving a good trade-off between accuracy and speed.

title: EPDNet: A method for identifying tomato leaf diseases with uneven samples
abstract: Tomato industry is one of the important parts of agriculture, and the timely diagnosis of leaf diseases plays a key role in ensuring its production safety. At present, most of the mainstream recognition technologies are based on laboratory standard images to construct recognition models. Although they can achieve accurate analysis of isolated leaves, it is difficult to cope with the practical challenges such as complex climate and environmental factors of plant growth in open environments. The recognition is difficult due to the influence factors of open environment, such as the distortion of disease spots caused by light, the occlusion of branches and leaves, and the confusion of soil attachment and real disease spots. To solve the problem of unbalanced distribution of tomato leaf disease samples in open environment and the big difference of similar diseases, this study proposes a single-modal recognition architecture for tomato leaf diseases based on Efficient localization and Physical information and Dynamic adaptive optimization Network (EPDNet). Firstly, an efficient positioning feature enhancement module is designed to effectively enhance the network’s attention to important regions by calculating and fusing the horizontal and vertical attention weights. Then, a physical information neural network-cross entropy hybrid loss function was designed to ensure the accuracy of prediction, while restricting the smoothness and continuity of the feature map to improve the robustness of the model. Finally, a dynamic adaptive optimization algorithm was designed to iteratively update the learning rate to improve the feature discrimination ability, so as to reduce the identification differences of diseases within the class. Experimental results show that the accuracy of EPDNet on the tomato leaf dataset reaches 93.62%, and the F1 score reaches 93.31 %, which is significantly better than the existing methods. This study provides an effective solution for the application of deep learning methods in crop diseases.

title: Realtime multi-RGBD SLAM framework for 3D reconstruction and phenotyping in large-scale apple orchards
abstract: Three-dimensional (3D) reconstructions of orchards offer richer data for digital phenotyping and underpin smart-agriculture applications. However, achieving high-level reconstruction quality and robustness is challenging due to the complex structure of the orchard. This study presents a novel framework that provides centimeter-level 3D realtime reconstructions and phenotyping for apple orchards. A multi-RGBD camera array was adopted, creating a wide overlapping view and robust features. The hybrid odometry front-end and the dual loop-closure strategy ensured low-drift pose estimation. The generated pointcloud was input into the ellipsoid-fitting routine to extract fruit diameter and volume. We validated this framework through reconstruction and phenotypic errors in four rows of an apple orchard with different tree spacings. The root mean square error of the absolute trajectory error in global reconstruction was less than 16 mm. The mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) of the local fiducial distance of approximately 5 m was less than 0.12%. The system was implemented at higher than 12.5 frames per second in an embedded system. The MAPEs of the fruit’s diameter were 2–2.17%, and those of its volume were 5.3–5.6%. Additionally, ablation experiments were carried out on multi-camera and loop-closed elements, and comparisons were made with existing methods to further demonstrate their effectiveness. In conclusion, this research provides an efficient and stable deployable solution for 3D reconstruction of orchards, which is conducive to the development of more advanced and multilayer modern orchard models and promotes the practice of smart agriculture.

title: Study on the effective furrow profile space affecting transversely arranged seed bed of stalk-seeds
abstract: A transverse planter utilizing double-bud cane stalks requires continuous individual sowing while widely trenching to bury seeds deeply, while the instant large-flow clay backfill stresses the placement space and posture of falling seeds, challenging effective planting depth. To this end, a controllable furrow opening method for large-flow soil transfer capable of spatio-temporal coordination with stalk-seed downstream was proposed. Based on this, the influence of backfill-shielding factors on the effective furrow profile space was investigated. The effective mode of integrating furrow-clearing drive surface and bilateral soil constraint boundaries for large-section furrow formation was analyzed, and their synergies with low-position seeding were confirmed to generate a dynamic furrow space of appropriate size in a timely manner. A discrete element model of interaction among trencher, heterogeneous clay layers and variable cane seeds was established, thereby clarifying the principle of regulating soil reflux with slope stability. Comprehensive virtual and field experiment results revealed the influence of various shield-characteristic factors on seed bed construction performance from spatio-temporal source angles, such as downward rolling drive, timing of backflow, capability to barrier accumulated soil and soil treatment capacity. Furthermore, through multi-objective optimization based on approximation models, confirmatory tests showed that the effective planting depth was improved by 30.4%, and the soil coverage thickness for seed anchorage stability was enhanced by 20.9%. This provided direct evidence for improved seed arrangement accuracy by enhancing systematic synergy between mechanical trenching and sowing processes.

title: Diagnosis of maize nitrogen status under contrasting water and nitrogen regimes using a canopy-stratified and multi-source remote sensing framework
abstract: Maize leaf nitrogen exhibits significant vertical heterogeneity within the canopy, which often compromises the accuracy of remote sensing-based nitrogen status diagnosis. To address the limited consideration of leaf-layer contributions and multi-source feature integration, this study proposed a three-dimensional coupled nitrogen diagnosis framework integrating progressive leaf-layer labeling, multi-source feature fusion, and machine learning modeling, based on spring maize experiments under various water and nitrogen regimes in Xinjiang, China. Stratified ground sampling was conducted to obtain leaf nitrogen weight (LNW) from the upper, middle, and lower canopy layers, and 22 vegetation indices (VIs), eight texture features (TFs), and 15 texture indices (TIs) were extracted from UAV multispectral imagery to construct a multi-source feature set. Results demonstrated that the combination of upper and middle canopy leaves best represented overall plant nitrogen status. Feature fusion significantly enhanced model performance, with extreme gradient boosting achieving the highest estimation accuracy for the nitrogen nutrition index (NNI) (R2 = 0.68, RPD = 1.77), and convolutional neural networks performing best in LNW estimation (R2 = 0.83, RPD = 2.31). The critical nitrogen dilution curves derived from the estimated LNW revealed that irrigation levels significantly influenced the curve intercepts and slopes, highlighting the dual regulatory effects of water on nitrogen uptake and dilution. Coupled with ArcGIS-based spatial visualization, the framework enabled dynamic monitoring of NNI across V6, VT, R3, and R6 growth stages. Overall, this framework effectively improved both the spatiotemporal resolution and estimation accuracy of maize nitrogen status, providing a theoretical basis and technical support for precision nitrogen management and the transition toward sustainable agriculture.

title: A top-view transformer-based framework for tiny tea bud detection with gradient-guided attention and position-sensitive loss
abstract: Accurately detecting tea buds under top-view imaging is essential for automating tea harvesting. However, this task is particularly challenging due to the buds’ extremely small size, blurred boundaries, high visual similarity to background leaves, and low inter-class variance—all of which result in sparse features and frequent mislocalization. Existing CNN-based detectors often struggle to preserve fine spatial details while modeling global context in such scenarios. To address these issues, we propose a Transformer-based framework for robust top-view tea bud detection, leveraging its global attention mechanism to enhance feature discrimination for tiny and ambiguous objects. Specifically, a Gradient-guided Class Activation Attention module enhances spatial sensitivity by generating attention maps from mid-level CNN features via gradient signals, allowing the model to focus on weak yet semantically relevant regions. An Explicit-Guided Decoder reinforces inter-layer consistency and structural modeling by leveraging feedback from previous predictions and stage-wise feature injection. In addition, a Spatial Position-Sensitive Enhancement Loss introduces a Gaussian-based weighting mechanism to emphasize central object regions, improving localization accuracy for tiny targets. Experiments on a top-view tea bud dataset demonstrate that our method outperforms state-of-the-art baselines (YOLOv11, DETR, RT-DETR), achieving a Precision of 0.8371 and mAP@0.5 of 0.8013. Moreover, evaluations on three public tiny-object detection datasets further confirm its generalization across domains. These results highlight the effectiveness and transferability of the proposed approach in both agricultural and general tiny-object detection scenarios.

title: Design and performance verification of an intelligent pollination robot for facility tomatoes
abstract: Given that the natural pollination of tomatoes is limited by the closed environment of facility agriculture, and the problems of low efficiency, high cost, or side effects associated with traditional artificial, insect, and hormone pollination methods, this study proposes an intelligent vibration pollination robot solution. Firstly, we designed the YOLO-MAF algorithm for detecting the flowering period of tomato flowers, which integrates the MPDIoU loss function module, the AFPN feature fusion module, and the efficient multi-scale attention (EMA) module to improve the accuracy of flowering period detection in complex environments; Secondly, the multimodal geometric feature fusion detection algorithm (MGFF) is used to achieve precise spatial pixel positioning of the flowers to be pollinated; Finally, the camera coordinate system is mapped to the robotic arm coordinate system through the hand-eye calibration algorithm, driving the end effector to complete precise vibration pollination. Experimental results show that the YOLO-MAF algorithm achieves a precision rate of 90.2 %, a recall rate of 85.4 %, an mAP@0.5 of 91.4 %, and a GPU inference time of 8.9 ms; the MGFF algorithm achieves the highest positioning accuracy of 91 %. By encapsulating the algorithm and integrating it with a vibrating pollination robot, validation tests have shown an average pollination success rate of 73.58 % and an average pollination time of 30.486 s. This technology can provide efficient and low-cost automated pollination technology support for facility agriculture, helping to improve the quality and efficiency of the tomato industry.

title: A multi-scale linear cross-modal fusion architecture for tomato leaf disease segmentation
abstract: Tomato, as a globally important economic crop, requires precise and timely disease management to secure yield and quality. Yet segmentation robustness is often limited by weak semantic understanding from single-modality images, narrow receptive fields of convolutional structures, and discontinuous boundary predictions. To address these issues, we propose the Multi-scale Linear Cross-modal Fusion Architecture for Tomato Leaf Disease Segmentation (MS-LCFNet). We construct a real-world field dataset covering five major tomato leaf diseases, annotated by experts with detailed textual descriptions to enable multimodal learning. MS-LCFNet strengthens semantic representation via cross-modal fusion, captures local and global context through an Adaptive Long-short Distance Perception module, and improves boundary continuity with a Physics-informed Smoothness-constrained Loss. Experiments show that MS-LCFNet achieves 87.13 % mIoU on our dataset and 90.78 % on PlantVillage, improving over previous state-of-the-art methods by + 4.62 % and + 4.48 %, respectively, and demonstrating superior accuracy and robustness in complex agricultural scenarios.

title: AdaFishCount: Advancing domain-invariant learning via domain-specific perturbation for cross-domain fish counting
abstract: Deep learning-based fish counting is crucial for intelligent aquaculture management. However, variations in water transparency, fish distribution, and camera perspectives introduce significant domain gaps, limiting the adaptability of data-driven counting methods across diverse real-world scenarios. To address this challenge, an unsupervised domain adaptation framework, named AdaFishCount, is designed for fish counting. AdaFishCount integrates domain-specific feature perturbation and domain-invariant feature learning. Specifically, the Domain-Specific Feature Perturbation (DSFP) module performs controllable perturbations in the source feature space to generate target-style samples, simulating domain shifts between different aquaculture environments. Subsequently, domain-invariant feature learning leverages an Attention-guided Domain-Invariant Selector (ADIS) and a Long-term Domain-Invariant Memory (LDIM) module to extract stable and discriminative fish representations. Moreover, a comprehensive loss function is devised to ensure consistent density distributions under various style perturbations and to enhance focus on domain-invariant features. Experimental results demonstrate that AdaFishCount achieves superior cross-domain performance, notably improving MAE, RMSE, and MAPE by 14.66, 15.24, and 43.96, respectively, compared to the state-of-the-art method on the target domain Tank 2, highlighting its strong robustness to domain gaps.

title: Recent developments and applications of weed detection, invasion prediction and early warning: A review
abstract: Weeds are invasive plant species that establish and proliferate in undesirable locations, thereby reducing agricultural productivity and disturbing ecological balance through competition for resources and the transmission of pests and diseases. They are increasingly recognized as a critical threat to the sustainability of global agriculture and the integrity of natural ecosystems. Consequently, effective weed management is essential to ensure both agricultural productivity and ecological stability. With ongoing advancements in science, technology, and agricultural practices, the accurate and timely detection of weeds, as well as the prediction and early warning of invasions, have become pivotal for implementing effective management strategies. Nevertheless, these tasks remain challenging due to the high diversity and complexity of weed species, their concealed and variable invasion pathways, and the intricate dynamics of ecosystems. The integration of advanced sensors, intelligent systems, and analytical methodologies enables the acquisition of comprehensive and precise weed-related data, thereby supporting accurate detection, invasion forecasting, timely warnings, and efficient site-specific management. Despite significant progress in recent years, a comprehensive synthesis of advances and applications in weed detection, invasion prediction, and early warning remains lacking. This paper presents a detailed review of the current state of research and technological development in these domains. It systematically examines the characteristics, advantages, and limitations of various sensor technologies and system architectures, and reviews implementation strategies for effective weed detection, invasion prediction, and early warning. Furthermore, applications in weed management and crop protection are summarized. Finally, the paper discusses current challenges and outlines future research directions to enhance the precision and efficiency of weed detection, invasion prediction, and early warning within sustainable agricultural systems.

title: Microalgal density modeling using a low-cost spectral sensor: A Kolmogorov–Arnold network approach
abstract: Microalgae cultivation has recently captured several applications in the field of biotechnology. Microalgae produce biomass that can be converted into a variety of valuable products, including biofuels, bioplastics, dietary supplements, and feed for aquaculture. In microalgae cultivation, monitoring microalgal density estimation is necessary. Traditional microalgae estimation techniques, such as manual counting and the use of a spectrophotometer, are prone to error, costly, and time-consuming. In this paper, we develop a low-cost integrated circuit (IC)-based spectral sensor with Kolmogorov–Arnold network (KAN) as the estimator model for density. The results indicate that the proposed KAN outperforms feedforward neural networks (FNNs). It shows that, despite its limited resolution, the sensor is capable of achieving acceptable performance.

title: FCNet: Accurate counting model of fish in complex underwater environments
abstract: Automatic fish counting in deep sea can help create optimal aquaculture environments, evaluate fishery resources, and enhance the development of marine fisheries. Currently, there is a growing interest in vision-based counting methods. However, there still exist numerous challenges in practical applications, such as complex backgrounds, low-resolution images, and irregular densities that can affect the accuracy of counting fish. To address these issues, a model for fish counting in complex underwater environments (FCNet) is proposed in this paper. Specifically, the Counting Information Enhancement Module (CIEM) is designed to strengthen the features related to counting by using the Counting Feature Convolution kernel (CFConv). Meanwhile, the interference loss function is introduced to separate the interference information in the features. In addition, the Feature Supplement Module (FSM) is designed to reduce overfitting and optimize the feature representation by connecting the original features. To evaluate the performance of the model, the Underwater_Fish_2024 dataset, which simulates the environment of the deep sea is constructed. The comparative experimental results show that FCNet is superior to state-of-the-art models and more suitable for counting in complex underwater environments. Generalization studies demonstrate that FCNet has good generalization and achieves accurate counting in real marine environments. The code and data are available at https://github.com/2226450890/FCNet.

title: FM-SAM: individual tree crown delineation and classification based on Segmentation Anything Model (SAM) and YOLOv10 in UAV imagery for forest monitoring
abstract: Forest monitoring plays a crucial role in the sustainable management and conservation of natural resources, with tree crown delineation being a key task for assessing forest structure and tree health. This study presents a novel framework, FM-SAM, integrating YOLOv10 and the Segment Anything Model (SAM) for precise tree crown segmentation and species identification in UAV imagery. The framework combines YOLOv10’s real-time detection capabilities with SAM’s strong segmentation, significantly improving segmentation and classification accuracy. SAM is also employed as a semi-supervised branch in FM-SAM to expedite the annotation process, offering a solution that reduces the need for extensive manual labeling. Experimental results on the MixedForestDataset , comprising both coniferous and broadleaf tree species, demonstrate that FM-SAM outperforms traditional deep learning frameworks such as DeepLabv3 and YOLO-based models, achieving high accuracy, precision, and recall values. The proposed method excels in complex forest environments, enhancing the effectiveness of tree crown delineation and classification for large-scale forest monitoring applications. • FM-SAM framework merges YOLOv10 and SAM for high-accuracy tree crown segmentation. • Efficient labeling with Semi-Supervised Approach, making MixedForestDataset . • The brightness of the images is correlated with the segmentation accuracy.

title: Impact of heat stress on cattle systems: Responses of production metrics to thermal stress
abstract: Heat stress (HS), a major consequence of climate change, significantly impairs cattle production and poses a threat to global food security. Assessing HS impacts in extensive production systems is challenging due to the diverse landscape and management practices. We evaluated the temporal HS effects on extensive beef and intensive dairy systems to identify thermal thresholds and inform adaptive strategies for sustaining productivity. The dataset comprised 1.3 million liveweight (LW) observations from 82,026 beef cattle over two years and 2,254 herd-average milk yield (MY) and compositional records from ∼300 Holstein dairy cows over seven years. The maximum temperature-humidity index (THI max ) was derived from climate data corresponding to production metrics. Cross-correlation analysis estimated lagged THI max effects, while linear regression and generalised additive models (GAM) assessed production impacts. We found an immediate (lag = 0 days) response of HS that increased LW ( b 1 = 0.0549 ± 0.0077, P < 0.0001), which progressively declined over time, reaching the highest negative influence at a 14-day lag ( b 1 = −0.0596 ± 0.0076, P < 0.0001). For MY, a delayed and substantial negative effect was observed at a 5-day lag ( b 1 = −0.0466 ± 0.0055, P < 0.0001), with similar patterns observed for protein and fat percentages at varying lags. Dairy cattle exhibited a THI threshold of 70, whereas thresholds for beef cattle remained inconclusive. Insights from dairy systems could inform HS impact assessment, the development of adaptive strategies, and the setting of regional thresholds for extensive beef production to sustain productivity and animal welfare.

title: Enhancing poultry multi-behavior detection with semi-supervised auto-labeling and prompt-driven zero-shot recognition
abstract: The poultry industry faces growing challenges in ensuring animal welfare, preventing disease outbreaks, and addressing labor shortages. Traditional vision intelligence-based behavior monitoring needs intensive manual labeling, which is impractical for large-scale operations, necessitating advanced, efficient, and scalable solutions. Therefore, this study explores a novel label-efficient learning approach that integrates semi-supervised and text-prompt-based zero-shot learning to enhance poultry behavior detection. Furthermore, the study introduced a dataset that includes 11 common poultry behaviors essential for monitoring to improve health, welfare, and productivity. A dataset comprising 200 annotated images (I-200) with 3,870 instances and 640 annotated images (I-640) with 14,552 instances was utilized for both supervised and semi-supervised training. Additionally, 2,500 unannotated images were incorporated to enhance the model’s performance through semi-supervised learning. This research aims to fully utilize the dataset, facilitate behavior monitoring, and support data-driven decision-making in poultry management by developing and refining an auto-labeling model using an active learning technique. The integration of prompt-then-detect zero-shot models (Clip, GDINO, and YOLOWorld) with a user-friendly text-based detection system further enhances the performance of the semi-supervised model. The results of this study demonstrated that the YOLOv9s model outperformed other supervised learning models, achieving strong performance metrics with a precision of 81.1 %, a recall of 77.9 %, and an F1-score of 79.5 %. With that as the starting point, the semi-supervised I-640 model, which utilized 2,500 pseudo-labeled images, achieved 86.9 % precision, 84.3 % recall, and an 84.9 % F1-score, outperforming all other supervised and semi-supervised baselines. This model improved performance by more than 4.6 % in precision compared to supervised model validation, but also achieved improvements of 5.8 %, 6.4 %, and 5.4 % in precision, recall, and F1-score for prediction results. Furthermore, the trained semi-supervised I-640 model with the integration of YOLOWorld text-prompt feature showed further performance improvements. This text prompt not only helps to detect specific behaviors but also assists users to easy auto-label images. This enhancement can significantly reduce manual annotation efforts and supporting timely intervention. These findings highlight the potential of AI-driven approaches for precision poultry monitoring, offering a scalable and efficient solution for sustainable poultry farming.

title: Cutting dynamics modeling and parameter configuration optimization of rubber tree multi bark-layer composite system based on dynamic finite element method and quasi-static mechanical testing
abstract: To address the challenges of imprecise control of cutting depth, nonlinear variations in cutting mechanics, and the unclear mechanism underlying minimum cutting power consumption during the operation of end-effectors in natural rubber harvesting robots, this study focuses on the outer layer of sand skin, inner layer of sand skin, and yellow skin of Hevea brasiliensis. A combined approach of numerical simulation and physical testing was employed to develop a cutting dynamics model of the multi bark-layer composite system (MBCS) and to quantify the nonlinear stress fluctuation effects during the cutting process. Based on this model, a multi-factor coupling objective equation was constructed, incorporating cutting force and cutting power consumption, to determine the optimal operational parameter set for rubber harvesting robots. Using composite material theory, mechanical constitutive models were developed for each bark layer. Basic physical and mechanical parameters of the layers were obtained through physical tests conducted with a universal testing machine. These parameters were used as input for an explicit dynamic finite element model that simulates the interaction between the bark layers and the cutting blade. The simulation results revealed the fracture and failure mechanisms of the MBCS under nonlinear cutting conditions and characterized the stress fluctuation behavior of the cutting tool. Furthermore, a multi-objective optimization function was established to identify the optimal cutting parameters. The longitudinal elastic moduli of the three bark layers were determined as 63.800 MPa, 62.791 MPa, and 25.883 MPa, respectively, and their anisotropic in-plane shear moduli were 50.154 MPa, 25.168 MPa, and 10.353 MPa. The maximum cutting force observed in the numerical simulations was 224.636 N. Stress in the bark initiated at the contact interface between the blade and bark and then propagated extensively. The optimal cutting parameters were identified as a cutting speed of 33.130 mm·s−1 and a cutting angle of 29.860°, corresponding to a minimum cutting power consumption of 111.747 mJ·mm−1 and a cutting force of 150.148 N. The relative errors between these values and the simulation-predicted values were 4.251 % and 5.617 %, respectively. The results demonstrate that the cutting dynamics model of rubber tree MBCS, developed using dynamic finite element analysis and quasi-static mechanical testing, effectively captures the nonlinear mechanical behaviors observed during actual cutting. Within acceptable error margins, the optimized parameters fulfill the requirements for low-damage and low-effort harvesting operations. This study provides both theoretical and technical support for the development of intelligent natural rubber harvesting robots and their mechanical cutting systems, and it offers references for the design of other agricultural machines involving branch or leaf removal.

title: Dynamic characteristics analysis of pneumatic collection device for continuous harvesting of dry safflower based on CFD-DEM
abstract: This study addresses the challenge of effectively and rapidly collecting filaments during continuous dry safflower harvesting. We investigate the airflow motion characteristics at the front and side inlets of the pneumatic collection device. Through mechanical analysis, we established the throwing trajectory of filaments detached by the roller brush. This led to the development of a coupled CFD-DEM simulation model for the pneumatic collection device. This model enabled the simulation and analysis of airflow motion characteristics and filament movement states within the device. Using collection rate and collection time as evaluation indicators, the airflow velocity and angle of the front and side inlets were optimized and determined through a weight analysis method. The simulation results indicate that optimal airflow velocities are 18 m/s for the front inlet and 12 m/s for the side inlet. The corresponding airflow angles are 15° and 9°. Under these conditions, the model predicts a collection rate of 99.0 % and a collection time of 0.93 s. Bench test results show an actual collection rate of 98.4 % and a collection time of 0.95 s. These results reveal errors of 0.3 % and 1.72 % from the predicted values, respectively, verifying the model’s reliability. This study provides a theoretical basis and serves as a reference for the design, analysis, and optimization of the pneumatic collection device in dry safflower harvesters.

title: Research on the influence law of the parallel fan structure of the large feeding capacity corn combine harvester on the airstream dynamics spatial characterization in the grain separation compartment
abstract: To enhance the cleaning effect of the grain harvester under the condition of large feeding volume, and to improve the adaptability between the airstream distribution law at the sieving interface and the dispersion pattern of mixed and extruded materials, and to efficiently utilize the airstream to blow and stratify the mixed and extruded materials at the sieving interface. This study focuses on the air current source of the cleaning device − the structure of the cleaning fan itself, and combines the physical properties of the grains themselves and their dispersion pattern at the sieving interface of the upper cleaning screen to study the distribution law of the internal airstream dynamics of the grain separation assembly under the changes of various key parameters of the parallel dual fans. A multi-factor optimization test was conducted on a parallel double fan structure, considering blade width, impeller diameter, number of blades, parallel clearance, and inclination angle of the splitter plate as objective factors. The wind speed distribution in front and behind the vibrating mesh served as the evaluation index. Response surface analysis demonstrates the interaction of critical factors on wind speed distribution both sieve windward region and leeward region. The optimal combination of operating parameters is determined through the utilization of a two-index optimization method: impeller diameter 500 mm, blade width 530 mm, number of blades 10, parallel gap 90 mm, and deflector plate Angle 24°. The results under this parameter combination are as follows: The airstream velocity at the front part of the screen is 12.07 m/s, and the airstream velocity at the rear part of the screen surface is 8.13 m/s. A test bench for the parallel dual-fan cleaning device was set up, and the determination of the airflow field was carried out. The experimental data demonstrate strong correlation with numerical simulation outputs. The optimized dispersion pattern of the airflow field is compatible with the dispersion pattern of the discharged substances at the sieving interface, meeting the requirements of the cleaning operation. The optimization model of the cleaning index is reliable. The findings offer substantial guidance for refining the cleaning fan structure of the harvester.

title: Multi-algorithm fusion based control strategy for electrically-driven wind pressure regulation in pneumatic precision seeders
abstract: To address the challenges of modular system information silos, high energy consumption in centralized fans, and limited wind pressure regulation capabilities inherent in traditional pneumatic seeders, this study proposes a differentiated pressure regulation control strategy based on distributed electric-driven fans. Furthermore, it develops an integrated pneumatic seeding electronic control system incorporating electric-driven seed metering, seeding monitoring, and data storage functionalities. An innovative pneumatic seeding electric control system based on distributed fans and integrated control has been developed. Through the collaborative design of a multi-fan distributed layout and integrated control architecture, dynamic regulation of seeding units’ differentiation and system information integration is achieved. The core lies in establishing an adaptive closed-loop system that combines Kalman filtering (with optimized parameters Q = 0.008, R = 0.1, Pk-1 = 0.1, Xk = 0) and incremental PI control (Kp = 12, Ki = 4), effectively addressing the challenges of wind pressure regulation under complex operating conditions. The experiments show that the system is able to achieve precise wind pressure tracking and adaptive control under different traveling speeds ranging from 4 km/h to 12 km/h. At a traveling speed of 8 km/h, the optimal wind pressures for corn and soybeans are 3.1 kPa and 5.5 kPa, respectively, with a seeding qualification rate exceeding 98 %. By establishing a cubic mathematical model between traveling speed and wind pressure, precise wind pressure matching is achieved under different operating conditions, and the excellent performance of the electric drive control system is further verified through field tests.

title: A hybrid and high-performance model for tea cultivars discrimination using canopy images with convolutional neural network and machine learning algorithm
abstract: Accurate and rapid discrimination of tea cultivars under field conditions is essential for precision tea plantation management. Traditional discrimination approaches rely on expensive instrumentation, labor-intensive manipulation, and destructive sampling, which causes difficult to implement. In this study, a hybrid and high-performance tea cultivar discrimination model, named EFLS_Model, was developed by combining convolutional neural network (CNN), feature extraction, dimensionality reduction and machine learning (ML) algorithm. A field dataset of 8,000 canopy images for 16 tea cultivars was constructed, and four discrimination methods were investigated based on EfficientNetV2. The results demonstrated that: 1) The fine-tuned EfficienetNetV2_L achieved 96.00% accuracy required long training time; 2) The approach of using the pre-trained EfficientNetV2 as the feature extractor and combined with ML algorithm substantially reduced training time; 3) Dimensionality reduction of the extracted deep features via linear discriminant analysis (LDA) alleviated redundancy and improved performance; 4) Better discrimination performance was achieved by integrating deep features and manually-extracted features. Among the developed models, the dimensionality of the combined features (including deep features extracted by the pre-trained EfficientNetV2_M, and manually-extracted color and texture features) was reduced to 15 by LDA. The EFLS_Model developed by support vector machine performed optimally with an accuracy of 98.50% and a training time of only 0.12 min. The discrimination performance of EFLS_Model outperformed other CNN models, including GoogLeNet, ResNet, VGG, MobileNetV3, and ConvNeXt. This study enables accurate discrimination of tea cultivars under field conditions, providing technical and theoretical support for developing intelligent tea plantation management platforms, while also offering a valuable reference for cultivar discrimination in other crops.

title: High-throughput extraction of individual plant height in rapeseed based on LiDAR-Camera data fusion
abstract: Efficient and accurate extraction of plant height (PH) plays an important role in analyzing its deeper phenotypic traits and improving breeding efficiency. Traditional methods make it difficult to measure PH at the individual plant level in the plot-level on a large scale, with high accuracy and low delay. To address this issue, we adopted a truss-type phenotyping platform to acquire LiDAR and RGB canopy data from 120 rapeseed genotypes from the two-leaf stage to the flowering stage, covering a total of 6 growth stages. (1) Object detection was performed to identify per plant of rapeseed images by the K-Means improved Faster R-CNN algorithm. (2) The image data before and after object detection and the point cloud data were fused to recognize per plant on the point cloud. Besides, the rapeseed plant point cloud and the ground point cloud were distinguished by color. (3) The Cloth Simulation Filter (CSF) algorithm is used to fit the ground points obscured by the canopy, which contributes to accurately extracting the PH of individual rapeseed. The field tests indicated that the mAP (IoU = 0.5) of the improved object detection method was 0.902, which achieved a high detection accuracy for rapeseed with different sizes in all periods. Specifically, in the PH accuracy verification of the No. 077 cultivar, R2 was 0.997, RMSE was 1.156 cm, rRMSE was 5.48 %, and the maximum difference between automatic recognition and manual measurement in the late stage of growth was less than 6 cm. Especially, the proposed method can extract of the height of individual plant with the values of R2 was 0.980, RMSE was 0.651 cm, rRMSE was 6.543 % in the seedling stage and the PH was lower than 20 cm. The differences of pH of 40 rapeseed genotypesunder cold stress were compared, which provide a reference for high-throughput PH extraction and exploring genotypic differences in plant breeding.

title: Corrigendum to “On-site rapid quantitative assessment of wet soil nutrients based on laser-induced breakdown spectroscopy fingerprint spectral lines corrected by near-infrared spectroscopy” [Comput. Electron. Agricult. 237, Part C, (2025) 110741]
An efficient and physics-informed regional maize yield estimation scheme by combining data assimilation and machine learning
abstract: Accurate regional crop yield prediction is essential for agricultural development and food security. Data assimilation (DA) frameworks combined with satellite observations improve regional yield estimation but remain computationally intensive at large scales. This study aims to develop an efficient, physics-informed regional yield estimation framework by integrating DA with machine learning (ML) to reduce computational costs and improve accuracy. An iterative ensemble smoother DA algorithm was applied with SWAP crop growth model to generate “virtual” yield observations across randomly selected maize pixels. These observations, together with remote sensing data, were used to train four ML models—Feature Tokenizer Transformer (FTT), Artificial Neural Network (ANN), eXtreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), and Random Forest (RF)—for regional maize yield estimation in Shandong Province, China. The results reveal that the DA-ML framework significantly reduces computational costs compared to traditional pixel-based DA methods (i.e., achieving a computational time saving of over 99.8 %), while maintaining comparable yield estimation accuracy. Among the model, RF achieved the best performance, with regional yield estimates across 114 counties showing R 2 = 0.62, RMSE = 1.19 × 10 5 t in the calibration year and R 2 = 0.49, RMSE = 1.28 × 10 5 t in the validation year. Furthermore, relative importance analysis from the DA–ML framework indicates that radiation, soil moisture, and rainfall during the jointing stage are the most influential variables for regional maize yield estimation, followed by wind speed, air humidity, and temperature during the reproductive stage, highlighting the critical role of environmental conditions in the later growth stages for determining final yield outcomes. This study showcases a reliable DA-ML system for rapid-responsive regional crop yield estimation and management decisions, with potential applicability to other crops and regions.

title: Integrating field camera imagery for monitoring maize phenology, biophysical traits, and agroclimatic factors in smallholder farms
abstract: • Field cameras detect key phenological stages across diverse agroecological zones. • Site-specific biophysical and agroclimatic variations captured effectively. • Crops in dryer ecosystems respond more rapidly to agroclimatic variations. • Inexpensive & high-frequency crop monitoring approach for smallholder farms. Accurate monitoring of crop phenology, biophysical attributes and agroclimatic variability is essential for optimizing agricultural practices, particularly in smallholder farming systems. In this study, we evaluated how field camera-derived Green Chromatic Coordinate (GCC) reflected variations in agroclimatic factors (rainfall and soil moisture) and biophysical attributes (leaf area index, crop height, chlorophyll content, and stomatal conductance) across agroecological zones (AEZs) in Kenya. Next, we utilized GCC time series to detect six key phenological stages of maize ( Zea mays L.) - emergence, stem elongation, tasseling, kernel development, ripening, and senescence - using an amplitude-based relative threshold method. This approach was cross-validated against field observed phenology. Our analysis revealed positive correlations between GCC and plant height, chlorophyll content, and leaf area index (LAI). Daily-scale Pearson lag correlation between GCC and agroclimatic factors revealed that crops in drier ecosystems exhibited shorter response times to agroclimatic fluctuations (32 days to rainfall and 14 days to soil moisture), highlighting site-specific differences in vegetation dynamics captured by field cameras. Furthermore, results indicate that GCC effectively captured phenological stages with high accuracy (R 2 = 0.9, RMSE = 7.1–7.7 days), though variability was observed across sites and growth stages. Comparisons between within-site and inter-site validation suggest that localized calibration can improve accuracy. Nevertheless, the method remains robust across varying conditions, which is supported by comparison against established curve-fitting methods. Our findings highlight the potential of field cameras as a cost-effective tool for crop monitoring at a high spatial and temporal scale, with applications in crop phenology detection, biophysical monitoring, and validation of remote sensing products. Integrating this approach into regenerative agriculture frameworks could enhance decision-making and management interventions in smallholder farms.

title: CSLTSM-Net: A lightweight two-stream mixed neural network for chicken sound recognition
abstract: Monitoring the physiological state and behavior of poultry during breeding was of great significance for the welfare and intelligent development of poultry breeding. Poultry audio contained a large amount of physiological state and behavioral activity information. Driven by the development of artificial intelligence, computer auditory monitoring of poultry based on machine learning has attracted more attention by researchers. This paper introduced CSLTSM-Net, a lightweight two-stream mixed neural network designed for processing chicken sounds. The aim was to explore deep learning applications in poultry physiological state and behavior monitoring. First, teacher-model convolutional neural network (TMCNN) and teacher-model time-series neural network (TMTSNN) for chicken sound recognition with complex structure and many training parameters were constructed. After training, both models demonstrated strong abilities to recognize poultry feeding sounds (99.75 % accuracy in TMCNN and 95.25 % accuracy in TMTSNN). Second, student-model convolutional neural network (SMCNN) and student-model time-series neural network (SMTSNN) with simple structure and few training parameters were constructed, and both student models were trained using their corresponding teacher models. Finally, SMCNN and SMTSNN model were mixed together to form a lightweight two-stream neural network CSLTSM-Net. The experimental results showed that the performance of the student model trained by the teacher model was higher than that directly trained by the original training set. SMCNN with teacher training achieved 96.25 % accuracy, 94.69 % specificity, 97.93 % recall, 94.5 % precision and 96.18 % F1-score in the test set. SMTSNN with teacher training achieved 94.25 % accuracy, 95.79 % specificity, 91.55 % recall, 96.06 % precision and 93.75 % F1-score in the test set. SMCNN with original dataset training achieved 95.75 % accuracy, 94.2 % specificity, 97.4 % recall, 94 % precision and 95.67 % F1-score in the test set. SMTSNN with original training set achieved 91.75 % accuracy, 93.72 % specificity, 89.95 % recall, 94 % precision and 91.93 % F1-score in the test set. The proposed CSLTSM-Net achieved 97 % accuracy, 97 % specificity, 97 % recall, 97 % precision and 97 % F1-score in the test set. Compared with SMCNN and SMTSNN alone, the overall performance was better. The lightweight two-stream mixed neural network could be compressed to a large extent at the cost of a small amount of recognition performance, which is conducive to solving the problem that the direct use of deep neural networks with complex structure and numerous parameters was not conducive to embedding in the miniaturized low-cost equipment with small storage capacity and weak computing power in poultry farms.

title: Book review
SAMConvFormer+LLM: Exploring synergistic fusion of Segment Anything Model with joint convolutional transformer and large language model to advance dense agricultural crop analysis
abstract: Accurate detection of densely fruited crops is essential for yield estimation, ripeness analysis, and actionable recommendations for optimized crop management using large language models. However, real-world agricultural environments present significant challenges, including varying illumination, diverse fruit sizes, and highly complex backgrounds, making robust detection non-trivial. Existing AI models in agriculture, customized on controlled datasets, struggle to generalize to real-field conditions, limiting their practical applicability. To address this, we introduce a real-field dataset capturing the complexities of a dense crop, which serves as a benchmark to expose model limitations and drive the development of more robust methods. Leveraging this, we proposed a novel detection framework (SAMConvFormer) that synergizes the Segment Anything Model (SAM) with a Joint Convolutional Transformer, combining their unique strengths for robust agricultural crop detection. This integration of SAM further significantly improves boundary delineation, particularly for overlapping clusters, blurring, and irregular fruit structures. In addition, we integrate the proposed SAMConvFormer framework with a Large Language Model to develop a comprehensive pipeline for yield estimation, ripeness analysis, and actionable recommendations for optimized crop management. The proposed model achieves state-of-the-art performance with 79.32% sensitivity, 62.64% IoU, and 77.03% Dice coefficient, representing relative improvements of 31%, 18.79% and 11.56% over the baseline model, highlighting its robustness and precision for the detection of densely fruited crops. To advance this research, we will publicly release the proposed framework and related materials, which offer a solid foundation for future studies. GitHub repository at https://github.com/Owais-CodeHub/SAMConvFormer-LLM . • SAMConvFormer integrates SAM with a Joint Convolutional Transformer. • CNNs and ViTs improve segmentation of small, irregular, and dense crops. • LLM-based support enables yield estimation and ripeness analysis. • Achieves 79.32% sensitivity, 62.64% IoU, and 77.03% Dice, surpassing baselines.

title: Routing enabled optimization and deep recurrent VGG-16 model for plant disease detection in IoT
abstract: Agricultural productivity is the major source of the economy of the agrarian nation and is also considered the major source of human activities. It is vital to detect and manage plant diseases to enhance the overall growth and quality of agricultural produce. Modern agriculture increasingly uses IoT and automation tools to monitor and collect valuable information on plant health and disease occurrence. Here, the plant disease is detected using Deep Recurrent Visual Geometry Group-16 (DRVGG-16) in the IoT platform with routing based on the Adam Dung Beetle Optimization (ADBO) algorithm. The DRVGG-16 is the combination of Deep Recurrent Neural Network (DRNN) with Visual Geometry Group-16 (VGG-16) and ADBO is the fusion of Adam optimizer with Dung Beetle Optimization (DBO). Initially, the captured agricultural images are transmitted to the base station via ADBO-optimized routing for plant disease detection. The base station initiates disease detection by applying a bilateral filter to preprocess the input plant leaf images. The preprocessed images are segmented using the DeepLabV3+ model, and features are subsequently derived from the segmented leaf areas. Finally, plant disease detection is performed using the proposed DRVGG-16 model. Furthermore, the performances of the proposed schemes are validated, where ADBO attained distance, delay and energy of 0.343 m, 0.305 ms and 0.375 J. The DRVGG-16 obtained superior results of 91.43 % accuracy, 90.63 % True Positive Rate (TPR), 90.73 % precision, 92.34 % True Negative Rate (TNR) and 90.68 % F1-score. Therefore, the proposed IoT-based framework combining DRVGG-16 and ADBO routing effectively detects plant diseases with high accuracy while optimizing energy and transmission efficiency.

title: Applications and prospects of photoplethysmography technology in animal husbandry: A comprehensive review
abstract: The increasing demand for sustainable and ethically managed livestock production has intensified the need for precise and continuous health and welfare monitoring. Photoplethysmography (PPG), a non-invasive and low-cost optical technique, shows strong potential for capturing key physiological signals related to stress, disease, and reproduction in animals. This review systematically examines the current progress of PPG in livestock farming, beginning with its principles and technical classifications, and evaluating its feasibility for use on animal body surfaces. It then explores practical applications in physiological monitoring, welfare assessment, and reproductive management. Finally, the review highlights major technical challenges and discusses emerging strategies to support the effective implementation of PPG in precision livestock systems. By integrating recent advances, this review provides a foundation for future research and facilitates the translation of PPG into practical tools for smart animal farming.

title: Robustness of CNN-Based model assessment for pig vocalization classification across diverse acoustic environments
abstract: • Robust pig vocalization classification model using Mixed-MMCT features and CNN. • Built datasets from three commercial pig farms for robustness evaluation. • Proposed a uniform 3-seconds segmentation method for real-time sound processing. • Achieved up to 91% average precision, recall, and F1-score in robustness evaluation. The study on pig vocalization classification has attracted the attention of many researchers. However, since it arises from different environmental conditions of pig farms, developing a robust model that works well across various farms remains a significant challenge. To address these challenges, this study employs a convolutional neural network (CNN) architecture to assess the effectiveness of a pig vocalization classification model in diverse farm environments. For the experiment, three datasets named GJDS, ISDS, and JEDS were collected from three actual pig farms. Each dataset consists of 4,000 audio files (1,000 non-vocal, 1,000 coughing, 1,000 screaming, and 1,000 normal), each with a duration of three seconds. A CNN with three convolutional layer blocks, max-pooling, and two fully connected layers is trained using spectrogram features. This study employed a 10-fold cross-validation to evaluate the performance of the model. Through rigorous experiments, the model achieved accuracy of 97.68%, 99.18%, and 97.45% on the GJDS, ISDS, and JEDS datasets, respectively. Robust experiments were conducted to evaluate the effectiveness of the model on an unseen dataset by using the combination of two datasets as a training set and one as a testing set. The average performances of robust experiments in terms of precision, recall, F1-score, and accuracy were 91.96%, 91.36%, 91.66%, and 91.32%, respectively. The model shows high reliability in classifying pig vocalizations within farm environments. Although performance drops under unfamiliar acoustic conditions, these findings point the way toward future improvements in model generalization.

title: High-Frequency, real-time parcel-level agricultural monitoring Framework: Integrating Tower-Based cameras and artificial intelligence
abstract: Traditional remote sensing approaches for agricultural monitoring are frequently constrained by limited temporal resolution, discontinuous coverage, and high operational costs. These limitations hinder the delivery of high-frequency, continuous, and unmanned agro-information that is critical for precision agriculture—especially in smallholder and autonomous farming scenarios. Meanwhile, communication towers equipped with video cameras are ubiquitously deployed in rural landscapes yet remain underutilized for agricultural applications. This study presents a high-frequency, tower-based, unmanned agricultural monitoring framework that progressively addresses three fundamental challenges, thereby enabling real-time, parcel-level agro-monitoring. In particular, our framework tackles: (1) accurate geo-referencing of oblique imagery through a quaternion-based geographic coordinate transformation, which precisely maps video streams to field parcels; (2) robust segmentation of cultivated parcels via a GIS-guided approach that integrates field boundary data with the Segment Anything Model (SAM) for automatic delineation; and (3) comprehensive temporal intelligence by leveraging a large language model (LLM)-based recognition strategy that fuses time-series imagery, crop rotation history, and field management data to identify crop types, growth stages, farming operations, and anomalies at the parcel level. The resulting hierarchical framework combines front-end local processing for initial event detection with cloud-based advanced analysis, enhancing operational efficiency while ensuring rapid responses. Field deployments in three agricultural regions of China demonstrate that the framework supports automated, hourly-to-daily monitoring of farming activities and crop conditions within a 1–2 km radius of each tower, with key agricultural events, growth stage transitions, and parcel-level anomalies tracked and mapped in near real time. Compared to conventional satellite and aerial remote sensing, this approach offers substantial improvements in monitoring frequency, spatial continuity, and labor efficiency.

title: Integrating tree-based machine learning with CROPWAT and ENSO for optimizing maize sowing dates in response to climate variability
abstract: Although machine learning (ML) offers advantages in agriculture, its practical adoption by farmers and extension services remains challenging, emphasizing the need for accessible tools that translate data-driven insights into actionable decisions. This study developed and evaluated a hybrid approach integrating tree-based ML models with the crop water requirement model (CROPWAT 8.0) and El Niño-Southern Oscillation (ENSO) data to predict optimal sowing dates for maize in rainfed systems in northern Thailand. Using daily climate and rainfall data from 1991 to 2022, CROPWAT 8.0 estimated maize yield reductions for different planting dates, and six tree-based ML models—Decision Tree, Bagging, Random Forest, AdaBoost, Gradient Boosting, and XGBoost—were assessed to identify criteria for minimizing yield reduction and selecting sowing windows by ENSO phase. The Random Forest model achieved the lowest RMSE (4.312), lowest MAE (1.948), and highest R2, adjusted R2, and NSE (0.959). After hyperparameter tuning, rainfall during the crop’s mid-season growth stage was identified as crucial for minimizing yield loss. For ≤ 5 % yield reduction, rainfall during this stage should be at least 108.75 mm and the number of days exceeding 35 °C during the development stage should not exceed 12.5 for sandy loam soils; for soils with higher moisture availability, the rainfall requirement decreases to 81.85 mm. Using these criteria, suitable sowing date ranges were determined and categorized by ENSO code. This hybrid approach provides practical tools for extension services, enabling farmers to plan more than a month in advance and enhance farm management and resource organization.

title: Cross-phenological domain adaptation for early-stage peach detection
abstract: Precision fruit thinning is a fundamental practice in modern peach orchards, directly influencing fruit size, quality, and yield stability. Agronomic researches have consistently demonstrated that thinning is most effective during the early fruitlet stage (BBCH 71–74), when fruits measure 10–40 mm in diameter and timely interventions determine the final crop outcome. However, thinning at this stage still relies heavily on manual labor, which is costly labor-intensive, and constrained by a narrow operational window. Automated solutions are urgently needed, yet early-stage fruit detection remains highly challenging due to the small size of fruitlets, dense canopy cover during vigorous vegetative growth, and their strong visual resemblance to leaves. To address these challenges, we propose a Cross-Phenological Domain Adaptation (CPDA) framework that transfers visual-semantic knowledge from the mature-fruit domain to the early-stage under few-shot conditions, thereby reducing reliance on large annotated datasets while improving robustness under small object and occlusion. Specifically, we design a dynamic loss function, called DyNG-Loss, to improve robustness under occlusion and imbalance, and an adaptive inference strategy, namely ASEI, to enhance detection across variable scales and sparse distributions. Extensive experiments on a self-created cross-stage peach dataset demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach, yielding substantial performance improvements over state-of-the-art fully supervised methods, with gains of +16.0% and +21.9% in AP@50 and F1-score, respectively. The resources can be accessed through the following link: https://github.com/lycode1202/CPDA.

title: Harnessing atmospheric dispersion models for predicting long-distance dispersal of small pest insects
abstract: • Atmospheric dispersion models (ADMs) are designed for abiotic matter dispersion. • Our method allows existing ADMs to be parameterized for small insect species. • Parameterization is made based on insect biological traits and flight aerodynamics. • Our method enables researchers to adapt existing ADMs to study insect dispersal. • Our method enhances ADMs’ accuracy and realism in simulating insect dispersal. Atmospheric dispersion models (ADMs) are state-of-the-art numerical simulation models for investigating atmospheric transport processes, thereby being often used to study microinsect (small insect) pest invasions via aerial pathways. However, ADMs are designed for non-living matter (e.g., gaseous and particulate pollutants). These tiny aerosols are usually represented by computational particles in 3D dispersion simulations, where they are passively dispersed. In contrast, living organisms such as airborne microinsects transported downwind have relatively large bodies. Their aerodynamic capacities depend largely on their biological characteristics (e.g., anatomical, behavioural, morphological, and physiological adaptations). Directly using ADMs without considering these characteristics could compromise their simulation realism and accuracy in predicting the long-distance atmospheric dispersal (LAD) of microinsects. To address such issues, we propose a generic method to enhance the simulation realism and accuracy by taking insect biological traits and flight aerodynamics into account. The method first allows insect species to be precisely defined and quantified as aerodynamically small enough to be passively transported in ADMs. Then it translates this species into their aerodynamic equivalence of computational particles, which can be readily parameterised for ADMs. To demonstrate and validate the method, the LAD of bird cherry-oat aphids, Rhopalosiphum padi (Linnaeus) (Hemiptera: Aphididae), from an area of irrigated pastures to the Wheatbelt at a large spatial scale in the south-west of Western Australia was simulated with 15 million aphids released. Compared with other conventional setting approaches, only our method successfully enabled ADMs to simultaneously reproduce multiple field observations, which led to biologically realistic and robust results that are essential for biosecurity management.

title: Saline patch identification using a semi-supervised knowledge integration deep learning framework based solely on UAV RGB imagery
abstract: Soil saline patches, as a direct and early indicators of soil salinization degradation, pose a serious threat to agricultural productivity and land sustainability in coastal and arid areas. However, most existing studies focus on regional-scale classification using medium- and low-resolution imagery, lacking fine-grained, high-precision identification of soil salinity patches. In this study, we propose a semi-supervised knowledge integration (SSKI) framework for the accurate extraction of soil saline patches using unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) RGB imagery. To address the time-consuming and labor-intensive problem of sample labeling, a dual-sample optimization strategy is designed. It simultaneously enhances the diversity of labeled samples via color and spatial augmentation, and selects reliable pseudo-labels for unlabeled samples through sample stability evaluation. Moreover, considering the unique characteristics of soil saline patches, a multimodal information learning network is proposed, which integrates multi-scale soil saline patch information, spectral-ecological features, and texture-semantic joint information, aiming to enhance boundary precision and inter-class discrimination. We validate the proposed method using a newly constructed UAV dataset (DongY) covering approximately 16 km2 of saline-affected farmland in Dongying, China in 2022 and 2024. Experimental results show that SSKI consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods. In particular, the multi-year, UAV-based saline patch identification demonstrates the strong temporal generalization capability of the proposed method.
