When applied to sugarcane extract samples, the platform exhibits accurate and reliable detection, with recovery rates ranging from 92.2% to 103.5% and RSD values between 1.6% and 3.2%. The exceptional performance stems from a synergistic quadruple-amplification mechanism involving CRISPR-triggered cleavage, SDA amplification, DNAzyme catalysis, and capacitor-assisted current enhancement. This work provides a powerful and field-deployable tool for the early diagnosis of sugarcane smut, showcasing significant potential in advancing precision agriculture and point-of-care pathogen monitoring.

title: Performance analysis and experimental study of flexible opening-closing single garlic seed metering device based on DEM-MBD coupling
abstract: In response to the problems of high multi-seed rate, empty seed rate, and low single seed rate in the existing garlic seed metering devices, a seed picking method of “retain one from multiple seeds” was adopted, and a flexible opening-closing single garlic seed metering device was designed. The parameters of garlic were measured in physical experiments, and the coefficient of friction was calibrated through Central Composite Design test using the repose angle as response value. The calibrated static and rolling friction coefficient of garlic-garlic and garlic-PLA were 0.202, 0.085, 0.308, and 0.108, respectively. The result of repose angle simulation test carried out under this parameter was 24.5°, with an error of 0.69% from the actual repose angle. A discrete element method − multibody dynamics coupling simulation test was carried out in combination with multibody dynamics, and comparison test between flexible opening-closing seed spoon (FSS) and L-shaped seed spoon showed that the single seed rate was increased by 10.62%. When the linear velocity of FSS was 0.15 m/s, the seed picking effect was best, with a single seed rate of 94.47%. The bench test result was 93.26%, with an error of 1.28%, proving the reliability of the simulation model and device design. When garlic number in FSS was 2 or 3, the seed clearing effect was better, with single seed rates of 92.96% and 94.70%, respectively. This study developed a seed metering device, which is of great significance for improving the mechanization quality of garlic planting.

title: Design and evaluation of a vision-guided robotic platform with root-zone drilling for targeted weed removal
abstract: Weeds pose one of the most persistent challenges to global crop production, competing with crops for nutrients, light, and moisture, and resulting in significant yield losses. Conventional weed management relies heavily on blanket herbicide application or traditional mechanical weeding, both of which suffer from limitations such as chemical resistance, environmental contamination, and lack of precision. To address these challenges, several research efforts have focused on intelligent, vision-guided mechanical weeding systems capable of selective weed removal. This study presents the design and development of MiniWeedBot, a robotic platform for autonomous target-based mechanical weeding employing a drilling-based uprooting mechanism actuated by a delta robotic arm. The system integrates an RGB imaging unit with a YOLO11n deep learning model for real-time crop–weed classification and spatial localization. The robotic platform comprises two independent subsystems—locomotion and autonomous control—linked through a UART communication interface between the NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin edge device and an Arduino Mega microcontroller, ensuring synchronized motion and actuation. The developed system utilizes readily available, cost-effective components and a modular hardware–software architecture, making it adaptable for research and field deployment. Its performance was experimentally validated under both laboratory and field conditions using sugarbeet (Beta vulgaris L.) as the target crop. Across experiments, average weed detection accuracy ranged from 89 to 94% for both the field and laboratory trials, while weed removal efficiencies ranged from 83 to 92% and the crop damage remained below 5%. Ground truth validation demonstrated reliable spatial alignment of the robotic arm with error deviation ranging between 0.34–1.43 cm. These errors remained within the projected weed canopy ensuring consistent weed engagement. Overall, the results confirm the feasibility of integrating vision-based localization with delta-arm manipulation for precise, on-the-go mechanical weeding, highlighting MiniWeedBot as a sustainable and extensible robotic platform for precision weed control, intended to complement or reduce herbicide usage through distributed or swarm-based operation.

title: Enabling early identification of nutritional deficiencies in hazelnut orchards through a data-driven robotic framework
abstract: Identifying nutritional deficiencies at an early stage is crucial for maximizing yield production and ensuring healthy plants. Conventional methods generally rely on time-consuming analysis conducted by agronomic experts. To address this challenge, this study presents a data-driven approach for the early identification of nutritional deficiencies in hazelnut orchards. Different custom datasets, composed of images acquired in a real hazelnut orchard as well as in a controlled laboratory environment, are collected, and the performance of five state-of-the-art machine learning models in early detecting nutritional deficiencies is compared. In particular, ResNet, DenseNet, MobileNet, EfficientNet, and ConvNext models, along with a baseline based on support vector machines, are considered. Data augmentation techniques are introduced to synthetically increase the datasets, and their effectiveness is extensively evaluated. Additionally, a pipeline is designed to carry out the early identification of nutritional deficiencies onboard an agricultural robot. Experimental results on the early identification show that ConvNext achieves the highest performance: 81.79% accuracy and 0.8168 F1 score on a real-world dataset with four classes, and 75.54% accuracy with 0.7552 F1 score for the more challenging six-class scenario. Furthermore, the effectiveness of the integrated system is validated in preliminary laboratory experiments using a Turtlebot2 mobile base and a Franka Research 3 arm, equipped with RGB-D cameras. • Data-driven pipeline detects hazelnut nutrient deficiencies from leaf images. • Real and lab-acquired hazelnut leaf image datasets collected and publicly released. • ConvNext achieves 85.50% accuracy on 4-class hazelnut deficiencies in lab conditions. • 75.54% accuracy on 6-class real orchard dataset validates field robustness. • Two-stage pipeline with leaf detection and classification enables onboard robot monitoring.

title: Pest localization through sequential data assimilation with pheromone sensors
abstract: Early detection and precise localization of insect pests are critical for the development of effective crop management strategies. To tackle such a challenge, a prior study proposed a Data Assimilation (DA) method that integrates a pheromone propagation model with data pheromone sensors to infer spatio-temporal pheromone emission maps and deduce insect localization. In continuity, this study proposes a Sequential Data Assimilation (SDA) method that iteratively refines sensor positioning by leveraging predicted pheromone plumes, enabling sensors to adaptively reposition toward areas of higher pheromone concentration. This approach combines data assimilation, large-scale physics modeling, and statistical optimization to improve localization accuracy over time. The method is evaluated through numerical experiments, including toy cases with unsteady wind conditions and multiple pheromone sources, as well as a realistic case based on real agricultural landscapes and meteorological data. Results demonstrate that the method significantly enhances the accuracy of pest localization compared to traditional data assimilation approaches. The sequential repositioning of sensors reduces errors in pheromone emission inference and reduces the false absence predictions from 100% to 0% within a few cycles, even in challenging scenarios such as unsteady wind or multiple emission sources. This study highlights the potential of SDA for robust pest localization, offering a promising tool for precision agriculture and sustainable pest management.

title: Accurate viscoelastic characterization of Camellia oleifera wood and finite element modelling of whole-tree dynamics for vibratory fruit harvesting
abstract: Tree dynamics modelling has emerged as a critical research focus in agriculture, particularly for the optimization of vibratory fruit harvesting systems. However, conventional models typically treat trees as linear elastic structures, neglecting their intrinsic viscoelastic behavior. This simplification often leads to inaccurate dynamic predictions and mismatched harvesting parameters. To bridge this knowledge gap, this study presents a novel modelling framework that explicitly incorporates wood viscoelasticity into tree-dynamics analysis. In this framework, an integrated testing-correction method was first developed to characterize the viscoelastic properties of Camellia oleifera (CO) wood. This method encompasses non-contact measurement of initial modulus and analytical correction of creep stress, thereby ensuring accurate determination of viscoelastic parameters while minimizing interference from interfacial friction. Finite element simulations demonstrate a consistency of over 97% between simulated and actual creep deformations, validating the accuracy of the identified viscoelastic parameters. Subsequently, these validated parameters were incorporated into dynamic analyses of the CO tree. Key findings include: (i) At a specific eigenfrequency, vibration amplitudes of branches significantly exceed those of the trunk; this branch-dominated resonance provides a definitive theoretical basis for the selection of excitation frequency. (ii) Compared with the elastic tree model, the viscoelastic tree model exhibits substantially smaller displacement and acceleration responses, accompanied by more rapid vibration attenuation, which is indicative of stronger material damping and greater dissipation of vibration energy. (iii) Under trunk excitation at the selected frequency (9.43 Hz), a high fruit detachment rate (93.94%) is achieved with a concomitant bud detachment rate of only 6.06%; this result demonstrates the potential for realizing precision vibratory harvesting of CO fruits, even under the challenging condition of concurrent flowering and fruiting of CO trees. Collectively, these findings advance the current understanding of wood biomechanics and tree dynamics, providing a model-driven foundation for the optimization of vibratory harvesting parameters for CO and other non-wood forest fruits.

title: A joint optimization method for weight estimation and re-identification based on a cattle back semantic disentanglement model
abstract: Reliable re-identification and accurate body weight estimation are fundamental for precision cattle management. This paper proposes a joint optimization method based on a semantic disentanglement model of dorsal cattle images, which improves body weight prediction accuracy while performing cattle dorsal re-identification. Specifically, the proposed model disentangles dorsal image representations into morphology, texture, and posture, and aligns each component with its corresponding downstream task, enabling more effective and independent feature learning. We further develop a method, identity-consistent multi-image aggregation, which is inspired by an information-theoretic approach to quantify the benefits of aggregating predictions across multiple images of the same individual. During inference, the proposed Weight-Constrained Identity Clustering (WCIC) method groups images by identity and filters out weight outliers to enhance cattle weight prediction accuracy. Extensive experimental results demonstrate that, compared with single-task baselines, the proposed method maintains re-identification accuracy while reducing the mean absolute error (MAE) of body-weight estimation by 4.89 kg, corresponding to an improvement of approximately 26.5%. These results highlight the effectiveness of semantic disentanglement and identity-consistent multi-image aggregation for robust, non-contact weight monitoring of cattle in real-world farm environments.

title: Influence of ground wheel encoder resolution on the performance of an electrically driven corn precision planter
abstract: The resolution of the ground wheel encoder is a critical parameter determining the speed measurement accuracy and seeding quality of electrically driven precision planters. However, the intrinsic influence mechanism of this parameter has not been systematically quantified. A corn electrically driven seeding control system compatible with multi-resolution encoders was developed. Comprehensive bench and field tests were conducted to evaluate the effects of six resolutions (50, 100, 300, 500, 1000, and 1500P·R−1) on seeding quality indicators, including the qualified seeding index (QFI) and the coefficient of variation for seed spacing (CVd). Results revealed a nonlinear relationship between resolution and seeding quality. The resolutions of 50, 100, 300, and 1000P·R−1 were identified as the “performance sweet spot,” where QFI consistently exceeded 97%. Within this range, the 300P·R−1 encoder demonstrated optimal robustness, achieving a steady-state speed measurement relative error (Δe) of only 0.31% and maintaining the lowest field QFI fluctuation. Conversely, significant performance degradation was observed in two specific zones: the “critical zone” (500 P·R−1), where specific frequency response characteristics amplified system noise, causing high speed-measurement deviation (σe= 0.774); and the “bottleneck zone” (1500P·R−1), where hardware processing limits led to severe pulse loss and a systematic error of 8.12%. Contrary to the assumption that higher resolution yields better control, this study confirms that the 50–300P·R−1 range offers the optimal balance of accuracy and stability for small and medium-sized planters using standard microcontrollers. This selection strategy effectively avoids instability and hardware-limited bottlenecks, facilitating the cost-effective adoption of precision seeding technology.

title: Early detection of cotton Verticillium wilt using hyperspectral and chlorophyll fluorescence imaging fusion
abstract: Cotton is a globally cultivated vital economic crop, highly susceptible to Verticillium wilt (VW), a disease caused by the fungus Verticillium dahliae. This infection leads to significant losses in biomass, lint yield, and fiber quality. Currently, the detection and control of VW in cotton primarily rely on visual inspection and fungicidal treatments, which are time-consuming, labor-intensive, and environmentally polluting. This study integrates hyperspectral imaging and chlorophyll fluorescence imaging techniques, while adopting a four-class classification (healthy, slight, moderate, and severe) for the accurate identification of slight infection samples—corresponding to the early disease stage—thereby facilitating the early detection of Verticillium Wilt (VW) in cotton via multi-source imaging fusion. By extracting hyperspectral data and chlorophyll fluorescence induction dynamic curves from cotton leaves with different VW infection grades, we investigate the phenotypic characteristic changes of cotton under varying VW infection levels. Using pixel-level, feature-level, and decision-level feature fusion strategies to integrate hyperspectral imaging and chlorophyll fluorescence imaging data, we identify cotton’s phenotypic characteristic information and construct a multi-input, single-output deep learning architecture based on such fusion strategies. This architecture amplifies the early phenotypic changes of VW-infected cotton and improves the timeliness and accuracy of VW detection and warning in cotton. The results show that compared with single imaging modeling, traditional machine learning and deep learning approaches using fusion strategies achieve overall improvements in detection accuracy and stability. Notably, the multi-source data feature-level fusion deep learning architecture with Resnet-1D as its main backbone exhibits significant enhancement. In this architecture, the detection accuracy for different VW infection levels in cotton reaches 99.57% on the training dataset and 97.88% on the testing dataset, respectively. The accuracy of early VW detection in cotton exceeds 99%. This research provides technical support for the green prevention and control of cotton VW, as it helps effectively reduce cotton yield losses while minimizing fungicide overuse, thus enabling precise regional spraying control. The code is available at https://github.com/TianyingYan/MISO.

title: SeqAttention-SH: Sequence attention module based convolution neural network for multiclass leaf features classification
abstract: This study proposes a new, three-module model, SeqAttention-SH, that will reduce the time, cost, and computational complexity of transfer learning-based image classification algorithms. In the first module, an edge-based model was developed to detect the region of interest (ROI) using a novel approach that leverages the strengths of the Canny edge detection algorithm. In the second module, each color channel within the ROI was subjected to a series of convolutional processes to extract distinct features. In the third module, parallel outputs from the second module are processed within the attention module. The attention module in the third stage of the proposed architecture uses a computationally efficient AND logic gate. Feature maps from the parallel channels are combined in this module, and only the most robust features, consistently active across all branches, are allowed to proceed to the final classification. This consensus mechanism increases the stability and reliability of the model. In contrast to the high parameter counts of established models like Faster RCNN (28.7 million) and VGG16 (127.6 million), the proposed SeqAttention-SH architecture is far more efficient model, containing a mere 6.5 million parameters. In contrast, it has a highly competitive structure, providing performance values of 0.9773 and 0.9978, respectively, when evaluated on the BananaLSD and Sunflower datasets used in this study. Furthermore, the training times of the underlying models are 7–23 min, while the training time of the proposed model is 3–5 min, significantly reducing training time. As a result of these performances, the SeqAttention-SH model is at a level that can compete with SOTA studies conducted on the same dataset in the literature.

title: Retrieval of forest LAI using UAV 3D real scenes combined with satellite remote sensing: a case study of moso bamboo forests
abstract: Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) three-dimensional (3D) real scene modeling is a new method to forest resource monitoring. This study presents a novel, multi-scale approach to estimate the LAI of moso bamboo forests, leveraging the high-resolution capabilities of UAV 3D real scene modeling and the regional coverage of satellite data. The objective of this study is to develop a multi-scale LAI inversion framework that bridges the scale gap between field measurements and satellite pixels by introducing UAV-based 3D reconstruction as an intermediate upscaling step. The study first utilized multi-angle UAV imagery and the Multi-view Stereo Net (MVSNet) algorithm to reconstruct highly detailed 3D models of sample plots. Structural parameters, including total plant count (Ntree), average tree height (H¯), and porosity (GF), were accurately estimated from the resulting Canopy Height Model (CHM) using segmentation. The coefficient of determination (R2) between these estimated and measured structural parameters reached up to 0.9. Subsequently, we developed a high-accuracy LAI estimation model directly from the UAV 3D model, yielding an R2 = 0.8173 with observed LAI values. Finally, the UAV-derived LAI served as reference data to construct a regional LAI inversion model. This model integrated optimized ICESat-2 canopy height with spectral and texture from Landsat 8, employing a Random Forest algorithm. The inclusion of ICESat-2 height proved crucial. The final large-scale inversion model achieved a robust prediction accuracy with an R2 value of 0.7226. Compared to using only Landsat 8, the R2 of the coupled model improved by approximately 80%, while the RMSE decreased by about 40%. This indicates that this model is more stable and the prediction of LAI is more accurate. This research demonstrates that integrating UAV 3D modeling with multi-source remote sensing data offers a high-precision and novel pathway for forest LAI inversion.

title: A machine learning-based lettuce fresh weight estimation framework incorporating agronomic traits and image features
abstract: Fresh weight is an important indicator for quantifying the growth state of lettuce. The utilization of raw RGB images and multidimensional features, in conjunction with advanced techniques such as machine learning, has become a popular trend for estimating lettuce fresh weight. However, there is currently a lack of comprehensive studies comparing the performance of various machine learning models in the task of lettuce fresh weight estimation. Moreover, the fact that machine learning models are data-driven means that the mechanisms behind the decisions these models make based on multi-source inputs are not easy to explain. In this study, a machine learning-based framework of lettuce fresh weight estimation taking agronomic traits and image features as input was developed using two self-made datasets. Our comparative study reveals that, out of the seven machine learning models evaluated, the deep neural network (DNN) exhibits the highest accuracy in estimating fresh weight, coupled with the strongest model stability and cross-variety applicability. For the DNN and extra trees (ET) models with relatively superior performance, we implement the Shapley additive explanations (SHAP) algorithms to quantitatively analyze the impact of input features on the models. The results indicate that agronomic traits contribute more to the estimation results compared to image features, and the number of leaves is the most dominant factor. The framework is capable of identifying the dominant factors influencing the model’s output, providing not only highly accurate estimations but also enhancing the understanding of the model’s decision making.

title: Generative AI empowers agricultural spectroscopy: Enhancing subsurface nutrient prediction with AE-DDIM and TimeLLM
abstract: Peanut roots serve as the primary organ for nutrient absorption and storage, and their spatio-temporal variations in nitrogen (N), phosphorus (P), and potassium (K) contents strongly influence yield formation. However, root samples are difficult to obtain due to their subterranean nature, and the complex nonlinear relationship between hyperspectral signals and nutrient contents limits the accuracy of traditional inversion models. This study proposed an AutoEncoder-Denoising Diffusion Implicit Model-Time-series Large Language Model (AE-DDIM-TimeLLM) framework that integrates physics-constrained generative augmentation with large-model semantic regression to generate peanut root hyperspectral data and achieve multi-element joint prediction across growth stages. In the AE stage, physical priors, such as reflectance range, band-group smoothness, and spectral coherence were embedded to ensure physically consistent latent representations. In the DDIM stage, Wavelength Positional Encoding (WPE), Bandwise Attention, and Dual-Domain block were introduced to further improve spectral structural fidelity. As a result, the generated spectra achieved superior performance in PSNR, MRAE, RMSE, and Valley-Corr, surpassing conventional generative models in both structural accuracy and physical realism. Based on the generated data, the TimeLLM model employed feature-driven prompt reconstruction to jointly predict N, P, and K contents across growth stages, yielding a 5–12% increase in Rp2 and approximately 20% reduction in RMSEp. Moreover, the study identified an optimal augmentation ratio that maximized model generalization without overfitting. These results demonstrate that integrating spectral physical constraints with Generative Artificial Intelligence (GAI) and semantic spectral-element modeling provides a promising pathway for accurate subsurface nutrient inversion, offering new data-driven insights for precision fertilization and nutrient management in peanut cultivation.

title: A generalization and lightweight recognition for citrus fruit harvesting based on improving YOLOv8
abstract: Abstracts For efficient performance of selective harvesting robots, accurate target recognition and locating are the prerequisite and foundation. Therefore, the adaptability of fruit target recognition algorithms, both for the multiple fruit species and for the embedded edge computing platforms, has the potential to expand the application scope of picking robots. Since the citrus fruits have diverse morphology and a wide distribution in orchards, a lightweight citrus fruit recognition model based on improved YOLOv8 was designed to recognize the oranges (Citrus sinensis), tangerines (Citrus reticulata) and pomelos (Citrus maxima) fruit on trees with less computation and tested on a picking robot arm by integrating with manipulator control programs. To improve the adaptability, the backbone network was replaced with lightweight ShuffleNetV2, a LightWeight Head detection head based on the concept of shared convolutional layers was constructed and the feature pyramid network (FPN) was redesigned into which SEAttention (Squeeze-Excitation Attention) was incorporated while integrating the advantages of MPDIoU and Focaler-IoU to construct an optimized CIoU loss function. With 7:1:2 as the ratio of training, validation and test sets, 2,250 images of orange, tangerine and pomelo fruit on the tree were involved in the training and test of the improved model. The weighted-average recognition precision, recall and mean average precision (mAP) of the test set were 92.5%, 82.0% and 89.4% for three species while the mAP values for independent orange, tangerine and pomelo test sets were 92.6%, 86.9% and 88.7%, respectively. Compared with the original YOLOv8 model, the improved model reduced the computational load by 58%, with the inference speed reaching 15.35 FPS on a workstation CPU (an improvement of 45.9%) and 0.76 FPS on a Raspberry Pi 4B (an improvement of 38.2%). The localization experiment results showed that, in the manipulator base coordinate system, the average errors of the predicted center coordinates for oranges, tangerines and pomelos were within 10 mm in the X, Y and Z directions and the radius errors under different postures were all within 6 mm. To verify the practicality of the improved algorithm, 312 fruit grasping tests were conducted in orchards. The results showed that, for oranges, tangerines and pomelos, the recognition success rates were 93.5%, 93.6% and 88.3%, the localization success rates were 90.2%, 88.1% and 83.8% and the grasping success rates were 88.0%, 76.1% and 68.5%, respectively. The proposed YOLOv8n-Light model has provided a technical basis for citrus fruit picking operations and references for the design and improvement of fruit recognition algorithms for diverse fruit species.

title: Simulation design and experiment of Dual-Roller and Guide-Rail type residual film pickup mechanism
abstract: Plastic film mulching has greatly promoted agricultural development, but it has also caused serious residual film pollution. Mechanized recovery of residual film has become the primary recovery method due to its low cost and high efficiency. Existing roller-type residual film recovery technologies and equipment suffer from problems such as complex structures, high susceptibility to film winding on the drum, and poor operational reliability. To address these issues, this study proposed a dual-roller and guide-rail type residual film pickup mechanism. A linkage structure consisting of dual rollers and a guide rail was adopted to replace the complex transmission structure, which regulates the periodic extension and retraction of tines, thus fundamentally eliminating plastic film winding. Meanwhile, rotational connections and rolling fits were employed to enhance the reliability of transmission and kinematic compatibility. Based on the established kinematic model of the pickup mechanism, optimal design software was developed, from which a set of optimal structural parameters for the mechanism was derived. On this basis, three-dimensional modeling and virtual prototype simulation were performed to verify the validity of the theoretical analysis. Furthermore, the film picking and film-impurity separation processes were analyzed through EDEM-ADAMS co-simulation, and the operating parameters of the mechanism were optimized accordingly. A prototype of the residual film pickup mechanism was fabricated and field tests were conducted. The test results demonstrated that when the machine operated at a forward speed of 7 km/h with the drum rotating at 45 rpm, the picking rate reached 92.26%, with a film winding rate of only 0.836% (well below the 2% limit of the industry standards NY/T 1227–2019) and an impurity content of 15.75%, showing excellent operational performance and high work efficiency.

title: LeafRemoval-YOLO-K: A hybrid visual recognition network for stem-petiole segmentation and cutting point localization in tomato plants
abstract: Automated leaf removal of tomato plants in greenhouse environments presents significant visual recognition challenges, including severe occlusion, structural complexity, and variability in stem–petiole morphology. To address the challenge of visual recognition in automated leaf removal of tomato plants within greenhouse environments, this study proposes a two-stage visual recognition strategy that integrates 2D image detection with depth-assisted spatial reasoning. After analyzing greenhouse growth conditions, plant structure, and workspace characteristics, three types of datasets were constructed: stem-petiole target detection, sub-image instance segmentation, and main stem semantic segmentation. A hybrid network model, LeafRemoval-YOLO-K, was developed combining YOLOv8 for keypoint detection and instance segmentation with MMSegmentation employing K-Net as the decoder head for semantic segmentation. Using self-collected datasets, YOLOv8 models achieved precision, recall, and F1-score of 85.3%, 88.9%, and 87.1% for keypoint detection, and 92.0%, 99.5%, and 95.6% for instance segmentation on sub-images. The K-Net semantic segmentation model demonstrated robust performance with a precision of 84.14%, recall of 87.09%, F1-score of 85.59%, mean Intersection over Union (IoU) of 73.34%, and overall accuracy of 86.09% in delineating the main stem region. The fused 2D features were leveraged in a cutting point localization algorithm to identify and segment the connection regions between the stem and petiole. Morphological processing refined the main stem and petiole masks, enabling accurate extraction of petiole endpoints and cutting point coordinates. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed strategy achieves a cutting point localization accuracy of 86.5%, providing an effective and reliable approach for the visual perception module of automated leaf removal in tomato plants. This work lays a theoretical and technical foundation for subsequent robotic manipulation in greenhouse agriculture.

title: A fusion framework for orchard heterogeneous images based on M-Unet semantic segmentation and transform-spatial domain
abstract: In complex orchard environments, to address the issue of reduced image quality resulting from the interaction between the foreground and background in apple heterogeneous image fusion, this paper proposes a heterogeneous image fusion framework based on modified U-net (M−Unet) semantic segmentation and transform-spatial domain. There are three modules in this framework, including parameter optimization plugin, semantic segmentation module, and transform-spatial domain fusion module. First, we propose a modified segmentation model named as M−Unet to semantically segment the source image and obtain foreground and background images. Then, the foreground and background images are subjected to Nonsubsampled Shearlet Transform (NSST) decomposition to obtain high-frequency and low-frequency subbands, respectively. Next, the high-frequency and low-frequency subbands are fused for the first time using weighted local energy (WLE) and weighted sum of eight-neighborhood-based modified Laplacian (WSEML). Subsequently, the high-frequency branch is fused by the optimized Parameter-Adaptive Pulse Coupled Neural Network (PAPCNN) model, and the low-frequency branch is fused by WLE and WSEML rule. Afterwards, the inverse NSST transform is operated to obtain the fused image of transform domain. Ultimately, this fused image and the original images are blended using a bilateral filter (BF) and a weighted least squares (WLS) optimization framework. It is the secondary spatial domain fusion to acquire the ultimate fused image. Experiments on two public datasets and one self-built dataset showed that the improved image fusion framework has significant advantages in orchard image fusion. Compared to other fusion algorithms, this fusion framework displays good performance on the detailed expression, clarity, and edge contour details of the image. It demonstrates that the fusion effect is improved by fusing the segmented images in transform domain and the source image in spatial domain. In addition, this study integrates the modular design of the framework, which has the characteristics of high cohesion and low coupling, making it easy to update and replace the modules.

title: Machine learning-based analysis of electrical impedance spectroscopy for predicting plant gravimetric dynamics
abstract: Sensor-driven field monitoring in precision agriculture requires innovative solutions for real-time plant assessment. This study introduces a novel four-point impedance spectroscopy technique integrated with machine learning algorithms to evaluate plant physiological status under field conditions. A dual experimental setup, combining a gravimetric system with a custom electrical impedance module, enabled synchronized data acquisition. The proposed machine learning ensemble achieves a coefficient of determination (R2) of 0.855 in predicting plant gravimetric dynamics, thus, outperforming conventional models and reducing error significantly. These findings support the advancement of impedance-based analytics as a scalable, non-invasive approach for large-scale agricultural monitoring.

title: Multimodal deep learning framework for robust individual identification of Holstein cattle using gait dynamics and coat pattern features
abstract: Accurate individual cattle identification is critical for precision livestock farming. Some of the challenges associated with identification in the outdoor farm environment include factors such as variable illumination, mud contamination, and frequent occlusions, which often degrade the quality of visual features, limiting the reliability of existing identification methods. Given the lack of specificity to identify and track uniform-colored cattle in outdoor environments using existing methods, this study presents a deep learning framework that integrates gait dynamics and coat pattern features to reliably identify Holstein cattle. Using ground-based video data capturing 54 cows, developed was the framework that employs structural similarity index −based gait cycle segmentation, a CNN-BiLSTM network with attention (FCANet) for gait feature extraction, and an AlexNet-based model for occlusion mitigated pattern recognition. A dynamic decision-level fusion strategy (gait-pattern weighting: 4:6 for patterned and 7:3 for patternless cows) enhances cattle identification accuracy. The framework achieved 96.76% Rank-1 accuracy for patterned cows and 92.15% for patternless ones, with dynamic fusion improving performance by 2.24%. Framework maintained 88.12% mAP for lame cattle, though health transitions affected feature consistency. Error analysis highlighted challenges from cattle head turning behaviour and environmental factors like structural shadows and mud on the cattle. Overall, the study developed a multimodal approach to address key limitations of unimodal biometrics, offering a practical solution for cow identification in heterogeneous cattle populations under farm conditions.

title: Transformer-based artificial intelligence for forecasting energy demand in irrigation districts
abstract: • Develop high-accuracy forecasting model for mid-term hourly irrigation energy demand. • Identify 12 key variables impacting irrigation energy consumption patterns. • Apply multi-head attention mechanism to enhance model interpretability and accuracy. • Optimize energy use, support sustainable operations, and reduce operational costs. Efficient energy management in pressurized irrigation systems is essential to optimize water and energy use. This study presents a novel hybrid forecasting model based on Transformer Neural Networks (TNNs) integrated with fuzzy logic (FL) for mid-term hourly energy demand prediction in irrigation districts (ID). The model was applied to the Valle Inferior del Guadalquivir Irrigation District (VIGID), Spain, using real data from 2020 to 2023. A total of 26 potential input variables were initially considered, including climatic conditions, energy prices, crop distribution, and historical energy demand ( ED ). Through a rigorous statistical analysis combining FL and correlation matrices, 12 key variables were selected to capture the most relevant temporal and meteorological influences. A sequence-to-sequence architecture was implemented to model complex temporal dependencies in ED patterns. The model achieved high predictive performance, with an average coefficient of determination (R 2 ) of 99.62%, Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE) of 0.038 and Mean Absolute Error (MAE) of 32.36 kWh, demonstrating its ability to capture nonlinear behaviour and seasonal variability. The multi-head attention mechanism enhanced interpretability by dynamically weighting inputs according to context, while FL contributed to robustness under uncertainty. Results confirm the effectiveness of attention-based architectures for irrigation energy forecasting, supporting data-driven decision-making. Accurate ED prediction is key to optimizing resource allocation, reducing operational costs, and facilitating the integration of renewable energy sources into agricultural systems. This research underscores the potential of AI-driven tools to enhance energy efficiency and promote sustainability in modern irrigation practices.

title: Tech-driven evolution of animal housing: an in-depth analysis of the impact of digital technologies, AI, and GenAI in the Era of precision livestock farming
abstract: Digital technologies and precision livestock farming (PLF) systems are transforming the livestock sector by enabling the monitoring and optimisation of farms and animal performance. However, the implications of integrating these systems into animal housing remain unclear, and an evaluation of how digitalisation is reshaping livestock facilities is lacking. To address this gap, a hybrid systematic and bibliometric review, combined with an exploratory analysis, was conducted without statistical inference or quantitative synthesis, following the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) guidelines. This review investigated the relationship between digital technologies and livestock housing across the bovine, pig, and poultry species. A total of 1,242 scientific papers were analysed by technology category, required inputs, provided outcomes, application areas, data transmission, and the use of Artificial Intelligence (AI)/Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) for data processing. Findings indicate a growing, consistent research interest across all species, driven primarily by themes related to animal monitoring, welfare, and housing. Topics such as “Engineering and Building”, “Herd Management”, and “Data Analysis and Modelling” emerged as recurrent throughout the analysed period. Animal-related technologies accounted for 21% of bovine papers, 6% of pig papers, and 1% of poultry papers, whereas software- and data-oriented tools were dominant in poultry systems. Data management and processing emerged as crucial components of PLF technologies, with cloud-based storage being predominant across all species (48% in bovine, 69% in pigs, and 63% in poultry). Artificial intelligence was used in approximately 30% of studies, with notable species variability: 29% in bovine, 63% in pigs, and 36% in poultry. GenAI remained limited, representing about 8% of AI-related papers, with applications focused on enhancing animal health and supporting farm management. The findings contribute to a deeper understanding of how digital technologies intersect with livestock housing, offering valuable insights into current developments and emerging trends in precision livestock farming.

title: A robotic harvesting system for occluded cucumbers using F2SA-YOLOv8 and HVSC
abstract: • Type-2 Fuzzy Self-Attention improves detection robustness under occlusion. • F2SA-YOLOv8 outperforms baseline YOLOv8 in occluded cucumber detection. • Multifunctional end-effector integrates cutting, grasping, and foliage-pushing. • A staged Hybrid Visual Servo Control enhances spatial alignment under occlusion. Cucumber harvesting in greenhouse environments faces challenges such as occluded cut-points and overlapping plant structures. This study presents a fully integrated robotic harvesting system that combines perception, control, and end-effector innovations to address these issues. In the perception module, a Type-2 Fuzzy Self-Attention (F2SA)-enhanced YOLOv8 module improves detection under occlusion, achieving an F1-score of 0.92635 with an average inference time of 256 ms per image, compared to 0.92056 F1-score and 903.9 ms for the YOLOv8n. The multifunctional end-effector enables simultaneous cutting and grasping, simplifying the mechanism and improving efficiency, while an eye-in-hand depth camera allows physical interaction with foliage to reveal occluded cut-points. A staged Hybrid Visual Servo Control (HVSC) strategy ensures reliable cut-point alignment even under occlusion. Experiments across five occlusion scenarios achieved success rates over 90% in laboratory trials and 81% in greenhouse tests, with average harvesting times of 55 s and 73.16 s per plant. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of a compact and occlusion-resilient design for real-time cucumber harvesting in cluttered greenhouse environments.

title: A filtering-based reinforcement learning strategy for adaptive task routing in multi-actuator robotic weeding
abstract: Robotic laser weeding offers high precision and environmental sustainability, making it a promising alternative to chemical herbicides. However, existing multi-actuator robotic systems struggle to balance planning latency, workload distribution, and actuator–chassis coordination, particularly under limited computational capacity and dynamic target distributions during chassis motion. To address these challenges, this paper presents ChronoRouteMaster (CRM), a dynamic task planning and collaboration strategy tailored for robotic multi-gimbal laser weeding. CRM formulates traversal planning as a variant of the Dynamic Vehicle Routing Problem, where the degree of dynamism is governed by chassis motion. The proposed method utilizes dynamic subspace partitioning with a filtering mechanism based on the penalty function, enabling sequential optimization of unassigned tasks. A reinforcement learning-trained agent adaptively allocates penalties and controls chassis motion according to real-time task distribution, improving both workload balance and motion coordination. Experimental results show that CRM achieves an average time of 0.93 s per actuator per weeding and a success rate of 92.7%, representing a 30% efficiency improvement over the traditional intermittence strategy. Beyond laser weeding, CRM can be extended to robotic pollination, seeding, and spraying in dynamic multi-actuator scenarios.

title: Detection method for missing seeding in plug trays for small vegetable seeds based on image registration
abstract: Vegetable seeds are small and diverse in morphology. Under high-speed sowing conditions, missing-seeding detection is affected by seed image blur, uneven illumination, and impurities, leading to low accuracy, slow processing, and poor model generalization. This study proposes an image-registration-based method for detecting missing-seeding in plug trays for small vegetable seeds. The method captures before- and after-sowing images of the same tray, performs high-precision registration to correct angular and positional discrepancies, and applies uneven illumination compensation to reduce reflections and brightness gradients. This enables stable identification of seeds and empty cells. Experiments were conducted with pepper, tomato, and radish seeds at five sowing speeds: 600, 800, 1000, 1200, and 1500 trays/h. The results showed that the detection accuracy was above 96% under all sowing speeds, with an average F1 score of 97.97%. The average F1 scores for single-seed, multi-seed, and missing-seeding detection were 96.57%, 87.09%, and 92.92%, respectively. Single-seed and multi-seed F1 scores improved by 11.67% and 12.70%, compared to YOLO11n, with an average tray detection time of 0.78 s. Under high-speed conditions (1500 trays/h), the F1 score remained at 97.47%, with accuracy decreasing by about 1.3% and F1 score by 1.2%. The system showed high stability under both high and low-speed conditions. The detection performance followed pepper > radish > tomato, with F1 scores above 97.50%, demonstrating strong adaptability for small, irregular seeds. This method enables precise, stable, and fast missing-seeding detection in high-speed sowing, providing an efficient solution for smart seedling technologies.

title: UAM-YOLO: Lightweight obstacle detection algorithm for unmanned agricultural machinery with structure reparameterized YOLOv11-Nano
abstract: High-precision environmental perception for unmanned agricultural machinery is pivotal for the advancement of smart farms. This study proposes a lightweight algorithm, UAM-YOLO, which optimizes YOLOv11n through structural re-parameterization and depthwise separable convolutions. Specifically, UAM-YOLO introduces a faster variant of cross stage partial network with 2 convolutions (C2f-Fast) module integrated with an spatial pyramid pooling fast with efficient channel attention (SPPF_ECA) module into the backbone network to enhance feature extraction in complex agricultural scenarios. The neck network integrates the proposed lightweight enhanced structurally reparameterized depthwise convolution (RepDWConvX) with ghost convolution (GhostConv) for efficient feature fusion. The detection head employs reparameterized efficient feature convolution (RefConv) and a novel loss function (generalized intersection over union (GIoU)) to improve localization accuracy during training. Experimental results on a custom dataset (comprising agricultural machinery (AM), field human (FH) and electric pole (EP)) demonstrate that UAM-YOLO achieves a high detection accuracy of 95.9% mAP@0.50 with merely 1.76 M parameters, 2.9 GFLOPs computational cost (model size 4717 KB), while operating at over 175 FPS. Compared to the original YOLOv11n, the proposed model exhibits significantly optimized performance metrics: it reduces the parameter count by 31.9%, computational cost by 53.9%, and model size by 12.3%, while simultaneously increasing inference speed by 54.9%. Furthermore, focusing on low-cost device applications, compared to YOLOv8, v9, v10, v11, and v12, UAM-YOLO achieves an FPS of 10.57 on the Qualcomm QCS6490 platform, outperforming their respective FPS of 7.27, 6.50, 7.76, 8.05, and 6.71. This represents a 31.3% improvement over the baseline YOLOv11.These advancements indicate that UAM-YOLO is a high-accuracy, lightweight, real-time solution with significant potential for environmental perception in unmanned agricultural machinery within smart farm systems.

title: Energy-based identification of dominant detachment dynamics in walnut harvesting using embedded sensing and motion decomposition
abstract: In vibration-based harvesting, fruit detachment is governed by complex dynamic inertial forces within the fruit–branch system, particularly in unstructured orchard environments. However, existing methods struggle to quantify relative motion and associated energy expenditure within this system, limiting both harvesting efficiency and control precision. To address this, we propose an energy-based dominant motion recognition algorithm for walnut harvesting that integrates a custom embedded sensing platform with a motion decomposition model. An “electronic fruit” equipped with an IMU module was developed to capture high-resolution inertial responses under manual impact excitation. The fruit’s motion is decomposed into five representative modes, and a normalised kinetic energy contribution metric is introduced to identify the dominant mode. Field experiments indicate that under impact excitation, the relative swinging motion between the fruit and branch constitutes the dominant mode, whereas torsional motion is negligible. This work provides a quantitative basis for optimising excitation parameters and contributes to the development of intelligent, energy-efficient vibration harvesting systems.

title: MCS-YOLO: A novel remote sensing image segmentation algorithm for mountain crops
abstract: Current agricultural information technology research has achieved notable success in high-precision crop image semantic segmentation for plain regions. However, significant challenges persist in complex mountainous environments, particularly in China’s Guizhou region, which is characterized by highly fragmented farmland and steep slopes. Therefore, we propose the Mountain Crop Segmentation-YOLO(MCS-YOLO), a model suitable for mountain crop segmentation. First, we introduce the Mixed Local Channel Attention (MLCA) mechanism in the backbone section, which adaptively adjusts local weights to effectively capture both global and local information. Furthermore, we employ the Multi-Scale Fusion Block (MSBlock) to extract feature information across different scales. Second, to reduce model parameters while maintaining real-time inference capabilities, we enhance the C2f module in YOLOv8′s neck section using the RepNCSPELAN4 lightweight module and incorporate the Focal-EIoU loss function to mitigate class imbalance issues and optimize model convergence. Finally, to validate the effectiveness of our proposed model, we conduct ablation studies, comparative experiments, and interpretability analyses. The results demonstrate that our model achieves optimal overall performance, showing significant advantages in segmentation accuracy within mountainous environments and enhanced precision in edge feature extraction.

title: Synergistic fusion network of GAN-based deblurring and target detection for high-speed potato seeding monitoring
abstract: Real-time, accurate monitoring of potato miss- and multi-seeding is critical for precision seeding, but challenged by motion blur induced by high-speed seed metering. Severe non-uniform, multi-scale blur causes a substantial loss of semantically discriminative features, rendering conventional “deblur-then-detect” pipelines ineffective. To overcome this, we propose a novel end-to-end GAN (Generative Adversarial Network)-based deblurring–target detection (GDTD) framework, underpinned by a synergistic training mechanism that jointly optimizes image restoration and object detection. Evaluated under high-speed potato seeding conditions with dynamic non-uniform blur, The GDTD achieved an mAP@0.5:0.95 (mean Average Precision) of 0.6843 and a Precision of 0.9115, outperforming two-stage fusion frameworks built on state-of-the-art deblurring (TSF-DeblurGAN) and detection (YOLO-based LGCSA-Detector) models by up to 19.7% and 5.73%, respectively. Furthermore, it sustained real-time inference at a processing speed of 27.3 FPS with low power consumption, making it suitable for embedded agricultural devices. By shifting the optimization paradigm from pixel-level fidelity to task-aware semantic restoration, this study provides important theoretical and practical support for precision seeding and other dynamic scenarios in smart agriculture, demonstrating that task-driven semantic restoration, rather than pixel-perfect deblurring, is the key to robust detection under extreme motion blur.

title: Growth monitoring of rice based on UAV hyperspectral images and improved deep learning method: The QRCNN-BIGRU-MLLA network
abstract: In recent years, drone-based hyperspectral imaging has become a research hotspot for monitoring crop growth status. To address insufficient multi-source data fusion and low accuracy in rice growth monitoring, this study utilizes drone hyperspectral imagery to obtain vegetation indices (VIs) across four growth stages (tillering, jointing, heading, filling), subsequently fusing these VIs with IoT sensor data (temperature, humidity, light) to measure Leaf Area Index (LAI), Plant Nitrogen Content (PNC), and Aboveground Biomass (AGB). An improved deep learning architecture, the QRCNN-BIGRU-MLLA model, is proposed, integrating grouped 1D-CNN, bidirectional GRU temporal modeling, Mamba-like linear attention (MLLA) for cross-modal fusion, and quantile regression (QR) for uncertainty quantification. Experimental results show that the model achieves satisfactory performance compared with existing methods: validation of LAI R2 is 0.92 (27.7% improvement over SVM), RMSE is reduced by 23.5% compared to SVM; PNC reaches R2 of 0.89 (30.8% improvement over MLR), RMSE decreases by 58.1% and MAE by 25%; AGB attains a R2 of 0.91 (28.2% improvement over MLR), RMSE reduces by 30.2%. The 90% Prediction Interval Coverage Probability (PICP) reaches 93.7% (LAI), 92.8% (PNC), and 89.6% (AGB). The fusion of hyperspectral and environmental data via this enhanced deep learning approach substantially improves the accuracy and reliability of growth indicator monitoring, providing robust technical support for precision fertilization and water management in rice growing regions.

title: SegTS: Subseries-driven temporo-spatial learning with Segment Anything Model for crop segmentation in satellite image time series
abstract: Crop segmentation employing satellite image time series (SITS) enables analysis of the temporo-spatial dynamics of crops. Although Transformer-based methods exhibit powerful temporo-spatial representation capabilities, frequent cloud cover in SITS still limits their ability to extract crop information from local temporo-spatial patterns. Furthermore, the extended temporal dimension of SITS exacerbates computational burdens. Herein, we present SegTS, an end-to-end SITS segmentation framework that combines local temporo-spatial modeling of subseries and global temporo-spatial modeling of overall series for accurate crop segmentation. For local modeling, we design TS-SAM, a Segment Anything Model (SAM)-based subseries encoding network that reorganises arbitrary-length SITS into subseries sets to learn local temporo-spatial patterns and filter cloud noise. It incorporates four key components: 1) a global-aware spectral compressor that aggregates key spectral information, 2) a regular subseries generator constrained by iterative or combinatorial rules to construct subseries sets, 3) a recurrent encoding mechanism with traceable temporal tags for subseries encoding, and 4) a dynamic compatible adapter that learns and adjusts temporo-spatial knowledge derived from SAM. For global modeling, we develop a dual-frequency temporo-spatial learning strategy. This strategy leverages SITS’s inductive biases and frequency decoupling to learn coarse-to-fine temporo-spatial semantics, reducing computational overhead while improving segmentation performance. Extensive experiments demonstrated that SegTS achieved MIoUs of 67.3% and 88.0% on the PASTIS and MTLCC datasets, respectively, outperforming the state-of-the-art TSViT by margins of 1.9% and 3.2%, with lower computational costs. Subseries modeling possesses a superior capability in learning local temporo-spatial patterns, offering potential applicability to diverse SITS data.

title: Development of a deep learning-assisted multispectral device for non-destructive detection and analysis of nicosulfuron stress in field maize
abstract: Early and rapid detection of herbicide-induced stress in maize is crucial for mitigating toxicity and promoting sustainable field management. Although numerous methods and equipment have been developed to monitor plant stress, many of these technologies face significant limitations, such as high costs, low accuracy, and limited integration, which hinder their practical application. In this study, we developed a portable multispectral device equipped with deep learning techniques to enable rapid, non-destructive detection of nicosulfuron-induced stress in maize. A herbicide stress experiment was first conducted on maize plants under field conditions. Spectral data and corresponding physiological indicators—SPAD value, leaf water content, and herbicide residue—were collected on days 2, 4, 7, and 10 after herbicide application. Based on these data, a multi-branch deep learning model was developed for both regression of physiological and biochemical indices and classification of stress levels. The trained model was subsequently integrated into the device, enabling on-site data acquisition, real-time computation, and visualization of results. Our results indicate that after 4 days of nicosulfuron treatment, the R2 values for SPAD, water content, and residue regression predictions were 0.79, 0.75, and 0.73, respectively, with a classification accuracy of 91.2% for stress levels. In tests using datasets from different years, the R2 values for SPAD, water content, and residue were 0.76, 0.73, and 0.70, with a classification accuracy of 87.91%. For different maize varieties, the regression R2 values were 0.71, 0.71 and 0.67, with a classification accuracy of 82.41%, demonstrating strong generalization and reliability. This study provides an effective solution for the precise detection of herbicide stress in maize fields.

title: High-Fidelity simulator for offline Pre-Validation of agricultural tractor navigation plans based on An optimized Multi-Stage steering model
abstract: Pre-validating agricultural tractor navigation plans is costly and risky when it relies on repeated on-site debugging with multi-ton machinery. This study develops an offline simulator, termed the High‑Fidelity Simulator (HFS), to support offline pre-validation and screening of navigation plans by reproducing accurate trajectory-level motion under a fixed velocity assumption and a specific tractor and controller configuration. Here, fidelity is quantified using trajectory reproduction error metrics, including Average, RMSE and Maximum trajectory differences and navigation tracking errors. The core technical contribution in this study is a multi-stage steering simulator with parameters optimization, which improves steering response matching and trajectory reproduction accuracy over a traditional first-order delay steering model. The HFS further includes farm terrain reconstruction, a basic tractor model, Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) error simulation, and a surface-specific empirical turning radius correction. In step response tests on asphalt and soil conditions, the HFS achieved satisfactory trajectory reproduction accuracy and showed advantages in challenging soil cases compared with the traditional first-order delay steering baseline. In real navigation test, the HFS produced navigation-level similarity with comparable navigation tracking errors to data logged from physical space. These results demonstrate accurate offline trajectory reproduction for the tested tractor and controller setting, suggesting that the proposed HFS can serve as a practical tool for offline screening of navigation plans under the tested use case to reduce costly and risky on-site debugging prior to field deployment.

title: Prediction of European cropland soil carbon and nitrogen using Vis-NIR spectroscopy with PLSR: Effects of spectral resolution and environmental variables
abstract: Quantifying soil carbon and nitrogen in croplands is pivotal for sustainable agriculture and soil health. Visible and near-infrared (Vis-NIR) spectroscopy has emerged as a rapid and cost-effective tool for predicting these soil properties. However, the analytical performance of Vis-NIR spectroscopy strongly depends on its spectral resolution. Moreover, environmental factors governing pedogenesis significantly influence the spatial variability in soil properties. Therefore, this study investigated the effect of spectral resolution and environmental variables on the prediction of soil organic carbon (OC), carbonates, and nitrogen in European croplands using Vis-NIR spectroscopy. The original Vis-NIR spectra were degraded to varying spectral resolutions using spectral resampling approaches. Climatic and topological variables were included for soil property prediction. Meanwhile, partial least squares regression (PLSR) is employed to model the relationship between soil properties and spectra. In the experiments, a total of 8,941 cropland soil samples collected across the European croplands were utilized. The results illustrated that Vis-NIR spectra with high spectral resolution (≤10 nm) yielded statistically consistent predictions of soil properties. In contrast, lower spectral resolution resulted in reduced prediction accuracies. The effect of environmental variables on predicting soil properties was related to the spectral resolution of Vis-NIR spectra. At high spectral resolution, the combination of Vis-NIR spectra and climatic variables provided superior predictions for soil OC and nitrogen. The optimal results for soil carbonates were obtained when Vis-NIR spectra were integrated with both climatic and topographical variables. At low spectral resolution (≥100 nm), the inclusion of environmental variables tended to reduce prediction accuracy compared to models using spectral data alone.

title: Clarification question generation for ambiguous agricultural knowledge graph question answering
abstract: Agricultural knowledge question-answering systems are a key component of agricultural knowledge services. However, agricultural questions often involve dynamically changing factors, and real-world user queries are typically brief, which can lead to ambiguity. Existing question-answering systems (Q&A systems) lack the ability to proactively ask clarification questions, resulting in a poor user experience. This paper investigates the proactivity of Q&A systems, focusing on clarification question generation (CQG) in ambiguous knowledge graph question answering (KGQA), using corn as a case study. We construct the first CQG dataset in the agricultural domain, which contains a corn knowledge graph consisting of 99,381 triples and 2447 ambiguous question-clarification question pairs. Furthermore, we propose KGQA-CQG, a CQG framework for ambiguous KGQA that incorporates knowledge retrieval and employs a joint encoding mechanism of knowledge and questions to effectively identify ambiguous scenarios. The experiments show a general improvement of 4.10% in ROUGE-L and 8.30% in BLEU-4, respectively. ClariCorn, the first CQG dataset in the agricultural domain, addresses the scarcity of Natural Language Processing (NLP) resources for agriculture and supports reproducible research in crop-specific question answering. Our proposed method provides a foundation for corn-specific intelligent agricultural knowledge services, with potential extension to other crops pending dataset expansion. The dataset and code are publicly available at https://github.com/HFIPS-znrz/KGQA-CQG.

title: Development of an integrated UAV-based precision aerial seeding system for rice-paddy artwork
abstract: Creative field crop landscapes, exemplified by rice-paddy artwork, can enhance the added economic value of agricultural produce and facilitate the integration of primary and tertiary industries. However, the current establishment of such landscapes by the traditional method relies heavily on manual labour, which is inefficient and costly. Moreover, conventional agricultural machinery is ill-suited to the complex boundaries of artistic patterns and the requirement for mixed-crop planting within designated areas. To address these challenges, an integrated unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV)-based precision aerial seeding (PAS) system for creating rice-paddy artwork was proposed. The core of this system is a section on-demand start-stop control (SODC) system for strip-seeding UAV, which integrates several key components: a mathematical model for calculating the midpoint coordinates of operational sections, a system lag distance compensation method, a polygon grouping-based algorithm for identifying pattern regions, a control strategy for generating operational commands, and a hierarchical aerial seeding plan. Simulation tests, site trials, and field experiments were conducted to evaluate the system’s performance. Results demonstrated that the programme execution time during aerial seeding was shorter than the GNSS module’s positioning cycle (0.1 s), fulfilling real-time operational requirements. With lag compensation enabled, the longitudinal deviation of seed deposition at pattern boundaries was reduced from 1 ∼ 1.79 m to −0.19 ∼ 0.17 m, confirming high planting precision. While an increase in flight velocity led to an average 7.6% decrease in pattern modelling accuracy, increasing the number of operational sections improved it by an average of 27.78%. In the field experiments, the pattern average similarity (AS) in two test cases reached 87.25% and 85.75%, respectively. Furthermore, the system achieved an average operational efficiency of 0.1 ha·h−1, which is 5.26 times that of the purely manual method and represents a 92.88% reduction in labour cost. These results validate the system’s capability for precise and efficient planting for rice paddy artwork in real field conditions. This study provides technical support and a reference for research on mechanised planting system for field crop landscapes and relevant precision agriculture applications.

title: Editorial Board
LSSCM-MobileTeaNet: A UAV-based lightweight spatial–spectral convolution model for large-scale estimation of chlorophyll and nitrogen content in tea plantations
abstract: Accurate estimation of leaf chlorophyll and nitrogen content is essential for precision management in tea plantations. This study proposes LSSCM-MobileTeaNet, a UAV-based lightweight spatial–spectral convolution model for the rapid and non-destructive prediction of chlorophyll and nitrogen levels in tea leaves. The proposed model employs a multi-stage stem to enable hierarchical feature extraction. In addition, an LSSCM-Block is introduced to strengthen spectral–spatial feature fusion. This design allows the network to effectively capture low-level spectral signatures as well as high-level spatial structures from multispectral UAV imagery. Ablation experiments demonstrate that each module provides distinct and complementary contributions to model performance. Their integrated implementation ensures both prediction stability and accuracy. Based on five-fold cross-validation, LSSCM-MobileTeaNet achieves a mean RMSE of 2.88, an MAE of 2.41, and an R2 of 0.85, indicating strong predictive precision and robustness. Furthermore, a user-friendly deployment system was developed to facilitate practical application. The system allows users to upload preprocessed spectral data in .npy format for automatic prediction of chlorophyll and nitrogen content. This functionality supports large-scale and high-throughput monitoring across entire tea plantations. Overall, the proposed system provides a practical solution for UAV-based canopy trait assessment and enables efficient, reliable, and site-specific nutrient evaluation over extensive tea-growing regions.

title: Multi-view multi-task deep neural network for effective tea classification and quantitative flavor factor evaluation
abstract: Rapid and accurate evaluation of tea quality using artificial intelligence (AI) algorithms is crucial for effective quality management. Existing algorithms primarily focus on one-dimensional data (typically the appearance of dry tea) for classification or grading, often overlooking the complexity of tea flavor. Here, we developed Tea MvMtNet, a multi-view, multi-task deep neural network that processes visual data from dry tea appearance, infusion color, and waste tea to assess all five flavor factors, including taste and aroma, and to classify teas into distinct categories. The model incorporates an attention-enhanced bidirectional feature pyramid network for multi-scale fusion, extracting both global and local details from each view. The semantic enhancement module incorporates prior knowledge, leveraging cross-modal attention and graph attention networks to refine visual features for accurate prediction of flavor factors. Additionally, the multi-view fusion dynamically aggregates the three visual features to predict aroma, taste, and tea category. To optimize task performance and address data imbalance, we develop a multi-task balanced focal regression loss function for multi-task learning. Our approach achieved a classification accuracy of 98.11% and demonstrated superior precision in evaluating dry tea appearance (average absolute error percentage: 19.60%), infusion color (28.40%), aroma (26.48%), taste (31.67%), waste tea (17.20%), and overall score (17.23%), demonstrating that the accuracy of the model was comparable to that of senior tea evaluators. Furthermore, the overall score achieved an R2 value of 0.8359, with the best performance for aroma and taste (R2 > 0.75). These results highlight Tea MvMtNet as a comprehensive and precise tool for automated tea quality management.

title: Structural equation modelling for sustainable land management: Assessing ridge-furrow rainwater harvesting and chopped straw effects on soil moisture dynamics and sainfoin yield in semi-arid slopes
abstract: Climate change-induced drought and erratic rainfall intensify soil erosion in semi-arid sloped regions, threatening long-term agricultural sustainability. Although plastic mulching in RFRH systems reduces erosion and water loss, increasing concerns about soil microplastic accumulation justify the evaluation of chopped straw as a biodegradable and eco-friendly alternative for sustainable crop cultivation. To enhance resource efficiency and sustainability, this study employed structural equation modelling to (i) assess the combined effects of RFRH and chopped straw application on runoff, sediment yield, soil water storage (SWS), organic matter, nutrients, soil temperature, evapotranspiration, fodder yield, and water use efficiency (WUE) of sainfoin; and (ii) identify optimal RFRH and chopped straw integration for sustainable crop-soil–water management in sloped landscapes. A two-year (2022–2023) field experiment with sainfoin (Onobrychis viciifolia) as the test crop used a split-plot design with chopped straw application patterns (0 and 4 × 103 kg ha⁻1) as main plots and RFRH methods (flat planting (FP, control), open-ridging (OR), and tied-ridging (TR)) as subplots. The results showed treatment effectiveness followed TR > OR > FP, and integration with chopped straw significantly enhanced soil conditions, WUE and sainfoin fodder yield. Compared to FP under no chopped straw, OR and TR reduced runoff by 28.6% and 44.4%, increased SWS by 8.77 and 28.13 mm, enhanced WUE to 1.86 and 2.83 kg ha⁻1 mm⁻1, and improved fodder yield by 9.9% and 16.9%, respectively. Under chopped straw application, OR and TR further reduced runoff by 31.4% and 52.6%, increased SWS by 16.70 and 32.28 mm, enhanced WUE to 3.53 and 6.71 kg ha⁻1 mm⁻1, and improved fodder yield by 13.1% and 18.3%, respectively. Chopped straw application improved total nitrogen (29.49%), phosphorus (16.40%), potassium (7.49%), and organic matter (19.85%), leading to an increased soil health index (0.29) and fodder yield compared to no chopped straw application. Structural equation modelling revealed that chopped straw application and RFRH had significant indirect positive effects (0.41) and (0.49) on sainfoin fodder yield, respectively. Tied-ridging combined with chopped straw proved most effective in optimizing soil quality and water use while enhancing sainfoin productivity. These findings offer practical strategies for sustainable soil-crop-water management in erosion-prone, water-scarce sloped areas.

title: Assessing in-season crop nitrogen status based on UAV multispectral imaging and AI-driven model optimization
abstract: • Red-edge and NIR VIs correlated best with N indicators at DC55 and DC65 stages. • NSGA-based feature selection improved model stability and estimation accuracy. • KFNN models outperformed RF in estimating N uptake and DM, with D-index gains >10% • Top 3 VIs yielded robust models with D-index >0.75 across all indicators and stages. Maintaining an appropriate nitrogen (N) status is crucial for achieving desirable grain quality in barley. N fertilization is typically applied at sowing, leaving limited scope for in-season adjustment. Timely monitoring is essential for grain N concentration prediction and quality assessment. This study aimed to develop an artificial intelligence (AI) driven framework to estimate N concentration, N uptake, N nutrition index (NNI), and dry matter (DM) using unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV)-based multispectral imagery collected at three key growth stages (jointing, DC30; heading, DC55; and flowering, DC65). Two machine learning algorithms, random forest (RF) and Keras-based feedforward neural network (KFNN), were used to estimate N-related indicators. Multiple vegetation indices (VIs) were extracted from multispectral data. Feature importance ranking and non-dominated sorting genetic algorithm (NSGA) were applied to optimize input variables for improving model performance and robustness. The results showed that N-related indicators were better estimated at DC55 and DC65 stage, while DM were well predicted at DC30 stage. KFNN consistently outperformed RF in modeling complex traits such as N uptake and DM, with D-index improvements exceeding 10%. NSGA-optimized feature sets outperformed traditional importance ranking by improving both model stability and predictive accuracy. The top 3 VIs combinations achieved a favorable balance between accuracy and redundancy. All models achieved D-index values above 0.75 across N-related indicators and DM. This study demonstrates that combining growth-stage-specific modeling with AI-based feature optimization provides a scalable and cost-effective approach for real-time N monitoring, supporting precision N management in spring barley.

title: A dual-to-multi-mode end effector: design, evaluation and optimal mode selection for abnormal leaf removal in hydroponic lettuce
abstract: Automated removal of abnormal leaves from hydroponic lettuce is a critical bottleneck restricting full-process automation of commercial harvesting. Based on manual removal motions, this study identifies rotation and translation as core basic motions, proposing six candidate mechanized removal methods with single or combined motions. A novel end effector with dual-mode configuration and multimode operational capability is developed for all candidates, mounted on a robotic arm to build a performance test platform. With removal success rate, normalized center Euclidean offset rate and single-leaf operation time as core indicators, systematic comparative experiments evaluate the comprehensive performance of different modes. Experiments under fixed lettuce conditions show that the large-angle rotational separation in the vertical plane mode performs optimally: 88.14% success rate, 44.53% offset rate and 2.864 s operation time. This mode fits the sequential root cutting and leaf removal process, and calibration can be performed at one-operation intervals based on offset characteristics, reducing frequency and overall operation time. Verification in non-fixed scenarios indicates that its success rate (88.68%) and operation time (2.864 s) are basically equivalent to fixed conditions, but offset rate exceeds 200%, requiring repositioning after each operation. This result first verifies the feasibility of non-fixed automated removal, supporting the construction of a parallel root cutting and leaf removal process. In conclusion, the proposed end effector and optimal mode adapt flexibly to different production scenarios, providing important technical references for improving the automated hydroponic lettuce production chain in vertical farming.

title: Edge-RegNet: An adaptive edge-aware fusion and task alignment framework for detecting Papilionidae larvae on citrus
abstract: Accurate detection of Papilio xuthus larvae in unstructured orchard environments remains a significant challenge due to their extreme camouflage (protective mimicry) and non-rigid body characteristics. Addressing the perception bottlenecks of general one-stage detectors regarding “camouflaged” and “soft-bodied” targets, this study presents Edge-RegNet, a lightweight detection architecture driven by biological characteristics. This framework constructs a dual computational mechanism comprising frequency-domain texture reconstruction and spatial topological alignment. First, we introduce an Adaptive Edge-aware Spatial Module (AESM), which employs multi-scale differential operators to explicitly enhance high-frequency boundary textures typically suppressed by the backbone network, thereby resolving mimicry-induced feature confusion. Second, a Cross-scale Dynamic Fusion Network (CDFN) is proposed, incorporating a bidirectional injection mechanism for semantics and details to achieve dynamic equilibrium in feature flow. Third, we integrate a Task-Aligned Dynamic Detection Head (TAD-Head), utilising dynamic convolution operators to adaptively calibrate the spatial distribution of classification and regression features, correcting localisation drift caused by non-rigid body deformation. Furthermore, a “structured pruning and knowledge distillation” joint optimisation strategy is adopted to achieve high-dimensional feature migration and extreme model compression.
