Empirical results demonstrate that the Edge-RegNet-n model achieves a mean Average Precision (mAP@0.5) of 91.8% and a real-time inference speed of 220 FPS, with a parameter count of only 2.62 M. This study effectively resolves the “accuracy–speed” trade-off in complex habitats, providing core algorithmic support for the low-cost edge deployment of intelligent field monitoring equipment.

title: Straw cutting mechanisms in a stabilizing ring-assisted rotary shear system revealed by multi-condition experiments and DEM simulations
abstract: Accurate assessment of straw mulch mass is essential for evaluating conservation tillage practices. However, conventional field sampling methods often suffer from boundary-induced errors due to unclear separation of surface straw, which can introduce significant measurement deviations. To address this limitation, a stabilizing ring-assisted rotary shear system is proposed to enable locally confined cutting and controlled severing of boundary straw prior to mass measurement. To mechanistically capture this process, a soil-straw-tool coupled discrete element method (DEM) framework is established, allowing simultaneous representation of multi-material interactions that are not resolved in conventional single soil or straw simulations. The effects of stabilizing ring confinement, severing column rotational sequences, axial velocity, and axial acceleration are systematically analyzed during cutting. Simulation results show that ring-assisted confinement stabilizes blade-straw contact, enabling sustained shear accumulation and improved cutting continuity. Rotation reversal interrupts shear transfer despite higher mechanical loads, reducing effective cutting. Displacement-based analysis further indicates that cutting under constant axial velocity is capacity-limited and governed by spatial progression, whereas axial acceleration enhances early-stage shear engagement through rapid blade-straw interaction. These findings provide new insights into the mechanics of confined straw cutting, and reveals the effects of coordinated confinement, rotational motion, and axial kinematics on cutting efficiency. The proposed system and methodology offer a practical foundation not only for accurate measurement of straw mulch mass, but also for optimizing mechanized straw management systems.

title: Fine-scale aboveground biomass estimation of restored vegetation in tailings ponds: integrating UAV multi-source data and explainable machine learning
abstract: • Constructs an interpretable ML framework fusing UAV LiDAR and hyperspectral data. • Boruta-RF model achieves high accuracy (R 2 = 0.86) by overcoming spectral saturation. • LiDAR height metrics (H10, H20, H25) critically mitigate signal saturation effects. • SHAP analysis reveals feature shift from texture to height metrics in high-AGB zones. Accurate and automated quantification of aboveground biomass (AGB) is a prerequisite for the precision management and digital evaluation of ecological restoration in complex terrains, such as tailings ponds. However, traditional optical remote sensing often suffers from signal saturation in dense vegetation and lacks interpretability in modeling. To handle these challenges, this study created an AGB inversion framework integrating UAV multi-source data and explainable machine learning (ML). Using the Boruta algorithm, 38 key variables were selected from an initial set of 128 features extracted from hyperspectral imagery and LiDAR data. These features were utilized to construct RF, XGBoost, SVM, and KNN models, with the RF model achieving the highest accuracy with R 2 = 0.86 and RMSE = 29.22 Mg/ha, and superior stability. Furthermore, independent validation using 24 external samples confirmed the model’s robustness (R 2 = 0.78). SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis revealed that while spectral vegetation indices were the dominant contributors overall, feature importance shifted across AGB gradients. Texture features were critical drivers in low AGB regions, whereas LiDAR canopy height metrics played a decisive role in high AGB areas, effectively mitigating spectral saturation. The estimated AGB exhibited marked spatial heterogeneity, ranging from 83.31 Mg/ha to 396.43 Mg/ha, with the highest AGB clustered in the northern regions. Furthermore, while Populus constituted 79.8% of the total AGB, Robinia demonstrated a superior aboveground carbon stock capacity per unit area. This framework offers a robust, interpretable approach for fine-scale AGB estimating, supporting green mine development and carbon neutrality goals.

title: In-situ self-compensation method for cavity-type hole seeding system
abstract: To address the issue of miss seeding and empty holes in existing simplified rice seed-metering devices during precision hole direct seeding with reduced seed rate, this study proposed an innovative light curtain cavity-scanning method for miss seeding detection and curve variable-speed in-situ self-compensation strategy based on the cavity-type seeding method and combined pulse principle. A combined pulse-based miss seeding judgment principle was established, and a mathematical model for curve variable-speed compensation under different continuous miss seed-filling cavity conditions was developed. A “filled and miss-filled combination” in-situ self-compensation method was designed and implemented. Subsequently, experiments were conducted on the curve variable-speed control accuracy of driving motor, seeding trajectory comparison, and seeding uniformity. The results indicated that the average error of start deviation angle and variable-speed motion angle of driving motor for seed compensation did not exceed 0.12°, and the error of variable-speed duration was no more than 0.0008 s, achieving precise control of variable-speed compensation. The seeding trajectory range of compensation was basically consistent with that of the normal seeding. The average errors of hole diameter and hole spacing between normal seeding and compensation were respective no more than 1.48 mm and 1.01 mm, demonstrating the capability of seeding system to achieve in-situ compensation. The seeding system reduced the miss seeding rate from no less than 11.11% to no more than 1.11% and increasing the qualified rate from no more than 79.11% to above 90% after integrating the proposed self-compensation method into the purely mechanical seeding mechanism.

title: Combining dynamic Bayesian prediction of the crop coefficient with automated lysimetry for highly accurate water-use control
abstract: Crop evapotranspiration is a key parameter for efficient irrigation, that can be estimated by means of the standardized FAO-56 technique based on a reference evapotranspiration and on a crop-specific coefficient (Kc). The latter, however, must be experimentally measured and varies with the environmental conditions and with the crop's leaf area development over time. The experimental assessment of Kc simulates intricate soil–plant-atmosphere interactions. This involves solving numerous equations that require extensive daily meteorological, crop, and substrate data over the entire growing season. Since this process demands significant time and resources, irrigation on the base of crop evapotranspiration is often disregarded. To make this method of irrigation feasible in soilless cultivation instead, we introduce a smart lysimeter composed of commercial off-the-shelf sensors, a cloud server and a lightweight IoT client that controls the irrigation duration such that the leaching fraction is kept constant. Sensor data acquired by the lysimeter is analyzed on the cloud server by means of an AI component based on a Dynamic Bayesian Network to produce a daily estimate of Kc. The AI component learns from sensor data over time to predict the evolution of Kc several days ahead and to adjust the irrigation threshold in the IoT client. Combining the Kc estimate with short-term weather forecast, the smart lysimeter can easily forecast the crop evapotranspiration and actuate an efficient irrigation, even across different geographical regions. The experiments conducted with the ornamental guelder rose (Viburnum opulus L.) under different weather conditions show that, during a Mediterranean summer, our lysimeter achieved 17% water savings in irrigation and a 64% reduction in runoff compared to manual irrigation by experienced farmers during periods of variable weather. The RMSE of Kc, averaged across all prediction horizons from one to seven days ahead, is 6.7% of full scale.

title: MDSN-Net: A multi-domain spectral nexus network for underwater accurate fish counting
abstract: Accurately estimating fish populations is essential for aquaculture, fishery resource assessment, and aquatic ecological monitoring as it provides a reliable scientific foundation for effective management and ecological protection. However, fish characteristics and environmental conditions are often highly entangled across different domains, such as varying lighting and underwater environments, leading to notable domain shifts. These shifts hinder the ability of existing methods to maintain stable counting accuracy and robustness in cross-domain scenarios. To address these challenges, this study proposes a Multi-Domain Spectral Nexus Network (MDSN-Net). This approach introduces a frequency-domain multi-scale encoding mechanism that decomposes underwater images into two complementary spectral-domain representations: low-frequency structural components and high-frequency texture components. This frequency separation effectively mitigates cross-domain feature entanglement. To enhance low-frequency information, an Evolution SSIM Low-Frequency Attention module is designed. By integrating brightness-contrast consistency with a gradually evolving process based on ordinary differential equations, it dynamically compensates for uneven illumination and contrast distortion. For high-frequency details, a Biphase Resonance High-Frequency Attention module is introduced. This module models in-phase and anti-phase dual-domain responses to accurately highlight fish edges and subtle textures while suppressing aliasing noise, thereby enhancing the separation of fish from complex backgrounds. Finally, both frequency components are normalized into a probability distribution using JSDFuse, enabling adaptive alignment and collaborative enhancement across frequency bands. This mechanism helps reduce domain shift in multi-domain scenarios. Experimental results demonstrate that MDSN-Net achieves an MAE of 2.32 and RMSE of 2.98 on CCD. It also shows strong counting accuracy and generalization performance on multi-domain fish counting datasets such as DGCD and UGCD, maintaining stable cross-domain performance under varying lighting conditions, underwater environments, and fish densities. These results offer valuable insights for underwater ecological monitoring and the sustainable management of fisheries.

title: Artificial intelligence-based identification of drought-resilient bean cultivars using multi-source data in the Delmarva region
abstract: • A multi-year AI framework identifies drought-resilient bean cultivars under variable climate. • Integrating agronomic and environmental data improves yield prediction across Delmarva seasons. • Random Forest and XGBoost capture nonlinear genotype–environment yield interactions. • Heat stress and precipitation emerge as dominant drivers of bean yield variability. • Framework supports climate-smart, cultivar-specific selection for resilient bean production. Beans play a vital role in food and nutritional security while enhancing soil fertility; however, their productivity in the US Delmarva region is frequently negatively affected by recurrent droughts and irregular rainfall patterns. This study aims to identify drought-resilient bean cultivars by integrating multi-year field data with artificial intelligence (AI). Drought resilience was evaluated across four bean genotypes and varieties comprising eleven cultivars using multi-year field data (2014–2020 and 2023) under natural weather variability. Agronomic traits related to growth and yield were evaluated alongside drought indices and seasonal temperature and precipitation. Multi-year agronomic and environmental data were integrated into an AI workflow using Random Forest (RF) and Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), with repeated k-fold cross-validation, to predict yield and identify drought-resilient bean cultivars. Yield varied widely across seasons (93.5–6279.9 kg ha −1 ), reflecting substantial interannual climate variability, with drought indices indicating pronounced stress in dry years and reduced sensitivity in wetter seasons. Correlation analysis indicated generally weak relationships; pods, seeds, and moderate biomass were more consistently related to yield, while the heat stress index (HSI) showed strong collinearity (r = 0.88). Feature-importance analyses highlighted genotype and climate drivers as dominant predictors of drought resilience. Year-wise model fits were excellent in 2017–2019 and 2023 (RF R 2 ≤ 0.98; XGBoost ≤ 0.96) but weaker in 2014–2015. These findings demonstrate that integrating multi-year field data with AI enables robust identification of drought-resilient bean cultivars and supports data-driven cultivar selection for climate-resilient bean production in the mid-Atlantic region.

title: You only look at triggers: spatiotemporal behavioral proposal generation for group-housed pig interactions
abstract: • Introduces new metrics for transparent benchmarking of proposal efficiency. • Trigger-based framework reduces redundancy in behaviour proposal generation. • Enables robust detection of multi-class concurrent pig interactions. • Provides the PigInteraction dataset for multi-class social behaviour analysis. Understanding social interactions in group-housed pigs is critical for the understanding and improvement of animal welfare, health monitoring, and advancing precision livestock farming. Computer vision is emerging as an objective and accurate manner to detect, classify and quantify important behaviors of farm animals. However, a major challenge lies in accurately recognizing multiple behavior categories that often occur concurrently and overlap in both space and time within untrimmed video data. To address this, we propose a trigger-based approach for spatiotemporal behavioral proposal generation, which achieves 100% recall while significantly reducing redundant background proposals across five key behavior types: fighting, tail biting, displacement at the feeder, feeder-visiting, and drinker-visiting. Combining evolutionary parameter optimization with posture recognition, keypoint detection, and spatial constraints, our approach enables efficient and scalable detection even in densely populated animal housing environments. This method achieves 100% recall for five welfare-relevant behaviors while reducing redundant spatiotemporal proposals by ∼ 10×, enabling efficient analysis of long, dense farm recordings. A unified, modular trigger framework built over standard key-points and rotated bounding box that support both animal to animal and animal to object interactions. Using this approach, we also constructed a publicly available benchmark dataset with efficiency metrics, called PigInteraction, which features diverse and well-annotated interaction samples for downstream behavior analysis. The dataset is accessible at: https://gitlab.kuleuven.be/m3-biores/public/m3pig .

title: A scalable consensus docking decision-support pipeline for aquaculture bridging foodomics and affordability
abstract: Marine seaweeds contain diverse metabolites, yet practical pipelines are needed to triage multi-target candidates for aquaculture and nutraceutical development. We developed a scalable decision-support workflow integrating foodomics, dual-engine consensus docking, network pharmacology, and targeted validation to prioritize bioactive metabolites from the red seaweed Agardhiella subulata. Dual-solvent extraction and UHPLC–HRMS profiling yielded 392 annotated metabolites. After exhaustive conformer generation (1,916 conformers), ligands were screened against nine fibrosis-relevant protein structures using AutoDock Vina and LibDock; only ligand–target pairs meeting stringent thresholds on both engines were retained to reduce single-engine false positives. This consensus rule reduced the shortlist to five metabolites (∼1.3% of the library), supporting cost-aware experimental triage. Consensus scoring highlighted flavin adenine dinucleotide (FAD) as an exceptional multi-target hit with concordant high-affinity binding to four targets (p62/SQSTM1, COL1A1, mTOR, ULK1), whereas saikosaponin E showed consensus binding to two autophagy regulators (ULK1 and Beclin-1). Network analysis placed FAD within riboflavin/oxidative-stress modules and positioned saikosaponin E within an autophagy-focused subnetwork. To test docking robustness, explicit-solvent molecular dynamics simulations (100 ns) were performed for representative complexes, showing persistent pocket association and favorable MM/PBSA estimates. Finally, in LX-2 hepatic stellate cells, A. subulata extract and saikosaponin E attenuated fibrogenic activation (COL1A1 and ACTA2) and modulated autophagy-related transcripts (MAP1LC3B and SQSTM1) at non-cytotoxic doses, providing preliminary biological support for the prioritized hits. This framework compresses large metabolomes into a tractable, high-confidence candidate set, enabling transferable screening of marine resources.

title: Online prediction and system implementation of seeding-unit vibration in no-till precision maize seeding using an improved metaheuristic LSSVM
abstract: No-till precision maize seeding exposes seeding units to complex and highly variable field conditions, which intensify vibration and compromise sowing quality. To enable real-time prediction and evaluation of these vibration responses, this study proposes an integrated framework combining multi-sensor vibration modeling with an online prediction system. Five accelerometers were deployed at key structural locations of the seeding unit, and their signals were fused to construct a composite vibration index representing the unit’s global dynamic behavior. A segment-based field experiment (SBFE) was conducted to collect 6,500 valid samples under five influential factors, including operating speed, seeding-unit self-weight, soil compaction, straw-coverage ratio, and surface undulation, and the multifactor interactions were analyzed using a Box–Behnken design (BBD).Based on the experimental data, a least-squares support vector machine (LSSVM) model was developed and optimized using an improved dung beetle optimizer (IDBO) to enhance prediction accuracy and convergence performance. Simulation results indicate that the proposed IDBO-LSSVM model consistently outperforms the conventional LSSVM and standard DBO-LSSVM, achieving R2 values exceeding 0.871 and RPD values ranging from 2.785 to 3.113. Building on this model, an Online Vibration Prediction (OVP) platform was developed to acquire soil-condition parameters ahead of seeding without disturbing the soil and to generate vibration forecasts in real time. Field validation demonstrates that the OVP system maintains good calibration and stable prediction performance across wide field-condition variations, even when the online optimization is limited to a maximum of 20 iterations. These results confirm the feasibility of online vibration prediction for no-till seeding units and provide technical support for improving operational stability and intelligent control of precision seeding equipment.
keywords: Seeding-unit vibration in no-till maize seeding

title: From time-series generation and model selection to transfer learning: A review and comparative analysis of pixel-wise approaches for large-scale crop mapping
abstract: Accurate and timely large-scale crop mapping is essential for crop management and food security. Over the past decade, a wide range of pixel-wise crop classification approaches have emerged for workflow elements including image preprocessing, sampling methods, feature selection, model architectures, and transfer learning strategies. To guide users in constructing robust workflows, we reviewed methods for supervised and transfer-learning-based workflow elements and propose selecting a crop-mapping workflow based on target-site sample size and domain shift from a sample-abundant source site. To comprehensively evaluate the reviewed approaches, we systematically analyzed how different time-series construction strategies, training sample sizes, variable sets, model architectures, and transfer-learning approaches affect performance for large-scale crop classification. The literature review and comparative analysis led to three key insights. First, in our multi-site experiments, generating time series with 7-day linear resampling combined with Transformer models consistently yielded the highest accuracies for both fully supervised and transfer-learning workflows, while Random Forests offered competitive accuracy with substantially faster training. Second, transfer learning increased workflow adaptability: unsupervised domain adaptation was effective for homogeneous crop classes, while fine-tuning was more robust across diverse transfer scenarios. Third, workflow selection depended strongly on the availability of labeled samples: below a certain ground-truth sample threshold, transfer-learning workflows were more viable for reliable crop mapping, whereas fully supervised workflows became preferable once sufficient labeled data were available. To support transparency and reproducibility, we provide all code, configurations, and results in an open GitHub repository: A review of pixel-wise approaches for large-scale crop mapping.

title: Real-time estimation of crop height and cutting width in rice combine harvesters using a deep learning–enhanced forward-looking vision system with dynamic camera attitude correction
abstract: Crop height and cutting width directly influence combine harvester feed rates, yet their measurement is often limited by separate sensing devices, fixed camera attitude assumptions, and small datasets, leading to high system complexity and reduced robustness. This study developed a deep learning–enhanced forward-looking vision system that employs a depth camera to capture synchronized depth and color images ahead of the combine harvester. For crop height estimation, depth and color data were fused through image alignment, color space conversion, global threshold segmentation, region-of-interest partitioning, and depth scaling. For cutting width estimation, images collected from three combine harvesters and five rice cultivars were used to train a YOLO11-SCC model enhanced with Swin Transformer, Context Aggregation, and CSP PConv Composite modules to detect harvesting boundaries. A dynamic camera attitude correction algorithm was proposed to compensate for pitch and roll variations. Validation results showed that dynamic correction reduced crop height errors by 43% in RMSE (Root Mean Square Error) and 47% in MAPE (Mean Absolute Percentage Error), and reduced cutting width errors by 24% in maximum error and 28% in MAE (Mean Absolute Error). The system achieved crop height RMSE of 0.59–1.78 cm and MAPE of 0.56–1.57%, and cutting width MAE of 2.04–4.20 cm with a maximum error of 2.19–7.61 cm. Field tests on three additional cultivars confirmed stable performance, with crop height RMSE of 1.41–1.79 cm and MAPE of 1.28–1.51%, and cutting width MAE of 2.18–2.71 cm and a maximum error of 4.23–5.32 cm. The proposed approach enables reliable, real-time capture of crop height and cutting width, providing a practical foundation for feed rate prediction and intelligent control in combine harvesting operations.

title: Nighttime apple harvesting image enhancement based on a global–local feature fusion diffusion model
abstract: Night-time harvesting is an important strategy for improving the efficiency of agricultural automation; however, image degradation under low-light conditions severely limits the perception accuracy of machine vision systems. In complex orchard environments, existing methods often suffer from detail loss and structural distortion, which makes it difficult to meet the requirements of high-precision operations. To address these limitations, this study proposes a generative diffusion model for image enhancement built on a U-Net backbone. A Transformer module is incorporated to capture global context, and a convolutional block attention module is used to strengthen features of fruit as well as branches and leaves. In addition, pyramid-based resolution sampling and a global color correction module are employed to balance detail recovery with color consistency. Experimental results show that the proposed method achieves a PSNR of 27.1144 dB and an SSIM of 0.8891 on a synthetic apple dataset. To further assess practical applicability, a comparative analysis is conducted using both a synthetic dataset and a real low-light dataset. The results indicate that the model offers measurable generalization to real scenes and provides improved detail reconstruction. After enhancement by the proposed model, the YOLOv13 detector’s mAP50–95 increases from 0.249 to 0.352. Overall, the proposed approach mitigates severe visual degradation under extreme lighting and provides technical support for all-day, high-precision automated agricultural operations.

title: Boundary-Consistent Ordinal Regression for wheat yield prediction using UAV-based multispectral time-series data
abstract: Accurate plot-scale wheat yield prediction from UAV-based multispectral time-series data is hindered by limited labeled samples, strong phenological variability, and the ordinal nature of yield evaluation in breeding programs. Conventional regression-only objectives minimize numerical error but ignore agronomically meaningful yield categories, often leading to implausible cross-class mispredictions. To address this, we propose Boundary Consistent Ordinal Regression (B-COR), a class-aware multi-task learning framework that jointly predicts continuous yield and ordinal yield classes while explicitly enforcing consistency between predicted yield magnitudes and class boundaries. The B-COR objective integrates three components: a regression loss, ordinal classification supervision, and a boundary-aware modulation term that scales regression penalties based on ordinal deviation. This formulation discourages large cross-category errors while preserving accuracy within yield classes. The framework is evaluated using multi-temporal UAV-derived multispectral data covering key wheat growth stages from booting to maturity, with synthetically generated time-series data employed to mitigate sample scarcity. Robustness and generalizability are assessed through cross-season validation, training on one growing season and testing on an independent season. Compared to a standard mean squared error objective, B-COR reduces RMSE from 1.28 to 0.81 t ha−1 and improves the coefficient of determination (R2) from 0.44 to 0.76, while ordinal classification accuracy increases from 41% to 79%. Notably, severe ordinal mispredictions where plots are assigned to non-adjacent yield categories are reduced from over 30% to approximately 1%. The proposed framework provides a robust, interpretable, and operationally aligned solution for UAV-based yield prediction in breeding trials, supporting more reliable selection and decision-making under real-world agronomic constraints.

title: CTF-TL: Coarse-to-Fine temporal localization framework for precise recognition of posture transition behaviors in periparturient sows
abstract: Monitoring posture transition behaviors in periparturient sows is critical for health and welfare assessment. However, their diffuse temporal boundaries present significant challenges for precise localization in unconstrained farm environments. To address this challenge, we propose a Coarse-to-Fine temporal localization framework (CTF-TL) that progressively refines action boundaries to improve localization accuracy. CTF-TL consists of two main stages: coarse-grained segment extraction and fine-grained boundary refinement. Specifically, the former identifies coarse candidate segments using dynamic posture entropy, which quantifies posture variability over time to highlight likely transition periods. The latter enhances boundary precision by introducing two targeted modules: a Short-Medium-Long (SML) unit to capture multi-scale temporal dependencies, and a Temporal Attention Unit (TAU) to strengthen context representation around action boundaries. These components jointly improve the temporal resolution and localization accuracy of posture transition events. Extensive results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves an average mAP of 84.45%, highlighting its effectiveness in recognizing posture transitions in periparturient sows.

title: ExoPrompt: Transformer-based greenhouse climate forecasting with structured conditioning and physics-based simulation
abstract: Accurate greenhouse climate forecasting is essential for optimizing crop yield, resource use, and climate control. Traditional physics-based simulators offer interpretability but often rely on simplified assumptions and fixed configurations, while data-driven models struggle with limited generalization due to scarce and localized sensing data. These limitations pose an obstacle to realizing intelligent and adaptive greenhouse systems. Digital twins (DTs), virtual replicas that mirror physical systems, offer a promising paradigm to overcome these constraints and enable real-time decision-making. Addressing this challenge is crucial towards enabling DTs with accurate, adaptive models operating across diverse conditions. We present a simulation-informed framework for robust greenhouse climate forecasting leveraging structured conditioning and synthetic data pretraining. Central to our approach is ExoPrompt, a lightweight conditioning mechanism that encodes environmental, structural, and crop-level attributes into prompt representations, enabling adaptation across diverse scenarios. The model is first pretrained on synthetic data generated using the GreenLight simulator, then fine-tuned on limited sensor data collected under varying lighting conditions. We evaluate our approach on synthetic and real-world datasets across multiple setups. Results show that simulation-based pretraining improves forecasting performance, yielding up to a 46.31% reduction in RRMSE for relative humidity and an 84.94% improvement in CO 2 prediction over simulator-only baselines. Conditioning on exogenous parameters further reduces RRMSE by up to 18.79% compared to vanilla models. Finally, we design a controlled simulation experiment varying a single exogenous parameter to isolate and validate the robustness of ExoPrompt under distributional shifts, achieving up to 49.20% RRMSE reduction for CO 2 on ground truth data.

title: YOLOv9s-multi: orientation-based fruit selection for robotic apple thinning
abstract: Accurate detection and orientation estimation of immature apples are crucial for effective thinning decisions in robotic apple thinning. Existing research either relies on computationally expensive RGB-D approaches with 3D geometric fitting to estimate orientation and size or requires multiple separate models for thinning decision, limiting their real-time performance on robotic platforms. To address these issues, a multi-task model, YOLOv9s-Multi, is proposed. First, this model integrates segmentation and keypoint heads to perform instance segmentation of immature apples and detect their calyx keypoint positions. Second, the detection head employs an efficient and lightweight Depthwise Convolution module (DWConv) to reduce model parameters while accurately capturing spatial features across channels. Finally, the orientation is derived from the segmentation centroid and calyx keypoint, enabling pixel-based fruit selection for thinning decision-making. This model is evaluated on a self-developed dataset that divides immature apples based on developmental stage: Flower-Retained Stage (FR-Stage) and Fruit-Visible Stage (FV-Stage). Results show that instance segmentation and keypoint AP@0.5 for FV-Stage are 89.3% and 86.4%, respectively, while for FR-Stage they are 71.6% and 79.8%. The model further achieves prediction accuracies of 92.80% (FV-Stage) and 72.59% (FR-Stage) within an acceptable error of 30 °. The pixel-based fruit selection method achieves 74.00% and 70.31% selection accuracy on the test and an additional measurement dataset, respectively. Compared with the baseline YOLOv9s-seg, the number of parameters is reduced by 11.4%. In contrast to 3D fitting methods, our approach provides lower computational complexity, faster inference speed, and higher accuracy. These results demonstrate that the proposed model can efficiently estimate the orientation of immature apples and perform fruit selection in close-range scenes and complex lighting environments, which are challenging for depth cameras to handle. The code and datasets are publicly available on GitHub: https://github.com/DIANSLEE/YOLOv9s-Multi.

title: S3WP: A novel method for online predicting weight of stacked seeds needed to grow seedlings based on binocular vision and improved YOLO11n-seg
abstract: The seeding parameters of the existing plug tray seeders could not be adjusted in real time according to the seed weight, which led to poor seeding performance, poor universality, and a low level of intelligence. For this reason, the stacked seedlings seeds weight prediction (S3WP) method was proposed in this study to address the challenges of online predicting the weight of stacked seeds needed for seedling cultivation. Firstly, the physical parameters of common vegetable and fruit seeds for seedling cultivation were measured and analyzed, and the functional relationships between the seed weight and width of different families were explored. Secondly, YOLO11n-seg was improved in terms of the attention mechanism, loss function, and upsampling to improve the accuracy of seed recognition and segmentation. Then, the seed family could be judged, and the pixel width of the seeds could be measured. Thirdly, a binocular camera was used to obtain the images and spatial depth information of the stacked seeds in the seed box of the plug tray seeder. The physical width of the seeds was obtained by combining the pixel width of the seeds with the depth information. Finally, by combining the functional relationship between the seed weight and width, a graphical user interface was developed to achieve the weight prediction of the seeds for facility seedling cultivation in the seed box of the plug tray seeder. The experimental results showed that compared with the original YOLO11n − seg, the Pbox, Rbox, mAP50box, Pmask, Rmask, and mAP50mask of the improved stacked seedlings seeds segment based on YOLO11n (S4 − YOLO11n) increased by 2.2, 3.6, 4.1, 1.9, 3.5, and 4.0 percentage points respectively. The accuracy rate of seed family judgment by the S3WP method reached 100%, and the average MRE of seed weight prediction was 6.05%. The time required for weight measurement was only 1.1% − 1.7% of that for manual measurement. This study meets the accuracy and calculation time requirements for non − contact online detection of seed weight, providing accurate seed weight data support for the adaptive adjustment of seeding parameters of intelligent plug tray seeders in industrialized seedling cultivation.

title: The estimation of tree-level key structural parameters based on ULS and BLS point clouds by evaluating prediction accuracy from tree stem analysis
abstract: Individual tree-level structural parameters are crucial for sustainable forest management and the evaluation of forest growth, as well as their ecological functions. The advanced Unmanned Aerial Vehicle-based Laser Scanning (ULS) and Backpack Laser Scanning (BLS) techniques offer a detailed three-dimensional insight into the forest structure information, have great potential for accurately estimating forest structural parameters in forest research and practices. However, tree-level key structural parameters (e.g., DBH, height and volume, etc.) extracted from ULS and BLS point clouds were usually evaluated by field measurement which has relatively low accuracy and high uncertainties especially under the complicated forest conditions. To quantify and comprehensively analyze the performance of ULS and BLS point cloud data in extracting key structural parameters of individual trees, this study conducted a multi-platform laser scanning remote sensing campaign in a typical Chinese fir plantation at Yangkou State Forest Farm, Fujian Province, along with field measurements of 16 sample Chinese fir trees. We processed the ULS and BLS point clouds and extracted structural parameters at tree-level by advanced algorithms, and then evaluated the tree height, DBH and volume by measurements from the field as well as felled trees through tree stem analysis by fitting a variety of taper models. Results demonstrated that 1) ULS outperforms ultrasonic altimeters in quantifying individual tree heights compared to felled tree height. The RMSE of tree height estimates from manually measured ULS data and automatically extracted ULS data were 0.77 m (4.00%) and 0.87 m (4.53%), respectively. 2) The accuracy of DBH estimated from BLS data was relatively high compared to field measured data, with an R2 of 0.96 (RMSE = 1.98 cm, relative RMSE (rRMSE) = 8.37%). 3) The Yamamoto-style binary volume model fitted in this study performed the best among all the models, with an R2 of 0.95 (RMSE = 0.05069 m3, rRMSE = 14.90%), followed by the binary volume model derived from the integral operation of the taper equation and the existing local generalized binary volume model. This study collected precious data by tree stem analysis through felled trees, also provided a solid quantitative demonstration of the robust capabilities of ULS in tree height estimation and BLS in DBH estimation, and their combination in estimating volume, which has rarely been done in previous studies.

title: Design of key components for a low-loss air-blowing sesame harvest header and study on material transport mechanisms based on CFD simulation
abstract: To address the high loss rates and high header residue rates in the mechanical harvesting of sesame, this study proposes a low-loss air-blowing sesame harvest header design. To minimize losses of sesame capsules and seeds during harvesting, a motion analysis and structural parameter optimization were conducted on the header’s key components. For the issue of significant material residue within the header, an air-blowing device was designed to sweep the harvester base plate with airflow, effectively reducing header residue rates. During bench experiments, the distribution of internal flow fields and variations in airflow velocity within the header are difficult to measure and visualize intuitively. Therefore, by combining computational fluid dynamics (CFD) technology with bench experiments, it was discovered that changes in airflow velocity significantly impact material residue within the header. Conduct single-factor and multi-factor trials using ground loss rate and header residue rate as experimental indicators to investigate the impact of each experimental factor and determine the optimal combination of header operating parameters. Field validation experiments demonstrate that the predicted values are generally consistent with the test results. Under optimal operating parameters, the test results yielded a 2.87% ground loss rate and a 3.66% header residue rate. This study combines header structure optimization with CFD simulation technology, effectively reducing losses and residues during mechanized sesame harvesting. It provides theoretical reference and technical support for the design and operational performance enhancement of harvesting equipment for other easily shattering grain crops.

title: UAV-based crop reconstruction and trait estimation using RGB imagery without external geospatial infrastructure
abstract: Unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) based digital plant phenotyping enables high-resolution crop monitoring. However, most existing approaches rely on industrial UAV platforms, specialized sensors such as DSLR or multispectral cameras, and external geospatial infrastructure such as Ground Control Points (GCPs) or RTK-GPS, which limits their adoption in resource-constrained settings. The objective of this work is to develop and validate a streamlined UAV phenotyping workflow that generates accurate orthomosaics and digital elevation models (DEMs) using only RGB imagery from a lightweight commercial drone. Specifically, we aim to: (1) reduce photogrammetric distortions commonly observed in DEMs produced by wide-angle cameras through a novel dual-altitude flight strategy with a simplified follow-course multi-S-shaped flight pattern; (2) enable reliable canopy height estimation via an automated RANSAC-based elevation correction; and (3) validate the utility of these products for plant-level phenotyping across multiple growth stages, including early-stage rice plant counting, mid-stage leaf discoloration detection, and late-stage panicle detection using pretrained computer vision models. Our proposed workflow achieves 94.95% accuracy in rice plant counting and 91.59% accuracy in panicle count. DEM-derived canopy height estimates show strong agreement with manual field measurements (Pearson correlation coefficient R=0.876, MAE=0.177 m, RMSE=0.203m), despite the absence of GCPs or RTK-GPS. Together, these results demonstrate that RGB-only UAV systems can support reliable relative crop phenotyping when paired with appropriate acquisition and processing strategies. To promote reproducibility and comparative evaluation, we release the UAV imagery, orthomosaics, DEMs, and annotation data associated with this study, providing a benchmark dataset for infrastructure-free phenotyping research.

title: Advancing agricultural trenching operations: A review of intelligent machinery, system integration, and development pathways
abstract: Trenching operations, as a critical component of agricultural efficiency and sustainability, encompass fundamental tasks such as seeding, drainage, and fertilization, presenting significant technical complexity. Despite rapid advancements in automation and intelligent technologies, very few commentaries have focused on the trenching operation. This study systematically addresses this gap by adhering to the PRISMA 2020 guidelines, employing bibliometric analysis to identify research trends, and conducting a systematic review of 123 publications. The study proposes an innovative three-dimensional framework—encompassing technical systems, intelligent development, and research methodology—to trace the evolution toward data-driven closed-loop systems in this domain. The study identifies core performance bottlenecks through a perception–decision–execution diagnostic lens—high resistance, low energy efficiency, and trade-offs between speed and precision—as stemming from systemic disconnects within this closed loop. It systematically reviews the technological architecture and developmental status of agricultural trenching operations and conducts a hierarchical attribution analysis of its core performance bottlenecks. This study not only analyzes current technical limitations but also provides guidance for developing next-generation adaptive trenching operations.

title: Real-time frame-level fish feeding behavior detection using a lightweight CNN-TCN architecture
abstract: Aquaculture, particularly fish farming, is a rapidly growing sector critical for global food security, where efficient feeding management is essential for economic and environmental sustainability. Real-time monitoring of fish feeding behavior can enable intelligent feeding control, thereby reducing waste and optimize growth. Here we proposed frame-level models to make real-time fish feeding behavior detection by combining a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) with a Temporal Convolutional Network (TCN) from video data. The CNN extracts spatial features from each video frame, while the TCN aggregates temporal dependencies through stacked dilated causal residual blocks, allowing reliable recognition of feeding behavior from frame sequences over time. The models were evaluated against baseline CNN models and CNN/MobileNet + GRU models using grayscale and/or optical flow frames as inputs. Results show that the gray CNN-TCN model achieved the best performance, with accuracy, precision, recall, F1 score, and ROC-AUC all exceeding 0.99, while maintaining real-time inference capability, reaching 1,029 frames per second and a mean latency of 7.77 ms and only moderate computational overhead. Moreover, the input of gray-scale frames alone is sufficient to capture fish feeding behavior, indicating that the commonly used optical flow may be a redundant input for the CNN-TCNs. To align real-time model training and inference, we proposed a three-phase feeding schema comprising the before-feeding phase (B), the immediate after-feeding phase (A), and the subsequent inference phase (S). The B-A-S schema allowed automatic sample labeling and provided a foundation for real-time and intelligent feeder control in recirculating aquaculture systems. The findings indicate that the proposed gray CNN-TCN model, combined with the B-A-S feeding schema, offers an effective and computationally efficient approach for fine-grained fish feeding behavior detection, supporting real-time model training and inference, and thereby enhancing the toolkit available for intelligent feeding control in aquaculture systems.

title: Discrete element modeling of a cultivated soil-residual film composite and simulation of spatial excavation-throwing kinematics
abstract: The accumulation of residual film in the plough layer inhibits root development and reduces crop yields. However, current recovery equipment struggles with low excavation rates and poor separation efficiency in deep soil environments. To address this, this study proposes a rotary-throwing excavation method using a novel soil-lifting blade. A soil-residual film composite model was developed using the Discrete Element Method (DEM) based on the characteristics of cotton field soil and residual film, showing a relative validation error of 5.91%. Single and multi-factor simulations were conducted to analyze the interaction mechanisms. Results show that the entry cutting angle and side-edge working length influence the forces acting on excavated particles, while rotational/forward speeds affect the particle throwing height/distance. The optimal parameters of entry cutting angle, side-edge working length, rotational speed, and forward speed are 57.1°, 65.1 mm, 151 r/min, and 1.56 m/s, respectively. Under this optimal combination, the soil excavation rate reached 92.93% with a coefficient variation of 1.36%, showing deviations of only 1.15% and 3.6%, respectively, relative to the field test results. This study demonstrated the applicability of the constructed model for analyzing residual film recovery in the plough layer and indicated that the developed device effectively excavates and throws the soil-film composite. This study provides a new solution for recovering residual film in the plough layer.

title: Kernel loss prediction and parameter optimization for seed-maize husking devices using MFBD-DEM and Bi-level BO-ISSA-BP
abstract: The seed industry is a strategic pillar of food security, and kernel damage and loss during the mechanized harvesting of seed maize severely constrain improvements in seed quality. To address the problems of insufficient modeling accuracy of maize ears, limited predictive capability of traditional optimization methods, and the high kernel detachment and damage rates observed during the husking process, this study constructs a bract–kernel–cob flexible composite model for seed maize based on the Discrete Element Method (DEM), and employs Multi-Flexible-Body Dynamics–Discrete Element Method (MFBD–DEM) coupled simulation to reproduce the husking process. On this basis, the effects of surface-pattern arrangement, rotational speed, and inter-roller gap on kernel-loss behavior are systematically analyzed. Furthermore, a bi-level optimized BP neural network model (BO-ISSA-BP), combining Bayesian Optimization (BO) and an Improved Sparrow Search Algorithm (ISSA), is proposed to achieve high-precision prediction and optimization of key kernel-loss indices. Compared with the conventional SSA-BP model, the BO-ISSA-BP model reduces RMSE, MAPE, and MAE by 7.42%, 15.37%, and 14.91%, respectively, with the coefficient of determination R2 reaching 0.975. In comparison with the BO-BP model, more substantial improvements are observed across all error metrics. Under the optimal parameter combination, the bench test yields a detached-kernel loss rate and a damaged-kernel rate of 1.613% and 0.369%, respectively; the relative errors with respect to the theoretical optimum are 8.47% and 6.65%, and those relative to the model predictions are 7.09% and 6.35%, confirming the reliability and feasibility of the proposed prediction model and optimization method under practical operating conditions. The research findings not only provide a reliable theoretical basis for parameter optimization and performance prediction of seed-maize husking devices in China, but also offer a methodological framework for flexible body modeling and multi-objective optimization in agricultural machinery design.

title: Hybrid Model Predictive Control for the regulation of carbon dioxide in plant growth chambers
abstract: Precise regulation of carbon dioxide (CO2) concentrations in plant growth chambers is critical for ensuring reproducible and physiologically relevant research outcomes. CO2 assimilation varies significantly with plant genotype, growth conditions, crop density, and phenological stage. However, control approaches heavily dependent on mechanistic crop models are at odds with the objectives of plant characterization units (PCU), where model availability for specific crops may be lacking. Moreover, in Bioregenerative Life Support Systems (BLSSs), such methods may struggle with multiple crops, intercropping, staggered harvesting and unknown growth stages.We present a hybrid Model Predictive Control (MPC) strategy for CO2 regulation, based on real-time estimates of photosynthetic and respiration rate. The controller operates independently of crop-specific assumptions, offering enhanced robustness against the dynamic conditions of BLSSs and effectively accommodating crops for which no mechanistic model is available. Moreover, the real-time estimate of plants’ gas exchanges can be leveraged by diagnostic algorithms or other control loops. To ensure reliable mass balances, we also address key practical challenges such as delay in CO2 measurements, and disjoint operating range of injection valves. We demonstrate the effectiveness of the approach on in vivo experiments in a PCU realized under the ESA-MELiSSA framework.

title: Key growth stage estimation of rice based on two-layer parameter optimization of remote sensing and growth model
abstract: Accurate monitoring of key growth stages in rice is crucial for precision fertilization and irrigation scheduling, as well as timely harvesting. Remote sensing products often suffer from reduced accuracy when estimating crop phenology. Process-based models perform well at field scale, yet their large-scale deployment is hindered by scarce parameter data and limited real-time forcing. This study integrates remote sensing-estimated growth stage data into a crop model, using the first layer of the two-layer parameter optimization to generate estimates for the entire growth period. Subsequently, the growth stage results estimated based on multiple remote sensing vegetation indices are combined with those generated by the first-layer optimization strategy, and the second layer of the two-layer parameter optimization strategy is applied to further improve the prediction accuracy. The results show that the average RMSE for estimating rice growth stages using remote sensing vegetation indices is 9.2 days. The single-layer parameter optimization strategy fills in the key growth stages that remote sensing methods cannot accurately estimate, resulting in an average RMSE of 9.3 days. The two-layer parameter optimization strategy proposed in this study reduces the average RMSE to 5.3 days, significantly improving the accuracy of full-growth period estimation for rice. Cross-year and multi-variety tests confirmed the method’s high robustness, showing an average RMSE reduction of 4.8 days over the single-layer method and demonstrating outstanding performance in early growth stage estimation. Regional-scale results show that the proposed method accurately captures spatial variations caused by climate and management differences, with minimal simulation errors. It demonstrates good performance in improving the accuracy and stability of rice growth stage estimation, providing a novel technical approach for crop growth stage monitoring.

title: Spatiotemporal pattern of wheat harvest duration and its driving factors in the Huang-Huai-Hai plain of China
abstract: Agricultural production is highly time-sensitive, and obtaining accurate time windows for mechanical harvesting is the key guidance information for cross-regional operations. Understanding the optimal harvest period for wheat on a large spatial scale and providing quantitative decision-making support for machinery scheduling and allocation are of great significance for improving the efficiency of agricultural machinery operations and ensuring wheat yield and quality. However, knowledge of how cropping pattern and weather impact wheat harvesting at large spatial scales remains unclear. This study developed a framework to analyze the spatiotemporal pattern of wheat harvest duration in the Huang-Huai-Hai Plain (HHHP) of China from 2022 to 2024 based on a unique large-scale agricultural machinery operation dataset. The results indicated that more than 98.5% of the towns in the HHHP had a wheat harvest duration within two weeks. We also developed four models for wheat harvest duration estimation and found that the Long-Short Term Memory-Artificial Neural Network (LSTM-ANN) model provided the highest accuracy (RMSE = 1.82 days). The Shapley Additive Explanation (SHAP) analysis revealed that the double cropping ratio was the most major driving factor of the wheat harvest duration in the HHHP. The results also indicated that the local and trans-regional harvesters contributed nearly equally to the wheat harvest in the HHHP from 2022 to 2024. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first study that systematically analyzes the wheat harvesting pattern at large spatial scales by integrating the harvesting trajectory data, cropping pattern data, remote sensing, and weather data. The quantitative analysis of harvesting patterns could provide guidance information for cross-regional operations of agricultural machinery in China.

title: A novel UAV-based fusion of spectral and textural features with canopy stratification for accurate estimation of vertical nitrogen distribution in cotton
abstract: Accurate monitoring of plant nitrogen accumulation (PNA) is crucial for precision management in cotton, a crop with a complex, multi-layered canopy. Existing unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) remote sensing approaches, predominantly reliant on top-of-canopy spectral vegetation indices (VIs) like NDVI, suffer from signal saturation and fail to capture the vertical heterogeneity of nitrogen within the canopy. To better characterize these limitations, this study developed and rigorously validated an innovative framework that synergistically integrates multi-source UAV features with a vertical canopy stratification strategy. We conducted a comprehensive water-nitrogen coupling field experiment and extracted key spectral indices (e.g., NDRE, GNDVI) and textural features (e.g., Entropy, Contrast). Three machine learning models were evaluated under stratified and whole-plant scenarios. The results demonstrate that the fusion of VIs and textural features within a stratified framework leads to distinct estimation performance across different canopy layers. The Random Forest Regression model applied to the upper canopy layer achieved the highest performance (R 2 = 0.833, RMSE = 1.463 g m⁻ 2 ), compared with an R 2 of 0.494 obtained from the conventional whole-plant approach. Furthermore, the stratification strategy enabled a quantitative characterization of dynamic nitrogen distribution patterns within the cotton canopy, with relatively uniform allocation at the budding stage and pronounced concentration in the photosynthetically active middle and upper layers during the boll-setting stage (e.g., middle-layer PNA reaching 121.84 kg ha⁻ 1 ). This study provides a three-dimensional perspective on canopy nitrogen distribution that helps link UAV-based observations with physiologically meaningful processes and offers a potential pathway for informing precision nitrogen management in cotton and other crops with complex canopy architectures.

title: A method for 3D reconstruction of trees via SfM guidance and depth estimation
abstract: 3D tree models are essential for accurately capturing tree morphological structures. However, image-based 3D tree reconstruction often suffers from a cascading failure problem in which degraded image quality leads to unreliable feature matching, which in turn compromises camera pose estimation in structure-from-motion (SfM), ultimately resulting in drifted or distorted tree point clouds during multi-view stereo (MVS) reconstruction. To address these issues, a method for 3D reconstruction of trees via SfM guidance and depth estimation is proposed. First, to mitigate the influence of dynamic objects and weak-texture backgrounds, the YOLO-SegNet model is employed to segment raw images. Second, a detector-free matching model termed DAT-LoFTR is proposed to improve the matching robustness for trees with repetitive textures and self-similar structures. This model is integrated into an SfM framework (DAT-LoFTR-SfM) for reliable camera pose estimation. Subsequently, image sequences and estimated camera poses are input into the CCFM-MVSFormer++ model to predict multi-view depth maps, which are fused to generate the final 3D tree models. The experimental results demonstrate that, compared with the ORB + NN, SIFT + NN, SP + SG and LoFTR models, the proposed DAT-LoFTR significantly improves the average feature matching accuracy on tree image pairs. In contrast to the LoFTR-SfM, the DAT-LoFTR-SfM method achieves enhanced performance on the tree dataset, with the average relative pose AUC (Area Under Curve) values increasing by 3.34, 4.31, 4.75, and 5.31 percentage points at the 3°, 5°, 10°, and 20° thresholds, respectively. Finally, compared with mainstream 3D reconstruction methods (e.g., UniMVSNet, TransMVSNet, and MVSFormer++), the proposed method achieves superior accuracy in both depth map estimation and 3D tree point cloud reconstruction.

title: MushroomSegDepth: A multitask model for segmentation and depth prediction of oyster mushrooms to support growth management
abstract: Reliable monitoring of mushroom growth is essential for determining harvest time, ensuring product quality, and improving yield management in commercial production. Recent developments explored monitoring growth using depth sensors directly, aiming to capture three-dimensional features such as cap volume, curvature, and structural changes that are important for predicting maturity. However, existing depth-sensing systems were often impractical for mushroom farms due to humidity sensitivity, artefacts, and deployment constraints. Other work also investigated estimating depth from 2D images, but general-purpose monocular depth models typically struggled in close-range agricultural environments and could not capture the fine-scale geometry required for reliable growth monitoring. To address these limitations, we proposed MushroomSegDepth, a multitask model that performed segmentation and depth estimation together using only RGB input, with depth predicted specifically within the mushroom regions. The model combined a ConvNeXt-based encoder, a feature pyramid structure, a pyramid-fusion module, and lightweight segmentation and depth heads. A dataset of 705 RGB-depth pairs collected from three viewpoints in a farm environment was used for training and evaluation. MushroomSegDepth achieved high segmentation accuracy (Intersection over Union = 0.935) and low depth error (Root Mean Square Error = 26.1 mm), outperforming several state-of-the-art monocular depth estimation models, including DepthAnything v2, DepthPro, and Marigold. Temporal depth changes computed from predicted masks closely matched ground-truth depth trends, enabling meaningful monitoring across the growth cycle. Overall, MushroomSegDepth provided a practical, task-specific solution for extracting depth information from standard RGB imagery, supporting more accurate growth monitoring and offering potential value for harvest-timing decisions and future automation in mushroom production.

title: PigInstance: An efficient Pig Instance segmentation framework for intelligent pig farming
abstract: Instance segmentation is a fundamental task in Precision Livestock Farming (PLF). It provides essential pixel-level information for advanced applications like automated weight estimation, individual tracking and behavior analysis. While significant progress has been made, deploying robust instance segmentation systems in real-world pig farms remains challenging. Supervised models such as Mask R-CNN require extensive manual annotation and struggle to generalize across diverse farm environments. In contrast, foundation models offer remarkable zero-shot capabilities but require computationally intensive fine-tuning. To bridge these barriers, we propose PigInstance, a novel framework for training-efficient adaptation of foundation models. Our main objective is to achieve robust instance segmentation under the challenging conditions of pig-to-pig overlap and facility occlusion, providing a deployment-oriented alternative to full fine-tuning. The proposed PigInstance framework utilizes a frozen foundation model backbone to extract robust image features, which are then refined by a lightweight adapter. Subsequently, a Probability-Guided Post-Processing (PG-PP) step is introduced to resolve inter-instance pixel conflicts. We demonstrate our framework’s effectiveness using Segment Anything Model (SAM) as the foundational backbone. Following a comparative analysis of its variants, we established SAM-B as the optimal foundation due to its balance of performance and efficiency. Building on this, our PigInstance framework achieves state-of-the-art results, reaching a mean IoU of 93.50% and a Dice score of 96.35%. The performance of our proposed PigInstance significantly surpasses the performance of the much larger SAM-H model (mIoU: 92.26%, Dice: 95.89%) and represents a substantial gain of +3.57% mIoU and +1.82% Dice over its SAM-B foundation. The framework’s superiority is most pronounced on our defined hard samples subset, where it boosts mIoU to 73.92%, far exceeding SAM-H’s 66.70%. Critically, PigInstance completely eliminates mask conflicts, reducing our proposed Structurally Significant Overlap Ratio (SSOR) to zero from SAM-H’s 0.46%. To foster further research, we introduce and release a high-quality, multi-source dataset for pig instance segmentation, available at https://github.com/linwjscau/PigInstance_Efficient-Pig-Instance-Segmentation-Framework-For-Pig-Farming.

title: Grapevine branch-bud detection with cross-regional dynamic tracking and counting for automated bud thinning
abstract: Grapevine bud thinning is a critical cultivation practice for enhancing grape yield and quality. However, traditional manual bud thinning approaches are inefficient, costly, and inconsistent, making them unsuitable for large-scale orchard production. Thus, the development of intelligent bud thinning robots is urgently required. However, achieving high-precision recognition, accurate localization, and dynamic counting of grapevine branches and buds in complex field environments still presents major challenges. To address this challenge, this study proposed a Feature-Aware and Structure-Enhanced Network for Grapevine Branch-Bud Detection (FASE-GBBD), integrated with a multi-object tracking algorithm and a three-region counting strategy to achieve precise branch-bud recognition, stable tracking, and dynamic counting across regions. Specifically, a Multi-Kernel Guided and Sequential Collaboration Network (MGSCN) was designed, in which the Adaptive Multi-Scale LoG (AMS-LoG) module fused multi-scale edge and structural semantic information to enhance the representation of branch and bud edges and structural details, while the Dynamic Feature Aggregation Module (DFAM) further improved the discrimination between targets and background, strengthening the discriminative power and attention focus of feature representation. Subsequently, a Focusing-Attention Hierarchical Diffusion Pyramid Network (FAHDPN) was constructed, employing a two-stage multi-scale diffusion mechanism to effectively improve the detection accuracy and semantic consistency of small bud targets. Finally, we achieved continuous cross-regional tracking and stable counting of branches and buds by integrating the ByteTrack tracking algorithm with a three-region counting mechanism. Compared with the baseline model, FASE-GBBD achieves an AP50 of 88.20% (+3.30%) and an AP50:95 of 60.10% (+4.40%). The APsmall is improved to 63.40% (+8.60%), while APmedium and APlarge reach 64.50% (+2.90%) and 69.90% (+7.70%), respectively, with an inference speed of 73.25 FPS. In tracking and counting tasks, the counting accuracy (Acc) reaches 90.67%. These results indicate that the proposed method not only enhances the detection accuracy and small-object recognition of grapevine branches and buds but also achieves stable counting across consecutive frames, providing reliable perception and decision-making support for automated bud thinning and exhibiting high application value and potential for broader adoption.

title: Quadratic optimization-based path planning for autonomous agricultural vehicles headland turning in orchard environments
abstract: Automated headland turning is a critical field operation for autonomous agricultural vehicles in agricultural production. Although traditional model-based and graph search-based path planning methods work well in arable farming, they struggle to generate a smooth, and collision free turning trajectory in complex and dynamically changing orchard headlands in real-time. To address this challenge, this paper proposed a quadratic optimization-based path planning approach for headland turning of four-wheeled agricultural vehicles in orchards. Firstly, when the vehicle arrives at the headland, an initial reference path is generated using an improved Reeds Shepp curve based on the vehicle’s position and heading angle, and the span width between initial and terminal points. Secondly, projection discretization, point sampling, and real-time dynamic planning are performed to obtain a preliminary obstacle-free path. Finally, a quadratic programming solver is designed that uses the constructed convex space to obtain the final path. Simulations and field experiments (in a digital peach orchard) were conducted to evaluate the performance of the proposed method by comparing it with an improved artificial potential field (APF) method in various types of headlands. Simulation and experimental results show that, when obstacles are present at the initial, middle, and terminal sections of the headland, the path generated by APF results in collisions. However, the proposed method generates smooth, collision-free paths, implying that the proposed method demonstrates a higher success rate in path planning. In addition, compared with APF method, the proposed method achieved a 6.69% reduction in path length, a 5.87% decrease in the time duration, and a 35.29% decrease in path curvature in field experiments. In conclusion, the proposed method can plan smooth, collision-free headland paths, significantly improving the operation safety and efficiency of unmanned agricultural unmanned vehicles during headland turns.

title: Recognition and temperature effect analysis of cucumber gray mold spore germination based on dual lightweight YOLOv8s
abstract: Gray mold, as a fungal disease, significantly affects both the yield and quality of cucumbers, and its spore germination is influenced by temperature. Thus, understanding spore germination conditions is essential for early disease warning and control. In this study, a dual lightweight YOLOv8s model for spore germination recognition was proposed to reveal the temperature-dependent germination patterns of gray mold spores. Specifically, the model’s first lightweighting was conducted by integrating C2F_EMBC, BiFPN, and EfficientRepHead into YOLOv8s. While maintaining high detection accuracy, this lightweight model achieved reductions of 35.14% in parameters, 22.38% in GFLOPs, and 34.67% in Model Size. Subsequently, redundant parameters were further removed from the lightweight model through the LAMP pruning technique, contributing to additional reductions in parameters, GFLOPs, and Model Size by 62.22%, 34.68%, and 61.22%, respectively. This brought about the values of 2.72 MB for parameters, 14.5G for GFLOPs, and 5.7 MB for Model Size. Furthermore, mAP@.5 and FPS were improved by 0.52% and 46.78%, reaching 96.8% and 809.8, respectively. These results underscore that the dual lightweighting approach enhanced detection accuracy and ensured the efficiency and practicality of the model in resource-constrained environments. Finally, the temperature response of gray mold spores was explored by the dual lightweight model. The results suggest that spore germination demonstrated a degree of flexibility and adaptability within the temperature range of 10℃ to 35℃. The germination rate generally exhibited an increasing trend over time, confirming the considerable influence of the time–temperature interaction on spore germination. The R2 values of spore germination kinetics models calculated based on temperature all exceeded 90%, allowing for effective prediction of spore germination rates across different temperatures. To sum up, the proposed dual lightweight YOLOv8s model was employed in this study to uncover the temperature-dependent germination patterns of gray mold spores, and a temperature-based spore germination kinetic model was developed. The findings lay a foundation for early disease prediction and management.

title: Performance assessment of no-fee GNSS augmentation systems for tractor guidance
abstract: • Unaugmented GNSS gives 2–3 m guidance errors, reduced below 1 m for pass-to-pass < 15 min. • EGNOS reduces guidance errors by ∼40% compared with unaugmented GNSS. • GLIDE reduces guidance errors below 20 cm for pass-to-pass intervals < 15 min. • VRS-NRTK slightly outperforms RTK with similar baseline lengths. • RTK guidance errors begin at 1 cm for on-site RTK and grow with baseline length. This study assesses the performance of no-fee GNSS augmentation systems for tractor guidance. Five no-fee augmentation systems: EGNOS, GLIDE, RTK, VRS-NRTK, and on-site RTK were evaluated in both static and guidance tests over short- and long‑term periods using three GNSS receiver types: low-cost Navilock NL8022MP, mid-range Novatel Smart2, and high-end Harxon TS108PRO. Static tests recorded 24 h of position data from 14 receiver-augmentation configurations on a fixed surface. Guidance tests recorded trajectory data from the 14 configurations during straight-line guidance using a tractor equipped with two GNSS receivers, one under test and one high-precision reference. Results found that: (i) unaugmented GNSS resulted in guidance errors of 2–3 m, reduced below 1 m in pass-to-pass intervals shorter than 15 min; (ii) EGNOS reduced these guidance errors by ∼41%; (iii) GLIDE reduced guidance errors to below 20 cm for pass-to-pass intervals shorter than 15 min, with no long-term improvement; (iv) RTK guidance error decreased as baseline length shortened: >100 km yielded > 17 cm, 20–100 km yielded 3–20 cm, and < 20 km yielded 2–3 cm; (v) VRS-NRTK slightly outperformed RTK with similar baseline lengths; and (vi) on-site RTK enabled 1 cm guidance error. In summary: low-cost receivers without augmentation or with EGNOS result in metre-level errors; mid-range receivers with GLIDE deliver decimetre-level guidance errors in the short term; and high-end receivers using on-site RTK or VRS-NRTK on baselines up to 100 km achieve centimetre-level errors, enabling farmers to replicate tractor trajectories consistently year to year.

title: Toward multi-class detection and localization of contamination in cotton fields: Comparing EfficientDet, Faster R-CNN ResNet50, SSD MobileNet V2, and YOLOv11
abstract: The economic value of a bale of ginned cotton decreases significantly if it contains plastic. One potential source of plastic is trash found in cotton fields. Detecting and removing plastic contaminating the fields will reduce the chance of plastic in the bale. Removal at the field is advantageous because harvest and postharvest machinery tend to break the materials into smaller pieces which are harder to remove. This paper compares multiple object detection architectures trained to find bags, bottles & cans, and general trash in a cotton field. Training and validation used a set of 15,200 images representing the 2021 and 2023 cotton crop in the Mississippi Delta with 80% of the images used for the training. Testing used 2526 images from the 2022 cotton crop. The best model checked on the validation set had a mean average precision of 0.91 and the best mean average recall was 0.75. Generalization to the 2022 crop test set did not perform as well with the best mean average precision falling to 0.83 and best mean recall falling to 0.57. This paper provides relevant information for reducing contaminants in cotton, minimizing the associated economic losses, and maintaining the United States cotton industry’s reputation.

title: Rigid-flexible coupling errors calibration based on machine learning for robotic harvesting arm in orchard
abstract: Apple harvesting robots provide a solution for the mechanized picking of fresh fruits, in which the dedicated apple picking robotic arms are the core components. However, various errors reduce the positioning accuracy and dynamic performance of the apple picking robotic arm, such as system errors from manufacturing tolerances and assembly errors, compliance errors caused by self-weight and load structures, and nonstructural errors caused by gear backlash. This paper introduces a novel method to improve the positioning accuracy of long-stroke picking robotic arm. A rigid-flexible coupling pose error model was established that integrates system error, self-weight and load compliance errors. Meanwhile, redundant parameters were eliminated to optimize the model through parameter error classification and analysis of the parameter error ratio. Moreover, a hybrid calibration method was proposed, combining iterative least squares method for parameter identification with a residual network for nonstructural error estimation. The identified errors were then compensated for using the error compensation method based on inverse kinematics. Simulation experiments demonstrated that the identification accuracy of the removing redundant parameters model was 93.478%. Compared with other traditional methods, the proposed method achieved the highest error estimation accuracy and the minimal calibration error. Physical experiment showed that the positioning error of the picking robotic arm decreased after calibration. The average position error and root mean square error of the picking robotic arm compensated by the proposed method were 0.278 and 0.202 mm, respectively, and the average orientation error and root mean square error were 0.230° and 0.178°, respectively. Compared to before calibration, the average position error and root mean square error decreased by 95.221% and 95.182%, respectively, and the average orientation error and root mean square error decreased by 94.080% and 93.541%, respectively. This work provides a methodological reference for error calibration in fruit picking robotic arms.

title: ToxiPlantNet: A UAV-based deep learning framework for toxic plant detection and quantitative analysis of spatiotemporal dynamics in grasslands
abstract: The rapid proliferation of toxic plants in natural grasslands suppresses forage growth, reduces ecosystem productivity, and destabilizes grassland functions. Effective management requires not only precise species identification but also a quantitative understanding of their fine-scale spatio-temporal dynamics. In this study, ToxiPlantNet is proposed as a pioneering UAV-based spatial analysis framework designed to facilitate a paradigm shift from basic individual-level detection to comprehensive ecological dynamic modeling. Using Euphorbia fischeriana as a representative species, the framework integrates high-precision deep learning with quantitative spatial indicators to characterize the fine-scale spatio-temporal evolution of toxic plant populations. TOXI-YOLO, an enhanced one-stage detector, serves as the core of the framework and incorporates a GhostDyna-RevCol (GD-RevCol) backbone, a ToxiFusion-Pyramid (TFP) neck, and a Dynamic Sparse Head (DS-Head) to strengthen multi-scale representation and contextual perception under heterogeneous grassland backgrounds. This architecture features a highly lightweight design (1.4 M parameters and 4.8 GFLOPs), providing a vital operational advantage for real-time deployment on edge devices during field monitoring. On the held-out test set, TOXI-YOLO achieves high-precision single-plant localization, with 89.3% precision, 85.2% recall, 91.1% mAP@0.5, and a mean geolocation error of 0.23 m. Based on the georeferenced detection results, key spatial indicators are introduced: the Spatial Aggregation Index (SAI) to quantify local clustering intensity, and the Detectable Density Change (DDC) to characterize spatio-temporal shifts between successive acquisitions. The application of these indicators identifies density hotspots and reveals the dynamic evolution of E. fischeriana populations. By coupling lightweight, high-precision detection with interpretable spatial metrics, ToxiPlantNet provides a robust and scalable framework for the dynamic assessment and sustainable agricultural and pastoral management of toxic plants in natural grassland ecosystems.

title: CFD numerical setting combinations for greenhouse natural ventilation across diurnal time points using multi-criteria analysis
