The study aims to distinguish various weed species to enable the precise application of herbicides on potato crops. To ensure a real-world representation, a diverse dataset was collected from the real potato fields, covering various climatic conditions, irrigation methods, and timestamps. This data was utilized for training YOLOv8, YOLOv9, and YOLOv12 detection models, resulting in detection accuracies of 90%, 92%, and 93% respectively. The results indicate that the YOLOv12 model obtained higher detection accuracy while localizing the weed instances accurately. Additionally, the average processing speed of 35 frames per second and 320 ms lag time between image acquisition and activation demonstrate the efficacy of the adopted YOLOv12 model. Following the result analysis, the high detection model (YOLOv12) is integrated with the spot-specific sprayer system for real-time detection of weeds in potato fields. The system accurately identified the weeds in the potato field and triggered the nozzles accordingly. The microcontroller is responsible for controlling this system to ensure the precise application of weedicide. The results indicate that the developed spot-specific sprayer system not only achieves a nearly 40% reduction in herbicide usage, leading to cost savings, but also reduces the environmental impact.

title: Editorial Board
LB-MPC drum-speed control strategy for a pepper harvester with feed-rate feedforward and torque-observation-based correction
abstract: • An LB-MPC method was developed for drum speed regulation under variable feeding conditions. • Vision-based feedrate feedforward and torque-observed BLM correction were jointly integrated. • GPR-based residual learning and chance constraints were introduced to improve torque safety. • The proposed method achieved real-time implementation in simulation and control experiments. • Its effectiveness was validated by 180 bench tests and field trials with near-zero torque exceedance. To mitigate drum-speed excursions and overload/impact risk caused by feed-rate fluctuations under strongly time-varying and stochastic fruit load, a learning-based Model Predictive Control is proposed with dual objectives of banded speed stability and torque safety. Firstly, vision-based short-horizon feed-rate prediction is converted into a drum-side equivalent-load prior and injected into nominal Model Predictive Control as a feedforward term, enabling earlier power matching and mitigating speed oscillations caused by incoming-flow uncertainty. Secondly, measured drive torque is treated as an online observation of equivalent load, and a Bayesian Linear Model is used to recursively learn the correction mapping between the vision prior and torque observation while providing uncertainty quantification. Finally, Gaussian Process Regression is adopted to learn the residual of nominal torque prediction online, where the residual mean corrects torque forecasts and the residual variance tightens chance constraints to suppress torque excursions at a prescribed confidence level. Comparative simulations against nominal Model Predictive Control and robust Model Predictive Control show that learning-based Model Predictive Control reduces speed RMSE by 66.1%, markedly decreases constraint violations, and completes online optimization within 18.4 ms. Bench tests with 180 repeated runs on real pepper plants and a physical drivetrain further demonstrate a 51.8% reduction in speed RMSE, a 67.1% shorter settling time after step disturbances, and zero torque violations. Field trials confirm deployability under practical operating conditions: at travel speeds of 0.6–0.8 m/s, band compliance remains around 96% and torque exceedance events are nearly eliminated. Results indicate that learning-based Model Predictive Control delivers reliable banded speed regulation and torque-safe operation under strong feeding variability and model uncertainty, offering a practical control route for safety-constrained intelligent agricultural machinery.

title: Mitigating data scarcity with AE-GAN: A novel approach to predicting pepper nitrogen use efficiency via multispectral data fusion
abstract: Efficient nitrogen utilization is essential for achieving high vegetable yields and supporting sustainable agricultural development. This study proposes an integrated framework for predicting nitrogen use efficiency (NUE) in pepper that addresses the key limitations of current monitoring approaches, including the reliance on single data sources, small sample sizes, and the “black–box” nature of predictive models. Therefore, hyperspectral and fluorescence hyperspectral datasets were combined to enable a multimodal analysis. Correlation and factor analyses were used to construct a comprehensive Nitrogen Content Utilization Index (NCUI) that integrates multiple agronomic indicators and provides a quantitative evaluation of nitrogen utilization efficiency. An AE-GAN model was employed for dataset augmentation, and competitive adaptive reweighted sampling (CARS) and iteratively retaining informative variables (IRIV) algorithms were applied to select sensitive spectral bands. Based on the preprocessed data, NCUI prediction models were developed using the CNN, CNN-LSTM, CNN-BiLSTM, and CNN-GRU architectures. The results showed that the AE-GAN effectively alleviated data scarcity, whereas the IRIV-CNN-GRU model achieved the best predictive performance, with a test set coefficient of determination (RP2) of 0.91. The selected spectral regions were closely associated with nitrogen-related physiological traits. Model interpretability analysis using LIME revealed that the red-edge region, chlorophyll absorption peaks, and key fluorescence bands made major contributions to NCUI prediction. This framework provides a reliable approach for estimating nitrogen-use efficiency in pepper and offers a novel technical strategy for precision nitrogen management in crop production.

title: Pose estimation-guided CNN for tea bud detection and plucking point identification
abstract: Accurate detection of tea buds and precise identification of plucking points are the essential prerequisites for intelligent tea-plucking robots. However, this task is challenging as the color of the targets exhibit color similarity with the background, and their shape, size, and morphology do not always coincide. Additionally, the tea buds are densely distributed and might undergo mutual occlusion within a visual horizon. In this paper, we draw inspiration from the analogy between plucking points and human keypoints and propose a framework, named PENet, that reformulates the plucking point localization task as a pose estimation problem. PENet splits the localization of the plucking points into two stages: tea bud detection and plucking point identification. In the first stage, we enhance a DINO-based detector by integrating spectrum attention module and multi-scale feature fusion, enhancing sensitivity to subtle color/texture contrasts. In the second stage, a modified High-Resolution Network with spatial coordinate encoding and bottlenecks transformer is used to accurately localize plucking points, even under occlusion or clustering. Owing to these two sequential stages, PENet can leverage the strengths of each stage to enhance flexibility on tea bud detection and plucking point identification in natural tea plantation environment. Through extensive experiments, PENet achieves competitive performance, with a mAP of 77.9% for tea bud detection and 86.2% for plucking point identification, outperforming several recent approaches under the same evaluation setting. These results demonstrate that PENet is a robust framework for intelligent tea harvesting—achieving high detection accuracy and plucking precision while reducing labor dependency and boosting operational efficiency in large-scale plantations.

title: A shapley additive exPlanations-informed, threshold-based environmental variable optimization strategy for enhancing soil organic carbon content
abstract: Machine learning combined with the Shapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) algorithm can identify the local influencing factors of soil organic carbon (SOC) in farmlands, facilitating the enhancement of SOC content through agricultural measures and soil environment optimization strategies. However, current studies offer only qualitative recommendations, such as improving irrigation and agricultural patterns, without providing schemes for quantitatively optimizing environmental variables and estimating SOC improvement after optimization. To address this gap, this study proposes a novel SHAP-informed, threshold-based environmental variable optimization strategy for augmenting SOC content. Initially, machine learning models incorporating SHAP were used to investigate the global and local control factors of SOC. SHAP dependency plots were subsequently utilized to determine the baseline and optimal thresholds for each environmental variable. These thresholds served as the target values for optimization. Finally, the spatial maps of the optimized results for each covariate were presented, along with the estimates of the SOC improvement. Wangkui County, which is a typical agricultural area in China, was selected as the study site. Among the six evaluated predicted models, Light Gradient Boosting Machine exhibited superior performance, achieving a predicted fitted R2 of 0.983, root mean square error of 0.150, and Lin’s concordance correlation coefficient of 0.991. SHAP analysis identified total nitrogen, total phosphorus, microbial diversity, total potassium, and pH as the main influencing factors of SOC, but their relative importance varied considerably across different subregions. SHAP dependency plots illustrated the nonlinear relationship of SOC with these five factors, enabling the identification of baseline points (168 mg/kg, 43 mg/kg, 108.3, 202.5 mg/kg, and 7.2) and optimal thresholds (192 mg/kg, 46 mg/kg, 107.6, 194 mg/kg, and 6.6 mg/kg). When all independent variables reached their respective baseline or optimal thresholds, the average SOC across the study area was projected to increase by 4.5% or 17.4%, respectively. This threshold-based approach offers a novel framework for quantitatively optimizing environmental variables and estimating SOC improvement outcomes.

title: Development of a decision-making algorithm to identify picking strategies for robotic mushroom harvesting
abstract: Button mushrooms (Agaricus bisporus) are harvested manually around the world to preserve high quality for the fresh market due to their sensitive skin. The United States mushroom industry, as one of the massive global mushroom producers, has confronted high production costs and labor shortages due to labor-intensive mushroom harvesting. The need for alternative solutions, such as robotic harvesting that imitates common manual picking strategies, specifically bending, twisting, and lifting, is becoming more and more important for the industry. This research seeks the development of a decision-making strategy to pick mushrooms with an effective picking sequence and bending orientation. The YOLOv5s model was utilized to detect and locate mushrooms. The maturity of the mushrooms and their clusters was identified using a pixel-based threshold. Bending distance was determined through geometric analysis, and spatial clustering was performed with the DBSCAN method. The spatial arrangements of the mushrooms were uncovered, a picking sequence was assigned, their bending directions were determined, and a human picking test was conducted to validate the approach. The results demonstrated a mean average precision (mAP) of 97% for the YOLOv5s model, R2 of 97% for maturity detection (pixel count vs. distance), bending distance defined by a product of a bending coefficient (k) of 0.21 ± 0.09 and the cap diameter of the targeted mushroom, and a weighted silhouette coefficient of 0.28 ± 0.13 for clustering performance. The developed picking strategy successfully identified spatial arrangements of the targeted mushrooms under various clustering conditions. All mushrooms detected during the model evaluation were successfully provided with the correct picking sequence and bending orientation (100%). These findings suggest that the proposed picking strategy can be employed to automate robotic harvesting systems in the future.

title: A novel benchmark for rice lodging assessment with X-band UAV-PolSAR and 3D-RLMamba
abstract: Typhoon-induced lodging disaster seriously affects the rice quality and yield. Timely acquisition of lodging information plays a pivotal role in the post-disaster management and agricultural insurance claims. Spaceborne optical and synthetic aperture radar (SAR) remote sensing is constrained by limited spatiotemporal resolution, which prevents the precise depiction of regional rice lodging heterogeneity. UAV optical remote sensing excels at characterizing the physiological changes of lodged rice rather than capturing direct structural transformations. However, its efficacy remains constrained by a high sensitivity to meteorological and lighting conditions. To circumvent these limitations, this work proposes a novel framework that integrates cutting-edge UAV-based Polarimetric SAR (UAV-PolSAR) with a state-of-the-art (SOTA) 3D Rice Lodging Mamba (3D-RLMamba) architecture for rice lodging assessment. This comprehensive framework establishes a benchmark for the intelligent inversion of key lodging parameters by detailing every stage from data acquisition and feature construction to algorithm development and parameter calculation. Initially, a full-polarization X-band UAV-PolSAR was deployed to acquire structure-sensitive radar imagery of rice fields in the aftermath of a super typhoon. A stacked feature cube was subsequently constructed, encompassing polarimetric backscatter coefficients, radar vegetation indices, and Pauli polarimetric decomposition features. To effectively capture local details and global dependencies embedded in complex spatial-polarimetric SAR features, 3D-RLMamba was designed as a novel patch-wise image classification algorithm. This new architecture facilitates cross-dimensional interaction and fusion of lodging-related information by combining the Mamba model with a multi-group strategy. A comprehensive performance comparison was conducted between 3D-RLMamba and numerous mainstream SOTA baselines, including classification models based on machine learning, CNN, Transformer, and Mamba architectures. The results indicate that 3D-RLMamba achieves the best performance, reaching an Overall Accuracy (OA) of 93.78%. Specifically, the classification accuracy for lodged rice reaches 87.87% even within natural backgrounds containing complex landcovers. These impressive classification performances lay a solid foundation for accurately mapping the spatial distribution of lodged regions and extracting their specific area and proportion. Overall, this study underscores the unique capability of advanced UAV-PolSAR in capturing the morphological features of lodged rice. Furthermore, it affirms the advantages of the 3D-RLMamba for global–local context modeling and spatial-polarimetric feature interaction. Consequently, the integration of SOTA deep learning and UAV-PolSAR technologies within this benchmark establishes a transformative paradigm for agricultural remote sensing.

title: A GDD-constrained allometric framework for UAV-based estimation of winter wheat aboveground biomass
abstract: Accurate estimation of winter wheat aboveground biomass (AGB) is essential for understanding crop growth processes and supporting agronomic management. However, remote sensing-based approaches are often constrained by spectral saturation and strong phenological dependency. This study developed a growing degree day (GDD)-constrained allometric framework that integrates UAV-derived vegetation indices (VIs), thermal time, and organ-level growth relationships to improve AGB estimation across growth stages. Multi-year field experiments (2022–2025) conducted under controlled irrigation conditions were used to characterise organ-specific biomass dynamics along a GDD scale. AGBleaf, AGBstem, AGBspike, and AGBtotal exhibited coherent developmental trajectories in GDD space, while water treatments primarily influenced biomass magnitude. The relationship between AGBleaf and AGBtotal followed a power-law allometric form, with parameters varying systematically with GDD. Based on these patterns, an allometric-VIs-GDD coupled model was constructed, in which AGBleaf was first estimated from VIs and GDD and subsequently transformed into AGBtotal using GDD-dependent allometric relationships. The proposed model outperformed the VIs-only and GDD-only baseline models as well as the VIs-GDD model, achieving a testing-set R2 of 0.691, an RMSE of 1.594 t·ha−1, and an MAE of 1.205 t·ha−1, and showed improved robustness and interpretability over the full growing season. External validation on an independent dataset further supported its improved robustness under independent experimental conditions.

title: Cropland soil salinity retrieval using a spectral-spatial cross-attention deep learning framework with environmental interpretability
abstract: Cropland soil salinization severely constrains crop growth and leads to substantial yield reductions, thereby constituting a critical ecological threat to national food security. Owing to its extensive spatial coverage and high temporal efficiency, remote sensing has become an indispensable tool for large-scale soil salinity monitoring. However, conventional remote sensing-based retrieval approaches are challenged by weak salinity-related spectral signals, complex coupling between soil salinity and environmental factors, and limited model generalization capability, which collectively hinder accurate characterization of cropland salinity patterns. To address these limitations, this study develops a multimodal deep learning framework, termed Spectral and Spatial Soil Net (SS-SoilNet), to retrieve soil salinity in coastal croplands of the Yellow River Delta. To enhance retrieval accuracy and capture the nonlinear interactions between soil salinity and the geo-environment, the model integrates multi-source inputs, including remote sensing observations, topographic features, and crop growth parameters. Specifically, SS-SoilNet incorporates a spectral sequence convolution module to extract dynamic spectral characteristics, a spatial attention module to account for surface heterogeneity and environmental features, and a multi-head cross-attention mechanism in which spatial features serve as queries to selectively guide spectral and vegetation index representations. Experimental results demonstrate that: (1) Compared with conventional machine-learning models such as Random Forest and Support Vector Regression, SS-SoilNet exhibits improved and more stable predictive performance. On the validation dataset, SS-SoilNet achieves an RMSE of approximately 3.6 g kg −1 , an MAE of about 1.7 g kg −1 , and an R 2 of around 0.68. (2) The integration of multimodal deep learning with multi-source covariates, including hydrological conditions, crop vigor indicators, and topographic factors enhances retrieval robustness relative to spectral-only approaches. (3) Interpretability analysis of covariate contributions reveals pronounced coupling effects among soil salinity, crop growth, and terrain. Overall, SS-SoilNet not only improves the accuracy and interpretability of soil salinity retrieval in coastal croplands but also provides quantitative evidence for understanding the environmental processes underlying soil salinization.

title: An end-to-end video-based action recognition pipeline for precision monitoring and success scoring of broiler breeder mating behavior
abstract: Efficient and accurate detection, tracking, and monitoring of successful mating behavior in broiler breeders are critical for assessing welfare, reproductive performance, and overall productivity in commercial farms. Computer vision and machine learning offer practical means for acquiring detailed insights into mating behaviors. Regardless, these technologies have rarely been applied to monitor mating events in their full dynamic context. In this study, we proposed an end-to-end video-based pipeline for recognizing and monitoring mating behavior in broiler breeders using a behavior recognition approach. The pipeline identified a four-step mating pattern through four main components: detection, tracking, action recognition, and scoring. The tracking algorithm was refined to manage movement challenges better, resulting in a 2% performance gain, while a Re-Identification module enhanced tracking during mating events by 70%. In addition, we introduced four datasets collected and annotated from a commercial broiler breeder farm, along with a scoring step designed to estimate the success probability of each mating event. The proposed pipeline achieved an overall accuracy of about 90% across multiple metrics. Despite the complexity of action-based mating behaviors, the results demonstrate strong potential for reliable automation in commercial use.

title: A spectral synergy correction model: Optimizing satellite spectra for improved soil organic carbon monitoring
abstract: Accurate quantification of soil organic carbon (SOC) in croplands is fundamental for sustainable land management. However, environmental interferences, such as variable moisture and surface residues, induce non-linear spectral attenuation in satellite imagery, significantly compromising monitoring precision. This study developed a highly transferable Spectral Synergy Correction (SSC) framework to establish a robust correction relationship between laboratory (ideal) and satellite (observed) spectra, effectively calibrating multispectral satellite reflectance to laboratory-grade proximal baselines by leveraging continental-scale soil spectral libraries. The framework was calibrated using a multi-scale Eurasian dataset (Site 1, N = 631) and independently validated over two consecutive years in a high-latitude Mollisol region (Site 2, N = 947). An environmental stratification strategy was implemented using the Moisture Stress Index (MSI) with a 1.25 threshold to derive independent correction matrices for disparate environmental conditions. Random Forest (RF) models were subsequently constructed using SSC-optimized features. Results indicated that the SSC model successfully restored the physical fidelity of remote sensing signals, elevating the Index of Agreement (IOA) between the SSC-corrected spectra and the ideal laboratory spectra to above 0.99. At Site 1, predictive accuracy (R2) improved from 0.3413 using raw satellite spectra to 0.5193 with SSC-optimized features. Independent validation at Site 2 revealed consistent and substantial performance gains: in 2018, R2 rose from 0.1702 to 0.4813, and in 2019, from 0.2369 to 0.4801. Notably, under severe moisture interference (April 2019), the SSC framework achieved an R2 of 0.4128, compared to 0.2087 for the raw data. The SSC process produced a feature-recovery effect where the importance rankings of key SOC-sensitive predictors—specifically GDVI and SWIR bands—converged with laboratory benchmarks, marking a transition from statistical noise fitting to radiometrically driven inversion. Ultimately, by establishing a robust correction relationship between ideal laboratory spectra and satellite observations, this framework provides a sensor-interoperable strategy correction for high-resolution SOC mapping, substantially reducing the reliance on synchronized field sampling.

title: A deep ensemble learning framework for precision image-level weed classification in paddy fields
abstract: Paddy cultivation plays a pivotal role in global agriculture, especially in regions where maximizing yield and sustainability is imperative. Among the most persistent challenges is the presence of weeds, which compete aggressively with crops for critical resources such as nutrients, water, sunlight, and space—ultimately suppressing plant growth and reducing productivity. This study presents a deep learning-based image-level weed classification framework tailored for paddy fields, designed to support precision agriculture by reducing the reliance on manual labor and chemical herbicides. A diverse dataset comprising approximately 950 field-acquired images was curated and annotated to reflect real-world conditions across different seasons and lighting variations. For image-level weed classification, a majority-voting ensemble of five pre-trained CNNs (InceptionV3, Xception, AlexNet, ResNet50, and VGG19) was created. This eliminated segmentation and allowed for quick on-device inference. Predictions were combined using an ensemble majority voting technique to improve classification reliability and overcome the shortcomings of individual models. Ties were settled by choosing the prediction from the model with the best validation accuracy. The proposed model achieved outstanding performance on the test dataset, with an accuracy of 99.70%, precision of 100%, recall of 98.87%, F1-score of 99.51% and AUC 99.42%. These results highlight the potential of deep ensemble learning in delivering accurate, consistent, and scalable solutions for intelligent weed management in precision rice farming.

title: CFD-DEM-based design of UAV precision seeding device and rice seed trajectory study
abstract: To address challenges in traditional rice direct seeding technologies, including low efficiency, insufficient seeding accuracy, and unclear flow field regulation mechanisms in UAV pneumatic seed metering devices, this study designed a UAV-based pneumatic precision ordered seed metering device for rice sprouted seeds. Its performance was systematically validated through CFD-DEM coupled simulations and field trials. First, the device prototype was constructed, comprising a variable-pitch screw conveyor, precision hole-wheel metering device, double-bent seed metering conduit, and airflow-assisted delivery system. Core component parameters were optimized via dynamic and kinematic analyses: the initial pitch of the screw was set to 20 mm, final pitch to 45 mm, and rotational speed to 250 rpm; the hole-wheel diameter was 128 mm with a rotational speed of 60 rpm; and 12 sprouted seeds were filled per hole to meet agronomic requirements. Second, a gas–solid coupled model was established using EDEM 2021.2 and CFD software to simulate the movement trajectories of sprouted seeds within the conduit under positive pressures of 0–5 kPa. This revealed the flow field regulation mechanism of “inner bend acceleration-outer bend deceleration.” Key findings included that a 4 kPa positive pressure could accelerate sprouted seeds to 4.54 m/s, reducing delivery time by 73% compared to gravity-based delivery and lowering collision frequency by 42%. Finally, field trials were conducted using a DJI T60 UAV with “Longjing 31″ as the test variety. Under flight speeds of 3 m/s and seeding densities of 300 seeds/m2, the device achieved a seedling qualification rate of 88.6%, a missed sowing rate of < 5%, a row spacing coefficient of variation (CV) ≤ 12%, and hole diameters all controlled within 50 mm. These results met the ISO 7256/1–1984 standard and agronomic requirements for rice cultivation in cold northern regions. The study confirmed that CFD-DEM coupled simulations can effectively guide the optimization of seed metering device parameters. The synergistic effect of the double-bent conduit and airflow-assisted system significantly enhanced seeding precision and stability, providing theoretical support and equipment solutions for UAV-based precision rice direct seeding technology.

title: ChatCEA: a knowledge-driven intelligent service agent for controlled environment agriculture
abstract: Controlled Environment Agriculture (CEA) faces challenges in accessing precise, actionable knowledge for efficient production management. Traditional expert systems and search engines often lack the flexibility and contextual understanding needed to address complex queries. Large language models (LLMs) exhibit strong generative and comprehension abilities, presenting an opportunity to enhance CEA practices. This study proposes ChatCEA, an intelligent service agent that integrates LLMs with domain-specific knowledge through a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) framework. The framework includes three main components: a two-source knowledge base module built from management manuals and journal papers, a retrieval module for contextual semantic search, and a knowledge integration module for processing unstructured data and refining information matching. This structure supplements general LLMs with specialized domain knowledge to improve response accuracy and relevance. ChatCEA also establishes the first CEA-specific benchmark with 1,025 question–answer pairs. The benchmark includes both qualitative and quantitative questions and supports systematic evaluation across the main subdomains of the entire production process. The framework also supports local deployment to protect data privacy and enable practical use in production environments. Experimental results show that ChatCEA achieves an answer correctness rate of 0.71, while GPT-4 and Google Search reach 0.41 and 0.44, respectively. The LLM-based evaluation scores are 4.3 for ChatCEA, 3.8 for GPT-4, and 2.5 for Google Search. ChatCEA also improved the handling of quantitative questions by extracting and reasoning with numerical information. These results demonstrate that ChatCEA provides accurate, data-driven support for CEA management. The knowledge base, Q&A benchmark, and source code are available at https://github.com/IDEAS-ZJU/ChatCEA.

title: Concept and rule guided neural network for early crop leaf nutrient deficiency diagnosis
abstract: Crop nutrition deficiency poses a major challenge to achieving optimal yield, particularly in smallholder farming systems where timely expert diagnosis is limited. Early detection is crucial to minimize losses and reduce unnecessary fertilizer or pesticide usage. While deep learning offers potential for automated visual diagnosis, most existing approaches operate as black boxes and lack interpretability, explainability, or actionable recommendations. In this work, we present a neurosymbolic framework for early nutrient deficiency detection in ash gourd leaves using the EarlyNSD dataset. Our approach integrates a ResNet-50 backbone with a dual-head design: a classification head for deficiency prediction and a concept-prediction head that quantifies physiologically meaningful visual patterns such as yellowing, edge discoloration, spots, and vein greenness. These concept scores are combined with predefined domain rules to guide the learning of the neural component and to generate transparent, human-aligned explanations for each diagnosis. Building on the model outputs, we incorporate a Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG)-based pipeline along with an agricultural knowledge base to generate targeted recommendations. This approach overcomes key shortcomings of pure neural models by incorporating domain knowledge in the form of differentiable fuzzy logic rules. The study demonstrates that the proposed framework improves both classification performance and interpretability compared to standard ResNet baselines. Grad-CAM analysis demonstrates that concept-guided attention aligns with symptom-specific regions, such as yellowed areas for Nitrogen deficiency or marginal discoloration for Potassium deficiency, providing visual validation of the reasoning process. Since EarlyNSD is limited in scale and visual diversity, the results are not directly comparable to large open-field datasets. Overall, our results establish a proof of concept for integrating neural detection with symbolic reasoning, enabling interpretable, actionable, and domain-informed nutrient management for practical applications.

title: Multi-objective hierarchical reinforcement learning for efficient and safe robotic manure cleaning in dairy barns
abstract: Autonomous mobile robots for manure removal in dairy barns must resolve conflicting objectives of cleaning efficiency, environmental impact, and animal welfare under highly cluttered and dynamic barn conditions. We introduce a Multi-Objective Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning (MO-HRL) framework that integrates a Global Evolutionary Scheduler (GES) for long-horizon cleaning task planning with an Adaptive RL-based Executor (ARE) for real-time, risk-aware robot motion control. The GES solves a multi-objective optimization problem over the robot’s travel distance, ammonia emissions, and cleaning yield via an evolutionary algorithm. The ARE employs a constrained Markov decision process enriched with historical high-loss weighting, adaptive action masking, and a final execution shield to guarantee smooth, non-injurious contacts with cows. In Webots simulations across three barn layouts (with ten, twenty, and thirty free-roaming cows, respectively), MO-HRL maintains high task completion ( ≥ 93 . 03 % ) with low comfort-distance violations ( ≤ 6 . 67 % ), achieves a peak throughput of 1 . 98 kg/min , and shortens completion time by up to 6× versus PPO (up to 8× in Small). Ammonia emission reduction reaches up to 0.144 kg m − 3 . These results indicate that hierarchical, risk-aware RL can translate long-horizon scheduling and real-time safety constraints into tangible gains for rapid, safe, and sustainable barn sanitation.

title: DynROI-Hybrid: Dynamic modeling of functional regions for feeding and drinking behavior detection in laying hens
abstract: The automatic identification of feeding and drinking behaviors in commercial laying hen houses remains challenging due to of high stocking densities, frequent occlusions, and the pendular movement of feeding and drinking equipment, which compromise approaches that rely solely on fixed regions or bounding boxes. This study proposes the DynROI-Hybrid framework, which integrates object detection with YOLOv11, selective segmentation with Segment Anything Model 2 (SAM 2), and dynamic modeling of functional interaction regions associated with feeders and drinkers. The methodology combines spatial criteria (overlap, proximity, and intersection) with temporal stabilization via hysteresis, enabling distinction between true interaction events and mere spatial proximity. Results demonstrate robust performance, achieving 94% overall accuracy and a Cohen’s Kappa coefficient of 0.91 compared to gold-standard validation. The proposed approach reduces false positives caused by equipment movement and structural resource geometry while maintaining computational feasibility for Edge AI applications. The method contributes to automated monitoring of feeding-related behaviors in commercial poultry production systems, with potential applications in welfare assessment and decision support within Precision Livestock Farming.

title: Individual and autonomous walk-over weighing crate with concentrate feeder – Development and validation of an improved mobile weighing system for sheep
abstract: • Development of a mobile, energy self-sufficient autonomous weighing system for sheep successfully tested on pasture. • Individual weighing by WoW crate, utilizing light barriers, gates, and individual concentrate feed-based motivation. • High repeatability (SD = 0.40 kg; CV = 0.48 %) and accuracy (R 2 = 0.999; CCC = 0.999) of autonomous WoW crate demonstrated. • Autonomous in-crate weighing supported by robust fail-safe systems designed to guarantee animal safety. • Automatic data upload to a web-based database, with remote control via mobile internet connection. Continuous weight recording is an important method in animal husbandry to gain information about the animals’ body condition. Traditionally, monitoring the body weight of sheep has been a labour-intensive and time-consuming task, as the animals must be caught or restrained and weighed manually. As a result, regular weight monitoring is often neglected in sheep farming. This paper presents the development of a modified autonomous weighing system for sheep, which combines the principles of a walk-over weighing scale with a weighing crate. The aim of the project was to develop an efficient, precise and autonomous solution for weighing sheep without human intervention. The result is a mobile, energy self-sufficient prototype that enables autonomous and individual weight recording for sheep as they pass through the system. The walk-over weighing crate integrates light barriers and automatic pneumatic gates that control the flow of animals, allowing each sheep to be weighed separately on the weighing platform. To encourage voluntary entry, a concentrate feeder dispenses a small amount of feed as motivation. The electrical components and the air compressor are powered by batteries and solar panels to ensure autonomous operation. To evaluate repeatability and accuracy of the system, 40 sheep and 88 lambs were randomly selected over two years. The lambs were first weighed on a static reference weighing scale, and these measurements were compared with the automatically recorded weights obtained from the walk-over weighing crate (R 2 = 0.999; CCC = 0.999). For the evaluation of the repeatability of the weighing, the sheep passed through the walk-over weighing crate in 19 different weighing cycles. On average, a standard deviation (SD) of 0.40 kg and coefficient of variation (CV) of 0.48 % were achieved. The final test was conducted under real pasture conditions. After a short adaptation phase of six days, 32.5 % of the animals voluntarily used the system. The development of the autonomous walk-over weighing crate offers an efficient and precise solution for continuous, non-invasive and autonomous weight monitoring in sheep farming.

title: Design and performance analysis of bionic petunia flexible end-effector based on citrus twist picking
abstract: To address the challenge of picking citrus fruits that grow in clusters and are easily obscured by foliage, a flexible end-effector was designed. It is capable of isolating individual fruits within dense canopies, and its design was inspired by the nonlinear deformation of petal contours during petunia blossoming. A twisting-based picking strategy was adopted to replace conventional shearing methods. A model was developed to describe the relationship between citrus geometry, picking posture, and the required driving force. Finally, the relationship between the driving force and the peak torque required for successful citrus picking was derived, providing a theoretical basis for the optimal application of gripping force. Field experiments showed that when the picking angle is less than 30°, the success rate for citrus fruits with diameters of 75–95 mm was 100%. In the range of 30°–45°, the success rate was 100% for fruit diameters less than 80 mm, and only 64.3% for diameters greater than 80 mm. When the picking angle exceeded 45°, the success rate is 29%. The average picking time per fruit was 3.4 s. Since a complete visual recognition system was not available in this experiment, timing began only after the end-effector had stabilized its grip. Timing ended when the citrus fruit stalk was observed to be snapped off. When the picking angle was controlled within 45°, the flexible end-effector achieved the highest picking success rate. These results demonstrated the feasibility of the “flexible end-effector + twist picking” strategy for citrus picking.

title: Automated detection system based on type-3 fuzzy logic for evaluating fly infestation level in cattle
abstract: Horn fly (Haematobia irritans) infestation represents a persistent challenge in cattle production, affecting animal welfare, productivity, and economic sustainability. Although recent advances in computer vision have enabled automated fly detection and counting, translating these outputs into reliable infestation severity assessments remains an open problem, particularly under uncertainty and subjective interpretation. This study proposes an integrated framework for automated assessment of horn fly infestation that combines deep learning-based vision models with a Type-3 Fuzzy Logic System (T3FLS) to provide an uncertainty-aware, interpretable evaluation. The proposed system employs You Only Look Once version 11 (YOLOv11) for animal segmentation and small-object fly detection under real-world conditions. From the detection results, three complementary descriptors are proposed: fly density, fly count, and spatial coverage. These descriptors are normalized using robust empirical references and serve as inputs to a Mamdani-type T3FLS, which explicitly models uncertainty arising from detection noise, environmental variability, and ambiguous infestation boundaries. The fuzzy system outputs a continuous infestation index in the range [0, 1] together with a linguistic classification (Low, Moderate, High). Experimental validation was conducted using 150 images evaluated by the proposed system and by three human experts. Comparative results show that the Type-3 fuzzy model clearly outperforms lower-order fuzzy systems, achieving balanced accuracy, macro F1-score, and Cohen’s kappa coefficient of 0.905, 0.891, and 0.854, respectively, indicating strong agreement with expert assessments. The proposed framework advances automated fly assessment beyond simple counting toward a holistic, uncertainty-aware infestation evaluation, providing a robust and practical decision-support tool for livestock management.

title: GDYEY: Grape detection and yield estimation framework based on YOLO architecture
abstract: Accurate yield estimation is crucial for optimizing agricultural management and market forecasting. However, the variable scale and occlusion of grapes cause their detection to have a negative impact, thereby reducing the precision of yield estimation. This study proposes a Grape Detection and Yield Estimation framework based on the YOLO architecture (GDYEY) by integrating a grape detection network into a depth estimation network. Specifically, a complex and diverse grape detection dataset was first constructed to facilitate verifying estimation performance and offer convenience to this research field. Moreover, a novel target detection mechanism based on Knowledge Distillation and Enhanced Convolutional Neural Networks (KD-ECNN) is designed by employing knowledge distillation to effectively transfer semantic information from the teacher to the student network. Generalization capability is enhanced through this approach. Additionally, a new yield estimation strategy based on Depth Estimation was presented by embedding the LapDepth Network to improve the accuracy of yield estimation. The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves a mAP of 81.6% in grape detection, surpassing 15 mainstream detection models. Additionally, grape yield estimation shows a significant improvement, with accuracy gains of approximately 25% and 10% over the counting-only and area-based estimation methods, respectively.

title: LeafCLIP: A detection method for the lesion areas of outdoor plants in complex lighting scenarios
abstract: Plant disease detection under complex natural field conditions is critical for sustainable agriculture but remains challenging due to severe photometric variations, frequent occlusions, and limited annotated data. Traditional visual models often struggle to generalize in real-world scenarios, where irregular shadows, dense foliage, and background clutter substantially degrade detection accuracy and robustness. To address these issues, we propose a unified and robust framework based on a cascaded CLIP architecture that combines multi-scale semantic feature alignment with physics-aware shadow correction. The framework introduces structure-preserving synthetic anomaly generation to enrich training diversity, lightweight adapters to fuse multi-depth CLIP visual features for precise lesion localization, and domain-specific learnable text prompts to enhance cross-modal alignment. Additionally, a dynamic mask-aware diffusion model is devised to reconstruct illumination-invariant representations by jointly refining shadow masks and restoring degraded regions. Experimental evaluations demonstrate that our method achieves state-of-the-art performance across multiple datasets on various benchmarks, such as Image-AUROC, mean Average Precision (mAP). In particular, on the Rice Leaf Images detection, our method reaches an image-level AUROC of 0.9900 and a mAP of 0.9973. Overall, the results verify the effectiveness and robustness of the proposed framework to appearance-level distribution shifts under challenging agricultural field conditions.

title: Comparative evaluation of machine learning models integrated with optimization algorithms for daily transpiration estimation in citrus orchards of dry-hot valley region in China
abstract: Accurate estimation of canopy transpiration (T) is essential for optimizing irrigation scheduling and improving water-use efficiency. Machine learning (ML) approaches have become critical for T estimation in smart agriculture. This study was conducted in citrus orchards within the Yuanjiang Dry-hot Valley, Yunnan Province, China. From 2020 to 2022, sap flow was monitored using thermal dissipation probes (TDP), and these data were integrated with multi-source meteorological and soil variables to develop T estimation models. The Random Forest-Recursive Feature Elimination (RF-RFE) algorithm was applied for feature selection. Twelve models were developed by combining three ML models, Random Forest (RF), Support Vector Regression (SVR), and Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGB), with three hyperparameter tuning algorithms, Grid Search (GS), Genetic Algorithm (GA), and Grey Wolf Optimizer (GWO). Shapley Additive Explanations (SHAP) was used to interpret the drivers of the best-performing model. Results demonstrated that RF-RFE effectively reduced input variables from 17 to 5 key factors: day of year (DOY), average air temperature (Ta), wind speed (u2), soil volumetric water content (VWC), and actual vapor pressure (ea). Among the 12 models, the GWO-XGB combination achieved the best performance (R2 = 0.91, KGE = 0.94, and RMSE = 0.18 mm d-1), ranking first in the Global Performance Indicator (GPI). SHAP analysis further revealed that DOY characterized seasonal climatic variations and phenological rhythms, Ta and u2 positively contributed to T, while ea showed a negative contribution, and VWC imposed a limiting effect at low levels. The proposed RF-RFE and GWO–XGB framework provides accurate and interpretable T estimation using only five key inputs. It offers a practical and scalable solution for precision irrigation decision support in dry-hot valleys.

title: Automated on-site viable primordia count estimation for Hypsizygus marmoreus through enhanced RSL-YOLOv8m based segmentation
abstract: The viable primordia in edible mushroom cultivation are the most critical factor determining yield and quality, yet its accurate quantification remains challenging due to morphological variability and low-contrast backgrounds. This study proposes an enhanced RSL-YOLOv8m-seg framework that significantly improves segmentation robustness through multi-scale feature enhancement and adaptive fusion mechanisms. Validated on a Hypsizygus marmoreus dataset containing 200,000 annotated instances, the model achieves 68.1% mAP@0.5–surpassing the baseline by 1.9 percentage points–while maintaining stable performance in industrial cultivation environments. The synergistic module integration elevates recall to 48.5% and true positive rate to 89.2%, with computational cost constrained within industrial deployment limits. Convex hull contour fitting is utilized to precisely quantify the aspect ratios of primordia. Subsequently, viable primordia are defined using an aspect ratio criterion greater than four. To the best of the researchers’ knowledge, this represents the first application of deep learning for detection and analysis of Hypsizygus marmoreus primordia, providing reliable technical support for intelligent cultivation regulation.

title: Non-destructive quantitative assessment of rice seedling transplanting injury using a CSI–hyperspectral framework
abstract: Mechanical transplanting often induces complex root–stem-coupled injury to rice seedlings, a critical bottleneck for stable yield formation that remains difficult to quantify. This injury mode generates a synergistic, non-additive stress state between root and stem tissues, driving a persistent high-stress regime that explains delayed regreening and seedling mortality. Existing assessment methods rely on subjective field sampling or isolated physiological indicators. These approaches fail to capture systemic root–stem synergy, yielding unstable ground truths for non-destructive phenotyping. To address this, we developed and validated a Comprehensive Stress Index–Hyperspectral Imaging (CSI–HSI) framework. Under controlled conditions, graded root–stem-coupled injury was imposed while measuring malondialdehyde (MDA), proline (Pro), soluble sugars (SS), the SPAD chlorophyll index, and chlorophyll fluorescence (Fv/Fm). Principal component analysis (PCA) integrated these variables into the CSI, which served as a linearized, robust modeling ground truth for systemic stress. Using hyperspectral data, we developed prediction models based on partial least squares regression (PLSR), support vector regression (SVR), random forest regression (RFR), and convolutional neural networks (CNN). When CSI was the response variable, model accuracy and robustness consistently outperformed those of models targeting single indicators. The CSI-targeted SPA–PLSR model (successive projections algorithm combined with PLSR) achieved the highest accuracy (Rp2 = 0.914, 95% CI: 0.882–0.923; RPD = 2.645), higher than the best single-indicator model (SPAD-targeted, Rp2 = 0.882). The CSI–HSI framework provides a physiologically grounded, non-destructive solution for quantifying complex transplanting injury, establishing a foundation for transplanter design optimization and intelligent, real-time quality monitoring.

title: MIRAGE: Biomechanically interpretable 3D generation and reconstruction of maize plants
abstract: Accurate 3D modeling is essential for automated plant phenotyping and biomechanical analysis. We present MIRAGE (MaIze Reconstruction And GEneration), a biomechanically guided framework for generating and reconstructing 3D maize plants from a single image. At its core is MaizeBR, an interpretable and controllable 3D biomechanical representation that introduces a novel parameterization model for maize organs. MaizeBR is motivated by plant biomechanics, incorporating structural constraints informed by biological principles, including stalk cylindricality, anisotropic leaf curvature, and phyllotactic attachment patterns, commonly observed as the key traits in real maize plants. These constraints enhance the structural integrity and biological plausibility of the reconstructed models. MIRAGE generates 3D structures using a voxel-based diffusion model, followed by NURBS (Non-Uniform Rational B-Splines) surface reconstruction guided by MaizeBR. To enhance generalization, we incorporate domain-specific augmentations that simulate natural plant variations such as leaf curvature and elongation. Experiments across multiple maize datasets show that MIRAGE outperforms state-of-the-art methods in both reconstruction quality and biological plausibility. Additionally, by enabling accurate 3D skeletonization, MIRAGE supports more precise phenotypic trait extraction compared to traditional 2D-based approaches.

title: End-to-end fusion of RGB and low-resolution NIR for enhanced crop-specific NIR generation
abstract: Near-infrared (NIR) imaging plays a crucial role in applications such as vegetation monitoring, remote sensing, and environmental analysis. However, NIR imaging systems are often expensive and limited in resolution compared to conventional RGB sensors. To address this limitation, we propose an end-to-end deep learning framework that generates high-resolution (HR) NIR images by fusing high-resolution RGB images with low-resolution (LR) NIR inputs. The framework integrates a lightweight image-to-image (I2I) backbone for extracting rich spatial features from the RGB domain, dual feature extractors operating in a multi-scale paradigm, and a learnable fusion module that adaptively combines spatial and spectral information. A decoder network then reconstructs the fused features into the final HR NIR output. Extensive experiments on paired aerial RGB–NIR crop datasets demonstrate that the proposed method significantly outperforms standalone RGB-to-NIR translation and conventional LR-to-HR NIR super-resolution approaches, improving performance from approximately 27.6 dB to over 34.2 dB Peak Signal-to-Noise Ratio (PSNR) and from 0.90 to 0.95 Structural Similarity Index (SSIM) when fusing 128 × 128 NIR inputs. Notably, even when the NIR input is 32 × lower in resolution (16 × 16), the framework consistently surpasses RGB-only baselines, achieving around 29.6 dB PSNR and 0.91 SSIM. Beyond quantitative evaluation, additional analyses including SSIM error map visualization, cross-resolution and cross-dataset testing, and reconstruction variability assessment provide deeper insight into the robustness, limitations, and behavior of the framework under challenging conditions. The modular design of the architecture further enables flexible adaptation to a broad range of multi-modal and cross-spectral imaging tasks. • New framework fuses HR RGB with LR NIR to generate HR NIR images • Backbone handles translation while attention fuses dual-stream features. • LR NIR improves RGB–NIR translation even at 32× downsampling. • Framework beats RGB-to-NIR and NIR super-resolution by large margins. • Robustness validated via cross-resolution, cross-dataset, and error-map analysis.

title: A corn seedling row detection method for fields based on YOLO-AP
abstract: To address interference factors encountered by field weeding robots during crop row recognition, including illumination variations, weed interference, and wheat stubble occlusion, an improved YOLOv11-based corn seedling detection model named YOLO-AP is proposed. High-resolution field images of corn seedlings were collected using a handheld DJI Osmo Pocket 3 and a ZED stereo camera mounted on a high-clearance weeding machine, and a dataset covering different planting modes was constructed. The YOLO-AP model was developed by embedding a PMSFA module that integrates partial convolution and spatial attention to address feature confusion and multi-scale challenges, and by introducing an AFPN structure to enhance the model’s robustness against environmental interference such as illumination and occlusion. Furthermore, a crop row extraction method combining affinity clustering and random sample consensus (RANSAC) is proposed. Row lines are first fitted using projection clustering; subsequently, outliers and abnormal intersecting segments are removed. The remaining outliers are then re-clustered and refitted. A temporal smoothing algorithm is further designed, utilizing multi-frame parameter fusion to improve row-line stability across consecutive frames, thereby enabling dynamic crop row extraction in complex field environments. Experimental results demonstrate that the improved YOLO-AP model achieves 94.19% mAP at 0.5, 90.38% precision, and 88.66% recall, which are 1.17, 0.69, and 2.92 percentage points higher than those of the baseline model (YOLOv11s), respectively. Under static conditions, the mean deviation angle across environments is 1.42° with a standard deviation of 1.31°. Under dynamic conditions, the mean deviation angle is 0.46° with a standard deviation of 0.71°. The average lateral pixel deviation is 28.3 px, the average vertical pixel distance ranges from 10.41 px to 14.89 px, and the average processing time per frame is 23.3 ms. This method provides an effective visual perception solution for the accurate autonomous navigation of weeding robots in complex field environments.

title: Learning standardized expert harvesting motions via kinematically regularized RNN-VAE for skill transfer
abstract: Manual harvesting of high-value crops relies on tacit hand skills that are difficult to teach and evaluate objectively. This paper presents a learning-from-demonstration framework that builds a reusable expert reference motion from glove-captured 3D hand joint trajectories. We train a recurrent variational autoencoder (RNN-VAE) to model expert harvesting motions and introduce kinematic regularization to improve physical plausibility, including velocity smoothness and bone-length consistency. After training, we extract a standardized expert template by aggregating latent representations from multiple expert demonstrations and decoding the aggregated latent into a single representative motion sequence. To compare motions under varying execution speeds, we employ Dynamic Time Warping (DTW) for temporal alignment and define template representativeness (RepScore) as the mean DTW distance from expert trials to a template (lower is better). Experiments on strawberry and apple harvesting, recorded at 60 Hz with five experts and approximately 20 trials per expert, show that the learned standardized template improves representativeness over a single random trial on strawberry (RepScore 13.13 vs. 17.16) and is comparable to DTW-barycenter averaging (DBA: 13.18). On apple, DBA yields a lower RepScore than the learned template (11.97 vs. 14.05), indicating that the optimal template construction strategy can be fruit-dependent. Qualitative reconstruction overlays and DTW alignment visualizations further illustrate faithful motion reconstruction and interpretable phase-level matching for expert-query comparison.

title: A review of visual navigation for agricultural robots in open fields and controlled environments
abstract: Vision-based navigation is fundamental to achieving intelligent and autonomous operation in agricultural robots. This paper reviews three key components of visual navigation: visual perception, localization and map building, and path planning. Applications in both open-field and controlled environment agriculture (CEA) environments are discussed, as they represent unstructured outdoor conditions and global navigation satellite systems (GNSS)-denied indoor settings. Although recent advancements in deep learning algorithms, higher-resolution imaging sensors, and more efficient edge computing hardware have enhanced perception accuracy and processing speed, significant challenges remain. These include reduced robustness when operating in dynamic and unstructured environments, limited real-time processing capabilities due to computational constraints, and a lack of diverse, high-quality datasets for training and validating models across different crops, growth stages, and environmental conditions. To address these issues, the paper outlines future research directions. These include the adoption of advanced sensing technologies, multimodal sensor fusion, reinforcement learning, and leveraging the reasoning capabilities of Large Language Models (LLMs) and Large Vision Models (LVMs) to enhance context understanding and decision-making. Emphasis is also placed on improving edge computing capabilities and leveraging synthetic datasets and simulation-to-reality (Sim-to-Real) transfer techniques to enhance model generalization and deployment robustness. This review systematically synthesizes the progress and challenges of vision-based navigation in agricultural robotics and highlights future research avenues, thereby establishing a conceptual and methodological foundation for advancing the precision, autonomy, and intelligence of next-generation agricultural robotic systems.

title: Design, development, and field evaluation of a dual-mode robotic-human system for in situ soil compaction assessment in agricultural fields
abstract: Soil compaction is a major constraint in mechanized agriculture. Its accurate measurement is essential for understanding machinery impacts, optimizing crop growth, and guiding soil management practices. However, its strong spatial and depth-wise variability makes it difficult to characterize with traditional hand-held penetrometers alone. This study aimed to develop and evaluate a robotic penetrometer system for field-scale compaction mapping in sandy-loam potato–forage rotations on Prince Edward Island (PEI), Canada, over two consecutive growing seasons (2024 and 2025) at six depths. In 2024, we collected co-located penetration-resistance profiles with a FieldScout SC900 and the robotic penetrometer in electrical-conductivity (EC) zones derived from SWAT Box maps in two potato fields. In 2025, after calibration, the robot was deployed on a regular grid in two alfalfa fields that had grown potatoes in the previous year. In total, depth-wise mean profiles from the two instruments showed excellent agreement (R2≈0.97), while point-wise paired measurements exhibited moderate but positive correlation (R2≈0.60), reflecting micro-scale heterogeneity and differences in insertion mechanics. Spatial results revealed low to moderate compaction with localized hotspots in the 2024 potato fields, but extensive, vertically coherent high-resistance zones in the 2025 alfalfa fields, indicating persistent subsoil compaction following intensive potato traffic and limited subsequent tillage. The study demonstrates that a calibrated robotic penetrometer can reproduce conventional measurements while providing higher spatial resolution, deeper and more consistent penetration, and seamless integration with geospatial analysis. These capabilities support controlled-traffic farming, targeted subsoiling, and data-driven decision support for managing soil structure in traffic-sensitive cropping systems.

title: EasyAphid: a comprehensive method for aphid infestation quantification in wheat using EVC-YOLO-Seg model and RGB images
abstract: Aphids are one of the most harmful pests in wheat production, and timely and accurate aphid monitoring is crucial for effective control. However, existing methods mainly rely on manual investigations, resulting in low quality and efficiency of pest monitoring. The main challenges in aphid monitoring include the small target size and insufficient segmentation accuracy under complex field conditions. To address these problems, we constructed an instance segmentation dataset of aphids and leaves based on 1,412 field images and proposed a leaf-scale instance segmentation model (called EVC-YOLO-Seg) by integrating the YOLO framework with the designed EV Block and Fusion Multi-scale Convolutional Attention (FMCA) module. Results showed that EVC-YOLO-Seg achieved mAP(M), mIoU, and F1-Score values of 0.888, 0.852, and 0.906, respectively. Furthermore, seven damage indicators (quantity, density, coverage, aggregation, cluster number, mean cluster size, and max cluster size) and a comprehensive indicator (Aphid Damage Indicator, ADI) were developed to quantitatively assess aphid infestation severity based on the model and statistical analysis. All proposed indicators showed a high correlation with actual values, with R² ranging from 0.814 to 0.978. By calculating eight key indicators, 157 materials were successfully classified into four categories with significantly different levels of aphid damage, demonstrating the effectiveness of the indicators. Finally, to enhance the utilization efficiency of the algorithm and ensure that the research outcomes benefit a broader community of scientific researchers, we integrated the above methods and developed a mobile-based automatic aphid damage analysis application named EasyAphid. Overall, the proposed method demonstrates high accuracy, robustness, and generalization capability for aphid segmentation and severity evaluation, providing reliable technical support for precision monitoring and timely control of aphid infestations in wheat production.

title: Advances in the principles and methods for nondestructive and noninvasive soil salinity measurements in the field: A review
abstract: Soil salinity impacts plant growth worldwide; thus, understanding the status of soil salinity is crucial for mitigating its adverse effects. Considering that the spatial and temporal distributions of soil salinity are naturally heterogeneous, three-dimensional monitoring in particular is necessary. However, the coupling of soil moisture and salinity makes accurate measurement of soil salinity in situ difficult. Although the traditional sampling method can achieve this, it is time-consuming, destructive and unrepeatable. In this paper, we reviewed the primary principles and applications of nondestructive and noninvasive techniques (soil solution conductivity, electrical resistance, electromagnetic methods, ground-penetrating radar, time domain reflectometry, frequency domain reflectometry and spectroscopy) for soil salinity measurements in the field. The advantages and disadvantages of these methods are discussed systematically. These techniques generally face challenges in practical applications, such as the inability to achieve three-dimensional monitoring of soil salinity and to separate the soil moisture and salinity contents from electrical signals, most of which are electrical conductivity. On the basis of the state-of-the-art of research, we hope to provide a reference for selecting appropriate methods for soil salinity monitoring in different scenarios. However, most importantly, the combined use of electrical resistance tomography and electrical capacitance tomography shows strong potential for three-dimensional mapping of soil salinity and may provide a promising approach to alleviating the current technical bottleneck in field-based soil salinity monitoring.

title: Dual-stage parameter-efficient tuning for in-field plant disease few-shot classification
abstract: In this paper, we address the challenge of classifying in-field plant disease data that is both scarce and visually complex. Existing methods typically treat these issues separately, but their performance often collapses when deployed on edge devices in real-world settings. To overcome both problems, we propose a two-stage, parameter-efficient adaptation pipeline with strong empirical robustness across multiple target domains. During an offline domain adaptation stage, the model adapters are trained extensively on complex plant-disease and domain-relevant datasets to gather domain-specific knowledge. Later, during the testing stage, new online adapters classify novel classes with fast task-specific few-shot testing. On challenging in-field datasets (PlantDoc, PlantSeg, PlantWild), our model achieves average accuracies of 76.13% (5-way 1-shot) and 89.00% (5-way 5-shot), improving over the base transfer-learning pipeline by 12.01% and 7.68%, respectively. Because of its adaptation strategy, modular design, and parameter efficiency, our approach demonstrates strong robustness in low-data scenarios and across novel disease types within the evaluated datasets, requires no expensive retraining on high-end hardware when upgrading backbone architectures, and imposes minimal memory and compute overhead for in-field edge device deployments.

title: Construction and validation of a characteristic apple discrete element model for mechanical compression and grasping
abstract: During the mechanized harvesting, transportation, and sorting of apples, the apple skin is prone to damage, resulting in economic losses. Therefore, accurately assessing the forces applied to apples and their degree of damage is of great significance for improving the quality of harvesting. This provides model support for the analysis of mechanical compression and grasping processes. This paper constructs physical models of three major apple varieties in the northwest region: Huaniu, Qincui, and Ruixue. Through three-dimensional scanning technology, collision bounce tests, and friction coefficient measurements, the collision recovery coefficients (0.33, 0.41, and 0.35, respectively) of Huaniu, Qincui, and Ruixue, as well as the friction coefficients between apples and materials, were determined. The mechanical property curves of the three apples were obtained through uniaxial compression tests. Using the Box-Behnken experimental design, a series of uniaxial compression simulation experiments was conducted. A regression model was established between bonding parameters (normal/tangential stiffness, normal/tangential strength, and bonding radius coefficient) and maximum load. The influence of parameter interactions on load response was analyzed, and the optimal bonding parameter combinations for the three apples were finally determined: Normal/Shear Stiffness per unit area for Huaniu, Qincui, and Ruixue are 1.67 × 108, 3 × 108, and 3.35 × 108, respectively; Normal/Shear Strength are 1.41 × 105, 2.58 × 105, and 1.73 × 105, respectively; Bonded Disk Scale are 1.11, 1.14, and 1.21, respectively. The results of the uniaxial compression verification tests showed that the deviations between the simulated maximum loads of Huaniu, Qincui, and Ruixue apples and the physical tests were 2.50%, 3.23%, and 4.30%, respectively. The load–displacement curve trends were basically consistent with the physical tests. Based on this, experiments were conducted to simulate the grasping of apples by a harvesting robot, and the maximum contact forces between the apples and the robot in physical and simulation experiments were compared. The results showed that the maximum contact force errors for the three apples were 2.37%, 5.00%, and 4.58%, respectively, indicating that the discrete element model can be applied to the simulation analysis of apple grasping. This study provides numerical models and technical support for characterizing contact forces and predicting damage during apple compression and grasping.

title: Automated computer vision monitoring of black soldier fly larval growth using metaheuristic optimization for waste-to-feed bioconversion
abstract: Sustainable conversion of organic byproducts into agricultural resources is vital for achieving circular bioeconomy goals. The black soldier fly (BSF, Hermetia illucens) offers an efficient bioconversion pathway, transforming organic residues into protein-rich feed and biofertilizer. However, variability in feed composition and high labor requirements constrain the scalability and profitability of BSF-based waste-to-feed systems. This study introduces an automated computer vision framework for monitoring the growth of black soldier fly larvae (BSFL) using instance segmentation and metaheuristic optimization. Sewage sludge from Taiwan’s wastewater treatment plants was used as a feed substrate, and a Pilgrimage Walk Optimization (PWO) algorithm was integrated with a You Only Look Once version 11-instance segmentation model (YOLO11-seg) to enhance hyperparameter tuning and detection accuracy. The model achieved high precision in estimating larval surface area and converting it to biomass weight, enabling real-time, non-contact monitoring of growth performance. An economic analysis using Net Present Value (NPV) and Internal Rate of Return (IRR) demonstrated that a 1:1 sludge-to-wheat bran mixture significantly improved bioconversion efficiency and financial returns, underscoring the feasibility of AI-driven computer vision for intelligent insect farming, organic waste valorization, and sustainable waste management. Nevertheless, these findings are based on laboratory-scale experiments, and field-scale studies are needed to validate scalability and real-world implementation.

title: Blueberry maturity detection model based on dual-branch frequency-aware feature fusion and frequency-enhanced Haar wavelet downsampling
abstract: Rapid detection of blueberry maturity holds significant importance in large-scale cultivation. However, mobile platform-based rapid maturity detection methods face challenges such as defocus blur in captured images and frequent occlusion of blueberry fruits. To address these issues, this study proposes an improved detection model called YOLO-DFEW, which enhances the accuracy and robustness of maturity detection under defocused blur and occlusion conditions. The model incorporates a dual-branch feature fusion architecture and integrates two novel modules: a frequency-aware feature fusion-based secondary upsampling combination module (FreqFusion-US2) and a frequency-enhanced Haar wavelet downsampling (FEHWD) module. The FreqFusion-US2 effectively combines high-frequency details with low-frequency global information through frequency-aware feature fusion, while the FEHWD module enhances critical features and reduces detail loss using frequency-enhanced Haar wavelet transforms. Experimental results demonstrate that YOLO-DFEW achieves state-of-the-art performance on both a Custom-developed dataset and an open-access dataset. On the custom-developed dataset, it yields a mean Average Precision (mAP@50) of 0.844 and an F1 Score of 0.787, exceeding those of YOLOv9m by 6.2% and 5.8% respectively. On the open-access dataset, it achieves a mAP@50 of 0.704 and an F1 Score of 0.695, outperforming YOLOv9m by 5% and 4.5% respectively. Additionally, YOLO-DFEW exhibits the lowest missed detection rate in scenario-based experiments under static/dynamic sampling and occluded/non-occluded conditions. Notably, the computational cost of YOLO-DFEW is significantly reduced, with a substantial decrease in the number of parameters to only 14.1 M, while maintaining high accuracy, making it suitable for rapid blueberry maturity detection on mobile platforms.

title: Rice seedling row detection based on leaf sheath localization
abstract: Rice seedling row identification is a critical component of intelligent field operations and holds substantial importance in promoting the advancement of precision agriculture. However, most existing vision-based methods rely primarily on leaf-based visual cues for seedling localization, which are highly susceptible to environmental disturbances such as wind-induced leaf deflection and background weeds, leading to unstable row detection in paddy field environments. To address these challenges, this study proposes a rice seedling row detection method based on leaf sheath localization points, aiming to mitigate the influence of leaf oscillation on detection accuracy. An enhanced YOLOv8 object detection model is developed by incorporating the Dynamic Serpentine Convolution (DSC-C2F) module, Convolutional Block Attention Module (CBAM), and a lightweight C3Ghost module to improve detection accuracy while maintaining computational efficiency. Furthermore, a seedling row extraction approach based on a vanishing point perspective system (VP-PSE) is proposed to improve row identification performance under perspective distortion in complex field conditions. Experimental results show that the improved YOLOv8n + DSC-C2F + CBAM + C3Ghost model achieves a 2.9% increase in mAP@50 compared with the baseline model while maintaining low computational complexity, making it suitable for deployment on low-power embedded devices. In seedling row detection, the VP-PSE method significantly improves fitting accuracy and reduces lateral distance error and angular error compared with traditional clustering algorithms such as k-means and DBSCAN. Compared with leaf-based detection, the proposed leaf sheath localization strategy reduces row detection error by approximately 70% under light wind conditions (0)–(2) m/s). This study offers a more stable seedling row detection scheme for automated field operations under mild environmental disturbances.

title: DyRFA-Net: Apple flower blooming stage detection based on anther color features
abstract: Monitoring the blooming stages of apple flowers is crucial for orchard management, as different floral stages directly influence the timing and success of pollination. A novel deep learning framework, DyRFA-Net, is proposed in this study, where the blooming stages of apple flowers are detected based on anther color features as the core visual indicator. Instead of adopting conventional physiological definitions, this study classifies apple flowers into two blooming stages based on anther color. Flowers with unopened florets or pale-yellow anthers are considered to be in the early blooming stage, while those with orange anthers are regarded as being in the later stage of flowering. DyRFA-Net integrates a Receptive-Field Attention Convolution (RFAConv) to enhance flower feature extraction in complex orchard scenes. A Partial Multi-Scale Attention (PMA) module is introduced to capture subtle changes in stamen color while maintaining a lightweight model architecture. Additionally, Dynamic Upsampling (DySample) is employed to improve detection precision for small and densely clustered flowers. The model is evaluated on a self-constructed apple flower dataset annotated according to the anther color-based blooming stage. Experimental results show that DyRFA-Net achieves mAP50 detection accuracies of 88.2% for flowers in the later blooming stage and 86.7% for those in the early blooming stage, with an overall mAP50 of 87.4%. For mAP50–95, the model achieves 69.3% and 68.2%, respectively. The proposed method also outperforms several state-of-the-art detectors in stage classification accuracy. These results demonstrate that DyRFA-Net provides an effective and biologically grounded solution for apple flower blooming stage detection, offering practical support for intelligent orchard management and precise pollination scheduling.

title: Mechanism analysis and experiment verification of narrow-spacing tuber mustard transplanting device based on MBD-DEM coupling method
abstract: Tuber mustard, a typical narrow-row spacing crop (12–14 cm), has long relied on manual transplanting due to the lack of specialized machinery, leading to high labor intensity and low production efficiency. To overcome this limitation, a dedicated transplanting device was designed to meet the narrow-spacing agronomic requirements. A simulation model of the tuber mustard transplanting system was established using multibody dynamics (MBD) and the discrete element method (DEM) to investigate the interaction mechanism among the transplanter, seedlings, and soil. Numerical simulation and kinematic analysis of the entire transplanting process were performed, with results validating the rationality of both the structural design and operational parameters. Field tests demonstrated excellent performance: the missing and injured seedling rates were only 2.5 % and 2.6 %, respectively, while the planting depth qualification rate reached 98 % and seedling uprightness was 97.3 %, resulting in an overall qualification rate of 90 %. Moreover, the average plant spacing of 130.6 mm (coefficient of variation: 3.4 %) confirmed stable device operation and conformity to narrow-spacing agronomic standards.

title: UAV-mounted electrochemical soil probing system for geospatial phosphorus mapping
