Additionally, a benchmark evaluation was conducted using state-of-the-art models, including YOLO (v5, v8, v10, v11) and RT-DETR, assessed via standard precision, recall, and F1-score metrics. Results showed that recent YOLO models (YOLOv10 and YOLOv11) achieved high detection performance, with mAP@0.5 values close to 0.892, and consistently outperform RT-DETR baselines (mAP@0.5 = 0.851) in terms of precision and inference speed. In this context, the structured design and high environmental diversity of the proposed dataset make it a valuable resource for developing and evaluating computer vision solutions in precision agriculture, including fruit ripening assessment, yield estimation, and automated harvesting.

title: Precision droplet deposition control in helicopter spraying: a novel valve-switch timing method accounting for headwind effects
abstract: Manned helicopter spraying pesticide, conducted at significant high speed and altitude, creates complex airflow (primarily involves the coupled effects of the forward-induced headwind and the rotor downwash) that disrupts pesticide droplet deposition, reducing efficiency and increasing environmental risk. This study used Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) to simulate this process and quantify the effective droplet deposition distance (DDS) during forward flight. A regression model linked this distance (DDS) to flight parameters (altitude and speed). Based on this model, a novel “delayed opening and delayed closing” valve actuation strategy was developed for pre-planned flight paths. Field trials showed this strategy increased target-area deposition by 21.07% and improved uniformity (37.78% lower variation), while significantly reducing off-target drift. By integrating droplet deposition dynamics with intelligent flight path planning, this research establishes a practical optimization framework for mitigating spray drift in manned helicopter applications. This methodology directly contributes to the advancement of precision agroforestry by enhancing the site-specific accuracy and environmental sustainability of aerial spraying operations.

title: DCS-YOLO: A blueberry maturity detection model in complex environments
abstract: Large-scale blueberry orchards still rely heavily on manual labor for fruit maturity assessment, with labor costs accounting for approximately 42% of the total production cost, which limits harvesting efficiency. Although automated harvesting technologies offer a promising solution, their effectiveness depends on accurate fruit localization and maturity classification. However, in complex blueberry agricultural environments, multi-scale distribution, dense clustering, and severe occlusion significantly increase the difficulty of object detection. To address these issues, this paper proposes DCS-YOLO, a lightweight model that achieves a balance between detection accuracy and efficiency. The proposed method can accurately identify three maturity stages of blueberries: unripe, semi-ripe, and ripe. Specifically, DCS-YOLO incorporates a multi-scale feature extraction backbone based on DBBNCSPELAN, a Channel weighted fusion module (CWFM), and a detection head enhanced by the separated and enhancement attention module (SEAM) to more effectively handle the challenges of multi-scale variations, dense distribution, and occlusion of blueberry targets in complex environments. We tested the DCS-YOLO model on a self-constructed blueberry maturity dataset containing 5567 images. Compared with YOLOv8, DCS-YOLO achieves improvements of 1.0% and 1.4% in mAP0.5 and mAP0.5:0.95, reaching 88.6% and 66.7%, respectively. Meanwhile, its number of parameters and FLOPs are reduced by 33.3% and 39.8%, and the inference speed reaches 68 frames per second, meeting real-time performance requirements. A bootstrap-based statistical significance analysis further indicates that the performance improvement of DCS-YOLO on the mAP0.5:0.95 remains stable within the 95% confidence interval (95% CI [0.87%, 1.96%]), demonstrating a consistent advantage over the baseline model and thereby validating that the proposed method can achieve stable performance gains under lightweight constraints. Moreover, DCS-YOLO outperforms other YOLO series models (YOLOv5 and YOLOv10) and classic detection models (Faster R-CNN and FCOS). In addition, DCS-YOLO can be seamlessly adapted to the latest YOLO series models (e.g., YOLOv11, YOLOv12, and YOLOv13), consistently achieving performance gains (mAP0.5:0.95 improved by approximately 0.6%–1.4%), demonstrating good generalizability. To further assess the robustness of DCS-YOLO in challenging environments, this study constructed a challenging blueberry subset for evaluation. On the challenging blueberry subset, DCS-YOLO still maintained good performance, achieving mAP0.5 and mAP0.5:0.95 scores of 88.0% and 65.1%, respectively. Additionally, we evaluated the generalization capability of DCS-YOLO on the Acfr-multifruit-2016 dataset, which features automated robotic imaging viewpoints and also presents challenges such as complex backgrounds, fruit occlusion, and scale variations. DCS-YOLO performed best in terms of accuracy among all compared models, with an mAP0.5 of 89.1%. These results demonstrate that DCS-YOLO can effectively perform blueberry maturity detection in complex environments and provide an algorithm-level reference for automated blueberry harvesting technologies.

title: UAV-prior-guided UGV path planning in ground-constrained orchards: a case study in banana plantations
abstract: UAV-prior-guided UGV path planning combines the wide-area perception capability of unmanned aerial vehicles with the execution capability of unmanned ground vehicles, offering a effective global planning solution for complex agricultural terrains. However, real-world orchards commonly contain ground constraints such as ditches, potholes, ridges, uneven terrain, and irregular row spacing. These factors tend to cause fragmented traversable areas, discontinuous path generation, and restricted maneuverability. Existing UAV-based perception and planning methods mostly focus on crop or inter-row structures, while overlooking the semantic recognition of ground constraints and their integration into the planning process. To address these challenges, this study proposes a UAV-prior-guided path planning framework that integrates ground-element perception and structure-guided optimization, and validates it in banana plantations as a representative application scenario. Unlike existing methods that only focus on crop detection, we design a multitask perception network that simultaneously performs crop center-point detection and ground-element segmentation, enabling a comprehensive geometric understanding of the planting environment. To improve path generation in unstructured geometry, we introduce a structure-guided skeleton extraction strategy that replaces traditional skeletonization with direction-aware clustering and convex-hull intersection, significantly reducing computational overhead. In addition, a unified trajectory generation strategy is developed that integrates curvature-constrained smoothing and structure-aware field entry-exit planning, enabling continuous, physically executable navigation across fragmented orchard terrains. Experimental validation demonstrates that our approach reduces turning segment curvature by 84.8% while improving computational efficiency by 3–4 orders of magnitude compared to conventional methods.

title: PigTracker: Sequential-vertices-based tracking framework for intelligent pig farming
abstract: Multi-object tracking (MOT) is essential in intelligent pig farming, playing a significant role in automated identification, behavioral analysis, and health monitoring of pigs. However, existing MOT methods for pig farming face challenges of low-accuracy and weak-generalization under occlusion, crowded and overlapping scenarios. In this work, we propose a MOT framework, namely PigTracker, for overcoming these challenges. The proposed PigTracker consists of two collaborative modules: the detection module and the tracking module. In the detection module, we propose an efficient sequential-vertices oriented bounding box (SV-OBB) detector with modulated loss function. By incorporating an attention mechanism module, our method generates orientation-aware detection boxes for individual pigs. In the tracking module, we augment the Kalman filter’s state vector with orientation information from the detection stage. Building upon this, we design a temporal-window-based outlier detection and correction mechanism, effectively rectifying false orientation originating from the detection phase. Experimental results demonstrate that our PigTracker framework achieves state-of-the-art (SOTA) performance on multi-pig tracking task under crowed environment. Our sequential-vertices orientation-aware detector achieves a Average Precision (AP50:95) of 89.0% and a Directional Mean Absolute Error (D-MAE) of 2.15° for orientation estimation. Tracking experiment attains a Higher Order Tracking Accuracy (HOTA) of 93.44%, surpassing the baseline HBB + ByteTrack (HOTA: 89.79%) by 3.65 points. In addition, the detection and tracking pig farming dataset build on this work will be publicly available for academic research, which can be accessed via https://github.com/linwjscau/PigTracker_MOT-Framework-For-Pig-Farming.git.

title: Latent diffusion meets semi-supervised learning: Enhancing plant disease detection with minimal labels
abstract: Accurate assessment of plant disease severity is essential for sustainable agriculture, but is often limited by the scarcity of annotated data. Generative models offer a promising solution by producing realistic synthetic samples that can enrich training datasets and improve model generalization. However, most existing approaches rely on large, fully labeled datasets, limiting their applicability when expert annotations are costly or difficult to obtain. This study introduces a semi-supervised latent diffusion model for the conditional generation of wheat leaf images with controllable yellow rust ( Puccinia striiformis ) disease severity. The model conditions generation on leaf segmentation masks and disease severity scores, leveraging a small labeled subset and a large set of unlabeled images. This enables the creation of realistic, severity-controllable synthetic images that effectively augment limited training datasets. Experimental results demonstrate substantial improvements in downstream regression performance, particularly under extreme annotation scarcity. Notably, when applying a per-range reduction strategy with only ten labeled images (one per disease severity bin), the baseline regression model trained exclusively on real labeled images achieved an R 2 of 0.44, whereas augmentation with semi-supervised synthetic images increased R 2 to 0.79—a gain of ＋0.35. Improvements were observed across all annotation levels, with consistent reductions in MAE and RMSE, highlighting the effectiveness of combining semi-supervised generative training with balanced sampling. These findings confirm that leveraging unlabeled data in generative diffusion models produces realistic, controllable synthetic images that enrich supervised learning. The proposed approach provides a scalable, cost-effective pathway to reduce dependence on large labeled datasets while maintaining precise control over disease severity.

title: Clustering in mixed broiler chicken batches for improvement of daily average weight
authors: Laura Emmanuella A. dos S. Santana
abstract: Flock management for industrial processing highly depends on the monitoring of their average body weight and uniformity. This paper presents a novel approach based on artificial intelligence clustering to improve the estimated average daily weight when the birds are reared together despite their sex (mixed batches), without additional hardware and based on data collected from existing scales within automatic weighing systems inside aviaries. Results from actual production cycle in 15 aviaries and 195,000 birds demonstrated that 86% of these batches reduced the Mean Absolute Error of the weight growth curve when compared to the reference weights and simple arithmetic average. Moreover, this new clustered average, used as input for the slaughter weight prediction model, reclassified 35.19% of the batches to the fully acceptable market tolerance of 2%, which refers to the difference between the actual and predicted slaughter weight. These achievements suggest that the application of even simple AI techniques brings remarkable improvement for the overall poultry processing industry.

title: Wintertime pollutant forecasting in northern sheep houses via a physics-constrained, multi-modal deep hybrid model
abstract: During winter in northern regions, the enclosed conditions of sheep houses result in poor ventilation, leading to the accumulation of pollutants, which severely impacts the health of mutton sheep. Realizing Precision Livestock Farming (PLF) necessitates high-precision forecasting models to transition management strategies from reactive responses to proactive, fine-grained interventions. To enable such proactive monitoring of the sheep house environment, this study proposes a deep hybrid model based on multi-modal fusion, FA-TMViT-XGB, for the prediction of indoor concentrations of NH3, CO2, PM2.5, and humidity specifically in enclosed sheep houses during winter. The study initially employs a sequential denoising strategy: Variational Mode Decomposition (VMD) is utilized to adaptively separate high-frequency noise from valid signal modes, followed by Kalman filtering to robustly track the underlying trend state. Subsequently, in the temporal branch, a frequency attention module is introduced to focus on low-frequency periodic components, combined with trend decomposition, periodic modulation, and a TimeMixer network to extract multi-scale temporal features. Simultaneously, the time series are encoded into two-dimensional images via Gramian Angular Fields (GAF) and Markov Transition Fields (MTF), which are then input into a Vision Transformer (ViT) to extract spatial patterns. The extracted temporal and image features are fused through a gated mechanism, optimized with a physics-constrained heuristic regularization loss, and finally fed into an XGBoost regressor to generate the concentration prediction results.In the single-step prediction of NH3 concentration, the FA-TMVIT-XGB model demonstrated superior performance, achieving a Mean Absolute Error (MAE) of 0.0270, a Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) of 0.0354, and an R2 of 0.9836 against the denoised reference trend. Crucially, robustness tests on raw sensor inputs confirmed the model’s resilience to high-frequency noise (R2>0.88). Compared to a pure Transformer model, the MAE and RMSE decreased by 73.6% and 70.8% respectively, and R2 increased by 21.8% Furthermore, multi-step forecasting experiments confirmed the model’s robustness (R2>0.9), serving as a supplementary safety buffer for risk warning. This complements the foundational single-step prediction, which satisfies the stringent precision requirements of PLF, enabling fine-grained ventilation adjustments to effectively prevent cold stress. By balancing immediate thermal stability with future air quality management, the model provides a comprehensive solution for improving flock health and production efficiency in wintertime enclosed sheep houses.

title: FENE: Fish-conditioned Expert Network using deep learning for multi-species marine distribution modeling
abstract: Accurate species distribution modeling (SDM) is essential for sustainable fisheries management and marine ecosystem conservation, particularly in environmentally heterogeneous regions such as the Mediterranean Sea. While existing SDM approaches capture aspects of non-linear relationships, spatial variability, or uncertainty, relatively few jointly model species-specific responses, geospatial structure, and predictive uncertainty within a unified multi-species framework. In this study, we propose FENE (Fish-conditioned Expert Network), a deep learning architecture that integrates environmental predictors, spatial information, and species identity for multi-species SDM. The framework combines species-conditioned feature modulation, continuous spatial encoding, and a mixture-of-experts prediction mechanism to capture heterogeneous ecological responses while producing probabilistic outputs. We evaluate the model on a public Mediterranean dataset comprising eight commercially important pelagic fish species. FENE achieves strong predictive performance (RMSE = 0.071, R2 = 0.952), outperforming commonly used machine learning baselines, including tree-based and kernel-based methods, under the same evaluation setting. Performance further improves with feature selection (RMSE = 0.060, R2 = 0.968), indicating robustness to high-dimensional environmental inputs. Beyond predictive accuracy, the model enables species-specific interpretation via feature-attribution analysis and produces spatially explicit uncertainty estimates. Higher uncertainty is observed in ecotonal and data-sparse regions, indicating reduced model confidence under environmental variability. These results demonstrate that FENE can jointly model species-specific responses and quantify predictive uncertainty within a multi-species SDM setting.

title: Multi-grouser interference effect and tractive performance of crawlers in wet-soft paddy soil based on DEM-MBD coupling
abstract: To tackle the critical issue of significant traction reduction in crawler combine harvesters due to the adhesive characteristics of wet and soft soils, optimizing grouser geometry to improve traction is crucial for enhancing trafficability in paddy fields. Although earlier research has proposed bionic inclined grouser designs based on analytical models, the microscopic interaction mechanisms and the dynamic rheological behavior of the soil have not been understood. In this research, a bidirectional coupling method that integrates the Discrete Element Method (DEM) and Multi-Body Dynamics (MBD) was utilized to systematically investigate the dynamic tractive performance of track shoes in wet-sticky paddy soil. The results indicated a notable multi-grouser interference effect: the shear failure caused by the leading grouser led to the fluidization of the soil structure, which resulted in the effective traction of the subsequent (trailing) grouser being only 14.77% of that of the leading grouser. Additionally, the influences of grouser height, spacing, and inclination angle on tractive performance were examined at the particle scale. Sensitivity analysis revealed distinct mechanisms for each parameter: an inclination angle of 30° generated a pre-compaction effect through a vertical force component, thus improving local soil shear strength; while a greater grouser height generally enhanced traction, it also increased deep soil shear resistance and intensified deep plastic flow; appropriate grouser spacing was determined as essential for minimizing the interference effect. Ultimately, an optimal parameter combination of 0.18 m spacing, 0.06 m height, and 30° inclination angle was identified, which contributed to maximum tractive efficiency while ensuring trafficability. This research clarifies the synergistic operation mechanism of multiple grousers at the scale of microscopic particles, laying a theoretical foundation for the optimal design of high-performance crawler chassis for wetland environments.

title: Autonomously estimating leaf parameters of sugarbeet plants in real agricultural environments
abstract: Our society needs food, feed, and fiber which stems in large part from agricultural crop production. Producing these for a growing world population in a sustainable manner and reducing the side-effects of agricultural production processes on the environment is a key challenge for a future-oriented society. A possible solution for tackling this challenge is the breeding of novel varieties that are more resistant to plant diseases and thus require less agrochemicals, but also produce more yield at the same time. For selection of promising varieties, breeders need to assess the development of the plants regularly, this process is called phenotyping. Until today, this is mainly performed manually by well-trained experts in a process that is very time-consuming, costly and often invasive. In this work, we propose a novel robotic approach to measure phenotypic traits in an objective, non-invasive, and repeatable manner on real sugar beet fields. For this purpose, we exploit point clouds of leaves, which are then used to fit a parametric mesh template. Using such a template model has several advantages for parameter estimation. Given the fitted template, we then can extract multiple key phenotypic leaf traits, such as leaf blade length, width and petiole length. We evaluate our approach on data from a greenhouse and real agricultural fields containing sugar beets. Our experimental evaluation shows superior accuracy compared to existing approaches, paving the way for more accurate automatic trait detection for improved breeding performance for a faster development of resistant, high-yielding varieties. • Phenotypic trait estimation in the field can be performed by fitting a leaf model. • A triangle mesh as leaf model models the thin structures well. • Using a prior leaf model makes the system robust to noise in the data. • The approach works well on data collected in densely planted crop fields. • The method presents good performance also on low resolution data.

title: A free-space method for microwave measurement of bulk crop dielectric properties in-situ
abstract: Radar is a sensing solution that can combat the durability and visibility issues contact sensing and camera sensing methods face in agricultural settings. To efficiently engineer radar systems in agriculture, the dielectric properties of the medium of propagation need to be known. Often, the propagation medium is a mixture of air and crop. This paper proposes a method for measuring the effective dielectric permittivity of this air–crop material mixture in-situ. The proposed method uses a Gate-Reflect-Line (GRL) free space calibration technique to move the reference planes to the plane of the crop material. This calibration technique allows for a rigid measurement structure, which decreases the variability from changing the distance between the measurement antennas, and decreases the test apparatus susceptibility to adverse environmental conditions, such as wind. Simulation software was used to validate the method against a known material, High Density Polyethylene (HDPE), and to characterize the sensitivity of the method to experimental error. A Vector Network Analyzer (VNA) was used to implement the proposed method to make free space dielectric measurements, first of HDPE, with a known dielectric permittivity, then of an arrangement of corn stalks with unknown permittivity. The method was accurate on the HDPE sample, both in simulation and in lab measurements. The method also gave reasonable data for the arrangement of corn stalks measured. The work presented here will allow for further data collection in-crop at various growth stages and environmental conditions, which will drive the creation of a library of dielectric measurements for crop material.

title: Effect of maize seed posture on filling performance of a positive-pressure pneumatic seed-metering device with irregular seed-holes
abstract: High-speed maize sowing often leads to reduced filling stability in pneumatic seed-metering devices. To address this issue, this study systematically investigates the mechanisms by which seed posture influences filling performance and proposes an optimized stepped seed-hole structure. By analyzing the mechanical behavior of maize seeds during the filling process, a flow-confinement strategy was introduced to enhance the attachment stability of seed postures that are prone to detachment. A computational fluid dynamics (CFD) model of a positive-pressure seed-metering device was established to examine the coupled effects of seed-hole geometry, seed posture, operating pressure, and forward speed. In addition, high-speed imaging experiments were conducted to quantify seed posture distributions under different structural configurations, enabling the determination of optimal operating parameters. The results show that optimization of the stepped seed-hole structure significantly increases the aerodynamic drag acting on seeds in unstable postures, thereby reducing both missed and multiple seeding events. After optimization, the qualified index exceeded 99.3% within a forward speed range of 8–12 km/h and remained above 97% under higher-speed conditions of 12–16 km/h. By incorporating the influence of seed posture on filling behavior into the structural optimization of the seed-metering device, this study provides a novel design approach for irregular seed-hole configurations and offers technical support for improving the operational stability of pneumatic seed-metering systems under high-speed conditions.

title: Design and experimental study of a seed potato cutting machine and its machine vision-based defective tuber removal system
abstract: To address the low efficiency of manual cutting in potato seed-tuber preparation and the high blind-eye rate and unstable quality associated with conventional mechanical cutting, this study designed a potato seed-tuber operation machine integrating cutting and seed-piece sorting. The machine innovatively combines mechanical centering-based cutting with online machine-vision sorting to establish an integrated operation mode, and its key structural parameters were determined. Automatic long-axis alignment and precise longitudinal cutting of seed tubers were achieved through differential-speed arrangement using a tapered roller set and a low-damage, high-speed disc-knife sliding-cutting technique. With a closed-loop system consisting of machine-vision sensing and pneumatic actuation, sprout-eye features were identified and unqualified seed pieces were rejected in real time. The prototype mainly comprises a feeding and elevating unit, an arranging and positioning unit, a longitudinal cutting unit, a single-row sorting unit, a vision recognition system, and an air-jet sorting unit, enabling coordinated operation between the orienting and conveying system, and the vision-based logical control system. To validate its performance, full-process prototype experiments were conducted using seed tubers weighing 60–120 g. Cutting capacity, qualified rate, blind-eye rate, and sprout-eye recognition accuracy were used as evaluation indices. The results showed that, under the regulation of the intelligent control system, the units operated cooperatively to sequentially accomplish feeding and arranging, oriented cutting, and online sorting. The machine operated stably, achieving an average cutting capacity of 8.56 kg/min, a qualified rate of 92.56%, a blind-eye rate of 3.24%, and a sprout-eye recognition accuracy of 91.42%. All indices met the agronomic requirements for potato seed-tuber processing. The proposed machine provides an effective mechanized solution for potato seed-tuber cutting and sorting, contributing to improved productivity and operational quality.

title: A novel circle-fitting algorithm combined with a height-diameter pair selection method improves the tree trunk volume estimation from terrestrial laser scanning
abstract: The shape of tree trunks and their volume are fundamental components of forest inventory systems, serving both commercial and ecological purposes. Terrestrial Laser Scanning (TLS) offers three-dimensional coordinate data regarding the tree surface, facilitating the non-destructive extraction of trunk volume. One of the existing approaches assumes that the cross-sectional shape of tree trunks is circular, where the circle-fitting algorithm and the height-diameter pair selection method (HDPSM) are critical steps. This study evaluated the performance of six combinations, formed by three circle-fitting algorithms – algebraic circle-fitting (A1), the extended Random Sample Consensus circle-fitting (A2), and the proposed circle-fitting (A3) paired with two HDPSMs – the proposed HDPSM (M1) and the existing HDPSM (M2), for trunk volume estimation from individual tree point clouds. The proposed circle-fitting algorithm (A3) modified the Random Sample Consensus framework by replacing the count of inliers with an inlier-derived value, with the aim of enhancing the ability to detect circular arcs. The proposed HDPSM was designed to deal with highly disorganized height-diameter pairs. The results showed that the proposed combination A3-M1 yielded the best performance in total trunk volume estimation, with 0.059 m3 of RMSE and 0.013 m3 of bias. This combination performed well on large trees, achieving 0.057 m3 of RMSE and 0.002 m3 of bias.
keywords: DBSCAN (Density-Based Spatial Clustering of Applications with Noise)

title: Video-level beef cattle weight estimation based on RGB-D sequences via Cross-Modal Spatial Registration and Frame Quality Refinement
abstract: Non-contact weight estimation of beef cattle is crucial for reducing animal stress and determining optimal slaughter timing in cattle farm production management. Existing approaches primarily rely on frame-level inputs, rendering them highly susceptible to low-quality data often encountered in complex farm environments, leading to significant estimation errors. This study proposes a video-level beef cattle weight estimation method based on RGB-D sequences. Firstly, two video encoders extract texture and geometric features from RGB sequences and HHA sequences, where the latter are geocentric encodings of depth maps. Secondly, a Cross-Modal Spatial Registration (CMSR) module is designed to spatially align these heterogeneous features. Subsequently, a DeMamba block captures spatial–temporal relationships and a Frame Quality Refinement (FQR) mechanism is developed to adaptively mitigate the impact of low-quality frames. Finally, cattle weight is estimated using a regression head optimized by a joint loss function that incorporates both regression and ranking losses to distinguish fine-grained weight differences. To evaluate the proposed method, a comprehensive dataset was established, comprising 3787 video segments from 75 beef cattle across four breeds, with body weights ranging from 218 kg to 822 kg. The proposed method achieves competitive accuracy across diverse breeds and growth stages, with an MAE of 17.126 kg, RMSE of 21.258 kg, MAPE of 3.341%, and R2 of 0.976. The robustness against low-quality data further validates the effectiveness of the proposed method for accurate and reliable beef cattle weight estimation, providing a practical solution for precision livestock farming. The dataset is available at https://github.com/IPCLab-NEAU/Beef-Cattle-Weight-Estimation.

title: HEDSPose: pigeon pose estimation in cage environments via hierarchical edge fusion and spatial-aware confidence calibration
abstract: Automated pose estimation is essential for precision livestock farming, providing the foundational technical capability for non-invasive behavioral monitoring that underpins downstream applications such as early disease detection and welfare assessment in commercial operations. However, existing pose estimation methods face significant challenges when applied to caged pigeon environments, struggling with complex visual interference from wire mesh structures, severe inter-individual occlusion in densely populated cages, and the visual homogeneity of commercially dominant white-feathered pigeons that severely degrade keypoint localization accuracy. To address these challenges, we propose HEDSPose, a specialized pose estimation framework whose primary contribution is robust keypoint localization under cage-induced visual noise, providing the accurate skeletal representations required for downstream health monitoring and disease screening in precision pigeon farming. This objective is achieved through four targeted technical innovations: a Hierarchical Edge Fusion (HEF) module for anatomical boundary enhancement with simultaneous cage mesh noise suppression; an ADown module for fine-grained feature preservation through frequency-selective downsampling; a Dual-Path Enhancement Fusion (DPEF) module for adaptive cross-level feature integration balancing local detail with global context; and the Spatial-Aware Keypoint Enhancer (SAKE) for confidence calibration against false detections caused by appearance uniformity. The experimental results demonstrate that HEDSPose achieves competitive performance with 94.0% mAP50 and 75.8% mAP50–95 representing improvements of 4.3% and 3.5% over the YOLO11s baseline respectively, while maintaining computational efficiency at 22.8 GFLOPs and 10.6 MB parameters. Cross-species validation on challenging pig pose datasets confirms robust generalization capabilities, providing an efficient and reliable solution for automated health monitoring in precision farming applications.

title: A structural and growth-constrained framework for individual-tree parameter extraction in complex forest environments
abstract: Accurate extraction of individual trees and structural attributes is crucial for assessing forest carbon stocks, ecosystem functions, biodiversity conservation, and sustainable forest management. Key individual-tree parameters, such as tree position, height, and diameter at breast height (DBH), are central to modern forest inventories. Mobile Laser Scanning (MLS) offers flexible and detailed understory measurements but remains challenged by understory occlusion, branch/leaf adhesion, and crown overlap, limiting the adaptability of existing methods. This study proposes a new MLS-based framework for individual-tree parameter extraction that integrates structural-feature-guided branch/leaf filtering and growth-oriented region growing. First, trunk–branch/leaf separation and trunk region identification were achieved using local density patterns and geometric regularity to suppress vegetation and adhesion interference. Second, trunk-based directional constraints and filtering rules derived from vertical growth characteristics guided region growing with adaptive thresholds and progressive optimization, enabling accurate segmentation of adhered trees. A reconstruction step was then applied to recover complete trunk and crown point clouds. The framework was validated on four public datasets and one self-acquired dataset (48 plots, 2,632 trees) spanning diverse forest structures. Results showed high performance, with F1-score of 0.95–0.99, Recall of 0.93–1.00, and Precision of 0.96–0.99. Height estimation achieved RMSE < 1 m ( R 2 up to 0.99) in some area, and DBH estimation achieved RMSE < 2 cm ( R 2 up to 0.95). Comparative analyses confirmed improvements over existing approaches, demonstrating enhanced generalization and interpretability. The method thus provides a reliable MLS-based solution for extracting tree location, height, and DBH in complex forest environments, supporting large-scale forest monitoring.

title: Recognition of sheep breed containing hybrid samples based on CSM-YOLO26m model
abstract: Automatic recognition of sheep breeds is essential for farmers to cultivate high-quality breeds, prevent and treat diseases, and monitor welfare. Modern farms raise large numbers of hybrid sheep in addition to local and introduced breeds, which makes breed recognition more challenging owing to the high degree of phenotypic similarity between hybrid breeds and their parent or maternal breeds. To address this problem, we added two hybrid breeds to the original sheep face dataset (SheepBreeds), which contains 10 breeds, creating an enhanced dataset called SheepBreeds2.0. The expanded dataset increases breed diversity and better reflects actual production conditions. We proposed a sheep breed recognition model, CSM-YOLO26m, which introduces an interclass similarity matrix to represent the degree of similarity among breeds. The matrix was weighted and fused with the hard breed labels of YOLO26m to generate soft labels for target breeds. A progressive learning strategy was employed to optimize the loss function of the YOLO26m network, thereby reducing the learning difficulty associated with distinguishing highly similar breeds. Experimental results show that CSM-YOLO26m achieved 97.75% precision and 96.60% mAP@[0.5:0.95] on SheepBreeds2.0. Moreover, integrating CSM into different YOLO families and model scales (YOLOv5/YOLOv7/YOLOv9/YOLOv11/YOLO26) consistently increased precision, recall, and mAP, demonstrating strong cross-model generalization. Considering both recognition performance and computational cost, CSM-YOLO26m requires only 20.4 M parameters and 68.2G FLOPs, and achieves an inference throughput of approximately 13 FPS on the RK3588 platform with a 640 × 640 input, balancing precision and real-time performance and demonstrating strong robustness and practical deployment value.

title: Hyperspectral response and quantitative monitoring of soil organic carbon on the Loess Plateau
abstract: The accurate estimation of soil organic carbon (SOC) is crucial for effective soil resource management, improvement agricultural productivity, and mitigating climate change. To investigate the hyperspectral response mechanisms of SOC and its influencing factors, this study was conducted based on a long-term conservation tillage experiment in a winter wheat field. Soil samples were collected from a depth of 0–60 cm during 2020–2023. Hyperspectral data were analyzed using multiple preprocessing and feature selection techniques, and prediction models for SOC and its influencing factors were constructed. The quantitative relationships between different transformed spectra and SOC, as well as its influencing factors, were determined. The optimal spectral features for SOC and its influencing factors were identified. Based on the response of SOC content to its stabilization mechanisms, the optimal spectral features of influencing factors were reorganized to form new characteristic wavelength combinations. These combinations were further used to develop an indirect spectral model for SOC prediction. This approach enabled the identification of the spectral response mechanisms of SOC stabilization processes. The results indicated that spectral reflectance was inversely correlated with SOC, GSSI (general soil structure index), Dm (fractal dimension of mechanical aggregates), MI-OC (microaggregate organic carbon), and SSA (soil sucrase activity). The characteristic regions for SOC were primarily distributed at 400–430 nm, 675–691 nm, and 713–754 nm. These regions were primarily located within the visible spectrum and did not overlap with the optimal characteristic wavelengths of its influencing factors. In the direct modeling of SOC, the optimal preprocessing and wavelength selection methods were the 1st-order differentiation and SBS (sequential backward selection), respectively. RF (random forest) was identified as the most effective modeling method (R v 2 = 0.69, RMSE v = 0.32, MAE v = 0.25). In the spectral estimation methods for SOC influencing factors, the 1st-order differentiation was the optimal preprocessing method, and RF demonstrated superior performance as the modeling approach. The spectral response effects of SSA, GSSI, mechanical aggregate parameters, and FSP-OC (total Organic Carbon of Free Silt and clay Particles) were higher than those of SOC. The indirect model for SOC constructed from the optimal combination of characteristic wavelengths of its influencing factors exhibited higher accuracy (R v 2 = 0.74, RMSE v = 0.27, MAE v = 0.21) than the direct model. SOC sequestration was influenced by the combined effects of multiple soil factors rather than a single indicator. The results confirm the feasibility of hyperspectral SOC monitoring and support its application in rapid soil fertility assessment.

title: Detection of tea heat stress in UAV multi-spectral remote sensing images based on spatial-frequency two stream network
abstract: Accurate detection of tea heat stress (THS) using uncrewed aerial vehicle (UAV) multi-spectral remote sensing images combined with deep learning techniques is crucial for THS management. However, most existing multi-spectral image fusion detection networks lack robustness in complex scenes and perform poorly in small-target feature extraction, leading to low detection accuracy. To address these issues, a spatial-frequency two-stream network (SFTNet) is proposed. It employs spatial feature extraction (SFE) and frequency feature extraction (FFE) branches to extract high-resolution spatial details from RGB images and rich frequency-domain features from NIR images, respectively. A feature enhancement structure with multiple attention mechanisms and channel interaction was designed at the output end of the FFE branch to effectively aggregate shallow and deep semantic information from the hierarchically aggregated feature maps. For multi-scale feature fusion, a multi-spectral spatial-frequency feature fusion (MSFF) module is developed to achieve tight alignment and integration of RGB and NIR features. To improve small target detection, a multiscale cross-attention aggregation (MCA) module has been proposed. By extracting fine-grained horizontal and vertical features while incorporating a cross-fusion strategy, the MCA module enhances SFTNet’s learning of small target THS features, thereby improving detection accuracy for small target THS. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed SFTNet outperforms state-of-the-art networks across 4 m, 6 m, and 8 m datasets, achieving mAP@50 improvements of 5.9%, 7.7%, and 4.6% respectively. Furthermore, when evaluated on terminal devices in a non-deployment testing setup, SFTNet achieves an inference speed of 15.3 ms per RGB-NIR image pair, suggesting high computational efficiency under these specific conditions.

title: UAV-based crop pest and disease monitoring: A review of multi-source sensing and intelligent methods
abstract: Crop pests and diseases represent persistent threats to global food security, necessitating efficient and precise monitoring solutions. Utilizing a dataset comprising 7,445 publications spanning 2008–2025, this study conducts a comprehensive bibliometric and thematic analysis to elucidate the synergistic evolution of multi-source sensing and intelligent methods for unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV)-based crop pest and disease monitoring. Results identify a three-stage developmental trajectory, progressing from initial platform validation to sensor-algorithm co-development, and subsequently to system-integrated intelligent monitoring. Analysis further demonstrates that crop structural characteristics constitute a fundamental determinant in shaping monitoring paradigms; structural variations ranging from discrete orchard canopies to continuous field crop systems directly influence the definition of observation units and the selection of analytical strategies, thereby leading to differentiated methodological pathways. From a technological perspective, research has transitioned from reliance on single-source red–green–blue (RGB) imagery to multimodal frameworks integrating multispectral, hyperspectral, thermal infrared (TIR), and light detection and ranging (LiDAR) data. Concurrently, methodological development has evolved from conventional machine learning (ML) to deployment-oriented deep learning (DL) and vision-language models (VLMs). Furthermore, increasing attention is directed toward prescription-map-driven closed-loop frameworks, where diagnostic outputs are translated into spatially explicit intervention strategies for variable-rate application. Despite these advances, challenges persist in model generalization, dataset bias, and cross-platform standardization. This study provides a structured perspective for the development of scalable, physiologically-aware, and structure-aware intelligent monitoring solutions, contributing to the advancement of precision agriculture.

title: In-situ 3D reconstruction and analysis of droplet motion characteristics in downwash flow of multi-rotor UAV
abstract: Precise pesticide application using unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) in unstructured orchards requires accurate characterization of droplet deposition and drift states. However, complex outdoor lighting conditions and strong rotor downwash interference pose notable challenges. Therefore, continuous in situ monitoring and analysis of fine droplet motion remain difficult in smart agriculture. To address these challenges, this study proposes a three-dimensional dynamic perception and visualization system based on light detection and ranging. First, a dual-UAV collaborative data acquisition strategy is employed, and an autonomous perception platform is established for dynamic droplet monitoring. Second, deep learning semantic segmentation is integrated with point cloud voxelization. This achieves precise extraction and preprocessing of droplet point clouds against complex backgrounds. Finally, a local optical flow estimation algorithm is applied to invert and analyze the microscopic motion field of droplet groups. The proposed method is evaluated in a real-world orchard scenario. Experimental results indicate the successful development of a comprehensive visualization framework spanning field data acquisition to microscopic motion analysis. The model demonstrates favorable performance in terms of training loss, intersection over union, and accuracy metrics. Furthermore, the dynamic characteristics of droplet flow fields under different operational heights and velocities (e.g., 1.5 and 2.5 m/s) are effectively resolved. Overall, this study achieves a synergistic integration of robust field perception and high-precision droplet dynamics inversion. A valid end-to-end solution is provided for evaluating UAV spraying effectiveness and optimizing operational parameters.

title: Centralized and vertical federated learning for Climate-Based crop yield prediction
abstract: Accurate crop yield assessment is critical for food security planning and climate impact analysis, yet centralized machine learning approaches are increasingly constrained by data privacy requirements and institutional fragmentation. Climate variables, crop model simulations, and yield data are often distributed across organizations, making centralized data integration impractical. This study evaluates federated learning as a privacy-preserving alternative for large-scale crop yield modeling by systematically comparing Centralized Federated Learning (CFL) and Vertical Federated Learning (VFL). Using Ethiopia as a case study, we integrate ERA5 climate variables with maize and wheat yield simulations from the LPJmL and DSSAT models under irrigated and rainfed conditions. While CFL assumes centralized access to all features and labels, VFL employs a split neural network in which data remain at separate institutions and only latent representations are exchanged. Results show that CFL achieves the highest predictive accuracy (R 2 = 0.88–0.91), while VFL exhibits a modest performance reduction (R 2 = 0.765–0.897) but maintains stable convergence and minimal train–test divergence. Validation against FAO yield statistics over a 15-year period confirms that both approaches capture interannual variability and long-term trends. This work provides the first systematic empirical comparison of CFL and VFL for climate-driven crop yield modeling and demonstrates that vertical federated learning can deliver reliable predictions under realistic data-governance constraints, thereby enabling privacy-preserving agricultural yield assessment at scale.

title: Deformable transformer framework for automated calf respiratory health scoring
abstract: • Developed a deformable transformer framework for calf respiratory health scoring. • Evaluated model on real-farm images across ocular, nasal, and ear indicators. • Built a dataset of 5,374 annotated frames from 100 Holstein calves. • Verified interpretability through Grad-CAM visualization of key facial regions. Respiratory diseases significantly impact calf health, welfare, and productivity. Traditional health evaluations rely on subjective human observation, leading to inconsistent diagnoses and scalability challenges in large herds and group housing systems. This study proposes a computer vision framework that automates visual health scoring of calves using images captured by mobile devices under natural farm conditions. The model focuses on key phenotypic indicators—ocular discharge, nasal discharge, and ear posture—associated with bovine respiratory disease. A vision transformer-based architecture was developed, incorporating a Swin Transformer backbone for multi-scale feature extraction, a deformable attention encoder for spatial adaptability, and a query-based decoder to perform 4-class classification aligned with standard scoring guidelines. A dataset of 5374 annotated frames from 100 Holstein calves was collected and labelled by three trained individuals using a standardized 4-point respiratory health scoring system. Evaluation on field-collected data achieved strong performance on the ocular task (Precision: 0.87, Recall: 0.85, F1-score: 0.86), nasal task (Precision: 0.86, Recall: 0.89, F1-score: 0.88), and ear posture task (Precision: 0.75, Recall: 0.90, F1-score: 0.82). Comparative analysis with baseline architectures confirmed the superiority of our method particularly in handling subtle variations in mild and moderate symptoms. Grad-CAM visualizations revealed that the model attends to biologically relevant regions. Additionally, an annotation consistency analysis was conducted and found that inter-annotator agreement significantly influenced model performance, especially in ambiguous scoring cases. These findings highlight the importance of standardized annotation protocols for model generalizability. This work contributes a scalable, non-invasive solution for early respiratory disease monitoring in calves, with potential to improve health outcomes and increase labor efficiency.

title: Quantifying the light interception and canopy photosynthesis of strip intercropping system based on 3D canopy photosynthesis model
abstract: Strip intercropping systems (SIs) improves grain yield through enhanced canopy light interception (LI) and radiation-use efficiency, but structural and physiological heterogeneity caused by configurations that complicates light-use mechanisms. Precise quantification of LI and canopy photosynthesis (Ac) is essential for configuration design and yield improvement. We developed a three-dimensional canopy photosynthesis model (3D-CPM) integrating ray-tracing algorithms, leaf-level light-response functions, and leaf-azimuth angle parameter to simulates LI and Ac of soybean-maize SIs with different strip width configurations. The model was verified its high accuracy in 3D structure reconstruction by measured leaf area and plant height of two crops. Based on that, the LI and Ac of soybean-maize SIs in spatial–temporal heterogeneity were been quantified. Our results showed that Ac was enhanced in SIs relative to the corresponding sole-cropping combination, with the Ac equivalence index reaching up to 4.35 in M2S2 and 4.03 in M2S4, indicating that the intercropping advantage was mainly driven by enhanced maize Ac associated with border-row advantages. Maize Ac depended more on the within-canopy distribution of photosynthetically active radiation rather than on total LI, whereas soybean Ac was more closely depended to total LI. Maize predominantly intercepted direct radiation in the upper canopy, and Ac peaked in the morning and afternoon due mainly to enhanced photosynthesis in wide rows. By contrast, soybean, mainly captured diffuse light in the lower canopy, with LI and Ac peaking at midday. These complementary patterns formed a spatiotemporal light-use synergy that enhanced system-level Ac. Strip-width impacts on diurnal LI and Ac patterns are minimized under conditions dominated by diffuse radiation. Integrating distinct photosynthetic parameters for wide- and narrow-row maize and for each soybean row allows the model to capture canopy heterogeneity in LI and Ac; this row-specific integration underpins its spatially explicit simulations. This study provides a novel modeling tool for accurate assess of photosynthetic processes and a theoretical foundation for understanding the high efficiency utilization mechanism of SIs, which laying a technical foundation for climate-smart, resource-efficient cropping strategies.

title: KDYOLO-Tracker: A Deep Learning Approach to Behavior Recognition and Tracking for Sika Deer
abstract: Accurate recognition and tracking of basic behaviors are key to intelligent health monitoring for sika deer farming. To solve the problems that the current object recognition algorithms have low recognition real-time and low accuracy of identity association caused by the diversity of deer farming environments and the rapid movement speed of sika deer, this research proposes an efficient sika deer behavior recognition approach KDYOLO and a tracking approach MO-Tracking, and constructs a multi-object behavior recognition and tracking method KDYOLO-Tracker. First, a sparse training mechanism is proposed which introduces a scaling factor in the batch normalization layer to adaptively screen and remove unimportant channels, so that the computational efficiency of the model is effectively improved. Second, this paper proposes to integrate the channel pruning algorithm into the KDYOLO to further reduce model size and computation, while the pruned model is fine-tuned by adjusting the learning rate and parameters to mitigate potential accuracy losses. In addition, this paper proposes a multi-object tracking algorithm MO-Tracking, which enhances the matching space for trajectory by expanding the detection buffer, to improve the accuracy of trajectory association. The proposed KDYOLO recognition algorithm is embedded into the MO-Tracking to construct the KDYOLO-Tracker tracking model, so that the performances of recognition and tracking are further improved. The experimental results show: compared with YOLOv8l, the proposed KDYOLO not only improves the detection accuracy but also reduces the model complexity (GFLOPs, parameters, and size) by more than 58%, among which GFLOPs are reduced by 71.66%; the mAP@0.5 and mAP@0.5:0.95 of KDYOLO reach 97.20% and 85.90%, respectively. Compared with mainstream algorithms of SSD, Faster R-CNN, and different versions of YOLO, KDYOLO consistently maintains the highest accuracy, with mAP@0.5 increased by up to 17.05% and mAP@0.5:0.95 increased by up to 31.46%. In terms of tracking performance, the HOTA, MOTA, MOTP, and IDF1 of KDYOLO-Tracker reach 85.70%, 88.30%, 93.60%, and 90.30%, respectively, which are all the highest compared with those of the five multi-object tracking algorithms DeepSort, ByteTrack, DeepMot, BotSort, and MO-Tracking. In addition, the detection speed of KDYOLO-Tracker has reached 108FPS, an increase of 19FPS compared with that without improvement. This research provides the technical support for monitoring the health status and alerting for abnormal behavior of livestock farming animals.

title: Mango Expert: a harvest-optimizing wearable decision support system based on multimodal optoelectronic fusion and graph temporal neural networks
abstract: As a tropical cash crop, the precise quality assessment of mangoes directly determines optimal harvest timing and supply chain efficiency. Premature harvesting results in insufficient flavor, while delayed harvesting leads to spoilage and decay. Traditional manual or static imaging methods suffer from high subjectivity and inability to capture the dynamic ripening process. To address this, we propose Mango Expert, an intelligent decision-support system integrating visible/near-infrared spectroscopy and impedance sensing via a flexible optoelectronic sensor network. The system combines EfficientNet-B1 for image feature extraction, a BiLSTM model with positional encoding for temporal modeling, and a Graph Attention Network (GAT) to dynamically model inter-fruit relationships. By fusing spectral and impedance data, our approach overcomes limitations of unimodal methods, achieving 98.54% classification accuracy, outperforming state-of-the-art techniques. Key innovations include adaptive graph construction and time-continuous batch sampling, which preserve biological correlations and enhance robustness. Deployed in real-world harvesting, the system reduces labor costs by 60% and increases premium fruit value by 20–30%. The system developed in this study demonstrates clear application value in precision fruit harvesting, providing a key tool for the fine-grained harvest decision-making in smart agriculture.

title: Research on an automated detection for sheep estrus based on multimodal fusion of thermal images and sensor data
abstract: Estrus monitoring is essential for improving reproductive efficiency and optimizing artificial insemination timing in ewes. However, existing studies mainly focus on binary estrus detection and often rely on wearable sensors, invasive physiological measurements, or vision-based behavioral analysis methods, which are insufficient for fine-grained estrus stage discrimination and are limited by animal stress, high deployment cost, and sensitivity to farm environmental disturbances. To address these limitations, this study proposes a non-contact multimodal framework for classifying ewe estrus stages into diestrus, estrus, and metestrus. Thermal infrared features were extracted using an improved ResNet18 incorporating initial convolution (INC), squeeze-and-excitation (SE), and multi-scale fusion (MSF) modules, denoted as INC-SE-MSF-ResNet18. In parallel, bilateral eye temperature features and environmental temperature and humidity features were extracted by multilayer perceptron (MLP)-based eye temperature feature extractor and MLP-based environmental variable feature extractor. These three types of features were then concatenated into a multimodal feature and classified using a Light Gradient Boosting Machine (LightGBM). Under the same LightGBM classifier, INC-SE-MSF-ResNet18 generated more discriminative thermal infrared features than ResNet18, MobileNetv3, EfficientNet, ShuffleNet, and DenseNet, yielding improvements of up to 15.10% in recall, 7.67% in F1-score, and 3.10% in accuracy. Under the same feature extraction and fusion strategy, LightGBM consistently outperformed support vector machine (SVM), eXtreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), gradient boosting decision tree (GBDT), random forest (RF), decision tree (DT), logistic regression (LR), and convolutional neural network (CNN) across all estrus stages, with precision improvements of up to 21.23% over CNN, 13.17% over DT, and 11.11% over RF. Temperature analysis further revealed clear stage-dependent divergence between bilateral eye temperatures and rectal temperature (RT). The bilateral eye temperatures peaked during estrus, whereas rectal temperature decreased during estrus and increased markedly during metestrus. These results indicate that surface and core temperatures reflect different physiological processes and exhibit unsynchronized temporal dynamics across the estrous cycle. Overall, this study extends infrared thermography-based ewe estrus monitoring from conventional binary detection to protocol-defined estrus stage classification, providing a feasible approach for ovulation timing inference and precision reproductive management in large-scale sheep farming systems.

title: Energy-Saving performance of Kalman filtering and artificial neural network algorithm for axle torque and battery SOC estimation of electric tractor using AMESim model
abstract: Electric tractors operate under highly variable soil resistance conditions during tillage, which induces rapid axle torque fluctuations and increases battery energy consumption when conventional motor controllers respond rely solely on delayed feedback. This study evaluated the energy-saving performance of a filtering-algorithm-integrated proportional–integral–derivative (PID) motor speed controller for a 19 kW single-motor electric tractor during plow tillage across three gear stages (L-2500, L-2800, and M−2000). For this, a one-dimensional electric tractor simulation model was developed in AMESim, incorporating motor torque–speed–voltage characteristics, efficiency maps, drivetrain components, and field-measured tillage load datasets. A Kalman Filter Algorithm (KFA) was integrated into the PID control framework to estimate axle torque and battery state of charge (SOC) in real time, and its performance was compared with an artificial neural network (ANN)-based estimator and a conventional PID controller without predictive filtering. Simulation results revealed that the KFA-integrated controller improved torque-estimation accuracy, suppressed transient overshoot, and stabilized motor-current response under dynamically varying field loads. Relative to the ANN and conventional PID controllers, the KFA-based controller maintained motor operation closer to the high-efficiency region and reduced battery energy consumption by approximately 0.38%, 0.42%, and 0.53% at L-2500, L-2800, and M−2000, respectively. These findings affirm that KFA-based predictive workload estimation enhances control stability and energy efficiency across gear stages, supporting the applicability of the proposed controller for next-generation electric tractors under energy-intensive tillage conditions.

title: Portable moisture-robust VNIR system integrating a PEPO algorithm for rapeseed chlorophyll quantification
abstract: Chlorophyll content is a critical determinant of rapeseed quality, significantly influencing the processing efficiency and oxidative stability of the resulting oil. However, moisture fluctuations during the harvest-to-processing cycle interfere with visible near-infrared spectroscopy, as moisture-induced spectral variance overlaps with chlorophyll spectral features. This study developed, a portable detection device for rapeseed analysis, and a partial external parameter orthogonalization (PEPO) method was implemented to reduce moisture interference. Compared to full-spectrum correction, PEPO uses a partial correlation analysis to calibrate moisture-sensitive wavelengths, aiming to retain target-specific spectral information. A comparison of machine learning architectures showed that an artificial neural network (ANN) combined with PEPO resulted in the highest predictive performance among the tested models. The model yielded a coefficient of determination in the prediction set of 0.891 and a root mean square error of prediction of 2.7 mg/kg. Relative to standard full-spectrum correction, the proposed approach reduced the performance gap between calibration and prediction sets, indicating improved model generalization. This study not only provides a technical basis for the rapid and non-destructive detection of rapeseed chlorophyll content but also offers an effective correction approach for the spectral analysis of complex agricultural materials susceptible to moisture interference.

title: Lightweight YOLOv11n model for efficient and accurate residual-film detection in cotton fields of arid regions
abstract: Persistent accumulation of residual plastic film (RPF), especially visible sheet-like RPF, in cotton fields of arid regions poses a critical challenge to sustainable cotton production. Image-based recognition offers an efficient approach for rapid monitoring and precise recovery of RPF. However, complex backgrounds, varying illumination, and blurred fragment edges limit the accuracy and efficiency of traditional detection methods. This study focuses on visible sheet-like RPF in arid-region cotton fields, constructs a field image dataset collected under different illumination and soil-background conditions, and develops a lightweight improved model based on YOLOv11n. Specifically, a PPLCNet-based lightweight backbone is used to replace the original feature-extraction structure, and CBAM is inserted after the SPPF module to enhance channel-spatial attention. In addition, an improved SimAM attention mechanism strengthens noise suppression and target-focused learning. An improved MPDIoU loss function is introduced for bounding-box regression to improve localization accuracy and training stability for irregular fragments. Experimental results show that the improved model achieves precision, recall, and mAP50 of 97.56%, 98.62%, and 99.38%, representing increases of 4.41%, 8.14%, and 3.19% over the original YOLOv11n. The model outperforms mainstream lightweight models, including YOLOv5n, YOLOv8n, and YOLOv10n, while maintaining only 2.14 M parameters and 5.07 GFLOPs. Deployment on a Jetson Nano achieves an average detection response time of approximately 2.07 s, indicating its potential for low-power field deployment and periodic detection on agricultural machinery. The main novelty of this work lies in a coordinated perception-attention-localization optimization strategy for lightweight RPF detection, providing a practical basis for intelligent monitoring and mechanized recovery of visible sheet-like RPF in arid-region cotton fields.

title: Multi-source remote sensing of banana LAI across full growth cycle using canopy spectral-morphological features and temporal Transformer-LSTM
abstract: Accurate estimating of banana leaf area index (LAI) is essential for growth monitoring and yield assessment, yet dense canopy three-dimension (3D) structure and temporal dynamics challenge remote sensing approaches. We propose a banana LAI estimation method based on multi-source remote sensing data fusion and a Transformer-LSTM temporal deep learning model. We develop a Regional Volume (RV) metric, a refined morphological parameter that excludes the void space beneath the dense banana canopy. Vegetation indices (VIs), texture features (TFs), and canopy morphological parameters (CMPs) are extracted from UAV multispectral imagery and terrestrial LiDAR point clouds. The hybrid Transformer-LSTM model was developed for banana LAI estimation throughout the eight growth stages, based on VIs, TFs, CMPs and their combinations. The results demonstrate the superior capability of the proposed RV metric over the conventional canopy height volume (CV) for LAI estimation, improving the testing R2 by over 0.14 to 0.878 with an RMSE of 0.72. Meanwhile, the Transformer-LSTM models using feature combinations (VIs + TFs, VIs + CMPs, VIs + TFs + CMPs) achieved better performance than those using single features (VIs, TFs, CMPs), with the VIs + CMPs combination yielding the highest accuracy (R2 > 0.93, RMSE < 0.52). The Transformer-LSTM model effectively captured both temporal dynamics and global dependencies, achieving optimal performance for banana LAI estimation on the full-cycle dataset (testing R2 = 0.951, RMSE = 0.458). Additionally, the model maintained stable performance across all growth stages, with testing R2 exceeding 0.93 at the seedling stage and reaching nearly 0.90 at the flowering stage while maintaining RMSE as low as 0.3. This study presents a reliable approach for accurate banana LAI estimation across the full growth cycle through the integration of the improved RV parameter and a temporal deep learning model.

title: Adaptive sliding mode observer with Metaheuristic optimization for accurate state estimation in distributed electric drive plant protection vehicles
abstract: In agricultural plant protection, plant protection vehicles (PPV) face significant stability challenges due to complex road conditions and the unique characteristics of specialized tires and high ground clearance. Accurate measurement of key parameters, such as longitudinal and lateral speeds and vehicle sideslip angle, is essential for advanced stability control. However, the high cost of precision sensors limits their use in agricultural vehicles. To address this challenge, this paper proposes a Chaotic enhanced particle swarm optimization adaptive sliding mode observer (CEPSO-ASMO) for distributed electrically driven propelled plant protection vehicle (DDEPPV). Firstly, the special agricultural tires used in DDEPPV were nonlinearly modeled in conventional hard soil road and soft soil road environments, and the accuracy of the model was verified by theoretical analysis. Secondly, a tire sliding mode observer with an adaptive feedback gain mechanism was designed. Then, a chaos mechanism and dynamic adjustment strategy were introduced to optimize the feedback gain, sliding mode surface parameters, and other aspects of the adaptive sliding mode observer, which improved the accuracy and robustness of the observer. The real vehicle experiments show that, compared with traditional methods, the CEPSO-ASMO significantly improved the tire force and driving state estimation accuracy of the DDEPPV. This method reduced the tire force estimation error by 38.32% and 42.1% under two typical road conditions, respectively, and effectively suppressed the chattering phenomenon. In addition, the normalized root mean square error of the vehicle’s driving state estimation was less than 5%. By using standard high-frequency onboard sensors, the CEPSO-ASMO can accurately estimate tire forces and dynamic driving state parameters of DDEPPV, offering promising engineering application prospects.

title: A hybrid machine-learning and process-based regional crop modelling framework to improve rice production strategies under data constraints
abstract: • Coupled PSO and DSSAT to model Lao rice systems under severe data scarcity. • Simulated rice yield and CH 4 , N 2 O, and NH 3 emission in Laos. • Identified a national economic N guidance band of 25–30 kg N ha −1 . • Province-specific N tuning improved profit while maintaining high NUE. Rice production in the Lao People’s Democratic Republic (Lao PDR) is fundamental to national food security, yet its productivity and environmental impacts remain poorly quantified due to limited monitoring and data availability. To address this challenge, we developed a spatially explicit and cost-effective regional rice crop modelling framework by coupling the Decision Support System for Agro-technology Transfer (DSSAT) model with a particle swarm optimization (PSO) algorithm. This hybrid framework was applied to simulate rice growth and associated environmental impacts across Laos from 2012 to 2022. Using available provincial yield statistics for model calibration, we quantified rice yields and greenhouse gas emissions in wet-season rain-fed rice systems. At the province scale, fertilizer response curves show that high fertilizer prices relative to rice prices substantially reduce the economically optimum N application rate. We identified a national guidance range of 25–30 kg N ha −1 with province-specific adjustments, capable of improving farm profitability (70–110%) while sustaining high N use efficiency (NUE) (90–110 kg kg −1 ). Our results highlight the potential for Laos to advance environmentally sustainable (green) rice production. The proposed PSO + DSSAT framework offers a transferable tool for supporting sustainable rice management in regions with limited data coverage.

title: A learning-based approach for forest row orientation estimation from UAV LiDAR point clouds
abstract: Reliable estimation of forest row orientation is crucial for understanding plantation structure and for supporting autonomous navigation and path planning. Unlike over-canopy imagery, Light Detection and Ranging (LiDAR) directly captures the three-dimensional structure of the under-canopy environment. However, determining this row orientation from LiDAR point cloud data in under-canopy environments remains challenging due to heavy occlusion, uneven point density, and measurement noise. This study proposes a learning-based method for row orientation estimation using Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) LiDAR point clouds. A Bird’s-Eye View (BEV) representation is constructed, and a pixel-level U-Net model (BEV-U-Net) is designed to achieve robust orientation prediction. To support model training and evaluation, a large-scale synthetic plantation dataset with orientation labels is generated using forest structure statistics from real plantations. Additionally, a complete navigation pipeline, including row fitting and waypoint generation, is implemented within a ROS and PX4 simulation framework. Simulation experiments show that the proposed BEV-U-Net achieves higher accuracy, stronger robustness, and better computational efficiency than frequency-domain methods, clustering-based geometric approaches, and lightweight learning baselines. When integrated into the navigation pipeline, the predicted orientations enable accurate row fitting and waypoint generation, allowing the UAV to follow plantation corridors smoothly with minimal deviation. These results confirm that the method provides an effective perception module for autonomous under-canopy navigation and flight.

title: Editorial Board
Dairy cow re-identification across multi-camera views via complementary-view feature fusion and orientation-aware learning
abstract: Dairy cow re-identification (ReID) aims to enable cross-view individual identification by matching the same individual across images captured by different cameras, which is crucial for intelligent farm management. However, the same individual can exhibit large intra-class appearance variations across viewpoints and body orientations, especially under opposite orientations. In addition, different individuals may also show high inter-class similarity, which jointly increases the difficulty of cross-view identification. To address these issues, this study proposes FOONet with three key components: Fine-grained Complementary-view Feature Aggregator (FCFA) is designed to fuse complementary-view features to alleviate cross-view visual bias and enhance the discriminability among visually similar individuals; Opposite Orientation Mask Mechanism (OOMM) is introduced to mitigate the mismatch between the generic ReID training paradigm and dairy cow ReID caused by opposite-orientation discrepancies of the same individual; and Orientation Weighting Strategy (OWS) is applied during retrieval to suppress false matches from visually similar negatives under opposite orientations. Furthermore, this study introduces an auxiliary evaluation metric, mAP-IOPS, to assess retrieval performance for positives with the same or adjacent orientations. To evaluate the proposed method, this study deployed eight cameras on a farm for data collection and constructed a cross-view dairy cow ReID dataset containing 16,330 images of 78 dairy cows. Experimental results demonstrate that FOONet achieves Rank-1, Rank-5, Rank-10, and mAP-IOPS scores of 96.9%, 98.5%, 100.0%, and 75.9%, respectively, verifying its effectiveness for cross-view dairy cow identification. The dataset is available at https://github.com/IPCLab-NEAU/Dairy-Cow-Re-Identification.

title: RBSS-YOLOv8: multi-scale feature enhancement for high-density pig aggression detection
abstract: Detecting aggressive behaviour in intensive commercial pig farms is vital for animal welfare and productivity, yet remains a formidable challenge due to frequent occlusions and complex environmental factors. Previous computer vision approaches have primarily focused on controlled, low-density settings and often underperform in authentic daylight commercial scenarios involving multiple pens and high stocking densities. To address these limitations, we propose RBSS-YOLOv8, an enhanced framework based on YOLOv8 incorporating three core architectural refinements: a Bidirectional Global Feature Pyramid Network (Bi-GFPN) for robust cross-layer feature fusion; a RepEMA module, which integrates RepVitBlock and EMA to bolster feature representation; and Space-Channel Reconstruction Convolution (SCConv) to mitigate interference from complex backgrounds. Furthermore, we introduce Dual-Scale Slice-Assisted Hyper-Inference (DSAHI) and Dual-Scale Slice-Assisted Fine-tuning (DSF) during the training and inference phases to better navigate multi-scale detection challenges. To support this research, we developed a high-density, multi-pen commercial pig farm dataset containing 2,179 annotated instances of aggressive behaviour, thereby addressing a critical gap in benchmarks for real-world commercial scenarios. Experimental results demonstrate that RBSS-YOLOv8 significantly outperforms both mainstream models (YOLOv11, YOLOv12, Mamba-YOLO, RTDETR, RTMDet, and DDOD) and specialised animal behaviour detection models (including YOLOv9-SENet, Improved YOLOv10 for fish and pigs, SAG-YOLO, YOLO-CE, and ECA-YOLO) in daylight high-density environments. Our framework achieved a substantial performance gain, increasing mAP@0.5 from 65.4% to 71.0%, reaching 77.2% with the integration of DSAHI. Crucially, RBSS-YOLOv8 maintains robust performance in low-density scenarios (94.6% mAP@0.5) while offering competitive computational efficiency (5.1 GFLOPs) and a compact model size (2.2 M parameters). These findings indicate that RBSS-YOLOv8 attains superior accuracy whilst remaining highly efficient; its bespoke design for occlusion and background interference in commercial high-density settings surpasses the capabilities of general-purpose detection models. This study confirms the practical utility of the proposed methodology for daylight monitoring in commercial pig farms. Moreover, the public release of the high-density dataset provides a vital benchmark for the field, directly addressing the urgent requirement for authentic commercial-scale data within the animal behaviour monitoring community.

title: Towards automated insect farming: A robust control framework for yield optimization and resource management in black soldier fly larvae rearing
abstract: To maximize biomass production and economic efficiency in the industrial rearing of Black Soldier Fly Larvae (BSFL), precise control of the production environment is required. This paper presents a robust hierarchical control framework designed to automate and optimize the BSFL rearing process. The proposed architecture consists of a supervisory upper level that generates climate trajectories, balancing trade-offs between optimal larval growth and operational costs derived from energy pricing and local weather forecasts. A lower-level Deep Reinforcement Learning controller ensures precise tracking of the trajectories despite potential actuator malfunctions. To address BSFL biological variability, a Moving Horizon Estimation algorithm is employed to estimate unmeasured states — specifically, current biomass of the larvae — and strain-specific parameters using only standard medium temperature and moisture measurements. This estimation capability allows the framework to dynamically re-optimize trajectories to correct for growth deviations, rendering the system robust to larval strains with uncharacterized responses to specific climatic variables, such as metabolic fluctuations under varying temperature and moisture gradients.
