The variable selection based on multicollinearity analysis can improve the prediction accuracy and reduce the uncertainty of the ensemble model with an R2 increase of 4.51%, an RMSE decrease of 5.03% and an MAE decrease of 3.50%, but it may lead to a potential reduction in the extrapolation reliability, with the area of application decreasing by 4.84% and the potential loss of information for model interpretation. This study provides a data-driven approach for high-accuracy mapping and driver interpretation of soil properties.

title: Editorial Board
Joint prediction of potato yield and nitrogen status at row closure using multi-task deep learning and UAV-derived LiDAR–multispectral data
abstract: • Fused UAV multispectral and LiDAR data quantified potato canopy structure and petiole nitrate-N at row closure. • Joint modelling of yield and petiole nitrate-N improved predictive performance compared with single-task approaches. • LiDAR height and structural metrics added complementary information to multispectral predictors. • Single-date UAV data at the row-closure stage were sufficient for nitrogen prediction but less informative for yield. • Feature attribution analyses indicated physiologically consistent relationships between canopy structure and nitrogen status.

title: LTF-YOLO: A lightweight framework for long-tailed agricultural pest detection in complex field environments
abstract: Early warning of agricultural pests is imperative for safeguarding crop yields, yet field-based pest detection remains challenging. Complex backgrounds, strict edge-computing constraints, and pronounced long-tailed class distributions impede reliable detection, especially for rare and visually similar pests. To address these challenges, this study proposes LTF-YOLO, a lightweight pest detection framework built on YOLO11n, designed to stabilize performance under long-tailed distributions in complex field environments. First, Pest Neighborhood Attention Transformer (PNAT) enhances feature robustness for tail-class and visually similar pests in cluttered scenes by strengthening local structural cues. Second, an efficient downsampling strategy (ADown) maintains a compact footprint suitable for edge deployment. Third, we propose Balanced-Proxy Loss (BP Loss) to mitigate long-tail-induced decision bias via class-frequency-aware logit reweighting and to improve boundary separation for underrepresented classes. Furthermore, we construct a multi-crop, cross-source pest detection benchmark, MultiCropPest-15 (MCP15), to support deployment-oriented evaluation under realistic long-tailed conditions. On IP102, LTF-YOLO achieves 57.4% mAP@0.5 and 36.0% mAP@0.5:0.95, improving by 4.4 and 2.2 points. On MCP15, it attains 77.7% mAP@0.5 and 47.0% mAP@0.5:0.95, improving by 7.2 and 5.2 points. An analysis across head, medium, and tail classes shows larger gains on tail classes, indicating effective mitigation of long-tail suppression. These findings highlight the significance of addressing long-tail-induced bias within a lightweight detection framework to ensure reliable and robust pest monitoring in agricultural environments.

title: The orchard tractor navigation method based on UAV photogrammetry combined with safety reinforcement learning
abstract: Autonomous navigation for orchard tractors faces significant challenges in robust path planning and reliable operation in unstructured orchard environments. To address these issues, this paper proposes a human-robot collaborative driving navigation method for tractors, based on UAV photogrammetry and safe reinforcement learning. First, rapid semantic segmentation and global path planning are achieved using UAV photogrammetry and an Attention U-Net model. Second, a composite control strategy utilizing APF-MPC-Safe RL-HIL is designed. This approach incorporates an Artificial Potential Field (APF) into Model Predictive Control (MPC) to provide safety-aware baseline path tracking. It further introduces the Twin Delayed Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (TD3) algorithm to learn residual steering corrections for the MPC controller in complex terrain conditions. Additionally, a Human-in-the-Loop (HIL) safety intervention mechanism is introduced to provide expert corrective actions during unsafe exploration, thereby accelerating reinforcement learning convergence and improving operational safety during the initial exploration phase. The system underwent pre-training and parameter iteration within a Gazebo simulation environment, followed by deployment and validation in real-world orchard scenarios. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method exhibits robustness in typical operations, maintaining an average lateral deviation within 0.13 m. This study provides a practical solution for the rapid deployment of autonomous navigation in orchard environments, with both theoretical significance and practical engineering value.

title: IoT-enabled edge-based cattle behavior monitoring framework using TinyML and IMU sensor fusion
abstract: Continuous smart behavior monitoring is more essential to predicting early symptoms of cattle’s health issues in advance for modern livestock husbandry. Existing traditional and conventional approaches consume more time and labor and are often prone to errors. A cow’s health, feed factors, and environmental changes directly affect milk yield; farmers lose approximately ₹8,000–12,000 per cow annually due to nutritional imbalances and a lack of adequate early disease detection. This study proposes an integrated Internet of Things Machine Learning (IoT-ML)-based real-time precision cattle behavior recognition system. The wearable neckband device with an Inertial Measurement Unit (IMU) sensor, micro SD card reader, and Quectel-GPS module that is interconnected with the ESP32 microcontroller, which is deployed on individual cattle, continuously acquires real-time sensor motions. To reduce unnecessary noise and placement disturbances while transitioning activities, the moving average filter (MAF) and extended Kalman filter (EKF) were applied to each IMU original sensor’s data. The integration of Hidden Markov Model (HMM) and Random Forest (RF) approaches delivered precise, robust motion prediction while transient activities occurred. The experimental findings showed a steady improvement in performance throughout the subsequent processing phases. The accuracy of the MAF pre-processing stage was 98.98%, whereas the EKF phase remained consistent at 98.65%. The final combined HMM-RF model achieved classification accuracy of 99.84% with an overall F1-score of 0.99 across the four behavioral classes. The proposed system employs a complete end-to-end pipeline (sensing → inference → IoT communication) on resource-constrained devices as ESP32 without cloud dependency, which is continuously, monitors the motion and behavioral patterns of cattle in real time so that farmers can easily identify early vital signs of diseases. Thereby, it prevents serious complications, reduces unexpected mortality rates, and provides a low-labor and low-cost solution to farmers, leading to increased overall farm productivity.

title: Assessment of thermal performance of conductive heating beds for cold stress dairy cows in severe cold regions using computational fluid dynamics
abstract: Cold stress critically constrains milk yield in high-latitude dairy operations. While conductive heating beds offer a promising localized solution, their thermal mechanisms remain underexplored for cold-stressed cows in severe cold regions (–30 °C). This study presents a coupled CFD-experimental framework that integrates computational fluid dynamics with field measurements to ensure predictive reliability and mechanistic insight. Through systematic three-factor parametric analysis (bedding material, heating temperature, and bedding thickness), the independent effects of each factor on thermal performance were quantified. Thermal performance was quantified by area-weighted average temperature of the bedding surface (AT), area-weighted average heat flux of the bedding surface (HF), total heat transfer rate of the bedding surface (HTR), and volume-weighted average temperature of the air inside the barn (VT). Results show sand bedding achieved optimal thermal performance (HF: 124.4 W/m2; HTR: 933.3 W at 20 mm thickness and 50 °C supply temperature), outperforming rubber and straw. Notably, ground temperatures exceeding 13 °C significantly increase ammonia volatilization from manure. Thus, the recommended heating range is 45 to 50 °C, balancing thermal performance and environmental health. Increasing bedding thickness from 0 mm to 250 mm reduced HF by 76.5 %, necessitating trade-offs between thermal performance and cow comfort. The CFD model was rigorously validated against experimental data, with relative errors below 7 % (average 1.33 %) for barn air temperature predictions, confirming the model’s fidelity for parametric analysis. These findings provide scientific foundations for designing energy-efficient heating systems in cold-region dairy barns.

title: Robust covariance feature selection for unsupervised clustering of ultrasonic measurements on standing trees
abstract: Ultrasonic testing is a practical tool for health assessment of standing trees, but the resulting measurements are often affected by noise, heterogeneity, and outliers, complicating reliable interpretation. This study proposes Robust Covariance Feature Selection (RCFS), a label-free unsupervised feature selection framework that integrates Minimum Covariance Determinant-based Mahalanobis distances, sigmoid-based sample reweighting, and singular value decomposition-based cosine-squared feature scoring. A key contribution is a clustering-aware optimization framework in which mean cluster entropy is minimized via Bayesian optimization to jointly determine reweighting parameters, the number of selected features, and the number of clusters. The same entropy-based optimization strategy is also applied as a wrapper to Spectral Feature Selection (SPEC) and Unsupervised Discriminative Feature Selection (UDFS), representing spectral- and discriminative-based baselines. Validated on ultrasonic datasets from two Australian sites, RCFS achieved accuracy gains of 4%–8%, normalized mutual information gains of 30%–45%, Silhouette improvements of 20%–45%, and entropy reductions of 50%–70% relative to the baseline methods, while also producing stable feature subsets under resampling. Ablation studies on COIL20 and ORL, including comparison with Unsupervised Soft-Label Feature Selection (USFS), further show that the proposed reweighting improves performance when outlier influence is pronounced while remaining effectively neutral when such influence is limited, thereby preserving the underlying data structure for feature ranking.

title: Assimilation of LAI and FAPAR within DSSAT guided by leaf growth dynamics to enhance maize yield phenotyping
abstract: Maize (Zea mays L.) yield phenotyping is essential for breeding high-yielding cultivars and addressing global food security challenges. However, because yield accumulates throughout the growing season and is shaped by complex genetic, physiological, and environmental interactions, accurate yield phenotyping remains challenging. Traditional yield phenotyping is labor-intensive, limited to harvest-stage assessment, and unable to capture the dynamic processes underlying yield development. The emergence of Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV)-based hyperspectral high-throughput (HTP) phenotyping provides a non-destructive, large-scale, and temporally continuous approach. These HTP data are commonly analyzed using machine learning (ML) models to extract yield-sensitive features and establish relationships with historical yield labels for prediction, whereas such models often remain limited in physiological consistency, interpretability, and performance stability. To address these limitations, a UAV-based data assimilation framework, HyperDA-Leaf, was developed to dynamically integrate weekly UAV-derived leaf area index (LAI) and fraction of absorbed photosynthetically active radiation (FAPAR) into the Decision Support System for Agrotechnology Transfer (DSSAT) for yield phenotyping. HyperDA-Leaf integrates a data exchange interface within DSSAT, enabling the coupling of leaf area dynamics with UAV-based data assimilation to generate physiologically realistic and observation-constrained growth trajectories for improved yield prediction. Results showed that HyperDA-Leaf produced daily LAI and FAPAR trajectories with fewer unrealistic fluctuations and exhibited stronger correlations with daily radiation and temperature. HyperDA-Leaf also achieved robust performance across three years in breeding-oriented experimental fields containing thousands of maize hybrids, achieving high yield prediction accuracy (R2 > 0.6) without using yield labels and outperforming comparative ML models. Furthermore, the optimized light stress factor (LSF) enhanced physiological interpretability by showing that high-yielding hybrids experienced lower light stress intensity and fewer stress days, owing to their greater photosynthetic efficiency, as reflected by higher LAI and FAPAR values. Overall, HyperDA-Leaf provides a physiologically grounded, interpretable, and robust solution for UAV-based maize yield phenotyping, supporting the understanding of maize yield formation and large-scale breeding applications.

title: Path tracking for electric rotary tillers based on fuzzy pure pursuit and IWOA-optimized feedforward sliding mode control under uneven soil resistance
abstract: During operation, horticultural electric rotary tillers encounter unequal soil resistance between tracks due to inconsistent soil compaction. On uneven terrain, lateral tilt further causes asymmetric tillage depths, resulting in dynamic load disturbances and bias torques that impair path tracking accuracy. To resolve these issues, we propose a hierarchical path tracking control method with rotary tillage resistance disturbance compensation. A variable universe fuzzy pure pursuit controller adjusts preview distance and turning radius based on path deviation. Target motor speeds are then derived using a kinematic model. A state observer estimates rotary and driving resistance torques and applies them as feedforward compensations. Sliding mode control (SMC) ensures precise motor speed control, with its parameters optimized via a whale optimization algorithm enhanced by chaotic reverse learning, Lévy flight, and inertia weight strategies. Simulations show that the SMC-based improved whale optimization algorithm with state-observer-based feedforward compensation outperforms proportional-integral-derivative (PID), fuzzy PID, and traditional SMC in speed response, steady-state error, and robustness. The integrated controller achieves mean lateral absolute errors of 0.0808, 0.0174, and 0.0299 m under S-curve, parabolic, and hyperbolic paths, respectively. Greenhouse trials show mean lateral deviations of 0.0330, 0.0862, and 0.1033 m and heading deviations of 2.7965°, 2.8839°, and 3.4595° at tillage depths of 4, 8, and 12 cm, respectively. These results confirm full coverage of the target area and provide theoretical support for intelligent navigation in facility tillage.

title: Numerical investigation of ventilation strategies for naturally ventilated dairy barns in severe cold regions: Applicability of anisotropic porous media models
abstract: The indoor environment of dairy barns is influenced by the coupled effects of multiple factors, which increases the complexity and uncertainty of simulations. Additionally, considering the geometric characteristics of cows is essential for simulating airflow and temperature distribution in large barns. However, relatively few studies have addressed full-scale simulations for the indoor environment of dairy barns that consider geometric characteristics. Therefore, this study comparatively analyzed the differences between full-scale models and anisotropic porous media models (APMM) in simulating indoor environment of dairy barns with a large number of cows. Additionally, the impact of various ventilation methods on the indoor environment of dairy barns was comprehensively examined. APMM was found to have significant efficacy in predicting the overall airflow rate and flow characteristics. Both full-scale models and APMM had average errors of less than 5% compared to the measured data. However, APMM had limitations in simulating local details and could not fully reproduce the complex flow and temperature variations observed in full-scale models. In addition, increasing ventilation openings significantly improved airflow and temperature distribution uniformity, but over-expanding the ventilation openings could lead to significant heat loss. This study provides theoretical support for the optimal design of ventilation systems in dairy barns and clarifies the strengths and weaknesses of APMM in practical applications.

title: In-situ precision sensing for smart agriculture using flexible wearable optical array sensing system with multiple regression integrated learning
abstract: Smart agriculture, a new agricultural model that optimizes production and improves efficiency through modern information technology, has optical sensors as one of its key components. However, most of the research on optical sensors is focused on a single scale, which often fails to adequately capture the diversity and complexity of crops under different environmental conditions. Therefore, this study develops a flexible wearable optical array sensing system and proposes a method for in situ prediction of crop growth quality parameters and health status monitoring, integrating multi-area spectral sensing, data fusion, and multi-regression ensemble learning. Innovatively, a flexible optical sensor array was designed, capable of covering a total of 18 spectral wavelengths ranging from 410 to 940 nm. Using data fusion technology, the system collects spectral information from the crop surface in real-time and employs a multi-regression ensemble learning model to predict the soluble solid content (SSC) and moisture content of the crops. Experimental results indicate that the coefficient of determination values of 0.951 and 0.958 for predicting SSC and moisture content, respectively. The relative prediction errors (RPD) were 4.54 and 4.80, both outperforming ablation models and state-of-the-art methods. Moreover, the system generates color-coded maps from spectral data to effectively differentiate between abnormal and healthy areas, enabling early-stage abnormality monitoring during fruit growth. This technology provides an efficient solution for non-destructive testing of crop quality and surface abnormality monitoring, promoting the intelligent and digital transformation of agriculture, and possesses significant theoretical value and application potential. The original data, data fusion code, program design code, PCB files, and application software for this paper have been open-sourced: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1IxmYnDb5xij8y7Z3ypGO4zBIAwGDiPp0/view.

title: Adaptive rotary tillage depth control with RBF-ADRC based on time-series prediction of tractor chassis pitch angle
abstract: To mitigate tillage-depth fluctuations induced by surface undulations and actuator nonlinearities in horticultural electric tractors, this study develops a predictive depth control method. A novel MSCNN–BiLSTM–Attention model is constructed to forecast pitch-angle variations. It utilizes multi-scale convolution to extract disturbance features across different temporal scales, while bidirectional temporal modeling combined with a multi-head attention mechanism enhances temporal representations. Model hyperparameters are optimized using an improved beluga whale optimization algorithm. The predicted pitch angle is integrated as feedforward compensation into the control loop. By fusing this prediction with a rotary-tillage kinematic model, future tillage depth is estimated, enabling the design of an RBF-based active disturbance rejection controller (RBF-ADRC) for adaptive compensation of system nonlinearities and time-varying disturbances. The proposed prediction model achieved MAE and RMSE of 0.0526° and 0.0686°, respectively, with a test-set R2 of 0.9931, and errors primarily within ± 0.03°. Simulations demonstrated that the proposed prediction-assisted control strategy outperforms RBFPID, optimal sliding mode, and model predictive controllers under step, sinusoidal, and slope disturbances, achieving zero overshoot, a steady-state error of 0.001 cm, and reduced dynamic errors. Greenhouse field experiments further validated the method, yielding average tillage depths of 4.03, 8.14, and 11.59 cm against targets of 4, 8, and 12 cm, with maximum fluctuations of approximately 0.6 cm. Overall, this deep learning-based predictive feedforward strategy significantly improves tillage-depth stability and control precision under complex surface conditions, providing a practical solution for intelligent electric tractors in protected horticulture.

title: Low-light image enhancement with shallow diffusion model based on collaborative sampling
abstract: Complex lighting conditions pose significant challenges to high-level fruit detection in robotic harvesting systems, because lighting issues cause images to suffer from a degradation in detail. Deep learning models have been widely adopted for image enhancement, among which diffusion models have demonstrated exceptional capabilities in recovering high-quality images. However, diffusion models are often constrained by time-consuming and excessive computational resource consumption owing to their pixel-level iterative process. To address these constraints, we propose a novel shallow diffusion model for image enhancement that performs in the frequency-domain measurements instead of the image space via collaborative sampling. The shallow diffusion mechanism accelerates the inference time by reducing the number of denoising steps. Moreover, we optimized the refined reconstruction process to improve image quality. Extensive experiments on mango datasets demonstrated that the proposed method achieved superior performance and efficiency. Our research addresses the challenge of poor visual imaging quality caused by variable lighting conditions in agriculture. This advancement improves downstream tasks, such as target recognition, and can be extended to intelligent agricultural vision applications.

title: The integration of artificial intelligence in plant Factories: Transforming the future of sustainable Agriculture, a Semi-Systematic review
abstract: This study presents a semi-systematic review of the integration of artificial intelligence (AI), the Internet of Things (IoT), and plant factory systems within Controlled Environment Agriculture (CEA). A structured literature search was conducted using Scopus and CrossRef databases, covering publications from 2018 to 2025. A total of 130 records were identified, of which 40 studies were selected following PRISMA-based screening criteria. The review addresses three key research questions: (RQ1) identifying the main technological components and applications of AI, IoT, and plant factory systems; (RQ2) evaluating how their integration enhances productivity, operational performance, and sustainability compared to standalone technologies; and (RQ3) analyzing the technical, economic, and operational limitations affecting scalability, interoperability, and long-term viability. The results indicate that integrating AI and IoT into plant factory systems enables precise environmental control, with AÍs primary benefit being advanced data analysis for improved decision-making and crop monitoring. This significantly enhances resource-use efficiency and productivity. However, several critical challenges remain, including high implementation costs, complex data integration, and scalability constraints in real-world conditions. Overall, this review provides a comprehensive synthesis of current technological advances and offers a system-level perspective to support the development of scalable, sustainable, and intelligent agricultural systems.

title: Multi-rate PWM flow regulation for canopy-adapted variable-rate spraying in a smart tree crop sprayer
abstract: Variable-Rate Application (VRA) in orchards can reduce pesticide waste and off-target contamination, but canopy-driven spraying remains challenging due to fast target appearance/disappearance, vehicle-speed variations, and intrinsically non-uniform vertical deposition. This paper proposes a real-time multi-rate control architecture for a smart tree crop sprayer that couples a predictive pressure loop with a fast Pulse Width Modulation (PWM) based flow regulation layer to improve canopy-dose accuracy and uniformity. The slow layer regulates manifold pressure through a three-way proportional valve using a fuzzy Generalized Predictive Controller (GPC), while the fast layer modulates nozzle duty cycles to track boom-level flow targets and to adapt the vertical spray profile using an adaptive fuzzy–Gaussian distribution based on canopy height and density. A PWM-oriented Proportional Integral (PI) law with anti-oscillation mechanisms is used for bar-flow regulation, and spraying is automatically suppressed outside the live canopy and in inter-tree gaps. The complete framework is designed for embedded deployment on an STM32F407 and is evaluated in simulation under identical canopy and speed profiles against a representative section-based baseline (four ON/OFF sections commanded at 100% duty). Canopy-region, area-weighted indices show that the proposed strategy substantially improves tracking and uniformity, reducing the canopy Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) of the applied dose and overdose by approximately 75%, increasing compliance area (within ±20% of the reference) to about 85%, and reducing the dose Coefficient of Variation (CV) by about 50% on both booms. These results indicate that fast PWM flow regulation and adaptive vertical distribution are key to achieving accurate and uniform canopy-adapted VRA under shared pressure-loop dynamics.

title: A multi-criteria evaluation framework for mobile weed classification: Balancing accuracy and efficiency across hardware tiers
abstract: • Framework evaluates DL models for weed classification. • MobileNetV3-Large and Small are Pareto-optimal in accuracy/efficiency. • Lightweight models outperform heavyweights in latency and memory. • Multi-tier benchmarking protocol ensures reproducibility. • Pareto-frontier analysis guides hardware-aware architecture selection.

title: Recognition of kiwifruit pruning position based on vine segmentation and dormant bud detection with their planar distribution
abstract: Kiwifruit winter pruning is a laborious, seasonal, and irreversible operation. The key to achieving automatic winter pruning of kiwifruit lies in the recognition of pruning position. In this study, a method based on kiwifruit vine segmentation and dormant bud detection with their planar distribution was developed to recognize the pruning position of kiwifruit vine. Firstly, YOLO11x-seg and YOLO11x were applied to segment vines and detect dormant buds, respectively. Secondly, the DBSCAN algorithm was applied to remove wrongly segmented vine, and vine skeleton was then extracted. Thirdly, dormant buds were matched with their corresponding canes based on the overlap ratio, and then ordered from the cane base. Finally, the pruning position was recognized based on the planar distribution of vines and dormant buds. Results showed that YOLO11x-seg and YOLO11x achieved an outstanding performance with segmentation and detection mAP of 82.5% and 89.0%, respectively. The method proposed in this study attained pruning position recognition accuracies of 77.3%, 81.8%, and 88.9% under the three pruning strategies of cane short-truncation, lateral cane removal, and cane renewal, respectively. These results indicate that the proposed method is promising for robotic winter pruning of kiwifruit.

title: Robust long-range obstacle detection in farmland via LiDAR-Camera fusion and cascaded ground filtering
abstract: To address the challenges of limited detection range, unstable tracking, and object flickering caused by ground interference from uneven farmland, inaccurate visual masks, and sparse LiDAR point clouds at mid-to-long distances, this study constructs a multi-sensor fusion perception system based on 3D LiDAR and cameras. Furthermore, it proposes an obstacle detection method incorporating cascaded ground filtering, multimodal feature fusion, and temporal tracking. The method first utilizes a cascaded algorithm combining Random Sample Consensus (RANSAC) and Cloth Simulation Filter (CSF) to address the challenge of ground clutter filtering in uneven terrain. To account for the varying reliability of sensor modalities at different distances, a matching strategy based on hybrid cost is developed. This strategy enables a robust association between LiDAR clusters and visual targets by adaptively weighting the precise boundary information from visual masks and the stable positional features from detection bounding boxes. A Kalman filter is subsequently integrated to impose temporal smoothness on the fusion results and eliminate long-range object flickering. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method reduces the ground false positive rate to 0.3% and achieves an overall average precision of 91.4%. Regarding mid-to-long distance detection, in contrast to the baseline method where the recall drops sharply beyond 35 m, the proposed method achieves an average recall of 98.2% within the entire 0–45 m range. Furthermore, accuracy (MOTA) and tracking continuity (IDF1) are improved to 92.93% and 98.03%, respectively. Therefore, the proposed method satisfies the requirements for high precision, high recall, and stable environmental perception in complex farmland scenarios.

title: Valuing RTK-GNSS signal degradation duration nowcasts: Mitigating threats to the A-B line
abstract: Context: Peanut production depends on RTK-GNSS guidance for precise row alignment across field operations. Signal interruptions from space weather, jamming, or spoofing can reduce yields, forcing producers to delay operations or continue without guidance. Objective: To quantify the economic value of GNSS outage duration nowcasts for peanut farming by assessing trade-offs between waiting for guidance versus continuing operations, estimating breakeven durations, and calculating expected value of perfect information (EVPI). Methods: A whole-farm linear programming model simulated representative southeastern US farms using USDA NASS data. Yield penalties were modeled with splines; continuing without RTK caused an 11% loss. Breakeven thresholds and EVPI were computed for outage scenarios. Results and conclusions Waiting was optimal early in the planting window, while continuing was favored later. Nowcast value ranged $10 million to $20 million in Georgia and $16 million to $33 million across the southeast; 5% of total peanut value, twice the value of terrestrial weather forecasts. Significance As the first economic valuation of GNSS outage nowcasts for agriculture, this study demonstrates that such forecasts deliver actionable decision support worth twice the proportional value of traditional weather forecasts, providing empirical justification for investments in space weather monitoring and GNSS resilience infrastructure.

title: Error-driven decision-level fusion with residual correction improves UAV multispectral prediction of winter wheat incremental yield
abstract: Water-nitrogen synergy is a key agronomic process shaping winter wheat yield and resource-use efficiency. Accurate characterization of its growth responses and yield-gain mechanisms is essential for climate adaptation and sustainable production. This study used multi-cultivar, multi-level water–nitrogen trials in Xinxiang, Henan during the 2023–2024 and 2024–2025 winter wheat seasons (hereafter referred to as the 2024 and 2025 seasons, respectively). UAV multispectral (MS) images at flowering and grain filling stages were collected and combined with field water-nitrogen management features (WN) and measured yield. We developed an error-driven decision-level fusion framework (RC-DLF) using SVM, RF, BRNN, and GLM as base learners. Reliability weights were derived from within-fold RMSE, and a lightweight residual correction (RC) layer refined the fused decisions. RC-DLF (RMSE⁻1) outperformed the best single learner, BRNN using WN + MS, at both stages. At flowering, R2 improved from 0.48 to 0.62, while RMSE decreased from 1194.26 to 1017.77 kg·ha⁻1. At grain filling, R2 improved from 0.53 to 0.67, and RMSE decreased from 1146.15 to 946.08 kg·ha⁻1. Residuals were centered near zero in the pooled two-season dataset, indicating limited overall systematic bias under the current experimental domain. RC-DLF provides a practical workflow for diagnosing water-nitrogen synergy and supporting precision irrigation and fertilization decisions.

title: Haar wavelet-guided dynamic Feature Pyramid Network for an efficient paddy leaf disease classification
abstract: Early and accurate identification of paddy leaf diseases is crucial for timely intervention and effective crop management. Although deep learning based approaches have demonstrated strong performance in paddy leaf disease classification, they often struggle to capture the diverse multiscale symptom patterns of diseases, resulting in the misclassification of challenging samples. Moreover, the high computational cost of deep learning based models remains a significant limitation. To address these challenges, this study proposes a novel Haar wavelet-guided deep Feature Pyramid Network (FPN) model. In the proposed framework, deep features are extracted using a backbone network, and a FPN is employed to capture multiscale disease symptoms. In parallel, Haar wavelet features are extracted to provide complementary texture cues that are not explicitly modelled by deep features. Guided by these wavelet features, a gating-based dynamic feature selection module is then utilised to identify image-specific FPN features, which are subsequently used for classification. In the second phase of the study, a lightweight variant of the proposed model is developed using a knowledge distillation technique, achieving high classification accuracy while substantially reducing the number of parameters and FLOPs. In addition, a new benchmark dataset, named NP-LankaPaddy, is constructed to address the limited availability of datasets representing Sri Lankan paddy leaf disease conditions. Experimental results demonstrate that both the proposed approach and its lightweight variant outperform state-of-the-art methods across four benchmark datasets, achieving notably high accuracies of 98.04% and 97.84%, respectively, on the well known Paddy Doctor dataset. The source code and dataset supporting this study are openly available at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.18334503.

title: Addressing representation instability, strategy rigidity, and class imbalance in active learning for agricultural pest and disease recognition
abstract: Agricultural pests and diseases cause substantial crop losses worldwide, yet deploying deep learning in smart agriculture is hindered by the high cost of expert annotation. Generative AI (GAI) techniques such as GANs can augment training data, but generated samples still require expert verification and their quality depends on real labeled data, leaving the annotation bottleneck unresolved. Active learning offers a complementary solution by selecting the most informative samples for labeling, yet existing methods suffer from three limitations: representation instability due to static prototype computation on noisy field images, strategy rigidity from fixed selection ratios across training stages, and neglect of class imbalance during sample selection. We propose a three-level active learning framework that introduces targeted innovations at each level of the learning pipeline. Dynamic Prototype Memory maintains stable class representations through momentum-based exponential moving average updating, providing provably lower variance than static prototype recomputation. Context-Aware Sample Selection employs a neural contextual bandit to dynamically adjust the branch combination ratio at each round, learning how to combine complementary selection strategies rather than which individual samples to select. Class-Balanced Scoring incorporates inverse-frequency weighting to prioritize underrepresented classes directly at the selection stage, filling a gap left unaddressed by existing active learning methods. Experiments on IP06 (insect pest) and Natural CW-10 (weed) datasets demonstrate that the framework achieves 83.36% and 85.07% accuracy at 90% data availability, outperforming the strongest competitor by 4.12 percentage points on IP06 and 2.68 percentage points on Natural CW-10 at 20% data availability, with the largest gains concentrated in low-data regimes. Integration with GAN-augmented data yields further additive improvements, with combined accuracy reaching 84.91% on IP06 and 86.42% on Natural CW-10, confirming the complementary role of active learning within GAI-empowered smart agriculture pipelines. These results demonstrate that principled annotation selection can substantially reduce labeling costs while maintaining competitive recognition performance, offering a practical and scalable solution for real-world smart agriculture deployment where expert annotation resources are severely constrained. Ablation studies verify that the three innovations are mutually complementary, and sensitivity analysis shows robustness to hyperparameter variation.

title: Improved estimation of daily maize evapotranspiration and its components by hybridizing long short-term memory with convolutional neural network and transformer neural network
abstract: Crop evapotranspiration (ET) and its partitioning into soil evaporation (E) and plant transpiration (T) are essential for understanding surface-atmosphere interaction, designing irrigation scheduling, and managing water resources. Nevertheless, direct measurement of ET and its components is time-consuming, labor-intensive and costly, which highlights the imperative of establishing accurate estimation models with readily available data. Two novel hybrid deep learning models, i.e. convolutional neural network-long short-term memory (CNN-LSTM) and transformer neural network-LSTM (Transformer-LSTM) models were proposed to estimate daily maize ET and its partitioning (especially E), and their performances were compared with SVM, XGBoost, DNN and standalone LSTM models. Meteorological (reference crop evapotranspiration, ET0), soil (soil water content, SWC; soil temperature, Ts) and crop (leaf area index, LAI; plant height, H) variables were grouped into eight input combinations to explore their effects on estimation accuracy. The percentage of the data used for training and testing was 4:1. The results showed that the inclusion of Ts and H can effectively enhance the model’s accuracy in estimating daily ET and its components, and it is necessary to take all variables into account while using the machine learning models to estimate daily maize ET and its components. The Transformer-LSTM exhibited satisfactory accuracy (R2 ≥ 0.841 and NRMSE ≤ 0.326) with only ET0. Crop variables, especially LAI, exerted greater influence than soil variables. The Transformer-LSTM model slightly outperformed CNN-LSTM, followed by LSTM, DNN, SVM and XGBoost almost under all input combinations, showing the best estimation accuracy of R2 = 0.894, MAE = 0.166 mm d−1, RMSE = 0.217 mm d−1, NRMSE = 0.266, and |MBE| = 0.000 mm d−1 for E estimation with ET0, LAI and H, R2 = 0.955, MAE = 0.221 mm d−1, RMSE = 0.296 mm d−1, NRMSE = 0.147, and |MBE| = 0.017 mm d−1 for T estimation and R2 = 0.955, MAE = 0.287 mm d−1, RMSE = 0.379 mm d−1, NRMSE = 0.134, and |MBE| = 0.021 mm d−1 for ET estimation with all variables. This study highlighted the potential of hybrid LSTM models and the importance of meteorological and crop variables for accurate estimation of ET and its components in maize fields.

title: Fusing hyperspectral, meteorological, and irrigation data for simultaneous estimation of soil and leaf water status via ensemble learning
abstract: Accurate and simultaneous estimation of leaf equivalent water thickness (EWT) and soil water content (SWC) remains challenging due to spectral interference between canopy and soil signals. This study aims to develop a regression framework for simultaneous estimation of SWC and EWT from a single hyperspectral observation by fusing disentangled spectral features with meteorological and irrigation data. We employed Recursive Feature Elimination method to select sensitive spectral matrices (SSMs) for EWT and SWC, respectively. Spectrum fusion and decomposition of the SSMs using the Non-negative Matrix Factorization and linear subtraction methods, which yields the moisture spectral feature matrix (MSFM). The MSFM combined with meteorological and irrigation indicators, were used as inputs for five base machine learning regressors. Their outputs were further optimized using ensemble algorithms, including Light Gradient Boosting Machine (LightGBM) and Bagging. The effectiveness of the above method in estimation EWT and SWC were tested with field experiments on different irrigation levels, film mulching treatments, and maize varieties in the Shiyang River Basin of Northwest China during 2021 and 2022. The results show that MSFM combined with meteorological and irrigation indicators yield highest prediction accuracy for EWT/SWC compared with MSFM, SSM or full spectrum. Among the five base regression algorithms, Random Forest regression yielded the highest estimation accuracy for SWC, while Multi-Layer Perceptron regression showed superior performance in estimating EWT. Both ensemble algorithms enhanced the testing accuracy of SWC and EWT compared with the five base regression algorithms, improving the coefficient of determination (R2) by 10.84–46.89%, and reducing the root mean square error (RMSE) and normalized RMSE (NRMSE) of 6.87–33.27%. Additionally, under the tested conditions, EWT and SWC errors remained below 28% when leaf area estimation errors were under 25%. This study demonstrates the potential of a unified modeling framework using a single set of hyperspectral observations to accurately estimate crop and soil moisture status under mixed soil–canopy conditions.
keywords: Purification of soil and crop moisture spectrum

title: FishKeypoints: A comprehensive stereo vision framework for fish behaviour monitoring and size measurement in aquaculture
abstract: The shift towards Precision Fish Farming (PFF) requires reliable, automated tracking of individual fish in dense, dynamic underwater environments. Many approaches targeting this topic are based on using computer vision methods and AI to detect and track the fish automatically. Most conventional approaches rely on the use of Horizontal Bounding Boxes (HBBs), however this approach has proven inadequate for accurately localising slender fish with variable orientation, particularly in scenes where fish density and occlusion is high. This study presents a new computer stereo vision framework that leverages Oriented Bounding Boxes (OBBs) for fish detection followed by keypoint detection for the localisation of the anatomical features of the detected fish. The method was set up to directly estimate 3D positions of the detected fish and keypoints and track these over time without external calibration targets. When applied to stereo video data collected from two field trials at commercial fish farms, the method estimated fish-camera distances and fish lengths that corresponded with reference data obtained through other sensors and manual sampling. These results imply that this new approach represents a step forward in non-invasive, automated monitoring and analysis of fish behaviour and growth, giving more detailed insights into farmed fish dynamics and contributing to further progress in the realisation of PFF.

title: Light-TDNN: A lightweight acoustic model for panic stress recognition of caged laying hens in intensive farms
abstract: Panic stress is a prevalent environmental stressor in laying-hen production, leading to severe consequences such as weakened immunity and reduced egg production. Traditional monitoring methods, including manual inspection and physiological sampling, are labor-intensive and invasive; moreover, blood sampling itself may induce secondary stress. Video-based monitoring is also constrained in intensive battery-cage systems due to severe visual occlusion. In contrast, acoustic signals are well suited to complex cage environments because of strong penetration, flexible deployment, and high information density. Leveraging these advantages, a lightweight panic stress vocalization recognition model, the Lightweight Time Delay Neural Network (Light-TDNN), was constructed. To support model development and evaluation, an acoustic dataset collected under diverse typical stressor stimuli was established. Built upon the TDNN architecture, Light-TDNN integrates three key optimization strategies: (1) a Dilated-Shuffle module that substantially reduces model size while capturing long-range temporal dependencies via an expanded receptive field; (2) a Time-Frequency attention module that focuses on the most discriminative time–frequency features and enhances the recognition of easily confused sounds like panic-induced cage noise and feeding sounds; and (3) a relational knowledge distillation strategy that transfers teacher model knowledge and elevates the student model’s performance ceiling without increasing inference cost. Experiments in real farming scenarios show that Light-TDNN achieves a precision of 96.44% and a recall of 93.75%, with only 0.34 M parameters and 39.86 M FLOPs, delivering a favorable accuracy-efficiency trade-off compared with mainstream models. Additionally, a real-time monitoring system was developed by deploying Light-TDNN on an NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin edge architecture. The system achieves an average end-to-end latency of 23.89 ms per 4-s window, enabling low-latency real-time monitoring in large-scale farms. This work offers a robust on-device solution for non-invasive stress detection, providing a quantitative metric to assess the welfare compatibility of intelligent agricultural machinery and inform welfare-oriented equipment design.

title: An LED-based multispectral discrete spectrometer for in-situ soil moisture sensing using machine learning algorithms
abstract: Accurate, low-cost, and field-deployable soil moisture content (SMC) sensing remains a key challenge in precision agriculture and environmental monitoring. This study presents a compact and energy-efficient approach for in-situ SMC estimation using discrete near-infrared (NIR) spectroscopy combined with machine-learning (ML) algorithms. For this purpose, a portable transfer-standard sensor was developed using seven selected NIR light-emitting diodes (LEDs), targeting strong water absorption bands (970, 1150, 1450, and 1900 nm) and weak-absorption reference wavelengths (1100, 1300, and 1650 nm) for soil reflectance measurements. The optomechanical design complies with international soil reflectance spectroscopy standards, employing nadir illumination and 45° detection geometry, while enabling direct comparability between laboratory and field measurements. SI-traceable calibration was performed using thermogravimetric methods over an SMC range from dry conditions to approximately 25% below saturation, utilizing more than ten soil types with varying composition and texture. Linear physical models based on relative absorption depth showed good performance under soil-specific calibration but degraded under heterogeneous field conditions, highlighting sensitivity to soil texture and composition properties. To address this limitation, six ML regression models were evaluated using stratified K-fold cross-validation, feature selection, and normalization. All ML models outperformed the physical approach, with Gaussian Process Regression achieving the highest accuracy, yielding errors below 0.5% for soil-specific calibration and below 2% under generalized field conditions, in agreement with gravimetric references. Wavelength subset analysis revealed diminishing returns beyond five LEDs, with a combination of strong and weak absorption bands providing the most informative feature set. Overall, the results demonstrate that LED-based discrete NIR spectroscopy integrated with ML offers a robust, scalable, and cost- and energy-efficient alternative to conventional spectroscopic systems for in-situ soil moisture monitoring.

title: A perception–grasping integrated soft gripper for nondestructive handling and size-based grading of fragile agricultural products
abstract: Fragile agricultural products such as fruits and eggs are highly susceptible to mechanical damage during harvesting and post-harvest handling. Conventional rigid grippers and perception–grasping decoupled systems often fail to provide both compliant manipulation and reliable tactile feedback. To address these limitations, this study proposes a perception–grasping integrated pneumatic soft gripper for nondestructive agricultural handling and size-based grading of agricultural products. The gripper adopts negative-pressure actuation to achieve adaptive enveloping grasping. Its structural configuration is optimized through finite element analysis, and a guided buckling structure with reinforcing ribs is introduced to improve stress distribution and pressure-bearing capacity, increasing the maximum sustainable negative pressure from −10.68 kPa to −16.36 kPa. A multidimensional tactile perception framework is established by fusing internal pressure signal with visual marker deformation inside the cavity, enabling simultaneous estimation of contact force, gripping force, and target diameter without relying on external scene vision systems. Experimental results show sub-millimeter accuracy in diameter estimation, with prediction errors below 0.2 N for gripping force and 0.1 N for contact force. The system successfully achieved nondestructive grasping of 12 objects with diverse properties and demonstrated reliable quail egg size grading solely based on tactile feedback. The proposed approach provides a practical solution for compliant handling and size grading of delicate agricultural products, supporting intelligent post-harvest handling and grading automation.

title: A self-supervised learning based method for fish disease diagnosis utilizing extremely limited samples
abstract: The extreme scarcity of high-quality annotated datasets in digital aquaculture severely hinders the application of deep learning-based fish disease diagnostics. In addition, general-purpose pretrained models may be less sensitive to the fine-grained pathological cues required for fish disease diagnosis. To address these challenges, this study proposes a fine-grained Masked Autoencoder (MAE) framework. This method aims to uncover the intrinsic structure within unlabeled domain data for robust fish disease diagnosis utilizing extremely limited samples. The framework first establishes an annotation-free preprocessing pipeline combining Grounding-DINO and the Segment Anything Model (SAM) to precisely eliminate complex background noise without human intervention. Then, an adaptive multi-view hybrid loss function covering pixel, frequency, perceptual, and gradient domains is designed, enabling the model to effectively capture high-frequency, fine-grained pathological features during reconstruction tasks. By integrating Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA), the model efficiently transfers pretrained knowledge to downstream tasks by updating only approximately 3% of its parameters, effectively mitigating overfitting risks under data scarcity conditions. Extensive experiments demonstrate that this framework exhibits significant performance advantages across various data scales. Particularly in the highly challenging one-shot scenario, its ROC-AUC and PR-AUC reach 82.1% and 82.8%, respectively. The performance exceeds general visual foundation models and traditional supervised learning models by over 14%. Results indicate that for extracting fine-grained fish pathological features, small-scale domain-specific pretraining yields more discriminative representations than large-scale general transfer learning. This study reveals a very promising strategy other than foundation models to address data scarcity for digital fish disease surveillance.

title: Prediction performance analysis of spatial interpolation methods for indoor environmental factors in the plant factory
abstract: This study aims to predict indoor environmental factors at unobserved points in a plant factory with the use of spatial interpolation and analyze their prediction performance. The research process consists of four steps. (i) Step 1: Data & Setting: Plant factory and sensor monitoring; (ii) Step 2: Predict indoor environmental factors at unobserved points using spatial interpolation; (iii) Step 3: Validate the prediction performance of spatial interpolation; (iv) Step 4: Visualize spatial interpolation results. As the best result of validating the prediction performance of the spatial interpolation methods, the CV(RMSE) of the inverse distance weighting method (IDW) was 2.06%, and that of the radial basis function interpolation (RBF) was 1.90%. These results indicate the following two trends: (i) As the maximum and minimum deviations of sensor measurements decrease, IDW exhibits excellent prediction performance, while RBF does not show consistent tendency; and (ii) both IDW and RBF tend to show better prediction performance in indoor air temperature and CO2 concentration as the distance between sensors decreases. Furthermore, as the distance between sensors increased, both IDW and RBF showed better prediction performance at relative humidity. In addition, the uneven distribution of indoor environmental factors was intuitively confirmed via visualization of the spatial interpolation results. It is expected that this study will be able to establish facility operation strategies to create a uniform growing environment through visualization of spatial interpolation results in the plant factory.

title: PB-DETR: multi-behaviour recognition of group-housed pigs with adaptive liquid neural network encoder and dynamic supervision
abstract: The behavioural recognition of group-housed pigs constitutes a fundamental pillar for animal health monitoring and precision feeding within the realm of intelligent husbandry. However, environmental complexities—including fluctuating illumination, occlusion interference, and significant scale variations across the full growth cycle—severely constrain the generalisation capabilities of existing models. To address these challenges, this paper proposes PB-DETR, featuring a redesigned encoder and loss function within the framework. Inspired by time series, we innovatively propose an adaptive liquid time constant enhancement (ALTE) network in image data, integrate the liquid time constant (LTC) mechanism into the Transformer-based encoder, and introduce a dynamic enhancement module to exploit the temporal modelling capabilities of LTC. By projecting 2D image features into a characteristic evolution space and solving ordinary differential equations (ODEs) inspired by biologically motivated neural dynamics, this module simulates the continuous non-linear evolution of features along the spatial dimension, thereby effectively alleviating the model’s dependence on background information. Building upon this enhanced representation, a Nexus Pyramid Network (NPN) is further constructed to resolve scale inconsistencies across feature maps. By employing a two-stage iterative refinement strategy and focal feature units with dilated receptive fields, the NPN establishes bidirectional semantic interaction pathways across multi-scale features, ensuring robust and accurate spatial perception of pigs across varying sizes. With respect to the loss function, a Dynamic Quality Boost Loss (DQBL) is proposed, which adopts an exponential moving average (EMA)-based dynamic benchmark to evaluate the relative quality of predictions with respect to the model’s current performance, and adaptively adjusts prediction weights to guide continuous optimisation. To rigorously evaluate the reliability of the model’s generalisation, this study developed a large-scale dataset encompassing four typical husbandry environments. Beyond performance comparisons on standard validation sets, independent cross-dataset inference tests were conducted across four heterogeneous scenarios. The results demonstrate that PB-DETR outperforms state-of-the-art methods across key metrics, achieving an mAP of 0.893 while maintaining low computational overhead, with 14.58 M parameters and 49.12 GFLOPs. This validates its practical utility and potential for deployment in complex farming scenarios.

title: Stereo vision controlled variable rate sprayer equipped with an automatic electric variable air assist system
abstract: • Stereo vision system detected canopy volumes and presence of apple trees in real time. • The system adjusted air assist and spray outputs of a sprayer with detection results. • The sprayer applied less spray and air volumes compared to a conventional sprayer. • The sprayer increased spray deposits up to 105.8% compared to a conventional sprayer. • The sprayer reduced spray drifts up to 77.4% compared to a conventional sprayer.

title: Graphs that know who started it: Role recognition in Pigs’ interactions
abstract: Social interactions among group-housed farm animals are important welfare indicators in housing systems. Computer vision approaches are emerging as important tools to detect, classify, and quantify interactive farm animal behaviors. However, because of their focus on appearance features (e.g. background, motion blur, etc.) convolutional recurrent neural network approaches struggle to capture the complex, role-specific dynamics of one-to-one interactions such as fighting, feeder displacement, and tail biting, among others, often capturing only the distinction between fast-moving and slow-moving behaviors. In this study, we propose a graph-based neural network (HeteroGNN) to model and classify both spatial and temporal relationships among key body landmarks of interacting pig pairs. Our method encodes a carefully engineered set of kinematic features into a graph structure, effectively capturing behaviors expressed through various movements over different durations. The model simultaneously classifies the interaction category (e.g. tail biting) and predicts individual roles (aggressor vs. victim) through a hierarchical two-level classification allowing targeted intervention for aggressors or victims. Validation of the model demonstrated good performance in behavior recognition, achieving an average F1-score of 94%. It was also able to demonstrate strong capabilities in discerning the role of each individual in one-to-one interactions, with an average F1-score of 90%. Testing on unseen farm environment yielded better generalization performance than a convolutional recurrent neural network (CRNN) model. Specifically, the CRNN, which relied on appearance features, experienced a 50% performance drop from validation to test environments, whereas our approach showed only a 12% drop. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of graph-based representations in discerning asymmetric interactions in pigs. Our framework lays the groundwork for more nuanced, role-aware animal welfare monitoring systems. More information and data are available at: M3-BIORES/Public/M3PIG·GitLab.

title: From passive contact to active Regulation: A Multi-Sensor-Based adaptive buffer pipeline system for Low-Damage apple collection
abstract: • Inspired by biological valve mechanism, an adaptive buffer pipeline system for apples is developed. • A multi-sensor fusion adaptive control method is proposed for precise apple buffering. • Optimal structural parameters are obtained via PB test, CCD and NSGA-II multi-objective optimization. • Bench and field tests confirm the system’s low damage rate and excellent harvesting efficiency.

title: Interactive trajectory refinement: A human–robot collaborative framework for continuous navigation skill evolution in stacked-cage farming houses
abstract: In spatially constrained stacked-cage farming houses (SCFHs), mobile robots that rely on static learning from demonstration (LfD) often fail because environmental dynamics render pre-recorded paths obsolete. We present interactive trajectory refinement (ITR), a human–robot collaborative framework that enables navigation skills to evolve as farm conditions change. The framework has two main components: (1) a route-refinement mechanism through which non-expert operators can provide “corrective demonstrations” during real-time intervention and write those corrections back into the stored route through topological stitching and B-spline kinematic repair; and (2) an adaptive controller arbitrator based on a multi-armed bandit (MAB) model, which selects policies from a heterogeneous controller pool using reward-driven switching while balancing tracking fidelity and operational safety. Experiments in simulation and physical environments, including an operational SCFH, showed that the Meta-MAB arbitrator handled complex trajectories on which several fixed-policy controllers failed or degraded markedly. During field deployment, the system executed an autonomous 537.9m round trip with high-fidelity tracking, maintaining a root-mean-square cross-track error of 3.6cm. The ITR workflow reduced active human maintenance time by 86.7% compared with traditional re-teaching methods, reducing reliance on expert retraining for route maintenance in resource-constrained agricultural settings.

title: SGHOA-VMD-based vibration characteristic analysis of an agricultural tractor under idle conditions
abstract: Tractor idle vibration signals are characterized by intense broadband noise and pronounced non-stationarity, posing challenges for traditional decomposition algorithms that rely on empirically determined parameters. To address these limitations, this study integrates Singer chaotic initialization and Gaussian random-walk perturbation into the Hiking Optimization Algorithm (HOA), resulting in the Singer-Gaussian HOA (SGHOA). The minimum joint Shannon entropy is employed as the fitness function, enabling SGHOA to globally optimize both the mode number and iteration count for Variational Mode Decomposition (VMD). This approach yields the SGHOA-VMD denoising scheme. Simulation results demonstrate its effectiveness: the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) improves by 6.65 dB, the root-mean-square error (RMSE) decreases by 0.1947, and the correlation coefficient (Cor) rises by 0.1553. Additionally, 90.66% of the signal energy is concentrated in the last intrinsic mode function (IMF), indicating robust energy aggregation and noise suppression. Field tests corroborate these findings, with the relative variation ratio (RVR) reduced by 2.3785, the signal energy ratio (SER) increased to 9.084 dB, and the noise mode (NM) lowered to 0.3313. Moreover, 92.99% of the primary energy is compressed into a single IMF, and repeated experiments further verified the stability and consistency of the SGHOA-VMD algorithm. Compared to VMD, Empirical Mode Decomposition (EMD), and Ensemble Empirical Mode Decomposition (EEMD), SGHOA-VMD exhibits superior performance in modal orthogonality, energy concentration, and signal fidelity.

title: Development and application of a deep learning (SF-TPP)-based intelligent detection system for granular fertilizer deposition distribution patterns
abstract: The performance evaluation of fertilizer spreaders is essential for improving the efficiency and accuracy of fertilizer application in modern agriculture. Traditional methods, such as manual collection boxes, are time-consuming, labor-intensive, and unsuitable for intelligent agricultural systems. To address these limitations, this study proposes a deep learning-based intelligent detection system for analyzing granular fertilizer deposition distribution patterns. The system integrates image acquisition, data processing, visualization, and storage functions, enabling real-time detection and operational optimization. A novel segmentation model, SF-TPP, was developed by combining a swin transformer backbone with a path aggregation network (PANet), region proposal network (RPN), ROI alignment, and enhanced by CBAM and feature refinement modules. Comparative experiments demonstrated that SF-TPP outperformed conventional models (F-TPP, SOLO, YOLOv5), achieving 92.8% precision, 91.3% recall, and an F1 score of 0.920. A strong correlation (R2 = 0.9626) was established between pixel area and fertilizer mass, enabling accurate mass estimation. Field experiments showed that the system achieved low mean absolute errors in key metrics, including a CV MAE of 0.99 and a fertilization amount MAE of 0.76 g. These results demonstrate the system’s high accuracy and practical potential for supporting precision agriculture.

title: Autonomous construction of crop pest and disease knowledge graphs at scale via LLM-driven expert modeling
abstract: Crop pests and diseases pose a serious threat to global food security, which create an urgent need for rapid and accurate plant protection strategies. Much of the domain knowledge required for such intervention, however, remains scattered across heterogeneous and largely unstructured literature. This fragmentation limits the effective use of agricultural data in intelligent diagnosis and decision support, and it has increased the demand for high quality domain specific knowledge graphs. Existing approaches to agricultural knowledge graph construction still rely heavily on manual or partially automated curation, which restricts the efficient use of unstructured multi-source data and slows the incorporation of updated domain knowledge. To address these limitations, this study presents CropKG, an autonomous AI driven framework for reconstructing the knowledge engineering workflow in agricultural protection. Unlike conventional semi-automated approaches, CropKG integrates automated prompt engineering with expert oriented role modeling. By encoding agronomic reasoning patterns and combining them with bottom-up ontology induction, the framework supports autonomous extraction of complex entity relations from long agricultural documents while reducing unsupported generation in large language models. The effectiveness of the framework is demonstrated through the construction of a large-scale domain knowledge graph containing more than 17,000 nodes. Experimental results show that CropKG achieves an F1 score above 90% in entity and relation extraction and outperforms strong universal extraction baselines. The framework also supports decision-oriented applications by enabling traceable and evidence constrained retrieval of pest control knowledge. These results indicate that autonomous knowledge graph construction provides a practical path from raw agricultural text to structured and actionable intelligence for precision plant protection.

title: Machine learning-based multivariate time-series forecasting for environmental monitoring in pig houses under high stochasticity
abstract: Ammonia gas concentration in intensive swine production pose serious environmental and health challenges, particularly in naturally ventilated systems. This study presents an application-oriented comparative evaluation of eight state-of-the-art forecasting models to predict NH 3 concentrations in a commercial pig house. First a factorial design assessed the impact of covariates, resolution time, window lengths, and pre-processing. Results identified data preprocessing as the primary driver of model accuracy, where causal non-centered smoothing significantly outperformed aggressive outlier removal, and the exclusion of non-essential covariates for predictions. Among the architectures, TiDE and D-Linear excelled in short-term forecasting. Targeted optimization of the TiDE model using only past covariates achieved an R 2 of 0.895 ± 0.005 and a Mean Absolute Error of 0.150 ± 0.012 for a 30-minute horizon, representing an improvement in variance explanation over the unoptimized baseline. For longer 60-minute horizons, models relying solely on past covariates showed diminishing returns; the optimized linear model (D-Linear) improved its R 2 to 0.507 ± 0.005, while the deep TiDE architecture plateaued at an R 2 of 0.583 ± 0.062. However, integrating future weather covariates proved essential for the Temporal Fusion Transformer (TFT), which utilized these inputs to stabilize multi-horizon forecasts, achieving a highly stable R 2 of 0.88 ± 0 at 30 min and maintaining a robust R 2 of 0.665 ± 0.015 at the challenging 60-minute horizon. These findings suggest a hybrid Precision Livestock Farming framework: employing optimized lightweight models like TiDE for immediate, real-time ventilation control, while reserving attention-based architectures enriched with meteorological forecasts for extended operational planning.

title: Early and stage-specific detection of Magnaporthe oryzae on rice leaves using hyperspectral imaging and feature-based machine learning
abstract: Rice blast, caused by Magnaporthe oryzae, is a major threat to rice production, initiating subtle biochemical and structural changes in rice tissues before visible symptoms develop. This study applied hyperspectral imaging combined with Fisher discriminant feature selection and machine learning to monitor rice blast progression over six consecutive days following pathogen inoculation. Based on symptom development, the infection process was categorized into three stages: (i) a latent asymptomatic stage (Days 1–2), during which plants remained visually indistinguishable from healthy controls; (ii) a very early symptomatic transition stage (Day 3), characterized by faint chlorosis, minor pigment non-uniformity, and microscopic pre-lesion points; and (iii) a progressive symptomatic stage (Days 4–6), marked by the gradual development of visible chlorotic halos and well-defined elliptical necrotic lesions. Feature importance analysis revealed that texture descriptors (energy, entropy, correlation, RMS, variance) were the most sensitive indicators during the latent stage, capturing oxidative stress and early chlorophyll destabilization primarily within the green reflectance region (430–580 nm). Descriptive statistical features (maximum, mean, median) became increasingly relevant during the early symptomatic phase (460–660 nm), reflecting progressive pigment degradation and water-content reduction. Shape-based descriptors (leaf area, perimeter, major/minor axis, circularity) were most informative in advanced stages (850–950 nm), when visible lesions expanded and tissue structure deteriorated. During the latent phase (Days 1–2), when no visual symptoms were present, RF achieved detection accuracies of 34.18% and 67.50% on Days 1 and 2, respectively, compared with SVM (25.80%, 54.50%), k-NN (20.10%, 43.30%), and DT (18.40%, 35.90%). As the disease advanced and visible symptoms began to appear, RF detection accuracy increased to 90.06%-93.19% on Days 3–4 and 96.32%-100% on Days 5–6. Hyperspectral analysis further revealed progressive spectral divergence in key wavelength regions (430–470 nm, 540–580 nm, 610–660 nm, and 850–950 nm), enabling sensitive detection during latent and very early symptomatic stages before lesion development. These results demonstrate that the integration of texture, color, and shape features enables precise, stage-specific detection of rice blast from pre-symptomatic infection to advanced disease manifestation.

title: Numerical Simulation of Fruit-Leaf Separation Process in Column-comb Vibration Harvesting of Litchi Based on CFD-DEM
abstract: To address the issue of high impurity levels, such as leaves and fruit stalks in litchi harvesting, this study proposes a pneumatic impurity removal device and integrates it into a litchi column-comb vibration harvester to reduce fruit impurity content and improve harvesting efficiency. By analyzing the airflow motion characteristics of the impurity removal device and the movement of leaves under airflow, the structural and operating parameters of the device were determined. A CFD–DEM coupled simulation model for fruit–leaf impurity removal was established to simulated and analyzed the motion characteristics and separation behavior of litchi fruits and leaves within the device. Using the impurity rate of the impurity removal device and the fruit collection rate as evaluation indices, a three-factor, three-level virtual response surface design simulation experiment was conducted to optimize the parameters, yielding the optimal combination: airflow velocity of the impurity removal device of 9.8 m/s, lateral inclination angle of 15.00°, and forward inclination angle of 7.10°. Under these conditions, the impurity rate of the impurity removal device of the harvester was 8.50%, the fruit collection rate was 91.55%, and the impurity rate of fruits in the collection box was 5.56%. Orchard harvesting tests showed that the impurity rate of the impurity removal device was 9.12%, the fruit collection rate was 90.86%, and the impurity rate of fruits in the collection box was 2.50% in the optimized harvester; the relative errors of the fruit collection rate and the impurity rate of the impurity removal device were 0.75% and 6.80%, respectively. High-speed camera bench tests on litchi fruit–leaf separation demonstrated that the motion directions and trajectories of litchi fruits and leaves under airflow were generally consistent with the simulation results, which to a certain extent verified the reliability of the coupled CFD–DEM simulation for litchi fruit–leaf impurity removal. This study provides a theoretical basis and reference for the design, analysis, and optimization of pneumatic impurity removal devices.

title: Knowledge-informed Gaussian process regression with agronomic priors for variable-rate nitrogen management in cereal crops
abstract: Empirical response curves often oversimplify yield-nitrogen (N) dynamics, while purely data-driven models like extreme gradient boosting (XGB) can be physically implausible and provide limited uncertainty guidance. A more reliable approach is needed, one that is both accurate and consistent with agronomic laws. This study introduces a knowledge-informed Gaussian process regression (KI-GPR) model that embeds a quadratic yield-N relationship within a Bayesian Gaussian process, adapting the law of diminishing returns and acknowledging toxicity at excessive N rates while learning from soil covariates. The study uses on-farm precision experimentation (OFPE) datasets from four arable fields in Flanders with soil properties measured by an online visible and near-infrared (vis-NIR) spectra sensing platform and laboratory analyses. Three models are compared, namely, a clustered empirical quadratic, a purely data-driven XGB regressor, and the proposed KI-GPR that learns soil-dependent parameters while constraining the response with agronomic priors. All three models are evaluated and compared using both statistical (coeffecient of determination [R2] = 0.86; root mean square error [RMSE] = 0.024 kg kg−1; and ration of performance to interquartile distance [RPIQ] = 3.920) and agricultural metrics (N-response curves and marginal yield curves). KI-GPR is found to outperform both empirical polynomial model (EMP) and XGB models, producing smooth, agronomically credible response curves and continuous optimal-N distributions. It also provides uncertainty quantification, which enables risk-aware recommendations and highlights data gaps. The approach is well-suited for variable-rate N management, decision support, and targeted experimental design.

title: A deep reinforcement learning-guided memetic algorithm for multi-objective collaborative scheduling of agricultural weeding robot fleets
abstract: The rapid deployment of intelligent unmanned systems is accelerating the transformation of precision agriculture. However, achieving autonomous, energy-efficient, and workload-balanced collaboration among heterogeneous weeding robot fleets in large-scale and structurally complex farmlands remains challenging. This study addresses a multi-objective collaborative scheduling problem for agricultural weeding robot fleets, aiming to minimize total travel distance, total energy consumption, and workload imbalance among robots. The problem is NP-hard, and conventional evolutionary approaches often suffer from limited adaptability due to static operator usage in complex search environments. To overcome these limitations, a deep reinforcement learning-guided memetic algorithm (DRL-MA) is developed. A dueling double deep Q-network is embedded within a Pareto-based memetic framework, where operator selection is formulated as a Markov decision process to enable adaptive exploration–exploitation balance. The framework further incorporates task-priority-based encoding, feasibility-preserving decoding, and a multi-stage hybrid heuristic initialization strategy to enhance convergence and solution diversity. Extensive experiments on benchmark smart-farm scenarios and a real-farm case study demonstrate that DRL-MA outperforms representative evolutionary, reinforcement-learning-assisted, and recent learning-based baselines. In the benchmark experiments, DRL-MA improves the mean hypervolume by approximately 11.7% and reduces the mean inverted generational distance by approximately 64.2% compared with the strongest competing algorithm. In the real-farm case study, DRL-MA contributes 78.31% of the globally non-dominated solutions, indicating stronger overall Pareto competitiveness. Moreover, runtime and scalability analyses show that the proposed method remains computationally feasible as the problem scale increases. These results indicate that DRL-MA provides an effective, scalable, and practically applicable scheduling approach for collaborative weeding robot fleets in smart farming.

title: Entropy-weighted spectrogram for enhanced watermelon quality inspection
abstract: Non-destructive detection of watermelon internal quality is critical for reducing postharvest loss, but existing acoustic inspection methods face challenges from redundant features and inflexible time–frequency resolution. To address these limitations, this study proposes an Entropy-Weighted Spectrogram (EWS) feature extraction method tailored to watermelon percussion response signals. By integrating spectral energy and spectral entropy into a composite metric, EWS dynamically quantifies the discriminative importance of frequency components and enables adaptive allocation of spectral resolution, thereby emphasizing informative bands while suppressing redundancy. Compared with representative conventional time–frequency features, EWS provides a compact and signal-adaptive acoustic representation while improving classification performance.
