Using the extracted EWS features, a stacking ensemble model achieved an overall accuracy of 93.59% in classifying four internal quality states: immature, mature, over-mature, and hollow. Further feature-level and short-term postharvest analyses indicated that EWS band features provided additional information related to internal quality variation and storage-related acoustic changes. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of EWS for acoustic-based non-destructive watermelon quality inspection and support its potential use as a compact feature representation for agricultural sensing.

title: HyperStitch: A high-quality stitching method for unmanned aerial vehicle hyperspectral images
abstract: Unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) hyperspectral imaging technology, renowned for its high spatial and spectral resolution, has found extensive applications in various fields, including environmental monitoring, disaster assessment, and precision agriculture. Effective utilization of these hyperspectral images (HSIs) for downstream applications requires robust hyperspectral image (HSI) stitching. However, existing stitching methods hampered by three critical challenges: unreliable feature matching under complex scenarios, illumination-induced spectral distortions, and registration-error artifacts in blended results. To address these challenges, this study proposes HyperStitch, an innovative seamless HSI stitching method that integrates auxiliary image generation using Multidimensional Multiclass Genetic Programming Band Selection and Fusion Method (M3GPBS-FM), spectral correction based on multi-scale Retinex, and optimal seamline estimation based on seamline quality evaluation. First, the M3GPBS-FM performs band fusion on HSIs, generating auxiliary images that enhance feature extraction and matching, providing reliable tie points for image registration. Next, an improved multi-scale Retinex spectral correction method, based on guided filtering, ensures spectral consistency within overlapping regions of adjacent flight routes. Finally, an optimal seamline estimation strategy, informed by seamline quality evaluation, mitigates visual artifacts and facilitates a seamless transition between stitched images. The proposed method was validated using hyperspectral datasets from 22 UAV flight routes. Experimental results demonstrate that HyperStitch outperforms state-of-the-art methods across all metrics. Compared to Optimal Neighborhood Reconstruction (ONR), HyperStitch improves the inlier ratios of feature matching by 41.55%. In terms of image quality, our method increases the Structural Similarity Index (SSIM) by 2.88% in overlapping regions and by 1.39% along seams over the Optimal Seamline Detection via Graph Cuts (OSDGC) algorithm. For spectral consistency, HyperStitch significantly reduces distortion compared to the Intrinsic Decomposition-Based (IDB) method: 27.73% lower Root Mean Square Error (RMSE), 27.23% lower Euclidean Distance (ED), and 7.84% lower Spectral Information Divergence (SID), along with a 5.00% improvement in Spectral Angle Mapper (SAM).

title: Vision-based livestock pose estimation for precision livestock farming: a systematic review and design framework
abstract: Camera-based pose estimation is becoming a key sensing approach for automated livestock monitoring, yet the selection of camera geometry, keypoint schema, learning model, and deployment strategy remains highly heterogeneous across species and applications. This systematic review synthesised the literature published or available online between 1 January 2015 and 31 December 2025 to identify task-aligned design patterns, reporting gaps, and practical routes toward on-farm implementation. Searches of ScienceDirect, Scopus, Web of Science, and Embase identified 273 records. After duplicate removal, eligibility screening, and methodological quality appraisal, 114 studies were included in the final synthesis. The reviewed literature shows that cattle and pigs dominate the field, while poultry, horses, goats, sheep, camels, and cross-species studies remain comparatively under-represented. Across applications, side-view RGB is most consistently suited to gait and lameness analysis, whereas fixed top-down RGB offers the best trade-off for group-level behaviour, feeding, tracking, and identity-related tasks. Stereo, RGB-D, and multi-view systems are most justified when the target output depends on absolute geometry, persistent occlusion handling, or three-dimensional posture recovery, particularly in body measurement and weight-estimation pipelines. The synthesis further shows that performance depends more on task-camera-keypoint alignment than on any single model family. However, progress toward robust deployment is limited by inconsistent landmark definitions, fragmented datasets, heterogeneous evaluation metrics, and insufficient reporting of runtime, calibration burden, and farm-system integration. A task-oriented reporting structure and preliminary species-specific core keypoint guidance are therefore proposed to improve comparability and reuse. Overall, livestock pose estimation is sufficiently mature for several structured farm applications, but broader adoption will depend on stronger standardisation, more diverse multi-site datasets, and more explicit validation under real operational conditions.

title: Optimal grasping direction of a flexible gripper and its RGB-D multimodal estimation method
abstract: In mechanized apple harvesting, when a gripper neglects the spatial orientation of apples and applies a fixed grasping direction, harvesting interference is likely to occur, and finger force imbalance results in grasp slippage and fruit damage. Existing studies on grasping direction primarily rely on heuristic geometric assumptions and lack quantitative criteria for direction selection. To address these limitations, this study establishes a closed-loop framework for optimal grasping direction determination, integrating mechanical definition, deviation adaptability quantification, multimodal online estimation, and mobile platform validation. Based on the biological characteristics of naturally grown apples, the constraints associated with pose deviation and cluster interference are explicitly identified for grasping direction selection. Grasping experiments and mechanical analysis demonstrate that the direction aligned with the stem–navel connection is the optimal grasping direction in terms of contact stress distribution, lateral slip, and separation force. Furthermore, a YOLOv11–ViTPose-SNC–RGB-D multimodal direction estimation framework is developed to achieve real-time estimation of the optimal grasping direction and is systematically evaluated using angular deviation, spherical arc-length error, and temporal stability. The proposed framework is then integrated into a mobile harvesting platform and validated through field experiments. The results indicate that the system achieves low directional error with good real-time performance and stability: more than 75% of the samples exhibit spherical arc-length errors within 1 cm, the harvesting success rate reaches 96.66%, and the damage rate is 0%. The method presented in this study offers a reusable design and evaluation paradigm for mechanized apple harvesting.

title: Accurate individual-tree aboveground biomass estimation via physics-guided machine learning on UAV-based LiDAR and multispectral data
abstract: Accurate estimation of individual-tree above-ground biomass (AGB) is critical for assessing carbon storage at fine-scale. Current methods are constrained because traditional approaches underuse structural information, and purely machine learning (ML) models often overfit and lack ecological plausibility with limited in-situ samples. To address the limitations, this study develops a physics-guided machine learning (PGML) method that synergistically infuses tree allometric equations with ML. The model utilizes structural and biophysical features derived from Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) Light Detection and Ranging (LiDAR) and multispectral data. Validation with in-situ measurements shows that the PGML model achieved high accuracy across three tree species (Larch, Mongolian Scots Pine, and Populus), with coefficients of determination (R2) of 0.80, 0.87, and 0.88, and root mean square errors (RMSE) of 8.14 kg, 9.56 kg, and 17.67 kg, respectively. The model also maintained low physical inconsistency ratios (PIR: 9.3, 9.84, 10.85) and outperformed three traditional methods by 12% to 18% in accuracy. Cross-regional direct transfer of the PGML model achieved R2 values of 0.43–0.73 in new plots. The primary innovation of this work is the effective fusion of physical growth mechanisms with data-driven ML, which concurrently enhances the predictive accuracy, stability, and ecological interpretability of individual-tree AGB estimation in complex forest stands.

title: Improving cotton biomass estimation by assimilating SAR data into a modified crop growth model with simple calibration
abstract: Aboveground biomass density (AGBD) is a key indicator in agricultural systems, directly reflecting crop carbon storage potential and yield levels. The World Food Studies (WOFOST) model is widely used for crop growth simulation due to its process-based interpretability. However, its application is limited by complex calibration demands and struggles with spatial heterogeneity. To address these limitations, this paper proposes an assimilation system that integrates Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) data into a modified WOFOST model, which requires simple calibration. WOFOST is run in potential production mode, which assumes ideal conditions to reduce input data requirements. Before assimilation, phenology-related temperature sums are aligned with phenology and meteorological data to match local growth stages. Two quantities are then estimated and updated in the model through data assimilation by minimizing the difference between SAR-derived and simulated AGBD. These quantities are the proposed yield reduction factor, which represents the proportional decrease in potential CO 2 assimilation under stresses, and the initial total dry weight at sowing. Validation experiments were conducted using multi-year cotton datasets from two farms in Georgia, USA, differing in whether irrigation was applied. Compared to WOFOST simulations and evaluated against in situ AGBD measurements, the assimilation results improve agreement and reduce error (approximately 43% RMSE reduction at the rainfed site and 15% at the irrigated site). It also delivers spatial maps of biomass, together with model-derived yield and harvest-index diagnostics, and remains operational under frequent cloud cover where optical observations are sparse. This SAR-based assimilation strategy reduces calibration demands, providing a novel and practical pathway to extend WOFOST applications to diverse agricultural scenarios.

title: Sensitivity of air exchange rate and airflow pattern to incoming wind angle in a naturally ventilated dairy barn under varying convection flow regimes
abstract: The precise determination of Greenhouse gas (GHG) emission is a paramount topic in nowadays research and society. In the case of naturally ventilated dairy barns, on-farm measurements are always accompanied with high uncertainties caused by dynamic weather conditions, animal activities, and the diversity of the barns’ dimensions and geometries. This poses an emerging challenge to mitigate emissions since mitigation measures can only be effective with in-depth knowledge about the gas emission process, ventilation performance, and the airflow patterns. We deployed computational fluid dynamics (CFD) models to investigate the relationship between incoming wind angle and the air exchange rate (AER) of a typical symmetrical dairy barn under three types of convection flow regime. In parallel, the flow pattern at three different heights were compared using the image analysis metric mean square error (MSE). We discovered that for natural convection the AER deviation is around 18% on average for different wind angles. For mixed and force convection, the AER deviation was below 30% for wind angles until 60°. Also, a critical wind angle round 63° was found, from which the wind angle strongly influenced the AER deviation as the forced convection became stronger. The analysis of the MSE values for the considered cases at the three heights showed similar variations in the airflow pattern. In conclusion, considering a wind corridor of up to +/- 60° relative to the crossflow can be considered reasonable for on-farm air exchange rate measurements.

title: Development and multiple cultivation seasons evaluation of a temperature-driven process-based model for tomato growth and yield in greenhouse conditions
abstract: As climate change intensifies, extreme environmental conditions increasingly threaten stable crop production, highlighting the need for reliable greenhouse management and accurate yield prediction. This study developed and evaluated a temperature-driven process-based model to simulate tomato ( Solanum lycopersicum L.) growth and yield under greenhouse conditions in Korea. The model was developed using data from the 2022–2023 season and evaluated using independent datasets from the 2023–2024 and 2024–2025 seasons. The model incorporates key developmental processes, including stem elongation, leaf emergence and leaf defoliation, fruit truss development, and harvest dynamics. It showed strong agreement with observed data for major growth variables, including stem length, leaf emergence, and fruit truss number ( R 2 > 0.96; nRMSE = 5.93–11.83%). For fruit yield, the model successfully reproduced the temporal patterns of cumulative yield across all cultivation seasons, showing strong agreement between observed and predicted values. It also demonstrated acceptable performance based on error metrics ( R 2 = 0.86–0.89; nRMSE = 17.50–22.80%). However, a consistent tendency toward overestimation was observed across cultivation seasons. Photo-physiological analyses, including chlorophyll fluorescence and pigment measurements, were conducted independently to interpret plant responses to environmental variation. Although these variables were not directly included in the model, their relationships with growth and yield helped interpret model uncertainty and potential directions for improvement. Overall, the results demonstrate that a simplified temperature-driven modeling approach can effectively capture major growth and yield dynamics of tomato under greenhouse conditions. The model provides a practical framework for greenhouse crop modeling with reduced input requirements, while highlighting the need to incorporate additional environmental and management factors to further improve prediction accuracy.

title: RO-RSMD: A region-optimized random shuffling multi-process combined degradation method for image super-resolution in free-range poultry farms
abstract: Low-resolution video images in free-range poultry environments pose challenges for advanced visual tasks, and image super-resolution (SR) technology can effectively address this challenge by enhancing image quality. However, research on super-resolution for free-range poultry farms is limited, and existing methods do not adequately consider the impact of the degradation process. This study explores the application of mainstream image super-resolution algorithms and degradation methods in free-range poultry farms. Specifically, we propose a Region-Optimized Random Shuffling Multi-Process Combined Degradation method (RO-RSMD) to address the issue of increased training time caused by redundant background information in high-resolution images. The degradation method combines a Patch-wise classification Vision Transformer (Pw-ViT) for patch-level classification and a Sliding Matching and Adaptive Region Replacement (SMART-R) for holistic background region replacement. Eight low-resolution datasets from diverse real-world were collected to evaluate RO-RSMD. Experimental results demonstrate that RO-RSMD achieves superior restoration performance with significantly reduced training time. Quantified analysis from training curves shows that RO-RSMD achieves training efficiency advantages in most configurations, with average training time savings of approximately 30–40% compared to the baseline method, and savings exceeding 60% in some configurations. Additionally, ablation experiments validate the effectiveness of the Pw-ViT module, with accuracy improvements of 11.4% and 13.8% and F1 score improvements of 10.2% and 8.8% for 1024 and 2048 pixel input images, respectively. Comparative experiments demonstrate that RO-RSMD achieves the best restoration results with superior generalization across different datasets.

title: An innovative approach to SCC prediction in cow’s milk using a low-cost RF/MW dielectric probe combined with DWT-CNN model
abstract: The key to online detection of somatic cell count (SCC) in cow’s milk based on radio frequency/microwave technology lies in reducing the cost of dielectric probes and improving model accuracy. This study proposed a quantitative method for milk SCC using a low-cost helix-electrode dielectric probe (HEDP) combined with a deep learning model. However, the influence of SCC on the milk S-parameter spectrum measured by HEDP and the predictive accuracy of this method remain unclear. The S-parameter spectra (20-4500 MHz) of milk samples with different SCC were measured with HEDP. Subsequently, the influence of SCC on the S-parameter spectrum (S11, S21) and their correlation characteristics were analyzed. A novel convolutional neural network (CNN) model integrating the discrete wavelet transform (DWT) was developed to predict milk SCC. The results indicated that the electromagnetic coupling between the HEDP and milk exhibited multiple-resonance characteristics. At the resonance frequencies, SCC showed positive and negative correlations with S11 and S21 spectra, respectively. A strong nonlinear relationship was observed between SCC and the S-parameter spectra (APaRPs: |Z|=8.571). The DWT-CNN model outperformed both CNN and chemometric models. The HEDP combined with DWT-CNN for milk SCC detection achieved good performance (RMSE: 0.163 log SCC/mL, RPD: 2.51). This method was low-cost and high-precision, and the probe was easy to calibrate and clean, making it suitable for online SCC detection. This study provided a new insight into the low-cost online detection of milk SCC and monitoring of mastitis in dairy cows.

title: High-fidelity finite element modeling method of the maize stubble-soil composite incorporating in-situ geometry and advanced constitutive laws
abstract: Accurate numerical simulation is crucial for developing high-performance conservation tillage equipment, yet existing models of stubble-soil composites oversimplify stubble architecture and constitutive behaviors. This study aims to develop and validate a high-fidelity finite element method (FEM) of maize stubble-soil composites incorporating realistic geometry and advanced constitutive laws . The in-situ 3D architecture of maize stubble was reconstructed via X-ray computed tomography (CT) scanning of an an intact stubble-soil composite sample. The fiber-reinforced stubble’s basal stalk was modeled as an orthotropic elastic-damage material calibrated via longitudinal and transverse tension, compression, and shear tests. The quasi-brittle failure behavior of desiccated roots was represented with an isotropic damage-plasticity model achieved by specific calibration of its ultimate tensile strength and damage parameters. Soil was modeled using the Drucker–Prager criterion with parameters derived from triaxial compression tests. The cohesive-frictional behavior of the root–soil interface was described using a Coulomb friction law incorporating critical shear stress and a friction coefficient calibrated via direct shear tests. The integrated FEM was validated against physical direct cutting tests under confined pressure at multiple locations. Simulations of the direct cutting process demonstrated exceptional predictive accuracy, showing excellent agreement with experimental force–displacement curves—exhibiting minimal average errors of only 0.78% in peak cutting force and 4.31% in absorbed energy across all tests. This validated modeling method provides unprecedented insights into intricate contact interactions among the cutting tool, soil, and root system for a specific scenario, serving as a powerfulin-silicotool for optimizing tillage equipment design and advancing sustainable soil management practices.

title: CoPix-Row: Structure-aware synthetic data generation for semantic segmentation in precision agriculture
abstract: Pixel-level annotation for satellite-imagery-based semantic segmentation is costly, especially for thin and structured targets such as one-pixel crop-row centerlines. This paper proposes convolutional conditional pixel-level row generation, CoPix-Row, a structure-aware synthetic data pipeline that preserves row topology while producing diverse top-view training tiles. A ControlNet-based diffusion generator is conditioned on centerline masks and guided by a layout alignment loss computed with a fixed Row-UNet so that the generated appearance remains faithful to the input geometry. An optional pix2pix-style refiner further adapts texture and noise statistics toward real satellite imagery. A Row-UNet segmenter trained with mixed real and synthetic tiles is evaluated on 50 held-out real test tiles. CoPix-Row achieves an F1-score of 0.521±0.086 and an IoU of 0.357±0.077, improving over real-only training by 0.041 in F1-score and 0.036 in IoU, and outperforming the strongest naive mixing baseline based on real and ControlNet-generated data. Additional DeepLabV3+ experiments show that the same trend is preserved across segmentation backbones. Rather than acting as a standalone global path planner, the predicted masks provide planner-consumable structural priors that are qualitatively compatible with existing downstream navigation processes. These results suggest that structure-aware synthesis can reduce labeling burden and improve the reliability of satellite-imagery-based agricultural navigation support under limited real-data conditions.

title: PlantDiff: A diffusion model for high-fidelity plant image generation with Discrete Wavelet Transform and Context-Augmented Cross Attention
abstract: In recent years, deep learning technologies have achieved remarkable progress in agricultural applications, yet their performance heavily relies on large-scale, high-quality datasets and still faces widespread challenges such as data scarcity and class imbalance. To address these issues, data augmentation methods, such as generative adversarial networks or diffusion models, can generate high-quality images, thereby alleviating the limitations caused by insufficient training data. However, several critical challenges persist in plant science: the generated images often lack fine details such as leaf textures and venation patterns, and exhibit structural anomalies like fused leaves or detached stems. These issues lead to discrepancies between the generated and real data distributions, thereby degrading downstream task performance. To tackle these challenges, we propose a novel latent diffusion model framework, termed PlantDiff. First, we design an Attentive Wavelet Feature Fusion (AWFF) module to optimize perceptual compression in diffusion models by decomposing images into high-frequency details and low-frequency global information using Discrete Wavelet Transform (DWT), and enhancing feature integration through an Attention Estimation(AE) and Dynamic Fusion(DF) mechanism, thereby significantly improving the preservation of high-frequency details. Second, we introduce a Context-Augmented Cross Attention (CACA) module into the denoising network. This module captures local stem-leaf relationships using depthwise separable convolutions and extracts global growth structural features through Enhanced Gated Channel Transformation (EGCT), ensuring generated plant morphologies align with natural growth patterns. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our method outperforms baseline models in plant image generation and benefits downstream tasks, with ablation studies confirming its effectiveness. The code of this paper will be available at https://github.com/Chuanyu-Li/PlantDiff.

title: Research on an automatic steering control strategy for unmanned tractors based on IDDPG-PID algorithm
abstract: The effective implementation of high-precision path tracking in unmanned tractors hinges on the performance of the automatic steering control system. However, traditional Proportional Integral Derivative (PID) control algorithms and commonly used optimization variants employed in existing hydraulic steering control systems for unmanned tractors often fall short in maintaining stable, long-term real-time parameter adjustments under the diverse and changing field conditions. To address this limitation, this study proposes a steering control algorithm based on an improved Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient algorithm for online PID parameter optimization (IDDPG-PID). The enhancement focuses on refining the experience replay and sampling mechanism of the standard Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (DDPG) algorithm, thereby enabling adaptive and continuous tuning of PID gains. This approach aims to improve the responsiveness, tracking accuracy, and operational robustness of the steering control system in autonomous tractors. The feasibility and performance of the proposed algorithm were evaluated through AMESim-Simulink co-simulation and field experiments. Simulation results demonstrated that the IDDPG-PID algorithm outperformed both traditional PID algorithm and standard DDPG-PID algorithm in tracking square-wave, sinusoidal, and random signals, exhibiting faster response, higher precision, and enhanced stability. Field experiments results further confirmed its effectiveness, under an initial positional deviation of 2 m, the IDDPG-PID algorithm achieved an alignment distance of 9.36 m and an overshoot of 0.013 m. During straight-line phase, the lateral deviation remained within 0.018 m, with a standard deviation of 0.0061 m. During Ω-turn phase, the system demonstrates faster entry into curves, superior path-holding capability, and rapid post-curve realignment, yielding a lateral deviation standard deviation of 0.093 m and a heading deviation standard deviation of 2.899° throughout the turning process. The IDDPG-PID algorithm surpassed both DDPG-PID algorithm and PID algorithm in path alignment efficiency, straight-line tracking accuracy, and Ω-turn maneuverability. These findings validated the effectiveness of the IDDPG-PID algorithm for steering control under the established upper-level path tracking framework, meeting the precision and robustness requirements for automatic steering control in unmanned tractors.

title: Soybean drought recognition method based on multi-view 3D image Fourier transform
abstract: Drought stress is an important adversity factor for soybean production. Accurate determination of drought is significant for water-saving irrigation and management. Existing low-cost 3D imaging technology based on Kinect sensors can capture the structural and phenotypic changes of plant canopies, but it is difficult to characterize the relationship between the spectral features of soybean 3D images and environmental factors changes. Thus, in this study, a soybean drought recognition method was proposed based on multi-view 3D image Fourier transform. First, the multi-view projection algorithm of the 3D point cloud was used to obtain 21 view projection images based on the depth and color information of the soybean canopy. Second, a discrete Fourier transform was performed to calculate the frequency-domain features of the images in each projection direction. In addition, a quantum genetic algorithm (QGA) was applied to obtain the optimal combination of feature weights. Finally, the features of the optimal projection images were extracted to establish the drought recognition model of soybeans based on a radial basis function (RBF) neural network. The result showed that the model’s recognition accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score were 95.75%, 95.70%, 91.70%, and 93.60%, respectively, and the four evaluation indexes have been improved by 8.39%, 11.57%, 0.2%, and 5.83%, respectively, compared with the back propagation (BP), random forest (RF), and support vector machine (SVM) methods. This research realized rapid and non-destructive detection of drought stress for the soybean plant, and provided a relevant basis and support for soybean water-saving irrigation and cultivation management.

title: CFD-DEM study on threshing characteristics and parameter optimization of corn ears using swirling airflow
abstract: During the harvesting and threshing process of corn ears, the traditional mechanical threshing method can cause damage to the corn kernels, resulting in a high damage rate. To address the aforementioned issues, this study proposes a novel threshing method based on vortex airflow. Using the CFD-DEM coupling method, based on the three-ball bonding model, the connection process of the corn kernel and corn cob was simulated. A discrete element model of the corn ear was created according to the “arrangement law”. By analyzing the movement and force conditions of the corn ear in the vortex airflow, the influence of various experimental factors on the threshing effect was investigated, and the parameters were optimized. Ultimately, high-speed photography was employed to test the experiments and determine the threshing mechanism of corn kernels. The results indicate that the experimental factors have a significant influence on both the threshing effectiveness and the flow field. Furthermore, the interactions among high-velocity airflow rate, intake angle, and the air pipe interval distance significantly affect the evaluation indices. When the optimal parameters were set as an intake angle of 82°, a high-velocity airflow rate of 109 m/s, and an air pipe interval distance of 284 mm, the threshing rate reached 100%, with a damage rate of 0.051%. Through high-speed photography, it was observed that the motion trajectory of corn kernels coincided with that of the vortex airflow. And the threshing process of corn kernels follows the discrete principle of “arrangement units”. When individual kernels become loose and begin to thresh, the arrangement law is disrupted. At that point, corn ears are more readily threshed within the vortex airflow. This study can provide theoretical and technical basis for low-injury corn threshing technology.

title: Digital Twin of a dual-arm autonomous seeding robot for hydroponic greenhouses
abstract: The technological transfer from industrial automation to agriculture in the last decade has accelerated the adoption of advanced tools for improving efficiency, productivity, and sustainability. Among these innovations, Digital Twin (DT) technology has emerged as a promising paradigm for modeling, monitoring, and analyzing complex agri-robotic processes. This article presents the design, implementation, and experimental validation of a DT for a dual-arm autonomous robot dedicated to the seeding process in hydroponic greenhouses. The system integrates a physical hydroponic environment with a virtual replica built in NVIDIA Isaac Sim, enabling simulation-based task testing, trajectory assessment, and hardware-in-the-loop evaluation under controlled geometric and operational conditions. The DT architecture is structured around IoT connectivity using FIWARE components, supporting bidirectional communication between the physical and virtual layers. The dual-arm robot is capable of perception-driven seeding tasks, including planter hole detection, cube positioning, seed collection, and deposition into rock-wool substrates, with collision-free manipulation strategies. The results demonstrate that the DT provides an effective framework for testing control algorithms, refining perception–manipulation strategies, and supporting robust operation under the evaluated greenhouse conditions. The proposed approach represents a step forward in applying DT technology to controlled environment agriculture, offering a basis for future scalable, AI-enhanced robotic systems that can optimize crop establishment and contribute to sustainable food production.

title: Soft semantic grouping and feature clustering for panoptic segmentation of tree crowns and trunks in LiDAR point clouds
abstract: High-throughput tree growth phenotyping depends on acquiring structural information. LiDAR-based point clouds enable 3D quantitative morphological analysis, but accurate crown–trunk segmentation is an essential prerequisite for extracting reliable phenotypic parameters and enabling subsequent high-precision phenotyping analysis. However, traditional 2D image analysis methods are limited by dimensional constraints, failing to quantify 3D structural features of crowns. The irregularity, sparsity, and noise of LiDAR point clouds cause traditional geometry-dependent algorithms to extract features with insufficient accuracy. Besides, difficulties in assigning instance labels in overlapping crown edges and semantic ambiguity in crown–trunk transition zones further exacerbate segmentation errors. Existing deep learning methods exhibit poor generalization and robustness, yielding inconsistent performance across multi-platform and heterogeneous forest point clouds. Currently, no unified panoptic segmentation framework exists that concurrently resolves crown–trunk semantic ambiguity, adapts to substantial LiDAR platform-specific point density variations, and accurately delineates instances in densely overlapping forest canopies. To address these, this work proposes the crown–trunk Segmentation (CTS) panoptic framework. A soft semantic grouping module resolves transition zone ambiguity by assigning points to multiple categories, and a feature clustering-deformable convolution module shifts canopy points to centroids, overcoming overlapping instance labeling issues. Validation on multi-platform point cloud datasets shows that the proposed CTS achieves a semantic segmentation overall accuracy of 88.15% and an instance segmentation F1 score of 99.31% in both mature and young forests. Ablation studies confirm significant synergistic gains from the soft semantic grouping and feature clustering modules. Comparisons on the public FOR-instance dataset show 8.7 average F1 score improvement over Point2tree and ForAINet, with 13.22 recall gain in complex overlaps. Extracted growth phenotyping parameters (trunk DBH RMSE 0.021, 3D crown area 6.354) demonstrate the potential of volume-area correlation analysis, and the improved segmentation accuracy could facilitate downstream 3D growth analysis as a potential application.

title: Advances in remote sensing techniques for surface soil moisture estimation: A systematic review of recent developments (2019–2024)
abstract: Surface soil moisture (SSM) is a vital variable for irrigation management, estimation of crop water stress, and agricultural drought management. This systematic review integrates recent progress (2019–2024) in remote sensing-based SSM estimation, based on 116 peer-reviewed articles selected using PRISMA guidelines. The review indicates that multi-sensor techniques, integrating optical, radar, and climate information coupled with machine learning (ML) and data assimilation methods, have immensely enhanced the spatial and temporal resolution of SSM products. These developments have brought SSM retrieval within the realm of useful, field-scale application for agricultural water management. Hybrid models and AI-downscaled approaches, in particular, have a very high potential for operational decision-making across varying agro-ecologies. Trends in performance, regional research gaps, and areas for improvement in terms of data coverage, especially for semi-arid and smallholder-dominated landscapes, are also addressed in this review. SWOT analysis of prominent retrieval algorithms identifies their advantages and limitations in application, revealing the compromises between complexity, scalability, and accuracy. Although there has been increasing technical development, with few exceptions, there is no large-scale application in actual irrigation systems. The article ends by placing greater emphasis on enhancing stronger validation protocols, improved application within crop and hydrological models, and region-tailored modifications of retrieval workflows. In the future, new satellite missions and enhanced ground data infrastructure offer opportunities to enhance the contribution of SSM to climate-resilient agriculture. This review offers a timely basis to advance SM monitoring systems that are not only scientifically valid but operationally pertinent to sustainable water management in agriculture.

title: ‘From growth monitoring to berry quality prediction: Advances and challenges in UAV remote sensing for precision viticulture
abstract: Unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) remote sensing has become a key enabler of precision viticulture, providing rapid, non-destructive, high resolution measurements to characterize within vineyard variability. This review systematically outlines the development of UAV remote sensing technology in vineyards over the past decade. It first summarizes the application platforms and sensors. Subsequently, the paper reviews the complete workflow encompassing data preprocessing, canopy segmentation, feature engineering, as well as machine learning/deep learning modeling. The research progress in six major application fields was systematically reviewed: nutritional status monitoring, growth and vigour monitoring, pest and disease detection, water stress monitoring, yield estimation, and berry quality assessment. Key persistent challenges in field applications were highlighted, including specific scenario constraints, insufficient model interpretability, limited generalization ability, high data requirements, and operational restrictions. To accelerate the application and promotion of UAV remote sensing technology in vineyards, future research should focus on standardized data acquisition and evaluation protocols, multi-temporal and multi-modal fusion, transfer learning and domain adaptation for cross-site generalization, targeted data augmentation or sample synthesis, and solutions combining lightweight models with low-cost sensing.

title: Cost-aware feature selection for classifying rapeseed cleaning-loss piezoelectric impact signals across sampling rates
abstract: To improve the monitoring accuracy of rapeseed cleaning-loss sensors during harvesting, a piezoelectric-ceramic loss-sensing mode was employed in this study. Impact waveforms were acquired on a test bench using a piezoelectric-ceramic loss sensor from three material classes, including rapeseed grain, straw, and pod husk. Trigger-aligned fixed-length 10 ms segments were extracted after each trigger to construct a representative dataset for short-window time-series multiclass classification. Considering computational cost and real-time constraints on edge devices, a cost-aware principle for feature selection was adopted. Under this principle, feature contribution, feature redundancy, sampling-rate sensitivity, and deployment cost were jointly considered. Four time-domain features were ultimately retained as classifier inputs: segment energy, kurtosis, maximum amplitude, and minimum amplitude. Classifiers from different model families were evaluated, and CatBoost provided the best overall accuracy–cost balance. At a 50 kHz sampling rate, classification accuracy approached saturation. Under this recommended configuration, CatBoost achieved a mean accuracy of 99.889%; on a single-core PC platform, the measured per-sample inference latency was 3.82 μs, feature extraction required 27.73 μs, and the trained CatBoost model size was 0.324 MB. Continuous-signal bench validation further showed that the trigger-windowing, feature-extraction, and model-discrimination pipeline could be extended to event-level recognition in continuously acquired waveforms. These results demonstrate that accurate and cost-aware identification of rapeseed cleaning-loss impact events can be achieved by using a small set of time-domain features at reduced sampling rates, supporting lightweight online loss monitoring in rapeseed combine harvesters.

title: Modeling PPFD propagation and transmittance in ePAR spectrum for canopy and intra-canopy adaptive greenhouse lighting
abstract: Supplemental light is a fundamental driver of plant growth and a key variable in optimizing crop productivity in controlled environments. Light-emitting diodes (LEDs), operating across distinct spectral channels, are widely adopted for their efficiency and demonstrated benefits. However, conventional top-lighting often produces non-uniform distribution, with excessive interception at the upper canopy and insufficient penetration into lower leaves. Intra-canopy lighting has emerged as a promising solution, yet the absence of rigorous models for spatial and vertical light distribution continues to limit optimization of supplemental lighting. In this study, we present and validate a unified mathematical framework for modeling the propagation and transmittance of photosynthetic photon flux density (PPFD, μ mol s −1 m −2 ) across the extended Photosynthetically Active Radiation (ePAR) spectrum (400–750 nm). The model accounts for individual spectral channels (blue, red, far-red, white) and their combinations, simulating three-dimensional spatial distribution and vertical PPFD profiles along tomato plants. Validation with multi-lamp experimental data demonstrated mean percentage errors below 1% in spatial top-canopy PPFD and below 2.5% in vertical PPFD transmittance, across all spectral channels. The proposed algorithm operates with low and linear computational overhead, achieving average execution times of 27 ± 10 μ s per PPFD point, ensuring scalability to large greenhouse systems. The proposed model enables precise PPFD monitoring and provides the basis for advanced supplemental lighting strategies, supporting the integration of real-time digital twins for adaptive light management in smart greenhouse environments.

title: Variational autoencoder enables unsupervised leaf diagnosis via hyperspectral imaging
abstract: Hyperspectral imaging provides rich spectral information for plant phenotyping, yet analyzing these high-dimensional data remains challenging due to limited labeled datasets and the reliance on manually extracted features, such as vegetation indices. Here, we present LeafVAE, a variational autoencoder framework that learns spectral signatures directly from hyperspectral leaf images without manual annotation. Our model encodes leaf spectra into a compact, two-dimensional latent space where pixels cluster by spectral similarity, creating quantitative leaf descriptors from signature composition that facilitate downstream phenotyping tasks. We show that the learned representations generalize robustly across genotypes, years, and imaging equipment on four different corn leaf datasets. We further demonstrate that LeafVAE outperforms traditional vegetation indices across multiple applications, including detecting nitrogen deficiency in corn, classifying herbicide stress in soybean, and identifying beech leaf disease using an affordable six-band multispectral camera. Pixel-level explainability, achieved by combining spectral signature composition with interpretable machine learning methods, identifies regions with abnormal spectral characteristics and highlights areas of the leaf that contribute to model predictions. By learning spectral features in an unsupervised manner while still allowing labels for interpretable diagnosis, LeafVAE provides a scalable foundation for automated plant phenotyping across diverse applications.

title: Adaptive sideslip angle fusion estimation and state-feedback path-tracking control for agricultural tractors
abstract: With the advancements in Global Navigation Satellite Systems, tractor path-tracking accuracy can achieve centimeter-level precision under ideal conditions. However, in unstructured agricultural environments, varying terrain and soil properties induce significant vehicle sideslip, severely degrading tracking performance. To mitigate this issue, this study develops a robust sideslip state fusion estimation framework and applies it as feedback compensation for the path-tracking control of agricultural tractors. Specifically, a dual-observer strategy is formulated by integrating an Extended Kalman Filter with a Luenberger observer. An adaptive fusion method is then employed to combine the estimates from both observers, thereby enhancing estimation accuracy and robustness of the estimation against external disturbances. Subsequently, the estimated sideslip angles are incorporated into the path-tracking controller to actively suppress lateral drift. Both simulation and field test results demonstrate that the proposed method accurately captures the sideslip dynamics. Furthermore, field evaluations confirm that the mean lateral error is reduced from 3.39 cm to 1.88 cm, and the maximum lateral deviation is decreased from 37.35 cm to 28.30 cm. Consequently, the proposed fusion-based estimation, combined with the state-feedback control algorithm, effectively enhances path-tracking performance and robustness under complex field conditions.

title: A feed rate monitoring system based on light loss in the conveyor trough of soybean combine harvester
abstract: In soybean combine harvesters, the lack of real-time monitoring and feedback on feed rate leads to frequent cases of blockage in machines and huge grain losses, considerably hampering efficient operational control. To overcome these challenges, this research aimed to develop and validate a feed rate monitoring system. A custom-designed light loss monitoring device was implemented in a conveyor trough to measure light intensity as it moved through the process. The developed system consisted of an angle sensor, a travel speed sensor, a microprocessor, and a terminal display. The core principle involves measuring the changes in luminous flux coming from a linear light emitter when hidden by the grain flow. The light loss ratio versus feed rate relationship was then determined from controlled bench tests. A feed rate prediction model was developed using an integrated Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO)–enhanced Backpropagation (BP) neural network that utilizes multiple sensor inputs. Experimental results showed that the light loss monitoring system yielded a mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) of 0.49%. The light loss ratio versus the feed rate for both soybean types studied followed a second-order polynomial function. Reinforced by these analytical results, the PSO-optimized BP predictive model achieved a coefficient of determination (R2) of 0.892 for feed rate, with an MAPE of 8.9%, a root mean square error (RMSE) of 0.21 kg·s⁻1, and a mean absolute error (MAE) of 0.17 kg·s⁻1, thereby validating the superior prediction performance. At low, medium, and high travel speeds, the MAPE of the PSO-BP-based feed rate monitoring system was 11.3%, 10.1%, and 9.9%, respectively. The monitoring system, based on light loss and the PSO-BP model, plays an important role in providing accurate and reliable feed rate prediction, and has great potential for enabling real-time control and preventing operational faults during soybean harvesting.

title: A multisource weakly supervised high-resolution crop mapping framework based on low-resolution noise labels
abstract: High-resolution (HR) crop maps are the foundation data for conducting precise agricultural monitoring and land use change analysis. However, HR crop mapping remains hindered by costly manual annotations, label noise from low resolution (LR) products, convolutional neural network (CNN) architectural limitations, and spatial-spectral constraints of single source remote sensing imagery. LR crop classification products serve as cost-effective weak supervision but introduce geometric and semantic label noise. Conventional CNNs struggle with preserving fine spatial details and modeling long-range contexts, while data-level multi-source fusion blurs parcel boundaries. To address these issues, we propose a multisource weakly supervised crop classification framework (MSWCF) that utilizes LR products to guide HR mapping. The MSWCF features dual parallel branches: the HR branch extracts parcel boundaries, while the LR branch captures semantic information. Each branch integrates spatial resolution preserving and Vision Transformer modules to concurrently extract local details and global contexts. A cross-attention module (CAM) adaptively fuses these features, while a noise label removal module suppresses boundary and semantic errors in LR labels. Experiments were conducted in Heilongjiang Province, China. Results show that MSWCF achieves superior performance (Overall Accuracy = 93.8 %) surpassing state-of-the-art baselines. Cross-spatiotemporal application indicates that it has generalization capabilities. Ablation studies confirm that the dual-branch structure and CAM fusion effectively utilize spatial-spectral information, preventing boundary smoothing. Feature visualization verifies that SRP focuses on boundaries while ViT captures global objects. MSWCF enables accurate, fine-grained crop mapping without manual annotations, validating its practicality for largescale HR crop mapping.

title: Accurate pose estimation of pigs with symmetric −aware keypoint detection
abstract: Accurate pose and action recognition of pigs is of great significance in modern precision animal husbandry, which helps to monitor the welfare status and potential abnormal behaviors of pigs in real time. However, the current work on pig pose estimation confronts several challenges. For instance, the majority of existing models are derived from human keypoints detection. These models encounter challenges in adapting the intricate body shape and occlusion issues that are closely associated with pig pose estimation. Moreover, due to the laterally compressed body morphology of pigs, certain symmetrical regions exhibit the characteristic of visible exclusivity, meaning that in many cases only one key point can be observed at a time, such as the left and right shoulders. This leads to ambiguity in the prediction of key points. Simultaneously, the substantial quantity of parameters in deep models and the relatively low deployment efficiency imposes constraints on their practical applications. This paper proposes a novel Symmetric-aware Keypoint Detection method to address these issues. Our approach enhances a High-Resolution Network (HRNet) backbone with the Convolutional Block Attention Module (CBAM) and integrates a visibility annotation-based adjustment strategy. This strategy is specifically designed to resolve the misclassification of symmetrically exclusive keypoints, reducing their inspection error rate from 11.7 % to 0.25 %. On our collected dataset, the method achieves an Average Precision (AP) of 89.67 % for keypoint detection, outperforming the baseline HRNet by 3.3 percentage points. For the downstream pose recognition task, it attains an accuracy of 94.52 %. Furthermore, we demonstrate that a simplified skeleton with only 8 keypoints can maintain a high recognition accuracy of 94.01 %. To enhance practicality, a distilled model reduces parameters by 59.9 % (from 28.98 M to 11.63 M) while retaining 84.43 % detection AP and increasing inference speed to 17.52 FPS. This work provides an efficient and integrated pipeline for intelligent pig monitoring.

title: Quality-aware generative distillation for robust and efficient livestock detection
abstract: Vision-based livestock monitoring in open pastures confronts two distinct bottlenecks: a quality problem—severe image degradation from variable illumination (e.g., nighttime, strong snow reflection) yields abundant but low-quality frames—and a scarcity problem—extreme weather events (e.g., heavy snow, rain) are rare, leaving few training samples for such critical conditions. Generative image editors can in principle enhance degraded inputs and synthesize rare scenarios. However, unsupervised generation frequently introduces semantic artifacts and geometric distortions; naïvely incorporating these corrupted samples into training misleads detectors and degrades performance. To harness generative data reliably while meeting edge-device constraints, we propose a quality-aware generative distillation framework. First, a dual-branch editing pipeline—built on the large-scale instruction-driven editor Qwen-Image-Edit—restores visibility in low-quality inputs (enhancement branch) and simulates diverse adverse-weather views from clear daytime images (style-edit branch), addressing both quality and scarcity issues at the data level. Second, because generative outputs are unreliable, we design a multi-metric quality assessment module combining perceptual similarity (LPIPS), region-of-interest edge consistency, and CLIP-based semantic alignment to automatically filter corrupted edits before training. Third, to avoid deploying heavy generative models at inference, we train a robust teacher detector on this curated multi-domain dataset, then distill its localization features into a lightweight student via feature-level knowledge transfer; the student trains only on raw images, incurs no enhancement overhead at deployment, yet inherits cross-weather robustness. Experiments on our SnowLivestockDet dataset demonstrate that YOLOv11 and RT-DETR students achieve up to 12.5% mAP@50–95 improvement on adverse-weather subsets compared to single-domain baselines, validating the effectiveness of quality-aware generative distillation.

title: Multimodal deep fusion of Low-Field NMR and proton Density-Weighted imaging for interpretable detection of Saline-Alkali stress in wheat
abstract: Saline-alkali stress is a major abiotic constraint on wheat growth and productivity, creating a need for non-destructive, sensitive, and physiologically interpretable phenotyping methods for fine-grained stress detection. In this study, we propose a dual-tower deep-fusion framework that integrates low-field nuclear magnetic resonance (LF-NMR) relaxometry with proton density weighted imaging (PDWI) texture analysis for the classification of saline-alkali stress levels in wheat seedlings. Specifically, 1D-T2 and 2D-T1-T2 relaxation spectra were combined with 3D-PDWI-derived grey-level co-occurrence matrix (GLCM) texture features to jointly characterise water-state dynamics and spatial structural heterogeneity. Based on an SE-ResNet backbone, early fusion, mid-level fusion, and dual-tower late fusion strategies were systematically compared under a unified evaluation protocol. The results showed that LF-NMR captured the conversion of free water into semi-bound and bound water, together with disruption of cellular compartmentalisation, whereas PDWI texture features reflected the progression of tissue structural damage from a spatial perspective. These multimodal signals were consistent with physiological and biochemical measurements. Among all models, the proposed DT-LF-SE-ResNet achieved the best test accuracy of 95.93 %, exceeding the single modality baselines by 35.00 % and 30.37 %, and clearly outperforming early fusion (71.43 %) and mid-level fusion (87.56 %). Feature importance analysis and Grad-CAM further indicated that the performance gain arose from the synergistic representation of water population redistribution and increased microstructural heterogeneity. These findings demonstrate the mechanistic and predictive advantages of dual-tower multimodal fusion and provide an explainable phenotyping framework for fine grained crop stress assessment.

title: LAI assimilation schedules to constrain uncertain cultivars and soils in CERES-Maize
abstract: In anticipation of large-domain crop model applications where precise local configuration and calibration is not possible, we describe benefits and potential drawbacks of employing a crop pest module to achieve leaf area index (LAI) assimilation into a high performing CERES-Maize crop model configuration at a field experiment site in Perry, Iowa. Simulation experiments explore the use of MODIS satellite-derived LAI to constrain and adjust LAI to counter imprecise cultivar and soil configurations often occurring in the absence of high-quality local information. Simulations using single-day, window, and continuous LAI replacement across 5 cultivars and 2 soil calibration approaches for nine corn rotation years from 2004 to 2020 led to different yield outcomes and reverberations throughout the field environment. Evaluating variance and mean bias, results indicate minimal interventions in early vegetative and grain-filling stages were more beneficial than use of continuous LAI adjustments, as they minimized disruptions to the internal resource balances governing plant stresses and grain production. LAI adjustment was particularly helpful in constraining growth related to uncertain thermal unit requirements and leaf tip appearance rates (P1 and PHINT cultivar parameters, respectively). Findings underscore the need to assimilate additional state variables to ensure internal biophysical coherence. This approach shows promise for applications spanning wider domains with prediction time pressure where detailed configuration, more complex assimilation methods, or recalibration of crop model parameters may not be practical.

title: Dead pine tree detection using an iterative semi-supervised framework integrating expert annotation and active learning
abstract: Pine wilt disease (PWD) poses a severe threat to forest ecosystems and resources, and unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) remote sensing combined with deep learning (DL) has become a widely used approach for its detection. However, DL-based methods typically rely on large-scale labeled datasets, while semi-supervised learning (SSL) still faces a key limitation in practice: the lack of a principled strategy for determining optimal annotation ratios, often leading to either insufficient supervision or unnecessary labeling cost, and existing static training schemes fail to adapt to dynamically evolving data distributions. To address this gap, we propose a human–machine interactive framework that integrates active learning (AL) with SSL through interactive training and expert-driven annotation. An AL method, object uncertainty sampling (OUS) strategy was employed to enhance annotation efficiency. Our results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves detection accuracy comparable to fully supervised approaches while using only 30 % of the labeled data (mAP = 64.9 %, mAP50 = 94.1 %), and improves performance by 3.1 %–11.4 % in mAP compared with other SSL methods. Moreover, when applied to new datasets, this method supports transfer learning, allowing the model to retain prior knowledge while improving performance on new data, with mAP and mAP50 reaching 55.32 % and 93.3 %, respectively. By integrating automated learning with expert judgment, it reduces manual effort and achieves optimal detection with minimal annotation. Additionally, the proposed strategy exhibits cross-model generalization and can be combined with multiple object detection models, including SSD, YOLOv12, and DETR, enhancing the performance of baseline models while reducing annotation requirements. This approach offers a novel perspective on PWD detection and control and demonstrates strong potential for broader applications in diverse object recognition and detection scenarios.

title: Unified nitrogen diagnosis in winter oilseed rape (Brassica napus L.): Integrating Bayesian critical N dilution curves and fractional-order three-dimensional spectral indices
abstract: Unified and management-oriented nitrogen (N) diagnosis in mulched dryland crops requires a physiologically consistent baseline that can support consistent interpretation across tested management scenarios and be retrieved non-destructively. To address this, we conducted multi-season field experiments on winter oilseed rape (Brassica napus L.) on the Loess Plateau using three mulching treatments (no mulching, straw mulching, and film mulching) and five N rates (0–280 kg N ha−1). Specifically, we aimed to integrate Bayesian physiological modeling with hyperspectral sensing. Aboveground dry matter (DM), leaf N concentration (LNC), canopy hyperspectral reflectance, and seed yield were measured across key growth stages. A Bayesian framework was used to estimate the critical N dilution relationship and quantify parameter uncertainty, supporting pooling across years and mulching treatments (posterior probability of practically negligible differences > 0.95). The resulting unified critical curve was LNCc = 35.732 × DM−0.15, enabling a consistent nitrogen nutrition index (NNI) threshold interpretation across mulching scenarios. To enable rapid diagnosis, canopy spectra were transformed using 0.8-order fractional derivatives, and tri-band three-dimensional spectral indices were optimized to predict NNI with machine learning. The best model (XGBoost) achieved R2 = 0.682 with RMSE = 0.092 on a held-out validation set. Agronomically, film mulching increased mean seed yield by ∼ 31.6% relative to no mulching, and yield response exhibited a clear N plateau: FMN3 produced yields only 1.05%–1.74% lower than FMN4 while reducing N input by 25%. The spectral NNI showed a consistent linear–plateau relationship with relative yield, with the plateau occurring near NNI ≈ 1.0. Overall, combining Bayesian Nc–NNI standardization with hyperspectral NNI retrieval provides a unified, management-oriented pathway for N diagnosis within the tested multi-year mulching conditions; however, further external validation across sites, cultivars, and independent years is still required, together with additional assessment of phenology-specific spectral bias, canopy vertical N redistribution, and uncertainty associated with large 3D-OSI feature screening.

title: Editorial Board
SLPT-Net: A spatiotemporal learning framework for automated sow contraction recognition and farrowing time prediction
abstract: The frequency of sow contraction behavior is a key physiological indicator of imminent parturition, and accurate farrowing time estimation is crucial for improving piglet survival rates. However, existing behavior recognition methods — mainly adapted from human action analysis — often face limitations in generalization and computational efficiency when applied in real farm environments. To address these challenges, this study proposes a two-stage recognition and prediction framework named sparse lightweight perception and transformer-based network for sow contraction recognition and farrowing time prediction (SLPT-Net), which integrates contraction behavior recognition and farrowing time prediction. In the first stage, a lightweight 3D convolutional sub-network called sparse lightweight perception network for 3D video-based sow contraction behavior recognition (SLP3D) is developed to identify contraction behaviors. It incorporates a lightweight spatial channel attention (LSCA) module, a partial bidirectional feature pyramid network (PBFPN), and the Swish activation function to enhance spatiotemporal feature representation while reducing computational overhead. In the second stage, a Transformer-based classifier utilizes sequences of contraction behaviors to estimate the farrowing stage, followed by a post-processing algorithm to predict the actual farrowing time. A video dataset of sow contraction behaviors was constructed for evaluation. Experimental results show that SLP3D achieves a mean accuracy of 96.40% at 65.66 FPS, outperforming mainstream methods in both accuracy and real-time performance. The farrowing time prediction model yields an average error of 1.17 h, demonstrating the framework’s effectiveness. This work presents a novel, efficient solution for intelligent monitoring of sow farrowing behavior, with strong potential for practical application in smart farming systems.

title: Binocular-depth-guided dual-view camera-LiDAR fusion for kiwifruit pose estimation in robotic harvesting
abstract: Accurate detection and pose estimation of kiwifruit are essential for robotic harvesting in modern orchards, which remains challenging due to complex lighting conditions and dense canopy in natural environments. In this study, a dual-view camera-LiDAR fusion methodology based on Depth-Iterative Canopy Filtering (DICF) method was proposed for precise pose estimation of kiwifruits. The proposed methodology aimed to overcome limitations of existing camera-based fruit pose estimation research by enhancing robustness under variable lighting and complex canopy conditions. The methodology integrated a lightweight end-to-end stereo matching network with the DICF, leveraging binocular disparity maps to guide LiDAR point-cloud adhesion noise suppression. YOLO11m was employed for kiwifruit detection, dual-view fusion increased detection accuracy of occluded fruits to 92.8%, representing a 28.5% improvement over single-view detection. Experiments conducted in commercial orchards demonstrated that the methodology achieved a mean absolute localization error of 6.54 mm and an orientation angle error of 7.70°. Moreover, filtering time was reduced to 1.12 s for point clouds containing 700,000 points, compared to 3.56 s required by the TSPFA, meeting the requirements of robotic harvesting. This study established a novel and efficient methodology for kiwifruit pose estimation and provided a foundation for end-to-end multimodal sensor fusion in future agricultural robotics.

title: FSC-Mamba: Integrating High-Frequency global context and Multi-Dimensional relational alignment for Few-Shot counting
abstract: Accurate individual counting and localization of poultry under high-density farming conditions remain challenging due to visual similarity, occlusion, and environmental variability. To address these issues, this paper proposes a Mamba-based Few-Shot Counting (FSC-Mamba) framework for chicken counting with minimal annotation requirements. The framework incorporates two key modules: a High-Frequency Global Interaction (HFGI) module and a Spatial-Shot-Channel Feature Alignment (SSC-FA) module. To reduce occlusion-induced ambiguity and lighting sensitivity in few-shot chicken counting, HFGI combines wavelet-driven high-frequency detail capture with Mamba-based global context at linear complexity, yielding consistent gains in boundary accuracy and localization. The multi-dimensional relational alignment within SSC-FA jointly models the spatial, shot, and channel dimensions to reinforce support-query semantic correspondence. It integrates Spatial-Mamba for global layout and long-range spatial dependencies, Shot Mix-Mamba for cross-shot feature mixing and rapid adaptation, and Channel-Mamba for inter-channel selection, producing discriminative fused representations that boost few-shot counting accuracy and robustness across scenes. In addition, we develop PoultryCount, a standardized in-the-wild benchmark built from over 152 h of farm monitoring videos across diverse growth stages and environments, enabling rigorous evaluation of few-shot chicken counting under high-density, cross-scene conditions. Experimental results show that FSC-Mamba attains superior counting accuracy and robust localization on PoultryCount, achieving 5.4% and 4.1% relative improvements in MAE and RMSE over state-of-the-art methods. Furthermore, evaluations on the public Dense-Chicken and Aerial Sheep datasets demonstrate that our method maintains high accuracy under cross-species distribution shifts, indicating robust transfer beyond poultry.

title: A trajectory prediction method for vibrating fruits based on the LSTM-DA-iTransformer fusion model
abstract: In the process of intelligent fruit harvesting, the vibrations caused by external disturbances significantly affect the robot’s ability to quickly grasp the fruit. Accurately predicting the trajectory of the vibrating fruit is crucial for efficient grasping. However, traditional trajectory prediction models often struggle to achieve an effective balance between dynamic adaptability and long-term sequence prediction accuracy. To address this issue, this paper proposes a hybrid model—LSTM-DA-iTransformer. The model utilizes LSTM to capture local temporal features and integrates a Differential Attention Mechanism (DA) module to dynamically optimize attention weights in real time, adapting to variations in the vibration amplitude of the fruit. Additionally, the iTransformer strengthens long-term sequence dependency modeling to effectively mitigate the vanishing gradient problem. Moreover, to further improve the model’s prediction accuracy and performance, the dataset was feature-adjusted by replacing position features with the position increments between time steps and timestamp features with the time differences between time steps. This adjustment helps avoid the impact of large-scale position features on model training and accelerates model convergence. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed model delivers superior performance in long-term sequence prediction tasks spanning 3 to 5 s. Specifically, within the 4-second time window, the Average Displacement Error (ADE) registers at 1.5475 cm, representing reductions of 41.6 %, 30.2 %, and 43.3 % relative to the GRU, BiLSTM, and Transformer models, respectively. In the 5-second time window, the Final Displacement Error (FDE) amounts to 2.2185 cm, marking a decrease of 22.7 % to 39.2 % compared with the baseline models, alongside a 33.8 % to 48.3 % reduction in the Root Mean Square Error (RMSE). Additionally, ablation experiments rigorously verify the essentiality of each integrated module; notably, the DA module yields a remarkable improvement in prediction accuracy under complex vibrational scenarios.

title: Adapting SAM with dynamic similarity graphs for few-shot parameter-efficient small dense object detection: A case study of chickpea pods in field conditions
abstract: Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning (PEFT) of foundation models for agricultural computer vision tasks remains challenging due to limited training data and complex field conditions. This study introduces a Dynamic Similarity-based Graph Adaptation (DSGA) module to adapt the Segment Anything Model (SAM) under extreme data constraints for precise foreground and instance segmentation of small dense objects in complex agricultural environments. Through dynamic similarity graph construction with a learnable polynomial decay-initialized weight ranking mechanism and adaptive local feature aggregation, DSGA establishes robust spatial and dynamic similarity representation with only 4.00M trainable parameters, which is 4.26% of the original SAM. Integrating this graph-based feature adaptation with Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) creates a complementary optimization framework that effectively captures both local and global dependencies in image embeddings while preserving model stability and parameter efficiency. Experimental results on a challenging chickpea pod dataset demonstrated that DSGA with LoRA achieved superior performance across multiple metrics evaluated under 2, 4, 8 and 10 shots, with progressive performance gains as shot count increased. Quantitative metrics showed a 17.31% improvement in Structure-measure and a 62.36% gain in adaptive F-measure compared to the baseline SAM fine-tuning. Comprehensive ablation studies and visualization analyses through Grad-CAM and t-SNE validated the framework's effectiveness in feature discrimination. The proposed adaptation demonstrated practical utility for automated agricultural monitoring applications, achieving accurate pod-counting with an adjusted R-squared of 0.8987 for images with 10 to 120 pods under challenging field conditions.

title: Design and validation of a human-inspired picking motion for tomato harvesting
abstract: Greenhouse automated harvesting is a fundamental research direction in smart agriculture. It plays an essential role in addressing labor shortages, reducing production costs, and ensuring high product quality. Although current tomato harvesting robots have achieved significant progress in structural design, they still face challenges such as high damage rates and limited adaptability. These limitations are primarily caused by the rigid motion trajectories of conventional robotic arms and a lack of focus on the biomechanical properties of the fruit peduncle. While structural biomimetics is widely explored, simply mimicking hand morphology cannot replicate the dynamic advantages inherent in manual picking. Therefore, a harvesting control strategy based on behavioral biomimetics was developed in this research. This approach shifts the focus from morphological imitation to the reproduction of optimal picking motion. Key picking motion was extracted from human kinematic data and integrated into the robot’s motion planning algorithm to actively minimize separation forces. Experimental results showed that the anthropomorphic motion reduced the peak harvesting force by 51.3% compared to traditional picking motion. In greenhouse field tests, a harvesting success rate of 62.2% was achieved. This study confirms that behavioral biomimetic strategies can effectively optimize mechanical interaction forces. It provides a novel technical path for low-damage and efficient automated harvesting.

title: A comprehensive survey on segmentation-enabled precision agriculture: Methodologies, applications, and the road to agriculture 5.0
abstract: By 2050, global food production must increase by 50%. Accurate farmland mapping is essential to meeting this target, yet the task remains technically challenging. Three persistent problems stand out: small and irregular field boundaries, dynamic crop phenology that alters spectral signatures, and the difficulty of fusing heterogeneous data sources. Existing reviews either address remote sensing broadly or focus on narrow algorithmic categories, leaving a gap in systematic treatment of segmentation-driven precision agriculture. This survey fills that gap by tracing the methodological evolution of farmland boundary extraction from traditional feature engineering to modern deep learning and foundation models, and by demonstrating how precise spatial delineation enables critical downstream applications. We introduce a 4D taxonomy that organizes methods along four dimensions: technical approach, data modality, spatial scale, and application use case. Our analysis covers 117 papers published between 2018 and 2026 across three developmental stages: traditional techniques, deep learning, and foundation models. From this review, three bottlenecks become clear. Even the most advanced models suffer substantial performance degradation in highly fragmented landscapes. Label scarcity remains a pervasive barrier to generalization. The complexity of multimodal data fusion also continues to resist robust solutions. To address these challenges, we outline a forward-looking roadmap built on three emerging paradigms. These include agricultural foundation models for self-supervised representation learning, physics-informed AI for trustworthy predictions, and federated learning for privacy-preserving cross-institutional collaboration. Together, these directions point toward reliable, scalable farmland mapping systems for next-generation precision agriculture.

title: Mapping Alpine pasture biomass and nutritional value from hyperspectral field and spaceborne sensors
abstract: Pastures are important components of Alpine cultural landscapes. However, due to unbalanced grazing pressure and climate change, the quality of pastures is degrading, diminishing their capacity to deliver essential ecosystem services and leading to widespread abandonment. Adaptive grazing management practices can address the challenge of under- or over-exploitation of pasture resources, balancing livestock forage demand and pasture productivity. This study evaluates the capabilities of spaceborne hyperspectral data for mapping pasture productivity and nutritional characteristics (i.e. biomass, protein and fiber content) in mid- to high-elevation Alpine environments. Agronomic and reflectance data (350-2500 nm) were collected in the field across different vegetation phenological stages for 128 pasture samples in two distinct Alpine regions. Field spectra were convoluted to simulate satellite PRISMA hyperspectral and Sentinel-2 multispectral sensor configurations, both used to calibrate and validate Gaussian Process Regression machine learning models. Hyperspectral-based models significantly outperformed multispectral-based ones, with an average R c v 2 improvement of 58.05% and an average R M S E c v reduction of 9.83% ( R c v 2 : 0.67, R M S E c v : 225.79 g m − 2 for AGB; R c v 2 : 0.55, R M S E c v : 1.87 % for CP; R c v 2 : 0.65, R M S E c v : 1.71 % for ADF; R c v 2 : 0.62, R M S E c v : 2.66 % for NDF). The best-performing models were demonstrated on a real PRISMA scene, and the estimations were evaluated against in-situ data, showing overall good agreement (average R 2 of 0.60 and average rRMSE of 11%) and high coherence with spatial patterns induced by pasture composition, grazing and topography. Our results confirm the potential of current (e.g., PRISMA, EnMAP) and upcoming operational hyperspectral missions (e.g., ESA’s CHIME) for regional forage biomass and nutritional quality assessment.

title: Fusion of Litest-HRNet and Skeleton GCN for real-time calf posture monitoring
abstract: Neonatal calves' early daily behaviors are closely related to their health status, serving as crucial early disease indicators. However, in single-calf isolation housing, manual inspection is inefficient, highlighting the need for real-time, non-contact posture monitoring solution for edge devices. To address this need, a lightweight posture monitoring framework for calf-hutch scenarios was proposed. The proposed method was realized by integrating a keypoint estimator and a skeleton-based classifier built upon Lite-est High-Resolution Net (Litest-HRNet). Rapid calf localization was first achieved using the nano-scale lightweight Real-Time Models for Object Detection (RTMDet). Litest-HRNet was then developed by incorporating Dilated Convolution and Squeeze-and-Excitation (SE) attention with coordinated depth–width scaling to improve keypoint regression stability under self-occlusion. Finally, a Skeleton Graph Convolutional Network (Skeleton GCN) with angle-feature enhancement was constructed to explicitly model keypoint topological dependencies for binary classification of standing and lying postures. Experimental results showed that RTMDet-n achieved an Average Precision (AP) of 0.959 with 3.60 G Floating Point Operations (FLOPs). For keypoint detection, Litest-HRNet achieved an AP of 0.9641 and Average Recall (AR) of 0.9701. Compared to the baseline Lite-HRNet, the model reduced FLOPs by 40.2% and Parameters by 43.3%, maintaining a compact size of 3.12 MB and an inference speed of 76.41 Frames Per Second (FPS).
