An overall accuracy of 90.10% was achieved at an inference speed of 32.7 FPS, demonstrating that the real-time requirements for calf posture estimation were realized. With its non-contact, real-time, and objective characteristics, the proposed method could provide an extensible solution for continuous monitoring of individual calf behaviors.

title: “Please, mind the gap”: A narrative review on digitalization gaps and barriers in the livestock sector
abstract: The livestock sector generates large volumes of data; however, these data remain underutilized. The Data Governance Act, the Data Act of the EU, and recent technological advances, provide an opportunity to automate and improve collection, integration, and use of livestock data. Data spaces, as secure and interoperable environments for data sharing, offer a promising framework to support this transformation. However, this can only be achieved by removing implementation barriers to data sharing and new data generating technologies. The aim of this paper is to provide an overview of key digitalization barriers and gaps in livestock sector. We synthesized existing knowledge across five topics: 1) interoperability, 2) economic viability, 3) technical skills, 4) data privacy and security, and 5) data robustness and quality. Finally, a narrative on how these gaps could be bridged was provided. We argue that bridging these gaps requires a holistic approach combining training, trust building, data governance, and collaboration. EU-level initiatives and projects address some of these areas, but better coordination is needed to maximize impact. The Data Act provides a regulatory foundation for data sharing, yet its limitations, such as its horizontal nature, narrowly defined or unclear terms and exclusion of insights derived from product and related service data, leave critical gaps and may lead to legal disputes. To overcome persistent data lock-in, proactive negotiation, public APIs, and an update on a voluntary industry code of conduct to align with the Data Act are essential for fostering transparency and accelerating adoption of digital solutions.

title: The speed–precision paradox in seeding technology: a system-level review of regime transitions, validation gaps, and energy trade-offs
abstract: High-speed precision seeding is essential for sustaining field capacity, yet placement accuracy degrades non-linearly beyond architecture-specific thresholds, a phenomenon known as the speed–precision paradox. No prior synthesis has characterized this degradation as a system-level integration problem or identified the governing regime transitions. This review synthesizes approximately 180 peer-reviewed studies (2015–present) spanning bench experiments, CFD–DEM–MBD simulations, and field evaluations across mechanical, pneumatic, electric-drive, and centrifugal seeder architectures. A four-tier validation hierarchy (simulation, bench, soil-bin, field) structures a unified, technology-agnostic framework for interpreting speed-dependent precision loss across the full seeding chain: metering, delivery, soil–seed interaction, sensing–control, and energy. Three operational regimes emerge: (1) metering-dominated precision below 10.0 km h⁻1 governed by singulation quality, (2) a transition zone at 10.0–14.0 km h⁻1 with amplified delivery-stage instabilities, and (3) system-level breakdown above 14.0–16.0 km h⁻1 dominated by vibration, control latency, and soil–machine interactions. These thresholds represent empirical, architecture-dependent ranges. Bench-to-field gaps follow the three-regime framework: below 2.0 percentage points in Regime 1, 3.44 pp for active-constraint delivery in Regime 2, and a representative maximum of 16.38 pp for air-assisted architectures in Regime 3, representing architecture-specific bounds rather than universal field limits. Centrifugal metering drives consume approximately 71 times less power than full pneumatic systems under reported subsystem boundaries, demonstrating that architecture selection is a fundamental energy-design decision independent of forward speed. The three-regime model, operating envelope framework, and evidence-graded validation hierarchy together provide a structured foundation for the design and field validation of next-generation high-speed seeding technologies.

title: An innovative solar radiation modeling incorporating roof deformation effect in solar greenhouse
abstract: The daylighting performance of solar greenhouses is fundamentally governed by the synergistic interaction between environmental conditions and structural parameters, critically determining overall productivity. While conventional solar radiation models typically assume geometrically invariant, smooth-arc profiles to assess light interception, practical installations exhibit wave-like surface distortions from east-west deformations. These deformations induce spatiotemporal heterogeneity in light incidence angles and transmittance characteristics, consequently diminishing light interception capacity. To address this limitation, this study develops an innovative solar radiation numerical model for Photonic-Film Synergistic Transmission Dynamics using vector-based computational methods, enabling precise quantification of solar incidence angles, transmittance dynamics, and interception efficiency across deformed surfaces. We further propose two novel deformation-specific metrics: the Deformation-induced Light Loss Index (DLLI) and Cumulative Transmittance Loss Rate (CTLR). Results demonstrate a 4.30% reduction in average diurnal equivalent transmittance, Solar radiation interception for the overall greenhouse, ground surface, back wall, and back slope decreased by 2.13%, 2.37%, 2.90%, and 2.02%, respectively. Light transmittance losses induced by deformation exhibit positive proportionality to cloud cover fraction, Annual variations revealed DLLI and CTLR ranges of 0.62–1.63% and 0.87–2.81%, respectively. This work establishes a Multiphysics framework that couples radiation dynamics with structural deformation mechanics, providing universally applicable computational tools for flexible transparent materials. The PFSTD model and associated metrics collectively establish a theoretical toolkit and quantitative foundation for dynamic, precision regulation of winter light environments in high-latitude cold regions.

title: Semantic metadata extraction from crop model components with large language models to facilitate platform interoperability
abstract: Process-based crop models encapsulate agro-ecosystem knowledge in modular components, yet structural heterogeneity across platforms limits component reuse and demands manual curation of semantic metadata, which is error-prone and time consuming. Here, we present a workflow that leverages large language models (LLMs) to automatically create Crop2ML model specifications by extracting input/output variables specifications and by generating descriptions, from source code written in three different languages among six simulation platforms. Evaluation on eight soil temperature components from six widely used platforms and on 31 various components from three platforms showed F1-Score above 93% for input/output variables extraction. The workflow successfully inferred plausible metadata when documentation was ambiguous or incomplete. These findings demonstrate that LLM-assisted extraction can accelerate the creation of interoperable, semantically rich model documentation while preserving accuracy, thereby lowering the barrier to crop model reuse.

title: Risk-aware Neural Lazy-Theta* path planning for orchard picking robots in complex terrains
abstract: Path planning for orchard picking robots is challenged by undulating terrain, irregular obstacles, narrow passages, and perceptual uncertainty from foliage occlusion. Conventional geometric planners often lack semantic awareness for maintaining safety margins, whereas end-to-end learning approaches often provide limited interpretability in safety–critical decisions. We propose Neural Lazy-Theta*, a neural-guided any-angle planner that couples learned traversability priors with an interpretable Lazy-Theta* search process. The network decouples traversal guidance from probabilistic safety estimation, while the planner uses these priors to validate candidate segments through risk-aware line-of-sight (LOS) checking under geometric visibility, clearance, slope, and uncertainty constraints. A closed-loop, planner-aligned training strategy with path-tube supervision and piecewise consistency constraints further reduces the gap between learned representations and online search behavior. Under the same constraints and evaluation protocol, Neural Lazy-Theta* achieves a 96.5% planning success rate on a held-out test set (N = 200) and a path quality score of 0.964 relative to the Lazy-Theta* reference. In planar environments, it reduces the average number of turns by 85.2% compared with A*. In complex sloped orchard scenarios, it yields zero inflated-occupancy violations and lowers the average path slope to 5.3°, whereas Lazy-Theta* exhibits a 43.36% violation rate. Ablation confirms that the probabilistic safety branch is critical: removing it drops LOS success from 92.1% to 3.5%. Simulations and outdoor mock-up experiments indicate that Neural Lazy-Theta* maintains path lengths comparable to baseline planners while reducing turning demands and increasing obstacle clearance in orchard-like settings.

title: Soil water movement modeling in cracked soil under upward groundwater flow: from single crack to stochastic cracks
abstract: The presence of soil cracks alters soil hydrological characteristics, but the combined influences of cracks and upward groundwater flow on soil water movement remain unclear, particularly in shallow groundwater areas. In this study, a two-dimensional numerical model integrating Richards’ equation and the cubic law was developed using the finite element method to simulate upward groundwater seepage and soil water dynamics. Model simulations were validated against sandbox experiments under eight scenarios with varying pressure heads (0 ∼ 15 cm), crack angles (30°∼90°), and crack burial depths (0 ∼ 10 cm). The validated model was then extended to stochastic crack networks. Results demonstrated that increasing the groundwater pressure head from 0 to 15 cm increased cumulative upward seepage volume by 87 % on average (based on experimental and simulated values). Steeply inclined cracks (60°) produced 17 % higher upward seepage than shallow cracks (30°) on average, whereas deeper crack burial (10 cm) reduced seepage by 31 % on average compared to surface‑connected cracks. The hydraulically effective crack length, defined as Leff = min(LC, H) from Richards’ equation, along with vertical crack alignment and shallow depth, maximizes upward water flux. Stochastic crack networks introduce additional flow complexity through crack interactions and connectivity, generating localized saturation zones and irregular wetting front. The proposed COMSOL‑based model accurately predicts wetting front advancement and cumulative seepage volumes, with R2 > 0.92 and NSE > 0.83 across all validation treatments. Future work should improve crack geometry characterization, integrate additional physical processes, and develop automated parameter calibration. These findings provide a theoretical framework and numerical tools for understanding water dynamics in cracked soils.

title: Multi-object fish behavior analysis in recirculating aquaculture systems using oriented bounding boxes and model pruning
abstract: Recent advances in underwater object detection and tracking provide important technical support for quantitative fish behavior analysis. However, body curvature often causes centroid displacement in bounding boxes generated by conventional axis-aligned bounding box (AABB)-based detectors. To address this issue, this study proposed a lightweight oriented bounding box (OBB)-based detection and tracking model. First, a lightweight shared-convolution with separated batch normalization and dynamic anchors (LSCSBD) was designed to reduce computational overhead while maintaining detection precision. Additionally, redundant channel information was removed using Layer-Adaptive Magnitude-based Pruning (LAMP) to obtain a compact model. Finally, the improved detector was integrated with BoT-SORT to track 51 fish across consecutive frames and was deployed as part of a front-end system for practical application. Experimental results show that the proposed method achieves a precision of 98.1% and a Multiple Object Tracking Accuracy (MOTA) of 77.81%, with a 72.8% reduction in the number of parameters compared with the original model. In addition, the deployed system quantifies fish behavior by extracting movement trajectories and swimming distances. The proposed method and system provide technical support for digital and intelligent aquaculture management.

title: Analytical model of duckfoots draught force prediction based on soil parameters and technical tools, and its validation in laboratory conditions
abstract: The scientific objective of this work was to develop an analytical model for predicting the draught force required to overcome soil resistance by row weeders' duckfoots. The model considered variable duckfoot geometry, dynamic soil effects (i.e., changes in density, moisture, cohesion, and friction under tool loading), and nonlinear soil-implement interactions. The model was validated for three duckfoots with widths of 105 mm, 133 mm, and 202 mm. The tools were mounted on two types of flexible tines: a conventional S tine (stiffness 5.3 kN·m−1) and a Vibro Crop tine (VCO, stiffness 8.3 kN·m−1). The experiments were carried out in a soil bin filled with clay sand with a moisture content of 10% and 14% and a compactness of 486 kPa, using an instrumented measurement setup based on strain-gauge, laser, and optical sensors to acquire draught force, working depth and travel speed at duckfoots depths of 30, 50, and 70 mm and working velocities of 0.84, 1.67, and 2.31 m·s–1. The draught forces were predicted considering optimised values of the soil internal friction, soil–tool friction, and tool setting angles identified from the measurement data. The model showed good agreement with the experimental draught force values. For 10% and 14% soil moisture, the global errors were 18.0% and 24.7%, respectively, and the mean relative error was 0.8% in both cases. The model was validated and confirmed the hypothesis, but it requires further refinement and probabilistic analysis.

title: Planar array radar–capacitive multi-sensor fusion for powdery organic fertilizer flow rate monitoring
abstract: The rational partial substitution of chemical fertilizers by organic fertilizers has turned out to be mainstream fertilization practice in contemporary crop production. With the advent of Precision Agriculture, one can now find growing research work involving monitoring outflow rate or discharge flow rate of granular fertilizers through sensing and computing methodologies. However, monitoring solutions for powdery fertilizers are not completely researched. A multi-source data fusion monitoring system comprising Planar Array Radar, Capacitive measurement chip, and rotational speed sensor was conceived in this work to fill such a void. Six Machine Learning (ML) models—including XGBoost (XGB), Random Forest (RF), Extremely Randomized Trees (ET), Support Vector Regression (SVR), Backpropagation Neural Network (BPNN), and Multilayer Perceptron (MLP)—were employed to develop two prediction models: one involving Filling Coefficient of fertilizer as well as one involving discharge flow rate of powdery organic fertilizer. XGBoost (XGB) and SVR showed optimum prediction ability among them all, with Coefficient of Determination (R2) achieving 0.904 and 0.958 and Root Mean Squared Errors (RMSE) achieving 0.058 and 0.61, respectively. Experimental results showed that proposed models compress relative prediction error by as much as 29.85 % compared to traditional empirical formulas and therefore verify their robustness and precision. This study offers one new and feasible reference for non-intrusive real-time monitoring and precision regulation for powdery fertilizer dosing and catalyzes wider sustainable development in agriculture.

title: Physics-Informed Neural Network methods for predicting plant height development
abstract: ABSTRACT Plant growth is a dynamic process affected by genes and growing environment, with all kinds of interactions between them. These complex relationships make the prediction of plant growth challenging. We propose a hybrid modelling framework that combines a logistic ordinary differential equation model with a Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) neural network, resulting in a Physics Informed Neural Network (PINN). While PINNs have been widely applied to physical dynamical systems, their use in modelling the dynamics of plant growth systems is still largely unexplored. We illustrate the construction of a PINN on plant height data in wheat and compare its performance with alternative models for longitudinal plant data. All temporal prediction models only require time and temperature as input. Among a set of competing models, our PINN had the lowest average root mean squared error (RMSE) of prediction and the smallest standard deviation across multiple random initialisations. Therefore, we conclude that incorporating biological growth constraints into data-driven growth models can enhance prediction accuracy of longitudinal plant traits. Highlights Integrating plant growth equations into a temporal neural network improves plant height growth prediction over ordinary differential equations and machine learning models, especially when training data are limited.

title: Multi-device RGB image alignment for color-based prediction of soil organic carbon
abstract: The close association between soil organic carbon (SOC) content and soil color means that portable devices such as smartphones have the potential to facilitate efficient SOC assessment using color-based predictive modeling. However, if multiple devices were to contribute images to a large-scale soil image database, soil color discrepancies arising from the different camera sensors could greatly reduce the modeling performance for SOC prediction. To address this, we developed a linear color transformation method of aligning soil RGB images acquired from seven different devices without the need for professional color-calibration tools. Then, the aligned multi-device RGB images were tested through two different SOC prediction strategies, while also exploring the effect of data spiking on model performance: (1) the dual-device model (DDM), where a calibrated partial least squares regression model from one device was evaluated against images from another device; and (2) the multi-device model (MDM), where images from six devices were pooled for model calibration and images from the seventh device were used for validation. Results show that, for the test samples (n = 144) taken in a catchment of Northeast China, the proposed color-correction method improved color alignment among different devices, as evidenced by the decrease in average color difference (ΔE¯) values from > 10 to < 3 in most cases. The effectiveness of the color-correction method was also evident from both models’ performances, which displayed satisfactory SOC prediction accuracies, particularly for MDMs (R2: 0.79–0.85; RMSE: 1.71–2.34 g/kg). The addition of the spiking dataset led to further improvements in SOC prediction accuracy for both strategies, with the performance of MDMs resembling that obtained by single-device models, thus highlighting the potential to use multi-device images for effective and efficient color-based prediction of SOC.

title: Corrigendum to “Multi-task geometric regression with agronomic priors for crop row and missing seedling detection in maize-soybean strip intercropping” [Comput. Electron. Agr. 243 (2026) 111383]
Global wheat disease identification via AI technologies: An in-depth survey with sustainability and future projections
abstract:
Context
Wheat is a prevalent staple crop globally and plays a significant role in ensuring the security of food. According to the USDA, the worldwide wheat output rate is declining by 3.6 % yearly during 2023-2024. Global wheat output for 2024/2025 is anticipated to be around 799.71 million metric tons. The fungal, bacterial, and viral illnesses impacting wheat awn, spike, stem, and root are leading to decreased production; hence, it is crucial to advance AI technology for detecting these diseases to facilitate sustainable management practices that mitigate globally occurring grain production losses.
Objective
The primary objective of this study is to assess and carefully analyze WD research published from 1960 to 2025. The authors endeavor to identify significant advancements in computer vision (image processing, classification, detection, and segmentation) and robotics (UAV and UAG), assessing resources, effectiveness, performance, quality, challenges, deficiencies, prospective and anticipated trajectories.
Method
This research utilized an advanced GCS methodology, selecting one thousand five hundred forty-three articles from various online source databases via WoS. One hundred seventy-five studies were eliminated throughout the investigation’s extraction procedure.
Results
The application proportions for DL, ML, and hybrid methods in the vision system were 87 %, 22 %, and 2 %, respectively. The illness distribution frequencies were PM (48 %), LR (31 %), WSR (11 %), and R (10 %). The predominant algorithms implemented were CNN (40 %), Yolov5s (35 %), and Unet (25 %), with an average maximum efficiency of 98.70 %. The targeted diseases for robotic and UAV applications were striped and rust, accounting for 2 %. China, the United States, India, and Australia were the most significant contributors to wheat disease identification, with shares of 23 %, 16 %, 6 %, and 5 %, respectively.
Conclusion
The bibliometric analysis pattern indicates a persistent robotics development deficit compared to visual systems and a strong association between biotechnology, computer intelligence, remote sensing, and inventive methods to sustainably manage WD. Furthermore, it highlighted the deficiencies and obstacles related to efficiency, quality, cost, environmental impact, and the saturation of the SDGs.

title: Effects of different LED light wavelengths on deep learning-based insect detection in arable crops
abstract: Approaches for automated image-based insect detection are rapidly maturing and becoming a reality for commercial use. However, complex image backgrounds, lighting variations and high variability between different insects’ physical appearance can reduce detection accuracy. Integrating artificial LED lighting into the image acquisition process can enhance the visibility of key insect morphological features, particularly in field applications, thereby improving feature extraction and overall detection performance of machine learning models. Achieving this requires the identification of light wavelengths that best reveal important insect characteristics, such as pigmentation, body patterns, and nanoscale-structural reflections, for more effective discrimination analysis and model training. We investigated the effect of five different LED wavelengths (red (600–700 nm), blue (400–500 nm), white (400–700 nm), UVA (315–400 nm) and a composite mixture of Blue, White, and red (BWR)) on insect identification and on the performance of deep learning-based detection methods in comparison with images taken in natural field conditions. Images of Colorado potato beetle on potato plants and ladybirds and aphids on potato, faba bean and sugar beet were collected with images comprising: (i) simple scenes containing a single insect and (ii) complex multi-class image scenes, with multiple insect individuals on a single image. Using the pre-processed datasets, two deep learning models, YOLOv11 and Swin transformer, were trained and evaluated. Results demonstrate promising potential on multi-class insect datasets, with the blue LED achieving the best detection performance (mAP@50 of 94.5 %) for adult ladybirds. Meanwhile, the composite mixture (BWR) produced the highest performance for both adult and larval Colorado potato beetles, with mAP@50 scores of 96.7 % and 94.4 %, respectively. The red LED performed best for pre-adult stages of ladybirds (84.2 % for eggs, 87.9 % for larvae and 95.3 % for pupae) and for eggs of Colorado potato beetles (88.0 %). For aphid detection, white LED light showed promising performance, achieving mAP@50 of 91.2 %, while the baseline outdoor imaging achieved an mAP@50 of 50.7 %. These results demonstrate that LED lighting enables better model learning and discrimination between different insect species and life stages. The use of LED lights demonstrates strong potential to improve model performance without increasing its architectural computational complexity, thereby facilitating future on-farm deployment of targeted pest management solutions.

title: A multirobot system for autonomous crop field scouting: System integration and demonstration
abstract: This paper introduces an integrated system for autonomous crop field scouting, which incorporates novel algorithms for crop row identification and multirobot task distribution. The system utilizes a flexible team of aerial and ground robots, coordinated by a central computer that manages both the user interface and the back-end software that handles crop row detection and task allocation algorithms. The user interface allows users to initiate the scouting process by selecting target areas on an aerial map and monitor and control the process in real time. Autonomous crop row detection, given aerial images of the target field, is realized via GIS-based autonomous geo-coordinate generation. This information is then inputted into the task allocation algorithms, which determine the number and types of robots and assign them to specific locations to cover the field optimally. The adaptable architecture accommodates different types and numbers of robots to scale to farms of varying sizes. Simulations and field tests were performed to validate system-level integration.

title: Multidepth soil sensing with an embedded hydrothermal stress index captures stratified stability in hardpan-limited tropical spodosol oil palm systems
abstract: Hardpan-limited tropical Spodosol oil palm systems can exhibit strong vertical hydrothermal stratification, yet operational monitoring often relies on single-depth measurements that overrepresent surface wetting–drying dynamics. This study developed and evaluated a multidepth hydrothermal monitoring system integrated with an embedded Hydrothermal Root Zone Stress Index (HRZSI) as a site-calibrated descriptor of root-zone stability. The system was deployed in a rainfed oil palm plantation in Central Kalimantan, Indonesia, with soil moisture and temperature measured at 0–10, 10–42, and 42–68 cm using RS485 probes connected to an ESP32-based photovoltaic platform. Hourly records were quality-controlled and aggregated into 227 daily observations. Independent validation against gravimetric–volumetric references showed strong sensing performance (R2 = 0.987, RMSE = 1.00 %, MAPE = 2.38 %). The profile showed depth-dependent hydrothermal behavior, with soil moisture variance of 20.81, 43.16, and 44.26 in Layers 1–3, indicating deeper seasonal storage–depletion dynamics rather than monotonic damping. Empirical thermal–moisture coupling became more structured with depth, with R2 increasing from 0.260 to 0.511. HRZSI classified the period into 161 Stable days (70.93 %), 46 Transitional days (20.26 %), and 20 Unstable days (8.81 %), with short-term persistence confirmed by autocorrelation and Markov transition analysis. Baseline comparison showed that surface-only monitoring poorly represented integrated stability (κ = 0.232), whereas combined moisture–temperature information provided closer agreement (κ = 0.915). KDE-based instability envelopes identified depth-specific moisture–stability domains. The proposed framework provides a traceable basis for multidepth soil monitoring and precision water-management support in hardpan-limited tropical plantation systems.

title: Optimized ensemble learning frameworks for early grain yield prediction in winter wheat using static and multitemporal multispectral UAV data
abstract: A stacked ensemble learning framework was developed leveraging the large-scale spatial and temporal diversity in a winter wheat breeding program. Multispectral data were collected from 1098 plots comprising 586 genetically diverse advanced breeding lines at tillering, stem elongation, reproductive, early grain filling, mid grain filling, and late dough stages. Raw spectral information, 28 vegetation indices and 16 grey-level co-occurrence matrices were used– both individually and in combination –to train five machine learning algorithms– elastic net , support vector regression , k-nearest neighbours , random forest , and extreme gradient boosting . Static and temporal models were trained for spatial interpolation and genetic extrapolation, followed by internal and external validation. Multispectral features showed stage-specific discriminatory power for separating yield groups, peaking between the reproductive and mid grain filling stages. Classification was limited by overlap between medium- and high-yielding groups. Models integrating multispectral data across growth stages outperformed all other strategies. Elastic net performed best overall, while support vector regression showed the most consistent ranking. Base learners achieved average prediction accuracy of 55.85 % and 46.00 %, with AUC values of 0.73 and 0.66 for internal and external validation, respectively. Selected base-learners were used for stacked elastic net ensemble learning, which increased overall prediction (∼18 %) and classification (∼7 %) accuracies, while reducing errors (∼10 %). These improvements were primarily attributed to reduced bias. Overall, this study presents a scalable machine learning framework trained and validated on an operational breeding program for data-driven UAV-assisted early generation selection, providing a methodological reference for future research and deployment.

title: Color-distance triggering endogenous actuation variable-structure soft grippers with intake-deflation mechanism in finger cups
abstract: Despite significant advances in pneumatic soft grippers, current designs still suffer from several limitations, including reliance on external air sources, complex active control requirements, and limited adaptability to targets with diverse geometries. In this work, we propose an endogenous actuation variable-structure soft gripper capable of effectively grasping both spherical and cylindrical targets through structural transformation of the palm. By monolithically integrating mini air pump within gripper and intake-deflation microchannels in cup arrays on the finger surfaces, bidirectional intake and deflation airflow are actively controlled, which enables efficient stiffness-adaptive grasping in unstructured environments without reliance on external pneumatic sources. Furthermore, by embedding a color sensor and a Time-of-Flight (ToF) laser sensor within the palm, the soft gripper achieves fully autonomous grasping triggered jointly by color recognition and distance detection, thereby dramatically simplifying the control architecture. This work presents a comprehensive exposition of the design and functionality of the proposed soft gripper. It details the design concept, structural composition, material, and fabrication processes of both the variable-structure palm and the soft finger, followed by comprehensive kinematic, pneumatic, and finite-element analyses and simulations. Optimization was performed on the geometric parameters of the variable-structure palm as well as the intake-deflation microchannels within the soft finger. This work further elaborates on the developed low-cost, fully integrated control system that incorporates actuation drivers and multimodal sensor modules, enabling precise variable-structure control and fully autonomous grasping triggered by fused color and distance sensing. Test validation, in the fruit grasping task, demonstrates that the soft gripper achieves an average success rate exceeding 95.5 % across two typical target geometries (spherical and cylindrical), with a variable-structure response time of 2.0 ∼ 2.5 s and a complete grasping cycle of 3.0 ∼ 6.0 s, while consistently ensuring adaptive and strictly non-destructive contact. The proposed gripper effectively overcomes limitations of pneumatic soft grippers, namely, low pneumatic integration, complex triggering control, and restricted structural adaptability, while offering operational simplicity and high scalability. It thereby provides a novel, practical solution for automated end-effector in agricultural non-destructive harvesting and food processing.

title: Pay more attention to electron transfer in agricultural soils
abstract: The functionality and health of agricultural soils directly influence food productivity and environmental safety. Biological electron transfer in redox reactions is a fundamental force for material transformation and energy transfer in soil and thus plays a crucial role in global biogeochemical cycles. In recent years, the significance of electron transfer in soil ecosystems has received increasing attention due to its role in regulating soil microbial functions. Electron transfer not only affects pollutant biodegradation and nutrient cycling in the soil but also influences greenhouse gas emissions by altering the structure and function of soil microbial communities. This review comprehensively examines the natural occurrence of electron transfer in agricultural soils, its influencing factors, and its various applications in the ecological environment, while highlighting future developments. This underscores the core role of electron transfer in soil function and lays the foundation for the development of innovative soil ecological regulation methods.

title: Advancing digital agri-food systems through integrated AI, robotics, IoT, and blockchain with a bibliometric analysis
abstract: Digital Agri-Food Systems (DAFS) are transforming agriculture by combining digital and intelligent technologies to enhance automation, traceability, and data-driven decisions. This study evaluates technical advancements in DAFS by examining 332 peer-reviewed articles retrieved from Scopus. Using a hybrid evidence-synthesis approach that integrates Systematic Mapping and the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA), it enables wide theme coverage requiring thorough screening, explicit inclusion criteria, and repeatability. The study identifies dominant research trajectories, methodological trends, and cross-domain technological interactions spanning crop production, livestock systems, food safety, and supply chain management. The findings show a marked transition toward hybrid intelligent frameworks that merge multimodal sensing with advanced analytical models for real-time crop monitoring, early disease detection, yield forecasting, autonomous robotics, and verifiable supply chain traceability. Internet of Things (IoT) sensor networks and unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV)-based imaging continue to strengthen precision agriculture practices, while blockchain-enabled systems support transparency, trust, and fraud prevention. Additionally, bibliometric analysis reveals strong international collaboration clusters and rapidly expanding research in precision agriculture, agricultural robotics, and intelligent supply chains. Key challenges persist, such as limited datasets, inconsistent validation, high computational costs, and insufficient focus on cybersecurity. The study shows that advancing DAFS requires scalable, unified architectures linking artificial intelligence (AI)-driven decision tools, interoperable IoT systems, and secure blockchain technologies. The integration is essential for building resilient, efficient, and sustainability-driven agri-food systems.

title: Path planning for citrus harvesting robot based on adaptive parallel-coupled RRT*
abstract: To address the challenges of path planning for citrus-harvesting robots in unstructured orchard environments, an adaptive parallel-coupled RRT* algorithm (APC-RRT*) is proposed. A three-phase expansion strategy, consisting of aggressive goal-directed exploration, improved tangential artificial potential field sampling, and adaptive ellipsoidal sampling, is introduced. This strategy is dynamically coupled with a manipulability-balanced feedback mechanism, which ensures that the search is guided away from difficult areas and that kinematically favorable configurations are given priority, thereby enabling efficient global exploration and precise obstacle avoidance. In addition, a pruning operation is applied to optimize the path, ensuring that smooth, dynamically feasible joint trajectories are generated while kinematically favorable configurations are maintained. Simulation results show that APC-RRT* reduces the average planning time by 35.7% compared with baseline algorithms, achieving a planning time of 0.09 s. In experiments with a six-degree-of-freedom citrus harvesting manipulator, the number of singular configurations was reduced from 8 to 2, and the harvesting success rate reached 93.3%. The proposed method improves planning efficiency and reduces singular configurations, providing a potentially practical approach to motion planning in autonomous citrus harvesting manipulators operating in unstructured orchard environments.

title: Dual end-effectors for grasping and cutting: an adaptive and damage-free approach to robotic pitaya picking
abstract: Pitaya fruits are primarily borne along the stem ribs and often remain pressed tightly against the stem surface, with short and robust peduncles lacking a natural abscission point or “snap”. In addition, the cluttered stem environment, together with the fruits’ large size, heavy weight, and delicate skin, poses significant challenges for mechanical harvesting. To achieve efficient and damage-free harvesting, an automated harvesting solution employing dual end-effectors for coordinated grasping and cutting is proposed. A cable-driven bionic three-fingered end-effector was developed for fruit grasping, with thin-film pressure sensors integrated into each phalanx to accurately perceive contact forces. Furthermore, a novel grasping quality metric, Q, was proposed to dynamically distribute grasping forces among the phalanges. In parallel, a dedicated cutting end-effector was designed to perform precise cuts on the fruit peduncle. Experimental results demonstrated that the grasping end-effector achieved stable grasps under various grasping patterns. In grasping pattern 2, the average contact force was 2.57 ± 0.35 N. In cases of missing contact point, the proposed control strategy adaptively increased the forces at the remaining contact points by 1.5–3.0 N to maintain grasp stability. The cutting end-effector successfully severed peduncles with diameters ranging from 5 to 10 mm, producing stem notch areas of 311.2–412 mm2. Overall, the proposed dual end-effector system demonstrates strong potential for efficient, stable, and low-damage automated pitaya harvesting in complex growing environments.

title: An integrated YOLO-WGAN-GP framework for cage removal and image restoration in Stacked-Cage chicken house
abstract: In stacked-cage poultry houses, image acquisition for chicken condition monitoring robots is significantly affected by interference from cage wire mesh, which leads to reduced accuracy in individual chicken or organ detection and segmentation. To address this challenge, this study proposes an innovative framework that integrated You Only Look Once algorithm (YOLO) with the Wasserstein GAN with Gradient Penalty algorithm (WGAN-GP), named YOLO-WGAN-GP, to effectively remove cage wire mesh interference and reconstruct high-quality chicken images. The approach first employs the improved YOLOv8n-seg algorithm to segment the cage wire mesh region and generate its corresponding binary mask. Subsequently, the improved WGAN-GP algorithm is utilized to eliminate the cage wire mesh interference information and restore the complete chicken image. Comparative experiments show that the improved YOLOv8n-seg achieves precision, recall, mAP50, and F1 scores of 90.6 %, 88.6 %, 90.5 %, and 89.6 %, respectively, outperforming YOLOv12n-seg, YOLOv11n-seg, YOLOv9n-seg, and YOLOv8n-seg.Ablation studies further confirm the effectiveness of the introduced modules. For image restoration, the proposed WGAN-GP achieves PSNR, SSIM, LPIPS, and FID values of 36.35, 0.98, 0.01, and 6.36, respectively, demonstrating superior reconstruction quality. The proposed YOLO-WGAN-GP framework is capable of generating a more complete and non-destructive contour image of caged chickens, thereby providing a technical foundation for minimizing the interference from cage wire mesh information during intelligent, unmanned, and non-contact image acquisition and analysis.
keywords: Segmentation of the cage wire mesh

title: Fusion of keypoint detection and posture-aware correction for body measurement of dairy cattle
abstract: Accurate and efficient non-contact body measurement of dairy cattle is essential for Precision Livestock Farming (PLF), enabling data-driven monitoring, management, and genetic improvement. Keypoint-based computer vision methods offer a powerful approach to this task. However, two critical challenges hinder its effective implementation: (1) Inaccurate localization of keypoints caused by weak visual features, and (2) Measurement deviations induced by non-standard postures. To address these issues, a novel method named CowSizeNet was proposed, which integrates keypoint detection, initial size estimation, and posture-aware correction into a coherent process. In the first stage, the Cattle Keypoint Detection Network (CKDNet) was developed to achieve reliable keypoint localization. Two dedicated modules introduced in this study, the Bidirectional Feature Enhancement Module (BFEM) and the Hyper-Graph Association Enhancement Module (HGAEM), were incorporated to enrich visual representations and strengthen spatial associations, significantly improving the localization accuracy of visually ambiguous regions. In the second stage, stereo image disparity and camera parameters were utilized to obtain depth information, enabling 3D projection of detected keypoints and initial body size estimation. In the final stage, a Posture-aware Correction Graph Convolutional Network (PC-GCN) was introduced to learn the nonlinear relationships among keypoint geometry, joint angles, and body measurement deviations under varying postures. By regressing and compensating posture-related deviations, the model yielded more accurate and consistent body size estimations. Experiments verified the effectiveness and feasibility of the proposed method. For Body Length (BL), Body Height (BH), and Hip Height (HH), the Mean Absolute Percentage Errors (MAPE) were 4.26%, 1.97%, and 2.19%, respectively, satisfying the accuracy requirements for automated body measurement in PLF. Furthermore, the design and development of supporting terminal devices and visualization platforms further enhanced the practical value of the proposed method, promoting its use in dairy farm management.

title: Unified vision: Multi-task learning for retinal image-based cattle trait classification
abstract: Reliable identification of demographic traits such as gender, breed, and age is fundamental to automated herd management in precision livestock farming. Traditional approaches based on external morphology or manual tagging are often labour-intensive, error-prone, or susceptible to tampering. In contrast, retinal imaging provides a non-invasive and stable biometric modality with high inter-individual variability. This study proposes a multi-task learning (MTL) framework for simultaneous classification of gender, breed, and age group from cattle retinal fundus images. The architecture incorporates multi-scale spatial feature fusion to capture fine-grained vascular patterns and broader retinal structures, positional encoding combined with Transformer-based relational modeling to enhance spatial dependency learning, and uncertainty-weighted multi-task optimization to balance task contributions adaptively. Experiments were conducted on a dataset of 1,206 retinal images from 233 individual cattle, annotated with demographic labels. The proposed model achieved strong performance across all three tasks. For gender classification, it attained 0.909 in accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score. Breed classification yielded scores of 0.880, 0.886, 0.880, and 0.883, while age classification achieved 0.926, 0.929, 0.926, and 0.927, respectively. Visualization analyses using t-SNE demonstrated that the multi-task framework produced more compact intra-class clustering and greater inter-class separability compared to single-task baselines. Grad-CAM visualizations further confirmed that the proposed model consistently focused on anatomically meaningful regions, particularly the optic disc and major vascular bifurcations. Comparative analysis confirmed the superiority of integrating multi-scale feature extraction, spatial relational modeling, and task uncertainty weighting in retinal image-based livestock phenotyping. This work highlights the potential of retinal imaging combined with multi-task learning for developing scalable, interpretable, and automated livestock phenotyping systems.

title: Feeding behavior rhythms of artificial Diet-Reared silkworms (Bombyx mori) based on Dual-Coordinate systems and multiscale signal analysis
abstract: With the adoption of whole-age artificial diet–based rearing in China’s sericulture industry, accurately capturing silkworm feeding behavior has become essential for intelligent farming management. Feeding behavior reflects physiological status and ingestive rhythm, yet current studies remain limited and traditional observations rely on manual experience, preventing continuous and precise characterization. This study proposes a non-invasive quantitative framework that integrates machine vision with multi-scale signal analysis to analyze feeding behavior under artificial-diet conditions. A YOLOv12 and ByteTrack pipeline is used for high-precision detection and continuous tracking of the silkworm head. A dual-coordinate analytical model combining Cartesian and dynamic polar coordinates is constructed to extract high-resolution motion trajectories. Kernel Density Estimation, Fast Fourier Transform, Time-domain analysis, and wavelet transform are applied to reveal multi-scale motion patterns and rhythmic features. Experiments were conducted on 4th instar silkworms at the post-ecdysis initial feeding stage, and the results showed that their feeding behavior presents a stable three-phase feeding rhythm structure composed of the rapid micro-swing phase, slow-rhythm adjustment phase and rest phase: a rapid micro-swing phase representing fine ingestive actions, a slow-rhythm adjustment phase involving directional and postural modulation, and a rest phase reflecting brief physiological pauses. Using the dual-coordinate system analysis model, this study achieved the decoupling of macroscopic movement paths and microscopic movements. The Cartesian coordinate system revealed the dominant gnawing rhythm at 1.5–2.2 Hz and the rapid micro-swings within the feeding zone, while the dynamic polar coordinate system demonstrated the high stability of the radial distance (87% of energy below 0.2 Hz) and the 1–2 Hz periodic bimodal swings of the polar angle around ± 90°. Finally, supplementary extended validation was performed on 3rd and 5th instar silkworms under artificial diet rearing conditions, which confirmed the cross-instar stability of the three-phase structure in 3rd to 5th instar silkworms reared on artificial diet, and clarified the variation trends of core parameters across different instars. This framework enables dynamic, fine-scale quantification of silkworm feeding behavior and provides new evidence for understanding ingestive mechanisms. It also offers a reusable technical pathway for automated behavioral monitoring and intelligent optimization of feeding strategies, and has important application prospects for promoting the intelligent and refined development of industrialized artificial diet rearing of silkworms.

title: A rubber tapping robot end-effector based on manual tapping curves for natural rubber harvesting
abstract: The harvesting of natural rubber trees is a labor-intensive and time-consuming process, and the advent of agricultural robots offers a promising alternative. The end-effector serves as a critical component of a rubber tapping robot, playing a vital role in the automation of natural rubber harvesting. To design an efficient end-effector for rubber tapping robots, this study presents a method that evaluates and analyzes manual cutting curves. The variation in bark response during the rubber tapping process was examined using a coupled knife-tree finite element model. A rubber tapping robot end-effector based on manual tapping curves was proposed and developed, and its performance was evaluated through testing in both simulated and field experiments. Finite element simulation tests reveal that a cutting angle of 30° and a cutting thickness of 1 mm produced relatively lower and more stable cutting resistance. Kinetic simulation results demonstrate that a single cutting operation requires approximately 40 s. Field experiment results for the end effector indicate that a single rubber tapping operation takes approximately 41 s, while a complete rubber tapping cycle requires 150 s. The clamping success rate is 96.7 %, while the cutting success rate is 93.3 %. Additionally, the bark damage rate is 22.7 %, and the rate of qualified cutting surfaces is 68.2 %. Positioning failures and collisions are identified as the primary causes of rubber tapping failures. This study offers a significant reference and theoretical foundation for the design of natural rubber tapping robots and their end-effectors.

title: Study on the mechanical behavior and failure mechnisms of pecans based on multiscale biomechanical modeling
abstract: High kernel damage and low processing efficiency are major issues plaguing the mechanical shelling of pecans. The lack of comprehensive theoretical research and precise quantitative analysis on shell cracking and kernel damage under mechanical load has impeded advances in processing equipment performance. Consequently, a multiscale biomechanical modeling-based approach was developed and verified in this study to analyze the compression mechanical behavior of pecans. The integration of Scanning Electron Microscopy (SEM), nanoindentation, X-ray Computed Tomography (CT), and mechanical property testing enabled a systematic investigation into the multiscale structural features, micromechanical properties, and macroscopic mechanical behavior of pecans. On this basis, a multiscale biomechanical model of the pecan was constructed. The finite element simulation successfully captured the complete failure progression from micro-damage initiation to macro-crack propagation. The predicted crack path and load–displacement curve showed excellent agreement with experimental data, thereby validating the model. The model not only reveals the crack propagation patterns in the shell and the damage mechanisms of the kernel under different loading modes and rates but also enables the visualization and quantitative analysis of the compressive mechanical behavior of pecans. The results indicated that the crack propagation path in the shell was closely related to the loading method, loading speed, and structural features, while the extent of kernel damage was significantly influenced by the loading rate. Optimization of the loading parameters paves the way for minimized kernel damage and maximized shelling efficiency. This study establishes a theoretical and technical foundation for the mechanical shelling of pecans, while also serving as a valuable reference for the biomechanical study and processing optimization of other nut varieties.

title: A narrow inter-row mobile platform with multi-sensor fusion navigation for greenhouse tomato phenotyping
abstract: Narrow cultivation rows and dense plant occlusion in greenhouses pose major challenges to autonomous phenotypic data acquisition for tomato production. This study presents the development of a Differential Drive Phenotypic Acquisition Robot (DiPARob) for greenhouse tomato phenotyping. The platform features an ultra-narrow body structure with a width of 30 cm, enabling operation within commercial greenhouse inter-row spaces. Given the degraded and intermittent GNSS signals caused by structural shielding and crop-induced multipath interference in greenhouse environments, a novel unscented Kalman filter (UKF)-based pose estimation method was proposed. This method fuses measurements from dual front-rear real-time kinematic (RTK) rovers, an inertial measurement unit (IMU), vision observations, and wheel odometry, effectively improving the localization stability of the robot under occluded greenhouse conditions. Field experiments conducted in commercial greenhouses demonstrated that the proposed platform maintains reliable navigation performance at traveling speeds of 0.2, 0.3, and 0.4 m/s, with average lateral tracking error and heading errors below 0.066 m and 3.84°, respectively. This study provides a practical technical reference for the structural design and autonomous navigation of mobile phenotyping robots for protected agriculture scenarios.

title: Surface reconstruction of orchard crops under weak covisibility enhanced by iterative semantic cues and geometric priors
abstract: In real orchard environments, harvesting robots often operate in dense foliage, narrow inter-row spaces, and under complex, dynamically changing illumination. These conditions limit the robot’s ability to obtain wide, continuous viewpoints, with common visual features between sequential frames often obscured by environmental disturbances. This leads to inherently weak-covisibility inputs, characterized by unstable spatial features due to alternating direct sunlight and shadows, small overlapping regions caused by hierarchical occlusions from branches and leaves, and low consistency in morphological and spatial feature distributions across different fruit species. Consequently, robots struggle to build a coherent understanding of orchard scenes and fruit targets, which limits performance in fruit volume estimation, yield assessment, fruit localization, and harvesting path planning.To address these challenges, this study analyzes the limitations of existing point cloud registration methods, particularly their reliance on initial poses, feature alignment, and error convergence. We propose a novel point cloud reconstruction framework that integrates iterative semantic cues and geometric priors into a unified optimization mechanism. By jointly constraining geometric priors and semantic segmentation, the proposed method establishes a dynamic iterative optimization process that significantly enhances the stability and accuracy of point cloud registration and surface reconstruction under weak-covisibility conditions. Quantitative comparisons demonstrate that the proposed method achieves a registration RMSE of 1.02 mm under weak-covisibility conditions. Field experiments in real orchard environments further demonstrate robust reconstruction under illumination variations, occlusions, and robotic motion, achieving a fruit reconstruction error of 8.34% and an average reconstruction time of 1.87 s per fruit.This work provides effective support for 3D modeling and autonomous operation of agricultural robots.

title: Layered cross-modal fusion for multispectral object detection: A case study on RGB–R walnuts
abstract: Multispectral sensing offers complementary spectral cues that can mitigate the failure modes of single-modal RGB detection under low contrast, illumination changes, and occlusions commonly observed in orchards. Targeting Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) imagery of walnuts, this paper regards RGB and the red-band (R; 650 ± 16 nm) as a practical visible-domain pair and proposes a hierarchical two-stream fusion framework precisely aligned with the YOLO feature pyramid. Concretely, we design three cooperative modules—Hierarchical Cross-Modal Dynamic Fusion Mechanism (HCM-DFM) at P3 for fine-grained alignment of geometry and texture across modalities, Cross-Modal Channel–Spatial Fusion (CM-CSF) at P4 for steady recalibration, and Cross-Modal Dynamic Routing Collaboration (CM-DRC) at P5 for long-range, semantics-aware consistency. In support of this study, we build WU-MID, to our knowledge the first RGB–R walnut detection benchmark, consisting of 717 registered image pairs and 63,504 annotated instances, all small objects with dense distribution. On WU-MID, the best mixed configuration — HCM-DFM at P3, CM-CSF at P4, and CM-DRC at P5 — outperforms the two-stream baseline in mAP, AP50, AP75, Precision, and Recall under controlled complexity, and ablation experiments confirm that each scale makes a non-redundant contribution. Cross-domain experiments on FLIR, VEDAI, and DroneVehicle indicate that the proposed scale-wise division of labor generalizes to heterogeneous sensors and scenes. Qualitative visualizations further reveal that the three modules respectively strengthen local alignment, suppress cross-modal noise, and enforce global semantic coherence. The framework is easy to integrate and shows promise for UAV-based orchard applications such as fruit counting, yield estimation, and anomaly monitoring.

title: AI-enabled electromagnetic sensor architecture for precision welfare monitoring in small ruminant production systems
abstract: Climate change and increasing heat stress present growing challenges for the welfare and productivity of small ruminants raised in arid and hot environments. In many production systems, animal health and welfare are still assessed primarily through visual observation, which may delay the detection of subtle physiological or behavioural changes associated with emerging welfare risks. Recent developments in precision livestock farming offer new possibilities for continuous and objective monitoring of animal conditions through advanced sensing technologies. This review explores recent progress in electromagnetic sensing technologies and their integration with artificial intelligence (AI) for monitoring animal welfare in small ruminant production systems. A literature search was conducted using the Web of Science, Scopus, and Google Scholar databases, focusing mainly on studies published over the past decade related to sensor-based livestock monitoring, electromagnetic sensing approaches, and AI-supported welfare assessment. Studies examining physiological, behavioural, or environmental indicators relevant to livestock welfare were considered. Recent studies indicate that electromagnetic sensing technologies—including microwave antennas, radar-based monitoring systems, metamaterial sensors, and dielectric sensing devices—can detect a range of welfare-related indicators such as respiration patterns, locomotor activity, and hydration status. When combined with machine-learning algorithms, these systems enable the interpretation of complex data streams and support more proactive approaches to welfare management. Based on the reviewed literature, this paper proposes a conceptual framework that integrates three key monitoring modules thermal comfort, locomotor stability, and hydration balance to illustrate how multi-sensor data can be analyzed through AI-driven approaches in small-ruminant production systems under arid climatic conditions. While these technologies show considerable promise, practical challenges remain, including sensor robustness in farm environments, economic feasibility, and the need for appropriate farmer training. Further research is therefore required to evaluate integrated sensor–AI systems under commercial farming conditions and to develop scalable decision-support tools for precision livestock management. To the best of our knowledge, this is among the first reviews to specifically focus on the integration of electromagnetic sensing technologies and artificial intelligence for welfare monitoring in small ruminants under arid climatic conditions.

title: A method for quantifying feeding behavior of grass carp in outdoor ponds with complex backgrounds
abstract: In aquaculture, precise quantification of fish feeding behavior is essential for formulating feeding strategies. However, dynamic background factors in outdoor pond farming can interfere with the extraction of fish school behavior characteristics. To address this, a novel method has been proposed for quantifying fish behavior under complex conditions. First, the MusFormer model was developed, integrating a mixed transformer encoder with a custom multi-scale feature fusion decoder. This decoder includes a residual MLP and a multi-scale feature fusion module, enabling the generation of high-precision semantic segmentation images of fish school feeding areas. Subsequently, a new method called QFA (Quantitative Feeding Activity Index) was established to quantify the spatial characteristics of fish school feeding behavior. By assigning weights to pixel points, this method reduces interference from segmentation errors and dynamic changes in the background mask. Finally, to evaluate its effectiveness under complex background conditions, the QFA framework was integrated with three mainstream temporal classification models: RNN, Transformer, and RCNN. This combination yielded classification accuracies of 90.97 %, 88.73 %, and 91.86 %, respectively, outperforming existing fish appetite assessment methods, which achieve a maximum accuracy of 84.17 %. These findings demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method for quantifying fish feeding behavior in outdoor ponds with typical complex background disturbances.

title: Estimating grass-clover mixtures quality using field spectroradiometry and stacking-based ensemble learning models
abstract: In this study, we designed a stacking ensemble machine learning method for accurate estimation of grass-clover biomass quality from high-resolution hyperspectral field data. Basic learners were support vector machine (SVM), K-Nearest Neighbor (KNN), random forest (RF), decision tree (DT), partial least square regress (PLS), shallow artificial- (ANN) and deep multi-layer perceptron (MLPs) neural networks. Three meta learners in the second layer were RF (stackingRF), eXtreme Gradient Boosting (stackingXGB), and CatBoost (stackingCat). We used 6 different datasets for the estimation, including the raw spectral reflectance, its 1 st and 2 nd derivatives, and their Standard Normal Variate (SNV). Quality indices were crude ash, crude protein, crude fat, crude fiber, neutral detergent fiber (NDF), acid detergent fiber (ADF), water-soluble carbohydrates (WSC), sugar, and fructans. The results showed that spectral feature selection by the PLS was useful in preprocessing. All machine learning methods predicted well quality from the raw reflectance, with PLS performing best (R 2 = 0.64–0.87) for all indices except crude ash. The stacked ensemble learning benefited the predictions, especially with stackingRF and stackingCat as meta learners (R2 increased by 2–8 % compared with the average of the four best machine learning algorithms in the first layer). SNV generally performed better than the original reflectance across most datasets. In particular, SNV applied to the 2nd derivative, combined with either PLS or StackingRF, yielded the best predictions for carbohydrates (sugar, fructans, WSC) and fiber (crude fiber, NDF, ADF), achieving the highest R 2 values (0.74–0.87) and the lowest nRMSE (5–15 %) among all pre‑processing options. The red‑edge region (700–780 nm) is the most important for all quality indices, except for ADF. This is among the first studies to systematically evaluate stacking ensemble learning, using the outputs of multiple machine‑learning algorithms as inputs, for predicting biomass quality and supporting field management in complex grass–clover mixtures. PLS‑based feature selection combined with stacking ensemble learning on second‑derivative SNV spectra appears particularly promising and warrants testing at larger spatial and temporal scales.

title: A generative compressed sensing-based method for reconstructing in-situ soil monitoring data
abstract: In-situ soil monitoring systems typically operate autonomously in field conditions, where hourly measurements consume substantial energy and accelerate equipment degradation. Compressed sensing (CS) can mitigate these issues through low-frequency sampling and subsequent reconstruction without sacrificing monitoring accuracy. In agricultural and environmental fields, however, standard CS methods are constrained by a theoretical minimum sampling ratio of 20% to 30%. Meanwhile, generative compressed sensing (GCS) methods, which hold promise for addressing this limitation through deep neural networks, remain insufficiently studied. This study proposes a GCS-CVAE method to achieve ultra-low frequency sampling in soil monitoring and establish a methodological foundation for the development of soil monitoring systems. This method utilizes the decoder of a high-latent-dimensional convolutional variational autoencoder (CVAE) as a data reconstructor, coupled with a multiple-optimization strategy derived from GCS mechanism analysis. Experimental results on a soil moisture content (SMC) dataset demonstrate that GCS-CVAE outperforms existing CS and deep learning methods in both accuracy and stability. Notably, it can reconstruct hourly SMC series at highly reduced sampling rates of 10% and 15%, achieving average R2 values that exceed 0.8 and 0.9, respectively. For future deployment, GCS-CVAE can be integrated with wireless sensor networks or the Internet of Things via asynchronous sampling and multi-node collaboration to alleviate temporal feature loss during sparse sampling.

title: Effects of particle-contact rheological properties on soil-tool interaction dynamics
abstract: Soil-tool interaction is a fundamental process in agricultural operations such as tillage and planting. However, existing soil-tool interaction models typically consider individual rheological elements or limited combinations, restricting the understanding of how multiple mechanisms collectively govern soil dynamic behaviour. This study presents a systematic investigation of various rheological element combinations and their influence on soil dynamic responses resulting from soil-tool interaction. Implemented within the discrete element method, soil was modelled using fundamental rheological elements: elasticity, friction, viscosity, and cohesion at particle contacts. The model was calibrated and validated against experiments involving a simple soil-engaging tool operating in sandy loam soil. Calibration of rheological parameters (normal stiffness, friction coefficient, viscous coefficient, and bond tensile strength) achieved a minimum overall relative error of 4.03% between simulated and measured macroscopic dynamic responses, including tool draft force, soil throw mass, and soil displacement. Validation across five soil cutting depths (25–125 mm) showed good agreement between simulated and measured dynamic responses, with most relative errors below 20%. Systematically combining rheological elements revealed distinct dynamic responses associated with differently combined mechanisms. Cohesive-frictional combination produced the highest draft force, whereas visco-frictional combinations minimized soil throw mass due to enhanced energy dissipation. Furthermore, parametric analysis demonstrated nonlinear relationships between rheological parameters and dynamic responses. The study provides a comprehensive approach that can potentially reduce reliance on soil-specific models and support more efficient modelling of soil-tool interactions.

title: Fatigue detection of tractor drivers based on facial occlusion restoration and temporal feature discrimination
abstract: Operating agricultural machinery while fatigued poses a significant threat to field safety. In complex farmland environments, frequent facial occlusions-caused by dust, shadows, and protective gear-often lead to missed detections and false alarms in fatigue monitoring systems. To address these challenges, we propose a novel fatigue detection framework that integrates facial occlusion restoration with spatio-temporal feature analysis, thereby overcoming the limitations of existing methods under realistic occlusion conditions. First, we constructed an enhanced occlusion detection model based on YOLOv8s. By incorporating the ShuffleNetV2 architecture into the backbone, we substantially reduced computational complexity and parameter count. Simultaneously, we embedded a Bidirectional Feature Pyramid Network (BiFPN) in the neck to enhance multi-scale feature fusion. These modifications yielded a lightweight yet powerful model well-suited for real-time detection. Subsequently, we developed an advanced facial restoration network for reconstructing occluded regions. We enhanced the CTSDG inpainting architecture by introducing a novel loss function that combines Dlib landmark-based local weighting with an LSGAN adversarial loss, enabling separate optimization of structural consistency and texture realism. Furthermore, the masks explicitly predicted by the improved YOLOv8s model guide targeted restoration of critical facial areas. This detection–restoration cascade framework exhibits strong spatial awareness and high controllability. To further improve fatigue state discrimination, we refined a spatio-temporal graph convolutional network (ST-GCN). We augmented the standard architecture by incorporating head pitch angle features and integrating Squeeze-and-Excitation (SE) attention mechanisms into the graph convolution operations. These enhancements enable the model to better capture discriminative spatio-temporal patterns associated with fatigue behaviors, such as prolonged eye closure and repeated yawning. We conducted comprehensive experiments to validate the proposed method. The optimized occlusion detection model achieved an inference time of 1.7 ms per image and reduced the parameter count by 16.2 million compared to the baseline, demonstrating high computational efficiency. The restoration network maintained high-quality reconstruction even under progressively increasing occlusion levels. The enhanced ST-GCN model achieved significant performance gains: accuracy, recall, and temporal accuracy improved by 1.36 %, 2.8 %, and 5 %, respectively, outperforming several contemporary approaches. This study provides an effective technical solution for safety monitoring in intelligent agricultural machinery and establishes a flexible framework that can be extended to other multimodal human state recognition tasks. The integration of occlusion-aware detection, semantic-guided restoration, and attention-enhanced temporal modeling offers valuable insights for future research in related domains.

title: Crab semantic segmentation method based on dual image encoders
abstract: Accurately obtaining the spatial distribution and morphological information of crabs in complex open enhanced aquaculture environment is a fundamental prerequisite for biomass monitoring and intelligent aquaculture ecological analysis. However, robust automatic recognition and segmentation remain challenging due to significant inter-individual appearance variations, complex backgrounds, underwater imaging degradation, and camouflage characteristics commonly encountered in natural environments. To address these challenges, we construct a high-quality real-world crab dataset, Crab1K, which contains 1000 images covering five coastal crab species. Based on this dataset, we propose a dual-encoder segmentation framework named DISA-Unet, specifically designed for complex Open-water environment for stock enhancement and aquaculture. The framework jointly leverages global semantic representation capability and high-resolution structural feature perception, forming a complementary semantic–structural feature fusion mechanism. An adaptor module is designed to achieve efficient knowledge embedding from SAM2 block to self-constructed dataset with minimal additional parameters, enabling better suitability for downstream segmentation tasks. Meanwhile, an Interaction module is built for DINOv3 block to enhance spatial consistency and structural representation while preserving global contextual relationships. Furthermore, Receptive Field Blocks (RFB) and a novel attention Feature-wise Linear Modulation (AT-FiLM) modules are integrated to effectively modulate and reduce high-dimensional features, providing more expressive and structured representations for subsequent feature fusion. Experimental results on the Crab1K dataset demonstrate that DISA-Unet achieves state-of-the-art performance, with scores of mIoU(0.881), Sα(0.953), Fβω(0.929), mEϕ(0.978), and MAE(0.008) across multiple evaluation metrics. In addition, cross-domain validation on four public marine organism datasets—MAS3K, RMAS, UFO120, and RUWI—further confirms the strong generalization capability of the proposed method under diverse open underwater environment. Ablation studies further verify that the dual-encoder architecture and individual modules significantly improve segmentation quality, particularly in terms of detail recovery and semantic modeling in complex environments. This work provides a novel methodological support for intelligent visual perception in agriculture and ecological monitoring applications. The source code will be made publicly available at https://github.com/Chengyilin123/DISA-Unet.

title: Design and optimization of a low-damage harvesting system for stems and leaves of leaf-vegetable sweet potato based on stem–leaf mechanical properties
abstract: To address stem entanglement, unstable feeding, and mechanical damage during the harvesting of stems and leaves of leaf-vegetable sweet potato (Ipomoea batatas L.), a self-propelled electric harvester integrating oscillating separation, reciprocating cutting, pneumatic conveying, belt conveying, and collection was developed. Based on the agronomic requirements of greenhouse-grown leaf-vegetable sweet potato, the physical and mechanical properties of stems and petioles were measured to provide input parameters for the design and optimization of key operating devices. The average densities of leaves and stems were 646.00 and 962.00 kg∙m−3, respectively. The average maximum shear force and shear stress of the stem were 7.37 N and 0.52 MPa, respectively, and the average bending, compressive, and tensile strengths were 7.20, 6.21, and 2.36 MPa, respectively. A finite element model of stem cutting and a collision model of vine separation were established to optimize the cutting and separating devices. Under the current model conditions, the optimal cutting parameters were an edge angle of 45°, a forward speed of 0.40 m∙s−1, and a cutter linear speed of 0.48 m∙s−1. For the separating device, the combination of a rotational speed of 120 r∙min−1 and an eccentricity of 80 mm yielded the highest closeness coefficient of 0.73 among the tested conditions. Experimental validation showed that the pneumatic conveying system provided stable airflow under the required operating conditions. Field experiments further showed that the prototype achieved a harvesting efficiency of 0.22 hm2∙h−1, a missing rate of 9.2%, and a damage rate of 4.5%, meeting the design requirements. The proposed method provides a reference for the development of low-damage harvesting equipment for leaf-vegetable sweet potato stems and leaves and similar flexible stem crops.

title: Supervised contrastive regression learning for predicting soluble solids content of blueberries using hyperspectral imaging
abstract: Hyperspectral imaging technology enables rapid and non-destructive assessment of fruits. However, acquiring a large-scale and well-balanced labeled dataset remains a significant challenge, primarily due to destructive reference measurements and difficulty sourcing samples that cover a wide and balanced distribution of quality attributes, which exacerbates overfitting risk when sample diversity is limited. Additionally, most deep learning methods optimize using mean squared error and regularization losses without explicitly learning feature representations relevant to regression tasks, making it difficult to learn robust, continuous feature representations. To address these challenges, we propose a spectral quantitative regression framework with supervised contrastive learning (SQR-SCL). A C-Mixup method selects sample pairs based on target-value similarity and interpolates their features and target values, enhancing sample diversity. A differential preservation and continuity feature learning (DPCFL) module learns continuous feature representations while preserving differences between samples. The DPCFL module draws samples with similar target values closer together and pushes those with differing values further apart, sorting features in the embedding space by target value. Such ordering prevents the model from making significantly different predictions for similar inputs, thereby improving prediction stability. A projection head in the DPCFL module ensures that extracted features preserve inter-sample differences and enhances their discriminative power. In this study, reflectance hyperspectral images and soluble solids content (SSC, ∘Bx) were acquired for 1010 blueberries in five sample groups. On this dataset, SQR-SCL achieved a test R2 of 0.884 and an RMSEP of 0.641(∘Bx), outperforming compared deep learning and traditional methods.

title: Fusion of multi-soil and crop parameters for map-based variable-depth seeding: A field-scale evaluation in fodder maize
abstract: Although variable-depth seeding (VDS) has the potential to improve crop growth and yield, its agronomic and economic benefits need to be evaluated in spatially heterogeneous fields using multiple soil and crop parameters. In this study, VDS was evaluated in two commercial fodder maize fields (Groot and Kleine) in Belgium using map-based VDS prescriptions implemented with an automated depth-control planter. Seeding depth prescriptions for VDS were generated using a predictive decision framework integrating proximal soil sensing and satellite-derived crop growth indicators. VDS was implemented using three depths of 35, 55, and 75 mm, and its performance was compared against a uniform-depth seeding of 55 mm (UDS55). Results showed that, in Groot, VDS increased yield relative to UDS55 by 0.45 t ha−1, with positive responses across the three depth classes. In Kleine, responses were depth-class dependent.
