Although the 35-mm and 75-mm classes outperformed UDS55, the 55-mm class exhibited a yield penalty, resulting in a mean yield decrease of 0.15 t ha−1 under VDS. Vegetation indices obtained from PlanetScope indicated improved early-season canopy vigour in VDS areas. A revenue evaluation (yield × price) showed contrasting field-level outcomes, with an area-weighted revenue difference of +56 € ha−1 in Groot and −24 € ha−1 in Kleine. The study suggests the agronomic and economic potential of VDS in fodder maize, while further validation across more fields and growing seasons is required to confirm the stability and transferability of the findings.

title: In-Season monitoring of rice phenology for massive germplasm resources using Explainable Machine learning and a Transformer CNN model
abstract: Timely, accurate, and intelligent monitoring of rice phenology is crucial for selecting germplasm resources of suitable phenology, but previous research on phenological estimation has been based primarily on a few major rice cultivars in large scale field, lacking numerous germplasm resources in small breeding plots. Consequently, we proposed an in-season phenology monitoring framework that first identifies the growth stage of each rice plot and then estimates the initiation dates of key phenological stages for massive germplasm resources. This study utilized UAV to acquire time series imagery of 3112 rice germplasm resources across eight ecological sites. The improved CNN-Vision Transformer combined model classified the phenological stages, and based on these results, vegetation indices (VIs) for different germplasm resources at various growth stages were calculated. Subsequently, a Bayesian random forest regression model estimated the initiation dates of key phenological stages, and its performance was validated using an independent dataset. Additionally, SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) analysis assessed the contributions of different VIs to phenological stages. The results demonstrated that Re-ViTAE achieved an accuracy, precision, recall, F1 score and MCC (Matthews Correlation Coefficient) values of 93.59 %, 93.03 %, 93.15 %, 93.08 % and 91.84 %, correspondingly, superior to all other eleven CNN and Vision Transformer models. RMSE of estimated initiation dates was 3.9d, 4.7d, 4.5d, and 3.7d for jointing, heading, grain-filling, and maturity, respectively, and the independent data validation accuracy was 5.6d, 5.3d, 5.8d, and 5.0d, respectively. Compared with the traditional RF model, the Bayesian-optimized RF model reduced the RMSE by 1.2 d, 1.2 d, 1.0 d, and 1.6 d, respectively. SHAP analysis revealed that different VIs contributed unequally to the estimation of key rice phenological initiation dates. Specifically, MTCI, NDVI, OSAVI, and Clgreen contributed most to the estimation of jointing, heading, grain filling, and maturity, respectively. The results of this study enable the quantitative classification for growth stages and estimation of initiation dates for massive rice germplasm resources, providing technical support for breeding scientists and companies in the selection of superior germplasms.

title: Robot-assisted Neural Radiance fields for plot-level cotton crop 3D reconstruction and yield estimation
abstract: Cotton boll counting is a critical component of yield estimation and plays a vital role in advancing plant phenomics and precision agriculture. However, the complex spatial distribution of cotton bolls and frequent occlusions in two-dimensional (2D) images pose significant challenges to accurate quantification. To address these issues, we developed a novel workflow based on Neural Radiance Fields (NeRF), which integrates high-throughput robotic image data acquisition, three-dimensional (3D) reconstruction, and cotton boll mapping at the plot level in a breeding field. A customized robotic platform equipped with ten cameras mounted around the canopy frame was used to capture overlapping red, green, and blue (RGB) images of plot-level cotton plants. NeRF was then employed to reconstruct detailed 3D models, and the reconstruction quality was evaluated. Furthermore, this study presents a comprehensive 2D-to-3D mapping approach based on an improved FruitNeRF algorithm, which effectively overcomes the challenges of 3D plot-level cotton boll annotation and limited training data. The proposed approach enables accurate quantification of cotton boll numbers and provides a reliable foundation for yield prediction. Experimental results demonstrated that the Lumix-camera configuration mounted on the robotic platform achieved the best overall reconstruction performance among the tested configurations, with a peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR) of 17.21 dB, a structural similarity index (SSIM) of 0.49, and a learned perceptual image patch similarity (LPIPS) of 0.54. This configuration was also better suited for high-throughput plot-level field phenotyping because it enabled more stable and standardized image acquisition. The reconstructed plot-level point clouds retained sufficient structural information for downstream cotton boll segmentation, counting, and yield estimation. In the exported plot-level point clouds, both cotton bolls and branches are clearly distinguishable. Based on Lumix data, the mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) for cotton boll number and boll weight prediction was 5.43% and 8.78%, respectively. Overall, this approach enables high-throughput phenotyping and the generation of plot-level cotton point clouds suitable for downstream boll counting and yield estimation, providing a valuable framework for plot-level cotton phenotyping and precision management for low-density, post-defoliated plots under the experimental conditions evaluated in this study.

title: A computer vision driven ecosystem for cattle monitoring: Multi-disease classification with severity grading, multi-view individual identification, and weight estimation
abstract: This study introduces a computer vision based cattle monitoring ecosystem, which (i) performs multi-disease classification and severity grading with 85.88% hierarchical accuracy, (ii) achieves multi-view cattle identification with 89.80% Rank-5 accuracy under cross-view-angle and domain shift conditions, and (iii) estimates body weight from four view RGB images and metadata with an MAE of 35.10 kg, developed using custom-collected, curated datasets combined with publicly available datasets. For the disease module, a hierarchical cross-attentional multi-task architecture classifies Lumpy Skin Disease (LSD), Foot-and-Mouth Disease (FMD), Infectious Bovine Keratoconjunctivitis (IBK), and Healthy cattle, while grading diseased cases into Stage-1 (mild), Stage-2 (moderate), and Stage-3 (severe) using clinically graded veterinarian supervised annotations, achieving 89.96% disease classification accuracy, 83.75% severity staging accuracy, and 85.88% hierarchical accuracy (disease → severity). On a custom collected dataset, YOLOv8s localizes cattle from left, right, front, and back views with an IoU of 0.93 and mAP@0.5 of 0.97, providing the basis for identification and weight estimation. Multi-view individual cattle identification achieves Rank-1 accuracies of 96.40% (Rank-5: 100%) under Leave-One-View-Out evaluation and 74.56% (Rank-5: 89.80%) under cross-view-angle and domain-shift testing using ConvNeXt-Tiny. In weight estimation module, ensemble learning over multi-view images and metadata achieves an MAE of 35.10 kg. Overall, the results demonstrate the potential of an affordable, low-shot, non-invasive RGB-based system for disease diagnosis with severity grading, multi-view cattle identification, and practical live-weight estimation without invasive sensors.

title: Optimization of efficiency and stability in a front-axle direct torque-coupled hybrid tractor during plowing via regenerative braking: a coordinated multilayer control strategy
abstract: Tractors plow energy efficiency and stability jointly determine economic performance and operational quality. In this paper, the previously proposed front-axle direct torque-coupled hybrid tractor powertrain (FADTC-HTP) is adopted. Mathematical and simulation models oriented to plowing scenario are then developed for this architecture. Based on these models, an efficiency-stability coordinated multilayer control strategy (ES-CMCS) is proposed to enhance longitudinal speed stability, lateral deviation stability, and energy efficiency during plowing. In the ES-CMCS, the FADTC-HTP is formulated as a linear state-space model with time-varying disturbance inputs. Based on this model, a linear time-varying model predictive control (LTV-MPC) strategy is employed to regulate the engine, front-axle torque-coupled motors, and eLSD clutch pressure, with the objective of improving tire-soil interaction efficiency and speed stability. The LTV-MPC is supported by a self-learning hidden Markov model-based predictor that provides tire longitudinal and tractive force predictions over a 0.5 s horizon to ensure reliable solutions of the time-varying parameter model. Meanwhile, a nonlinear MPC (NMPC) is adopted to enhance tractor lateral stability by regulating the front-wheel steering angle using the LTV-MPC outputs together with real-time tractor dynamic parameters. To compensate for the inability of MPC to explicitly exploit engine and motor efficiency maps as prior knowledge, a deep reinforcement learning-based action compensator is introduced to further optimize control commands. Finally, the proposed hybrid tractor powertrain system and control strategy is evaluated on a controller-hardware-in-the-loop (CHIL) test bench. The results indicate that, compared with a steer-only control strategy, the equivalent fuel consumption rate is reduced by 7.11 %, the standard deviation of lateral path deviation decreases by 28.70 %, and the RMSE of longitudinal speed tracking is lowered by 65.88 %. Relative to other baseline multi-objective control methods, operational stability and energy efficiency are also improved markedly. Another noteworthy finding is that, under the proposed FADTC-HTP configuration, operating the front-axle electric machines in regenerative braking mode during plowing effectively constrains tire slip, enhances tire-soil interaction efficiency, and positively affects diesel engine fuel economy. This study offers an alternative perspective for the structural design and model-data hybrid driven control strategy development of hybrid tractors.

title: An adaptive multi-stage hybrid ensemble with iterative feature optimization for oil palm seed system analytics
abstract: Oil palm seed systems involve sequential dependencies from upstream fertilization and productivity to germination quality and downstream distribution market outcomes, yet these stages are commonly analysed as isolated prediction tasks. This study proposes an adaptive multi-stage hybrid ensemble framework with iterative feature optimization for integrated oil palm seed system analytics. The framework is built from heterogeneous real-world data covering fertilization, production, germination, certified seed distribution, producer sales, and market share. These data are structured into three connected analytical stages: seed productivity, germination quality, and downstream distribution market analytics. At each stage, engineered features are refined through iterative feature optimization and modelled using a hybrid ensemble of Random Forest, XGBoost, LightGBM, and CatBoost, followed by adaptive weighting and stacking. The resulting predictions are then propagated across stages, allowing upstream productivity signals to inform germination modelling and both productivity and germination signals to inform downstream analytics. The results show that the oil palm seed system is more effectively represented as a connected multi-stage predictive structure than as separate stage-specific models. Ablation analysis further identifies iterative feature optimization and cross-stage propagation as the most influential components, particularly for downstream prediction.

title: Evaluation of relative grazing intensity based on UAV aerial photography and trajectory tracking technology—a case study of a desert steppe household pasture
abstract: Non-uniform livestock utilization in household pastures is important for understanding grassland growth status and grassland utilization management. However, traditional relative grazing intensity (RGI) evaluation methods are often labor-intensive and limited in their ability to capture fine-scale spatial patterns of livestock utilization, which constrains the characterization of spatiotemporal variation in grassland use. In this study, a desert steppe household pasture in Inner Mongolia, China, was selected as an exploratory integrated framework to analyze cattle herd movement regularities and estimate RGI variation based on unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) photography and trajectory tracking technology. Results showed that: (1) The results from observing trajectory points revealed that cattle herds’ activity within the household pasture is non-uniform. Specifically, the density of trajectory points in densely populated areas is 16 times greater than that in sparsely populated areas; (2) UAV survey not only has high accuracy in cattle population observation (with R 2 and RMSE of 0.83 and 22.56 sheep unit /ha respectively, compared to ground-based observation), but also reflects the spatial activity regularities of the herd. The distribution area of the cattle herd shows a trend of first increasing and then decreasing as the distance to the livestock enclosure increases (P < 0.001); (3) Compared with the traditional method, which divides the livestock population by the area, the spatial and temporal distribution of RGI based on UAV photography and trajectory points shows high consistency (with R 2 ranging from 0.927 to 0.984, compared to ground-based observation), and it can describe the heterogeneity of RGI in more detail; (4) From May to July, the cumulative RGI in pasture showed a trend of gradually decreasing from the northwest and northeast to central area. Our results indicated that, compared with traditional field-based monitoring approaches, the method based on UAV aerial photography and trajectory tracking technology at the pasture scale was less labor-intensive and more time-efficient, while enabling a more detailed characterization of the heterogeneity in RGI caused by non-uniform livestock utilization. As an exploratory case study, this framework shows potential for improving the assessment of spatial heterogeneity associated with non-uniform livestock utilization.

title: Deep learning-based keypoint detection for 3D biometric measurement of tuna using underwater stereo vision
abstract: Accurate and scalable estimation of tuna size during transfer and farming operations is essential for stock assessment and management. This study presents a fully automatic processing pipeline that combines deep learning-based keypoint detection with stereoscopic vision geometry to estimate fish length, height, and width from underwater stereoscopic imagery. The system exploits videos acquired while freely swimming fish under real underwater conditions from two different viewpoints: a lateral view, from which length and height are measured, and a ventral view, which provides length and width. Having measurements of individual fish in all three dimensions can significantly improve the accuracy of estimating biomass and schools for large-bodied species. For each view, a Keypoint R-CNN model was trained on heterogeneous datasets of 850 stereo pairs annotated independently by three human operators. To account for annotation variability, per-keypoint normalization constants were computed and used to adapt COCO-style Object Keypoint Similarity (OKS) metrics to this domain. The proposed Keypoint R-CNN system achieved 2D keypoint localization accuracy comparable to human annotators (mean OKS = 0.91). The resulting 3D biometric measurements yielded relative errors of approximately 1%–2% for length-related dimensions and 2%–5% for height and width, within the range observed for inter-annotator variability. Measurement bias remained below 0.2% for all evaluated dimensions, and no systematic over- or under-estimation trends were observed. Automatic and manual size distributions were statistically indistinguishable, while processing throughput was compatible with offline operational analysis requirements. Overall, the proposed approach provides a reliable and scalable foundation for automated 3D size monitoring in tuna aquaculture.

title: TP-Duck: A cage-reared duck behavior recognition model with lightweight interaction mechanism and text prompts
abstract: Accurate and automated behavior recognition is critical for welfare assessment and production management in intensive duck farming. However, cage-reared duck behavior recognition remains challenging due to the high visual similarity among behaviors and the tendency for subtle discriminative motion cues to be misinterpreted by the duck’s dominant body appearance under cage interference. To address these challenges, this study proposes a lightweight vision–language model with partial-star operation and text prompts for cage-reared duck behavior recognition (TP-Duck). Specifically, a Lightweight Partial-Star Operation Block (LPS) is designed to efficiently capture fine-grained discriminative features through partial convolution for channel-sparse computation and star operation for high-dimensional non-linear feature excitation. Building upon LPS, a Text-Prompted LPS Block (TP-LPS) is further developed to leverage pre-trained vision–language embeddings for cross-modal feature modulation, thereby enhancing the model’s capacity to disambiguate behaviors with similar postures in complex cage environments. Extensive experiments were conducted on a self-built cage-reared duck behavior dataset. TP-Duck achieves an F1 score of 89.4%, surpassing the baseline YOLOv11s and state-of-the-art YOLO26s by 2.2 and 5.0 percentage points, respectively, while reducing parameters by 0.64 M and 1.18 M. The results demonstrate that the proposed model achieves superior recognition accuracy with reduced model complexity, providing an effective solution for automated duck behavior monitoring in intensive farming systems.

title: PA-SWE: a posture-aware sow weight estimation framework via skeleton-calibrated multimodal fusion
abstract: Accurate body weight monitoring of gestating sows is critical for precision feeding and reproductive performance optimization. While deep learning has shown promise in image-based weight estimation, existing RGB-based methods are sensitive to posture variation, and depth-based alternatives incur higher deployment costs and environmental constraints. This study introduces Posture-Aware Sow Weight Estimation (PA-SWE), a posture‑aware RGB–skeletal framework that uses posture as an auxiliary source of structural information rather than treating it as nuisance variation. The framework comprises an upstream module that simultaneously outputs instance segmentation masks and anatomical keypoints from the top‑view RGB images, and a downstream module that fuses RGB appearance features with a skeletal graph via compact bilinear pooling to jointly predict body weight and posture. Evaluation on a commercial farm dataset containing 48 gestating sows of a single breed follows an event‑level protocol: image‑level predictions within each weighing event are aggregated using the median to produce the final event-level estimate. PA‑SWE achieves an event‑level mean absolute error of 2.814 kg, a root mean square error of 3.513 kg, and an R2 of 0.975, together with a macro‑averaged F1‑score of 92.89% for three‑class posture classification. Pig‑level statistical analyses further showed that the error reduction relative to RGB‑only baselines is significant and consistent across individuals. These results suggest that explicit integration of skeletal cues can reduce posture‑related estimation errors and improve event‑level weight estimation in the current farm‑specific setting. The proposed framework therefore offers a practical option for contactless monitoring of gestating sows without requiring strict standing-posture standardization under crate-based monitoring conditions.

title: Soybean leaf physicochemical parameter inversion based on radiative transfer model screening constraints and measured-noise enhancement
abstract: Accurate monitoring of soybean leaf physicochemical parameters (e.g., chlorophyll, dry matter, and equivalent water content) is of great significance for evaluating crop growth status and guiding field management. Although the physics-driven radiative transfer model (PROSPECT) can quantitatively analyze the response mechanisms between leaf optical properties and physicochemical components, its inversion process is frequently constrained by the “ill-posed problem” inherent in hyperspectral inversion and the distribution discrepancy between simulated data and real-world environments. To systematically address these challenges, this study proposes a synergistic inversion framework integrating a spectral-parameter dual screening strategy with noise enhancement. First, targeting the initial look-up table (LUT) constructed based on the PROSPECT-5B model, a dual screening strategy based on spectral similarity and parameter consistency was developed. By employing dual constraints on spectral morphology and physicochemical parameters to eliminate redundant and pseudo-parameter combinations, an improved LUT with enhanced physical consistency was constructed. Building upon this, a measured-data-based noise enhancement strategy was designed. Guided by field-measured data as prior knowledge, an enhanced hybrid dataset was generated, encompassing both physical mechanistic integrity and real-world field distribution characteristics. Subsequently, the successive projections algorithm (SPA) was utilized to select characteristic wavebands, and three inversion models — Extreme Learning Machine (ELM), Random Forest (RF), and eXtreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) — were trained based on the enhanced dataset. Experimental results demonstrated that the enhanced dataset effectively mitigated the simulation bias of the physical model and the overfitting problem associated with localized data. Among the three algorithms, the ELM model exhibited the optimal performance. Notably, for Cm, which exhibits weak signal characteristics, the model achieved a coefficient of determination R2 of 0.987 on the validation set, with a root mean square error (RMSE) as low as 0.0003 g/cm2. Overall, compared to inversions relying solely on the traditional empirical dataset, the proposed model reduced the average RMSE for the inversion of four physicochemical parameters by 18%–25%. By incorporating prior knowledge from measured datasets, this study significantly enhances the spatial generalization capability of the physical model in complex field environments, providing a robust data foundation and solution for the precise inversion of multiple soybean leaf parameters.

title: Optimized design of a hanging-cup planting principle based on pineapple seedlings and spatio-temporal analysis and experimental study of seedling-machine-soil coupled interaction
abstract: To address the scarcity of mechanized transplanting equipment and poor planting quality for pineapples in China, in this paper, we take "Bali" pineapple seedlings as the research object to conduct an optimized design of a hanging-cup planting principle and a study on the "seedling-machine-soil" coupled interaction mechanism. First, through multi-scale seedling dropping experiments, the optimal caliber for the square seedling cup was determined to be 130mm. Based on the principle of a parallel four-bar mechanism, a kinematic model of the planting mechanism was constructed, and a human-computer interactive parameter design platform was developed to optimize key linkage parameters. The optimal spatio-temporal parameters for the duckbill device were innovatively determined (critical opening angle γ=60°, delayed closing angle Δγ=50°, and maximum opening width W=100 mm). Furthermore, a "seedling-machine-soil" bidirectional coupled simulation model, integrating a flexible body seedling model, multi-body dynamics rigid components, and discrete element-based soil particles, was constructed. This model revealed the spatio-temporal interaction mechanism among the duckbill device's motion trajectory, the seedling's release posture, and soil disturbance during the planting process. The simulation results showed that the optimized planting mechanism could achieve a qualified planting rate of 95.2%. Through indoor soil bin tests and field validation trials, the reliability of the simulation model was systematically verified. The field trial results indicated that at an operating speed of 0.66 km/h, the qualified planting rate reached 90.2%, the miss-planting and lodging rates were 5.1% and 4.7%, respectively, and the coefficient of variation for plant spacing was 4.6%. All indicators were significantly better than the preset standards. This study establishes a systematic research and development methodology for pineapple transplanters, encompassing mechanism revelation, parameter optimization, and multi-environment validation, which can provide a theoretical basis and technical support for the development of high-efficiency transplanting equipment for specialty crops.

title: WheatSim: A process-based wheat model linking organ development, plant architecture, and field-scale responses under environmental variability
abstract: Wheat ( Triticum aestivum L.) underpins global food security, yet process-based simulations of wheat growth remain challenging under variable weather and management conditions. Traditional crop growth models (CGMs) mainly aim to reproduce field-scale outcomes but often simplify organ growth dynamics and plant architecture, whereas functional-structural plant models (FSPMs) represent detailed organ-level growth but are typically confined to single stems and vegetative stages. Explicit plant architecture can integrate organ-specific details from FSPMs into the production-oriented framework of CGMs, thereby establishing a computational pathway that links organ-level responses to plant architecture and field-scale functioning. In this study, we developed WheatSim, a new process-based framework that explicitly integrates organ-level morphology and physiology, plant-level architecture, and field-level production. In WheatSim, organs are encapsulated as self-contained modules with organ-specific models for emergence, growth, and senescence, while multiple organs are organized and coordinated through a tiller hierarchy that defines a botanically realistic plant architecture. A representative plant approach is established alongside the hierarchical tillers to provide a simplified averaging bridge from organ-level simulation to field-scale outcomes. WheatSim couples biochemical photosynthesis and stomatal regulation to simulate carbon assimilation and transpiration, and exchanges state variables with external soil and climate modules for interoperable simulations. Across APSIM NextGen field experiments spanning diverse environments, management practices, and stress regimes, WheatSim showed good agreement with observations for both morphological properties (leaf number, tiller population, and leaf area index) and biomass-related properties (aboveground and grain biomass and nitrogen mass), with relative mean absolute errors typically ranging from 0.1 to 0.3. Temporal trends were also reasonably reproduced, as indicated by linear regression slopes between simulated and observed values that were generally close to 1. The combination of explicit plant architecture and organ-specific models also provides a useful basis for interpreting integrated crop responses to interacting environmental drivers in selected field sites. WheatSim therefore provides an effective computational framework to simulate wheat growth across organ, plant, and field levels, and may also inform future development of process-based models for other cereal crops.

title: In-situ monitoring of photosynthesis information in plant leaves using flexible wearable impedance spectroscopy
abstract: In-situ monitoring of photosynthesis-related physiological activity can provide direct data support for tracking changes in plant demand, evaluating plant health status, and analyzing whether plants are under stress. For this reason, we propose a method that uses flexible wearable Electrochemical Impedance Spectroscopy (EIS) to estimate the net photosynthetic rate (Pn) of plant leaves in situ. Firstly, an enhanced photosynthetic rate leads to an increase in intracellular ion concentration, resulting in a decrease in leaf electrical impedance. Therefore, a flexible electrode is attached to the abaxial leaf surface to detect these changes. Secondly, to eliminate systematic errors, the impedance of a dark-adapted plant is used as an “anchor point”. The normalized “impedance change rate (α)” is the core feature parameter. Lastly, a Tabular Prior-Data Fitting Network (TabPFN) was used to establish a detection model. The experimental results show that the optimal sensing frequency was identified at 3700 Hz. At this frequency, the impedance change rate reached a peak of 24.6%, ensuring maximum sensitivity to light-driven physiological activity. The TabPFN model achieved excellent performance (R2 = 0.9872, RMSE = 0.1196). In continuous the continuous monitoring of day-long dynamic validation experiments, the system accurately tracked real-time changes in net photosynthetic rate measured by a commercial gas-exchange instrument. The model’s predictions matched actual measurements almost perfectly (R2 = 0.9776, RMSE = 0.1357). Single-frequency impedance sampling requires only 10 s per data point. Furthermore, this study provides a method for continuous, non-destructive estimation of plant photosynthetic rates from leaf electrical impedance under controlled environmental conditions.

title: Machine learning–based decision support for harvest optimization in commercial microalgae photobioreactors: A field validation study
abstract: Operational decision-making in commercial microalgae cultivation remains largely heuristic despite the increasing availability of high-frequency farm data. In photobioreactor-based production systems, harvest fraction selection is a key management decision that affects short-term biomass recovery, culture stability, and overall production efficiency. This study presents a machine learning–based decision-support framework for optimizing harvest management in commercial tubular photobioreactors cultivating Nannochloropsis sp. The framework integrates three years of heterogeneous farm data, including operational logs, meteorological variables, and FlowCam (a digital imaging system used to measure microalgae concentration and cell morphology) data. A supervised regression approach was used to predict next-day post-harvest cell concentration, and several learning algorithms were evaluated. A Random Forest model achieved the best predictive performance (R2 = 0.705), demonstrating robust prediction under noisy commercial production conditions. The trained model was implemented in an inference module that evaluates candidate harvest fractions and recommends the fraction expected to maximize short-term biomass recovery. The system was validated in a four-week farm-scale experiment across 12 commercial photobioreactors (96 planned harvest events), comparing model-guided and operator-guided harvest decisions. While the machine learning–guided strategy achieved comparable productivity levels to expert human decision-making, it reduced variability. These results provide a successful proof-of-concept for the operational feasibility of a data-driven framework to stabilize and scale commercial microalgae management. These findings demonstrate the practical feasibility of integrating machine learning into daily farm operations as a hybrid human–AI decision-support layer. The proposed framework highlights the potential of data-driven decision systems to enhance stability and scalability in commercial microalgae photobioreactor production.

title: A full-scale climate model of the Chinese solar greenhouse
abstract: Greenhouse climate models serve as a basis for optimal management of greenhouse climate. However, a thoroughly tested mechanistic model of the Chinese solar greenhouse (CSG) climate that integratively simulates shortwave radiation, air temperature, humidity, and CO2 concentration is still lacking. This study developed such a full-scale CSG climate model for the standard CSG that describes the effects of outdoor weather, greenhouse structure, crop states, and greenhouse controls on the indoor climates. The model is structured into eleven submodules, incorporating new insights and expanded descriptions, such as the switch of condensation to deposition on the south roof, and shading effects of the north roof on the north wall. It depicts crop activities specifically targeting lettuce, and has been validated in CSG lettuce production scenarios involving two greenhouse structures and across both warm and cold seasons. The model demonstrated acceptable performance. Simulated CSG climates closely mirrored the measurements throughout the crop growth cycles, with the RRMSE being 12.6–23.0 % for shortwave radiation, 14.5–21.1 % for air temperature, 17.7–30.8 % for relative humidity, and 3.0–12.4 % for CO2 concentration predictions. Contributions of energy, water vapour, and CO2 fluxes to indoor climates were further explored. Additionally, layering was found necessary to describe temperature dynamics of the north wall and indoor soil with heat storage capacities. Ice layer formation and seasonal shading variations indicated that incorporating related processes could improve model completeness. The developed model can be used for model-based CSG climate control considering its acceptable accuracy, high computational efficiency, and robust generalisation.

title: A machine-vision based seedling replenishing system for pepper plug seedling transplanter
abstract: To address the issues of high seedling deficiency rates of existing fully automatic transplanters, a seedling replenishing system based on visual detection technology was designed, and a compact intelligent transplanter was developed that combines a high-speed pneumatic seedling picking and depositing device with an electrically driven seedling conveying device. The seedling conveying mechanism employed two sets of seedling cups driven by dual motors arranged coaxially, enabling coordinated operations where one set received seedlings while the other performed orderly seedling dropping and variable-speed seedling replenishment. A lightweight YOLOv8n model was utilized to construct an empty seedling cup identification system, significantly enhancing real-time detection performance while maintaining identification accuracy. The control system integrated a programmable logic controller (PLC), industrial cameras, and RK3566 embedded equipment, completing circuit design and variable-speed seedling replenishment program development. Bench test results showed that at transplanting frequencies of 80, 100, and 120 plants/min, the success rate of empty seedling cup identification approached 100 %, with seedling replenishing success rates of 100 %, 100 %, and 93.33 %, respectively. After activation of the seedling replenishing system, the number of empty seedling holes significantly decreased. Field tests indicated that at the same planting frequency, the planting success rates without activating the seedling replenishing system were 93.33 %, 90 %, and 87.50 %, respectively, which increased to 98.33 %, 96.67 %, and 94.17 % after activation, representing an average increase of approximately 6.11 %. The study enabled precise reseeding during high-speed transplanting by integrating an electric variable-speed conveyor and visual recognition technology, boosting planting success rates significantly.

title: MSSVT: Multi-branch spatial-spectral volumetric transformer for rice lodging segmentation with UAV multimodal fusion
abstract: Deep learning-based fine-grained segmentation of typhoon-induced rice lodging provides important support for high-precision disaster assessment using unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) remote sensing. However, many existing unimodal, flat multimodal, or generic cross-modal segmentation methods process heterogeneous UAV-derived features without explicitly preserving the semantic relationships among feature groups, which may limit modality-specific representation and spatial-spectral interaction. To address this challenge, this study investigates structured UAV multimodal fusion by organizing RGB physical features and multispectral physiological signatures into a semantically grouped volumetric representation. A Multi-branch Spatial-Spectral Volumetric Transformer (MSSVT) is proposed for fine-grained rice lodging segmentation. MSSVT uses a Hybrid Volumetric-Planar Backbone (HVPB), in which the Volumetric Spatial-Spectral Backbone (VSSB) models inter-group spatial-spectral dependencies, while the Planar Spectral Backbones (PSB) preserve fine-grained intra-group attributes. Within VSSB, the Volumetric Hybrid Attention (VHA) module combines dynamic sparse routing and selective scanning to capture salient lodging regions and refine boundary details. A progressive feature fusion mechanism is further used to integrate band-compressed, adaptively modulated, and multimodal aggregated features. To support this study, a multimodal Volumetric Rice Lodging (VRL) dataset was constructed for the investigated typhoon-induced lodging area. The dataset organizes 55 heterogeneous channels spanning RGB, color, texture, structure, multispectral, and vegetation-index features into a structured volumetric representation. Extensive experiments on the VRL dataset demonstrate that MSSVT achieves 90.72 % mIoU, representing a 1.31 % improvement over the strongest competing method. The proposed model obtains class-wise IoU values of 97.59 %, 78.10 %, and 91.02 % for normal rice, mild lodging rice, and severe lodging rice, respectively, with the largest gain observed for mild lodging rice (+5.16 %). These results indicate the potential of structured UAV multimodal fusion for fine-grained rice lodging segmentation under the investigated typhoon-induced field scenario. Code is available at: https://github.com/AG-WDS/MSSVT.

title: Geometrically consistent ordinal mixture-of-experts for weight estimation of sows from multi-view point clouds
abstract: Accurate liveweight estimation of sows is challenging due to significant morphological changes and unconstrained postures across a broad weight range. Conventional 2D imaging and standard regression models are limited in capturing these complex geometric deformations. To address this, this study proposes a Geometrically Consistent Ordinal Mixture-of-Experts (GcoMoE) framework utilizing multi-view 3D point clouds to explicitly decouple postural deformations and decompose the complex shape-weight mapping into localized sub-tasks. First, to eliminate geometric distortions induced by head or limb movements, we introduce Slice-Adaptive Geometric Encoding (SAGE), which reliably isolates the rigid torso to extract posture-invariant physical descriptors. These descriptors are subsequently integrated with global point cloud features via a Dual-Pathway Differential Fusion (DPDF) strategy, explicitly preserving absolute volumetric scales. Furthermore, to reflect the morphological continuity across the weight distribution, we replace artificial, rigid classification boundaries with a Smooth Gaussian Ordinal Labeling (SGOL) mechanism. This soft-labeling approach enables the gating network to dynamically route samples to specialized local experts under a three-phase optimization paradigm. Evaluated on a custom-built multi-view 3D dataset acquired in a commercial farm setting, our proposed GcoMoE achieves an MAE of 5.55 ± 0.49 kg, MAPE of 2.72 ± 0.22% and R2 of 0.80 ± 0.04. Furthermore, an independent external validation on a separate commercial farm demonstrated strong zero-shot generalization, with an MAE of 4.90 ± 0.11 kg, MAPE of 2.31 ± 0.06%, and an R2 of 0.70 ± 0.01. The results demonstrate that combining multi-view geometric correction with ordinal expert decomposition offers a robust and practical solution for unconstrained sow monitoring. Our code can be found at: https://github.com/xmcvcodes-260616-vision/GcoMoE.

title: SDrAwberry: Scale-referenced Depth-Anything-3 long-sequence reconstruction for Strawberry canopy volume estimation
abstract: Canopy volume is a key structural trait for crop monitoring and phenotyping platforms, but reliable plant-level canopy volume estimation in commercial strawberry fields remains challenging due to repetitive canopy structure, limited texture on bed surfaces, and the need to process long, nearly linear image sequences without loop closure. This paper presents SDrAwberry, a scale-referenced long-sequence 3D reconstruction and plant-level canopy volume estimation pipeline using synchronized tri-view RGB images collected by a ground robot across eight strawberry plant beds on one representative field acquisition date. The proposed pipeline enables a memory-efficient processing of long sequence data by partitioning the data into overlapping batches, fusing the partitioned batches into a global reconstruction in the form of point cloud, and estimating plant canopy volume by segmenting individual plants, mesh reconstruction, and scale calibration with reference boxes. The pipeline was validated by comparing the number of segmented plants and manual plant counts, and by evaluating metric scale recovery with reference-box volume self-validation. The instance extraction stage showed strong agreement with manual plant counts, with a mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) of 5.36 %. Reference-box self-validation also indicated consistent metric scale recovery, with an MAPE of 3.95 %. Direct plant-level canopy-volume ground truth was not available, so plant-volume outputs were interpreted as scale-referenced reconstructed traits rather than direct volume-accuracy validation. These results indicate that feed-forward multi-view geometry transformers can be extended to field-scale, metrically meaningful phenotyping via batching-and-fusion and scale-referenced volumetric reconstruction. Code and data are available at: https://github.com/Sycamorers/SDrAwberry.

title: Forecasting adult emergence dynamics of wood-boring pests using time-series X-ray imaging and deep learning
abstract: Forecasting adult emergence dynamics of wood-boring pests is critical for improving monitoring efficiency and optimizing control timing. However, because these insects remain concealed within tree trunks before emergence, conventional approaches cannot exploit empirically observed developmental dynamics, limiting both forecast reliability and temporal resolution. To address this, we developed a field-deployable, non-destructive forecasting framework that integrates portable X-ray radiography, deep learning-based life-stage discrimination, and developmental-lag mapping to predict adult emergence dynamics from concealed development. We acquired X-ray images of wood-boring pests inside infested logs and developed X-BorerStageNet, a lightweight two-class life-stage detector (larva vs. pupa-adult). X-BorerStageNet introduces two task-specific networks—a structure-preserving backbone, the Efficient Dual-Stream Fusion Network (EDSFNet), and a frequency-aware multi-scale encoder, the Spectral-Attentive Multi-Scale Fusion Network (SAMFNet)—comprising five novel modules in total. Within EDSFNet, the Anisotropic Pseudo-Shift Downsampling Module (APSDM) preserves directional structural cues during early downsampling, and the Dual-Stream Hierarchical Ghost Block (DSHGB) reduces redundancy via complementary parallel branches that jointly capture fine details and coarser context. Within SAMFNet, the Spectral-Enhanced MetaFormer Block (SEMFB) couples global attention with FFT-based spectral modulation to enhance pest contours while suppressing repetitive wood textures; the Progressive Hybrid Aggregation Module (PHAM) strengthens cross-scale integration through an anchor–refinement design; and Tri-Scale Focused Fusion (TSFF) fuses three adjacent feature scales to balance fine details with semantic context. The model achieves 66.3% AP50:95 and 92.8% AP50, exceeding the D-FINE-N baseline by 6.9 and 4.2 percentage points, respectively, with fewer parameters and fast inference. Applied to time-series X-ray monitoring of 9 infested logs, the framework recovered the pupation dynamics of 72 Anoplophora glabripennis individuals and translated them into emergence forecasts using a mean pupation-to-emergence interval of approximately 20 days. Predicted emergence dynamics closely matched observations at both 3-day (r = 0.913, WAPE = 0.278) and weekly (r = 0.972, WAPE = 0.167) scales, and accurately recovered key phenological landmarks, including emergence onset, peak timing, and the 10%, 50%, and 90% cumulative-emergence dates. This framework offers an effective and interpretable approach for forecasting wood-boring pest emergence dynamics, supporting early warning and timely control. Source code: https://github.com/bihaojie/X-BorerStageNet.

title: SRSE-Fusion: A self-adaptive robot state estimation framework via multimodal perception
abstract: Reliable robot state estimation leveraging the complementary characteristics of multi-sensor data is essential for the autonomy of agricultural robots. However, inherent perceptual discrepancies, scene dependencies, and range limitations of heterogeneous sensors often degrade the accuracy and stability of multi-modal fusion in complex environments. This paper proposes SRSE-Fusion, a self-adaptive robot state estimator that integrates IMU, cameras, LiDAR, and GNSS data within a unified factor graph optimization framework. To enhance fusion reliability, we develop a hybrid coupling architecture that synergizes the benefits of both loose and tight coupling. Furthermore, a dynamic performance evaluation strategy is introduced based on odometry uncertainty analysis, enabling the system to assess sensor status in real-time and adaptively adjust sensor confidence weights during the optimization. Experimental results on public datasets and field tests in orchards demonstrate that the proposed method significantly improves localization robustness. The system achieves a root mean square error below 0.867 m and a mean error below 0.731 m, effectively overcoming the challenges of sensor uncertainty and environmental variability in precision agriculture applications.

title: MaizeStereo: 2D Gaussian splatting-driven stereo foundation model for in-field proximal 3D maize phenotyping
abstract: Three-dimensional (3D) maize phenotyping is instrumental in capturing the spatial structural features essential for crop breeding and guiding agricultural practices. Among existing 3D sensing technologies, stereo vision has achieved remarkable progress in reconciling cost‑effectiveness, environmental robustness, and operational efficiency, owing to its inherent advantages as a passive sensing modality. However, its limited precision collectively impedes the broader application for organ-level phenotyping. Building on advancements in stereo vision propelled by supervised stereo matching paradigms and large-scale foundation models, this study proposes a 2D Gaussian Splatting (2DGS)-driven stereo foundation model approach for in-field proximal 3D maize phenotyping (MaizeStereo), which capitalizes on the intrinsic generalization potential of stereo foundation models while enhancing the adaptability to field proximal sensing via domain-specific optimization. Field experiments were conducted using a custom binocular image acquisition system on 50 maize plants across five growth stages (V3, V5, V7, V12, R3). The proposed MaizeStereo framework addresses real-field scenarios by synthesizing a high-fidelity stereo matching dataset through an advanced multi-view 2DGS reconstruction method. Leveraging the dataset for supervision, an optimal module-freezing strategy is developed to fine-tune the stereo foundation model for domain-specific performance enhancement. Based on the resulting disparity predictions, the framework further implements organ-level phenotypic trait extraction. Evaluated results showed that the fine-tuned foundation model outperformed benchmark methods in stereo matching with a global end-point error (EPE) of 1.846 pixels and a D1 error of 6.806%, achieving only a marginal 5.55% EPE increase compared to full fine-tuning while reducing trainable parameters by 45.7%. For phenotypic trait extraction, the pipeline delivered high accuracy with mean absolute percentage errors (MAPE) of 3.822% for plant height, 3.432% for stem diameter, and 7.741% for leaf area. The corresponding coefficient of determination (R2) values were 0.994, 0.952, and 0.986 respectively. These results demonstrate that the proposed method enables efficient and precise maize phenotyping in complex field conditions, providing a valuable tool for crop breeding and agricultural research.

title: Optimization control of motor torque for a hybrid electric tractor under plowing conditions based on DP-MPC
abstract: Aiming at the problems of insufficient power control accuracy, poor stability of the electric drive system, low traction efficiency, and unsatisfactory energy economy in hybrid electric tractors during field operations, this paper proposes a DP-MPC multi-objective cooperative optimization control strategy that integrates improved Dynamic Programming (DP) and Model Predictive Control (MPC). Targeting an Output-Split Electrically Continuous Variable Transmission (OS-ECVT) configuration hybrid tractor, multiple subsystem models were established to construct a hierarchical control architecture. This architecture features DP-based multi-objective global optimization at the upper layer and improved MPC for torque tracking at the lower layer. The DP algorithm takes motor torque tracking error, average current fluctuation, wheel slip control error, and motor operating efficiency as comprehensive optimization objectives. For comparison, a rule-based MPC strategy, which combines upper-layer rule-based control with lower-layer MPC, is also established. Simulation and bench test results show that, compared with the Rule-MPC strategy, the proposed DP-MPC strategy reduces the average motor torque tracking error by 37% and 34.3%, decreases the average current fluctuation by 24.2% and 23.5%, lowers the wheel slip control error by 16.6% and 13.1%, and improves the average operating efficiency by 0.11 and 0.18 percentage points, respectively. The comprehensive evaluation scores are increased by 5.7 and 4.9 points, respectively. Bench test results verify the effectiveness of the DP-MPC hierarchical control strategy. This study demonstrates that the proposed DP-MPC strategy can effectively balance the dynamic control performance of the drive motor with global energy efficiency optimization under plowing operations, providing a theoretical basis and technical pathway for the control design and energy efficiency improvement of high-horsepower hybrid tractor powertrains.

title: Toward optimal sampling rate selection and unbiased classification for precise activity recognition of farm quadruped animals
abstract: With the rapid advancements in deep learning techniques, wearable sensor-aided animal activity recognition (AAR) has demonstrated promising performance, thereby improving livestock management efficiency as well as animal health and welfare monitoring. However, existing research often prioritizes overall performance, overlooking the fact that classification accuracies for specific animal behavioral categories may remain unsatisfactory. This issue typically stems from suboptimal sampling rates or class imbalance problems. To address these challenges and achieve high classification accuracy across all individual behaviors in farm quadruped animals, we propose a novel Individual-Behavior-Aware Network (IBA-Net). This network enhances the recognition of each specific behavior by simultaneously customizing features and calibrating the classifier. Specifically, considering that different behaviors require varying sampling rates to achieve optimal performance, we design a Mixture-of-Experts (MoE)-based Feature Customization (MFC) module. This module adaptively fuses data from multiple sampling rates, capturing customized features tailored to various animal behaviors. Additionally, to mitigate classifier bias toward majority classes caused by class imbalance, we develop a Neural Collapse-driven Classifier Calibration (NC3) module. This module introduces a fixed equiangular tight frame (ETF) classifier during the classification stage, maximizing the angles between pair-wise classifier vectors and thereby improving the classification performance for minority classes. To validate the effectiveness of IBA-Net, we conduct experiments on three public datasets for goat, cattle, and horse activity recognition. The results demonstrate that our method exhibits strong and competitive performance across all three datasets compared to existing approaches. Specifically, it achieves the highest values across three datasets: for goat, 93.17 % accuracy, 87.17 % F1-score, and 91.71 % recall; for cattle, 91.42 % accuracy, 90.62 % F1-score, 88.06 % precision, and 93.64 % recall; and for horse, 84.34 % F1-score and 84.05 % precision. Notably, the recall values exhibit substantial enhancements, surpassing the baseline method by 16.98 %, 15.78 %, and 4.91 % on the goat, cattle, and horse datasets, respectively. These improvements are particularly evident for the minority classes, while high recognition performance is maintained for the majority classes. These results confirm that IBA-Net effectively enhances classification accuracy across all animal behavioral categories, while aligning with the initial goal of achieving high recall values and maximizing overall classification performance.

title: Planning the tactical major fruit harvest in multiple orchards through a multi-objective GRASP metaheuristic approach
abstract: Harvest is a critical stage of the fruit supply chain that must be coordinated with other stages based on market arrival times and fruit characteristics, such as the degree of sweetness. Moreover, it accounts for the highest fruit losses due to diseases, changing weather conditions, and other factors. Harvest complexity increases when managing multiple orchards, which is a common scenario for fruit export companies. Consequently, this study proposes a multi-objective GRASP (MO-GRASP-C) metaheuristic to support tactical harvest planning for major fruits, minimizing harvest costs, fruit loss, and harvest duration. The MO-GRASP-C metaheuristic incorporates a path relinking algorithm and a clustering method to improve accuracy and eliminate non-dominated solutions while preserving Pareto frontier diversity. This study calibrates the metaheuristic parameters and applies them to a real case study, where tactical harvest plans vary significantly depending on the prioritized objectives. It also compares the results of the MO-GRASP-C metaheuristic with those of a mono-objective GRASP metaheuristic and a multi-objective exact method. In this comparison, the MO-GRASP-C metaheuristic solutions outperform those obtained by the mono-objective GRASP metaheuristic across all three minimization criteria. However, the computational time increases by approximately 13% to obtain the complete set of solutions on the Pareto frontier. Furthermore, according to the inverted generational distance metric, the MO-GRASP-C metaheuristic generates more diverse solutions than the multi-objective exact method, while requiring only approximately 1% of the computational time needed by the exact method. On the other hand, according to the hypervolume metric, the Pareto frontier obtained by the exact method is 0.5% better than the MO-GRASP-C metaheuristic, whereas, according to the INT-SBM metric, it is 17% better than the proposed metaheuristic. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of the multi-objective approach and the flexibility of the MO-GRASP-C metaheuristic in adapting tactical harvest plans to varying conditions and decision-maker preferences.

title: An automated dynamic adaptive tracking and counting method for grazing sheep based on UAV imagery and YOLO11-OBB
abstract: Accurate counting of grazing livestock is a fundamental prerequisite and key basis for the sustainable development of grasslands. Unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) provide significant advantages in flexibility and maneuverability, making them ideal for grazing livestock counting. However, practical grazing sheep counting accuracy on UAV imagery is often limited by dense crowding, high appearance similarity between individuals, and frequent viewpoint changes along UAV flight paths or resulting from sheep motion. To overcome these challenges, this study develops a UAV imagery-based grazing sheep counting framework that integrates rotated object detection, dynamic adaptive tracking, and density-aware strategies. Specifically, a rotated bounding box detector is employed to mitigate background interference resulting from random viewpoint variations and changes in animal orientation. To reduce target loss caused by transient occlusions during movement, a dynamic adaptive tracking algorithm with a motion-direction consistency constraint is introduced. A novel Sine-Decoupled Angle (SDA) loss function is proposed to address target multi-scale variations and angle prediction deviations caused by UAV flight altitude changes. Furthermore, dynamic density-aware modeling, trajectory state maintenance, and identity consistency mechanisms are incorporated to enhance counting stability. Field experiments were conducted on the integrated pipeline, which combines OBB detection, motion-constrained tracking, and density-aware counting. The system achieved an average counting accuracy of 98.23% and an IDF1 score approaching 99.00%. These results confirm that the proposed approach effectively adapts to UAV-based visual detection of moving livestock and robustly mitigates tracking failures caused by rapid motion, occlusion, and high object density. Overall, it provides a practical and reliable technical solution for automated livestock counting and management in intelligent pasture systems.

title: An integrated SNR-adaptive diffusion model and lightweight dual-backbone network for orchard obstacle detection under dataset imbalance and edge deployment constraints
abstract: Accurate and real-time obstacle detection plays a critical role in ensuring the safety and operational reliability of orchard robots. However, existing detection frameworks are constrained by class imbalance prevalent in agricultural datasets, which degrades model performance, in addition to the high computational overhead associated with Transformer architectures, thereby hindering practical implementation in resource-limited edge platforms. To overcome these limitations, the present work introduces a framework that integrates a novel generative data augmentation strategy with a lightweight dual-backbone detection network. First, a signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) adaptive normalization denoising diffusion probabilistic model (SNRA-DDPM) was designed to mitigate the scarcity of minority class samples. By incorporating an SNR-aware adaptive normalization mechanism, SNRA-DDPM dynamically regulates feature distributions according to noise intensity, thereby generating high-fidelity samples to effectively rebalance the dataset distribution. Second, a lightweight detector, DBFNet, was developed based on the Transformer architecture. This network employs a dual-backbone structure combining High-Performance Graphics Processing Unit Network version 2 (HGNetv2) with an improved Cross Stage Partial Darknet (CSPDarknet), designed to synergistically capture global semantic information and fine-grained frequency-domain features. Furthermore, a dual-backbone fusion (DFusion) module was designed to address the inherent feature heterogeneity between the two backbones. This module utilizes channel and position attention mechanisms to adaptively align and fuse these features, significantly enhancing cross-branch information interaction and feature complementarity. The experimental results showed that SNRA-DDPM obtained Fréchet Inception Distance (FID) scores of 42.8348 and 46.4346 for minority classes, including baskets and ladders, respectively, exceeding the performance of the standard DDPM. In detection tasks, DBFNet achieved an 88.21% mean Average Precision (mAP) and 208.79 frames per second (FPS) with only 34.1 giga floating-point operations (GFLOPs), surpassing the Real-Time DEtection TRansformer based on Residual Network-18 (RT-DETR-r18) baseline in both accuracy and efficiency. Notably, the integration of the SNRA-DDPM augmentation strategy further improved model accuracy. Deployment on a harvesting robot platform showed that the proposed method achieved an inference speed of 44.48 FPS at 640-pixel resolution using 16-bit floating-point (FP16) precision, corresponding to a 17.2% improvement over the baseline and confirming its real-time capability in orchards. These results demonstrate that integrating generative data augmentation with lightweight detection networks is both effective and engineering-feasible for alleviating data imbalance and enabling deployment on resource-constrained edge devices in agricultural vision tasks.

title: A frequency-aware and multi-scale feature enhancement network for maize seedling grading
abstract: Maize (Zea mays L.) seedling grading is a crucial step in speed breeding, with accurate grading playing a significant role in enabling rapid trait identification. However, existing computer vision grading methods struggle to capture edge details and small-scale seedlings. To address these challenges, a frequency-aware and multi-scale feature enhancement framework was developed for maize seedling grading. In order to address the loss of high-frequency details, a Frequency Selective Downsampling (FSD) module was introduced. Discrete wavelet transform (DWT) was applied to explicitly decompose frequency-domain features and adaptively enhance them at the channel level. This design effectively enhances edge details and preserves structural information. To overcome the limited ability to capture multi-scale features in existing methods, a Scale-Adaptive Feature Enhancement (SAFE) module was designed. It employs multi-scale depthwise separable convolutions with spatial and channel attention to adaptively fuse features and enhance multi-scale seedling perception. Experimental results on a maize seedling instance segmentation dataset showed that it achieved 98.79%, 87.26%, and 71.34% for mean Average Precision at Intersection over Union thresholds of 0.50 (mAP50), 0.50–0.75 (mAP50:75), and 0.50–0.95 (mAP50:95), respectively. Meanwhile, it maintained a real-time inference speed of 42.4 Frames Per Second (FPS). Furthermore, the model demonstrated superior segmentation performance under varying lighting, density, and occlusion conditions. The proposed method enables accurate grading of maize seedlings under controlled conditions and provides seedling-stage phenotypic information. Its applicability under extremely dense and heavily occluded conditions warrants further investigation.

title: Autonomous crop and weed detection in multiple agricultural fields using YOLO-based models with combined real and synthesized images
abstract: Accurate crop and weed detection is critical for targeted weed control, particularly for weeds in intra-row areas. Site-specific weeding where weeds appear can reduce herbicide use and labor costs. However, field variability, including crop growth stage, soil texture, illumination, and camera viewpoint, remains challenging. This study presents a practical data-construction workflow that integrates synthetically generated images with labeled real images to train crop-weed detection models. You Only Look Once (YOLO) versions 4 and 8, convolutional neural network (CNN) architectures, were evaluated because of their detection performance and computational efficiency. Training YOLOv8 with a mixed synthetic-real dataset derived from four crop types collected across agricultural fields in four Japanese prefectures improved detection of 11 crop and weed classes. On the validation data, the model achieved a precision of 0.92, a recall of 0.89, an F1-score of 0.90, and a mean average precision (mAP50) of 0.92. On independent real test images, the proposed YOLOv8 model achieved a mAP50 of 0.88, with class-level Recall50 values ranging from 0.67 to 0.97 and a mean Recall50 of 0.85. These results show that synthetic images are useful for reducing annotation effort and improving class balance when combined with real field images, but they do not replace independent real-image validation. The method therefore provides a promising perception component for future intra-row weeding systems, while robot-level testing, embedded inference, and actuation accuracy remain necessary before autonomous deployment.

title: Trait-Adaptive Hierarchical Attention Fusion of RGB-D data for automated lettuce phenotyping in hydroponic systems
abstract: Lettuce is one of the most widely cultivated leafy vegetables worldwide, and its production in controlled-environment hydroponic facilities is expanding steadily. Monitoring canopy growth at high temporal resolution enables growers to adjust nutrient delivery and harvest timing at each developmental stage, yet existing image-based phenotyping methods rely on fixed-weight RGB-D fusion that does not adapt to the requirements of individual morphological traits. We propose Trait-Adaptive Hierarchical Attention Fusion (TAHAF), an architecture that fuses RGB and depth features at three spatial scales through learned attention gates and employs trait-conditioned prediction heads to estimate five lettuce traits simultaneously. All experiments use true RGB-D inputs in which the camera RGB stream and the metric depth stream are processed as separate modalities throughout the network. TAHAF was evaluated on 5039 daily observations from 180 Romaine lettuce plants grown across six NFT hydroponic channels and two 28-day growth cycles, and validated against 156 destructive sampling measurements. All reported numbers are means of multiple independent random seeds. The three-scale TAHAF variant attains a macro R2=0.9415±0.0036 (n = 4 at 1.45 GFLOPs and 7.84M parameters with per-trait scale-attention weights for transparent reasoning; a late-scale variant with the trait-conditioned head reaches the highest single-model accuracy at R2=0.9577±0.0018 (n = 4, exceeding the strongest external fusion baselines under matched scale and training budget (SA-Gate 0.9544±0.0039, Concat 0.9538±0.0015, CBAM 0.9531±0.0027; all n = 5. A controlled benchmark of 14 architectures under identical protocols confirms that pretrained encoders are the dominant design choice (drop of 0.037 in R2 when removed). Physical validation against 156 destructive samples shows that image-derived volume correlates with fresh weight at r=0.535 (p<10−4, n = 156 after controlling for day of growth (raw r=0.832). Intrinsic attention analysis reveals that RGB features dominate early scales while both modalities converge to near-equal weighting at semantic levels, and Grad-CAM confirms attention to biologically relevant plant regions.

title: Salmonella risk prediction in poultry farms via deep learning image classification Models, Cross-Region Validation, and edge computing
abstract: Salmonella remains a major cause of foodborne illnesses that are commonly associated with the consumption of contaminated poultry products. Therefore, there is a strong emphasis and a crucial need to reduce Salmonella across the farm to fork continuum. However, there are no easy and rapid on-farm prediction tools to estimate if a flock carries Salmonella . In this study, we used deep learning to develop a Salmonella risk classification model for chicken feces. The model was developed using a two-part framework combining deep learning and tree-based classification techniques. In the first stage, deep learning models such as ResNet152, Xception, VGG19, and others were employed to extract high-level features from chicken fecal images. In the second stage, these features were used by decision tree classifiers including Random Forest and Gradient Boosting for binary classification into Salmonella PCR Positive or Negative. The model was developed using fixed train-validation-test splits on two datasets: an American dataset with 720 images from a controlled multi-serovar Salmonella challenge study and African dataset with 4333 publicly available images. This integrated approach achieved up to 85% classification accuracy when validated across geographical regions. The developed framework was integrated into a user-friendly mobile and web application and allows users to custom train the deep learning classifiers to improve the classification of unseen fecal images. Although the model was primarily validated with the same dataset, this proof-of-concept framework can serve as a decision-support tool for Salmonella control and intervention, contributing to enhanced food safety. Overall, the objective of this study is to develop and validate a hybrid AI approach for Salmonella prediction using fecal images, with explicit cross-region evaluation and proof-of-concept deployment applications.

title: MoeBi-ViT: Non-destructive shoot-stage phenotyping of lettuce in plant factory via dual-branch mixture-of-experts network and enhanced segmentation
abstract: In plant factories, increased crop yield often comes at the price of higher energy inputs. Understanding the relationship between environmental regulation and crop growth helps maximize energy use efficiency. Thus, dynamic monitoring of crop biomass is critical for optimizing crop management practices. The morphological parameters (canopy length and width, plant height, leaf area) and biomass indicators (fresh weight and dry weight) jointly form the key metrics for evaluating crop growth and development. However, traditional manual measurement methods are typically inefficient, costly, labor-intensive, and time-consuming. This study proposed a rapid, non-destructive lettuce biomass estimation method based on two-stage multi-modal deep learning: firstly, a gated attention-enhanced segmentation model—Mambaout-Mask2Former (MOMF)—was adopted to address background interference in lettuce phenotypic estimation, which reduces parameter count and model complexity while enabling accurate lettuce mask extraction and background elimination; secondly, a dual-branch Mixture-of-Experts regression network (MoeBi-ViT) was constructed to lower the computational complexity of the biomass regression network while ensuring generalization across scenarios, which was achieved via the combination of a Transformer-based Mixture-of-Experts encoder (TEME) and bi-attentional feature fusion (BAF). MoeBi-ViT activates only ∼ 37 % of weights per inference (compared to fully parameter-activated models) while maintaining precise biomass regression performance. Experimental results have shown that MoeBi-ViT outperformed the baseline Vision Transformer (ViT) significantly in lettuce biomass estimation with only a marginal increase in inference parameters, achieving a coefficient of determination (R2) of 0.936 for fresh weight prediction and a 12.3 % overall improvement in the aggregated R2 metric. Ablation studies confirmed the effectiveness of TEME and BAF. To explain the model’s operating mechanism, activation frequencies were counted to analyze the contribution of different expert types in the final Mixture-of-Experts layer to various phenotypic parameters. Additionally, the trained model was applied to an unlabeled lettuce dataset to verify its accuracy in continuous growth monitoring. The results demonstrated that the predicted growth curves were consistent with their actual one. The framework proposed in this study provides an effective non-destructive monitoring approach for crop management, with potential applications in smart decision-making for plant factories.

title: LSCDNet: leveraging fine-grained contextual cues for precise detection of small target crop disease spots in complex field environments
abstract: Timely crop disease monitoring is essential for stable grain production and quality improvement, with accurate identification of small, visually similar disease spots still a key challenge in complex field environments. The traditional disease detection methods are inefficient, high in cost, and highly dependent on experts’ experience for support. This study introduces an advanced YOLO framework for precise crop disease detection, which consists of three core improved modules: Firstly, a novel convolution structure, SSRConv, is proposed to adaptively capture the irregular textures and topological changes of crop disease spots with extremely low computational overhead, thereby achieving high-robustness feature extraction in resource-constrained agricultural scenarios. Secondly, the proposed C2F-S2Block module adopts a dual-branch structure with star convolution as its core. It enhances cross-scale feature dependencies, enabling precise characterization of crop diseases while effectively suppressing background interference. Thirdly, we design the CLDA-Head detection module, which integrates cross-layer attention and distribution-aware regression to enhance feature fusion accuracy and bounding box localization stability. Further leveraging the enhanced CLLABlock and SimAM attention mechanisms, the module simultaneously improves multi-scale perception and classification capabilities. Experimental results on the large-scale crop disease dataset DCrop12 show that the proposed LSCDNet model achieves 52.6 % mean average precision (mAP50) at a detection rate of 77 FPS, representing an improvement of 2.7 percentage points over the baseline model. The proposed model outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods and establishes a new benchmark for real-time crop disease detection in complex field scenarios.

title: Unsupervised keypoint detection for automated livestock phenotyping: A multi-species approach based on pre-trained foundation models
abstract: In the realm of precision livestock farming, the identification of keypoint in livestock is a crucial area of research. Traditional supervised learning approaches face challenges in adapting to the complexities of livestock environments, including varied poses, occlusions, and inter-species differences, due to their reliance on extensive annotated datasets. To overcome these limitations, this research introduces a novel unsupervised keypoint detection methodology grounded in pre-trained foundation models. Our innovative approach combines the strengths of Stable Diffusion (SD), known for its exceptional fine-grained texture perception, with DINOv2′s structural similarity representation. We employ a normalized weighted fusion strategy to seamlessly integrates these complementary features, enabling multi-scale semantic alignment. Additionally, we have developed a unique multi-template voting mechanism that utilizes Mean-Shift clustering and inverse-distance weighting, significantly enhancing both the accuracy and stability of keypoint detection. To support this research, we have compiled a comprehensive livestock dataset encompassing 2204 images horse (804), cattle (309), sheep (767), and pig (324). Our experimental analysis, conducted across these species, reveals a high average detection accuracy (91.21% for horses, 91.09% for cattle, 84.76% for sheep, and 93.78% for pig), using the PCK@0.05 metric, which outperforms the SOTA method by 3.07, 4.62, 11.19, and 3.10 percentage points (pp), respectively. The proposed method demonstrates robust cross-species generalization capabilities, effectively managing significant pose changes and non-rigid deformations. It offers a versatile and efficient solution for keypoint detection, applicable to automated body measurement or animal behavior analysis in precision livestock farming applications. For access to the code and dataset, please visit https://gitee.com/wbxue/keypoints.

title: Visual-language-guided task planning for horticultural robots
abstract: Crop monitoring is essential for precision agriculture, but current systems lack high-level reasoning. We introduce a novel, modular framework that uses a Vision Language Model (VLM) to guide robotic task planning by actively querying heterogeneous data sources—including enriched RGB camera feeds and 2D semantic occupancy maps—interleaved with robotic action primitives. We contribute a comprehensive benchmark for short- and long-horizon crop monitoring tasks in monoculture and polyculture environments. Our results show that while zero-shot VLMs perform robustly for short-horizon tasks (achieving 87% success, comparable to human experts), success drops significantly to under 10% for complex long-horizon, multi-target tasks. Despite this decline, task completion rates remain above 76% under noiseless conditions. Critically, the system degrades when relying on noisy semantic maps, demonstrating a key limitation in current VLM context grounding for sustained robotic operations. This work offers a deployable framework and critical insights into VLM capabilities and shortcomings for complex agricultural robotics. Supplementary material: https://kendallkoe.com/Visual-Language-Guided-Task-Planning-for-Horticultural-Robots/ .

title: NearStitch: Robust near-surface image stitching for phenotyping
abstract: High-throughput phenotyping platforms (HTPPs) are widely used for efficient phenotyping. Near-surface image stitching is one key technology required by HTTPs. However, it is challenged by large-distortion, large-parallax, and homogenous features of images, leading to poor alignment, edge distortions, and ghosting. This study developed an artifact-free, robust, and scalable near-surface image stitching algorithm (NearStitch) with a self-constructed dataset (PlantStitch). It is characterized by its hierarchical structure, primarily comprising three modules: layered feature extraction, layered image alignment, and warping and post-processing. The PlantStitch comprises 34,299 images of various crop types, growing stages, and altitudes, collected using field gantry phenotyping and unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) platforms. The adjacent and multi-line stitched results showed that NearStitch had fewer artifacts and less distortion than other commercial software and public algorithms. Besides, NearStitch produced Integrated Local Natural Image Quality Evaluator (ILNIQE) scores of 22.97 for the GS3 dataset (gantry-collected soybean images at 3 m) and 23.12 for the GW3 dataset (gantry-collected wheat images at 3 m). Meanwhile, the average angle difference of checkerboard (AADC) values for the GS3 and GW3 datasets were 1.68 and 0.40, respectively.
