Compared to the six state-of-the-art (SOTA) methods, the ILNIQE scores improved by approximately 7 % on average, while the AADC scores showed an average improvement of around 10 %. Additionally, the algorithms are transferable to other image data types, such as multispectral and thermal infrared stitching. The NearStitch algorithm and software are publicly available on GitHub. We believe that the PlantStitch and NearStitch, as common image processing datasets and methods, will support image-based crop stress assessment and variety screening in high-throughput plant phenotyping by enabling reliable near-surface image stitching.

title: Energy-Efficient path tracking control for autonomous tractors equipped with Hydro-Mechanical continuously variable transmission based on coordinated control methods
abstract: Autonomous tractors often prioritize tracking performance at the expense of operational energy consumption, negatively affecting their economic efficiency. To address this issue, this study proposes a coordinated control method that considers both tracking accuracy and fuel economy. First, a model predictive control algorithm is used to design the path tracking system, where longitudinal and lateral errors as tracking objectives, while acceleration and front wheel steering angular velocity as constraints. Then, a plowing resistance prediction model for tractors is developed using Long Short-Term Memory neural networks based on historical tractor plowing resistance data. Next, a dual-variable economic control strategy is developed to minimize the engine fuel consumption rate and optimize the hydraulic-mechanical continuously variable transmission efficiency ratio. The predicted working speed from the path tracking system and the predicted plowing resistance from the resistance prediction model are then passed to the economic control strategy, forming a coordinated control method that integrates tracking accuracy with fuel economy. We used pure pursuit and Stanley, both with a single-variable fuel-economy control strategy, as baselines. The proposed strategy’s effectiveness is validated through simulations and hardware-in-the-loop experiments. The results show that, compared with the alternative method, the proposed approach effectively reduces path tracking error and improves economic efficiency. Compared with the first and second comparison methods, the proposed approach reduces the standard deviation of speed variance by 70.27% for both methods, decreases longitudinal tracking error by 57.14% and 33.33%, respectively, reduces lateral tracking error by 33.33% and 55.56%, respectively, and lowers fuel consumption by 28.49% for both methods. This study provides valuable insights for improving both path tracking performance and energy efficiency in autonomous tractors.

title: Estimation model of total flavonoids content in Ginkgo biloba leaves based on airborne hyperspectral canopy image
abstract: Total flavonoids are a key indicator of the medicinal value of Ginkgo biloba leaves. To address limitations of traditional chemical detection methods, this study proposes a non-destructive estimation method based on UAV-borne hyperspectral canopy images. Hyperspectral images were acquired using a UAV. The study evaluated the effects of various preprocessing methods, including Multiplicative Scatter Correction (MSC), Savitzky–Golay smoothing combined with Multiplicative Scatter Correction (SG-MSC), and Standard Normal Variate (SNV), as well as feature selection techniques, including Successive Projections Algorithm (SPA), Competitive Adaptive Reweighted Sampling (CARS), Principal Component Analysis (PCA), and the proposed Squeeze-and-Excitation Augmented Competitive Adaptive Reweighted Sampling (SEACARS), on model performance. Subsequently, random forest regression (RFR), support vector regression (SVR), XGBoost, and a novel DeepXGBoost-FM (DXF) fusion model were constructed, and spectral-textural multimodal fusion was explored. SG-MSC yielded optimal performance. Among all combinations, the SEACARS-DXF model demonstrated superior performance (Rp2 = 0.8221, RMSEp = 6.93 mg/g). After further integrating textural features, the predictive capability of the DXF-TF model was significantly enhanced (Rp2 = 0.8720, RMSEp = 6.66 mg/g; compared with DXF, P < 0.01), outperforming traditional models in terms of accuracy, efficiency, and robustness. This study demonstrates that the integrated (SG-MSC)-SEACARS-(DXF-TF) framework, combining efficient preprocessing, intelligent feature selection, and multimodal fusion, achieves high-precision non-destructive estimation of total flavonoid content in the canopy of three-year-old medicinal Ginkgo biloba during the mid-August harvest period under experimental conditions, providing a feasible technical solution for monitoring total flavonoids at the canopy scale in medicinal Ginkgo biloba nurseries during the harvest period.

title: Wind-excited audio-based leaf area density estimation in apple-tree canopies: Mechanism-guided generative denoising and attention-based spectrogram learning
abstract: Leaf area density (LAD) describes canopy compactness in apple orchards and supports variable-rate spraying decisions. However, real-time in-field LAD sensing remains challenging because occlusion, illumination variability, and strong equipment noise reduce the reliability and learnability of canopy observations. This study proposes a mechanism-guided wind-excited acoustic sensing framework for LAD grade estimation in apple-tree canopies. First, mechanism-based analysis was used to identify the dominant noise sources and key frequency bands, and passive noise reduction was adopted to improve acquisition consistency. Then, a correlation-mean-square-error (MSE) constrained deep neural network (CM-DNN) was used to reconstruct low-SNR wind-excited audio. Finally, a spectral-centroid statistical prior was introduced to guide frequency-axis attention, and a spectral-centroid attention deep convolutional neural network (SCA-DCNN) model was used to classify log-power spectrum spectrograms. The results showed that passive noise reduction decreased device background noise from 72.7 dB to 65.4 dB, and 10 m/s was selected as the unified acquisition condition. On this basis, SCA-DCNN improved accuracy by 3.50 percentage points over the baseline DCNN and achieved 91.50 % accuracy on independent field samples. Overall, the proposed combination of mechanism-guided noise control, low-SNR signal reconstruction, and prior-guided attention improved the learnability of orchard acoustic data and provided a deployable sensing pathway for prescription-oriented canopy grading.

title: Multispectral UAV imagery-based forest tree species classification using MEDA-UNet
abstract: Multispectral unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) remote sensing offers an efficient and cost-effective solution for single-tree segmentation and tree species classification, thereby facilitating precise forest management, biodiversity monitoring, and ecological assessment. To address the high costs, limited spectral resolution, and complex data processing associated with traditional approaches based on hyperspectral, red–green–blue (RGB), or Light Detection and Ranging (LiDAR) data, we propose MEDA-UNet, an enhanced deep segmentation framework that leverages single-temporal multispectral imagery for tree species identification in heterogeneous forests. The model employs MambaOut as its backbone and incorporates multi-scale feature Enhancement Block (EBlock), Debluring Block (DBlock), an Edge-Gaussian Aggregation (EGA) module, and a dynamic activation function (DynamicTanh), enabling high-precision semantic segmentation of multiple tree species in complex forest environments. Evaluation on a real-world multispectral dataset from Northeast China, including red-edge and near-infrared bands, demonstrates that MEDA-UNet achieves 72.74% mean Intersection over Union (mIoU), 83.39% mean Average Precision (mAP), and 86.21% F1-score, outperforming mainstream models such as UNet and DeepLabv3+. Additional experiments further confirm that the original five-band input outperforms both RGB and commonly used vegetation index combinations, highlighting the critical role of red-edge and near-infrared bands in tree species identification. Overall, the proposed method strikes a balance between accuracy, computational efficiency, and practical applicability, providing robust support for the intelligent interpretation of multispectral imagery in automated forest resource surveys and dynamic monitoring.

title: XylemVision: A Knowledge-Distilled deep learning framework for High-Throughput quantification of root anatomy in peanut
abstract: Manually quantifying root anatomy from microscope images has been a major bottleneck in crop research. Deep learning can automate this process, but requires large, labeled datasets that are expensive to create. Newer foundation models, like the Segment Anything Model (SAM) or DINOv2, appear to offer a solution but struggle with specialized scientific images. Even after fine-tuning, these models still require precise prompts such as bounding boxes or points to specify what to segment. A common workaround is to use an object detector (like YOLO) to create these prompts, but this reintroduces the original challenge of needing extensive labeled data to train the detectors itself. To address this bottleneck, a knowledge distillation (KD) framework was developed to train object detectors with minimal labeled data. Initially, a large DINOv2 teacher model was used to pretrain student detectors (YOLO11 and RT-DETR) on unlabeled root images, transferring its rich visual feature representation capabilities without requiring any labels. This pretraining phase enabled the student models to extract high-level generalized spatial features of the root images. The pretrained student detectors were then fine-tuned using a small, labeled dataset to detect anatomical features including xylem, vascular bundles, and the total root. Finally, the resulting bounding boxes were passed to a SAM-integrated segmentation pipeline to produce precise, pixel-level masks for trait extraction. Together, these steps form XylemVision, a unified and data-efficient pipeline for xylem phenotyping that demonstrates accurate detection, segmentation, and trait extraction with limited labeled data. Results showed that the KD-pretrained YOLO11 model demonstrated superior detection performance (0.922 mAP50–95) compared to its supervised baseline (0.884) and maintained comparable accuracy (0.917 mAP50–95) even when the labeled dataset was reduced by 25 %-75 %. By leveraging these precise bounding boxes as prompts, the SAM-based segmentation pipeline proved highly effective, achieving mean Intersection over Union (IoU) scores of 0.85–0.95 across all anatomical traits substantially outperforming YOLO11′s built-in segmentation module, which achieved only 0.10–0.58 IoU. Beyond these performance gains, the KD framework ensured strong transferability across species, successfully adapting to soybean root cross-sections without additional fine-tuning. Overall, this study develops a data-efficient framework that makes plant image analysis efficient and more accurate across different crops.

title: Optimal design of multi-link automatic seedling picking and placing device
abstract: To improve transplanting efficiency and reduce damage during seedling picking and placing in automated transplanters for pepper plug seedlings, this study proposes a multi-link mechanism with rotation-translation compound joints that automatically reorients the picking claw. The claw is parallel to the plug-tray surface at the picking point and parallel to the ground at the placing point without additional actuators, thereby simplifying both the mechanical structure and control system. A kinematic model was established and a five-objective optimization model was solved using a multi-objective genetic algorithm to obtain an optimal trajectory for near-vertical extraction and gravity-aligned delivery. Kinematic analysis showed zero velocity at both the picking and placing points, low-speed stable operation during working stages, and high-speed efficient return. Experimental validation showed close agreement between actual and simulated trajectories (maximum error ≤5 mm). Clamping force was quantified via thin-film pressure sensors and verified to remain below the biological yield force of pepper stems, with no mechanical damage observed across all tests. At rotational speeds of 60–90 r/min, the device achieved seedling picking success rates of 90.6%–97.2% and placing success rates of 91.5%–97.1%, respectively. The optimal performance was obtained at 60 r/min (120 plants/min), with a 97.2% picking success rate and a 97.1% placing success rate. These results demonstrate that the proposed design provides a feasible solution for reliable, low-damage, and high-efficiency transplanting of pepper plug seedlings under controlled prototype conditions.

title: Spectral partitioning, per-band normalization, and spatial scale shape the efficacy of imaging spectroscopy to estimate grassland diversity
abstract: Effective monitoring of grassland biodiversity is essential, yet remains challenging because imaging spectroscopy estimates of plant diversity are highly sensitive to methodological, including scale-related, choices. Using unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV)-based imaging spectroscopy over a long-term nitrogen addition experiment in Inner Mongolia, China, we evaluated how spectral partitioning, per-band normalization, plot size, spatial resolution, and normalized difference vegetation index (NDVI) affect spectral diversity (SD) estimation of species richness. We compared four SD metrics across five plot sizes (1, 4, 9, 16, and 25 m2) and three spatial resolutions (2, 10, and 20 cm) under full-spectrum and partitioned frameworks with no, local, or global normalization, and quantified the contributions of spectral regions and NDVI. Spectral partitioned models generally outperformed full-spectrum models, but the optimal normalization was metric-specific: local normalization favored coefficient of variation (CV) and spectral variance (SV), whereas global normalization favored convex hull area (CHA) and spectral species richness (SSR). Except for SSR, local normalization also produced more stable SD–species richness relationships across plot sizes. Sensitivity to spatial coarsening of spectral data was strongest in smaller plots and weakened in larger plots, whereas CHA remained robust across different spatial resolutions. NDVI mainly improved predictions when SD alone performed poorly, especially for SV and SSR. Spectral contributions also diverged among metrics: near-infrared contributions increased with plot size for CV and SV, whereas CHA and SSR were driven mainly by visible and red-edge information. These results highlight the need to match SD metrics and processing workflows to target sampling scales for scalable grassland biodiversity monitoring.

title: Integrating feature selection and machine learning for nitrogen assessment in grapevine leaves using in-field hyperspectral imaging
abstract: Nitrogen (N) is one of the most critical nutrients in winegrape production, influencing vine vigor, fruit composition, and wine quality. Because soil N availability varies spatially and temporally, accurate estimation of leaf N concentration is essential for optimizing fertilization at the individual plant level. In this study, in-field hyperspectral images (400-1000 nm) were collected from four grapevine cultivars (Chardonnay, Pinot Noir, Concord, and Syrah) across two growth stages (bloom and veraison) during the 2022 and 2023 growing seasons at both the leaf and canopy levels. An ensemble feature selection framework was developed to identify the most informative spectral bands for N estimation within individual cultivars, effectively reducing redundancy and selecting compact, physiologically meaningful band combinations spanning the visible, red-edge, and near-infrared regions. At the leaf level, models achieved the highest predictive accuracy for Chardonnay (R^2 = 0.82, RMSE = 0.19 %DW) and Pinot Noir (R^2 = 0.69, RMSE = 0.20 %DW). Canopy-level predictions also performed well, with R^2 values of 0.65, 0.72, and 0.70 for Chardonnay, Concord, and Syrah, respectively. White cultivars exhibited balanced spectral contributions across the visible, red-edge, and near-infrared regions, whereas red cultivars relied more heavily on visible bands due to anthocyanin-chlorophyll interactions. Leaf-level N-sensitive bands selected for Chardonnay and Pinot Noir were successfully transferred to the canopy level, improving or maintaining prediction accuracy across cultivars. These results confirm that ensemble feature selection captures spectrally robust, scale-consistent bands transferable across measurement levels and cultivars, demonstrating the potential of integrating in-field hyperspectral imaging with machine learning for vineyard N status monitoring.

title: Context-aware adaptive pesticide spraying for agricultural robots under changing weather and terrain using Vision–Language Models
abstract: Precision pesticide spraying is essential for optimizing application efficiency and ensuring uniform chemical distribution. Spraying performance is influenced by multiple factors, including environmental conditions such as temperature and wind speed, pesticide type, and the robot's capability to accurately perceive crops and target spray locations. Existing approaches predominantly emphasize crop detection and rely on predefined spraying parameters, whereas human operators dynamically adjust their spraying strategies by considering environmental conditions, region-specific crop characteristics, and the type of pesticide being applied. In this study, we propose a context-aware adaptive spraying framework based on Vision-Language Models (VLMs), which enables robots to leverage spatial reasoning and integrate information from multiple sources, including crop type, pesticide type, and weather data, to make adaptive and optimized spraying decisions. Subsequently, a trajectory-tracking controller based on Model Predictive Path Integral (MPPI) control is employed to ensure precise navigation and accurate spraying at crop locations. The comparative results demonstrate that the proposed method improves accuracy by at least 30% in detecting crop rows. In addition, the experimental evaluations conducted in two environments further demonstrate the robot's ability to flexibly adjust spraying volume and travel speed, while reducing pesticide drift.

title: Concept-guided deep learning with UAV-satellite sample augmentation for daily 10 m crop AGB mapping
abstract: Aboveground biomass (AGB) is a fundamental variable for characterizing crop growth, yield potential, and agricultural carbon cycling. Achieving daily 10 m resolution crop AGB mapping at regional scales remains challenging. Here, a unified UAV-satellite framework is developed that integrates sample augmentation with concept-guided deep learning (DL) to enable high-resolution AGB mapping. UAV-derived canopy structural and spectral information is fused with satellite spectral and cumulative temporal features to generate virtual quadrats aligned with the Sentinel-2 pixel scale, thereby expanding the training dataset and mitigating the scarcity of field-based AGB measurements. These quadrats facilitate the development of a novel light-use-efficiency-guided Long Short-Term Memory model (LUE-LSTM), in which AGB is formulated as a cumulative state variable driven by photosynthetically active radiation, enforcing physiological constraints on AGB dynamics. Experiments in the Hetao Irrigation District demonstrate improved physical consistency of AGB temporal estimation, characterized by near-ideal temporal behavior (Normalized Time Variability Index, NTVI ≈ 1.0) and low deviation from realistic growth dynamics (Logistic Fitting Error, LFE < 60 g m⁻2). Cross-year and cross-region validation further demonstrates enhanced generalization, with R2 increasing from 0.741 to 0.815 and RRMSE decreasing from 0.220 to 0.185. Using the proposed framework, daily 10 m AGB maps were generated for 2019–2025, demonstrating strong potential for regional crop monitoring and agricultural carbon assessment.

title: A vision-based time-delay modeling and control method for target-oriented trenching fertilization in spindle-shaped orchards
abstract: To address the challenge of fertilizers utilization efficiency in trenching application within spindle-shaped orchards, this study proposes a visual target-oriented fertilization control method that enables precise application of fertilizers with fixed lengths and quantities to the active root zones of fruit trees. By analyzing the control system in terms of target detection, communication delay, device response, and fertilizer discharge, a visual target-oriented fertilization time-delay model was established, thereby determining the safe operating speed range of the machinery.A quadratic regression model was developed to describe the relationship between fertilization and the rotational speed of the fertilizer applicator. Based on the Newton-Raphson iterative method, a multi-input single-output control algorithm was designed. Experimental results showed that the system achieved a fertilization error of 8.4 %, a fertilization length error of 1.82 %, and a coefficient of variation for uniformity of 7.69 %, meeting the operational requirements of orchard fertilization. The proposed visual target-oriented fertilization time-delay model and control method improve fertilization accuracy and stability in spindle-shaped orchards, enabling intermittent fertilization within the active root zone. This method contribute to improved the accuracy and spatial precision in fertilization and provide technical support for precision orchard management.

title: Adaptive connection line filtering for the image registration of UAV-Based visual and thermal infrared imagery in rice phenotyping
abstract: The integration of visual and thermal infrared sensors is crucial for rice phenotyping, and image registration serves as a prerequisite for data fusion and phenotypic analysis. The mainstream image registration methods rely on feature descriptor derived from hand crafted or deep learning for keypoint matching. Such methods cannot address the challenges brought by abundant self-similarities of rice canopy and modal variation between sensors. To address this problem, this study employed the adaptive connection line filtering (ACLF) for homography estimation. Specifically, this framework utilized the geometric topology from global pairwise correspondences, and introduced a connection line filtering (CLF) algorithm to eliminate keypoint mismatches, followed by a fine-grained matching (FGM) approach to refine the keypoint location. Also, color contrast enhancement (CCE) was applied prior to representation learning to enhance the keypoint detection. Cross year and cross sites field experiments demonstrated the effectiveness of our method. Specifically, the proposed method outperformed the state of the art by 1.98 in RMSE at seedling stage, and 0.38 in RMSE at tillering stage. This study lays the foundation for phenotypic analysis using UAV-based visual and thermal infrared data, which can accelerate the process of large scale rice breeding and ensure food security. Our data and code will be available at: https://github.com/huanghsheng/ACLF.

title: Revelation of the mechanism by which charging of cotton leaves enhances electrospray deposition: systematic verification based on multi-physics field coupling simulation and high-speed camera observation
abstract: Aiming at the bottleneck problems of low liquid coverage, severe droplet drift and low pesticide utilization in electrospray operations in arid and semi-arid cotton-growing areas, this study focused on the previously proposed “cotton leaf and droplet dual-charged” electrospray method, aiming to systematically reveal the internal mechanism of enhancing droplet deposition and complete the systematic research from mechanism verification to field application. Firstly, through the voltage attenuation test on the surface of cotton leaves, the charge-carrying characteristics of cotton leaves as “active electrostatic electrodes” were clarified, and the optimal polarization voltage range was determined to be 15–20 kV. On this basis, a multi-physics field model coupling electric field, flow field and particle motion was constructed. The simulation results showed that the electric field of opposite point charges formed by the dual-charged mode could exert continuous Coulomb attraction on droplets, significantly converging their motion trajectories toward the target. Compared with the single-charged mode, the terminal deposition deviation was reduced by 69.8%, and the lateral convergence was increased by 167.1%. Furthermore, high-speed camera technology was used to observe the droplet motion behavior. It was found that the average deflection angle of droplets under the dual-charged condition was reduced by 71.4% compared with that under the single-charged mode, and the trajectories tended to be more vertical, which verified the active guiding effect of the electric field on droplets. Finally, a dual-charged field test prototype was integrated and developed, and verification tests were carried out. The field data showed that under the optimal parameters, the dual-charged mode increased the droplet coverage on leaves to a maximum of 50.33% (11.61% higher than that of the single-charged mode), reduced the volume median diameter (VMD) by approximately 3.7%, and improved the deposition spectrum simultaneously. Through multi-scale research of “model simulation, process observation, field verification”, this study systematically revealed the electro-mechanical coupling mechanism of active cotton leaf charging, enhancing droplet adhesion, which provides a theoretical basis and equipment support for parameter optimization and engineering application of this technology.

title: A geometry–radiometry correction framework for hyperspectral LiDAR and 3D spectral index mapping in plants
abstract: High-throughput plant phenotyping requires the simultaneous characterization of three-dimensional structural and spectral properties across organ to canopy scales. Hyperspectral LiDAR (HSL), which integrates the spectral resolution of two-dimensional hyperspectral imaging with the spatial sensing capabilities of LiDAR, offers the potential to generate 3D spectral point clouds but still faces a key challenge: obtaining comparable reflectance estimates from raw intensity measurements under varying range and incidence-angle conditions. Here, we propose a correction framework consisting of (i) a change-point optimized, automatic-separation piecewise distance-effect model (CP-ASP) and (ii) an incidence-angle correction based on the Lambert–Beckmann formulation. CP-ASP estimates a system-level shared breakpoint through global change-point optimization using a fixed candidate set and an aggregated objective over wavelength bands, improving reproducibility and robustness of range normalization across bands. We evaluated the workflow in controlled indoor experiments using full-waveform HSL data with 21 wavelength bands to generate plant-level spectral point clouds and demonstrate 3D mapping of representative spectral indices (SR, PRI, and CRI). The workflow provides a reproducible basis for plant-level 3D spectral mapping under controlled conditions, while indicating that points near leaf boundaries and at extreme incidence angles may remain challenging and should be further evaluated in outdoor heterogeneous canopies.

title: Stage-specific estimation of rice leaf area index and above-ground biomass from UAV LiDAR-derived structural features
abstract: Accurate extraction of phenotypic traits in low-stature crops is essential for precision agriculture and phenomics research. This study evaluates a stage-specific framework for estimating rice leaf area index (LAI) and above-ground biomass (AGB) using unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) light detection and ranging (LiDAR) data across four key growth stages: tillering, jointing, booting, and heading. Following point cloud preprocessing and the extraction of canopy structural features, we identified stage-wise candidate predictors using random forest recursive feature elimination (RF-RFE) and Spearman correlation. Physically informed variables, such as the transformed canopy-cover term −ln(1−fcover) and a derived volume metric, were integrated into the modeling process. For evaluation, multiple linear regression (MLR), random forest (RF), and extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost) were compared using plot-level grouped cross-validation for LAI and a plot-aware within-plot validation strategy for AGB, acknowledging the limited sample size and spatial dependence of samples. The results demonstrate that LAI can be estimated with reliable performance across all growth stages. The gap-fraction-based baseline model achieved RCV2 values of 0.743–0.919, while the best multivariate models yielded RCV2 values of 0.747–0.917 with low error metrics. In contrast, AGB estimation exhibited stronger stage dependence and lower overall performance, with the best test R2 ranging from 0.306 to 0.586 and relatively better performance observed at the booting and heading stages. Because the AGB results were evaluated under a plot-aware within-plot validation strategy, they should be interpreted as indicative of within-plot predictive performance rather than as evidence of fully plot-independent generalization. Notably, MLR frequently matched or exceeded the performance of machine learning models (RF and XGBoost) under limited-sample conditions, highlighting the advantage of using compact, physically interpretable predictor combinations. These findings suggest that a stage-aware modeling approach using LiDAR-derived structural features provides a useful basis for rice phenotyping, although the generalizability of these results across different cultivars and environments warrants further investigation.

title: Toward fish counting in large-scale aquaculture: a novel weakly supervised density estimation framework
abstract: Accurate estimation of fish quantity in dense aquaculture ponds is critical for optimizing feeding strategies, managing stocking density, and improving operational efficiency. However, dense fish schools present unique challenges: individual fish are often severely occluded, their boundaries are difficult to delineate, and the cost of obtaining location-level annotations is prohibitively high. These limitations hinder the scalability of fully supervised methods, particularly in practical large-scale pond aquaculture environments. To overcome these constraints, we propose a weakly supervised fish counting method based on density map regression, a common form of density estimation. The proposed method integrates a small number of location-level annotations with a large set of classification-level labels to guide the learning of robust and spatially coherent density map representations under limited supervision. As a form of weakly supervised learning, this approach significantly reduces annotation cost while maintaining high accuracy. To further improve model stability and structural fidelity, we introduce an auxiliary branch regularization framework and a decoupled training mechanism, which enhance multiscale consistency and mitigate supervision interference. We also construct a high-resolution dataset, Dense Feeding Scene Fish Image Dataset (DFS-FID), using unmanned aerial vehicle imagery captured during peak feeding periods in intensive aquaculture ponds. Experimental results show that our method outperforms representative fully and weakly supervised baselines such as CSRNet and CUT, achieving a mean absolute error of 47.3 and a root-mean-square error of 70.5 on DFS-FID. It also demonstrates strong generalization on the cross-domain dataset IOCfish5K and the cross-pond dataset FishAdapt-P3. The proposed method provides a scalable, noninvasive solution for density-based fish counting under weak supervision, offering practical value for intelligent aquaculture applications.

title: A layered domain adaptation method for wheat head detection via state–space hybridization and channel-guided cross-scale fusion
abstract: A core bottleneck for UAV remote sensing in precision agriculture is the performance degradation models face when transferred from standardized datasets to degraded field environments. Legitimate and common scenarios such as thin haze, airborne dust, sprinkler mist, and low sun angles at dawn or dusk frequently cause low-contrast and partially under-exposed imagery. These conditions weaken critical edge and texture features and amplify cross-domain discrepancies, posing a major generalization challenge. To overcome this, we propose a Layered Domain Adaptation (LDA) framework aimed at learning more degradation-robust feature representations. The framework integrates Selective State–Space Multiscale Convolutional Attention (SSMCA) modules into the detector backbone to enhance long-range dependencies and weak-texture representations, and employs a Channel-Guided Cross-Scale Fusion (CGAFusion) neck to stabilize localization. A synergistically optimized multi-granularity alignment strategy, including image- and instance-level adversarial learning, output and attention consistency, and contrastive regularization with semantic prototype supervision, collectively guides the learning process. For controlled evaluation, we constructed an unlabeled target domain with systematically simulated low-contrast and low-light conditions, to evaluate robustness under degradation-induced domain shift. In a transfer experiment from the GWHD dataset to this target domain, our framework increased AP@50:95 from 58.6% to 61.5% and AP@50 from 80.3% to 90.1%. These results demonstrate that proactively addressing common imaging degradations is an effective pathway to improving wheat head detection performance and model generalization under the present controlled degraded-domain benchmark.

title: A unified training framework with masked pixel–semantic reconstruction for agricultural image segmentation
abstract: Accurate agricultural image segmentation (AIS) is crucial for ensuring food security, enhancing agricultural production efficiency, and improving resource utilization. However, constrained by the seasonal nature of agricultural production, incomplete sensor networks, and the specialized nature of annotation, segmentation models trained under data-scarce conditions face challenges of overfitting and poor generalization capabilities. To enhance segmentation accuracy and generalization capabilities of existing models under existing labeled data, this study proposed a two-stage unified training framework for agricultural image segmentation models, named AgriSTF. The first stage employs the developed Masked Pixel-Semantic Reconstruction (MPSR) for self-supervised pretraining of the segmentation model’s encoder. The second stage utilizes labeled data for supervised fine-tuning of the segmentation model. MPSR defines the self-supervised proxy task as jointly predicting masked pixels and semantic tokens, establishing bidirectional constraints between local details and high-level semantics through a carefully designed Joint Decoder. Over 600 experiments conducted across five AIS tasks and seven representative baselines demonstrated that AgriSTF consistently improved baseline accuracy without requiring additional data, achieving competitive results even in settings utilizing only 50% of training epochs or only 50% of labeled data. Additionally, comprehensive ablation experiments were conducted to investigate the optimal hyperparameter settings for MPSR. AgriSTF is model agnostic and data efficient, providing a new approach for training under existing labeled data and showing the potential to become a foundational training paradigm for developing AIS models under limited-data conditions in the future. The code is available at: https://github.com/CAU-COE-VEICLab/AgriSTF.

title: Automated insect behavioral phenotyping with computer vision and deep learning: Current knowledge and future directions
abstract: Insect behavior refers to the observable actions and activity patterns of insects in response to internal physiological states and external environmental stimuli. Understanding and quantifying insect behavior can provide essential insights in many applications, including agriculture, ecology, neuroscience, and bioengineering. Although current computer vision and deep learning technologies have achieved remarkable progress in insect detection and recognition, their application in the quantitative analysis of insect behavior remains relatively limited. This article provides a comprehensive review of computer vision and deep learning technologies for insect behavior analysis, spanning application domains, research organisms, behavior categories, and adopted methods. The survey summarizes the methodological frameworks into spatial part location methods and spatiotemporal feature extraction methods, systematically examining their key components from video acquisition, data annotation, object tracking, to behavior quantification. In addition, representative approaches are analyzed and compared in terms of their strengths, limitations, and applicability under different experimental conditions. The survey also scrutinizes extant datasets and open-source platforms, offering a detailed explanation of dataset characteristics, annotation challenges, and factors affecting model generalizability. Finally, emerging research directions, including foundation models, self-supervised learning, and multimodal sensing for behavior analysis, are discussed to highlight potential opportunities for advancing the field of insect behavior studies.

title: An explainable SR-GAN and MobileNetV2 framework for aerial pest detection in precision agriculture
abstract: As pest problems in agriculture continue to grow, there is now greater demand for systems that can quickly spot them. It is common to use human scouts for spotting pests or standard machine-learning techniques, but they cannot easily process the low-resolution images taken by Unmanned Aerial Vehicles(UAVs). Using blurred or poor quality data in deep learning usually causes the model to miss some items and select the incorrect choice. To deal with the mentioned problems, this research combines Super-Resolution Generative Adversarial Network (SR-GAN) technology with a lightweight classifier called MobileNetV2 for more effective monitoring of aerial pests. The main function of the SR-GAN module is to transform UAV images with low resolution into ones with high resolution that keep important details of each pest. After improving the images, MobileNetV2 is used to classify them effectively and accurately. Trust in the framework is further increased by Grad-CAM which makes it clear which features of the input affect the prediction of the model. Images created using super-resolution are deemed visually better due to the boost in PSNR, SSIM and MSE. Classification tests show that the improved models have superior accuracy, graphs and analysis of important features. The method improved upon the base CNN by 18%, reaching a 92.6% rate of correct predictions. Moreover, the test results indicated that PSNR values were 5.2 dB higher than with the CNN. The proposed method has more consistent outputs and better behavior under varied farming conditions with Accuracy = 92.6%, Precision = 93.1%, Recall = 92.2%, F1 Score = 92.4%, Parameters = 2.3 M, FLOPs = 0.3G, Inference Time = 30 ms, which can effectively detect the pests even in occluded, shadow, or low-visibility cases. It combines various approaches and remedies the existing system problems, offering flexibility for immediate use in agriculture to help save crops and make pesticide use more efficient.

title: A robot herding strategy combining CMFF and MPC for shepherding
abstract: Agricultural robots are considered a key technological path to alleviate labor shortages, but existing applications are mostly focused on crop production, and research on herding scenarios is still relatively weak. To address the limited effectiveness of herd guidance and control in complex pastoral environments, as well as the lack of real-world validation for robotic herding, this paper proposes a robot herding strategy that integrates the collective motion flow field (CMFF) with model predictive control (MPC), enabling stable driving and guidance of non-cooperative herds. First, a coupled collective motion model of the heterogeneous multi-agent system is established based on the multi-machine collaborative herding platform, and a unified dynamical foundation is thereby provided for subsequent strategy design. Second, at the collective level, a guidance mechanism based on CMFF is formulated to characterize the global motion tendency of the herd and generate dynamic guidance cues. Next, at the robot level, a nonlinear MPC framework is introduced, in which the predicted herd evolution over the prediction horizon is incorporated into the optimization process. Constraint-satisfying optimal control actions are then planned to achieve anticipatory guidance of the herd. Simulation results demonstrate that at a herd size of 300, the success rate of the proposed strategy is 90 %, which is significantly higher than those of the three baseline methods. Compared with the V-formation push strategy, the robot travel distance is reduced by approximately 70 %, and the completion time steps are reduced by approximately 60 %. Meanwhile, the proposed strategy demonstrates strong adaptability to collective behaviors under different self-organization rules. Finally, real-world experiments further demonstrate the engineering feasibility. With appropriate parameter configuration, the real-world experiments of both scales achieve a 100 % success rate. Through the robustness analysis of the real-world experiments, it is confirmed that the proposed strategy can achieve stable and reliable herd guidance in complex pastoral environments, offering new insights and practical references for non-cooperative multi-agent guidance and robotic herding.

title: A physics-informed neural network for continuous rice canopy thermal monitoring and forecasting from sparse UAV observations
abstract: Continuous monitoring of canopy temperature (Tc), a key indicator of crop water-heat stress and physiological dynamics, using unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) imagery is inherently limited by temporal discontinuity and the limited physical realism of purely data-driven models. This study develops a physics-informed neural network (PINN) framework to transform temporally sparse UAV thermal observations into continuous hourly rice Tc reconstruction and 48 h forecasting products. The model leverages sparse UAV thermal measurements as supervisory signals while integrating them with continuous meteorological forcing and daily UAV-derived crop phenotypic features. Validated through a comprehensive season-long rice field experiment using walk-forward cross-validation, the proposed PINN framework demonstrated superior performance. It achieved R 2 values of 0.92 for reconstruction and 0.90 for forecasting, with RMSE of 0.71 °C and 0.82 °C, respectively. Ablation analysis further showed that crop phenotypic variables contributed more strongly than temporal descriptors, reducing predictive uncertainty by approximately 4.8–14.3 %, while the integration of SEB physical constraints and uncertainty modeling improved R 2 by 8.4–9.5 % and reduced Total STD by 28.4–37.7 %. The model successfully captures diurnal dynamics, spatial variability, and canopy thermal hysteresis while maintaining physical consistency through improved energy closure. This framework bridges sparse aerial observations with continuous physiological monitoring and highlights its potential to support precision irrigation, early stress detection, and high-throughput phenotyping in smart agriculture.

title: Modeling photosynthetically active radiation for crop suitability and yield potential assessment in building-integrated agriculture: a simulation–measurement framework
abstract: As climate change and urbanization intensify, there is an increasing need for computational tools that support crop planning and performance assessment in space-constrained urban environments. This study presents a simulation–measurement framework for modeling Photosynthetically Active Radiation (PAR) to enable quantitative crop suitability assessment and relative yield potential evaluation in building-integrated agriculture (BIA) within high-density tropical cities. The methodology integrates climate-based computational simulation with high-resolution environmental sensing and empirical benchmarking using in-situ PAR measurements collected in Singapore. Model validation demonstrates a strong level of agreement between simulated and measured data (Mean Absolute Error = 164.5 μmol·m⁻ 2 ·s⁻ 1 ), supporting the reliability of the approach as a benchmarking tool. The validated model is applied across multiple spatial scales, including the generation of Singapore’s first country-scale PAR maps based on Typical Meteorological Year (TMY) data, and building-scale analyses that incorporate three-dimensional urban morphology. Crop suitability and relative yield potential are derived by linking simulated light availability to literature-based crop light requirements and optimal production conditions in controlled environment agriculture. Yield indicators are interpreted as comparative performance metrics rather than absolute production forecasts. The proposed framework establishes a multi-scalar, sunlight-informed decision-support tool for crop selection and energy-efficient agricultural system design in complex urban environments.

title: Cattle behavior classification using Hidden Markov Models
abstract: The increasing demand for meat production necessitates more sustainable and data-driven livestock management practices. Precision Livestock Farming (PLF) leverages sensor technologies and computational methods to monitor individual animals, enhancing productivity and welfare. In this study, we use Hidden Markov Models (HMMs) to classify free-range cattle behavior using GPS and tri-axial accelerometer data collected from 22 Angus-based cows over a nine-week winter period in western Montana, USA. Following model validation, HMM-predicted behavioral states were used to examine large-scale behavioral patterns across the entire dataset. The analysis revealed pronounced diurnal activity cycles, temperature-dependent shifts in behavior, and significantly greater nighttime grazing activity during full moon periods. Generalized Linear Mixed Models (GLMMs) further demonstrated significant interactions between temperature and time of day, showing that cattle increasingly shifted grazing activity toward cooler periods as temperatures increased. These findings provide insight into how environmental conditions influence free-range cattle behavior and demonstrate the value of sensor-based monitoring for precision grazing management. To enable this analysis, we engineered four features; step size, turning angle, and the mean and variance of Signal Vector Magnitude (SVM), and used these in a three-state HMM to classify grazing, resting, and traveling behaviors. Model development was conducted using leave-one-out cross-validation to assess generalizability across individuals, achieving an average classification accuracy of 92.72%. Our findings demonstrate the utility of HMMs as robust, transparent, and computationally efficient tools for cattle behavior classification in extensive rangeland settings. The approach holds promise for real-time PLF applications such as early anomaly detection, resource allocation, and adaptive grazing management.

title: A generic framework for evaluating the effectiveness of bio-stabilization: Integrating data-driven and model-driven approaches
abstract: Single-dimensional assessments often fail to capture the coupled chemical and structural effects of bio-stabilization, defined here as biologically mediated soil strengthening and contaminant immobilization, on soil functionality. To address this limitation, this study develops an integrated framework to evaluate both the effectiveness and potential side effects of microbial-induced carbonate precipitation (MICP), a representative bio-stabilization technique based on microbially driven carbonate mineralization, at the pore scale. Multi-level and piecewise mixed-effects modeling demonstrates that MICP efficiency plays a dominant role in cadmium (Cd) immobilization and overall stabilization performance (β=−0.43,p<0.01). High-resolution micro-computed tomography (micro-CT) analysis shows that increasing bio-stabilization intensity reduces porosity from 51.0% to 46.9% and shifts the structural model index (SMI) from 2.111 to −2.617, accompanied by an increase in isolated pores and improved structural integrity. To overcome the limited data volume inherent to micro-CT imaging, a conditionally constrained deep generative model based on a conditional variational autoencoder and a Wasserstein generative adversarial network with gradient penalty (CVAE-WGAN-GP) is employed to support continuous analysis of pore-scale structural evolution. The results show that intensified bio-stabilization enhances anisotropy and pore network heterogeneity, while confining seepage to a few dominant flow channels, with potential implications for soil water retention and nutrient transport. Overall, the proposed framework provides a quantitative basis for optimizing bio-stabilization strategies and supporting risk-informed decision-making in sustainable soil remediation.

title: FHBSight: multimodal UAV-Based early detection of wheat fusarium head blight using sensitive vegetation indices and RGB phenotypic features
abstract: Fusarium head blight (FHB) is a destructive wheat disease that threatens grain yield, quality, and food safety. Early-stage FHB detection is critical for timely field management but remains challenging in UAV imagery because infected regions are often small, sparsely distributed, and weakly contrasted. In this study, early-stage FHB refers to the initial phase of visible symptom development, typically occurring approximately 8–14 days after infection onset, and characterized by slight spikelet discoloration and limited infection within wheat ears. Physiological stress responses associated with this stage may also precede clearly visible symptoms, providing a potential basis for vegetation-index-assisted (VI-assisted) detection. To address these challenges, this study proposes FHBSight, a UAV-based multimodal semantic segmentation framework that integrates RGB-derived phenotypic information with vegetation-index-derived (VI-derived) physiological cues for FHB detection. FHBSight adopts a dual-branch SeMask-FPN backbone to separately encode RGB spatial features and VI-based stress-sensitive representations. An Adaptive Cross-Modal Attention module dynamically reweights cross-modal features to reduce redundancy and enhance fine-grained lesion representation. A Joint Loss combining cross-entropy and Dice Loss is designed to improve sensitivity to small and early-stage lesions under severe lesion-background class imbalance. A UAV multispectral dataset containing 5,059 RGB images and 19 VI datasets was constructed for model evaluation. Experimental results showed that the anthocyanin reflectance index, normalized difference vegetation index, and green difference vegetation index provided relatively sensitive cues for FHB detection. Using these selected VIs, FHBSight achieved an mIoU of 73.01%, an mAcc of 86.17% and an mDice of 83.21%. Compared with the SegNeXt, FHBSight improved mIoU and mAcc by 1.25% and 6.34%, respectively. These results indicate that combining RGB imagery with compact VI-derived physiological information can improve early FHB detection under complex field conditions. The proposed framework provides a practical approach for UAV-based wheat disease detection and field-scale precision management.

title: A weed detection model based on dual-stream attention and multiscale contextual fusion
abstract: To address the limitations in detection accuracy of existing deep learning-based weed detection algorithms, particularly under conditions characterized by significant background complexity and target scale variation, this paper proposes an improved object detection model designated as DEA-YOLO11. First, a Dual-Stream Vision Network (DSV-Net) is introduced in place of the original backbone to strengthen the complementary extraction of shallow local textures and deep global contexts. Second, an Enhanced Receptive Field Module (ERFM) is designed to augment the model’s capability for capturing multiscale targets without compromising spatial resolution. Finally, an Adaptive Context Guided Fusion Module (ACGF) is constructed to replace the conventional concatenation operation, facilitating the dynamic suppression of background interference while actively promoting focus on target regions. Experimental results on a self-constructed Xinjiang Weed Dataset (XWD) demonstrate that the proposed DEA-YOLO11 achieves a mean Average Precision (mAP50) of 91.50% and an F1-Score of 88.10%, representing performance increments of 3.82 and 2.84 percentage points over the YOLOv11n baseline, respectively. Furthermore, evaluations conducted on multiple public benchmark datasets corroborate the model’s superior generalization capabilities. This research thus provides a robust implementation that attains a highly favorable balance between detection accuracy and operational efficiency, establishing it as a practical solution for real-time weed detection in complex agricultural environments.

title: Intelligent decision-making method for optimal maize seeding rate based on synergistic driving of multi-source field information
abstract: In variable-rate maize seeding, optimal seeding rate (OSR) decisions are jointly shaped by multiple interacting field factors, including climate, management, and soil conditions. However, the prevailing two-stage “yield prediction-optimal search” framework struggles to effectively capture the synergistic effects among heterogeneous features and is prone to error propagation and accumulation, thereby compromising decision stability. Meanwhile, the long duration of field trials and strong environmental disturbances lead to limited and unevenly distributed OSR ground-truth samples, further constraining predictive accuracy and generalization. Therefore, it is imperative to develop a multi-source, synergy-driven OSR decision-making approach tailored to small-sample scenarios. To this end, climatic variables, field management data, and soil organic matter (SOM) information covering interannual environmental variability were collected over four consecutive years under real-world maize production conditions. Based on these data, a Dual-dimension Adaptive Gating OSR Decision Network (DA-AGNet) was proposed. DA-AGNet incorporates multi-head self-attention, a dual-dimension weighting module, and a gated weighted aggregation mechanism to enable adaptive weighted fusion of multi-source inputs, thereby mitigating the adverse effects of noise in small-sample settings and enabling direct end-to-end prediction of OSR. To improve training stability under small-sample conditions, a coarse-to-fine yield-guided ladder training architecture (CF-YLTA) was constructed. CF-YLTA leverages a yield prediction model to generate pseudo-OSR data for coarse-stage pretraining of DA-AGNet and to initialize transferable prior weights, and then conducts fine-stage end-to-end training by combining these priors with data-augmented OSR ground-truth samples, thus improving prediction accuracy and generalizability. For yield predictor selection, multiple machine learning algorithms were benchmarked, and gradient boosting decision trees (GBDT) achieved the best performance, with the root mean square error (RMSE) of 360.71 kg/ha, a mean absolute error (MAE) of 248.70 kg/ha, and R2 of 0.88. DA-AGNet trained using CF-YLTA delivered the best OSR prediction on the test set (RMSE = 1646.64 seeds/ha, MAE = 1247.96 seeds/ha, R2 = 0.74), outperforming conventional approaches overall. Qualitative analysis of the predicted OSR indicated an S-shaped increasing trend as SOM increased, which can be partitioned into a low-OSR plateau (SOM 16–25 g/kg), a rapid-increase region (SOM 25–37.5 g/kg), and a high-OSR plateau (SOM 37.5–44 g/kg), consistent with established agronomic understanding. To evaluate model effectiveness, the variable-rate seeding prescriptions derived from DA-AGNet were compared with constant low- and high-density seeding schemes, and the variable-rate strategy showed a yield advantage. Overall, the proposed OSR decision model provides reliable intelligent decision support for determining maize OSR in variable-rate seeding operations under varying crop growth environments.

title: Integrated collaborative iterative optimization of energy management and parameters for hydrogen fuel cell tractors
abstract: Due to the highly dynamic and heavy-duty nature of tractor operations, the hydrogen fuel cell tractor (HFCT) currently face critical challenges regarding energy sustainability and inefficient energy consumption, with existing research remaining in the preliminary exploration stage. To address these issues, this paper proposes a parameter-coordinated iterative optimization framework for the HFCT. First, a calculation method for the continuous operating time of the HFCT is proposed based on tractor operational characteristics, which serves as the basis for the parameter matching of key powertrain components. Then, a near-optimal control algorithm (NOCA) strategy is developed to balance energy economy with system durability. This strategy is achieved by training the results derived from dynamic programming, enabling the near-optimal power allocation for online execution. To avoid redundant design cycles and maximize overall system performance, a multi-objective parameter optimization framework driven by parameter sensitivity is established. In this framework, core design variables are identified through Sobol sensitivity analysis, In this framework, core design variables are identified through Sobol sensitivity analysis, and multi-objective optimization—targeting the minimization of the full life-cycle cost and comprehensive energy consumption—is conducted using the NOCA strategy as the performance evaluation core and the proposed improved non-dominated sorting whale optimization algorithm (INSWOA) as the outer-loop solver. Finally, the proposed method is validated through hardware-in-the-loop testing and field experiments. Experimental results demonstrate significant improvements in energy economy, operational efficiency, and system durability. Specifically, field plowing tests show that the proposed strategy and optimization method increase operational efficiency by 7.45%, reduce equivalent hydrogen consumption by 9.78%, and mitigate the degradation rates of the fuel cell and battery pack by 29.18% and 10.95%, respectively. This research provides a robust theoretical foundation for the design and optimization of HFCT powertrain systems.

title: Learning adversarial augmentation policies for robust garlic seedling detection
abstract: Accurate seedling detection during early growth stages is essential for timely replanting and effective crop management in precision agriculture. However, existing studies are mostly evaluated under relatively stable imaging conditions, such as UAV imagery or greenhouse environments, leaving robust detection under severe and spatially heterogeneous illumination in ground-based outdoor monitoring insufficiently explored. In addition, many illumination-robust detection methods rely on additional enhancement or feature-extraction modules, which increase inference-time overhead and are not tailored to seedling detection and downstream missing seedling localization. To address these gaps, we construct a new garlic seedling dataset captured using a ground-based monitoring platform under real outdoor field conditions with highly variable illumination. We further propose an illumination-robust seedling detection framework based on adversarial augmentation policy learning. The proposed method jointly optimizes a stochastic augmentation policy agent and an object detector, enabling the detector to learn robust representations under challenging visual conditions. A structural penalty is introduced to prevent unrealistic distortions while encouraging challenging augmentations during training. Extensive experiments show that the proposed approach achieves an AP$_{50}$ of 91.6%, improving the baseline by 0.9 percentage points and outperforming the previous best-performing method by 0.2 percentage points. For downstream missing seedling localization, it achieves 75.0% precision and a 67.0% F1-score, improving the baseline by 4.8 and 2.0 percentage points, respectively. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework for practical ground-based agricultural monitoring under complex outdoor lighting conditions without additional inference-time computational overhead.

title: Field-scale assessment of ridging operation quality using UAV LiDAR point clouds
abstract: Ridge tillage in cold regions improves soil hydrothermal conditions and drainage, but its agronomic effectiveness and compatibility with mechanized operations depend on whether ridge geometry satisfies field-scale operational specifications. In practice, ridging operation quality (ROQ) assessment still relies heavily on labor-intensive and spatially sparse manual inspections. This study reformulated field-scale ROQ assessment as a ridge-support construction problem and developed a UAV LiDAR-based framework to construct valid ridge-wise supports from ridge-furrow microtopography, estimate ridge width, ridge height, and ridge-top width, and generate indicator-level and overall qualification maps. The framework integrates residual microtopographic representation, ridge-oriented normalization, and continuity-constrained furrow tracking to suppress broad-scale terrain variation, standardize cross-sectional profiles, and maintain furrow correspondence across adjacent segments. Validation against 100 field samples yielded MAEs of 0.027 m, 0.014 m, and 0.021 m for ridge width, ridge height, and ridge-top width, respectively, with corresponding qualification accuracies of 0.91, 0.88, and 0.96. Under the full framework, ridge-wise supports remained structurally stable, with a continuity ratio of 95.81% and a support invalid ratio of 3.03%. Component ablation and orientation perturbation analyses showed that residual representation primarily affected geometric accuracy, whereas tracking and orientation consistency governed support continuity, indexing stability, and width-related indicator reliability. These results indicate that reliable field-scale ROQ assessment in the studied post-ridging setting depends on both local geometric accuracy and structurally valid ridge supports. The framework provides an ROQ-specific support-construction approach for field-scale assessment in post-ridging cold-region fields, while broader evaluation across additional scenarios remains necessary.

title: Occlusion-aware pinching point positioning using shoot morphology for robotic summer pruning of kiwifruit
abstract: Pinching is a summer pruning practice in kiwifruit cultivation that involves permanently removing the shoot’s growing tip after the distal bud. Automating this practice requires accurate positioning of pinching points, which remains challenging due to dense canopies and variability in shoot type. This study proposed a novel automated method for positioning pinching points by combining YOLO11s-seg for segmenting branches and shoots with a morphology-guided kiwifruit pinching point positioning algorithm (KPPPA). KPPPA integrated two sequential sub-algorithms: the direction-aware mask mending (MaskMend) reconstructed the occlusion-induced fragmented mask of shoots by estimating the local search direction for candidate reconnection extreme endpoints; then, proportion-based point locating (PPL) utilized the reconstructed mask for computing shoot geometric features to distinguish non-terminating from terminating shoots and ultimately position optimal pinching points. Experimental results show that YOLO11s-seg model achieved a mean average precision of 91.7% for detection and 61.1% for mask segmentation, while KPPPA positioned pinching points obtaining success rate of 87.0% and Average Euclidean error of 5.8 pixels with Mean absolute errors of 3.6 and 2.7 pixels along x, and y-axis, respectively. The findings of the study show that the proposed method can effectively position pinching points for kiwifruit in summer at a minimal computation speed of 136.6 ms per frame, making it feasible for real-time robotic pinching operation in kiwifruit orchards.

title: Robust multimodal fusion for terrain perception and autonomous robot navigation in unstructured agricultural environments
abstract: Autonomous navigation of agricultural robots faces persistent challenges in unstructured environments, including canopy occlusion, specular reflections from pooled water, and ridge-induced platform vibrations that cause temporally varying sensor degradation. Existing multimodal systems fail to maintain both reliability and real-time responsiveness, while accurate delineation of safety–critical classes (especially waterlogged zones) and the direct translation of perceptual quality into navigational safety remain key bottlenecks. We present a lightweight real-time adaptive multimodal perception system that establishes a complete perception–planning closed loop. Built on MobileNetV3-U-Net-Lite, the architecture integrates (1) six-channel early RGB–LiDAR fusion for deep cross-modal complementarity from the shallowest layers, (2) stepwise collaborative filtering with learnable anisotropic boundary weights supervised by a composite CE + Dice + boundary loss to handle directional terrain margins and low-frequency safety–critical classes, and (3) a 10-dimensional physical state vector (IMU vibration signatures + RGB illumination descriptors) that drives an MLP-based dynamic modality weighting mechanism reinforced by physical-consistency regularization. The fused output generates a quantitative risk map encoding slope, surface undulation, water-accumulation probability, and vegetation obscuration, which directly feeds the Agri Path planner for risk-guided path refinement and global map accumulation. Deployed on the NVIDIA Jetson Orin NX, the system achieves 47 FPS with 3.4 M parameters and 7.8 W power consumption. On the RELLIS-3D benchmark it attains 62.56 % mIoU, 40.42 % puddle IoU, and boundary F1 scores exceeding all baselines. Field trials at Xihua University demonstrate a 91.7 % improvement in minimum safe distance over the IMU-ablated baseline and reduction of peak yaw-rate to 37.5 % of the control group. These results demonstrate a viable pathway toward physically grounded, temporally adaptive safety navigation: shifting from static precision-centric fusion to physically grounded, temporally adaptive, risk-quantified safety navigation under tight edge-computing constraints. Field validation under dusk post-irrigation conditions confirms system robustness under compound sensor degradation; the proposed mechanisms demonstrate strong potential for transfer to orchards, vegetable fields, and wheat croplands, subject to further validation under full nocturnal and adverse-weather conditions.

title: Riemannian geometry–based structured modeling of excitation–emission matrix fluorescence for nondestructive single-kernel maize seed viability assessment
abstract: Reliable and nondestructive assessment of seed viability is essential for seed quality control, yet conventional optical sensing methods often provide limited biochemical and structural information. This study used excitation–emission matrix (EEM) fluorescence spectroscopy to characterize aging-related fluorescence changes in single maize kernels and developed a Riemannian geometry-based framework to extract structured spectral features. In this framework, each EEM was represented as a symmetric positive definite covariance matrix by calculating covariance relationships among emission wavelengths along the excitation dimension, followed by tangent-space embedding for compact feature generation. EEM analysis showed that accelerated aging induced a fluorescence transition from short-wavelength phenolic-related emission to enhanced long-wavelength emission associated with oxidative deterioration and lipid peroxidation. Compared with flattened EEM and DINOv2-derived features, the proposed Riemannian framework more effectively captured this structured fluorescence variation, achieving 88.24 % accuracy for six-level aging-duration classification, an R2 of 0.7985 for malondialdehyde (MDA) content prediction, and 92.31 % accuracy for viability discrimination. Correlation and perturbation analyses further identified long-wavelength EEM regions as key contributors to MDA prediction and viability discrimination. Overall, this study provides a biochemically interpretable and structurally robust fluorescence-based strategy for nondestructive seed viability assessment.

title: Enhancing soil organic matter prediction by Decoupling soil moisture effects with a conditional generative adversarial network
abstract: Soil moisture significantly affects soil spectral reflectance, and its high variability severely undermines the accuracy of soil organic matter (SOM) prediction. To address this issue, soil samples were collected from northern and northeastern China to construct three independent datasets. A deep generative model, Wet Spectrum to Dry Spectrum (Wet2dry) was then developed to capture the structural characteristics of one-dimensional spectral features. On this basis, three moisture-correction methods—Direct Standardization (DS), External Parameter Orthogonalization (EPO), and Wet2dry—with three SOM prediction models: Random Forest, Transformer, and SE-Transformer were systematically compared. Results show that the Wet2dry method effectively eliminates moisture interference and improves SOM prediction accuracy, offering a robust solution for soil property spectral inversion under high moisture variability. In SOM prediction tasks, the SE-Transformer model, which integrates the Squeeze-and-Excitation (SE) attention mechanism, exhibited stronger responsiveness to critical spectral bands. When combined with the Wet2dry correction model, the SE-Transformer consistently achieved excellent prediction performance across different moisture levels (5%, 10%, 15%), with R2 > 0.75 and RPD > 2. This study extends image-generation network architectures to one-dimensional spectral modeling, providing a feasible solution for stable SOM prediction under moisture interference.

title: Evolution of intelligent nitrogen management systems: a two-decade global research analysis
abstract: Intelligent nitrogen management systems integrating robotics, remote sensing and artificial intelligence (AI) have emerged as critical components of smart agriculture to address climate variability, soil degradation and increasing food production demands. Conventional uniform nitrogen fertilizer applications often fail to account for spatial and temporal variability in soil and crop conditions, resulting in reduced nitrogen use efficiency (NUE) and environmental risks such as nitrogen losses, greenhouse gas emissions and nutrient leaching. Despite substantial advancements in digital technologies for precision nitrogen management (PNM), a comprehensive quantitative synthesis of global research trends and thematic evolution remains limited. This study presents a two-decade bibliometric analysis (2004–2024) to evaluate the development, research structure and collaboration patterns in AI, remote sensing and robotics enabled nitrogen management. A refined dataset of 369 research articles was extracted from the Web of Science database and analysed using the bibliometrix R package and VOSviewer for performance indicators, co-occurrence networks, thematic mapping and temporal evolution. Results indicate a steady annual growth rate of 11.61%, reflecting expanding global interest in computational nitrogen management systems. The United States, China and Canada emerged as leading contributors. Early research focused primarily on canopy reflectance and nitrogen management zones, whereas recent studies emphasize machine learning, hyperspectral imaging, UAV-based crop nitrogen monitoring and autonomous nitrogen application systems. Thematic clustering revealed a clear transition from diagnostic approaches toward predictive and prescriptive frameworks integrating sensing, modeling and robotic actuation. Overall, the findings highlight the rapid evolution of intelligent nitrogen management technologies and provide strategic insights to guide future research, innovation and sustainable agricultural intensification.

title: An integrated free-space microwave transmission-based measuring system for non-destructive prediction sensing of moisture content and bulk density in wheat
abstract: Moisture content and bulk density are critical parameters for wheat storage, handling, and post-harvest quality management. Measuring both rapidly and without damaging the grain remains a practical challenge. This study presents an integrated free-space microwave transmission-based measurement system for the simultaneous and non-destructive prediction of moisture content and bulk density in wheat. The system uses synchronized RF/LO operation, direct intermediate-frequency sampling, and Fast Fourier Transform-based vector processing to extract the attenuation and phase shift of microwave signals transmitted through wheat samples over the 2–4 GHz frequency range. From these transmission parameters, the dielectric constant (ε′), loss factor (ε″), and loss tangent (tanδ) were calculated and used, together with attenuation and phase shift, as model inputs. Four wheat cultivars widely grown in Türkiye, namely Bezostaya, İkizce, Kenanbey, and Tosunbey, were evaluated over four harvest years under varying moisture content and bulk density conditions, producing a dataset of 2,420 experimental trials. Thirteen regression algorithms were evaluated under single-frequency, reference-frequency, and multi-frequency scenarios. The results revealed a strong dependence of prediction performance on operating frequency. For moisture content prediction, the highest test performance was obtained at 3900 MHz using SVR-RBF (R2 = 0.9433, RMSE = 0.4505), followed by TabPFN-v2 (R2 = 0.9404, RMSE = 0.4621) and EBM (R2 = 0.9370, RMSE = 0.4751). For bulk density prediction, the best single-frequency performance was achieved at 3400 MHz with SVR-RBF (R2 = 0.8342, RMSE = 0.0137), closely followed by TabPFN-v2 (R2 = 0.8331, RMSE = 0.0138) and EBM (R2 = 0.8239, RMSE = 0.0141). These results demonstrate that the dielectric signatures captured by the developed free-space microwave transmission system contain sufficient information to predict moisture content and bulk density. The proposed system offers a compact, non-contact, and non-destructive sensing framework with potential for future sensor-level applications in post-harvest grain quality monitoring.

title: Boosting cough recognition of livestock animals in farming environments through parameter-efficient tuning of multimodal audio pre-trained models
abstract: Deep learning-based acoustic sensing has significantly advanced the early detection of respiratory diseases in livestock. However, most existing models remain species-specific and rely heavily on manually labeled data, limiting their scalability and generalization across heterogeneous livestock farming environments. In this study, a novel multimodal approach for cough recognition (MAP-DA) across pigs and calves was proposed by integrating waveform-guided multimodal audio pre-training with dense-adapter-based efficient adaptation. During pre-training, the multimodal audio pre-training (MAP) framework exploited complementary information from Mel spectrograms and waveforms, learning robust animal vocalization features. During fine-tuning, dense-adapter (DA) tuning enabled efficient downstream adaptation through densely connected lightweight adapters. The results showed that MAP learned robust feature representations and consistently outperformed evaluated state-of-the-art audio pre-training paradigms, demonstrating the value of multimodal audio representation learning in acoustically complex farming environments DA-tuning effectively translated the learned animal vocalization knowledge into more accurate cough recognition by strengthening feature reuse and task-specific refinement. MAP-DA achieved accuracy values of 92.32% in pigs and 98.34% in calves, surpassing evaluated state-of-the-art cough recognition approaches. Importantly, MAP-DA benefited from joint downstream fine-tuning on larger and more diverse labeled datasets, achieving superior performance compared with the corresponding specialist models and demonstrating the potential as a generalist model across the evaluated livestock animals. Besides, MAP-DA demonstrated its ability to reduce dependence on manual annotation, achieving an accuracy of 90.90% with only 5% of the labeled training samples. This study provides a promising basis for developing scalable acoustic monitoring methods for livestock respiratory health in acoustically complex farming environments.

title: Precision agriculture meets explainable AI: A highly competitive ET0 prediction framework based on hybrid deep learning
abstract: Accurate prediction of reference crop evapotranspiration (ET0) is crucial for smart agriculture and efficient water resource management. However, the strong non-linearity and non-stationarity of ET0 time series pose significant challenges to existing prediction models. To overcome current limitations in prediction accuracy, this study designs and implements an enhanced hybrid deep learning architecture (E-CBT: Enhanced CNN-BiLSTM-Transformer) combined with Discrete Wavelet Transform (DWT) preprocessing, forming the DWT-E-CBT framework aimed at capturing complex multi-scale spatiotemporal dependencies within ET0 time series. This architecture integrates three optimized components: a deep convolutional network with residual connections, a stacked layer-normalized bidirectional long short-term memory network (BiLSTM), and an advanced Transformer encoder employing a Pre-norm structure. Notably, we introduce a multi-head attention pooling mechanism to replace traditional pooling methods. We rigorously compared the performance of the E-CBT model with various baseline models under a range of signal decomposition preprocessing techniques. Experimental results demonstrate that signal decomposition techniques significantly improve prediction accuracy, with discrete wavelet transform (DWT) performing optimally in providing input for the E-CBT model.
