Ultimately, the proposed DWT-E-CBT framework exhibits superior prediction performance, achieving highly competitive performance within a comprehensive benchmarking framework for ET0 prediction. The coefficient of determination (R2) reaches 98.99%, while the root mean square error (RMSE) and mean absolute error (MAE) are as low as 0.1655 mm·day⁻1 and 0.1125 mm·day⁻1, respectively. Through SHAP explainability analysis, we further reveal the model’s decision-making process and identify key driving factors for ET0 prediction. The DWT-E-CBT framework proposed in this study provides a novel and powerful paradigm for complex time series prediction, demonstrating significant application potential in precision irrigation.

title: Physics-Informed hybrid path planning for standardized orchard Navigation: A parameter space learning paradigm via Dual-Head Networks
abstract: Standardized orchard navigation requires path planners to balance safety, smoothness, and kinematic feasibility under narrow-row and semi-structured operating conditions. To address the limitations of conventional search-based methods, artificial potential field (APF)-based methods, and end-to-end learning methods, this paper proposes a physics-informed hybrid path-planning framework. The core idea lies in a parameter-space learning paradigm, in which a neural network predicts the key physical parameters of the APF, while the final trajectory is generated by a physics-based executor, thereby enhancing both adaptability and interpretability. To further coordinate global path consistency and local obstacle avoidance, a dual-head architecture is designed to decouple direction prediction from APF parameter adaptation. In addition, a two-stage training strategy that combines supervised warm-up with reinforcement fine-tuning is introduced to improve physical consistency and dynamic smoothness. Experimental results on more than 400 benchmark maps demonstrate that the proposed method achieves a 100 % success rate, together with stable safety margins and a Mean Jerk of 0.0072 rad. Ablation studies, Gazebo simulations, dynamic obstacle-avoidance tests, and real-world orchard experiments further verify the robustness and deployment potential of the proposed framework for safe and smooth autonomous navigation in complex orchard environments.

title: Mitigating occlusion: a spatial-aware diffusion model for pose estimation in quadrupedal livestock
abstract: In livestock management, accurately capturing pose changes in quadrupedal livestock is crucial for disease prediction and behavioral analysis. However, due to inter-animal occlusion and obstructions from farming facilities, livestock in practical farming environments are often partially visible, making pose estimation highly challenging. Existing livestock-specific pose estimation models and transferred human pose estimation frameworks are limited by fixed structural constraints and insufficient discrimination of highly similar livestock features, resulting in inaccurate localization and missed detections of body keypoints under occlusion conditions. To address these issues, this paper proposes SADPose, a Spatial-Aware Diffusion Model for pose estimation in quadrupedal livestock. The proposed framework combines noise-guided pose generation with hybrid-scale spatial constraints to improve robustness under severe occlusion. Specifically, a Hybrid-Scale Graph Convolutional Network is embedded into the diffusion framework to model local and global skeletal relationships. During the forward diffusion stage, the model constructs a feature space covering diverse livestock pose distributions, while the reverse denoising process progressively suppresses interference through multi-scale feature fusion, thereby reducing localization bias and missed detections of occluded keypoints. Experiments on two public datasets involving representative quadrupedal livestock species demonstrate that SADPose significantly outperforms existing methods in occlusion scenarios, improving keypoint localization accuracy and overall pose estimation performance in complex occlusion scenarios.

title: Key behavior recognition with tracking for brooding layer breeder chick based on RTM-BHJ
abstract: Monitoring the behavior of layer breeder chicks during the brooding period is critical for evaluating their welfare and health status. However, high chick density, frequent occlusions, and rapid fine-grained movements make automated monitoring challenging. To address these issues, this study introduces RTM-BHJ, a real-time framework for multi-chick monitoring based on RTMDet and SlowFast. The framework integrates a Body–Head Joint (BHJ) detector, the NorFast tracker, which combines NorFair-v2 and FastReID, and a SlowFast-based Tracking-Motivated Behavior Recognition (SF-TMBR) model. The BHJ detector incorporates a novel detection head optimized by DSC, DA-SPP-Lite, and Flash Layer to improve detection accuracy while maintaining computational efficiency. For tracking, FastReID extracts discriminative appearance features from a pre-trained model. In addition, the temporal aggregation of detected head features along tracked trajectories enhances feature representation for recognizing key behaviors with rapid motion. Experiments across four chick age groups showed that the proposed framework achieved strong detection and tracking performance, with an mMR −2 of 20.8%, a HOTA score of 66.8%, and 272 identity switches. For behavior recognition, the SF-TMBR model achieved AP scores of 78.3% for preening and 72.1% for pecking, and improved Frame-mAP and Video-mAP by 3.9% and 3.8%, respectively, compared with the original SlowFast network. These results demonstrate that RTM-BHJ provides an effective and practical solution for intelligent monitoring of layer breeder chicks during the brooding period.

title: LEGDeeplab: A lightweight edge-guided model for semantic segmentation of maize leaf rust
abstract: Maize leaf rust, a typical fungal disease, causes significant yield losses. Semantic segmentation of maize leaf rust in field images remains challenging due to complex background interference, sparse and small lesions, blurred boundaries, and deployment constraints on mobile or edge devices. To better address these issues, this study develops LEGDeeplab, a lightweight edge-guided semantic segmentation framework through a task-oriented redesign of DeepLabv3+. The framework adopts a parallel encoder consisting of an edge-aware branch and a main feature extraction network. The edge-aware branch provides low-cost boundary priors for lesion boundary modeling, while the main branch uses ResNet18 as the backbone and incorporates depthwise separable convolutions along with effective feature enhancement modules, including LskBlock, AGCA, and a simplified ScConv. An edge fusion attention (EFA) module is further introduced to strengthen the integration of edge cues and semantic features. In the decoder, multi-level features are progressively fused to improve lesion representation under complex field conditions. Experiments were conducted on a self-built maize leaf rust dataset containing 743 images. The experimental results show that, on the validation set, LEGDeeplab achieves superior overall performance compared with the ResNet18-based DeepLabv3+ baseline and the comparison models. The proposed model achieves 88.67% mIoU and 72.44% lesion IoU, exceeding the baseline by 4.25 and 7.84 percentage points, respectively, with only 1.56M parameters (9.73% of the baseline) and 14.20 GFLOPs. Five-fold cross-validation showed stable performance, with mIoU ranging from 87.90% to 88.88%. Evaluations on three external datasets and feature visualizations of original field images further confirm the model’s robustness in complex real-world scenarios, supporting precision management of maize leaf rust.

title: A process-based mechanistic modeling framework for soil–plant zinc dynamics and rice zinc biofortification
abstract: Zinc (Zn) deficiency remains a major challenge for both crop productivity and human nutrition, and rice is a key target for Zn biofortification. To support mechanism-based Zn management, this study developed a coupled Rice Zinc Dynamics Model (RZDM) by integrating WOFOST, HYDRUS-1D, and a Zn translocation-remobilization module, with field experiments used for model calibration and evaluation. Field data were collected from 17 plots representing unique variety-fertilizer-method combinations rather than independent experimental replicates, testing three rice varieties (Huanghuazhan, 99-25, and Nanjing-9108) and three zinc fertilizers (ZnSO4⋅H2O, Zn-EDTA, and zinc sugar alcohol chelate (Zn-SA)) under two application methods (soil and foliar). Field evidence indicated that foliar Zn application outperformed soil application for grain Zn enrichment, with Zn-SA and ZnSO4⋅H2O generally showing higher effectiveness than Zn-EDTA. RZDM achieved satisfactory performance for crop growth indicators (R2 = 0.45–0.96) and crop Zn content (R2 = 0.57–0.96), though soil Zn concentrations showed limited predictive accuracy(R2 = −0.87), indicating its utility for quantifying Zn transport and allocation across the soil–plant–grain continuum. Under the conditions of this study, scenario simulations suggested that weekly foliar ZnSO4⋅H2O or Zn-SA application starting one week after flowering showed potential to improve grain Zn concentration, while requiring further validation across broader environments. This work provides a process-based modeling framework for hypothesis-driven design of rice Zn biofortification strategies.

title: Estimating plant density of maize across the growing season via dynamic fusion of UAV-based multimodal data
abstract: Plant density is a key indicator in maize breeding for evaluating the density tolerance of varieties, assessing yield potential, and selecting ideal plant types. However, in the later stages of maize growth, the leaves of the plants cover each other, which affects the accuracy of the unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) estimation of plant density. A Dynamic Dense Adaptive Feature Fusion Network (DS-Net) based on UAV hyperspectral imagery(HSI) and Light Detection and Ranging (LiDAR) multimodal data is proposed for estimating plant density during the growing seasons of maize. The UAV multimodal dataset was collected from the maize inbred-line experiments at different sites over two growing seasons. The maize plant density across multiple growth stages exhibited a good relationship with hyperspectral features and point cloud density. DS-Net achieved a coefficient of determination (R2) of 0.923 and a root mean square error (RMSE) of 0.268 plants/m2 on the internal validation set. Ablation tests further confirmed the contribution of the proposed multimodal dynamic fusion strategy to estimation accuracy. The model was further evaluated using an independent 2023 dataset from Xinji, Hebei Province. On this external dataset, DS-Net achieved an R2 of 0.737, indicating a certain degree of inter-annual transferability under comparable acquisition protocols and agro-climatic conditions. Overall, DS-Net provided a stage-aware multimodal framework for UAV-based maize plant density estimation and offered a potential tool for crop phenotyping across the growth stage.
keywords: Dynamic Dense Adaptive Feature Fusion Network

title: Decoupled active in-row following strategy for collaborative tobacco-harvesting robots based on ultra-wideband localization and visual perception
abstract: In hilly tobacco-growing regions, a collaborative mode involving manual harvesting and robotic transportation provides a practical solution, as it combines human expertise in maturity assessment with mechanized transport. However, when a transport robot follows a farm worker in narrow inter-row corridors with dense occlusion and uneven terrain, the system may suffer from unstable speed switching, cumulative lateral deviation, and row-departure risks. These problems arise because longitudinal following and lateral safety are not explicitly decoupled, while localization alone cannot provide sufficient environmental constraints. To address these challenges, this study proposes a decoupled active in-row following strategy that integrates ultra-wideband (UWB) localization and vision-based perception. The following task is decomposed into longitudinal decision-making and lateral safety-constraint enforcement. These two components were implemented separately at the control-command level to reduce the mutual influence of multiple information sources. For longitudinal control, we adopted a single-anchor-single-tag UWB configuration, in which phase difference of arrival (PDOA)-based angle estimation and double-sided two-way ranging (DS-TWR) were jointly used to estimate the relative human–robot pose and derive the longitudinal relative distance. An extended Kalman filter (EKF) was combined with a hysteresis-based Stop-Slow-Follow finite-state machine (FSM) to achieve stable state transitions and speed regulation. For lateral safety, we developed a vision-based constraint method to monitor row-departure and ridge-collision risks, and enable adaptive heading correction. A lightweight Stalk-YOLO network (YOLO: You-Only-Look-Once) was used for real-time tobacco-stalk detection, while row boundaries and the inter-row centerline were estimated through root-feature extraction, clustering, and random sample consensus (RANSAC) fitting. Field experiments showed that the proposed strategy improved both relative localization stability and lateral safety. EKF filtering reduced the UWB ranging root mean square error (RMSE) from 0.056–0.156 to 0.020–0.045 m, while the vision-based lateral estimation achieved a mean navigation-line deviation of 3.43 px and a mean heading-angle error of 0.302°. In 30-m full-system field trials, visual lateral constraints reduced manual interventions by 83.3% and severe ridge-collision events by 71.5%. These results demonstrate that the proposed UWB-vision perception framework and decoupled following strategy can achieve stable longitudinal following, while improving lateral safety during human–robot collaborative tobacco harvesting.

title: Drone adoption and farm performance in smallholder rice farming: Evidence of adoption without adaptation from Vietnam’s Mekong Delta
abstract: While agricultural drones have demonstrated technical benefits in controlled experiments, their real-world adoption patterns and performance among smallholders remain underexplored. This study examines drone uptake and its economic impacts on rice farmers in Vietnam’s Mekong Delta, where commercial drone services have expanded rapidly in recent years. Using panel data from 756 seasonal observations across 387 households over six rice cropping seasons from 2022 to 2024, we employ generalised linear models and generalised linear mixed models to examine adoption determinants and linear mixed-effects models to assess farm performance outcomes. Results show that drone adoption is primarily determined by structural factors, farm size and local service availability, rather than farmer characteristics, such as education or training, whose effects are conditional on operational scale and disappear once household-level heterogeneity is accounted for. Drone adopters achieved modest yield (1.9%) and revenue (3.3%) gains, especially on smaller farms; however, higher spraying costs entirely offset these gains, resulting in no net improvement in profitability. Drone use did not reduce pesticide or fertiliser expenditures, revealing an “adoption without adaptation” pattern where technology uptake occurs largely without corresponding adjustments to input management practices. Additionally, larger farms adopt drones more readily, yet productivity and revenue benefits are concentrated on smaller farms, a structural paradox in technology diffusion. Since adoption alone does not ensure economic benefits, policies should bundle drone services with agronomic guidance and invest in cooperative-based delivery models to improve accessibility. Grounded in actual farming systems, this study advances evidence-based understanding of digital agricultural technology adoption under real-world conditions.

title: Estimating fine-scale soil moisture content and wheat yield in drought-heterogeneous farmlands using machine learning regressions on multispectral UAV imagery
abstract: With the development of precision agriculture, soil moisture content (SMC), a key factor affecting wheat yield, requires efficient and near real-time monitoring at the field scale. This study applies soil line indices derived from unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) multispectral imagery to estimate fine-scale SMC and wheat yield in two farmlands with distinct spatial SMC distributions (i.e., farmland drought heterogeneity) in Kinmen, Taiwan. By comparing traditional linear regression with several machine learning approaches, including support vector regression (SVR), gradient boosting regression (GBR), and convolutional neural network regression (CNNR), key indices contributing to SMC and yield estimation across different wheat growth stages were identified. The results indicate that both SMC and wheat yield can be reasonably explained when significant farmland drought heterogeneity is present. Linear regression achieved optimal coefficients of determination (p < 0.01) of 0.65 for SMC using the perpendicular vegetation index and 0.93 for wheat yield using the normalized difference vegetation index. Areas with higher SMC within a farmland were found to negatively affect wheat growth. Among the machine learning models, GBR and CNNR based on the selected indices (VAPDI and NDVI, respectively) achieved estimation accuracies of 98.0 % and 72.2 %, respectively, for total wheat yield across the two experimental farmlands. Temporal validation across different growing cycles suggests the potential for cross-year wheat yield prediction. Deviations from expected estimation patterns may be considered preliminary indicators of abnormal yield conditions, and early-stage yield estimation shows promising potential. Overall, these findings provide preliminary evidence for early-stage yield prediction and offer valuable insights for optimizing irrigation timing and enhancing the development of AI-driven agricultural decision support systems.

title: Multi-sensor point cloud analysis for canopy volume estimation in a steep-slope Mediterranean vineyard: a comparison of LiDAR and RGB approaches
abstract: Volumetric analysis of tree canopies is increasingly important for farmers 4.0, as it enables the adoption of targeted agricultural practices. Additionally, the recent European and Mediterranean Plant Protection Organization (EPPO) guideline introduced a new labelling system for plant protection products based on biometric indices as references to express the dose. Currently, conventional manual methods used for volumetric assessments are generally time-consuming. The present study aimed to undertake a comparative analysis of canopy volumes derived from various combinations of monitoring technologies and analytical methods applied to the point cloud, in conjunction with reference volumes obtained from manual measurements, within a highly complex scenario like the Mediterranean steep-slope vineyard. The technologies tested for UAV monitoring included LiDAR, low and high cost RGB cameras, whilst terrestrial monitoring was carried out with terrestrial LiDAR (GeoSLAM TM ). The analytical methods applied were alphashape (α = 0.1–0.5), convex hull, and voxelization (s = 0.05–0.10 m). The results showed that for UAV-based surveys, the convex hull was the most appropriate analytical method (RMSE: 0.10, 0.13, and 0.35 m 3 ), while for terrestrial LiDAR, the alpha shape with α = 0.5 was the most appropriate (RMSE: 0.10 m 3 ). Overall, the results showed that volumetric data can be obtained through rapid surveys, provided the most suitable analytical method is adopted.

title: Early crop type classification and mapping combining remote sensing and ancillary data
abstract: Accurate and timely crop type classification is critical for agricultural management and food security monitoring. Most existing approaches rely on the spectral response time series obtained from satellite imagery, primarily focusing on end-of-season classification. By providing accurate crop maps early in the season, policymakers, irrigation managers, and producer organizations can optimize water allocation, forecast production, and stabilize food prices. This study introduces a novel AI framework that integrates remote sensing data with ancillary information, such as cloud cover percentage, previous-year crop type, and irrigation type, for early crop type classification. The framework is validated on a dataset of approximately 130,000 fields in the region of Lleida, Catalonia (Spain), a representative Mediterranean agricultural landscape. Leveraging remote sensing data from the previous growing season enhanced early-stage classification performance, achieving an accuracy of approximately 70% at the season’s onset—a significant improvement over traditional approaches relying solely on current-season data. Ancillary data played a key role in mitigating challenges such as cloud-induced data gaps and limited spectral information and better predicting crop types in fields with permanent crops or no crop rotation. Incorporating ancillary data boosted accuracy by 10%, resulting in an overall accuracy of 80% early in the season, which increased to 88% by the season’s end. Despite these advancements, underrepresented crop classes remained difficult to classify accurately due to class imbalances, underscoring the need for improved dataset balancing techniques. The findings underscore the potential of integrating multi-source data to improve crop type classification, especially early in the season.

title: MFFT: an improved method for stable ID tracking and counting of multi-class mango segmentation with multi-feature fusion in complex occlusion scenarios
abstract: Accurate mango segmentation, counting, and biomass estimation are critical for orchard yield prediction. To address the challenges of low fruit segmentation accuracy, frequent ID switches, and large tracking and counting errors under complex occlusion scenarios, this paper proposes a multi-feature fusion tracking method termed MFFT. The method is built on the Swin-T backbone and a customized Transformer decoder, integrated with shallow feature enhancement, boundary attention, and background gating modules. For mango segmentation, the proposed approach achieves 0.71 mIoU and 40.32 FPS for both on-tree and fallen mangoes. In the tracking stage, IOU, HSV, shape, and diagonal features are fused, together with an improved Kalman filter and ID lifecycle management, resulting in a MOTA of 0.6513 and a significant reduction in ID switches. The system innovatively introduces diagonal length as a computational metric, achieving a counting relative error of only 4.30% and a biomass estimation error of 4.49%. It outperforms mainstream algorithms such as Mask R-CNN, YOLOv8, DTER, and ByteTrack across multiple metrics. The proposed method exhibits strong application potential in orchards and provides more precise data support and a decision-making foundation for digital agricultural production management. The code and dataset for this study have been made open source on Google Drive: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1UzvgiqlXn-C2aJZsHmcLAWSYaVYA0bnH/view?usp=sharing.

title: Research progress of autonomous navigation path planning methods for agricultural ground machinery: a review
abstract: Autonomous navigation of agricultural ground machinery is a key enabler of large-scale, precise, and sustainable crop production. In the past few years, numerous path-planning solutions have been proposed for tractors and unmanned ground vehicles (UGVs) operating in open fields, orchards, and protected environments. However, the evidence remains fragmented across scenarios and information sources, and a scenario-aware synthesis is still limited. This review systematically maps and analyses research on autonomous navigation and path planning for agricultural ground machinery published between January 2019 and September 2025. Following Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) 2020 and the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR), 564 records were screened and 210 studies were included. Studies were coded by the dominant planning information (static, real-time, or hybrid), operation mode (single-vehicle or multi-vehicle), scenario, platform, sensing configuration, and validation strategy. Descriptive statistics, cross-tabulation, and keyword co-occurrence analysis were used to synthesize the landscape. Results indicate that single-vehicle systems predominantly rely on real-time information, particularly in open-field and orchard operations, whereas multi-vehicle studies still mainly adopt static, map-based coverage planning. Hybrid approaches that integrate global maps with online perception, navigation, and control are emerging, with increasing attention to complex environments such as orchards and greenhouses. Across scenarios, the dominant technical trajectory evolves from static global coverage planning to real-time local planning and obstacle avoidance, and further to hybrid, multi-source fusion strategies. This review provides a scenario-aware framework that summarises representative algorithms and sensing–control configurations, benchmarks them against commercial systems, and identifies key challenges in perception robustness, information fusion, cooperative planning, evaluation protocols, and deployment feasibility. The resulting insights support the design of practical autonomous navigation stacks and help prioritise future research on path planning for agricultural ground machinery.

title: Complementary-aware collaborative fusion: Advancing precise wheat lodging mapping using UAV-borne RGB imagery and LiDAR data
abstract: Wheat lodging, where stems bend or fall to the ground, substantially reduces both yield and quality. Accurate mapping is crucial for assessing severity, guiding the selection of resistant varieties, and estimating agricultural losses. Existing deep learning approaches based on unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV)-acquired RGB imagery often fail to capture vertical structure differences between healthy and lodged wheat. To overcome this limitation, we propose integrating LiDAR-derived Digital Surface Models (DSMs) with RGB imagery to enable multimodal lodging mapping. We present MWLNet, a novel multimodal network designed for wheat lodging characterization. MWLNet incorporates three modules: (1) the Discrepancy Modality Recalibration (DMR) module, which explicitly extracts complementary information across modalities and recalibrates features through cross-modal interaction; (2) the Dynamic Feature Consolidation (DFC) module, which adaptively fuses recalibrated features with contribution-aware weighting; and (3) the Bi-directional Semantic Synchronization (BSS) module, which enhances semantic alignment between modalities and mitigates intra-class diversity caused by varying lodging degrees. Experiments on two UAV wheat lodging datasets show that MWLNet consistently outperforms unimodal and multimodal baselines. These results confirm the effectiveness of multimodal fusion for crop lodging mapping. The code are available at https://github.com/WangYuPeng1/MWLNet.

title: Numerical investigation on turbulent airflow and heat transfer in open dairy barns with different fan layouts
abstract: Effective ventilation is essential for maintaining a stable barn environment, reducing heat stress, and supporting dairy cow health and productivity. Turbulent fans are widely used in open dairy barns, but their installation is often based on experience rather than systematic analysis. This study used computational fluid dynamics (CFD) to examine the effects of fan layout parameters on airflow distribution and convective heat transfer around dairy cows in an open barn. A simplified three-dimensional barn model was developed. Fan center height (2.0 m, 2.5 m,3.0 m), installation angle (20°, 30°, 45°, 60°), spacing (6 m,12 m), and rotational speed (345 RPM, 480 RPM, 550 RPM, 690 RPM (Revolutions Per Minute)) were analyzed under multiple operating conditions. The airflow and convective heat transfer around the head, dorsal, and abdominal regions were evaluated using velocity fields and convective heat transfer coefficients (CHTCs). The results indicated: Increasing the fan height reduces airflow speeds around the dorsal and abdominal regions of the cows. As fan angle increased from 20° to 60°, both airflow speeds and CHTCs initially rose and peaked at 30°, then declined, with dorsal and abdominal airflow decreasing by 16.7 % and 2.1 % at 60°, reducing airflow coverage and uniformity. Increasing fan spacing from 6 to 12 m slightly improved the uniformity of the airflow in the front region of the jet, but the airflow speeds and the CHTCs in the middle and rear regions decreased by 8.9 % and 19.7 %, respectively. Compared with the 690 RPM and 12 m spacing configuration, the 480 RPM and 6 m spacing configuration increased airflow speeds near the head, dorsal, and abdominal regions by 23.6 %, 28.1 %, and 1.8 %, respectively. The corresponding CHTCs increased by 16.5 %, 7.4 %, and 1.2 %, while hourly fan energy consumption decreased by 22.0 %. The results indicate clear coupled effects of fan height, angle, spacing, and rotational speed on airflow distribution around different body regions of dairy cows. Balanced fan configurations are therefore required to improve ventilation performance under practical operating conditions. These findings provide theoretical support for environmental control and ventilation management in open dairy barns.

title: An automated High-Precision farm mapping pipeline using UAV point clouds
abstract: High-precision farm maps are fundamental for achieving centimeter-level localization and precise path planning in autonomous agricultural machinery. Existing mapping methods, however, predominantly target urban road networks and lack automated solutions tailored to farm environments. To address this gap, we propose an automated pipeline for farm map construction using UAV-based Structure-from-Motion (SfM) point clouds. Low-altitude imagery is reconstructed to generate centimeter-accurate 3D point clouds, from which we build a labeled dataset covering eight land-cover categories. To balance large-region coherence in farm environments with fine-boundary delineation of small targets, we propose FarmSeg-Net, a point-cloud semantic segmentation network that integrates Rotary Position Embedding (RPE), Attention Fusion Module (AFM), and Nested Multi-Scale Decoder (NMD). Subsequently, field boundaries are vectorized via an adaptive α-shape algorithm, farm track center points are extracted through morphological skeletonization, and entrance nodes are identified using graph-theoretic betweenness centrality, yielding a triadic “field–entrance–track” topological structure. Experiments on four representative scenarios from the farm point cloud dataset demonstrate an overall accuracy (OA) of 92.9 %, a mean Intersection over Union (mIoU) of 78.1 %, mean field boundary error of 0.0827 m, and mean track-center error of 0.0783 m. Ablation studies confirm that RPE, AFM, and NMD collectively improve mIoU by 6.4 % over the baseline. The proposed framework provides a complete and reliable solution for high-precision map construction in complex, unstructured farm environments, and establishes a mapping foundation for subsequent path planning and operation scheduling of agricultural machinery.

title: RaMor3D: adaptive registration and morphology-aware reconstruction for meat rabbits in confined spaces
abstract: To support vision-based and reduced-handling phenotypic measurement of meat rabbits in Precision Livestock Farming (PLF), this study proposes a 3D reconstruction method tailored for confined spaces. This approach addresses registration difficulties caused by low point cloud overlap in restricted spaces, as well as measurement failures of key morphometric traits (e.g., body length) arising from occlusion-induced geometric holes (e.g., the rump and face). We propose an adaptive registration pipeline integrating planar pose normalization, adaptive key region extraction, and yaw angle constraints to improve accuracy and robustness under low-overlap conditions. Additionally, an Adaptive Morphology-Aware Surface Completion (AMASC) algorithm was introduced to recover biologically realistic surfaces lost to occlusion by utilizing geometric guide lines for dynamic morphology inference. Experimental results demonstrated that the proposed registration method achieved low physical measurement error, while AMASC substantially improved the reconstruction of occlusion-sensitive traits, particularly body length. Notably, compared with Poisson and ReMESH, AMASC achieved effective performance in Chamfer Distance (CD = 0.751 × 10-5 m2) and F-Score (93.92%). It enables effective restoration of body length measurements hindered by missing morphology, significantly reducing the mean relative error from 5.83% (incomplete) to 0.82%, while exhibiting a high linear correlation with ground truth (R2 = 0.988). Overall, this study provides a viable solution for precise, vision-based, and reduced-handling 3D phenotyping in confined environments.

title: Vision-based autonomous leaf-level spraying using wrist-inspired manipulators for integrated pest management in papaya greenhouses
abstract: Papaya plants exhibit complex canopy structures, which make spray application highly dependent on manual labour, requiring physical effort and considerable experience of the farmer. The shortage of skilled labour and the hazards of pesticide exposure further emphasise the need for automated precision spraying systems. This study presents an autonomous robotic sprayer (ARS) for precision spraying in papaya greenhouses and to support sustainable integrated pest management (IPM). The mechanical system was designed as a twin-sided mechanism with two degrees of freedom on each side, allowing it to mimic the key motions of the human wrist while maintaining mechanical simplicity and low production costs. The system is driven by an integrated leaf-segmentation module with depth-retrieval fusion and by a wrist exoskeleton that supplies motion-capture input. These inputs enable the system to reproduce the natural spraying motions of experienced farmers in the small-scale greenhouse. By integrating a Neutral Density filter with a depth-retrieval algorithm, the perception module sustains over 72 % leaf-recognition accuracy under greenhouse conditions. Compared with manual knapsack spraying, the proposed ARS reduced ground deposition by 39 % and improved spray coverage and uniformity across canopy layers. The system also achieved effective suppression of two major pests, two-spotted spider mite and silverleaf whitefly, confirming the biological relevance of the system. These results highlight the potential of ARS to reduce dependence on manual labour, minimise operator exposure, and enhance precision spraying in greenhouse cultivation.

title: A collaborative diffusion-VLM data synthesis framework for improving fine-grained cotton pest and disease classification
abstract: Deep learning applications in crop protection are impeded by the scarcity and high redundancy of existing datasets, which hinders models from learning discriminative representations for fine-grained diagnosis. While generative AI offers a potential solution, existing methods struggle to trade-off between pathological fidelity and diversity, as domain-specific models often lack variety while generic models suffer from feature hallucinations. To address this, we propose the collaborative diffusion-VLM framework (CDVF), a novel paradigm that synergizes distinct generative engines to synthesize high-value cotton pest and disease imagery. Specifically, our framework implements a two-stage strategy: (1) Distribution internalization: As the primary engine, a stable diffusion model tailored with category-specific low-rank adaptation is employed to faithfully reconstruct distinctive lesion textures, effectively scaling up sparse dataset. (2) Distribution extrapolation: To further transcend the visual homogeneity of seed samples, we leverage a vision-language model (VLM) via in-context learning. By unlocking its pre-trained world knowledge, the VLM injects diverse open-world contexts (e.g., complex backgrounds and varying illumination) absent in the source domain. Furthermore, we construct CoD14-plus, the most categorically diverse benchmark to date. Experiments demonstrate that expanding the dataset approximately 4 × yielded a 13.19% accuracy improvement in downstream classification, significantly outperforming the traditional augmentation strategy, which yielded a 6.91% gain. This validates our approach as a scalable solution for overcoming data bottlenecks in intelligent agriculture.

title: Editorial Board
Experimental study on flow field distribution and material separation characteristics in a pneumatic potato impurity removal device based on CFD-DEM coupling
abstract: Aiming at the problems in potato combine harvesting, such as incomplete removal of impurities including potato vines, residual plastic film and stones, high difficulty in manual sorting, and easy skin damage to potatoes caused by mechanical cleaning, this study designed a pneumatic impurity removal device for potato cleaners applied post-harvest and prior to warehousing, adopting the impurity removal technology of “vibration stratification + pneumatic suspension”. The detailed research is as follows: Based on the description of the main structure and working principle of the device, the arc length of the air guide plate in the ventilation duct and the flow distribution principle of the splitter chamber were analyzed via fluid mechanics, and three types of vibrating sieve structures with air permeability of 25%, 30% and 35% were defined. The effects of the inclination angles of the air guide plate and airflow deflector in the air supply device on the internal flow field distribution were analyzed using Fluent 2022 R2. Through CFD-DEM coupled simulation, the influence of the coupled effect of vibration stratification and pneumatic suspension on the cleaning performance of potato-impurity mixtures was studied. Taking air velocity, sieve surface air permeability and airflow deflector opening angle as test factors, BBD response surface tests, analysis of variance and response surface plotting were carried out. The optimal parameter combination was obtained as follows: air velocity of 36.14 m/s, sieve surface air permeability of 30.82%, and airflow deflector opening angle of 62.04°. Under this parameter combination, the potato cleaning rate was 98.96% and the potato loss rate was 2.24%. A prototype of the pneumatic impurity removal device for potato cleaners was fabricated and verified through bench tests. Repeated verification tests under the same parameters yielded average cleaning rate and loss rate of 97.9% and 4.3%, respectively. The research results can provide a reference for the development and optimization of non-contact pneumatic flexible impurity removal devices for potatoes.

title: Improved estimation of dissolved oxygen levels in commercial aquaculture using the ensemble Kalman filter
abstract: Dissolved oxygen is an essential environmental variable for Atlantic salmon in commercial aquaculture. Hypoxic conditions inhibit growth and increase the risk of mortality, leading to reduced welfare and profitability. Accurate and precise monitoring of dissolved oxygen levels is, therefore, a crucial aspect of optimal operation of aquaculture facilities. This has stimulated an ongoing research campaign seeking to utilise engineering cybernetic methodologies to improve oxygen estimation in commercial aquaculture. Previously, a mathematical model of the oxygen levels in sea-cages was developed based on the advection-diffusion equation. While this model estimated oxygen levels that matched those measured at a commercial site, its accuracy and precision would be greatly improved if it could assimilate real measurements into the estimation framework. Such an expansion would also help adapt the framework to future operational use, where measurements from a farm are assimilated into the framework in real time to provide a more accurate representation of the oxygen conditions therein. This study improves the previously developed oxygen estimation framework by applying the ensemble Kalman filter, a sequential Monte Carlo data assimilation method. The results are unambiguous since the filter implementation is more accurate and precise than the stand-alone oxygen model in both a practical and simulated setting. The estimation framework’s run rates are approximately 10 times faster than real-time on a standard laptop, enabling future deployment on the hardware setups commonly used at aquaculture facilities. This work represents a novel use of the ensemble Kalman filter and expands the frontier of environmental variable estimation in aquaculture.

title: Pest-induced damage detection in corn leaves using improved Faster R-CNN
abstract: Pest-induced damage detection in cereal crops, such as corn, is challenging because of the small and irregular nature of damage symptoms, which can closely resemble plant diseases or environmental stress and foreign-attached substances in leaves. Delays in identification or misdiagnosis can result in substantial yield and economic losses. Previous studies have primarily focused on pest species or diseases. This study presents a task-specific adaptation of Faster R-CNN for detecting pest-induced damage in corn leaves caused by Grasshoppers and Fall Armyworms by customising the RPN with parallel dilated convolutions and an adaptive attention module. A new field-collected corn leaf pest-induced damage dataset comprising 1,390 images, was annotated in collaboration with an agricultural expert. Forty images containing the artefact were embedded in the training dataset to enhance the model performance. The model was assessed using five-fold cross-validation, and four major evaluation metrics were evaluated. The introduction of the artefacts into the training data resulted in an improvement in mAP, along with a reduction in misdetections attributable to the artefacts. Furthermore, the incorporation of parallel dilated convolutions in the RPN of Faster R-CNN led to enhancements in mAP 50:95 (54.06%) and exhibited a high equilibrium between precision and recall, achieving an F1-score of 80.13% with increased computational cost. Compared with the baseline Faster R-CNN model, the proposed model achieved a +1.38-percentage point increase in recall for Fall Armyworm damage and a +1.79-percentage point improvement in mAP 50:95 for Grasshopper damage. This result suggests an improved detection of small objects (Fall Armyworms) and accurate localisation of larger, irregular objects (Grasshopper), both individually and when co-occurring. This research suggests a potential future applicability for farmers in the timely identification of pest infestations, thereby mitigating yield losses. These findings provide guidance for future research on detecting a wider variety of pest-induced crop damages across diverse geographical regions in agricultural computer vision applications.

title: Improving the cotton leaf area index estimation from multi-source remote sensing data based on ensemble learning model
abstract: As a core parameter characterizing vegetation growth status, the accurate estimation of the leaf area index (LAI) is crucial for the efficient management and optimized cultivation of cotton crops. While most existing studies rely on single data sources and individual algorithms to develop LAI estimation models, limitations persist in the selection of feature variables from multi-source data and the implementation of cross-algorithm ensemble learning strategies. This study aimed to develop a multi-source data-driven ensemble learning model for estimating cotton LAI. Three types of cotton canopy image data, including visible light (RGB), multispectral (MS), and thermal infrared (TIR), along with corresponding in-situ LAI measurements, were collected throughout the entire cotton growth period under a waterlogging stress experimental framework. A comprehensive set of feature variables was extracted from each of these three data modalities. Correlation analysis, decision tree-based feature importance ranking and recursive feature elimination (RFE) were sequentially employed to screen and optimize remote sensing feature variables, after which seven distinct data fusion schemes were designed. Integrating 10-fold cross-validation and paired t-tests, the robustness and performance disparities of LAI estimation models were systematically evaluated across varying conditions: distinct single machine learning algorithms, diverse ensemble learning approaches, and varied data fusion schemes. The results revealed that color and vegetation indices exhibited the strongest correlation with LAI (r = 0.841), whereas texture features generally showed weak correlations. The integration of tree model-based feature importance ranking and RFE effectively filtered feature variables, reducing the initial set of 106 variables to a refined subset of 29 variables with relatively high predictive importance. Among single machine learning algorithms, the artificial neural network (ANN), decision trees (DT), and gaussian process (GP) models demonstrated comparable performance, whereas the support vector machine (SVM) model exhibited inferior performance and high sensitivity to data schemes. Among ensemble learning approaches, the partial least squares (PLS) meta-model achieved the best performance, with the TIR univariate, MS + TIR bivariate, and RGB + MS + TIR trivariate schemes emerging as the optimal data configurations. Furthermore, ensemble learning models, particularly the PLS meta-model, significantly outperformed single machine learning models (e.g., SVM) in terms of accuracy, with improvements reaching up to 277% for the trivariate scheme. Independent validation conducted using the optimal ensemble scheme showed results consistent with those obtained during training, where the MS + TIR bivariate data fusion yielded the highest performance (R2 = 0.90, MSE = 0.21, MAE = 0.34). Overall, this study underscores the significant potential of ensemble learning methods for cotton LAI retrieval, which can facilitate the advancement of cotton production management and agricultural decision-making.

title: Active and incremental learning with RAUNet for advancing soil cover monitoring from mobile digital imaging through deep learning
abstract: Effective soil cover management is vital for sustainable agriculture, influencing soil health, erosion control, and carbon sequestration. Conventional monitoring methods are labor-intensive and often fail to capture spatial and temporal variations in soil and crop residues. To address this, we developed a deep learning framework utilizing the Residual Attention UNet (RAUNet) and a unique dataset comprising diverse residue types and agricultural scenarios. Active and incremental learning paradigms were employed to iteratively enhance segmentation accuracy by targeting underrepresented and complex scenarios, reducing the need for full model retraining. RAUNet demonstrated superior performance, achieving an Intersection over Union (IoU) of 93.09%, precision of 97.08%, and an F1-Score of 96.00% for residue segmentation. Validation against traditional dot-screen methods and ground-truth data confirmed its effectiveness in segmenting bare soil, green cover, and crop residue. The model excelled in challenging agricultural conditions, including diverse textures, lighting variations, and occlusions, underscoring its robustness and adaptability. This framework enhances mapping accuracy and efficiency and supports sustainable farming by accommodating environmental and agricultural variability. RAUNet’s lightweight design facilitates its integration with drone and satellite imagery, enabling real-time, large-scale residue monitoring. By setting a new benchmark in soil cover mapping, this approach paves the way for scalable AI applications in agriculture, promoting precision and sustainability.

title: An automatic parameter search framework for agricultural machinery trajectory operation mode identification by deeply weakly informed deep reinforcement learning
abstract: Agricultural machinery trajectory operation mode identification aims to automatically distinguish field operation scenes and road driving scenes by leveraging the spatiotemporal features of massive agricultural machinery trajectories and is a key basis task in precision agriculture. In recent years, machine learning algorithms have been increasingly applied to agricultural machinery trajectory operation mode identification. However, these models typically depend on hyperparameters, and the empirically determined parameter structures often limit the model’s potential performance, resulting in inferior generalization across different trajectory scenarios. To address this challenge, we propose a parameter search framework based on deeply weakly informed deep reinforcement learning (DWIDRL) for agricultural machinery trajectory operation mode identification, which can automatically determine the parameter structure according to the features of trajectory samples. First, we leveraged deep reinforcement learning to model parameter search as a Markov Decision Process (MDP) and developed an automated parameter search framework, enabling intelligent parameter optimization. Second, it incorporates the state aggregation context module, which encodes both global and local states, enabling the model to adaptively search for parameters according to different trajectory scenarios. Third, we propose a deeply weakly informed learning strategy that enables the model to interact with the agent’s output, adaptively adjusting the optimal parameter search policy based on past experience. Finally, to increase the accuracy of the parameters within extensive search spaces, we propose a gradual search mechanism based on parameter space attenuation, which methodically narrows the search scope at each successive layer, thereby significantly improving the precision of the results. To validate the effectiveness of the proposed framework, we conducted parameter optimization experiments on five agricultural machinery trajectory operation mode identification models across four distinct trajectory scenarios. Consequently, on one trajectory dataset, our method achieves a maximum improvement of 20.95% in average F1-score and 15.31% in accuracy. The results demonstrate that the proposed framework significantly enhances model performance and generalizability by identifying optimal parameter configurations in a shorter amount of time.

title: Behavioural phenotyping in red deer: Machine learning classification of accelerometer data from micro-movements to grazing
abstract: Monitoring deer behaviour continuously and objectively is essential for accurate welfare assessment in pastoral farming, yet conventional observation methods are labour-intensive and prone to subjective bias. We present an unsupervised machine-learning pipeline for classifying farmed red deer ( Cervus elaphus ) behaviour from wearable accelerometer data. Tri-axial accelerometers mounted on the head and ear of stags recorded movement at 50 Hz over 48 h. k -means clustering of the normalised signals yielded eight prototypical movements spanning three behavioural categories: inactive states (lying, resting with or without rumination/panting), grazing (stationary and walking), and rapid ear flicks. A first-order Markov chain then linked these prototypes into higher-order sequences we call ”super-prototypes”. These compound behaviours included ear-flick bouts and alternating grazing-stepping cycles. Within the single 24-h window, activity varied with time of day, ear flicks being markedly more frequent by day. Against independent video annotation, the eight categories agreed with the observer’s labelling at a mean of 0.96 across prototypes. Because classification reduces to a nearest-centroid operation, the algorithm runs on a 16 MHz microcontroller at over 4 × 1 0 8 classifications per second, four orders of magnitude faster than the sensor sampling rate. The pipeline requires no hand-labelled training data and runs in real time on the animal, a feasible basis for welfare monitoring in extensive deer farming systems once validated under field conditions.

title: Modeling the temperature–humidity coupling dynamics of soybean pod borer population and assessing the predictive performance of the PCM-NN algorithm
abstract: Against the backdrop of global climate change and agricultural globalization, soybean production is increasingly threatened by pest outbreaks, with Leguminivora glycinivorella (commonly known as the soybean pod borer) being a major pest species. This pest is widely distributed, particularly in northeastern China, the country's primary soybean-producing region, where its outbreaks have significantly affected both yield and quality. Although statistical and mechanistic models have been applied to pest forecasting, existing approaches often fail to effectively integrate climatic factors with pest dynamics and lack sufficient expressive power. To address these limitations, this study proposes a novel pest prediction method based on Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs). Specifically, we formulate a logistic-type ordinary differential equation (ODE) that incorporates microclimate factors, temperature, humidity, and time, to describe the temporal dynamics of the soybean pod borer population. This ODE model is embedded into the PINN framework to develop the Pest Correlation Model Neural Network (PCM-NN), which is used to jointly infer the microclimate-driven parameter function alpha(T, H, t) and fit the pest population dynamics. We evaluate PCM-NN using daily monitoring data of soybean pod borer collected in Changchun, Jilin Province, from July to September during 2020-2023. Experimental results demonstrate that PCM-NN preserves biological interpretability while exhibiting strong nonlinear representational capacity, offering a feasible pathway for pest modeling and forecasting under multi-factor climatic conditions. This approach provides valuable support for agricultural pest monitoring, prevention, and control strategies.

title: A conditional generative diffusion model enables joint retrieval of rice LAI and LCC
abstract: The critical growth stages of crops have short observation windows and are easily affected by environmental factors, which often limits the availability of field measurements for remote sensing inversion. This limitation is more pronounced in the synergistic inversion of leaf area index (LAI) and leaf chlorophyll content (LCC), where canopy structure and chlorophyll related traits may show similar spectral responses in the visible region. Such spectral overlap can lead to parameter confusion and estimation bias, highlighting the need for methods that can expand training samples while preserving the relationships among spectral features and crop traits. With recent advances in generative modeling, Generative Artificial Intelligence (GAI) provides a potential solution by learning data distributions and generating synthetic samples that preserve these relationships. To address these issues, the study developed a conditional inversion for Remote Sensing model based on a Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Model (CIRS-DDPM). In this model, LAI and LCC were embedded as continuous conditional variables and fused into the noise prediction network during reverse denoising, allowing the generated samples to better preserve the joint distribution among crop traits and remote sensing features. A Fully connected residual network for One-Dimensional Sequence Features (1D-ResMLP) was introduced as the backbone to improve noise prediction for tabular remote sensing data. The samples generated by CIRS-DDPM were compared with those generated by the Tabular Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Models (Tab-DDPM) and PROSAIL. The results showed that CIRS-DDPM generated data had feature distributions highly consistent with measured samples. Models trained with CIRS-DDPM generated data also showed strong validation performance using real measurements. The one-dimensional residual network (1D-ResNet) model achieved R2 = 0.822, RMSE = 1.314, and MAE = 1.087 for LAI, and R2 = 0.735, RMSE = 10.397, and MAE = 8.251 for LCC. Compared with models trained using PROSAIL and Tab-DDPM generated data, the R2 values increased by 20.0 % and 57.0 % for LAI, and by 18.4 % and 31.8 % for LCC, respectively. These results indicate that CIRS-DDPM can improve data support for the synergistic inversion of LAI and LCC and provide an effective solution for data limited remote sensing modeling in agriculture.

title: CVITrack-GDResYolo: An instance segmentation and tracking method for Pleurotus eryngii point clouds based on multi-view stereo vision
abstract: In preprocessing phenotypic parameter measurements for Pleurotus eryngii based on 3D technology, instance segmentation of Pleurotus eryngii point clouds in occluded scenes is a crucial step. However, when applied to Pleurotus eryngii point clouds in occluded, low-feature scenarios, current point-based point cloud instance segmentation methods exhibit high dataset annotation costs, low processing accuracy due to limited discriminative features, and weak real-time processing capabilities. To solve these problems, this paper proposes an instance segmentation method for Pleurotus eryngii point clouds based on multi-view stereo vision, which is composed of a multi-modal image instance segmentation method, GDResYolo, and a point cloud multi-object tracking method, CVITrack. In GDResYolo, taking grayscale images and corresponding depth maps as inputs, we propose a DFE (Depth Feature Extraction Module) and an MCFF (Multi-channel Feature Fusion Module) to effectively fuse multi-modal features. The proposed model exhibits stronger spatial perception ability compared to baseline models, and achieved a Recall of 0.978, an mAP0.5 of 0.991, and 0.893 of mAP0.5:0.9 on the validation set. In CVITrack, we determine instance IDs by calculating inter-instance similarity scores. On the complete point cloud instance segmentation validation set, the proposed method achieved an AP of 0.937, an AR of 0.963, and an AP90 of 0.901, outperforming all compared baseline methods. In addition, we also conducted validations on the discriminative feature richness of different point cloud representations across different methods, providing valuable reference for the selection of point cloud instance segmentation methods for Pleurotus eryngii under similar controlled settings. In summary, the method proposed in this paper offers a novel approach to solving the point cloud instance segmentation problem of Pleurotus eryngii under low-feature and occluded scenarios using the proposed multi-view structured-light acquisition setup. Validation results demonstrate that the scheme exhibits practicality in this specific controlled environment and can potentially provide technical support for Pleurotus eryngii phenotypic parameter measurement under controlled settings with similar data acquisition configurations to those used in this study.

title: Multi-sensor integration and cloud-native AI for climate-smart agricultural monitoring: A systems framework
abstract: Climate change intensifies drought, heat stress, and production instability, requiring scalable monitoring systems to support climate-smart agriculture. Remote sensing has evolved into operational decision-support infrastructure enabled by open-access satellite archives, multi-sensor integration, cloud-native computing, and machine learning. This review synthesizes peer-reviewed literature (2000–2025) and proposes a unified five-layer computational framework for agricultural climate adaptation. The framework integrates data acquisition, cloud processing, machine learning analytics, data fusion, and decision-support outputs into end-to-end workflows. The synthesis is based on a structured review of 120 core peer-reviewed studies, complemented by additional foundational and methodological references to ensure technical depth. Comparative evidence indicates that multi-sensor fusion enhances robustness relative to single-source approaches. Optical-radar integration using Sentinel-1 and Sentinel-2 has achieved classification accuracies of up to 89 % in cloud-prone regions, compared to approximately 76 % using optical data alone. ML-based yield prediction models frequently improve performance by 5–20 % in R 2 relative to empirical regression under data-rich conditions, while multi-temporal ML approaches enable detection of crop stress 2–4 weeks before visible symptoms occur. However, ML superiority over process-based models is conditional on calibration quality, data availability, and cross-regional transferability. Cloud-based platforms have reduced computational barriers and enabled large-scale time-series analysis, supporting operational monitoring from field to regional scales. Despite these advances, reproducibility limitations, ground-truth data scarcity, and reduced transferability across agroecological zones remain significant constraints, particularly in smallholder-dominated systems. Advancing climate-smart agricultural monitoring therefore depends not only on improved sensing technologies, but on interoperable, reproducible, and transferable computational frameworks capable of delivering reliable decision support across heterogeneous agricultural landscapes.

title: Corrigendum to “Accurate localization of fruit targets and picking points with multi-dimensional attention and dynamic upsampling”, [Comput. Electr. Agr. 240 (2026) 111211 doi: 10.1016/j.compag.2025.111211]
A dataset for investigating dust removal for person detection
abstract: Autonomous agricultural machinery must be able to operate safely in harsh conditions, such as dust. Dust raised during tillage can obscure objects such as an approaching person, thus posing a safety risk. One way to cope with this is to remove the dust from the image data, thereby increasing the detectability of the person. Hence, this study investigates the extent to which dust removal improves person detection. A dataset containing real-world dusty and dust-free images is presented and enriched with synthetic dusty images. To achieve this, dust was added synthetically to the dust-free images. The developed method recreates the temporal formation of dust during tillage and its influence by wind. Subsequently, state-of-the-art image dehazing and translation methods were benchmarked on the dataset. Additionally, a YOLO11 model was utilized for person detection and trained on different dataset configurations. Training on synthetic dusty images increased detection performance, measured in terms of mAP, by 55.11 percentage points compared to a pretrained detection network. Furthermore, combining synthetic and real-world dusty images increased mAP by 2.78 percentage points compared to training on real-world dusty images alone. Moreover, dust removal improved the detection performance in heavy dusty conditions by 27.23 percentage points compared to a pretrained network. More importantly, the combination of a dust removal method and a retrained YOLO11 on the specific output of the dust removal method outperformed a YOLO11 trained on real-world dusty images by 3.39 percentage points in heavy dusty conditions. The results highlight the potential to enhance the safety of autonomous agricultural machinery by removing dust from images prior to detection.

title: Novel traceability strategy based on redactable blockchain for food supply chain
abstract: In recent years, blockchain technology has emerged as a promising solution for enhancing the security and transparency of food traceability systems. However, challenges such as data immutability, privacy concerns, and regulatory compliance have limited its widespread adoption. To address these issues, we propose a novel food traceability strategy that integrates redactable blockchain technology with attribute-based encryption. The strategy enables secure and efficient data editing, fine-grained access control, and distributed storage, ensuring the integrity and privacy of food traceability data. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed strategy significantly improves transaction execution time, transaction per second (TPS), and data transmission efficiency compared to existing solutions. This research contributes to the development of more secure, flexible, and scalable food traceability systems, with potential applications in enhancing food safety and supply chain transparency.

title: Physics-guided GAN and ANN hybrid framework for small-sample performance prediction of seed-maize harvester conveying device
abstract: The scarcity of simulation data limits the modeling accuracy for performance prediction of seed-maize harvester conveying devices. This study proposes a hybrid intelligent modeling framework that integrates physical mechanisms with data-driven methods. First, a high-quality dataset of 32 sample points is constructed using a DEM-MBD coupled simulation. The dataset incorporates three key operational parameters: conveyor belt speed, elevator inclination angle, and secondary stalk-roll speed. To overcome small-sample learning challenges, a physics-constrained Wasserstein Generative Adversarial Network (PC-WGAN) is developed. This network embeds differentiable constraints, derived from projectile motion equations and collision momentum conservation laws, into the generator’s loss function. The PC-WGAN subsequently generates 100 physically credible augmented samples. Based on this, the proposed PC-WGAN-GP-ANN hybrid framework achieved an R2 value of 0.827 in predicting the stalk removal rate and ear damage rate of the conveying device, representing a 219.28% improvement compared to the baseline ANN model. Although the random forest (RF) achieved a slightly higher R2 (0.832) on the same augmented data, the proposed method enables the otherwise poor-performing ANN (original R2 = 0.259) to achieve competitive accuracy, demonstrating its effectiveness in leveraging generated data under small-sample conditions. Field validation tests demonstrate that under the optimal parameter combination (conveyor speed: 3.452 m/s, inclination angle: 55.2°, stalk-roll speed: 652 r/min), the stalk removal rate reaches 96.2%. This field result is essentially consistent with the simulation predictions. This study confirms that incorporating physical prior knowledge as constraints into the generative data augmentation process enhances the accuracy and generalization capability of agricultural equipment performance prediction models under small-sample conditions. Therefore, the proposed PC-WGAN-GP-ANN hybrid model provides an effective data-driven solution for the intelligent design of agricultural machinery under small-sample conditions.

title: Green pepper fruit instance segmentation in near-color field environment using the SDBnet network
abstract: Accurate fruit instance segmentation is the premise of intelligent picking, precision spray and phenotypic parameter measurement. A green pepper fruit instance segmentation method based on SDBnet in near color environment is proposed in this paper. Based on the mutual constraints between the semantic representation ability and geometric information representation ability of feature maps at different levels, a network architecture design method suitable for effective feature map extraction based on the characteristics of target size is proposed. Specifically for elongated green pepper targets, a Shallow Feature Enhancement Network Architecture (SFENA) is proposed based on this method. The proposed Dual View Channel Attention Block (DVCAB) utilizes dual view channel attention created by pooling mean view and convolutional weight view, as well as convolution branch and optional residual branch construction, to achieve the extraction of multi-dimensional fruit effective feature information. A Binary Distribution Focal Loss (BDFL) is proposed based on the idea of probability distribution, which optimizes the probability of the left and right positions near the binary segmentation label, so that the segmentation positions focus on the vicinity of the label value. Multiple Population Genetic Algorithms (MPGA) optimizes the weight coefficients α and β of BDFL to achieve the optimal comprehensive accuracy of the model. The results of the field near color environment test showed that the Mask mAP50 and mAP50:95 for SDBnet fruit instance segmentation were 81.6% and 49.1%, which were 4.2% and 4.5% higher than the baseline model, respectively. The SDBnet parameter size is only 7.9 M, and the detection speed is 56.8f/s. Compared with the other 10 mainstream instance segmentation models, SDBnet has the highest accuracy performance indicators (Box/Mask mAP50 and mAP50:95), and the model has the smallest parameters and weight sizes. Therefore, SDBnet is the current State-of-the-Art model for green pepper fruit instance segmentation, which willprovide technical support for intelligent planting of green peppers.

title: A phenology-aware organ-specific multi-temporal UAV framework for maize shoot phosphorus uptake estimation and field-scale mapping
abstract: Harvest total shoot phosphorus uptake (TSPU) is difficult to estimate from unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) canopy imagery because phosphorus (P) accumulation is unevenly distributed among leaves, stems, and grains, whereas UAV observations primarily capture an integrated and stage-dependent canopy signal. Here, we developed a phenology-aware organ-specific multi-temporal UAV framework that shifts maize TSPU estimation from conventional direct regression to organ-aware target construction. Multi-temporal spectral and textural features acquired at the jointing, grain-filling, and milk-ripe stages were integrated to compare three strategies under the same leakage-aware feature-selection and validation framework: direct TSPU prediction (M1), organ-specific uptake decomposition (M2), and concentration–biomass integration (M3). In the Site 1 fixed-split benchmark, M2 with fused spectral–textural inputs achieved the highest validation accuracy, reducing root mean square error (RMSE) by 9.53% and mean absolute error (MAE) by 12.07% relative to M1 with the same inputs. Additional organ-level uncertainty analysis showed that this improvement should not be interpreted as uniformly high predictability of all organ components. The TSPU reconstruction was mainly supported by stem P uptake (SPU) and grain P uptake (GPU) and was primarily controlled by GPU-related uncertainty. Leaf P uptake (LPU) remained weakly observable from canopy-level UAV predictors, indicating that M2 should be interpreted as an organ-specific diagnostic reconstruction framework. By contrast, M3 did not further improve performance, indicating that physiologically explicit intermediate predictions may introduce additional uncertainty when canopy observability is constrained. External-field evaluation showed that local calibration supported TSPU reconstruction at Site 2, with strong agreement in full-sample reconstruction (R2 = 0.87, RMSE = 5.81 kg ha−1, n = 120) and moderate accuracy in fixed-split validation (R2 = 0.61, RMSE = 10.03 kg ha−1, n = 36). The matched validation further confirmed that external-field uncertainty was dominated by GPU-related residuals, which accounted for 81.2% of the total absolute organ-level residuals and 97.4% of the component residual variance, highlighting the need for local recalibration and organ-level residual diagnosis. Field-scale mapping experiments further showed that the finest UAV resolution was not necessarily the most practical for P uptake mapping. In this study, an intermediate resolution of approximately 2.5 m provided a locally suitable compromise between preserving within-field heterogeneity and reducing map fragmentation. These findings demonstrate that organ-specific target construction combined with multi-temporal spectral–textural UAV information can moderately improve maize TSPU estimation under fused inputs and, more importantly, diagnose the organ-level sources of prediction uncertainty, thereby providing practical guidance on local calibration and mapping resolution for field-scale P uptake mapping and potential precision P management.

title: Energy saving laser weeding: Heat transfer simulation to reveal ablation mechanism and predict energy consumption
abstract: Laser weeding is an environmentally friendly weed control method, and the laser beam can be flexibly and precisely controlled. However, the limited operating endurance of laser weeding systems restricts the further development and practical application of this technology. To investigate the mechanisms by which different factors affect laser weeding performance and to identify a laser application strategy that maximizes energy utilization, this study developed a multiphysics coupling simulation model based on porous media theory. By combining laser ablation experiments with heat transfer simulations, the ablation mechanism of weed stems under laser irradiation was analyzed. The results showed that the laser incidence angle and stem dimensions were the main factors affecting the ablation performance, primarily because they changed the effective power density acting on the stem surface. When the laser beam was incident perpendicular to the stem surface, the maximum power density was obtained, resulting in the best ablation performance. Finally, a regression model for predicting the required ablation energy was established based on the simulation results, and the model was further corrected by incorporating Fresnel reflection. Validation experiments conducted at four incidence angles, namely 80°, 70°, 50°, and 40°, showed that the overall mean relative error between the predicted and experimentally determined ablation energies for the three weed species was approximately 8.61 %. This result indicates that the corrected regression model can provide a reliable prediction of the actual ablation energy. This study provides a methodological framework and theoretical support for energy optimization in intelligent field laser weeding systems.

title: A comprehensive review of wearable sensors for animal information acquisition in precision livestock farming
abstract: Global livestock systems are undergoing a technology-driven transformation, and wearable sensors are now widely used for physiological monitoring, behavioral analysis, early disease detection, and production management. Following PRISMA guidelines, this review synthesizes studies published between 2015 and 2025, including 98 studies retrieved from major academic databases. Unlike earlier reviews that focus mainly on single species or single functions, this study provides a cross-species, multi-sensor synthesis of wearable sensor applications in animal husbandry, covering motion, acoustic, optical, thermal, and emerging sensor technologies. Beyond listing sensor types, it examines how sensor performance and deployment strategies shape core monitoring functions, including behavioral monitoring, physiological assessment, and spatial tracking across livestock species. These functions include detecting feeding, locomotion, rumination, and activity patterns, as well as measuring of body temperature, heart rate, respiratory rate, and location-related parameters. Despite major technological progress, current wearable systems still face challenges in detection accuracy, long-term stability, wearer comfort, and cost. This review synthesizes current research findings, summarizes technological advances, identifies persistent technical and application barriers, and outlines future research directions. It provides an integrated account of the current state and the main directions field.

title: Study on pig cough recognition and spatial localization based on multi-source noise separation
abstract: Automatic monitoring of pig coughs at the individual level remains challenging in group-housed production systems because barn recordings are strongly affected by background noise, overlapping vocalizations, and unreliable identity attribution. This study developed an integrated acoustic monitoring framework for individual pig cough recognition and spatial localization under pig-house conditions. The framework combined adaptive spectral subtraction and finite impulse response (FIR) filtering for front-end noise reduction, non-negative matrix factorization (NMF) constrained by Kullback–Leibler (KL) divergence with soft masking for source separation, and an improved TFA-Net for sound classification and acoustic identity modeling. The proposed TFA-Net adopted a dual-branch CNN–Transformer architecture with time–frequency attention to jointly capture local transient patterns and long-range time–frequency dependencies. In addition, an eight-channel microphone array coupled with generalized cross-correlation with phase transform (GCC-PHAT) was used for sound-source localization and trajectory estimation. Experiments were conducted on recordings collected from 10 fattening pigs across four sound categories, including cough, feeding, snoring, and normal vocalizations. The annotated recordings were divided into training, validation, and test sets at a ratio of 80:10:10, and data augmentation was applied only to the training set to reduce evaluation bias. The acoustic identity database achieved F1-scores ranging from 91.44 % to 98.10 % across individuals. For sound classification, the proposed model obtained a top-1 accuracy of 96.79 %, mean precision of 96.74 %, mean recall of 96.40 %, mean F1-score of 96.56 %, and mean average precision (mAP) of 98.58 %. For the cough category, precision, recall, and F1-score were all 97.09 %, with an average precision of 98.77 %. Under mixed acoustic interference, NMF-based source separation increased cough recall from 50.60 % to 87.00 % and reduced the cough miss rate from 49.40 % to 13.00 %. Sound-source localization errors ranged from 0.058 m to 0.361 m, and independent validation on unseen pigs yielded an average localization error of 0.158 m. These results indicate that the proposed framework has the potential to support cough detection, individual attribution, and spatial localization under tested pig-house conditions, providing preliminary technical support for precision respiratory health monitoring in swine production.

title: DELKNet + LLM: lightweight multi-model integration real-time perception and pre decision analysis for facility tomato
abstract: Precise phenotypic perception and reliable decision-making are critical for the intelligent management of greenhouse tomatoes. However, existing methods often lack an integrated closed-loop “perception-to-reasoning” workflow and struggle with high computational costs on edge devices.
