Water-sensitive paper (WSP) is widely used for spray assessment but requires sample collection and post-processing and provides only endpoint measurements. This study developed a spherical water sensor (SWS) for continuous, direction-sensitive monitoring of droplet deposition. The SWS comprises a 3D-printed hollow spherical frame, embedded circuitry, and absorbent polyvinyl alcohol material. Deposited droplets form conductive liquid bridges within the absorbent layer, producing resistance-induced voltage changes. Its multi-zone spherical architecture enables droplets arriving from different orientations to be detected by separate sensing zones, reducing dependence on a single installation angle. Paired SWS–WSP spray tests were conducted under controlled conditions. Using WSP coverage as the reference, an expanded 0.8 m dataset containing 20 independent paired observations was used for regression modeling and validation. The no-intercept model achieved an uncentered R2 of 0.972. Leave-one-out cross-validation yielded RMSE, MAE, and MRE values of 13.91%, 10.84%, and 17.01%, respectively. External validation at 1.6 m maintained an uncentered R2 of 0.983 but showed a mean bias of − 7.90%, indicating that distance-aware calibration is required when spraying distance or droplet transport conditions change. Overall, the SWS provides continuous electrical responses reflecting deposition occurrence, relative deposition level, and temporal trends. This study establishes a reusable spherical multi-zone resistive sensing framework that complements WSP-based endpoint assessment by providing real-time and direction-sensitive deposition information.

title: Toward intelligent pig farming: Advancing health and welfare monitoring through computer vision–based behavioral analysis
abstract: Modern pig production is increasingly moving toward smart and intelligent farming systems, integrating advanced technologies such as artificial intelligence for precision management. Camera-based computer vision has emerged as a promising non-contact sensing tool for monitoring pig health and welfare through behavioral analysis, given the strong association between behavioral patterns and physiological status. Following a PRISMA-based search, 45 studies were included for critical synthesis on computer vision-based behavioral analysis in pigs, with emphasis on detectable behavioral indicators, imaging configurations, model architectures, post-processing strategies, and deployment constraints. Findings show that posture and nutritive behaviors are the most mature targets for monitoring because they are visually distinctive, biologically informative, and compatible with lightweight object-detection pipelines. In contrast, aggression, biting, enrichment interaction, suckling, and individual activity metrics require stronger temporal modeling, segmentation, or multi-object tracking, which increases annotation burden, computational cost, and susceptibility to occlusion and identity errors. Recent pig-specific modifications to YOLO, transformer-inspired, segmentation, and tracking models have improved performance through attention mechanisms, multi-scale feature fusion, occlusion-aware regression, lightweight convolution, and detector-tracker coupling. However, high reported accuracies often reflect controlled datasets rather than commercial robustness. Critical barriers include limited multi-farm validation, inconsistent annotation and post-processing rules, insufficient anomaly-detection thresholds, weak long-term identity preservation, and hardware constraints for edge deployment. Future efforts should prioritize developing standardized benchmarks, biologically grounded behavioral metrics, explainable and domain-adaptive artificial intelligence, and edge-ready architectures that convert model outputs into interpretable management alerts. This review provides a deployment-oriented framework for advancing computer vision from experimental behavior recognition toward scalable behavioral monitoring and intelligent decision support in pig production systems.

title: Hybrid AWD-GCN-BiGRU model for edge-optimized dissolved oxygen prediction in recirculating aquaculture systems
abstract: Accurate prediction of dissolved oxygen in recirculating aquaculture systems (RAS) is crucial for precise aeration control, hypoxia mitigation, and energy efficiency optimization. However, conventional methods struggle to capture the complex, nonstationary dynamics of multivariate time series and largely ignore the dual requirements of edge deployment and model interpretability. This study proposes a novel lightweight hybrid framework (AWD-GCN-BiGRU) that integrates adaptive wavelet decomposition (AWD), graph convolutional networks (GCN), and bidirectional gated recurrent units (BiGRU). The pipeline utilizes correlation-based feature engineering to isolate the core driving variables. Structurally, it synergizes multifrequency adaptive denoising, multivariate interaction modeling, and bidirectional temporal extraction operations of AWD, GCN, and BiGRU, respectively, thereby finalizing the predictions via linear regression optimization. Natively optimized for Jetson edge devices, the model significantly outperformed nine benchmarks (including Transformers and long short-term memory networks) across three independent datasets. Ablation studies validated the synergistic effect of the modules in this architecture. The model maintained robust accuracy for multistep forecasting up to 15 steps ahead and achieved a single-sample inference latency of 0.3218 ms, perfectly satisfying real-time operational constraints. Furthermore, noise injection tests confirmed superior robustness against 2% data perturbation. By employing the Shapley additive explanations analysis to quantify key feature contributions, the model ensured algorithmic transparency. This study provides a high-precision, edge-deployable, and interpretable solution for RAS water quality regulation, effectively bridging the gap between theoretical modeling and practical smart aquaculture applications.

title: Energy-efficient high-precision electric seed metering system: achieving high-speed, high-precision seeding with low energy consumption
abstract: As electric-driven maize precision planters evolve toward higher operating speeds and multi-row configurations, the power demand of the electric drive system increases. How to maintain seeding accuracy under high-speed operation while mitigating the impacts of elevated energy consumption on machine endurance and operational reliability has become a critical bottleneck limiting performance improvements in seeding equipment. To address these challenges, this study developed an Energy-efficient High-Precision Electric Seed Metering System (EHPE-SMS). The core contribution of this study is the development of a coordinated control architecture integrating Linear Active Disturbance Rejection Control and Simplified Field-Oriented Control for a two-phase (LADRC–SFOC), four-wire hybrid stepper motor, which jointly optimizes the speed loop and current loop to improve disturbance rejection and energy utilization efficiency. To support practical deployment of this control framework, a machine-learning-based fitting and optimization method was further used to tune key LADRC parameters, and an integrated drive-and-monitoring circuit was developed to provide step-loss detection, seed blockage detection, and seeding quality monitoring. Bench tests show that, under a regulated 12 V supply, the proposed EHPE-SMS has the lowest calculated electrical input power among the tested motor-drive combinations, with reductions of 70.90%, 60.29%, and 53.39% relative to the tested brushed DC motor-drive, commercial closed-loop stepper motor-drive, and brushless DC motor-drive combinations, respectively. Under identical seeding protocols on the same hardware, LADRC-SFOC further reduced average operating power by 8.04% relative to conventional PID control. Across a speed range of 3–24 km/h, relative to conventional PID control, the proposed LADRC-SFOC strategy reduces the average coefficient of variation of motor speed by 3.92% under constant-speed conditions and shortens the average response time by 406.33 ms; under both constant-speed and noise-disturbance modes, it reduces the average coefficient of variation of seed spacing by 21.7 percentage points and lowers average power consumption by 8.04%. Field experiments further demonstrate that, over the same speed range, the system achieves an average seeding quality index (QI) of 95.04% and an average seed-spacing coefficient of variation (CV) of 24.54%. However, due to factors such as seed bounce under high-speed conditions, seed-spacing uniformity remained somewhat limited at speeds above 15 km/h. Moreover, the integrated monitoring module successfully detected and responded to the tested abnormal events, indicating its functional effectiveness in improving system safety. Overall, the proposed EHPE-SMS substantially reduces energy consumption while maintaining high-speed, high-precision seeding performance, and enhances system stability and intelligence, supporting efficient, clean, and sustainable precision seeding equipment.

title: ST-CAFNet: A visual–olfactory multimodal cross-attention fusion network for freshness prediction of cold plasma-treated salmon
abstract: Accurate and non-destructive freshness prediction of aquatic products is essential for intelligent cold-chain quality control, yet single-modality sensing approaches cannot fully capture multidimensional spoilage dynamics, especially after non-thermal preservation treatments. In this study, a visual–olfactory multimodal fusion framework was developed to predict the freshness of cold plasma-treated salmon during refrigerated storage. Salmon fillets were treated using cold plasma at different discharge frequencies (CK, 100 Hz, 200 Hz, and 300 Hz) and monitored using computer vision and electronic nose, with total viable count (TVC), total volatile basic nitrogen (TVB-N), and thiobarbituric acid-reactive substances (TBARS) measured as reference freshness indicators. The 200 Hz treatment showed the strongest preservation effect, delaying the increases in TVC, TVB-N, and TBARS compared with the control. Visual analysis revealed progressive surface discoloration, exudate accumulation, and texture degradation during storage, while electronic nose responses captured the evolution of volatile odor fingerprints associated with microbial metabolism, protein degradation, and lipid oxidation. To integrate complementary spatial visual features and temporal E-nose response sequences recorded during each acquisition, a Spatio-Temporal Cross-Attention Fusion Network (ST-CAFNet) was proposed, consisting of an EfficientNet-B0–CBAM visual branch, a 1D-CNN–Bi-LSTM olfactory branch, a bidirectional cross-modal attention module, vector-gated fusion, and an uncertainty-weighted multi-task regression head. On the independent test set, ST-CAFNet achieved R2 values of 0.9742, 0.9853, and 0.9681 for TVC, TVB-N, and TBARS, respectively, with corresponding RMSE values of 0.2429, 0.9416, and 0.0635. These results demonstrate that visual–olfactory deep fusion enables rapid, non-destructive, and multi-indicator freshness prediction of cold plasma-treated salmon.

title: Online rice plant counting method from harvester’s perspective based on HRCNet density graph model
abstract: Online identification of the number of rice plants to be harvested during the operation of rice combine harvesters is of great significance for improving the level of intelligent operation. Traditional counting methods face challenges from a harvester’s perspective, such as small, densely distributed rice ears, similar backgrounds, and severe occlusion, resulting in limited recognition accuracy. Therefore, this study proposes a rice plant counting method based on a density map model. First, a dataset of rice plant images from the harvester’s perspective was constructed, and a dedicated point annotation tool was developed, resulting in a cumulative annotation of 256,803 plants. Second, a density map counting model HRCNet(Harvester-rice-counting-network) was designed. This model used SepViT as the backbone network and combined a multi-scale fusion mechanism to enhance the ability to extract global context information. It also introduced a feature transformation module (FTM) to enhance the leaf texture and edge detail features. Finally, the model results were systematically analyzed and discussed. Test results showed that HRCNet achieved MAE and RMSE on the test set within 16.87 and 20.56 plants, respectively, with a MRE of only 6.19%. The error remained below 10% across different density ranges. Compared with mainstream counting models, HRCNet achieved the best performance. Ablation study further validated the synergistic effectiveness of the SepViT backbone and the FTM. Furthermore, the model demonstrated good robustness and counting accuracy under different lighting conditions, vibration conditions, cutting widths, and missing area scenarios, with MREs all less than 10%, providing reliable technical support for density sensing during rice harvester operations.

title: Anti rollover strategy of tracked tractor on sloping land based on DEM-MBD coupling
abstract: Crawler tractors have low ground pressure and high adhesion, which can reduce soil stress and compaction. They are suitable for operations in hilly areas and complex environments. However, the most serious safety issue is the tripping rollover on steep slopes. This article analyzes the impact of changes in the center of gravity position of the entire machine on slope driving, and designs a remote-controlled proportional prototype of a track with adjustable center of gravity in both horizontal and vertical directions. The stability and anti rollover strategy are evaluated based on the distribution of ground pressure on the track, and the uniformity of ground pressure distribution under 5-20° slope conditions before and after adjusting the center of gravity of the test vehicle is compared and analyzed. An active anti rollover control strategy based on the technology of “turning towards the high side of the slope in situ + longitudinal shift of the center of gravity” is proposed. A research method combining DEM-MBD coupled simulation experiments with proportional physical prototype experiments was adopted to establish a dynamic model of tracked vehicles and slope soil, and experiments were conducted. It provides a reliable and cost-effective framework for developing anti-rollover strategies. The simulation and platform test results both indicate that the control strategy proposed in this paper can effectively improve the uniformity of the ground pressure distribution of the rolling tracked vehicle, which can provide technical reference for the anti rolling of tracked tractors.

title: A lightweight DDC-YOLO and inspection-robot system for dead broiler detection in caged broiler houses
abstract: In caged broiler houses, dead-broiler detection typically relies on manual inspection, which is labor-intensive, inefficient, and difficult for high-level cages. To address these problems, this study proposed an automatic detection system for dead broilers in cage environments and deployed it on an inspection-robot platform for automated monitoring. First, to mitigate complex lighting and image blur, Gamma transform and Gaussian blur were applied for data augmentation to simulate real breeding scenes and improve model robustness. Second, the DDC-YOLO (DeadChicken-YOLO) detection model was developed; it uses a UIB lightweight backbone, the WIoU loss, the SimAM attention mechanism, and a DBFF feature-fusion module to enhance feature extraction and target detection while reducing model complexity, combined with TensorRT on edge devices to accelerate inference. Finally, a self-iterative mechanism was implemented that links robot data collection and detection with cloud-based transfer learning and model backhaul updates so the model could continuously adapt to new scenarios, such as different broiler breeds after deployment. The experimental results showed that the proposed DDC-YOLO achieved a precision of 96.8%, a recall of 85.4%, an F1 score of 90.8%, and mAP@0.5 of 93.1%. Compared with the original YOLO11, the model reduced parameters by 1.437 M and decreased size by 2.8 MB. In real farm environments, the model achieved real-time, accurate detection of dead broiler chickens with the continuous migration and adaptation across broiler-breed scenarios. Overall, the proposed method balanced detection accuracy, edge-deployment capability, and continuous optimization potential, and it can provide technical support for unmanned and reduced-staff broiler cage farming.

title: Hierarchical causal discovery and bridge forecasting for greenhouse leaf temperature control
abstract: Leaf temperature is a key indicator of crop physiological status in greenhouses, but its dynamics are governed by a hierarchical transmission process in which control actions alter the indoor microclimate and shape physiological responses. Existing correlation-based analyses and black-box prediction models provide limited interpretability for identifying these transmission pathways and supporting control-oriented decision-making. This study presents a hierarchical AutoLag-PCMCI+ and causal bridge forecasting (CBF) framework that combines action–state–physiology constraints with adaptive lag selection to support interpretable leaf-temperature decision-making. AutoLag-PCMCI+ imposes layer-specific constraints across control, state, and physiology variables and uses validation to determine an acceptable lag range for each target variable, thereby identifying robust causal links through stability analysis. The discovered structure is used to construct a CBF framework for leaf temperature prediction, and the resulting forecasts are examined in a downstream replay-based control evaluation. A deployment-oriented proxy early warning scheme based on the leaf-to-air temperature difference (ΔT) is evaluated; this scheme requires leaf temperature and air temperature measurements but does not rely on more complex physiological monitoring. Air temperature and photosynthetically active radiation were identified as statistically supported lag-1 direct parents of leaf temperature, serving as thermal and radiation-related bridges. In the replay-based control evaluation, the CBF policy showed higher estimated resource-saving potential at 30–120 min, with estimated reductions in heating, supplemental lighting, and CO2 dosages of 32.79–40.19%, 71.60–81.86%, and 73.17–82.02%, respectively, while remaining more conservative at 10 min. Overall, the framework characterizes hierarchical leaf temperature pathways and supports interpretable, risk-aware climate decision-making.

title: PINN-AMF: A physics-informed neural network with attention-based multi-source fusion for robust chlorophyll retrieval from UAV hyperspectral imagery
abstract: Leaf chlorophyll a + b content (Cab, μg cm⁻2) is a key indicator of crop nitrogen status and can support variable-rate fertilization. UAV-based hyperspectral imaging provides rich spectral information, yet retrieval of leaf-level Cab from canopy spectra remains challenging because of reflectance saturation, background mixing, and spectral ambiguity. Purely data-driven models often lack physical grounding and can be sensitive to changes in canopy structure, whereas RTM-based inversion is typically ill-posed and computationally expensive. This study proposes PINN-AMF, a physics-informed framework that fuses canopy spectra with agronomic priors and enforces radiative-transfer consistency within a unified learning architecture. The model uses a dual-stream encoder to extract spectral and metadata embeddings and a gated fusion module to adaptively balance multi-source contributions. Physical consistency is imposed by a PROSAIL-based differentiable surrogate (CanopyEmuNet) embedded as the decoder and optimized end-to-end using a composite objective that combines Cab regression, full-spectrum reconstruction, and red-edge position consistency. Experiments on UAV hyperspectral data from three potato field campaigns (N = 414) showed that PINN-AMF achieved R2 = 0.838 and RMSE = 4.99 μg cm⁻2 under stratified 10-fold cross-validation, corresponding to a 35.5% RMSE reduction relative to the CNN baseline. Together with grouped leave-one-year, leave-one-site, and leave-one-cultivar analyses, these results indicate that PINN-AMF improved within-dataset accuracy and retained partial transferability across the represented years, sites, and cultivar groups.

title: A lightweight, few-shot ready embedding framework for cattle identification using retinal images
abstract: Precise livestock identification is central to modern livestock management system. It enables health surveillance, supporting insurance and liability verification, and ensuring transparency in trade and market transactions of livestock. Various biometric modalities have been explored for bovines such as muzzles, face, coat pattern and retinal imaging. However, retinal imaging offers distinct advantages with its inherent stability and unique vascular structure. This study proposes a lightweight and few-shot ready embedding framework for cattle identification using retinal images that comprises four main components: (1) a lightweight convolutional neural network backbone for retinal feature extraction, (2) a parameter free attention mechanism to enhance feature representations without increasing model complexity, (3) a triplet Siamese network architecture with hard negative mining function to further enhance a discriminative feature learning, and (4) a few-shot identification module that employs cosine distance to compare a query sample against a single image support set. The proposed method highlights the design that operate effectively even when only two labeled images per animal are available for enrollment and verification. This makes it suitable for data constrained retinal biometric cattle identification scenarios. Our method demonstrates identification accuracy of 97.40% under low data regimes while maintaining a compact model size of 4.4MB and an inference latency of 15ms. In addition, the study enhances transparency in the proposed cattle biometrics by providing interpretable insights into the learned representations through explainability and interpretability tools, such as Grad-CAM and t-SNE visualizations, respectively.

title: Machine learning and physical modeling for water regulation at different phenological stages in efficient green paddy field production
abstract: Influencing both crop growth and the agro-ecological environment, water regulation is a key factor in agricultural production. However, few studies have considered the impact of dynamic field-scale blue and green water migration processes on farmland water regulation. A water–food–environment multi-objective collaborative optimization model incorporating stage-specific blue–green water migration processes was developed to establish the surrogate-modeling framework. Linear, multiplicative, and Transformer-based yield prediction models were compared, while an empirical drainage-based model served to represent the grey water footprint. To characterize stage-specific blue–green water partitioning and support irrigation optimization under different hydrological scenarios, the Transformer model was coupled with field water-dynamics simulation and the NSGA-II optimization algorithms. This framework allows the evaluation of stage-specific irrigation strategies that consider yield, blue water productivity, and drainage-related non-point source pollution risks. Using four hydrological-year types and six decision preferences, the framework was evaluated using field data from Nanjing, Jiangsu Province, China, a representative rice-growing area in the lower Yangtze River region. The model generated coordinated trade-off solutions across the three objectives. Across the evaluated scenarios, the optimized solutions were associated with higher yield and blue water productivity and lower grey water footprint relative to baseline strategies, with average changes of approximately +30%, +176%, and −35%, respectively. The proposed framework functions primarily as a methodological template for site-specific offline irrigation decision support under different hydrological conditions. Although the quantitative optimization outcomes depend on local agro-hydrological conditions, the stage-based coupling framework and optimization workflow can be adapted to other rice-growing regions after local recalibration, validation, and scenario reconstruction.

title: Real-Time Automated Body Condition Scoring of Dairy Cows in a Commercial Rotary Milking Parlor Using RGB-D Two-Stream Deep Learning
abstract: Automated body condition scoring (BCS) can improve the frequency, objectivity, and decision-making value of dairy cow monitoring, but its deployment in commercial rotary milking parlors remains challenging because animals are imaged under continuous flow, variable posture, changing backgrounds, and strict real-time constraints. This study presents a deployment-oriented RGB-D framework for automated BCS estimation during routine milking in a commercial rotary parlor. Synchronized RGB and depth images were acquired with an overhead Kinect sensor during three daily milking sessions, while RFID-triggered acquisition linked each image pair to individual cow identity. Expert reference scores were assigned using the Ferguson five-point BCS protocol with 0.25-unit increments. After quality control, the dataset comprised 25,700 RGB-D image pairs from 1,025 lactating cows. The proposed pipeline integrates YOLOv26l-based cow localization, RGB-D region-of-interest alignment, pad-and-resize preprocessing, and continuous BCS regression using a Two-Stream ResNet18 architecture with late feature fusion. Performance was assessed using an animal-wise split and compared with single-modality and alternative backbone models. The Two-Stream ResNet18 achieved the best performance, with MAE = 0.076, Accuracy0 = 83.6 %, Accuracy0.25 = 95.76 %, and Accuracy0.50 = 99.35 %, while maintaining an end-to-end latency of 95.0 ms. By combining RFID-linked RGB-D sensing, modality-aligned fusion, and low-latency inference, the framework enables automated BCS estimation under routine commercial rotary milking conditions. The resulting industrial-scale RGB-D dataset provides a reproducible benchmark for future precision dairy monitoring systems.

title: Intelligent red-blue supplemental lighting control system for greenhouses: balancing photosynthesis and carbon footprint
abstract: Supplemental lighting enhances the productivity of greenhouse crops, while the energy consumption and carbon footprint associated with greenhouse environmental control are critical to sustainable production. To address this, the study proposes an intelligent decision − making and control system for red − blue supplemental lighting based on multi − objective optimization for light intensity and spectrum, and the optimization incorporates two objective functions: a photosynthesis prediction model based on a genetic algorithm − optimized least squares support vector machine and the carbon footprint function. A quadratic polynomial and linear regression − based decision model is established and deployed on an elastic compute service. An intelligent control system, integrated with a wireless sensor network, acquires real − time greenhouse temperature and photosynthetic photon flux density data, generates control commands via the decision model, and controls light sources through pulse width modulation. The photosynthesis prediction model achieved a determination coefficient of 0.968 and a root mean square error of 0.717 μmol·m−2·s−1, accurately characterizing the photosynthesis response to the environment. For red and blue light, the output light intensity decision model based on greenhouse temperature achieved determination coefficients of 0.849 and 0.809, respectively, with average control errors of − 2.52% and − 2.48% for the control system. Additionally, system validation experiments showed that the dual − target control of light intensity and red − blue ratio achieved an average carbon footprint of 162 mg·m−2·s−1, representing a 33.80% reduction compared to the fully loaded system, while the net photosynthetic rate was enhanced by 17.47% relative to the control group. Compared with the light intensity − only control method, the proposed method increased fresh weight and fruit weight per plant, and demonstrated superior performance in photosynthesis and plant characteristics. The developed system effectively balances high productivity with a low carbon footprint, offering a practical solution for intelligent greenhouse lighting management.

title: DA-MOT: a directed-angle-aware multi-object tracking framework for dairy cows
abstract: Accurately tracking and quantifying key behaviors of dairy cows, such as feeding, drinking, and lying, provides essential data for early health warning systems. Multi-object tracking technology serves as a core approach for the automated analysis of dairy cow behavior. However, in group-housing environments, the high similarity of dorsal spotting patterns, diverse body orientations, and nonlinear movements significantly reduce tracking accuracy and lead to frequent trajectory fragmentation. Therefore, this study adopted a detection-based tracking framework and proposed DA-MOT, which consists of the YOLO-CCSA detector and AngUK-Tracker, enabling high-precision dorsal detection and tracking of nonlinear motion targets at arbitrary angles. First, within the backbone network of YOLOv11X-OBB, two CCSA module structures were designed, which incorporate an SRU and a CRU. These modules constitute YOLO-CCSA, enhancing the extraction of dorsal spotting pattern features by reducing redundant information in both spatial and channel dimensions. Second, an angle-aware state vector, including angle and angular velocity components, was introduced into the ByteTrack motion model to enable the prediction of target states at arbitrary angles. In addition, a rotated IoU calculation method was proposed for efficient detection-to-tracking association, reducing background noise interference and enabling accurate tracking of cows at arbitrary orientations. Finally, a prediction–update mechanism of the angle-aware state vector was optimized using an unscented Kalman filter, resulting in the AngUK-Tracker, which improves the accuracy of tracking cows exhibiting nonlinear motion. The YOLO-CCSA achieved an AP50 of 99.5%, representing a 1.4% improvement over YOLOv11X-OBB. Compared with ByteTrack, DA-MOT achieved a HOTA of 70.66%, a MOTA of 90.06%, a MODA of 90.07%, and an IDF1 of 92.82%, corresponding to improvements of 7.94%, 19.42%, 19.39%, and 23.52%, respectively, while IDSW decreased from 56 to 14. The proposed DA-MOT achieves remarkable improvemants and provides a solid data foundation for the automated analysis of dairy cow behavior.

title: Thin Gaussian Splatting for high-quality geometric reconstruction of peach tree
abstract: Dense 3D reconstruction is essential for peach tree phenotypic analysis, providing detailed morphological data for trait-environment studies. While 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) methods excel in photorealistic rendering for agricultural scenes, they typically neglect geometric surface fidelity, limiting high-precision reconstruction. This deficiency introduces substantial errors in phenotypic trait measurements. To solve the problem, we propose a novel thin Gaussian Splatting architecture for high-quality geometric reconstruction of peach trees, incorporating the improved densification and optimization modules. Specifically, through scale regularization, 3D Gaussians are first flattened into thin primitives. Multi-view consistency and planar consistency constraints are introduced to enhance geometric accuracy. Furthermore, a geometry-adaptive densification strategy is proposed to ensure planar modeling quality, while the opacity of cloned Gaussians is reduced to mitigate opacity bias in the rendering process. We constructed a six-category peach tree dataset using an RGB-D sensor and developed a geometric accuracy evaluation mechanism based on depth map error computation. Experimental results show our algorithm achieves the best average geometric accuracy compared to two NeRF-based and five 3DGS-based methods on our constructed datasets. Relative to the standard 3D Gaussian Splatting algorithm, AbsRel and RMSE errors are reduced by 27.27% and 16.05%, respectively, while depth prediction accuracy improves by 9.31%. Rendering metrics (SSIM, PSNR, LPIPS) match or exceed 3DGS levels. This method enables accurate 3D reconstruction of fruit trees, providing essential data for phenotypic analysis to advance precision agriculture and crop improvement.

title: LCDNet: A lightweight controller-oriented dual-output network for crop inter-row navigation on edge devices
abstract: Under the hardware constraints of edge devices, visual navigation for agricultural robots in crop inter-row environments must balance accuracy, real-time performance, and deployability. Existing methods mostly rely on multi-stage pipelines with complex post-processing, whereas single-stage approaches rarely provide both an interpretable regional output and controller-oriented navigation parameters. To address this limitation, a lightweight controller-oriented dual-output network, LCDNet, is proposed. In a single forward pass, pixel-level drivable-area masks and controller-oriented navigation parameters (dx,θ) are generated simultaneously. The network uses a compact encoder-decoder architecture. An adaptive asymmetric weighted atrous spatial pyramid pooling (AAW-ASPP) module is introduced to improve adaptation to directional inter-row structures and scale variation. A row-geometry bidirectional coupling module (RG-BCM) is further designed to establish structured bidirectional coupling between segmentation and navigation. On a mixed public dataset containing images from multiple crops, LCDNet achieved a mean intersection over union (mIoU) of 93.05 % with 0.69 M parameters and a strict accuracy (Strict Acc) of 91.67 % for navigation parameter prediction. After TensorRT acceleration on a Jetson Xavier NX, LCDNet achieved a preloaded-input throughput of 50.35 frames per second (FPS) using a 640×360 input resolution. Transfer learning on self-collected strawberry and cherry tomato datasets yielded a maximum Strict Acc of 92.00 %. Heterogeneous edge-device deployment and preliminary closed-loop field experiments further supported the deployment feasibility of the proposed method.

title: A pipeline for 3D image pre-processing, classification, segmentation, and feature extraction of beef cattle in feedlots
abstract: This study presents an integrated framework designed to support the development of computer vision systems for commercial beef cattle feedlots, focusing on the acquisition and processing of 3D images of cattle during water intake. The study addresses key challenges associated with real-world feedlot environments, including dependence on ambient lighting that makes RGB imaging sensitive to time of day, cloud cover, and shadows, variable lighting, and unrestrained animal movement. The proposed framework comprises four modules: (1) image quality enhancement through depth and infrared image fusion; (2) image classification using transfer learning to identify usable images; (3) GAN-based data augmentation to reduce false positives; and (4) animal body segmentation and morphometric feature extraction to support future weight prediction and body condition assessment applications. Results showed that combining infrared and depth images enabled correct segmentation of approximately 20% more intact animal bodies compared with depth images alone. The AlexNet classifier applied to combined images achieved a false positive rate of 0.031, which was reduced to 0.008 (74% reduction) following GAN-based augmentation with 500 curated synthetic images. Marker-Controlled Watershed Segmentation isolated the animal body with a mean IoU of 0.888 relative to ground-truth annotations. Area-based morphometric features extracted from the final dataset of 1,286 images showed Pearson correlations above 0.9 with gold-standard measurements, whereas boundary-sensitive features exhibited lower correlations, with important implications for future feature selection in weight prediction models. This study establishes a foundational pipeline for future automated computer vision applications in commercial feedlots while providing transparent reporting of methodological decisions that facilitates replication, future embedded deployment, and technology transfer.

title: A two-stage method based on images and videos for detecting weaned pig behavior under environmental enrichment conditions
abstract: Environmental enrichment serves as a pivotal strategy for enhancing the activity levels and expression of natural behavior, significantly improving animal welfare in weaned pig farming. Continuous and accurate monitoring of pig behaviors is essential for evaluating the efficacy of environmental enrichment. This study proposes a novel two-stage framework integrating image and video recognition to detect lying, standing, object interaction, and aggressive behaviors in weaned pigs exposed to varying environmental enrichment objects. In the first stage, the YOLO11n algorithm is employed to detect all behavioral of pigs in static images. This initial detection enables a rapid, computationally inexpensive search for potential actions. Frames flagged for potential aggression at a low confidence threshold are identified, and their subsequent 5-second video clips are extracted. In the second stage, a lightweight TSM-MobileNetv2 model is employed to recognize the video clips for aggressive behavior. This two-stage approach is to overcome the high computational cost of full video analysis for all behaviors, and achieves a balance between speed and accuracy in behavioral monitoring. The results show that the recognition accuracy for lying, standing, interaction, and aggressive behaviors reach 95.2%, 96.1%, 86.5%, and 89.6%, respectively. The proposed method achieves a balance between speed and accuracy: when processing the same video, it reduces computation time by 74.7% compared to the video recognition method and improves accuracy by 14.3% over the image detection method. In the initial period of observation, pigs with environmental enrichment showed an average reduction of 8.1 percentage point in lying behavior and an average increase of 4.8 percentage point in standing behavior compared to those without enrichment. This same trend persisted throughout the seven–week study, with the non–enriched group consistently exhibiting more lying and less standing. Among the enrichment materials, soft rubber rings had the most pronounced effect. Over time, the aggressive behavior of pigs notably reduced in the later weeks compared to the first week. However, the comparison between the environmentally enriched group and the control group did not reveal clear differences in aggressive behavior. These findings indicate that environmental enrichment enhances pig activity levels, and that pigs’ interest in enrichment objects diminishes rapidly. This research establishes a novel approach for pig behavior detection and provides critical insights for optimizing environmental enrichment strategies in weaned pig management.

title: Rice panicle detection from unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) imagery via image restoration and pseudo-depth prior
abstract: Accurate rice panicle detection using Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) imagery is a key prerequisite for automated counting and yield-related phenotyping. However, existing detection methods generally assume clear input imagery and rely primarily on two-dimensional RGB appearance, making them vulnerable to motion-induced texture degradation and the strong visual similarity between rice panicles and background foliage in dense canopies. To address these limitations, we propose a novel framework for rice panicle detection via image restoration and pseudo-depth prior fusion. First, we introduce the Spectral-Geometric State Space Network (SG-SSN) to explicitly recover task-relevant high-frequency textures from the temporally accumulated blur commonly generated during UAV cruising. Second, we utilize the Depth Anything V2 vision foundation model to infer pixel-aligned pseudo-depth maps from the deblurred images, providing complementary relative geometric cues. Finally, these dual representations are processed by our proposed Rice Panicle Detection with Pseudo-Depth (RPDet-PD) model, which leverages hierarchical pseudo-depth fusion and frequency-spatial structure preservation to achieve precise panicle localization. Evaluations on a large-scale, multi-site, and multi-variety UAV field dataset show that SG-SSN achieves a PSNR of 32.19 dB on a synthetic temporal-accumulation restoration benchmark. Furthermore, the complete cascaded pipeline utilizing RPDet-PD achieves a mean average precision (mAP@0.5) of 91.6 % under the evaluated field conditions, outperforming the evaluated baseline methods. The experimental results indicate that the proposed cascaded framework provides a feasible approach for rice panicle detection under complex field conditions.

title: LMD-Net: A lightweight multi-scale detection model for rice disease detection in complex field environments
abstract: Early rice disease lesions in complex field environments are often characterized by small size, weak texture, and blurred boundaries, while occlusion, specular reflection, illumination variation, and background interference further increase the difficulty of accurate detection. To address these issues, a rice disease object detection dataset, rice_leaf_disease_v1, was constructed for complex field conditions, containing 19,422 images and six common rice diseases. Multiple augmentation strategies, including rotation, translation, brightness and contrast adjustment, Gaussian noise, and motion blur, were applied to improve data diversity and scene realism. On this basis, a lightweight multi-scale detection model, termed LMD-Net, was developed based on YOLOv13n. Specifically, the LAE module was introduced into the backbone downsampling stage, the C3k2_MSCB1 module was embedded into the backbone and neck, and the Detect_MBConv module was adopted in the detection head to enhance multi-scale feature extraction while reducing computational cost. Experimental results across multiple random seeds showed that LMD-Net achieved 92.7 ± 4.8 % precision, 84.2 ± 5.1 % recall, 89.1 ± 5.4 % mAP@50, and 64.6 ± 1.7 % mAP@50:95. Compared with YOLOv13n, LMD-Net improved the mean precision, recall, mAP@50, and mAP@50:95 by 1.8, 3.6, 2.4, and 3.9 percentage points, respectively. Meanwhile, the model achieved a weight size of 4.9 MB, 2.19 M parameters, and 5.7 GFLOPs, demonstrating a favorable balance between detection accuracy and lightweight deployment. These results indicate that LMD-Net provides an promising solution for real-time rice disease detection and edge-assisted smart agricultural applications under complex field environments.

title: Corrigendum to “A multisource weakly supervised high-resolution crop mapping framework based on low-resolution noise labels” [Comput. Electron. Agric. 251 (2026) 112003]
Multimodal adaptive cross-mamba for tomato leaf disease diagnosis built on real-world agricultural data
abstract: Diagnosing tomato leaf conditions in real agricultural environments remains challenging because of symptom variability, complex backgrounds, and limited domain-specific multimodal annotations. To address this problem, we propose Multimodal Adaptive Cross-Mamba (MACM), a task-oriented multimodal framework that integrates CLIP-based representation learning, dual cross-attention, an Adaptive Sparse Self-Attention GLU (AGLU), and Cross-Mamba fusion for image-text interaction. We further construct a field-collected tomato leaf image-text dataset comprising 3,788 annotated pairs across six leaf condition categories. Under the current held-out evaluation protocol on this single-site dataset, MACM achieves 90.82% accuracy, 90.34% precision, 90.03% recall, and 90.18% F1-score, outperforming the unimodal and CLIP-based multimodal baselines considered in this study. Ablation experiments support the contribution of each module, while qualitative examples illustrate representative success and failure cases under real-world symptom variability. These results suggest that MACM is a promising framework for practical tomato leaf condition diagnosis, while broader multi-site validation and repeated-run evaluation remain necessary for stronger generalization claims.

title: Conventional MFCC and phase-difference MFCC interaction network for durian days-after-anthesis estimation
abstract: Precise assessment of durian maturity is important for harvest scheduling, whereas conventional methods are often destructive or dependent on human judgment. Although farmers commonly use knocking sounds in practice, systematic estimation of Days After Anthesis (DAA) from acoustic recordings remains limited. Most existing acoustic approaches for durian maturity assessment have focused on discrete ripeness classification or single-feature representations, which provide limited information for fine-grained harvest scheduling. To address this problem, this paper proposes a dual-stream acoustic regression framework, named the Conventional MFCC and Phase-Difference MFCC Interaction Network (CPDMIN), for estimating continuous durian DAA from knocking sounds. The framework is based on conventional Mel-Frequency Cepstral Coefficients (MFCC) and Phase-Difference Mel-Frequency Cepstral Coefficients (PDMFCC). The MFCC stream is extracted using the standard MFCC procedure from the original spectral representation. PDMFCC is introduced not as a replacement for conventional cepstral analysis, but as an additional phase-aware representation of the same acoustic signal. Specifically, PDMFCC is derived from a phase-difference-modulated spectral representation formed by combining spectral magnitude with adjacent-bin phase-difference information prior to mel filtering and discrete cosine transformation. By jointly modeling magnitude-related cepstral information and phase-difference-informed cepstral cues, the proposed method aims to provide a more informative acoustic representation than conventional single-stream MFCC-based approaches. The proposed CPDMIN framework employs two parallel encoders, a bidirectional interaction module, and an adaptive gated fusion module to learn and integrate the two feature streams before final DAA prediction. The proposed framework was evaluated against eight representative deep-learning baselines, including ResNet, EfficientNet, MobileNet, ConvNeXt, and vision-transformer-based architectures, under the same experimental protocol. Under the present experimental setting, CPDMIN yielded the most favorable overall results among the compared baselines, with a mean absolute error (MAE) of 2.33±0.24, a root mean square error (RMSE) of 3.82±0.45, a mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) of 2.18±0.23, and an R2 of 0.965±0.010. These results suggest that jointly modeling MFCC and PDMFCC may be useful for non-destructive durian DAA estimation within the current dataset and acquisition conditions.

title: Autonomous Tissue-Interfaced Plant-Machine Interface for Real-Time Physiological Control of Phosphate
abstract: The emergence of smart agriculture has motivated the development of smart fertigation management system (FMS) to replace conventional scheduled-meter-based fertigation. For smart agriculture, these new FMS should possess five key characteristics: robotic, in vivo microneedle-based electrical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) sensing; machine-learning (ML)-based instant data interpretation; automated precise nutrient formulation and delivery; real-time feedback-driven fertigation adjustment; and identified optimal growth phosphate status. However, sensors, ML, or automated fertigation injector reported to date typically fulfill one or two requirements at the same time, and rare are examples of FMSs that fulfill all five requirements simultaneously. Here, we present a bio-integrated computerized FMS that meet all five requirements simultaneously. TheMobile Sensing Platform provides stable, high-throughput measurements (16 plants/h) with minimal tissue disruption, with equipped MN sensors accessing into plant compartments to enable instant detection of physiological phosphate status; the lightweight Extra Trees classifier translated impedance spectra into plant phosphate states with 89% accuracy in <1s; These predictions triggered automated nutrient formulation and delivery within 15 min and 0.25 g/L precision, demonstrating continuous electronic-biological feedback control. Deployment in indoor strawberry cultivation identified an optimal phosphate regime that improved yield while reducing fertilizer input relative to conventional recommendations. By bridging the gap between tissue-interfaced sensing and closed-loop actuation, this work establishes a prototype of potentially scalable bioelectronic framework that couples living plant physiology with autonomous electronics, unlocking new avenues for sustainable, bio-integrated automation in smart agriculture

title: Leaf pigment profiling for sensitive detection of nutrient deficiency syndromes in strawberry
abstract: Nutrient deficiencies disrupt photoprotective pathways, but their specific effects on pigment composition and stress resilience remain unclear. We aimed to establish distinct photoprotective fingerprints for nitrogen (N), phosphorus (P), potassium (K), and calcium (Ca) deficiencies in strawberry (Fragaria × ananassa) leaves. In a hydroponic experiment with optimal supply and each nutrient deficiency at 5 % of control, we analyzed young and mature leaves separately after 11 weeks using non‑invasive pigment indexing (Dualex), HPLC carotenoid profiling, chlorophyll fluorescence (PAM), and a UV-B stress assay. Mineral profiling confirmed the induction of targeted deficiencies in leaves. Distinct nutrient-specific pigment signatures emerged as N deficiency suppressed chlorophylls/carotenoids (e.g., β-carotene and neoxanthin reduced by 49 % and 72 %, respectively) in mature leaves, while P deficiency increased chlorophyll content in young leaves. Ca deficiency decreased β-carotene and lutein in mature leaves. Functionally, K deficiency impaired NPQ induction when compared to the control. N-deficient plants exhibited a greater NPQ induction in mature leaves under UV-B radiation compared to the control group, and K deficiency resulted in increased non-regulated energy dissipation. Flavonols and neoxanthin coincided with preserved PSII function under UV-B exposure, while K deficiency increased non-regulated energy dissipation, and Ca deficiency impaired photoprotective function. Young leaves exhibited greater performance relative to mature leaves in pigment plasticity and stress recovery, suggesting an ontogenetic prioritization of photoprotection. Multivariate analysis further indicated that these responses represent distinct, nutrient-specific reorganizations of pigment profiles and photosynthetic parameters. Taken together, these findings suggest that alterations in photoprotective pigments might serve as sensitive, nutrient-specific physiological fingerprints. They may inform future non-invasive diagnostics and sensor calibration for precision agriculture, and could serve as targets for resilience breeding of crop plants.

title: PRISM: A methodological framework for reproducible data-to-model translation in spatial crop modeling
abstract: Process-based crop models are increasingly applied to forecast yields and assess climate risks in rainfed smallholder agriculture across sub-Saharan Africa. However, the prerequisite step of transforming heterogeneous agricultural data into standardized, model-ready inputs remains a major challenge for reproducible and comparable spatial crop modeling. Here we present PRISM (Platform-Ready Inputs for Spatial Modeling), a framework that formalizes data retrieval, quality control, gap-filling, spatial harmonization, and format conversion to produce standardized input packages compatible with multiple crop modeling frameworks. PRISM separates agronomic specifications from model-specific settings, with provenance records documenting preparation decisions. Case studies across four crop modeling frameworks in Mali, Niger, Nigeria, and Senegal demonstrated that all generated packages loaded without manual editing and that simulated outputs fell within published benchmark ranges. By automating the data-to-model translation process, PRISM enables systematic data preparation for spatial crop modeling across platforms in data-scarce regions, facilitating multi-model comparison studies for yield estimation, climate impact assessment, and agricultural planning.

title: LCSNet–FedPerGC: An efficient federated learning framework for rice leaf disease classification in the Mekong Delta
abstract: Rice leaf disease classification under distributed data settings requires strict data privacy preservation and timely decision support across geographically dispersed agricultural regions, which closely reflects practical rice cultivation conditions in Vietnam. In this paper, we propose a federated learning framework that integrates a lightweight deep learning backbone with an optimized federated optimization strategy to address these challenges. We introduce a compact convolutional neural network family, termed LCSNet, designed for efficient feature extraction with high classification accuracy and fast inference. Experimental results demonstrate that LCSNet 3 achieves 95.44% classification accuracy with an inference speed exceeding 325.5 FPS, substantially outperforming conventional backbones in efficiency-critical scenarios. LCSNet also maintains consistently high macro F1-scores across multiple datasets, demonstrating strong cross-dataset generalization and robustness to domain shifts. To further enhance training stability and convergence in federated environments, we propose FedPerGC, an improved federated optimization framework incorporating gradient similarity analysis and contribution-aware weighted aggregation. Under both IID and non-IID data distributions, FedPerGC consistently outperforms FedAvg, FedAdam, FedProx, and baseline FedPer, achieving 96.60%, 97.35%, and 98.25% accuracy on private datasets for α=0.5,0.8, and 1.0, respectively, with stable convergence and balanced client participation. Overall, the simulation results indicate that the proposed LCSNet–FedPerGC framework provides an efficient and scalable solution for rice disease classification, designed to enhance data privacy, and demonstrates strong potential for deployment in distributed agricultural monitoring systems.

title: Field-condition-aware cleaning-loss intensity estimation in rice combine harvesters using a lightweight 1D CNN_GRU virtual sensor with multi-sensor fusion
abstract: Cleaning-loss strongly affects rice combine harvesting efficiency, yet piezoelectric monitoring can become unreliable when the machine transitions between wet, dry, and combined paddy zones. This study developed a field-condition-aware lightweight 1D CNN_GRU virtual sensor to estimate voltage-based cleaning-loss intensity using machine-dynamics measurements. A multi-sensor platform was deployed on a ZOOMLION rice combine harvester, integrating dual IMUs (sieve and chassis), fan/rotor proximity RPM sensors, field-measured agronomic variables, and RTK-GNSS, while piezoelectric thin-film array and ceramic sensors provided training targets. Raw piezoelectric signals were sampled at 1000 Hz and down sampled to a synchronized 1 Hz logging rate for multi-sensor fusion. Field data were collected across wet, dry, and combined field conditions (15,000 time-aligned samples retained for each condition). Indoor grain-dropping calibration test confirmed the quantitative relationship between known grain impact mass and piezoelectric voltage response. The proposed 1D CNN_GRU model (∼73 k parameters, ≈ 0.28 MB) was benchmarked against machine-learning (ML) baselines (Ridge, SVR, Random Forest, XGBoost) and deep-learning (DL) baselines (1D_CNN, GRU, LSTM, CNN_LSTM, CNN_LSTM_GRU). The proposed model outperformed traditional ML and DL baselines, achieving (Coefficient of Determination (R2) / Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE) values of 0.87/0.238 V and 0.90/0.211 V; 0.96/0.013 V and 0.97/0.012 V; 0.98/0.126 V and 0.98/0.105 V) under wet, dry and combined field conditions for the array and ceramic sensors, respectively. Under wet conditions, the virtual sensor outperformed the best ML baseline XGBoost (ΔR2 = +0.25 for array and ΔR2 = +0.23 for ceramic). Sensor ablation and SHAP analysis identified field condition dependent dominant predictors, while MC Dropout provided uncertainty aware prediction intervals. These findings demonstrate that the proposed virtual sensor provides an accurate and redundant cleaning-loss intensity estimation channel that remains operational when direct piezo measurements become unreliable, supporting embedded-oriented monitoring for smart rice harvesting.

title: Unified gated basis modulation for agricultural virtual-to-real translation
abstract: Parametric virtual farms provide a cost-effective way to generate structurally accurate and controllable virtual scenes for training agricultural vision models. However, a substantial appearance gap remains between virtual and real farmland images. Meanwhile, agricultural tasks are highly sensitive to geometric structures such as crop rows, plant contours, and field boundaries, making it difficult for existing virtual-to-real (V2R) translation methods to balance visual realism and structural consistency. To address this issue, we propose Agri-UGBM, a structure-preserving V2R translation framework for parametric virtual farms. The core design philosophy is to treat structural maps, diffusion timesteps, and semantic prompts as dynamic modulation signals rather than static conditions, so that appearance transfer can be guided without freely distorting task-relevant geometry. Built on a Stable Diffusion v1.5 latent diffusion backbone, the method introduces a unified gated basis modulation (UGBM) module into the ControlNet conditional residual injection pathway. By jointly leveraging structural conditions, diffusion timesteps, and text prompts, UGBM dynamically modulates multi-scale conditional residuals to enhance structure preservation. Experimental results demonstrate improved trade-offs between realism and structural consistency. On the VegAnn dataset, UGBM reduces FID from 136.4 to 103.8 and improves Edge F1 from 0.756 to 0.823 compared with the strongest baseline, ControlNet++. Under fixed maize structural inputs, the method achieves a CLIPScore of 31.0 and an Edge F1 of 0.829 under sunny noon prompt. In downstream near-field plant segmentation, U-Net trained on UGBM-generated data improves Boundary IoU from 43.6 to 69.8, reaching 71.9 with TransUNet. These results indicate that UGBM enables structure-preserving and controllable image generation while providing task-useful synthetic data for boundary-sensitive agricultural segmentation.

title: Development of a two-step cross-cultivar grape quality prediction model using outdoor hyperspectral imaging in three grape cultivars: Rondo, Zweigelt, and Kerner
abstract: Sensing technologies that are independent of berry-color variation across grape cultivars, particularly under varying environmental stress conditions, are crucial for advancing precision viticulture. This study developed a two-step cross-cultivar quality prediction model for three grape cultivars with red or white berries—Rondo, Zweigelt, and Kerner—using an outdoor hyperspectral camera (HSC). We introduce a seamless soft-clustering approach that groups spectral characteristics without prior cultivar labels, using a coefficient-boosting method integrated with two dimensionality-reduction techniques: principal component analysis (PCA) and uniform manifold approximation and projection (UMAP). For Brix prediction across the three grape cultivars, the R 2 values were 0.72 (normal model), 0.75 (PCA-boosted), and 0.83 (UMAP-boosted); for pH prediction, the values were 0.70, 0.75, and 0.82, respectively. UMAP-boosted models consistently outperformed the normal model (without boosting), and PCA-boosted models also improved performance. While both the normal and PCA-boosted models improved performance, the UMAP-boosted models demonstrated superior accuracy for Brix and pH across both single- and cross-cultivar settings suggesting that UMAP more effectively captures the local and global structures of hyperspectral data, accounting for the complex reflectance curve variations between different cultivars. The primary UMAP-boosted model outperformed six mainstream machine learning and deep learning models—including PLSR, SVR, and NN—achieving the highest R 2 values and lowest RMSE. This framework enables automated clustering and enhances Brix and pH prediction from outdoor hyperspectral data under challenging field conditions. Future work should adapt the sensing platform for varying sunlight intensity and diverse geographical regions.

title: Corrigendum to “Physics-guided GAN and ANN hybrid framework for small-sample performance prediction of seed-maize harvester conveying device” [Comput. Electron. Agric. 253 (2026) 112064]
Automated homogeneity-check of agricultural parcels using machine learning: increased performance in compliance with EU common agricultural policy
abstract: Accurate assessments of agricultural parcel geometries are crucial for calculating financial subsidies. Today, authorities use aerial images to check parcels for homogeneous cultivation and incorrect parcel geometries (homogeneity-check). Due to the large number of parcels and the limited resources in authority offices, there is a need for an automated method of preselecting a manageable sample of parcels for manual review. To this end, this study introduces (i) a novel method for automated homogeneity-check including (ii) a user utility metric reflecting its ability to preselect presumably heterogeneous parcels, i.e., those that benefit from manual review. The new is metric (ii), called Precision of Prioritized Items (PPI), was used to evaluate the performance of four machine learning approaches for homogeneity checking (i): Image Classification, Semantic Segmentation, Edge Detection, and Clustering. Moreover, the evaluation also assessed the robustness of these approaches regarding image resolution. The results show that all approaches performed similarly in terms of the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) and the PPI metric; Image Classification: AUROC = 77.4%, PPI = 90%, Semantic Segmentation AUROC = 83.0%, PPI = 100%, Edge Detection: AUROC = 79.2%, PPI = 90%, and Clustering: AUROC = 84.4%, PPI = 100%. However, only the Clustering approach consistently maintained a stable PPI of 100%, regardless of image resolution, demonstrating superior robustness. The implementation of the Clustering approach enabled the authorities to improve their performance in this task by 294% from 2023 to 2024.

title: BioLQM: a novel hybrid intelligent model for feed optimization and growth evaluation in juvenile spotted knifejaw (Oplegnathus punctatus)
abstract: Precisely optimizing feeding strategies and evaluating growth of juvenile fish in complex aquaculture environment, remain critical challenges to be addressed. This study proposed a novel hybrid intelligent decision-making model for aquaculture, BioLQM integrates the strengths of bioenergetics, reinforcement learning (Q-learning), and model predictive control (MPC) to accurately evaluate the growth trajectory of juveniles and provides feeding decisions. Juvenile spotted knifejaw (Oplegnathus punctatus) was selected as the research subject. It was validated under offshore aquaculture net pen (OANP) and recirculating aquaculture system (RAS). Results proved that BioLQM exhibits good fitting performance within the limited sample (MSE≈0.0005, MAPE≈0.16 %, and R2≈1). And in retrospective simulation, model feeding strategies reduced the feed conversion ratio (FCR) from 1.79 to 1.42 in OANP and from 2.77 to 1.52 in RAS. A juveniles growth validation experiment confirmed the rationality of model-based feeding decisions, achieving a FCR of 1.2. Furthermore, it met the target weight requirements, with MSE of 0.1558, MAPE of 2.5937 %, and R2 of 0.9989. Comparison results showed that BioLQM addressed the limitations of traditional growth models. It could accurately describe fish growth trajectories and adaptively provide feeding decisions under controlled and uncontrolled conditions. Q-learning was incorporated to mitigate uncertainties in parameters of mechanistic model and to reduce its high sensitivity to external disturbances. MPC was incorporated to mitigate the lack of predictive capability for system dynamics and future states in Q-learning, facilitating continuous optimization and smoothed constraint enforcement to avoid extreme control decisions. BioLQM could be employed in commercial intensive aquaculture to monitor fish growth trajectories and optimize feeding management. It could be extended to other fish species by calibrating specific parameters within the mechanistic model.

title: Multi-site dissolved oxygen prediction using physics-guided graph convolutional network in aquaculture ponds
abstract: Dissolved oxygen is a critical water quality parameter in aquaculture ponds, with its spatiotemporal prediction holding significant importance for aquatic health. In this paper, we propose a novel Spatiotemporal Physics-Graph Fusion Network to achieve accurate prediction of dissolved oxygen at multiple key locations within a large ecological pond. It integrates the Environmental Fluid Dynamics Code mechanistic model with graph convolutional networks by a layer-by-layer residual injection strategy, completing effective fusion of physical constraints and data-driven learning. The model further incorporates dual attention mechanisms within a dual path temporal convolutional network, to concurrently capture short-term fluctuations and long-term dependencies in DO dynamics. Additionally, to enhance temporal modeling efficiency, a lightweight temporal attention mechanism is designed, which can dynamically adjust the update frequency of attention matrices. The experiments in pond verify the effectiveness of the proposed models, with mean RMSE, MAE, and MAPE values of 0.8197 mg/L, 0.5866 mg/L, and 1.29% respectively, outperforming the mainstream baseline models.

title: GeoDaRT: Contextual geospatial data infrastructure for distributed on-farm experimentation
abstract: On-farm experimentation (OFE) is increasingly recognized as a pathway for developing sustainable and context-specific agricultural practices under real-world production conditions. However, OFE outcomes are difficult to interpret, compare, and aggregate when the environmental and biophysical context of each experiment is not described in a consistent and reproducible way. The main barrier is not only access to public geospatial data, but the repeated transformation of heterogeneous soil, terrain, weather, drought, and satellite products into traceable, analysis-ready covariates linked to agricultural fields and experimental time windows. This study presents the Geospatial Data Retrieval Tool (GeoDaRT), a web-based system that implements a reproducible contextual data workflow for OFE and related agricultural research. GeoDaRT organizes retrieval around experiment-oriented requests consisting of an area of interest, temporal parameters, selected data products, and processing options. The workflow standardizes access, clipping, file formatting, naming, metadata, packaging, and provenance while preserving native source resolution and coordinate reference information where appropriate. GeoDaRT was evaluated through a distributed field-scale analytical-readiness workload involving 200 corn and soybean fields in New York State and the U.S. Midwest over three growing seasons. The system produced 105,984 contextual files representing 600 site-years. These outputs supported an end-to-end multivariate analysis of 19,900 field pairs without custom reformatting. The analytical-readiness workload produced a coherent contextual feature space and demonstrated that GeoDaRT outputs could support residual-tail summaries and mapped interpretation. These results demonstrate that GeoDaRT makes contextual covariate generation more feasible, auditable, and reusable for distributed OFE.

title: A Lightweight Identification Method for Banana Leaf Diseases Based on Improved YOLOv11n
abstract: The early and accurate identification of banana leaf diseases is important for maintaining banana yield and quality. To address variable lesion morphology, the missed detection of early micro-lesions, and the deployment constraints of edge devices, this study proposed Strip–SPD hybrid downsampling–VCA YOLO (SSV-YOLO) based on YOLOv11n. A C3k2_Strip module was introduced to enhance the extraction of vein-oriented and strip-like lesion features. A hybrid downsampling strategy combined Space-to-Depth Convolution (SPDConv) in the shallow backbone with ADown in the deeper backbone and feature pyramid to preserve fine-grained information and improve feature fusion. In addition, a Variance Channel Attention (VCA) mechanism was designed to replace C2PSA by using global mean and standard-deviation statistics for lightweight channel weighting. On the constructed banana leaf disease dataset, SSV-YOLO achieved an mAP@0.5 of 96.6% and an mAP@0.5:0.95 of 80.2%, representing improvements of 2.4 and 6.6 percentage points over YOLOv11n, respectively. The parameter count was reduced by 30.8% to 1.8M. These results indicated that SSV-YOLO achieved a favorable balance among detection accuracy, model size, and inference efficiency for real-time banana leaf disease detection.

title: Rapid detection of maize seed vigor via multi-branch interpretable deep learning integrated with multimodal data fusion optimized by environmental factors
abstract: Seed vigor is a core indicator of seed quality and field emergence performance. Existing rapid detection technologies perform poorly in field applications, neglecting the fusion of multimodal data and the effects of environmental factors on seedling emergence. Here, we collected 700 maize seed samples from diverse sources and acquired multimodal phenotypic data, including machine vision (MV), reflectance spectra (RS), and fluorescence spectra (FS). Seed vigor labels were obtained via a cold-soak germination test, with continuous recording of temperature and humidity during the process. Considering the complexity of seed vigor, we constructed a Four-branch Combined Dual-path Attention Mechanism Residual Network (FDRNet) to simultaneously classify seed vigor levels (low/high) and predict physiological indicators (fresh weight, germination energy, germination percentage). Furthermore, an AIseed Vigor software was developed, and its field performance for seed vigor prediction was verified via UAV remote sensing technology. The main conclusions are as follows: (1) Multimodal data fusion (RS + FS) with FDRNet achieved the highest performance in seed vigor classification (Accuracy = 96.8%) and physiological prediction (Rp2 = 0.742/0.582/0.642). (2) SHAP interpretation revealed the spectral preferences of different physiological indicators: seed fresh weight was mainly determined by the 500 nm green band, while germination energy and germination percentage primarily depended on the 453 nm blue band, and combined with feature interaction analysis further verified the complex nonlinear relationships between spectral features and various seed physiological traits. (3) Incorporation of environmental factors reduced the RMSE of model by 5%–33%, with RHmax and Tstd showing greater effects on seedling emergence. (4) Emergence monitoring and vegetation index analysis based on remote sensing imagery confirmed that high-vigor seeds identified by AIseed Vigor exhibited significantly (P < 0.01) higher emergence rates and better early growth than low-vigor seeds, demonstrating robust transferability from laboratory to field.

title: Optimal compaction ratio-oriented path planning for combine harvesting of first crop in ratoon rice production under unloading constraints
abstract: Compaction damage to stubbles during the combine harvesting of the first crop in ratoon rice production directly affects the regrowth performance and subsequent yield. Most existing studies on harvesting path planning focus on optimizing harvesting trajectories alone while the effects of grain unloading operations caused by limited grain tank capacity on overall compaction damage and operational efficiency are largely overlooked. To address this issue, this study proposes an integrated path planning method which incorporates unloading constraints for harvesting the first crop of ratoon rice. First, a basic harvesting path was generated based on a quadrilateral full-coverage strategy and the principle of minimizing compaction area, and theoretical full-tank positions were estimated. The unloading process was then categorized into boundary unloading and fixed-point unloading, for which corresponding unloading strategies were designed. In particular, under the fixed-point unloading mode, the multi-point integrated path planning problem was formulated as a planar geometric optimization model based on Fermat point theory. By determining the optimal grain unloading positions, the total unloading travel distance and the associated additional compaction area were minimized. In medium-sized fields (Field 2, 2616.7 m2), the proposed optimization method achieved the highest average compaction ratio reduction of 11.49%, while in small fields (Field 3, 1141.5 m2), a reduction of 4.12% was achieved under the non-fixed unloading mode. This study contributes: (i) a unified harvesting–unloading planning framework; (ii) a Fermat-point-based optimization method for unloading location selection; and (iii) a compaction ratio-oriented evaluation of unloading strategies under different field sizes and unloading modes. Overall, the proposed method reduces unnecessary travel and repeated compaction, thereby improving operational efficiency and providing a path-planning basis for reducing compaction damage during first-crop harvesting in ratoon rice production.

title: A mathematical model for land reform planning: A cutting and packing approach with regular plots
abstract: Land reform is a pivotal issue in Brazil, playing a key role in fostering territorial organization, promoting social equity, driving economic development, and preserving traditional landscapes. Despite its importance, effective territorial planning faces significant challenges due to diverse factors, including property size, topography, environmental constraints, infrastructure, and societal needs. This study introduces a mathematical model based on the cutting and packing problem to aid in the subdivision of lands designated for land reform projects. The model takes into account different soil aptitudes, a desired number of assigned plots, and a minimum productivity level for each plot. Two approaches are considered: maximizing land coverage, and minimizing the maximum productivity of the plots while ensuring a minimum coverage, to balance productivity among plots. Through a set of computational experiments, we obtained solutions that can be used as a practical initial approximation for addressing agrarian reform projects. The resulting properties have rectangular shapes and exhibit good balance, equity, and connectivity. Our study promotes the UN’s sustainable development goals, particularly SDG 1 (No Poverty), 8 (Decent work and economic growth) and 10 (Reduced inequalities).

title: Meteorology-driven early warning of aflatoxin risk in peanuts using combinatorial data augmentation and contrastive learning
abstract: Aflatoxin contamination in peanuts, primarily associated with Aspergillus flavus and Aspergillus parasiticus, poses a severe threat to food safety and public health. However, the limited availability of labeled contamination records and the low prevalence of high-risk observations have hindered the development of accurate and robust aflatoxin risk-prediction tools. This study therefore aims to develop and evaluate a machine-learning framework for predicting short-term aflatoxin risk in peanuts from observed meteorological time-series data during the 30 days preceding harvest, under conditions of limited labeled-record availability and class imbalance arising from the low prevalence of high-risk records. High-risk records were defined as county-year records with mean AFB1 concentrations reaching or exceeding the Chinese national maximum limit of 20 µg/kg for peanuts, while the other records were defined as low-risk. The proposed framework integrates combinatorial data augmentation and contrastive learning to improve high-risk classification within the environmental domain represented by the available observations. Among 1,304 county-year records, 141 were high-risk and 1,163 were low-risk. On the enriched held-out test set, combinatorial data augmentation and contrastive learning (CDA-CL) achieved an accuracy of 0.82, recall of 0.80, precision of 0.55, F1 score of 0.65, and balanced accuracy of 0.82. The framework estimates an aflatoxin risk rather than confirming contamination, which still requires laboratory measurement. By identifying elevated risk from observed meteorological conditions during the 30 days before harvest, the framework may support risk-based handling and targeted confirmatory testing at harvest and post-harvest management. Forecast-driven warning before the relevant meteorological window has occurred remains a future extension requiring dedicated validation.

title: Satellite remote sensing-based in-season prediction of optimal nitrogen rates for corn under diverse on-farm conditions
abstract: Efficient technologies for identifying spatial variability in crop nitrogen (N) responses are urgently needed for optimizing N management under diverse on-farm conditions. Here we present a satellite remote sensing and calibration strip (RSCS) framework for translating in-season crop spectral responses into site-specific optimal N rate (ONR) recommendations in corn (Zea mays L.) production systems. Thirty-five on-farm N rate and management trials were conducted across Minnesota from 2020 to 2024. Gradient preplant N calibration strips enabled block-specific ONR estimation using vegetation index (VI)-based responses derived from PlanetScope satellite imagery. Thirty-four multispectral VIs were evaluated across different corn growth stages (V5–VT), with normalized difference vegetation index (NDVI) and top-performing indices (Top VIs) benchmarked against agronomic and economic optimal N rates (AONR and EONR), farmer N rates, and regional maximum return to N.
