Substantial spatial variability in ONRs was observed across and within fields (112–307 kg N ha−1; CV = 19–20 %), demonstrating that uniform N management strategies could not adequately meet site-specific crop N requirements. The VI-based ONR predictions showed growth-stage dependence, with the V7–V9 window offering the most reliable balance between accuracy and bias, where NDVI performed comparably to Top VIs. Within the V7–V9 window, RSCS achieved near-zero mean bias and 70–74 % Perfect + Good agreement (≤ ±34 kg N ha−1) with EONR across calibration and independent evaluation datasets. A rule-based refinement based on weather, soil, topography, and management interactions was incorporated into the improved RSCS (IRSCS), reducing excessive N recommendations by 2–5 % and increasing Perfect + Good agreement by 3–4 % without raising under-estimation risk. It is concluded that the RSCS and IRSCS strategies can support scalable, adaptive in-season site-specific N recommendations under heterogeneous on-farm conditions.

title: Sensor–algorithm co-design with two-dimensional optical sensing and spatiotemporal labelling for seed passage detection in precision planters
abstract: Accurate seed detection in precision planters is challenging when seeds pass through the seed tube in close spatial or temporal proximity. This work presents a two-dimensional (2D) optical sensor array combined with a spatiotemporal labelling algorithm, which is designed to overcome the limitations of conventional one-dimensional optical and impact-based sensors. The system creates a virtual sensing plane using two perpendicular optical barriers and applies connected component labelling to resolve overlapping shadow events. Experiments involving corn, soybean, and sunflower seeds were conducted under varying seed flow rates, sensor–tube distances, and tube inclinations. These experiments were validated using 500 fps high-speed video. The results demonstrate that the 2D sensing approach achieves a high level of detection accuracy, exceeding 97 % for corn and soybean seeds and 98 % for sunflower seeds when the independent-axis method is applied at short sensor distances. The independent-axis detection strategy also reduced the number of missed and extra detections associated with closely spaced seed passages compared with the combined detection method. Most undetected seeds occurred near the boundaries of the sensing area or at inter-seed intervals below 10 ms. The sensor–algorithm co-design approach provides a robust and computationally efficient alternative to camera-based systems for real-time seed monitoring.

title: A scenario-wise exploring-to-learning planner generation approach for robust path planning of fruit-picking robot
abstract: Fruit picking robots face cluttered environments dense with obstacles and narrow passages—conditions under which traditional sampling‐based planners must plan from scratch, often failing to find feasible paths within time constraints and producing low‐quality paths, suffering from low efficiency and poor robustness. Our key insight is that a robot can autonomously explore complex path planning scenes to accumulate high‐quality path data and then distill them into a knowledge base of efficient local planners—capable of effective sampling—which can then be leveraged to generate scenario-wise global planners for future task scenes. To this end, this work introduces a scenario-wise exploring-to-learning planner (SWEL planner) generation approach, an integrated three‐layer framework for fruit-picking path planning. In the exploring layer, a workspace‐guided exploring algorithm generates high-quality data in simulation and encodes each local region via voxelization and octree structures. The learning layer applies a weighted EM algorithm and position–orientation component matching to model these data into local planners, which populate a knowledge base. In the planning layer, octree‐based similarity retrieval and a virtual‐force‐field fine‐tuning mechanism select and adapt the optimal local planners for the current scene, concatenating them into a global planner to compute a collision‐free path. Extensive simulation and real‐world experiments demonstrate that a knowledge base of 300 local planners is sufficient to meet the needs of fruit-picking path planning, achieving over 80 % success rates and path qualities comparable to hierarchical collaborative algorithm proposed in our previous work, outperforming RRT, AIT*, and maintaining planning times comparable with sampling‐based methods. Physical deployment further confirms SWEL planner’s efficiency and reliability in real world.

title: A novel model for precise segmentation and disease diagnosis of economic forest images in complicated backgrounds
abstract: Dense cultivation of economic trees, along with cluttered backgrounds of bare soil and overgrown weeds, presents significant challenges for accurate canopy segmentation and disease identification from low-altitude UAV images. To solve this problem, this study developed a Haar-UNet based framework for ginkgo canopy segmentation and leaf disease classification, enabling pixel-level recognition of healthy leaves and four disease types in Ginkgo biloba . The proposed model was enhanced by integrating multi-scale convolution (MSC), squeeze-and-excitation (SE) attention mechanisms, and Haar wavelet downsampling (HWD). On the test set, the Haar-UNet canopy segmentation model achieved a mean intersection over union (mIoU) of 93.53% and a pixel accuracy (PA) of 97.92%. Haar-UNet outperformed six other regularly used semantic segmentation models, with an average gain of 5.66% in mIoU and 1.86% in PA. The leaf disease classification model, Haar-DiseaseNet, achieved 95.96% accuracy (Acc) with 0.01 Loss. In compared to commonly used classification models, it improved average Acc by 7.22% and reduced average Loss by 57.52%. These findings show that the Haar-UNet-based canopy semantic segmentation and disease classification framework can identify diseases accurately even in densely planted areas with complicated background interference. The proposed approach can support disease monitoring in Ginkgo biloba plantations and provide a valuable reference for identifying diseases in other economic forests by drone photography.

title: Hwc-YOLOv8n-based optimal harvest-plane estimation and combing-brushing mechanism pose synthesis for Hangzhou white chrysanthemum
abstract: Hangzhou white chrysanthemum is a clustered crop with multiple rounds of harvesting. Harvesting remains largely manual, and the current efficiency cannot meet the increasing market demand. Therefore, intelligent harvesting technologies suitable for unstructured environments are urgently needed. This study aimed to develop an integrated perception–decision–execution approach to address picking-point localization, optimal harvest-plane estimation, and end-effector harvesting execution for selective batch harvesting of Hangzhou white chrysanthemum in unstructured field environments. Building on the previously developed Hwc-YOLOv8n detection model for Hangzhou white chrysanthemum, this study proposes a centroid-offset-based picking-point localization method tailored to the geometric characteristics of the crop. The localization success rates reached 83.9 % for bud-stage chrysanthemums and 87.6 % for full-bloom chrysanthemums. On the basis of the spatial distribution of picking points, an optimal harvest-plane estimation strategy was further developed for Hangzhou white chrysanthemum, and its performance was compared with that of a conventional mean-based harvest-plane estimation strategy in five comparative trials. Compared with the conventional mean-based harvest-plane estimation strategy, the precision and recall of the proposed method improved by up to 40.0 % and 37.5 %, respectively, indicating superior accuracy and adaptability in harvest decision-making. In addition, on the basis of an analysis of the combing-brushing trajectory and poses in the manual harvesting sequence of entry, picking, exit, and unloading using handheld combing teeth, a cam–four-bar integrated harvesting end-effector with four-pose constraints was designed. Using linkage synthesis via the solution region method and the cam inversion method, the four-bar dimensions were determined as follows: crank, 163 mm; coupler, 365 mm; rocker, 365 mm; and frame, 409 mm. Finally, field validation trials were conducted in three trial blocks in the chrysanthemum field. The harvesting trials yielded block-level mean ± SD values of 81.30 % ± 5.82 % for the full-bloom chrysanthemum proportion, 18.24 % ± 0.83 % for the flower damage rate, and 15.60 % ± 6.32 % for the root breakage rate, demonstrating the feasibility of the proposed harvesting system for selective batch harvesting of Hangzhou white chrysanthemum under unstructured field conditions.

title: An explainable deep learning-integrated decision support system for field diagnosis and management of botrytis grey mold in castor
abstract: Botrytis grey mold (BGM) is one of the most economically damaging diseases of castor, causing severe spike infection and substantial yield losses under conducive field conditions. This study developed an artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled decision support framework that integrates deep-learning based disease diagnosis with four years of operationally validated fungicide efficacy experiments. Multiple machine-learning (ML) and deep-learning (DL) algorithms were evaluated for automated BGM detection. Traditional ML models achieved 90–97% accuracy, with a shallow artificial neural network performing best among ML approaches. Deep-learning architectures consistently outperformed ML models, with the Inception Network achieving the highest classification performance (accuracy = 0.97; precision = 0.98; recall = 0.98; F1-score = 0.98; AUC = 1.00). Confusion matrix analysis showed that Inception produced the lowest misclassification rate (9 errors), compared with CNN + Softmax (27) and VGG16 (15). McNemar’s test confirmed the statistically significant superiority of Inception over CNN + Softmax (χ2 = 13.13, p < 0.001) and the improved performance of VGG16 over CNN + Softmax (χ2 = 4.27, p = 0.039). Explainability analysis using Grad-CAM confirmed biologically meaningful learning, with more than 90% of high-activation regions overlapping with BGM lesions, while t-SNE visualisation revealed clear separation between healthy and infected samples. Learning-curve analysis demonstrated stable convergence of accuracy (0.94–0.98) and precision (0.95–1.00) without overfitting. The trained Inception model was deployed through a web-based decision support system for real-time field diagnosis. Four-year field trials identified propiconazole at 2.0–2.5 ml l − 1 as the most effective treatment, consistently achieving low disease severity (9–12%), high yield gains (108–182%), and superior economic returns (B:C ratio = 2.7–2.8). Yield modelling revealed a strong negative relationship between disease severity and yield (r = −0.98), with an estimated yield loss of 13.4 kg ha⁻1 per 1% increase in disease intensity. Overall, this study presents an interpretable, field-validated AI-driven decision support system for accurate BGM diagnosis and evidence-based fungicide management in castor.

title: Toward autonomous inspection in livestock environments: A multi-sensor semantic SLAM framework for pigsty patrol robots
abstract: Automated patrol robots hold great promise for advancing livestock farming by enabling precise monitoring of animal health and environmental conditions. However, their deployment in dense and dynamic environments such as pigsties remains challenging due to the reliance on manually annotated waypoints, which are required to define inspection targets a process that is labor-intensive, inefficient, and lacks flexibility. To address this limitation, we propose a modular multi-sensor semantic SLAM framework that enables fully autonomous navigation through intuitive semantic commands. The system integrates LiDAR, RGB-D camera, and IMU data to construct a unified geometric and semantic representation of the environment in real-time. Key facilities (e.g., troughs, fences, and vents) are automatically detected using a YOLO11n model, and their semantic labels are projected onto the global map frame. An Extended Kalman Filter (EKF) fuses sensor data to ensure accurate coordinate alignment for reliable semantic registration. Comparative experiments against RTAB-Map and DS-SLAM demonstrate that our method achieves superior localization and navigation accuracy. The mean localization error was reduced to 0.6 m, and the navigation deviation averaged 0.7 m representing an improvement of twenty percent over the baseline systems. Moreover, defining navigation goals semantically rather than manually reduces mission configuration time from about five minutes to under 30 s per task. These results highlight the robustness, precision, and operational efficiency of the proposed semantic SLAM system, offering a practical solution for autonomous robotic inspection and livestock management in complex farm environments.

title: Postharvest moisture-level classification using LiDAR point clouds: Integrating 3D structure and spectral intensity
abstract: Moisture content plays a decisive role in the postharvest quality and preservation of horticultural produce. Most non-invasive sensing methods capture either spectral or spatial features, failing to account for structural heterogeneity in fresh tissue and introduced during moisture loss. In this work, a dual wavelengths 3D LiDAR sensor was employed for moisture classification in broccoli and mushrooms. The dataset is comprising spatial coordinates and reflectance intensities at 1320 nm, 1450 nm, and a combined moisture index. Samples include paired ground-truth labels for core and periphery regions, with moisture content categorized into high, medium, and low levels. Results show that by using only reflectance intensity features, the baseline models achieve moderate moisture-level classification performance, with accuracies not exceeding 0.82. Combining geometry with reflectance, particularly at 1450 nm and moisture index, PointNet++ yields the most accurate predictions, achieving up to 0.93 accuracy. Geometric features alone offer limited class discriminability, but contribute to prediction robustness across structurally diverse samples. Spatial generalization experiments reveal an asymmetry: models trained on dense, homogeneous core segments generalize effectively to peripheral regions, whereas those trained on periphery segments exhibit reduced accuracy when evaluated on core data. Modality perturbation shows that intensity provides the dominant moisture-sensitive signal, particularly at 1450 nm, while geometry contributes complementary cues that stabilize predictions. At 1320 nm, showing low spectral sensitivity to moisture, reliable classification requires joint use of both modalities. These findings establish LiDAR as an efficient non-invasive moisture monitoring tool in heterogeneous agricultural products. Code: github.com/majharB/vegPoint .

title: Map-constrained LiDAR-IMU localization and segmented tracking control for tracked orchard robot navigation
abstract: Autonomous navigation is essential for orchard inspection and spraying robots, but it is challenged by degraded GNSS signals, dense 3D point clouds, and unstable headland maneuvers of tracked chassis. This study develops a transferable Perception–Decision–Execution (PDE) navigation system for inspection-mapping, lightweight spraying, and high-capacity spraying tracked platforms. Prior 3D orchard point clouds are converted into lightweight 2D topological maps for segmented path generation, while the original 3D map is retained for map-constrained LiDAR–IMU localization. GNSS/IMU supplies a one-time startup pose anchor, after which prior-map LiDAR–IMU matching maintains continuous localization. At the execution layer, a segmented PBR (SPBR) controller decomposes tracked-chassis motion into inter-row tracking, in-place heading alignment, and post-turn recovery. Field experiments in a standardized apple orchard demonstrated functional operation on all three tracked platforms, and quantitative trajectory-tracking evaluation was conducted on the 70 L boom-spraying platform. In repeated startup trials, GNSS/IMU anchoring achieved successful direct initialization in 3/3 trials and recovered all 3/3 manually biased initializations, whereas biased manual initialization alone succeeded in 1/3 trials. In repeated open-field experiments with five tracking-control configurations, SPBR achieved an RMSE of 0.0681±0.0066m, reducing RMSE by 65.0% and 51.7% relative to continuous PID and continuous differential orthexp, and by 35.8% and 30.5% relative to the corresponding turn-aware configurations, respectively. In an additional canopy-occluded field test, the robot completed all 11/11 path segments in three repeated runs using continuous prior-map LiDAR–IMU localization feedback. The coverage-complete run supplied 18 quality-gated RTK checkpoints, providing a sparse external check of RTK-to-path proximity at the sampled locations. These results provide a reusable navigation reference for tracked orchard management robots.

title: Co-optimization of productivity and environmental sustainability in China’s maize systems under future climate scenarios
abstract: Balancing agricultural productivity, environmental sustainability, and economic viability is a central challenge for future food systems under climate change. In maize production, yield gains are often pursued through intensified management, frequently at the expense of higher nitrous oxide (N2O) emissions and production costs. This study integrated interpretable machine learning and multi-objective optimization to balance maize yield and N2O emissions under 2050s climate scenarios, followed by an economic evaluation of the optimized strategies. A national dataset of 10,505 field observations across six maize-growing regions in China was assembled to develop interpretable machine-learning models, achieving strong predictive performance for maize yield (R2 = 0.9146) and N2O emissions (R2 = 0.8651). Future climate conditions were derived from Coupled Model Intercomparison Project Phase 6 climate projections, and Pareto-optimal solutions were identified using the non-dominated sorting genetic algorithm II. Results revealed a robust non-linear yield–emission trade-off, with environmental costs increasing sharply as yield approached its upper range. Relative to the baseline scenario, cooperative solutions achieved national average improvements of 48.26% in yield and 13.59% in N2O emission reduction while avoiding excessive input costs. Pronounced regional heterogeneity was observed, with yield generally decreasing from north to south and N2O emissions remaining relatively higher in southeastern regions. Cooperative outcomes were achieved through region-specific combinations of agronomic management practices, with yields spanning 6.71–14.23 t·ha−1 and N2O emissions ranging from 0.42 to 6.05 kg N2O–N·ha−1. These findings demonstrate that shifting from input intensification toward region-specific management provides a viable pathway for economically feasible and climate-resilient maize production.

title: FTP-Stitch: rapid UAV thermal infrared remote sensing image stitching based on feature alignment and flight trajectory preservation
abstract: Thermal infrared image stitching in agricultural remote sensing often suffers from challenges such as low texture, temperature drift, and low geometric resolution. Furthermore, real-time responsiveness is highly demanded in agricultural applications, making it imperative to develop efficient and robust stitching methods. To address these challenges, we propose FTP-Stitch, a fast and robust thermal infrared image stitching method based on feature alignment and flight trajectory preservation under similarity transformation constraints. Specifically, building upon the similarity transformation model adopted in MegaStitch, we introduce a Flight Trajectory Preservation (FTP) term, which utilizes prior GNSS-based UAV flight paths to provide stable pixel shift estimation for each image, thereby accurately preserving their relative positions in physical space. Then, by jointly optimizing the feature alignment term and the FTP term, we construct a least-squares optimization model under similarity transformation constraints to solve the corresponding transformation matrices. To validate the effectiveness of the proposed method, we conduct extensive experiments on a thermal infrared remote sensing dataset that covers various crop types, flight altitudes, and environmental conditions. We evaluate the stitching results both subjectively and objectively in terms of alignment accuracy, visual naturalness, and stitching efficiency. Experimental results demonstrate that, compared with existing state-of-the-art thermal infrared stitching methods, the proposed method reduces the average RMSE by 19.7 % compared with OP-GSP and by 35.1 % compared with MegaStitch, while reducing the average stitching time by 78.0 % compared with OP-GSP. Meanwhile, superior performance is achieved in both geometric alignment and visual quality. This offers an effective solution for rapid large-scale thermal infrared image stitching in agricultural UAV remote sensing applications.

title: A ConvNeXt–Liquid Neural Network framework for accurate RL disease classification
abstract: Accurate identification of Rice Leaf (RL) diseases plays a vital role in precision agriculture and global food security. This study proposes a hybrid ConvNeXt–Liquid Neural Network (ConvNeXt–LNN) framework for classification of RL diseases using image data acquired under real-field scenarios. The proposed architecture couples hierarchical convolutional feature extraction provided by ConvNeXt with the continuous-time learning dynamics of LNNs, thereby enabling refinement of disease-related feature representations for RL disease classification. The proposed framework is evaluated on a benchmark RL image dataset comprising ten categories, including multiple disease types and healthy leaves collected under heterogeneous illumination, complex background conditions, and varying levels of disease severity. The proposed architecture achieves the accuracy of 97.51% compared with traditional algorithms. The proposed ConvNeXt-LNN achieves competitive classification accuracy with only 7.8 million trainable parameters, approximately 625.79 s per training epoch, and reduced computational cost. These results indicate the potential of the proposed framework for future deployment in smart agriculture ecosystems, including mobile, edge, and UAV-based crop monitoring platforms.

title: Industrial applications of integrated fluidized systems with biomass-air separation and impurity sorting: a novel CFD-DEM and PIV synergistic approach
abstract: The efficient classification of agricultural biomass, which involves the separation of elongated particles from the air stream (particle-air separation) and the sorting of spherical impurities, remains a significant challenge in sustainable biorefining. Traditional fluidized beds often struggle to balance the conflicting hydrodynamic requirements for these two processes within a single, efficient system. This study first puts forward an integrated vortex-dominated bifurcation fluidized system, with its performance validated through synergistic CFD-DEM simulations and scaled-model PIV experiments. For elongated particle fluidization, flow bifurcation occurs in the Z-shaped channel, with particles either following vortex streams or ascending toward the particle-air separation section. Industrial applications for spherical particle sorting are also explored, supported by image experiments. The results show that after multiple iterative designs, the final optimized model reduces the system height by 304 mm and enhances particle-air separation by 71% compared with the initial model, with only 2% of usable particles entering the right side of the baffle. Approximately 8% of usable particles enter the spiral transport channel with impurities, increasing mixture separation efficiency by 33%. High-speed image experiments with the scaled model suggest that the outflow ratio of clean particles mixed with impurities was measured at 10%, slightly higher than the simulation results (3%). This synergistic CFD-DEM-PIV methodology provides new insights into designing and optimizing integrated fluidized systems for intelligent agricultural equipment, demonstrating substantial potential for energy efficiency and environmental sustainability in biomass processing.

title: A TRNSYS-CONTAM model as a simulator to identify energy-VPD trade-offs in Nordic greenhouses
abstract: This study presents a validated modeling framework to optimize microclimate control in naturally ventilated tomato greenhouses. An integrated TRNSYS-CONTAM model incorporating natural ventilation dynamics, evapotranspiration, CO2 enrichment, and condensation effects, is developed addressing critical gaps in existing greenhouse models. Validation against January-November operational data using ASHRAE Guideline 14 showed strong temperature performance, with monthly NMBE ranging from −3.24% to 4.07% and CV(RMSE) from 6.44% to 14.75%. Humidity predictions were more variable: relative humidity NMBE ranged from −7.19% to 18.11% and CV(RMSE) from 13.27% to 25.56%, while absolute humidity NMBE ranged from −9.06% to 18.96% and CV(RMSE) from 15.62% to 26.71%. The model explicitly accounts for plant-related heat losses (20% of total), significantly improving energy balance accuracy. The analysis reveals only 43% of vapor pressure deficit (VPD) measurements fell within the optimal 0.5–1.2 kPa range for tomato growth under natural ventilation. Three simulation scenarios were then evaluated: (1) natural ventilation only (43.85% VPD satisfaction), (2) natural ventilation, mechanical dehumidification, and fogging (61.19%), and (3) mechanical dehumidification and fogging without natural ventilation (75.27%). Relative to natural ventilation only, VPD satisfaction improved by 17.34 percentage points in Scenario B and 31.42 percentage points in Scenario C, while simulated thermal-energy demand increased from 427 to 1878 kWh/m2. These findings highlight a critical efficiency frontier in greenhouse climate control, where each percentage point of VPD improvement requires careful energy investment. The study provides three key contributions: first, a validated microclimate prediction tool; second, quantitative benchmarks for VPD control strategies; and third, clear evidence supporting the development of adaptive control algorithms to optimize the energy-VPD trade-off.

title: Digital twins in poultry farming management: A review
abstract: Digital twins, defined as dynamic virtual representations of physical systems, offer potential to facilitate real-time monitoring, improve predictive capabilities, and support data-driven decision-making. The application of digital twins in poultry farming management has attracted increasing attention, however, it remains insufficiently explored, particularly in terms of framework development and layer-wise functionalities. This review presents a comprehensive study of digital twin development and components in poultry farming management, addressing the current lack of structured frameworks and systematic analysis in this domain. In this context, poultry farming management is defined as the strategic planning and implementation of a series of farm operations, including monitoring, detection, and prediction, to enhance production efficiency and achieve economic sustainability. Based on the existing literature, a three-layer digital twin framework is proposed, consisting of a data collection layer, a model layer, and an application layer. Within this framework, farm data are first captured and gathered in the data collection layer, then processed and simulated in the model layer, and finally utilized to support decision-making in the application layer. Through a detailed layer-wise analysis, the study highlights the critical role of model calibration and synchronization in ensuring consistency between physical and virtual systems. While offering promising potential, the adoption of digital twin technology in poultry farming faces several challenges, including challenges in real-world deployment, limited system integration, issues related to data quality and ownership, and insufficient solutions to ensure animal health and welfare. Finally, the study summarizes future research directions for digital twin applications in livestock production systems.

title: A Scalable Pipeline Combining Procedural 3D Graphics and Guided Diffusion for Photorealistic Synthetic Training Data Generation in White Button Mushroom Segmentation
abstract: Industrial mushroom cultivation increasingly relies on computer vision for monitoring and automated harvesting. However, developing accurate detection and segmentation models requires large, precisely annotated datasets that are costly to produce. Synthetic data provides a scalable alternative, yet often lacks sufficient realism to generalize to real-world scenarios. This paper presents a novel workflow that integrates 3D rendering in Blender with a constrained diffusion model to automatically generate high-quality annotated, photorealistic synthetic images of Agaricus Bisporus mushrooms. This approach preserves full control over 3D scene configuration and annotations while achieving photorealism without the need for specialized computer graphics expertise. We release two synthetic datasets (each containing 6000 images depicting over 250k mushroom instances) and evaluate Mask R-CNN models trained on them in a zero-shot setting. When tested on two independent real-world datasets (including a newly collected benchmark), our method achieves state-of-the-art segmentation performance (F1 = 0.859 on M18K), despite using only synthetic training data. Although the approach is demonstrated on Agaricus Bisporus mushrooms, the proposed pipeline can be readily adapted to other mushroom species or to other agricultural domains, such as fruit and leaf detection.

title: Tuning into plant ultrasonics: Can acoustics enable smart agriculture?
abstract: Plant ultrasonic acoustic emissions (UAEs) are low-intensity sound signals that arise primarily from physiological processes associated with transpiration-driven water transport. By monitoring these emissions, researchers and farmers can detect physiological changes related to water/drought stress, heat stress, or disease, allowing timely interventions and optimized resource management. However, substantial variability in UAEs across plant species and environmental conditions, together with limited detection sensitivity and a lack of standardized measurement protocols, present significant challenges for robust interpretation and large scale deployment. Recent advancements in portable sensor technologies and network integration, supported by collaborations between crop physiologists, engineers, and data scientists, aim to address some of these challenges. Standardization efforts and more robust methodologies for data collection and analysis are emerging, alongside innovative applications in precision agriculture. These developments promise to boost crop yields, enhance sustainability, and increase resilience to environmental stressors. In this perspective article, we review the current state of plant acoustics research,critically assess available sensing and analytical approaches, and discuss both their opportunities and limitations. We further argue that targeted research into the biological interpretation of UAEs’ including their potential roles in plant-to-plant and plant–animal interactions, in natural ecosystems as well as in controlled environments like greenhouses and vertical farms, is crucial. Within a smart farming toolkit, plant acoustics may become a complementary tool for applications in agriculture, forestry, plant breeding, and conservation, provided that integration across sensing, data analytics, and agronomic decision-making is achieved.

title: A free-view registration network with geometric generation for unrestricted pig body size measurement
abstract: Multi-view point cloud registration is essential for non-contact pig body size measurement. Existing systems usually rely on calibration objects, fixed acquisition scenes, or passage-based constraints, which increase manual workload and may affect pigs’ natural posture. To address these limitations, this study develops an unrestricted three-view RGB-D acquisition system and an automatic registration network, named FVGG-RegNet, for pig body size measurement in native pen environments. The proposed Free-View Geometric Generation (FVGG) module generates free-view point clouds from fixed-view data under geometric constraints, thereby enriching geometric priors and improving the adaptability of the model to different camera configurations and acquisition scenes. In addition, FVGG-RegNet adopts a coarse-to-fine registration strategy, in which attention-based superpoint matching is first used to establish robust correspondences, followed by dense point matching for accurate transformation estimation. This end-to-end network enables automatic multi-view point cloud registration without calibration objects or manual intervention. Experimental results show that FVGG-RegNet achieved an Inlier Ratio (IR) of 85.7%, a Relative Rotation Error (RRE) of 0.51°, and a Relative Translation Error (RTE) of 1.2 cm. Measurement experiments across five body dimensionsresulted mean absolute errors (MAEs) ranging from 1.2 to 2.1 cm. These results indicate that the proposed system has practical applicability for scalable, non-contact, and low-stress pig body size measurement in large-scale farm environments.

title: Computational approaches for modelling soil water repellency: A comprehensive review
abstract: Soil water repellency (SWR) is a significant soil constraint in agricultural systems, impacting water infiltration, crop establishment, and productivity, especially in sandy soils. Accurate assessment and prediction of SWR are essential for enhancing soil and water management practices. Traditional measurement techniques, including molarity of ethanol droplet and water drop penetration time tests, provide reliable assessments on point-based samples. However, these methods require significant labour and time inputs to extend SWR assessments to farm and regional scales. Recent computational approaches integrating statistical analysis, remote sensing, machine learning, deep learning, and geospatial techniques have emerged as promising alternatives for SWR assessment and prediction. This study reviews existing computational approaches used for modelling SWR and related soil properties across agricultural systems. It synthesises commonly used data sources, including remote sensing imagery, vegetation indices, climate variables, topographic information, and soil properties, together with preprocessing techniques, modelling methods, and evaluation metrics. Furthermore, the review examines the strengths and limitations of existing approaches in terms of prediction accuracy, scalability, spatial–temporal generalisation, and interpretability. Particular attention is given to explainable artificial intelligence techniques for understanding the environmental drivers influencing SWR variability. Based on the reviewed literature, this study identifies existing research gaps and presents future research directions for developing scalable, interpretable, and data-driven computational frameworks for SWR modelling and precision soil management.

title: Label-efficient structure-aware learning framework for wheat tiller density estimation from UAV remote sensing
abstract: Tiller density is an important agronomic trait related to wheat growth diagnosis and yield formation. UAV remote sensing enables field-scale monitoring, but reliable estimation is challenged by changing canopy appearance, soil and shadow interference, and costly ground-label collection. We propose a label-efficient, structure-aware framework for wheat tiller-density estimation from UAV RGB and multispectral imagery. The framework integrates 3B-SSCL for self-supervised crop-background segmentation, MVDINO for RGB canopy-context representation learning, and GIDVF for guided fusion with multispectral vegetation indices. Using 377 source-field samples from Field 1 collected across four dates, the model achieved R2 = 0.8811 ± 0.0249 under repeated random validation and R2 = 0.8753 ± 0.0141 under leave-location-out validation. Under cross-field adaptation to an independent Field 2, it achieved R2 = 0.8145 ± 0.0959 with 50 target-field labels under a locked target-test protocol. At this budget, its mean R2 exceeded the corresponding values of the evaluated baseline methods when they used the complete 70-label adaptation pool. Across the tested budgets, the proposed framework maintained this advantage, with its learning curve approaching a stable performance level at approximately 50 labels. Together, these results show that the framework can achieve effective cross-field transfer with a practical target-field label budget while reducing reliance on extensive new labels.

title: Performance trade-offs between single-task and multi-task in multi-source prediction of yield and grain protein content in winter wheat
abstract: Early-season prediction of winter wheat yield and grain protein content is essential for guiding fertilizer and irrigation decisions and reducing uncertainty in variable agroecosystems, as yield affects profitability and quality affects market value and nutrition. Although multi-source data and both single-task learning (STL) and multi-task learning (MTL) are widely used for predicting grain yield and quality, the conditions under which each approach performs best remain poorly understood, especially when data availability, noise, and measurement or computational constraints vary. To address this gap, we conducted a three-year field experiment in Henan Province, China, compiling environmental, agronomic, and proximal-sensing variables across five growth stages. Seven subsets were constructed, including environmental, agronomic, sensor, and combined subsets, and STL/MTL variants of Multilayer Perceptron (MLP), Transformer, and Random Forest (RF) were benchmarked. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis quantified feature- and stage-level contributions and guided construction of compact Top-K subsets for accuracy–efficiency trade-offs. Multi-source fusion substantially improved accuracy over single-source inputs, with the combined agronomic-sensor subset providing the best performance (yield R 2 = 0.823; GPC R 2 = 0.743). Under the current stage-aggregated multi-source representation, MLPs outperformed Transformers and RFs across configurations, indicating that compact nonlinear models were better suited to the present medium-dimensional tabular setting. MTL provided the greatest benefit with sparse feature sets or imbalanced predictive difficulty, whereas STL performed better when information was abundant and signals were strong. SHAP analysis showed that agronomic and sensor features associated with biomass accumulation, nitrogen status, water availability, and canopy light interception were key drivers of model predictions, particularly during erecting and early grain filling. These findings further show that the value of STL versus MTL depends on data-source composition and information richness, and that SHAP can be used not only for interpretation but also for reduced-feature subset design. Within the present plot-scale setting, this study therefore provides a decision-oriented framework for identifying both accuracy-oriented and efficiency-oriented configurations, with efficiency referring to feature parsimony, reduced input and preprocessing burden, and computational time for winter wheat yield and GPC.

title: WMA-YieldNet: A weather-modulated attention network for cross-year winter wheat yield prediction using multi-stage hyperspectral data
abstract: Accurate prediction of winter wheat yield is essential for precision agricultural management and assessing food security. However, existing methods still have limitations in utilizing multi-stage growth information and adapting to interannual environmental variation. This study proposes WMA-YieldNet, a multimodal deep learning model that integrates canopy hyperspectral data and stage-specific meteorological variables from the jointing, flowering, and filling stages. The model improves environmental adaptation through FiLM-based meteorological modulation, enhances multi-stage feature integration through stage-attention fusion, and strengthens learning from extreme-yield samples through a dynamic weighted-loss strategy. WMA-YieldNet achieved stable performance on the independent 2025 test set, with an R2 of 0.80 ± 0.01, an RMSE of 871.74 ± 28.58 kg ha⁻1, and an nRMSE of 15.11 ± 0.50%, outperforming SVR, RF, 1D-CNN, Bi-LSTM, TCN, and Stage-Transformer. Preliminary independent-site validation using the Xinxiang 2026 field dataset showed moderate transferability, with an R2 of 0.75 ± 0.03, an RMSE of 1255.58 ± 71.60 kg ha⁻1, and an nRMSE of 16.99 ± 0.97%, although predictions showed a tendency toward yield underestimation. Ablation experiments and interpretability analysis revealed that FiLM-based meteorological modulation, stage-attention fusion, and the dynamic weighted-loss strategy all contributed to model performance. Attention-weight and meteorological-importance analyses further indicated that flowering and filling stages contributed most to yield prediction and that radiation and precipitation were key environmental drivers. These results suggest that WMA-YieldNet provides an effective framework for multi-stage, weather-aware winter wheat yield prediction under independent field conditions.

title: Effects of Plasma-Assisted atomization and nozzle diameter on droplet dynamics and lettuce performance in aeroponics
abstract: Optimizing droplet behavior, nutrient chemistry, and root-zone conditions is essential for improving aeroponic crop production. This study evaluated plasma-assisted aeroponics with five nozzle diameters (0.2–1.0 mm) under controlled-room and greenhouse conditions to investigate mist dynamics, nutrient-solution chemistry, microclimate behavior, and lettuce performance. A non-plasma treatment was applied only under the 0.6 mm nozzle condition and served as the control. Plasma was generated using a needle-to-needle corona discharge device with a maximum voltage of 38 kV and applied three times daily for 5 min. Chamber temperature, relative humidity, plasma-related gases (NH3 and O3), and nutrient-solution properties (pH, electrical conductivity, and oxidation–reduction potential) were continuously monitored during cultivation, while lettuce growth and yield traits were measured. Three-dimensional computational fluid dynamics simulations were conducted to analyze droplet transport, spatial distribution, deposition behavior, and wall-film thickness development inside the aeroponic chamber. Mesh independence analysis confirmed the numerical robustness of the CFD model. Simulated wall-film trends agreed with a theoretical model (R2 = 0.932; MAE = 3.2 %), reflecting CFD–theory consistency rather than experimental validation. Droplet size strongly influenced deposition and mist uniformity, with the 0.6 mm nozzle performing best. Plasma treatment reduced pH, increased oxidation–reduction potential, and influenced electrical conductivity through treatment–environment interactions, while intermediate droplets produced more stable microclimatic conditions than finer sprays. The 0.6 mm plasma nozzle produced the highest nitrate concentration, lowest nitrite concentration, leaf area, and greatest biomass and edible yield, exceeding the non-plasma control by 25–45 %. Overall, plasma-assisted aeroponics improved nutrient utilization, stability, and lettuce productivity.

title: Hybrid modeling of greenhouse tomato growth using a scale-adaptive temporal convolutional network
abstract: Accurate estimation of plants’ growth is critical for precise greenhouse control. Current process-based models are often difficult to parameterize, while general deep learning methods often operate at fixed temporal scales and lack mechanisms to prevent physiologically implausible predictions. To address these limitations, this study proposes a knowledge-and-data-driven hybrid model for tomato plant growth estimation, leveraging adaptive temporal feature extraction. The core contribution is a scale-adaptive temporal convolutional network (SATCN) that dynamically captures multi-scale features from environmental data, thereby strengthening tomato plant growth representation capability by adapting to distinct response patterns to environmental changes across developmental stages. The SATCN is integrated with an Informer module to further strengthen its feature extraction capability. In addition, a threshold-based loss function during training effectively constrains outputs to reasonable ranges. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed SATCN-Informer model achieves high prediction accuracy, with RMSE s of 18.52 gm-2 for cumulative leaf dry mass (CLDM), 7.34 gm-2 for cumulative stem dry mass (CSDM), 19.47 gm-2 for cumulative fruit dry mass (CFDM), and 0.30 for leaf area index (LAI). The model significantly outperforms existing methods, including fixed-scale deep learning approaches. Performance improvement was particularly evident in early growth stages, where it reduced relative error by 10.28 percentage points for CLDM, 6.90 percentage points for CSDM, 21.17 percentage points for CFDM, and 6.37 percentage points for LAI compared to the best baseline, confirming enhanced robustness to growth dynamics. This approach enables non-destructive estimation of the growth of tomato plants based on greenhouse-environment and cultivation factors, holding promising practical value.

title: A virtual nozzle model for the DEM-CFD simulation of agricultural spraying processes
abstract: In crop protection, the assessment of innovations such as spot spraying, pulse width modulation or variable rate application requires new test methods. Their dynamic parameters (e. g. on/off, changing volume flow and concentration of active ingredient) raise new questions concerning, for example, lateral distribution, accuracy of spraying or drift measures under a wide range of parameter settings and spraying techniques used. This cannot be answered easily using conventional test methods. For this reason, new approaches are necessary for the assessment and also for a better understanding of the dynamic behaviour during application. Simulation can be a helpful tool for this problem, but it requires a suitable and precise nozzle model. In this paper results from the creation of a virtual flat fan nozzle and its coupled DEM-CFD simulation are presented. Based on measurement data from various test rigs in the laboratory, the behaviour of a real nozzle was analysed in a plane 100 mm below the orifice in order to create a virtual nozzle in MATLAB that does not require iterative calibration of parameters such as the droplet velocity and the angle of flight, as is necessary for the simulation models described to date. This virtual nozzle was used for bidirectional coupled DEM-CFD simulations using Altair EDEM and AcuSolve. In these the movement of the droplets between the virtual nozzle and the target surface and their interaction with the surrounding air were calculated. A validation of the shown approach to create a virtual nozzle model was carried out by comparing the measured lateral volumetric distribution with the distribution in the simulation model for one and five nozzles on a spray boom at two spraying heights. Furthermore, a scenario with a crosswind was simulated as an example application of the virtual nozzle in order to analyse the drift of the spray fan.

title: A feature-preserving and imbalance-aware network for strawberry maturity detection
abstract: Accurate strawberry maturity detection is essential for intelligent harvesting and grading but remains challenging because adjacent maturity stages are visually similar and class distributions are imbalanced. This study proposes AD-YOLO26, an improved detector for three-class strawberry maturity recognition. The model combines architectural and loss-function improvements. An adaptive downsampling module (ADown) is introduced into the backbone to preserve discriminative color, texture, and local morphological information during feature compression, while a dynamic upsampling module (DySample) replaces fixed interpolation in the neck to enable content-aware reconstruction of fine-grained maturity features. In addition, annotation-derived class weights are incorporated into the BCE loss to increase the contribution of minority classes and reduce prediction bias toward the majority class. The main contribution is the problem-driven coordination of these established components as an architecture–loss design, supported by controlled ablation experiments and cross-dataset validation. AD-YOLO26 was compared with YOLOv5, YOLOv8, YOLOv10, YOLOv11, YOLOv12, YOLOv13, RT-DETR-r18, RT-DETR-r50, and YOLO26 under identical experimental settings. Across three repeated experiments, AD-YOLO26 achieved the best overall performance, with mean precision, recall, F1-score, mAP@50, mAP@75, and mAP@50–95 values of 0.9797, 0.9831, 0.9813, 0.9924, 0.9331, and 0.8258, respectively. Compared with YOLO26, it improved mAP@75 and mAP@50–95 by 0.1220 and 0.1295, while reducing GFLOPs from 5.2 to 4.4 and model size from 29.3 MB to 25.6 MB. AD-YOLO26 achieved an average inference speed of 327.63 FPS on the local server. When deployed on an NVIDIA Jetson Orin NX 16 GB platform in MAXN SUPER mode, it reached 25.50 FPS, compared with 30.49 FPS for YOLO26, demonstrating practical real-time or near-real-time edge deployment capability. Validation on three public strawberry and tomato datasets further confirmed good generalization and transferability. Overall, AD-YOLO26 achieves a favorable balance among detection accuracy, computational complexity, and deployment efficiency, providing a promising solution for intelligent strawberry maturity detection.

title: Editorial Board
LARIS: a local-state active reasoning and integrated switching framework for robotic harvesting under partial observability
abstract: Robotic tomato harvesting in dense greenhouse clusters remains difficult because local visibility, accessibility, and contact safety change during observation and execution. Existing harvesting pipelines often separate perception from execution, which can lead to redundant views or failed harvesting attempts. This study proposes LARIS, an execution-oriented framework that integrates local-state reasoning with feasibility-guided observation–harvesting decision-making. LARIS formulates an integrated local execution-state representation to describe target geometry, neighboring local-structure evidence, free-space evidence, and residual uncertainty. Based on this state, it switches between supplementary observation and harvesting according to execution sufficiency rather than visual completeness alone, and adapts approach, contact, and retraction margins to residual uncertainty. In greenhouse experiments, LARIS achieved a harvesting success rate of 79.6% (133/167; 95% CI: 72.9–85.0%), with 1.60 ± 1.33 supplementary observations and a cycle time of 8.71 ± 1.33 s per attempt. In indoor reconstructed-cluster experiments, LARIS achieved a success rate of 84.1% (127/151; 95% CI: 77.4–89.1%). These results indicate that LARIS can improve harvesting reliability and efficiency under the tested greenhouse conditions with dense tomato clusters.

title: Validation of CFD-SAAS, a modeling tool for predicting pesticide spray deposition and drift from air-assisted sprayers in apple orchards
abstract: A computational fluid dynamics (CFD) based computer program, Simulation of Air-Assisted Sprayers (SAAS), was developed to predict pesticide spray deposition and drift risk for conventional and intelligent orchard sprayers under various weather and field conditions. However, the predictive accuracy of SAAS must be validated to ensure reliability. The CFD simulations used to generate the SAAS data (CFD-SAAS) and the direct output of the SAAS were both analyzed. In-field measurements of airborne drift and spray deposition on the canopy and ground from a conventional and intelligent sprayer in an experimental apple orchard were used for the validations. Mass balances of total spray deposition and airborne drift were included in the validation analyses. CFD-SAAS was valid for predicting the deposition on the canopy and ground at specific locations, with average relative errors of 36.4% and 34.4%, respectively. In addition, the model successfully predicted spatial distributions of airborne drift at distances from 3 m to 12 m downwind and heights up to 2 m above the ground with average relative errors of 16.8% and 20.4% for a conventional and intelligent sprayer, respectively. Furthermore, the CFD-SAAS was able to accurately predict the droplet mass balance for the ground deposition at downwind distances up to 48 m for the conventional sprayer and up to 12 m for the intelligent sprayer with an overall relative error of 37.5%.

title: AquaAgent-OSPy: an auditable LLM tool-agent system for simulation-grounded irrigation decision support
abstract: Irrigation scheduling in agricultural water management requires balancing crop yield, water efficiency, and safety constraints under inter-annual rainfall variability. Existing approaches − fixed irrigation calendars, numerical optimizers, and conversational AI advisors − share a common gap: they do not deliver model-grounded recommendations that are simultaneously traceable, safety-checked, and adaptive to climate conditions. AquaAgent-OSPy is an A4-class code-executing large language model (LLM) tool-agent that orchestrates AquaCrop-OSPy irrigation scenario simulations, non-dominated sorting genetic algorithm II (NSGA-II) multi-objective optimization, Google Earth Engine (GEE) site context verification, and an illustrative seasonal-irrigation safety checker to generate auditable action memos with full tool provenance. The system was evaluated at two confirmed Korean paddy rice sites (Gimje, Jeollabuk-do and Hampyeong, Jeollanam-do) across three contrasting climate years (403–824 mm May-September growing-season precipitation) using a five-item binary faithfulness rubric (F1-F5). As a pilot unit-audit of memo traceability, not a statistical reliability estimate for LLM behavior, four confirmed-site action memos passed all rubric items (20/20 combined). The evaluation produced four findings: (1) the GEE land-cover and Sentinel-1 synthetic aperture radar (SAR) pipeline caught an automated site-selection error and confirmed paddy rice phenology at both sites; (2) in a severe drought year (2015, 403 mm), the fixed weekly schedule triggered the illustrative high-irrigation safety flag (239 mm > 200 mm) and achieved lower water productivity (WP) than the selected low-irrigation threshold strategy under shared AquaCrop-OSPy assumptions; (3) across all four primary evaluation cases, the agent recommended soil-moisture threshold (SMT) scheduling or zero irrigation and never recommended a safety-flagged strategy, while scenario results from all six case-year combinations supported the same within-model water-saving advisory pattern; (4) AquaCrop-OSPy PaddyRice outputs were qualitatively aligned with a published Thailand site (Veerakachen and Raksapatcharawong, 2020; rainfed yield 4.77 t/ha within a reported 3–5 t/ha range), providing a plausibility check rather than Korean field validation. Soil hydraulic parameters were cross-checked against SoilGrids v2.0. AquaAgent-OSPy is intended for agronomist review: it links recommendations to simulation outputs and safety checks, but it does not authorize or actuate irrigation.

title: BOD-YOLO: a Mamba-like linear attention and UniRepLknet framework for oriented bee detection and counting in infrared hive imagery
abstract: Real-time detection and quantification of honeybees are vital prerequisites for effective colony health management and in-depth studies of pollination behavior in agroecological monitoring, the accuracy of existing detection methods is significantly limited by factors such as frequent object occlusion, dynamic bee flight postures, and the inherently low resolution of infrared images captured in dense colony settings. In this study, we propose the BOD-YOLO directional target detection framework, which addresses the limitations of the traditional horizontal bounding box (HBB) in complex bee colony infrared images with high background interference and high overlap rate of detected frames by means of a oriented bounding box (OBB) and an improved attention mechanism. The method is based on the improved YOLOv11 architecture, which employs Mamba-Like Linear Attention (MLLA) to enhance small-target feature focusing capability, combines UniRepLKNet and C2PMA to optimise multi-scale feature extraction, and introduces Linear Deformable Convolution (LDConv) to improve the model adaptability. In addition, a BODC2025 dataset containing 3,875 infrared images and more than 300,000 instances is constructed. Compared with the benchmark approach, quantitative experiments reveal that BOD-YOLO achieves significant performance gains, boosting mAP@0.5 and mAP@0.5:0.95 by 2.8 % and 2.9 %, respectively. In terms of efficiency, BOD-YOLO reduces GFLOPs from 22.5 to 14.1 and decreases the stored model size from 22.8 MB to 19.11 MB, with only a slight increase in parameter count from 9.71 M to 9.67 M, demonstrating a favorable accuracy-efficiency trade-off. Furthermore, the framework operates at a real-time inference speed of 204 frames per second (FPS). This framework provides a highly efficient solution for the directional detection of dense small targets in agricultural scenarios, which supports ecological research, pollination analysis, and precision agriculture applications.

title: An efficient lightweight XHP-CNN with multi-task adaptation for mango leaf disease recognition on mobile edge devices
abstract: Timely and accurate identification of plant diseases is critical for effective disease management and agricultural sustainability. However, existing deep learning-based approaches are often limited by high computational costs and hardware demands, restricting their deployment in field environments. A cross-layer hybrid pooling (XHP) mechanism, combining max and average pooling to enhance feature extraction while mitigating overfitting caused by complex backgrounds, is incorporated into an efficient lightweight convolutional neural network (CNN), termed XHP-CNN, proposed in this study. The proposed model achieves 99.3 % accuracy on field-collected mango leaf disease datasets, utilizing only 0.35 million parameters significantly fewer than conventional models. Moreover, XHP-CNN demonstrates robust generalization, attaining an average accuracy of 96.0 % on previously unseen mango leaf diseases through multi-task learning and fine-tuning without requiring full retraining. The model is successfully deployed on Android-based edge devices, achieving a practical accuracy of 90.7 % in real orchard environments. This lightweight and scalable solution meets the growing demand for cost-effective, edge artificial intelligence (AI)-based mango leaf disease diagnosis in smart agriculture applications.

title: Systematic review and meta-analysis of adoption, acceptance, and perceptions of precision livestock farming technology
abstract: Digital technologies are increasingly reshaping livestock production systems, with precision livestock farming (PLF) emerging as a key innovation that uses sensor-based monitoring and data analytics to support animal management, welfare oversight, and decision-making on farms. Despite PLF’s technical potential, adoption across the livestock sector remains uneven, and stakeholder perceptions of these technologies vary widely. This study provides a meta-analysis of empirical research examining adoption, acceptance, and stakeholder perceptions of PLF technologies, aiming to identify key social determinants shaping the diffusion of digital livestock technologies. Following PRISMA 2020 guidelines and a registered protocol (PROSPERO: CRD420261282807), systematic literature searches were conducted in Scopus, Web of Science, and PubMed/MEDLINE. Twenty-nine peer-reviewed studies met the inclusion criteria and were included in the quantitative synthesis, contributing 421 study-level effect-size estimates that constituted the unit of analysis. Random-effects meta-analysis (restricted maximum likelihood, REML) was used to estimate pooled adoption rates, acceptance scores, and perception outcomes across stakeholder groups, with heterogeneity assessed using I2 statistics, and within-study dependence addressed through cluster-robust variance estimation (RVE, CR2). As approximate summary patterns rather than firm benchmarks given the still-limited evidence base — the pooled estimate indicates that adoption of any PLF technology pooled to approximately 53% (95% CI: 38–68%; five studies), whereas adoption of individual technologies pooled to only ∼17% (95% CI: 12–22%; 146 estimates from 16 studies) — most stakeholders use at least one PLF tool, but uptake of specific technologies remains low. In this study, acceptance refers to stakeholder attitudes or evaluations of PLF technologies measured on Likert-type scales (additionally rescaled to a percent-of-maximum-possible (POMP, 0–100) metric to enable cross-scale comparability), while perception refers to the direction and valence of stakeholder views, including the proportion expressing positive assessments. Perception analyses suggest that approximately 69.0% (95% CI: 63.5–74.0%; k = 69 effect sizes from 7 studies) of respondents expressed positive views of PLF technologies, and pooled acceptance and perception scores on the POMP metric were approximately 71.5% (95% CI: 68.2–74.8%) and 63.2% (95% CI: 59.1–67.3%), respectively. However, substantial heterogeneity was observed across all outcome categories (I 2 > 90%), and all pooled estimates should be interpreted with appropriate caution as indicative patterns rather than precise benchmarks. A principal methodological limitation of this synthesis is the very high between-study heterogeneity and the small number of eligible studies (k = 29; 421 effect-size estimates clustered within studies). The results suggest a gap between positive stakeholder attitudes and actual technology uptake. These findings highlight the importance of addressing economic, technical, and institutional barriers to facilitate broader adoption of PLF technologies and support socially responsive digital transformation in livestock systems. To the best of our knowledge, this synthesis provides the first quantitative estimates of PLF adoption and perception rates across stakeholder groups and livestock sectors, though the small evidence base warrants cautious interpretation. The findings offer actionable insights for policymakers, technology developers, and agricultural advisors seeking to align digital livestock innovations with stakeholder needs, institutional capacities, and societal expectations for responsible agricultural transformation.

title: A lightweight keypoint detection network and pose-based error calibration method for body measurement of dairy goats
abstract: Accurate body measurement is essential for dairy goat breeding and growth assessment, yet existing automated methods are limited by slow processing and difficulty in handling geometric distortions caused by non-standard postures. To address these challenges, a lightweight integrated approach for dairy goat body measurement is proposed. Based on our proposed keypoint detection model LEKDNet (Lightweight Edge Keypoint Detection Network), this model integrates Star Block, C2PSM, and Slim-Neck modules to achieve real-time inference on edge devices with only 1.88 million parameters, maintaining 98.7 % accuracy. By combining detected keypoints with depth images, six body sizes: withers height (WH), hip height (HH), chest width (CW), hip width (HW), body length (BL), and chest depth (CD) are extracted. Measurement errors were observed to increase and consistency to decrease under non-standard postures when evaluated on the GBSK2025 dataset of 77 dairy goats, indicating that pose variations exert a notable effect on measurement accuracy. To address this, 16 skeletal keypoints from the body of dairy goat are further extracted to compute pose feature sets, and a stacking ensemble regression model comprising Neural Network, XGBoost, and Random Forest as base regressors with a Gradient Boosting meta-learner is employed to predict and correct posture-induced measurement errors. After calibration, the mean absolute errors of WH, HH, CW, HW, BL, and CD were reduced to 1.78 cm, 1.53 cm, 1.15 cm, 1.12 cm, 1.73 cm, and 1.22 cm. These results indicate that the proposed calibration method achieved consistent error reduction across all body sizes, thereby enhancing measurement stability and reliability. To implement the aforementioned proposed method in practical pasture applications, a channel-based measurement system equipped with top-mounted and side-mounted depth cameras is developed. This integrated system achieves cumulative delays of only 2.5–3.8 s per cycle for image acquisition, body measurement, and error correction. These findings demonstrate that the proposed method provides a reliable and efficient solution for automated body measurement in the precision management of dairy goats.

title: An electrically driven omnidirectional self-leveling tracked chassis with event-triggered sliding-mode control for hilly orchard operations
abstract: Hilly and mountainous orchards impose stringent requirements on agricultural mobile platforms because complex terrain, frequent slope transitions, and confined operating spaces can compromise chassis stability, payload safety, and operation quality. To address these challenges, this study developed an electrically driven omnidirectional self-leveling tracked chassis (EOSC) integrating distributed electric drive and an active pushrod suspension (APS), enabling coordinated chassis attitude adjustment in roll, pitch, and height. An event-triggered sliding mode controller (ET-SMC) was designed to maintain leveling accuracy while reducing redundant control updates, and a Jacobian velocity mapper (JVM) was established to transform the roll–pitch control output into coordinated velocity commands for the four servo-electric cylinders. Field experiments were conducted under cross-slope, oblique-slope, and longitudinal-slope conditions, with PID-BT and SMC-BT used as practical baseline controllers for comparison. The results show that ET-SMC achieved a global normalized attitude error (Eglobal) of 0.0688, which was comparable to that of SMC-BT (0.0628) and lower than that of PID-BT (0.0734). Meanwhile, the global attitude violation index (ηglobal) of ET-SMC was 3.14%, remaining close to that of SMC-BT (2.3867%) and substantially lower than that of PID-BT (9.0728%). More importantly, ET-SMC reduced the global normalized control update count (Jglobal) to 4.2722 updates/deg, corresponding to reductions of 83.73% and 83.89% relative to PID-BT and SMC-BT, respectively. In addition, ET-SMC reduced the mean actuator duty cycle to 70.65%, compared with 92.26% for PID-BT and 82.12% for SMC-BT, indicating a lower actuator workload and potential energy-related demand. These results demonstrate that the proposed EOSC, together with the ET-SMC and JVM-based actuator coordination strategy, can provide effective omnidirectional attitude stabilization in representative hilly orchard conditions while substantially reducing unnecessary actuator command transmissions. The study provides an integrated mechanical–control solution for self-leveling agricultural and off-road robotic platforms operating in narrow and uneven terrain.

title: Robust Approach to Potato Detection in Variable Environments
abstract: Reliable potato detection during harvesting is challenging because weather-related visual degradation and visually similar non-target objects, such as soil clumps and harvester components, can increase missed and false detections. This study developed a robust YOLO-based potato detection approach by combining the Convolutional Block Attention Module (CBAM) with one-class classification (OCC)-inspired auxiliary losses. CBAM was inserted into the YOLOv11n backbone to refine channel-wise and spatial feature responses, while compactness and descriptiveness losses were combined with the original detection loss during training to encourage compact potato representations and clearer separation from non-target features. The proposed model was evaluated on a temporally and regionally distinct test set, simulated fog, rain, and dust corruptions across five severity levels, and an independent external field dataset acquired with a different camera under dusty harvesting conditions. The proposed model achieved an mAP@50 of 93.6%, compared with 89.3% for the YOLOv11n baseline, and its performance advantage widened as corruption severity increased. On the external field dataset, it achieved an mAP@50 of 74.8%, compared with 61.8% for the baseline, and reduced FPPI on negative images from 3.13 to 0.72. The proposed approach improved performance across the evaluated YOLO versions, while the OCC-inspired auxiliary losses improved performance across the evaluated non-YOLO detector architectures. Edge-device benchmarking on an NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano showed a throughput of 26.7 FPS with minimal additional inference overhead. These results support the robustness and edge-deployment potential of the proposed approach under the evaluated harvesting conditions.

title: Trajectory-synchronized diode laser actuation and dose-response field evaluation for precision weed control using a delta robot
abstract: Weed control in Vidalia onion production is constrained by a narrow management window, where delays in intervention can result in yield losses of up to 96% in direct-seeded systems. This challenge often forces growers to rely on costly transplanting practices and labor-intensive hand weeding, while the limited availability of effective post-emergence herbicides further restricts in-season control options. Robotic laser weeding offers a precise, non-chemical alternative by selectively targeting individual weeds while protecting crop health and minimizing environmental impact. This research introduces the application of a delta parallel robot equipped with a 60 W diode laser to achieve photothermal weed control by targeting the leaf emergence point (LEP). The manipulator used a lightweight structure, combining aluminum proximal arms with carbon fiber distal arms to support fast motion with limited vibration. A microcontroller-based control stack executed analytical inverse kinematics and synchronized waypoint sequencing, with transistor-transistor logic (TTL) based laser triggering to ensure precise synchronization between motion and laser actuation. The motion planner excluded targets outside the robot workspace and adaptively reduced speed in regions approaching kinematic singularities to maintain stability and accuracy. Positional accuracy was evaluated in a greenhouse setting across 100 commanded targets, yielding a mean radial error of 0.83 mm. Moreover, field positional validation across five sites yielded a mean radial error of 1.11 mm and a 95 th percentile error of 1.50 mm. Field experiments were conducted using Brassica rapa ‘Twister’, selected for its uniform morphology (canopy width: 10.0 ± 1.5 cm, height: 5.0 ± 1.5 cm), arranged in a completely randomized design. Treatments consisted of laser exposure durations of 0.5, 1, 2, and 3 s at 60 W, with 10 replicates per treatment level. Weed injury was quantified using Chlorophyll Content Index (CCI), visual necrosis, half rosette span, and plant height. Measurements were collected prior to treatment and at 0 (control), 24, 36, 48 and 240 h (10 d) post-treatment. By 10 days after treatment, CCI decreased by 92% and 59% at exposure durations of 3 s and 2 s, respectively. Correspondingly, weed mortality reached 90% at 3 s and 60% at 2 s. In contrast, 1 s and 0.5 s exposures induced only transient injury, followed by recovery, with no mortality observed in controls. Overall, the system delivered repeatable millimeter-scale dosing with deterministic motion-actuation synchronization. Integrating perception and navigation modules could further extend this framework toward fully automated, non-chemical weed control in Vidalia onion production systems.

title: EDM–UNet: edge–aware and dynamically receptive Mamba–UNet for segmentation of Elymus nutans from UAV RGB imagery on the Qinghai–Xizang Plateau
abstract: Elymus nutans is a dominant perennial forage grass on the Qinghai–Xizang Plateau, and accurate assessment of its coverage in early spring is essential for grassland management. Its regreening is spatially asynchronous, such that newly emerged green leaves and structurally intact yellow tillers that remain viable and will regreen coexist within the same field, and both must be counted as live plants. While manual surveys can reliably identify these plants, they are prohibitively time–consuming and costly over large areas, and existing deep learning methods have rarely been designed for this specific requirement. Furthermore, pasture and meadow scenes often present additional difficulties including ambiguous boundaries between grass and background, large variation in patch size, and weak global context. To address these challenges, we constructed a dedicated UAV dataset and propose EDM–UNet, a lightweight semantic segmentation network for precise Elymus nutans delineation from RGB imagery. EDM–UNet integrates three complementary modules. The ESCCB strengthens boundary perception and reduces feature redundancy in the encoder. The DRFM adaptively fuses multi–scale context to capture both sparse tufts and dense meadows. The Mamba module at the bottleneck models long–range dependencies with linear complexity, improving global semantic consistency. Experiments show that EDM–UNet achieves an mIoU of 93.12% with 25.11 M parameters and an inference latency of 14.2 ms per frame, and it exhibits robust performance across varying flight altitudes, providing a practical solution that advances segmentation quality for intelligent alpine meadow monitoring.

title: Differences in estimation of sugarcane phenotypic parameters using unmanned aerial vehicle multispectral and hyperspectral data
abstract: Sugarcane is the world’s foremost sugar crop and a cornerstone of agricultural economies in numerous countries, including China, where it accounts for approximately three-quarters of national sugar production. Accurate, high-throughput retrieval of key phenotypic parameters—plant height, leaf area index (LAI), chlorophyll content (SPAD), and sugar content—is essential for cultivar breeding, yield forecasting, and precision field management. Traditional ground-based measurements are labor-intensive, destructive, and limited in scalability, whereas unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) remote sensing provides a non-destructive, high-resolution alternative. However, systematic comparisons of multispectral and hyperspectral sensors for sugarcane phenotyping across cultivars, growth periods, and nitrogen regimes remain scarce. This study systematically evaluated UAV-derived multispectral and hyperspectral data for estimating four phenotypic parameters (plant height, LAI, SPAD and sugar content) in two predominant Guangxi sugarcane cultivars (GT42 and GL05136) during stem elongation and maturity periods under four nitrogen levels. Synchronous canopy imagery and ground-truth phenotypic measurements were acquired. Sensitive hyperspectral bands were identified through spectral response analysis, and vegetation indices (VI) were selected and optimized using principal component analysis (PCA) and grey relational analysis (GRA). Linear, exponential, quadratic, and logarithmic curve-fitting models were developed to compare the estimation performance of the two sensor types. Results showed that: (1) Substantial phenotypic variation was influenced by cultivar, growth period, and nitrogen treatment. SPAD values generally declined with progression, LAI exhibited treatment-specific patterns, and plant height and sugar content increased consistently. (2) Hyperspectral sensitive bands were concentrated in the blue (475–491 nm), green (544–558 nm), red (622–644 nm), red-edge (702–718 nm), and near-infrared (834–880 nm) regions. (3) Hyperspectral data generally outperformed multispectral data in most scenarios, with optimal VI and curve forms varying by parameter, cultivar, and period. The best models achieved R2 = 0.987, RMSE = 1.233 for sugar content (hyperspectral-based quadratic model for GT42 during stem elongation); R2 = 0.939, RMSE = 0.386 for LAI (hyperspectral-based quadratic model of GT42 during stem elongation); R2 = 0.876, RMSE = 10.128 for plant height (hyperspectral-based exponential model of GT42 during stem elongation); and R2 = 0.801, RMSE = 3.384 for SPAD (multispectral-based exponential model of GT42 during stem elongation). Model accuracy was higher during stem elongation than maturity, with GT42 yielding more reliable estimations than GL05136. These findings reveal acomplex performance pattern: hyperspectral data generally achieved higher accuracy, particularly for biochemical and key economic traits, while multispectral data proved comparable or even superior in specific scenarios, depending on the target parameter, cultivar, and growth period. This provides a scenario-driven framework for sensor selection in high-throughput sugarcane phenotyping.

title: A vision-based dual-modal system for adjusting the orientation and plant spacing of ginger with biharmonic depth completion and rapid hand–eye calibration
abstract: Consistent shoot orientation and uniform plant spacing are essential for high-yield, mechanized ginger production. However, current seeding systems still rely heavily on manual ginger seed placement, which limits the level of automation, particularly under stacked and occluded conditions. In this study, we present an integrated vision-guided robotic system for automatic ginger seed picking, shoot orientation adjustment and spacing control. For visual perception, we develop an enhanced YOLO11-seg detector with three architectural modifications: an asymmetric dual-stream RGB-D backbone for joint appearance and geometric feature extraction, a lightweight depth branch built with GhostConv and a proposed C3Ghost-SS module integrating SimAM and SGE attention, and an additional small-object detection head to improve shoot recognition in stacked and occluded scenes.
