To support reliable 3D localization, we further develop a rapid board-free hand–eye calibration procedure and a training-free biharmonic depth completion method. These perception and localization modules are integrated with a low-cost robotic arm to form a closed-loop system for seed picking, reorientation, and in-row spacing control. Across model scales (n → x), the improved network raises mAP@0.5 by 7.2 %, 7.6 %, 6.8 %, 7.0 %, and 6.5 % over the YOLO11 baseline. The calibration achieves 90th-percentile absolute errors of 1.85 mm (X), 2.07 mm (Y), and 2.91 mm (Z). For depth completion, the biharmonic equation method reduces MAE and RMSE by ∼ 62 % and 67 %, and increases PSNR and SSIM by ∼ 28 % and 5 %, respectively, while maintaining high computational efficiency. System-level tests yield 76.5 % seed-picking success, 86.3 % reorientation success, and spacing accuracy within ± 2.3 cm. These results demonstrate the feasibility of the proposed closed-loop robotic system for automated ginger seed manipulation under complex planting conditions, and provide a practical step toward more autonomous ginger planting.

title: Tea-shoot pose estimation based on light field multi-cue fusion depth estimation
abstract: Tea shoots exhibit diverse spatial poses and frequent occlusion in field environments, making their three-dimensional localization difficult using two-dimensional images alone. This study presents a light-field-based framework that integrates tea-shoot detection, multi-cue depth reconstruction, and point-cloud-based pose estimation. In the proposed framework, a light field camera is used as the visual sensor, and the R3Det rotated-object detector is used to localize tea shoots and estimate their bounding-box orientations. For the detected tea shoots, a light field depth estimation method based on defocus cues is employed to obtain preliminary depth data as prior information. Subsequently, a multi-cue light field depth estimation algorithm based on the Transformer network is proposed to obtain the final depth estimation results. Finally, an efficient tea-shoot pose estimation algorithm based on point cloud processing is introduced to achieve the estimation of the spatial poses of tea shoots. Unlike active depth sensors that depend on projected illumination, light field imaging passively records both spatial and angular information in a single acquisition. The resulting sub-aperture views enable defocus and angular-parallax cues to be jointly exploited, providing complementary geometric observations for weakly textured tea shoots and partially occluded boundaries. On the public light field benchmark, the proposed method achieved an average MSE of 1.047 with an inference time of 0.214 s, indicating performance comparable to that of the evaluated methods. The framework also achieved mean absolute errors of 3.281°, 2.744°, and 1.989° for pitch, yaw, and roll, respectively, demonstrating its feasibility for vision-guided robotic tea harvesting under the evaluated conditions.

title: Nutrition label traceability for food security: A traceability-based information infrastructure
abstract: Reliable nutritional information on food labels supports informed dietary choices, yet labeling integrity remains uneven across regulated food markets, particularly in emerging economies. When the lineage of declared nutritional values cannot be traced from laboratory certification to consumer access, label data becomes susceptible to discrepancy, weakening the informational basis of food utilization. This study develops a traceability-based information infrastructure that records and links nutrition label data across four stages of the regulatory licensing lifecycle: facility certification, product distribution permit, batch-level certificate of analysis, and shipment. Using a Design Science Research (DSR) approach, a proof-of-concept (PoC) was implemented and evaluated through the Technology, Organization, and Environment (TOE) framework and Institutional Theory (IST) to assess technical, organizational, and environmental conditions for adoption. Within the PoC scope, the system sustains sub-five-second response times and low per-transaction costs, indicating operational viability at the scale of small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs). By strengthening the informational foundation of nutrition labels in regulated markets and enabling affordability-supportive governance without imposing prohibitive compliance costs on SMEs, this infrastructure contributes to the utilization and affordability dimensions of food security relevant to the FAO framework.

title: Machinable varieties and full-process mechanization equipment technology for pineapple: A review
abstract: Autonomous farming systems depend on close alignment between crop traits, cultivation practices and field machinery. Pineapple, a major tropical fruit grown in large-scale fields in southern China, offers a useful case for assessing autonomous fruit production. Drawing on more than 130 references overall, with a primary focus on publications from 2020 to 2025, this review evaluates full-process mechanization for pineapple production across land preparation, planting, field management and harvesting. Mechanization has progressed in land preparation, planting and field management through integrated tillage, mechanized planting and tractor-based or drone-based spraying, but harvesting remains the least mature stage. Semi-automatic harvesting devices improve efficiency by 16%–26% compared with manual operations, whereas fully automatic mechanisms report 82%–85% harvesting rates. In current pineapple recognition and detection studies, most deep-learning-based detection methods report average precision of 80.30%–97.9%, although occlusion, variable lighting and dense planting still limit robustness. Varietal assessment indicates that Tainung No. 17, Tainung No. 21 and Tainung No. 23 are suitable machinable candidates under plant heights of 75-85 cm and single-fruit weights of 1.1-1.5 kg. Future work should strengthen machinery-agronomy integration, intelligent sensing and control, modular equipment design and generalized deployment.

title: Mechanistic investigation of seed damage during operation of a centrifugal high-speed precision maize seed metering device
abstract: High-speed precision sowing improves maize production efficiency and contributes to stable yield formation. However, in centrifugal high-speed precision seed metering devices, seeds frequently contact metering components during high-speed filling and clearing, which may cause seed damage. Existing studies on centrifugal seed metering devices have mainly focused on metering performance, whereas the mechanisms of seed damage and the effects of key operating parameters on seed damage remain poorly understood. To address the above research gap, this study established a mechanism-oriented research framework to systematically characterize maize seed damage during centrifugal high-speed precision seed metering. A calibrated Bonding V2-based maize seed fracture model was incorporated into a discrete element method (DEM) model of the seed metering process, and theoretical analysis, DEM simulations, bench tests, and germination tests were jointly conducted. The results showed that seed damage was mainly caused by shear, compression, and impact. Shear damage was concentrated in the mechanical interference zone between the shaped hole ears and the seed-clearing outlet; compression damage mainly occurs in the constricted channel and narrow-gap regions; and impact damage is associated with high-frequency collisions between seeds and rotating components or the housing. Seed plate rotation speed (SPRS) mainly affected seed kinetic energy and impact intensity, and seed damage increased markedly when SPRS exceeded 300 r·min−1. Initial seed stock in the seed chamber (ISIC) mainly affected local crowding and compressive forces, with higher ISIC increasing the risks of compression and shear damage. Based on a central composite design and multi-objective optimization, the optimized low-damage operating parameter combination was SPRS = 297.8 r·min−1 and ISIC = 37, yielding a measured seed breakage rate of 0.5 % and a germination rate of 97.75 %. Critical damage speed tests indicated a critical value of 300 r·min−1, and multi-variety tests showed variety-dependent tolerance to mechanical loading. These findings provide guidance for low-damage design and operating parameter optimization of centrifugal high-speed precision seed metering devices.

title: Research on grain distribution regulation and hopper loading optimization methods for cooperative grain unloading of combine harvesters
abstract: During mechanized rice harvesting, hopper loading efficiency in cooperative grain unloading between a combine harvester and a grain transport vehicle directly affects operational continuity and transfer efficiency. To address the low space utilization and uneven grain distribution associated with experience-based unloading, this study designed a multi-degree-of-freedom adjustable unloading spout and proposed a multi-objective optimization method that integrates a discrete element method (DEM)-based regression model, a particle accumulation model that considers hopper boundaries and adjacent grain piles, a bilevel non-dominated sorting genetic algorithm III (BI-NSGA-III), and the multi-criteria optimization and compromise solution (VIKOR) method. The proposed method uses a bilevel optimization framework to decouple global unloading-point layout planning from local control-parameter tuning. The upper level determines the unloading-point layout under a fixed serpentine sequence, whereas the lower level matches local control parameters for each point. For the three hopper sizes, the optimal layouts were 2 × 2, 2 × 3, and 3 × 4, achieving global coverage rates of 46.56%, 58.55%, and 70.39% and total loading masses of 631.98, 1940.28, and 10057.20 kg, respectively. Field experiments showed that, compared with experience-based unloading, the proposed method increased global coverage by 17.9%, 55.2%, and 98.4% and total loading mass by 9.8%, 14.3%, and 17.4%, respectively. The relative errors between the field-measured means and the optimization predictions were below 5% under the tested conditions. These results demonstrate that the proposed method effectively improves hopper space utilization and provides theoretical and methodological support for unloading-strategy optimization and the future development of adaptive unloading systems in combine harvesters.

title: A novel method for underwater crab mass estimation based on Dfe-Mask Transfiner and XGBoost
abstract: Crab mass is an important indicator of growth status and can support feeding adjustment and health assessment in aquaculture. Conventional weighing requires manual handling and may cause stress or injury, whereas underwater image-based estimation offers a potential non-destructive alternative. This study developed a carapace-segmentation-based framework for underwater mass estimation of Chinese mitten crabs. A task-oriented Dfe-Mask Transfiner model was constructed by adapting Mask Transfiner, integrating existing deformable large kernel attention (D-LKA) and efficient multi-scale attention (EMA) modules at task-specific feature levels, and redesigning the feature pyramid network (FPN) to improve multi-scale feature exchange for carapace-boundary delineation. On the validation set, Dfe-Mask Transfiner achieved the highest AP50 and AP50–95 among the evaluated segmentation models, with values of 97.04% and 87.07%, respectively. The predicted masks were then used to extract interpretable morphometric and RGB descriptors for regression. On the manually screened valid-sample test set, XGBoost achieved the best overall performance among the evaluated regressors when shape and color features were jointly used, with an RMSE of 12.30 g, an MAE of 8.48 g, an R2 of 0.8921, and a MAPE of 9.39%. These results indicate that carapace mask quality influenced downstream feature reliability and that combining morphometric and color descriptors improved mass estimation under the tested conditions. However, segmentation performance decreased under high turbidity and in multi-crab images, and the regression dataset was constructed from manually screened valid single-crab samples. External validation across broader farm, camera, and water-quality conditions is therefore still required.

title: A physics-guided hybrid framework for peanut nitrogen monitoring: Fusing radiative transfer physics with machine learning
abstract: Nitrogen, significantly affects peanut agricultural yield and development. Therefore, the effective detection of nitrogen is important for crop growth in the context of agricultural economics. However, conventional measurements of canopy nitrogen concentration are labor-intensive and time-consuming, limiting high-throughput monitoring. In this study, we developed a radiative transfer process-guided model for estimating nitrogen content in peanut canopy by integrating radiative transfer theory with empirical modeling approaches. A hyperspectral platform was utilized to monitor the canopy spectrum of 241 peanut accessions grown under four distinct environmental conditions. The peanuts canopy nitrogen content (CNC) monitoring model was constructed using spectrum data, combining a Wasserstein Generative Adversarial Nets (WGAN) physiological parameter optimization with empirical models optimized via hyperparameter tuning. Compared to the conventional empirical model (R2 = 0.7544, mean squared error (MSE) = 13.0612), the proposed POSNH framework, a pre-trained LSTM network guided by optimized radiative transfer processes, attained significantly higher accuracy in CNC estimation (R2 = 0.8815, MSE = 5.8432). The POSNH model also exhibited exceptional robustness across data scarce which maintaining high predictive accuracy (R2 = 0.8612) when the training set is reduced to 10 % and demonstrating generalization across independent environment yielding MSE values of 7.54, 5.07, 5.27, and 2.85 for Experiments 1–4. By leveraging Monte Carlo Dropout (MC Dropout) for simultaneous point estimation and uncertainty quantification, the model ensured high predictive reliability, with 95 % prediction intervals achieving 97.75 % empirical coverage. The POSNH demonstrates the potential of applying an optimized PROSAIL, hyperparameter search and modular training to improve the accuracy and cross-environment robustness of CNC prediction, providing a new approach for sustainable agricultural management.

title: Soil fertility prediction using SoilGRU-XNet: An explainable GRU-based framework for precision agriculture
abstract: Soil fertility plays a vital role in precision agriculture by directly affecting crop growth, crop productivity, nutrient intake, and sustainable farming practices. The conventional methods of soil fertility evaluation are labour-intensive and even very complex with temporal, soil, and environmental parameters. This work develops SoilGRU-XNet (Soil Gated Recurrent Unit-eXplainable Network), an explainable deep learning framework for soil fertility prediction using multivariate time-series data from IoT-based soil and crop sensors. The proposed model integrates a Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU) temporal model with SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) for improved soil fertility prediction accuracy. The proposed SoilGRU-XNet model captures temporal dependencies and effectively generates a continuous soil fertility index. Extensive experiments were conducted to evaluate the proposed SoilGRU-XNet model, and the results are compared with baseline deep learning models. The proposed model produces the lowest Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) and Mean Absolute Error (MAE) as 3.268 and 1.0114, respectively, with the highest R2 (0.7753). Thus, the results demonstrate the superiority with better predictive accuracy and stability. The SHAP explanations align with the agronomic proofs, such as soil nitrogen, phosphorus, potassium, and electrical conductivity, which are the dominant contributors to fertility prediction. Furthermore, Wilcoxon statistical tests confirm that the performance of the proposed SoilGRU-XNet is statistically significant (p < 0.05) over baseline models. Accordingly, statistically validated results ensure that the developed model is well-suited for real-world deployment in precision agriculture and decision-support systems.

title: A conditional scenario-analysis tool for base feed selection in precision-fed pig: Balancing feed cost and nitrogen excretion
abstract: The strategic formulation of base feeds in precision feeding (PF) systems for growing-finishing pigs remains a critical upstream challenge for balancing production costs and nitrogen (N) excretion. This study evaluated a conditional scenario-analysis tool designed to identify optimal standardized ileal digestible lysine (SID Lys) concentrations for high-protein (H) and low-protein (L) base feeds. Daily feed intake and body weight records from 179 Duroc × (Large White × Landrace) barrows (days 17 to 84 of fattening) were used as a fixed performance baseline. A simulation pipeline explored a grid of 1,368H/L feed combinations (H: 10.1–11.8 g/kg SID Lys; L: 2.5–10.0 g/kg SID Lys) across three historical feed price scenarios (September 2021, July 2022, and March 2023). Feasible candidate feeds were filtered using a dual feasibility criterion based on the i100 limitation index (paired Wilcoxon signed-rank test P ≥ 0.05 and median i100 difference ≤ 1.5 percentage points relative to the trial). Formulations with H feed below 11.5 g/kg SID Lys systematically increased nutrient inadequacy (P < 0.05). Retained candidate pairs demonstrated that H = 11.5 g/kg SID Lys achieved minimal feed cost per animal across all price scenarios, while optimal L feed concentrations shifted between 6.6, 7.9, and 7.6 g/kg SID Lys depending on ingredient market volatility. From an environmental perspective, H = 11.5 g/kg and L = 7.4 g/kg SID Lys minimized estimated N excretion to 43.34% of N intake (1.245 kg N/animal). Temporal clustering of the fattening period into three phases yielded only marginal feed cost reductions compared to a single full-period base feed specification. Consequently, swine operations can prioritize a single, robust pair of base feeds (11.5 g/kg H and intermediate L) managed via daily dynamic blending without increasing operational or logistical complexity.

title: HMSA-Net: A lightweight transfer learning model for agricultural disease segmentation
abstract: Accurate and efficient segmentation of diseased regions in infected leaf images is the cornerstone of precision agriculture and automated crop monitoring. Although current deep learning methods have achieved remarkable results, they often struggle to strike a balance between segmentation accuracy and computational efficiency—particularly when deployed on resource-constrained agricultural equipment. To address this, we propose a lightweight segmentation network, the Hierarchical Multi-Scale Attention Network (HMSA-Net), which adopts a hierarchical encoder–decoder architecture and introduces newly designed bottleneck and skip-connection modules for efficient feature extraction. This paper focuses on binary lesion segmentation tasks (diseased region versus background). Comprehensive experiments on agricultural disease datasets demonstrate that the proposed method achieves 83.78% Intersection over Union (IoU) with only 1.28 million parameters, outperforming comparative networks. To verify the model’s transfer learning capability, cross-domain evaluation on marine animal datasets (74.73% IoU) further confirms the robustness and adaptability of this unified architecture. The model has been successfully deployed on an embedded platform; while the performance metrics are suboptimal due to limitations of the development board itself, it demonstrates practical value for mobile crop lesion detection and localization. This work achieves a favorable trade-off among accuracy, efficiency, and deployability, providing our solution for lesion localization in precision agriculture.

title: AMSF-SLAM: an agricultural multi-sensor fusion SLAM system for globally dense mapping in unstructured orchard and tea plantation environments
abstract: Reliable localization and high-fidelity three-dimensional (3D) mapping are essential prerequisites for the autonomous operation of agricultural robots in unstructured orchard and tea plantation environments. However, uneven terrain, repetitive vegetation patterns, and substantial variations in illumination make it difficult for existing methods to maintain global consistency during long-term operation while preserving high-quality dense local perception. This paper proposes AMSF-SLAM, an agricultural multi-sensor fusion simultaneous localization and mapping (SLAM) system specifically designed to construct dense point cloud maps in unstructured orchard and tea plantation environments. A loosely coupled multi-sensor fusion framework, based on an error-state Kalman filter (ESKF), was employed to integrate measurements from vision sensors, LiDAR, and inertial measurement unit (IMU). Loop closure detection and nonlinear optimization were incorporated to mitigate drift accumulated during long-term operation and enhance global trajectory consistency. Using the optimized fused odometry, dense mapping of multi-source sensor observations was performed within a unified spatial reference frame. Extensive experiments in real-world orchard and tea plantation environments demonstrated that the proposed system reliably detected loop closures and produced smooth, globally consistent trajectories under uneven terrain and challenging illumination conditions, thereby enabling dense point cloud mapping across large-scale, unstructured agricultural environments. The main contribution of this work lies in the design and validation of a dense mapping framework for unstructured orchard and tea plantation environments. The resulting dense maps provide a reliable spatial foundation for navigation, environmental perception and crop-level observation by agricultural robots in complex orchard and tea plantation environments.

title: Field portable soil spectroscopy: What’s beyond Vis-NIR?
abstract: The use of spectroscopy in soil properties measurement has been extensively investigated. To qualify and quantify soils with high speed and accuracy, field portable soil spectroscopy (FPSS) is a promising tool to carry out in situ soil surveys. These sensors can produce continuous spectra from different chemical principles, and soil properties can be either directly or indirectly inferred from the spectra. This review summarised the theories and applications of eight FPSS, including some already widely implemented and some still in an early stage of development. These FPSS are characterised by the information they provide, namely organic, mineralogical, elemental, and physical information about soils. Visible, near-infrared and mid-infrared spectroscopy methods are the primary vibrational spectroscopy method used to measure organic and mineralogical properties. Raman spectroscopy, another vibrational spectroscopy, is also promising, but requires more quantitative validation. X-ray fluorescence and laser-induced breakdown spectroscopy are effective in quantifying elemental concentrations and are commonly used as complementary sensors to the vibrational spectroscopy. Gamma-ray spectroscopy detects gamma radiation and is used to identify and quantify radioactive elements. Lastly, nuclear magnetic resonance and terahertz spectroscopy are two emerging sensors that have the potential to characterise organic matter and soil physical properties, respectively.

title: Uav-based precision irrigation strategy for winter Wheat: Estimating soil water content via leaf water content
abstract: Accurately monitor soil watercontent (SWC)is the key to achieving precise irrigationof winterwheat. In the case of high crop coverage, the SWC cannot be directly estimated by canopy spectrum, which limits the application of UAVimaging inpreciseirrigation of winterwheat. This study proposes a UAV-based irrigation volume decision method of winter wheat across various growth stages. The method relies on the quantitative relationship between leaf water content (LWC) and SWC. Initially, sensitive vegetation indices for LWC were identified from UAV multispectral imagery collected across five growth stages. Then a UAV multispectral LWC estimation model was developed. Subsequently, four algorithms, linear, polynomial, exponential, and logarithmic were compared to select an optimal transformation model linking SWC and LWC. These models were then employed to predict SWC, enabling the determination of optimal irrigation volume for each growth stage of winter wheat. The findings indicated that the Random Forest model performed best for estimating LWC in five growth stages,with determination coefficient (R2)of 0.8654, 0.7916, 0.8009, 0.8054, and 0.8706, respectively. The corresponding RMSE values were recorded as 0.0182, 0.0362, 0.0416, 0.0432, and 0.0705, respectively. The SWC and LWC at five growth stages were all positively correlated, and the validation R2 of polynomial fitting were 0.7149, 0.9045, 0.9392, 0.8261, and 0.8672 respectively. The validation R2 of SWC indirectly estimated by UAV was 0.8523, while the RMSE is 0.0131. Another growing season experiment was carried out to verify. The estimation of LWC achieved the validation R2 of 0.8904, 0.8567, and 0.9461 respectively, and the RMSE were 0.0483, 0.0382, and 0.0682 respectively. Polynomial fit between SWC and LWC achieved the validation R2 of 0.8572, 0.8818, and 0.8616. The estimation of SWC achieved the validation R2 of 0.7714 and the RMSE of 0.0157. Finally, the mapping of irrigation volume at five growth stages of winter wheat was achieved. The UAV-based precision irrigation strategy performed well when applied to another growing season of winter wheat. This study provides a irrigation volume decision method for winter wheat at multiple growth stages using UAV-based multispectral imagery, which offers a reference for the application of UAV imaging technology in precision agricultural management.

title: Explainable artificial intelligence for plant disease detection: a scoping review of methods, datasets, and evaluation practices
abstract: Explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) is increasingly integrated into plant disease detection to improve transparency and trust, yet the literature remains fragmented regarding which approaches are used, what datasets underpin them, and how explanations are evaluated. This PRISMA-ScR-guided scoping review maps XAI research in plant disease detection and identifies gaps limiting trustworthy, field-ready deployment. We searched six databases and arXiv, supplemented by Google Scholar and citation chasing, for studies published January 2020 to October 2025, yielding 88 eligible articles. Model architectures, XAI techniques, dataset characteristics, and evaluation strategies were extracted and synthesized using a two-axis taxonomy based on explainability scope (local vs. global) and model transparency (intrinsic vs. post-hoc). Convolutional neural networks remain dominant, with growing adoption of Vision Transformers and hybrid architectures. Post-hoc methods overwhelmingly dominate. Grad-CAM and variants appeared in 54.5 % of studies, followed by LIME (37.5 %) and SHAP (18.2 %), while intrinsic and concept-based approaches remain underexplored. The evidence base is skewed toward controlled datasets, with PlantVillage or equivalent sources underpinning 34.1 % of studies and only 20.5 % incorporating field or hybrid data. Evaluation is largely performance-centric (accuracy: 53.4 %), with rigorous explainability assessment uncommon only 2.3 % reported quantitative explainability metrics and 3.4 % incorporated expert validation. Key challenges include dataset bias, poor field generalization, qualitative treatment of explanations, and limited reproducibility. Advancing trustworthy agricultural XAI requires field-realistic benchmarks, standardized explainability metrics, and human-centered validation protocols, forming an actionable research agenda for reliable AI-driven decision-making in real farming environments.

title: Precision livestock farming and farm animal welfare: a scientometric analysis of research trends and technological innovations
abstract: Precision Livestock Farming (PLF) is increasingly recognized for its potential to improve the health and welfare of farm animals, their productivity, and environmental sustainability. Nevertheless, the critical transition of PLF from a theoretical research concept to practical field implementation remains essential for realizing its full potential. This study undertakes a scientometric review of PLF and its application in the monitoring of farm animal welfare, covering the period from 2006 to 2025. The study employs a mixed-corpus scientometric approach to concurrently assess trends in PLF publications (n = 1,594) and patents (n = 3,239), revealing a strong co-evolutionary relationship (r = 0.913, 95% CI 0.79–0.97, p < 0.001) between academic and industrial PLF activity, with annual growth rates of 32.2% and 20.2%, respectively. The analysis identifies key research subfields and traces the evolution of PLF themes across three overlapping phases: a hardware validation phase (2006–2015), a welfare outcome validation phase (2016–2020), and an artificial intelligence integration phase (2021–2025). The study underscores the importance of integrating scientific literature and patent data for comprehensive insights into PLF’s role in enhancing farm animal welfare and highlights persistent gaps between proof-of-concept research and commercially deployed, welfare-validated systems.

title: An Uncertainty-Aware multimodal physiological sensing framework for Simulator-Based agricultural Machinery Operator-State monitoring and Task-Completion-Score prediction
abstract: Continuous agricultural machinery operation requires monitoring approaches that can capture short-timescale operator states while also estimating longer-timescale task performance. However, EEG, ECG and eye-tracking signals differ in physiological origin, sampling characteristics and response timing, and their reliability may decrease during prolonged operation. This study proposes an Uncertainty-Aware Hierarchical Multi-Scale Fusion Network (UAHMF-Net) for joint operator-state monitoring and task-completion-score prediction in a simulator-based agricultural machinery task. The framework encodes EEG, ECG and eye-tracking windows with modality-specific spatiotemporal encoders, preserves local temporal tokens for cross-modal interaction, estimates modality reliability through evidential uncertainty, and uses an asynchronous masked joint loss to align 30-s physiological windows with 20-min task-completion-score labels without artificial label padding. A 5-h simulator experiment was conducted with 12 experienced participants, and subject-independent performance was evaluated using leave-one-subject-out cross-validation. UAHMF-Net achieved a Macro-F1 of 91.4 % for fatigue classification, a workload RMSE of 4.35, a task-completion-score RMSE of 2.65, and an R2 of 0.852. Fusion-strategy comparisons and ablation results indicated that token-level multimodal interaction, uncertainty-guided reliability weighting and asynchronous label handling contributed to the joint prediction task. Under simulated sensor degradation, the proposed framework showed more stable prediction performance than the compared baselines, although severe degradation still reduced information quality. These results suggest that uncertainty-aware multimodal physiological sensing may support simulator-based operator-state monitoring and safety-warning research for agricultural machinery operation. Before practical deployment, the framework requires validation in real field environments with larger and more diverse operator cohorts, field-recorded disturbances, and practical wearable sensor configurations.

title: Physics-informed deep learning for robust maize leaf area index estimation using multi-source data
abstract: Maize is one of the most important staple crops worldwide. Accurate leaf area index (LAI) estimation is essential for precise maize management. However, most existing methods rely on common machine learning models, which often suffer from poor spatiotemporal generalization. To address these issues, this study proposes PhysLAINet, a physics-informed model for maize LAI estimation based on multi-source data fusion. The model takes bi-temporal spectral–textural features and phenological variables as input, adopting a dual branch structure. The physical branch is built on a dynamic leaf area density (LAD) model, while the phenological branch is based on an enhanced logistic model. The outputs of the two branches are fused using an adaptive weighting strategy. In addition, an uncertainty weighted loss is introduced to constrain multi-stage LAI predictions. PhysLAINet incorporates explicit physical constraints, which helps reduce saturation effects and improves sensitivity to abnormal crop growth. Experimental results show that PhysLAINet achieves strong accuracy and generalization performance. It achieves favorable performance on the 2025 dataset (R2 = 0.8866, RMSE = 0.6147, rRMSE = 15.29%) and the 2023 cross-year and cross-cultivar dataset (R2 = 0.7119, RMSE = 0.4663, rRMSE = 30.63%), surpassing all baseline methods in overall performance under both scenarios. The model is lightweight and can be deployed on edge devices for high-speed inference. Moreover, an end-to-end LAI estimation system was designed and validated in real-world scenarios. Overall, PhysLAINet shows strong potential to integrate physical priors into deep learning for precision agriculture.

title: From dynamic scene understanding to stable feed delivery: A multi-sensor robotic system for autonomous precision feeding in intensive goat barns
abstract: Autonomous precision feeding in intensive goat barns is challenged by dynamic herd-induced LiDAR interference, longitudinal localization degradation in repetitive corridors, and visual occlusion during feed delivery. To address these coupled problems, this study develops and field-evaluates a multi-sensor robotic system that combines geometry-guided spatial masking, vision-triggered one-dimensional Extended Kalman Filter (1D-EKF) correction, and decoupled feed control. The spatial masking module suppresses scattered animal points while preserving structural fences and walls before FAST-LIO2 state estimation. A Frequency-Enhanced Feature Fusion (FEFF) module improves the instance segmentation of slender metal fences, which are used as semantic anchors for periodic longitudinal correction. For feed delivery, pen-level herd inventory is estimated before dispensing and converted into feed targets; feedforward auger control and post-dispensing mass calibration are then executed without relying on real-time visual counting. Under the tested barn conditions, compared with the FAST-LIO2-based configuration using spatial masking but no semantic correction, the vision-triggered 1D-EKF reduced the longitudinal Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) by 76.8% (from 0.1792 m to 0.0415 m). The system achieved a mean pen-level herd-counting accuracy of 96.20% and an average absolute relative dispensing error of 3.04% relative to the automatically generated pen-level feed targets during a complete ten-pen pass at 0.10 m/s. These results show that the proposed workflow reduced the influence of dynamic interference, longitudinal drift, and feeding-induced visual occlusion, while improving dispensing stability and mass accuracy under the tested conditions.

title: Weather-based prediction of black locust (Robinia pseudoacacia L.) honey yield and quality: a reproducible computational system with operational deployment
abstract: Black locust (Robinia pseudoacacia L.; marketed as “acacia”) honey production in South Korea—accounting for over 70% of national honey output—has been increasingly affected by weather-driven disturbances, resulting in substantial production declines, notably in 2018 and 2020 ( Kim et al., 2022 ). Such episodes have been broadly attributed to impacts of climate change; however, a diagnostic framework identifying which weather variables, and at which phenological stages, drive the simultaneous decline in yield and quality has remained unavailable. Existing approaches rely either on uninterpretable machine-learning models that require large training data unavailable at the farm scale, or on single-variable rules-of-thumb that fail under multivariate weather conditions. Therefore, we present a reproducible computational system that addresses this gap through three integrated components: (i) two interpretable hierarchical weather indices—the Honey Harvest Weather Index (HHWI) for yield and the Honey Moisture Weather Index (HMWI) for moisture content—derived from five meteorological variables (maximum temperature, precipitation, relative humidity, wind speed, and solar radiation) across three phenological stages (bud formation, pre-flowering, and flowering); (ii) a generalized raster pipeline producing spatially-explicit predictions from gridded meteorological data; (iii) an operational forecast module generating real-time decision-support maps via inverse-distance interpolation. The system was validated using 570 farm-year records from 95 black locust apiaries (2020–2025) in South Korea and benchmarked against seven machine-learning alternatives. HHWI achieved a cross-validated R2 value of 0.395 (RMSE = 16.85 kg/colony) using three effective parameters and outperformed XGBoost in terms of cross-validated stability, exhibiting a 15-fold reduction in the overfitting gap. HMWI achieved a cross-validated R2 value of 0.668, with a moisture-grade classification accuracy of 96.0% (within ± 1 grade, Cohen’s κ = 0.41). This demonstrates its operational feasibility for weather-based quality prediction. Retrospective decomposition of the 2020 production minimum (18.4 kg/colony) indicated that approximately 60% of the deficit relative to the 2024 peak year (60.5 kg/colony) was attributable to maximum temperature during the pre-flowering stage. Cumulative temperature contributions across all phenological stages accounted for 80% of the deficit, transforming broad climate-change attribution into actionable diagnoses of specific weather variables and phenological stages. The data-driven breakpoints converged with published physiological thresholds for Apis mellifera , supporting the mechanistic interpretation. The complete system—including analysis script, raster pipeline, forecast module, and 22-checkpoint verification—was released as an open-source code, providing beekeepers and policymakers with a deployment-ready, weather-based decision-support system that requires only routine meteorological data. All codes and anonymized data are available on Zenodo ( https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.20612458) .

title: The MBD-DEM magnetic coupling modeling method and mechanism analysis of the magnetic pointer-type seed metering device
abstract: This study addresses the problems of poor stability of traditional mechanical seed metering devices during high-speed operation and the lack of an MBD-DEM magnetic coupling modeling method. A magnetic pointer-type high-speed precision seed metering device was designed, which integrates a dual-seed disc, a three-point seed-fixing structure, and magnetic collaborative drive technology to achieve stable seed separation and holding under high-speed operation, thereby improving seed metering performance. An equivalent driving-based MBD-DEM magnetic coupling simulation method was proposed. By embedding the STEP and COS periodic function drives in Adams to control the movement of the pointer, the magnetic coupling simulation was realized, overcoming the technical challenge of interactive simulation between magnetic forces and mechanical systems. Simulation and bench tests were conducted to analyze the effects of operating speed, fingertip inclination, and magnetic induction on seed arrangement performance, leading to the identification of an optimal parameter combination. The results showed that at an operating speed of 9.52 km/h, a fingertip inclination of 19.35°, and a magnetic induction of 242 mT, the qualified rate, leakage rate, and multiple rate were 93.27 %, 3.52 %, and 3.23 %, respectively. This research provides theoretical and technical support for the design and optimization of efficient, high-speed, precision seed metering equipment.

title: Boundary-prior-guided 3D LiDAR segmentation and structural parameter extraction of plough furrows for tillage quality assessment
abstract: Plough furrow geometry serves as a key indicator for evaluating ploughing quality and consistency. However, current precision agriculture systems still lack real-time quality feedback during ploughing and rely primarily on sparse manual sampling, which cannot adequately quantify spatial heterogeneity. Moreover, image sensors are highly susceptible to environmental variations, including weather conditions and changes in illumination, which significantly hampers the reliability of real-time plough furrow detection in complex field environments. To address this gap, we propose a LiDAR-based method for segmenting plough furrows and extracting structural parameters from farmland point clouds. The primary objectives are to jointly screen plough furrow boundary candidates using geometric pose and local morphological constraints and then obtain left and right boundary lines via DBSCAN clustering, to construct a lateral distance field and a boundary-line-based spatial prior and incorporate them into morphology-constrained region growing to segment plough furrow instances in unstructured field point clouds robustly, and to extract key furrow structural parameters via orthogonal slicing and cross-sectional profile analysis along the furrow direction. Field validation demonstrates high segmentation consistency, achieving an IoU of 0.8745 and an F1 score of 0.9330. For parameter-extraction accuracy, the coefficient of determination (R2) for furrow depth, top width, and slope angle were 0.956, 0.963, and 0.953, respectively. The average processing time was 131.7 ms, satisfying real-time requirements. Stability analysis during continuous operation yielded coefficients of variation below 15% for all parameters, supporting the reliability of the algorithm under real-world conditions.

title: From visible to yield-contributing opened bolls: An interpretable PAI-based correction framework for cotton boll estimation under canopy occlusion in UAV imagery
abstract: Accurate estimation of yield-contributing opened cotton boll density from UAV imagery is limited by canopy occlusion, because nadir-view detection models can only identify opened bolls exposed on the canopy surface. To address this problem, this study developed an interpretable correction framework that converts visible opened boll density into yield-contributing opened boll density by incorporating Plant Area Index (PAI) as a canopy-structure proxy. The framework integrates a position-specific lightweight YOLOv8n detector, a sliding-window and deduplication-based plot-scale counting pipeline, and a PAI-based correction model. Field data collected from 2023 to 2025 were used, with the 2024 dataset serving for detector training, counting-pipeline development, and correction-model calibration, while the 2023 and 2025 datasets were reserved for independent cross-year validation. The improved detector achieved an mAP@0.50:0.95 of 0.789, with 2.15 million parameters and an inference time of 2.90 ms. In the 2024 calibration dataset, the PAI-integrated correction model reduced the estimation error from 8.26% using visible opened boll density alone to 3.48%, with an RMSE of 5.09 bolls·m −2 . In independent validation across 102 plots from 2023 and 2025, the framework achieved an overall MAPE of 2.24%, with treatment-level errors ranging from 0.20% to 8.58%. The resolution sensitivity analysis indicated that the framework remained stable when the spatial resolution was finer than 0.37 cm·pixel −1 . These results demonstrate that explicitly modeling canopy occlusion with PAI enables a robust and interpretable conversion from visible opened boll counts to yield-contributing opened boll density estimates, providing a practical pathway for UAV-based organ-scale cotton phenotyping and yield-component assessment.

title: A novel light-informed computational framework for structure-radiation optimization and allocable space mapping in agroforestry
abstract: Current agroforestry management systems still lack a computable and reusable framework for explicit structure-radiation evaluation, rapid optimization, and spatially explicit analysis. Existing tools provide limited support for light-environment characterization, and the integration of simulation, optimization, and usable-space mapping remains insufficient. To address this, we propose a novel light-informed computational framework based on structure-radiation coupling, including four core modules: (1) Constructing a virtual stand light-field digital twin to reconstruct three-dimensional stand scenes and designing a novel GPU-accelerated, parallel, component-wise differentiable forward radiative tracing simulator (GPU-PCDFRT) to unify structure reconstruction, quantitative light-transport solution, and radiation-response evaluation; (2) Constructing a structure-radiation surrogate model for rapid representation and repeated invocation of attribute–structure–radiation relationships; (3) Designing a light-integrated stand structure optimization agent (LiSSO-Agent) based on an Elite-enhanced Soft Actor-Critic (E-SAC) to generate selective-harvesting decisions under dual constraints of structural quality and light-environment quality; (4) Identifying, delineating, and mapping potentially allocable understorey space after harvesting to support management-oriented space identification based on post-harvest light-environment reconstruction. The framework enabled detailed three-dimensional reconstruction for 50 pure Chinese fir (Cunninghamia lanceolata) plots and effectively captured radiation distribution patterns within complex stands. The generalized additive model (GAM) trained on 1868 individual-tree samples achieved an R2 of 0.840 in ten-fold cross-validation. The E-SAC-based LiSSO-Agent improved three core optimization metrics NL, LightQ, and SR by 83.45 %, 11.33 %, and 22.58 %, respectively, with optimized NL consistently surpassing the initial state and overall outperforming heuristic baselines, and showing high stability across the 50 plots (mean CV = 0.149 %). The framework also reconstructed post-harvest understorey PAR patterns and identified potentially allocable space for the spatial arrangement of light-demanding understorey crops in agroforestry systems. Overall, this study presents a light ecological process-based optimization paradigm that explicitly integrates light into management decisions, enabling coordinated stand structure-radiation regulation and precise understorey resource allocation in agroforestry systems.

title: Research on path tracking control for agricultural mowers with adaptive look-ahead distance based on an improved salp swarm algorithm
abstract: This paper presents an improved path-tracking control method that combines an improved Salp Swarm Algorithm (ISSA) with the pure pursuit algorithm to optimize the look-ahead distance and enhance the tracking accuracy of agricultural mowers on composite paths. To address the insufficient search capability and local-optimum tendency of the conventional Salp Swarm Algorithm (SSA), the proposed ISSA introduces time-varying dynamic weighting and Lévy-flight perturbation as a combined improvement strategy. A fitness function is developed using the predicted positional and heading errors at the next time step, and a curvature-dependent dynamic look-ahead distance range is designed to prevent excessively large look-ahead distances on curved trajectories and overly restricted search ranges on nearly straight paths. Simulation results indicate that the combined ISSA strategy improves convergence stability and reduces premature stagnation under the tested conditions. In variable-curvature simulations with typical agricultural disturbances, ISSA-PP achieved the best overall stability among the selected baseline methods. Real-machine tests further showed that, during straight-line experiments under different initial conditions, the stable mean lateral error was reduced by 35.31 %. For U-shaped composite paths, the overall lateral error of ISSA-PP had a mean of 0.041 m, a standard deviation of 0.063 m, and a maximum error of 0.217 m. The overall mean lateral error was reduced by 0.057 m compared with the fixed-look-ahead pure pursuit algorithm. These results demonstrate that the proposed method can improve pure-pursuit tracking accuracy and stability for agricultural mowers under the tested composite-path conditions.

title: S2SegNet: A semantic-instance joint segmentation network for point clouds of single-stem tomatoes
abstract: Accurate segmentation of plant point clouds is a prerequisite for plant phenotypic analysis. However, existing plant point cloud organ segmentation methods rarely study joint semantic and instance segmentation and lack segmentation schemes designed to address plant structural characteristics. Furthermore, existing data are often collected from the same growth stage under different environments, resulting in limited differences in the overall plant morphology, making it difficult to fully verify the generalization ability of methods across growth stages. Therefore, this paper constructs a greenhouse tomato point cloud dataset covering the seedling and growth stages and proposes a dual-neighborhood graph attention-gated network, S2SegNet, for joint semantic-instance segmentation of single-stem tomato point clouds, considering the structural characteristics of tomato plants. This network constructs Static Geometric Adjacency (SGA) and Local Dynamic Geometric Adjacency (LDRA), and introduces Local Spectral Shape Description (SSD) as a structural prior within the adjacency graph. Two-stage attention (TSA) is then performed, and the output is fed to the decoder through a gated branch fusion (GBF) module. Considering the characteristics of the single-stem task, this paper further improves the semantic-gated instance learning objective loss function and post-processing method. Experimental results show that S2SegNet achieves precision, recall, F1 score, and mIoU of 94.00 %, 92.62 %, 93.28 %, and 87.65 % respectively in the semantic segmentation task on the dataset presented in this paper. In the instance segmentation task, mPre, mRec, mCov, and mWCov for leaves reach 81.33 %, 77.09 %, 74.31 %, and 78.24 % respectively; while mPre, mRec, mCov, and mWCov for stems reach 100 %, 100 %, 80.09 %, and 80.09 % respectively.

title: Field validation of video feedback delay effects in open-field agricultural vehicle teleoperation using frequency-domain steering analysis
abstract: Remote intervention is an important function for agricultural robots operating under remote supervision, but video feedback delay can affect both vehicle tracking performance and operator steering behavior. In open-field agricultural vehicle teleoperation, however, field-based evidence linking controlled video delay to operator control behavior remains limited. This study field-validates video-based teleoperated driving of an agricultural robot tractor under controlled glass-to-glass delay conditions and examines how delay affects lateral tracking performance and the frequency-domain characteristics of operator steering behavior. A teleoperation function was integrated into an autonomous robot tractor, and an in-line network emulator imposed additional fixed one-way delay on the upstream video stream. Teleoperated driving trials were conducted on an agricultural road to emulate between-field travel, with eight participants completing four delay conditions. Time-domain tracking performance was evaluated using lateral RMSE, while steering behavior was analyzed using frequency-domain metrics derived from the steering-rate spectrum. Lateral RMSE tended to increase with delay but exhibited substantial inter-individual variability and did not show a significant condition effect. In contrast, the spectral centroid and the 95% roll-off frequency of the steering-rate spectrum decreased significantly with increasing delay, with substantial within-subject effect sizes. Under the present low-speed controlled task, significant decreases relative to the 0.118-s reference were observed in both frequency-domain metrics at the tested 0.318- and 0.418-s conditions. Correlation analyses suggested that the spectral shifts were not consistently explained by tracking-error changes alone. These findings provide field-based evidence that frequency-domain steering metrics can complement conventional tracking-error measures when evaluating the effects of communication delay on open-field agricultural vehicle teleoperation under the tested low-speed conditions and may inform delay-adaptive operator assistance.

title: Non-contact measurement of breast angle in live chickens based on improved ResNet and multi-source information fusion
abstract: Precise selection breeding is a key method for improving chicken breeds and enhancing production performance, with the breast angle of live chickens serving as one of the important physical parameters for guiding practical applications. This study proposes a Breast Angle Measurement Model (BAngle) that uses Residual Network (ResNet) as a backbone network to integrate features from both visible and infrared images of live chickens. The model incorporates both a Criss-cross Attention Module (CCA) and an Efficient Channel Attention (ECA) module, introduced before and after the final pooling layer, respectively, to achieve stable and efficient measurement of the breast angle. Experimental results showed that measurements based on individual visible images exhibited moderate correlation with the observed values (Pearson correlation coefficient of 0.493), and those based on infrared images displayed weak correlation (Pearson correlation coefficient of 0.282). However, the breast angle measurement model, using fused image features as input, yielded the best results, with a Pearson correlation coefficient of 0.701 with the observed values. The mean coefficient of variation for repeated measurements of a single chicken was 0.54%, with a mean floating error of 1.78% and a mean standard deviation of 0.58°. In terms of overall measurement accuracy, the model achieved a Mean Absolute Error (MAE) of 1.21° and a Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) of 1.41°. This study provides a new solution for the efficient, accurate, stable, and standardized measurement of the breast angle of live chickens, offering a valuable reference for future research in this field.

title: KBTrack: cloud-enabled temporal identity inference for accurate counting in ornamental plant inventory management
abstract: Efficient and accurate counting is essential for ornamental nursery inventory management to support yield prediction, production planning, and sales forecasting. However, conventional manual counting remains labor-intensive, error-prone, and unsustainable at commercial scales. Existing image-based and video-based approaches improve efficiency but still suffer from identification errors, occlusion and identity switches. To address these limitations, we present KBTrack, a multi-object tracking and counting framework specifically designed for ornamental nurseries. The framework combines an ensemble of transfer learning and CutMix-augmented YOLOv11x-seg models to improve detection under dense canopies, which feeds into a temporal identity inference module built on ByteTrack that uses segmentation masks across frames to recover plant identities after occlusion. This design deliberately trades trajectory continuity for identity stability, a choice validated by a Corrected ID Precision of 90.3%, confirming that increased fragmentation reflects successful recovery rather than tracking failure. Because occlusion-driven identity loss is a pervasive challenge across agricultural monitoring systems, this has potential applicability to other dense-canopy environments though validation was limited to two species in a single nursery. The system is deployed within a georeferenced cloud microservice architecture that integrates UAV orthomosaics for bed-level inventory visualization. Evaluated on Azalea and Ligustrum ’Sunshine’ beds, the ensemble backbone achieved mAP@50 of 0.982. KBTrack reduced identity switches by 24% over ByteTrack, the strongest competing tracker, using the same ensemble backbone, and achieved counting accuracy of 0.987 with RMSE of 4.19, compared to 44.1 to 67.2 for conventional trackers.

title: Synergistic mechanism of seed intake-recirculation of a high-speed centrifugal maize metering device based on coupled numerical simulation
abstract: A synergistic inclined tube based on the Venturi effect was developed to address the velocity mismatch between seed intake and recirculation flows in high-speed centrifugal precision maize seed metering devices. Based on theoretical analysis, the structural configuration and geometric parameters of the device were systematically designed and optimized. A coupled CFD–DEM simulation approach was employed to investigate the effects of key geometric parameters on airflow characteristics and seed dynamics. The results showed that a contraction angle of 40° effectively balanced airflow acceleration and energy dissipation, while a diffusion angle of 20° optimized the trade-off between airflow deceleration and seed trajectory convergence. A recirculation angle of 40° provided an appropriate balance between axial throat velocity and seed trajectory stability. In addition, a seed inlet turning distance of 20 mm improved flow stability and promoted smoother seed trajectories, whereas an inlet tube inclination angle of 15° enhanced airflow stability within the throat and improved the uniformity of seed motion, thereby reducing seed collisions and enhancing both seed intake and recirculation performance. Bench validation experiments further demonstrated that the optimal operating conditions were achieved at an air pressure of 1000 Pa and a forward speed of 15 km/h. Comparative experiments with a previous-generation maize seed metering device confirmed that the proposed seed intake–recirculation synergistic inclined tube significantly improved overall seeding performance.

title: Lightweight real-time detection of sweet potato virus disease by a hybrid CNN–Transformer network
abstract: Timely and precise detection of sweet potato virus disease (SPVD) is essential for ensuring crop health and improving yield quality in precision agriculture. However, conventional deep learning models often struggle to capture subtle lesion features under complex field conditions. This paper proposes Swin-SPVDNet, a hybrid CNN-Transformer detection framework with task-specific architectural enhancements that combines convolutional neural networks (CNNs) with a modified Swin Transformer to effectively integrate local spatial details and global contextual information. Unlike conventional hybrid models that simply stack convolutional and transformer blocks, the proposed network introduces three key structural designs: (1) A C2PSA-enhanced convolutional backbone for improved local feature sensitivity. (2) A C3STR module that tightly integrates convolutional operations with Swin Transformer blocks for joint local–global feature interaction. (3) A Residual Attention Block (RAB) that refines feature representations while stabilizing gradient propagation. A field-collected SPVD image dataset was constructed using handheld RGB imaging under real agricultural conditions. Extensive experiments and ablation studies demonstrate that Swin-SPVDNet achieves competitive performance compared with representative state-of-the-art detectors while providing a favorable balance between detection accuracy and deployment efficiency, attaining a mean Average Precision (mAP@0.5) of 86.8%, a precision of 85.1%, and a recall of 75.6%. Compared to Yolov5-v11 models, our approach demonstrates improved robustness in detecting small and irregular lesions, particularly under occlusion and lighting variability. These results confirm the practical value of Swin-SPVDNet for real-time field deployment and support its application in intelligent disease monitoring.

title: DINOv3 meets YOLO26 for enhanced crop-weed detection toward precision vegetable weeding
abstract: The development of robust plant perception models for precision vegetable weeding remains constrained by the scarcity of large-scale, annotated datasets and the limited representational capacity of conventional supervised deep learning frameworks. To address these challenges, this study proposes a foundational crop–weed detection framework that leverages unlabeled heterogeneous datasets via self-supervised learning and integrates a DINOv3-finetuned ViT backbone into the YOLO26 architecture. A multi-source pool of 618,642 crop-weed images was assembled and systematically refined to 199,338 images to fine-tune the DINOv3 ViT. Linear probing on a multi-class crop-weed classification task demonstrated that the fine-tuned ViT outperformed the official DINOv3 ViT by 2.2 % on average after Gram Anchoring. Although classification accuracy dropped after high-resolution adaptation, detection performance improved in preliminary experiments, suggesting a trade-off between global context representation and enhanced local spatial features. The fully fine-tuned ViT was integrated into a modified YOLO26, serving either as a primary backbone or part of a dual-backbone architecture. A feature alignment loss was introduced in the dual-backbone design to facilitate feature fusion with minimal computational overhead. Comprehensive evaluations were conducted against advanced real-time detectors, including YOLOv8 to YOLO26 series and DEIMv2, on both in-domain and cross-domain crop-weed detection. Experimental results show that the DINOv3-pretrained ViT-small YOLO26-large (DINOv3-YOLO26*) achieved up to a 5.4 % mAP@50 gain over the original YOLO26-large on in-domain images collected in the 2025 season. Furthermore, the fine-tuned version (DINOv3*-YOLO26*) model demonstrated strong cross-domain generalization with mAP@50 gains of 14.0 % and 11.9 % on datasets collected from the 2021–2023 and 2024 seasons, respectively, compared with the original YOLO26. Despite a 45.6 % increase in parameter count and a 2.9× increase in inference latency, the proposed model maintains real-time performance at 28.7 frames per second. The software programs developed in this study have been made publicly available to support future research in precision agriculture.

title: Restoration of occlusion in residual film images and curling degree prediction based on UAV in pre-sowing cotton fields
abstract: To mitigate assessment errors in residual film pollution in pre-sowing cotton fields caused by occluders (e.g., drip tapes) and residual film curling, this study develops a UAV-based method for occluded image restoration and prediction of residual film curling degree. Specifically, an improved U-Net model is first used to extract four types of occluders for foreground segmentation and occluder removal. Then, the FSR (Frequency Selective Reconstruction) algorithm is adopted to restore the occluded images. Meanwhile, a curling index is defined to characterize the degree of curling in residual films. An SVR (Support Vector Regression)-based RFCI (Residual Film Curling Index) model is constructed by integrating color and texture features of residual films to predict the unfolded area of curled residual films. Experimental results verify the feasibility of the proposed method: the MPA and MIOU of the multi-object semantic segmentation model reach 79.48% and 69.32%, respectively. The FSR algorithm achieves excellent restoration performance with a PSNR of 39.32 dB and an SSIM of 0.9907. The SVR model delivers favorable regression performance with an R2 of 0.62 for RFCI prediction and 0.65 for unfolded area prediction. Validation on UAV datasets confirms the method’s stability, with an R2 of 0.63 for the regression between true and predicted unfolded film pixel areas. This method reduces pollution assessment errors caused by occlusion and curling, providing reliable technical support for the precise quantitative assessment of residual film pollution in pre-sowing cotton fields.

title: FusFormer: An efficient transformer-based semantic segmentation method for grafting excision point localization
abstract: In the study of automated grafting machines for cucurbit vegetables, accurate recognition and precise localization of seedling characteristics are essential for successful automation. However, current automatic grafting technologies typically rely on selecting seedlings with similar morphological parameters and manual positioning, leading to increased seedling waste and positioning errors. To address these challenges, this paper introduces a novel method for grafting seedling recognition and target localization based on efficient semantic segmentation. Initially, the FusFormer model was developed by combining the MiT B0 encoder with a custom decoder that incorporates multi-scale feature fusion. The decoder includes a nonlinear post-processing multilayer perceptron (NMLP) and a multi-scale fusion module, enabling the generation of high-precision segmentation images for grafting seedlings. Subsequently, a method for grafting excision point localization was proposed, which utilizes segmentation masks to detect the 2D coordinates of excision points in grafting scenarios. Extensive validation was performed on a self-constructed grafting seedling dataset. The experimental results show that the proposed method achieves 81.53 %, 87.78 %, and 88.68 % intersection over union (IoU) for cotyledon, removepart, and stem segmentation, respectively, on the cucurbit seedling dataset, with an MIoU of 90.57 %. For the watermelon seedling dataset, it achieves 99.17 %, 91.34 %, 84.57 %, and 96.98 % IoU for background, cotyledon, stem, and block segmentation, respectively, with an MIoU of 93.02 %. These results significantly outperform current leading models such as DeepLabv3+, U-Net, and PSPNet. Moreover, FusFormer contains only 27.4 %, 12.8 %, 38.7 %, and 20.1 % of the total parameters of PSPNet, U-Net, HRNet, and DeepLabv3+, with its FLOPs comprising 16.4 %, 4.2 %, 46.3 %, and 11.5 %, respectively, of these models. The grafting excision point localization method is employed to determine the grafting excision point coordinates for different segmentation results, which are then compared with the actual positions. The results show that the FusFormer(Feature-Fusion SegFormer)-based method achieves horizontal grafting excision point errors of 1.22 ± 1.2 (cucurbit) and 1.67 ± 1.22 (watermelon), and vertical errors of 9 ± 4.33 (cucurbit) and 1.56 ± 1.13 (watermelon). These errors are notably lower than those achieved by other methods, highlighting the superior localization accuracy of the proposed approach.

title: Artificial intelligence and digital sensing for multiscale soil structure: from observation to decision-making
abstract: Soil structure governs water storage, aeration, root growth, trafficability, nutrient transport, and carbon stabilization, but agricultural monitoring still relies largely on sparse, destructive, and labor-intensive measurements. Digital imaging, spectroscopy, geophysics, in situ sensors, proximal sensing, and remote sensing now provide multiscale observations, yet converting them into reliable structural information remains limited by sparse ground truth, scale mismatch, domain shift, and inconsistent validation. This structured narrative review synthesizes how artificial intelligence (AI) transforms these heterogeneous observations into useful soil structure information for agricultural monitoring and management. We organize the literature around a sensor-to-decision workflow: observation, representation, scaling, discovery, and decision-making. At the pore scale, deep learning improves image enhancement, segmentation, and reconstruction of pore and aggregate architecture from imaging technologies. At pedon and field scales, machine learning links spectra, geophysical signals, mobile proximal sensors, and in situ time series to structural proxies and subsurface states. At landscape scales, AI enables data fusion, downscaling, and transfer learning from UAV, satellite, LiDAR, and mobile sensing platforms. We further examine how physics-guided learning, uncertainty quantification, explainable AI, surrogate modeling, and soil digital twins can improve transferability and support management of transport processes, mechanical resilience, and biological carbon dynamics. By linking sensing modality, AI method, validation design, and management applications, this review provides practical guidance for selecting deployable soil structure monitoring workflows for compaction avoidance, irrigation management, trafficability assessment, carbon stabilization, and resilience monitoring.

title: Transfer learning and multi-branch intermediate fusion deep neural network for wheat nitrogen concentration monitoring using multi-scale multi-modal remote sensing information
abstract: The demand for precise monitoring of wheat plant nitrogen concentration (PNC) has prompted the adoption of remote sensing technology for precision crop management. However, most existing remote sensing studies rely on a single observation scale, making it difficult to fully leverage the synergistic potential of multi-modal data due to inherent scale differences among spectral and texture features. To address this issue, this study developed a multi-scale observation framework to fully explore the representational potential of multi-modal remote sensing data. A data-driven cross-modal feature interaction mechanism was constructed to augment information exchange among heterogeneous features, and a Multi-Branch Intermediate Fusion Deep Neural Network (MBIF-DNN) was proposed to effectively integrate multi-scale and multi-modal information. Transfer learning was also incorporated to support cross-year model generalization. The results demonstrated that spectral features, particularly MS-NIR and RGB-Green bands, were sensitive to scale variations (p < 0.05), while texture features showed even higher sensitivity (p < 0.001). At a single observation scale, multi-modal data fusion significantly improved PNC estimation accuracy. Among all models, MBIF-DNN achieved the best performance, with R2 increasing by 0.087–0.588 and root mean square error (RMSE) decreasing by 0.518–0.837%. Furthermore, integrating optimal features across multiple observation scales further improved model performance, with MBIF-DNN achieving the highest accuracy (R2 = 0.943, RMSE = 0.326%). In cross-year validation, MBIF-DNN combined with transfer learning maintained stable predictive performance (R2 = 0.733, RMSE = 0.560%), demonstrating strong robustness and generalization ability. This study provides an effective framework for wheat PNC monitoring and offers methodological support for precision nitrogen management and agro-ecological sustainability.

title: Lavender electrical signal classification
abstract: Bioinspired approaches offer promising strategies for the development of advanced sensing systems. In this work, we investigate the electrophysiological responses of Lavandula dentata to controlled tactile stimuli applied to different anatomical regions. Electrical signals were recorded under multiple stimulation conditions, including single-finger contact, two-finger contact, and inflorescence compression. The results show that the plant generates distinct and reproducible electrical potential patterns depending on both the stimulation type and the anatomical location. Classification performance reached precision and recall values above 0.95 under single-finger stimulation. Although accuracy decreased under more complex interactions, such as two-finger contact and inflorescence squeezing, responses remained robust for stimulations applied to the stem, peduncle, and leaves. Observed voltage ranges further indicate inter-individual variability across plant samples. In addition, electrical conductivity analysis suggests that detectable responses are preserved under dehydration conditions. These observations suggest that residual ionic conduction and remaining water content may contribute to the persistence of electrical responses under dehydration. The possible influence of essential oils stored in glandular trichomes remains speculative and requires further investigation. These findings support the feasibility of using plant electrophysiology for tactile sensing and highlight the potential of L. dentata as a biohybrid sensing element. The results contribute to the development of plant-based interfaces and open new avenues for integrating living substrates into next-generation tactile sensing technologies.

title: A deep learning framework for non-invasive quantification of wing and foot phenotypes in live broiler chickens
abstract: Accurate phenotypic quantification in poultry is essential for precision breeding and genetic improvement. Recent advances in deep learning have substantially improved the automation and accuracy of phenotyping. However, non-invasive and precise measurement of specific anatomical traits, particularly wings and feet, remains challenging. To address this challenge, we propose a CT imaging-based framework combined with deep learning to quantify wing and foot characteristics in live chickens. Specifically, we develop the DGCUNet for estimating the volumes of eight phenotypic targets associated with wings and feet. The encoder incorporates dilation transformer modules and stage-specific learning strategies to capture hierarchical representations, while the decoder employs a multi-scale fusion architecture to enhance feature integration. Four CT datasets covering multiple chicken breeds are constructed to validate the proposed framework. On the WB2024 dataset, five-fold cross-validation results demonstrate that DGCUNet achieves a Dice similarity coefficient of 86.41%, a 95th percentile Hausdorff distance of 3.28 mm, and an average symmetric surface distance of 0.69 mm. Furthermore, regression models establish relationships between segmented volumes and ground truth weights, and Bland-Altman analysis illustrates the agreement between estimated and actual weights. Overall, our framework enables fine-grained quantification of individual phenotypic traits rather than coarse whole-body measurements, demonstrating the potential of CT imaging and deep learning for advancing poultry phenotyping.

title: A scheduling framework for heterogeneous tractor fleets under operational disturbances: A case study of crop protection operations at Zhaoguang Red-Star Farm
abstract: Coordinated scheduling between operating tractors and supply vehicles is essential for improving the efficiency of large-scale crop management. This study proposes a framework for scheduling heterogeneous machinery swarms in large-scale farm operations while accounting for operational interferences arising from machine capability variations and operator proficiency. The framework comprises two main components: (i) an environment setup module that performs task generation and tractor-vehicle navigation over field and road networks, and (ii) a decision-making module based on LSTM-PPO for joint task-tractor-supply selection. Experimental results show that the environment setup module can generate executable tasks and routes that guide machinery to complete field operations, rendezvous for pesticide refilling at field access points, and return to the warehouse; field tests further verify the feasibility of the generated within-field paths and road-network routes. Tests show that the generated paths can guide tractors to conduct field operations and travel along the road network to and from the warehouse, or rendezvous with a supply vehicle for pesticide refilling. In addition, time deviations associated with task execution and refilling operations are recorded from 15 complete field operation-transfer-service cycles to provide empirical inputs for disturbance modeling and case-specific evaluation of large-scale machinery scheduling. Considering labor and machinery induced disturbances, LSTM-PPO achieves better scheduling performance than baseline methods, including PPO, GA, and ACO, by reducing and stabilizing total operation time. Compared with the static, open-loop ACO baseline, LSTM-PPO reduces the mean total operation time by 478.19 min (7.97 h; 37.3 %) to 802.20 min (13.37 h) across five independently trained random seeds. The results also demonstrate that the trained policy can adapt dynamic decision, maintaining high operational efficiency of the tractor-vehicle-warehouse system under varying disturbance conditions.

title: Simulation and experimental research on the electromagnetic bionic vine killing mechanism inspired by biological joints
abstract: Vine killing is a critical agronomic procedure for improving potato yield. To address the limitations of poor terrain adaptability, high missed-cut rate, and uneven stubble height associated with the widely adopted traditional rigid vine killing mechanism (RVKM), this study designed an electromagnetically driven bionic vine killing mechanism (BVKM) based on the sensory perception and passive-active synergistic adjustment mechanism of flexible biological joints. Transient response simulation and optimization analysis of the flexible structure’s bending section thickness and coil excitation current were performed via multi-physics coupling simulation. Furthermore, an adjustable prototype and a bench test system were developed to characterize the electromagnetic induction signals and control response processes of the BVKM under different load conditions. The results indicate that the optimized BVKM with a 5 mm-thick bending section thickness exhibits electromagnetic induction signal peaks of 0.096 ± 0.021 V and 0.611 ± 0.048 V under cutting and impact loads, respectively, which are consistent with the simulation results. Under impact loads, when a 2 A response current is applied for 10 ms, the mechanism can undergo active buckling deformation without exceeding the yield strength of the flexible structure, achieving flexible buffering and obstacle avoidance. Finally, soil bin tests were conducted to verify the operational performance of the mechanism, which showed significantly superior performance compared to the rigid mechanism. This study demonstrates that the BVKM, integrating operational condition monitoring and buckling-threshold regulation functions, can achieve flexible buffering and terrain-adaptive vine killing during operation.
