The research provides a flexible bionic design concept and methodological support for operating equipment under high-impact and variable-load conditions.

title: Acoustic species-incremental learning with uncertainty-guided dual distillation for fish feeding intensity recognition in aquaculture
abstract: Fish feeding intensity recognition (FFIR) is essential for optimising feed efficiency in aquaculture. Acoustic sensing offers a non-invasive alternative to vision-based monitoring, unaffected by turbidity and lighting and requiring no per-tank camera infrastructure. However, existing acoustic FFIR models are trained on a fixed, closed set of species, so introducing a new species requires costly retraining or fine-tuning that causes catastrophic forgetting. We formulate acoustic FFIR under an expanding set of species as species-incremental learning (SIL), a domain-incremental setting in which the four-level intensity label space is fixed while new species arrive sequentially. We then propose AquaRecall, the first SIL framework for acoustic FFIR. AquaRecall combines an ordinal regression head based on cumulative binary decomposition, dual distillation at the output and feature levels with strength scaled to the number of accumulated species, and an uncertainty-guided exemplar selection strategy that retains decision-boundary samples. We evaluate on Audio-SIL-FFIR, a publicly released benchmark constructed for this study comprising 100,585 acoustic clips across seven fish species at two aquaculture facilities. With only 1.96 M parameters, AquaRecall achieves 76.2 % average accuracy and 70.6 % at the final phase, outperforming the strongest exemplar-based baseline, iCaRL, by 5.7 points while retaining higher accuracy on previously introduced species. Its forgetting stays flat across all six incremental phases, whereas iCaRL degrades progressively. Per-species analysis further shows that forgetting is driven by acoustic similarity rather than time since introduction: the two congeneric tilapia species interfere bidirectionally, each losing roughly 20 points when the other is introduced, regardless of order. These results position AquaRecall as a practical solution for acoustic monitoring as facilities scale to new species.

title: Rice seedling diagnosis of light and water stress based on green – blue channel feature enhancement
abstract: Environmental stress during the rice seedling stage induces subtle phenotypic variations under combined changes in light intensity, spectral composition, and water availability, posing challenges for vision-based diagnostic methods. Existing approaches often suffer from limited sensitivity to fine-grained color features under compound stress or rely on computationally heavy models that hinder real-time deployment. To address these limitations, we constructed a balanced phenotypic image dataset covering multiple combinations of light and water stress conditions and propose a lightweight diagnostic model, termed YOLO-CG, based on the YOLOv8 framework. The proposed model integrates a Convolutional Block Attention Module (CBAM) to enhance discriminative feature representation and Ghost modules to reduce redundant computation and improve efficiency. Without sacrificing diagnostic performance, the Ghost-based design reduces the parameter count by 18.7%. Experimental results demonstrate that YOLO-CG consistently outperforms the YOLOv8 baseline and single-module variants, achieving high diagnostic performance with an F1 score of 0.94, an accuracy exceeding 91%, a precision above 93%, and a recall close to 95%. The proposed approach provides an efficient framework for rice seedling stress diagnosis under controlled imaging conditions and offers a useful basis for future deployment-oriented phenotyping systems.

title: Integrating UAV-derived enhanced disease detection index and texture features for monitoring southern corn rust severity
abstract: Southern corn rust (SCR) is a destructive disease that threatens corn production and food security. Conventional field investigations for assessing SCR severity are time-consuming and difficult to conduct over large areas. Integrating unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) and multispectral remote sensing technology provides a practical approach. In this study, we proposed an Enhanced Disease Detection Index (EDDI) for UAV multispectral imagery, guided by hyperspectral responses across SCR severity levels. Three classifiers were evaluated using four combinations of features: texture features, traditional vegetation indices (VIs), EDDI, and EDDI combined with texture features, to classify severity into Levels 1–5. The results showed that EDDI was highly correlated with SCR severity, and the Pearson correlation coefficient was −0.90. On the held-out test set, the EDDI-only configurations achieved F1-scores that were 7.3–13.5% higher than those of the traditional VI-based configurations. Adding the texture feature to EDDI further increased the F1-score by 1.6–4.8% across the three classifiers. The K-nearest neighbors (KNN) model combining EDDI and the texture feature achieved the highest accuracy (0.733) and F1-score (0.724). Based on this model, the spatial distribution of SCR severity among the breeding materials was mapped, classifying five levels across the study area, with the highest proportion of Level 3 (34.0%), followed by Level 4 (25.2%). Overall, the classification model combining EDDI and texture features provides an interpretable and lightweight approach for SCR severity assessment under the tested field conditions, supporting high-throughput field phenotyping for SCR resistance breeding.

title: Adapting SAM3 for 3D fruit counting with cross-view contrastive learning and Hough voting
abstract: Fruit detection and 3D localization have been shown to be critical for precision agriculture applications, such as yield estimation and robot harvesting tasks. However, real-world agricultural settings can be associated with high density of fruits, strong occlusions, and variable illumination, leading to difficulty in accurately detecting and localizing fruits. Although there exist 2D approaches dedicated for fruit counting, these approaches may easily merge adjacent fruits due to projection effects in dense occlusions, thus limiting their effectiveness. Motivated by this, in this paper, we explore the problem of 3D fruit detection and localization with vision foundation model adaptation and 3D Gaussian-based scene representation. Particularly, we use low-rank adaptation to leverage SAM3 to generate high-quality instance masks with different crops and illuminations. Meanwhile, to address noisy pseudo label issue, we adopt cross-view contrastive learning with uncertainty weighting for enhanced 3D feature representation. Moreover, we devise a Hough voting procedure in the 3D Gaussian space to integrate multi-view evidence of occluded fruits, followed by clustering to estimate the number of fruits as well as their 3D locations. The proposed approach has been extensively tested with thousands of fruits from synthetic orchard scenes, real apple orchard datasets, as well as greenhouse sweet pepper scenes. Experiment results show significant performance gains for densely occluded cases, with the F1-scores reaching 0.971 and 0.977 for plum and mango, respectively. Meanwhile, our approach can achieve more than a twofold boost for 3D instance segmentation over FruitNeRF. More notably, the adapted weights and the post-processing settings transfer from the open-field apple orchard to greenhouse sweet pepper scenes, where only the SAM3 text prompt is changed and the 3D Gaussian representation is still optimized for each new scene.

title: ERG-Mask: An edge–region collaborative instance segmentation model for greenhouse table-grape clusters
abstract: Accurate instance segmentation of grape clusters is important for visual perception in grape-harvesting robots. However, grape clusters in greenhouse trellised table-grape scenes often have irregular contours and dense berry structures, and may appear as individual, adjacent, or overlapping targets. These conditions make it difficult for existing models to obtain complete masks and distinguish cluster instances, especially when adjacent clusters have similar color, texture, and boundary characteristics. To address this problem, this study proposes ERG-Mask, an edge–region collaborative instance segmentation method for table-grape clusters. ERG-Mask consists of a modified ResNet-based backbone, a dual-branch prediction structure, and a polar-coordinate contour reconstruction module. The dual-branch structure predicts grape cluster category and location while estimating boundary information. The contour reconstruction module integrates instance localization and boundary information in polar coordinates to recover cluster contours and generate masks and bounding boxes. Under different natural illumination conditions, ERG-Mask achieved a mean intersection over union (IoU) of 92.12%, an average precision (AP) of 91.61%, and an average segmentation time of 0.14 s per image. The IoU reached 93.39% for individual grape clusters and 90.16% for overlapping grape clusters. Compared with benchmark methods, ERG-Mask remained competitive in individual-cluster scenes and provided more effective instance separation in overlapping-cluster scenes. Greenhouse field trials further showed IoUs of 89.18% and 84.15% for individual and overlapping grape clusters, respectively. These results indicate that ERG-Mask can provide reliable instance-level visual perception for grape-harvesting robots.

title: Scene-graph-grounded vision–language reasoning to action for autonomous multipurpose agricultural robots
abstract: Robotic manipulation in horticultural production remains challenging due to canopy occlusion, mechanically diverse foliage, and the need to prioritize agronomic tasks under uncertain visual evidence. This paper proposes a scene-graph-grounded vision–language reasoning-to-action framework that links structured perception to dual-arm access-oriented manipulation for autonomous multipurpose agricultural robots. Given an observation, a scene-graph generation (SGG) module extracts object instances, attributes, and relationships, which are transformed into a grounded FACT set used as the only visual evidence for planning. A constrained vision–language reasoning module generates a task-level plan and a dual-arm strategy while enforcing strict schema compliance, FACT consistency, and feasibility screening to prevent unsupported visual claims from reaching the robot controller. A minimal reasoning-to-action interface converts the verified plan into executable approach and push primitives for target access and cooperative occlusion management. Field validation is conducted on a dual-arm platform in a commercial greenhouse with N=50 trials (11 harvesting, 14 leaf-removal/pruning, and 25 thinning; 14 cooperative trials). Under standard SGG evaluation, the perception stack achieves relationship recall@50/mean recall (mR)@50 of 63.5/36.2 (predicate classification), 44.1/27.5 (scene-graph classification), and 35.0/22.1 (scene-graph detection; SGDet), with attribute performance of recall@50/mR@50 = 64.0/47.0 (SGDet). End-to-end evaluation yields a plan-validity rate of 0.82 for PSR ∧ FnE ∧ CAS and a strict accepted-validity rate of 0.78 after excluding hallucination-flagged trials. The component-level scores are 0.90 for precondition satisfaction, 0.82 for feasibility/executability, 0.90 for correct action sequencing, and 0.90, 0.82, and 0.82 for task, cooperation, and target agreement, respectively, with a hallucination rate of 0.16. Physical execution achieves an action success rate of 0.60 and a successful-and-safe execution rate of 0.56; all invalid logical plans were blocked before execution (UEPR = 1.00). These results indicate that scene-graph-grounded vision–language reasoning provides an auditable bridge from structured perception to access-oriented multipurpose manipulation in occlusion-heavy environments, while execution robustness remains the primary bottleneck beyond plan-level validity.

title: Assessing social stress in Nile tilapia through AI behavioral analysis and biosensor integration
abstract: Measurements of stress responses in fish using a glucose biosensor make it possible to measure variations in blood glucose concentration – an indicator of stress in fish – as fluctuations in output current, even while the fish are allowed to swim freely. In this study, a new method was developed that integrates the glucose biosensor and AI-based posture estimation. Using the Nile tilapia (Oreochromis niloticus), variations in the concentration of stress indicator substances in the fish’s body were measured by the biosensor, and the fish’s behavior in the water tank was quantified using AI posture estimation. By integrating these datasets, we visualized the behavioral impacts of increase of biosensor current output induced by conspecific agonistic interactions. Conventional standalone physiological monitoring cannot characterize how an altered biosensor current output manifests behavioral change. When social interactions between two fish of different sizes were observed, the behavior of each individual differed. In addition, when focusing on the fish that was attacked violently by the dominant individual, it was confirmed that the range of behavior in the water tank changed in conjunction with the increase in biosensor current output. The results of this experiment showed the observational example of impact of aggressive social interactions on the stress levels and behavior of fish. The findings reported in this paper are based on a single aggressive pair and a single non-aggressive pair. Therefore, they primarily serve to demonstrate technical proof of concept.

title: Hyperspectral multi-indicator ripeness perception model for mechanized harvesting of “Yulu Xiang” pears
abstract: Accurate and rapid determination of fruit ripeness is an important prerequisite for the autonomous operation of harvesting robots. However, existing hyperspectral ripeness detection models are mostly constructed using post-harvest laboratory samples, limiting their applicability under field conditions. Moreover, these models often focus on a single quality indicator and fail to fully exploit the intrinsic spectral correlations among multiple indicators. To address these challenges, we propose a multi-indicator ripeness perception framework for “Yulu Xiang” pears to meet the demands of in-field mechanized harvesting. First, multiple quality indicators, including soluble solids content (SSC), pH, and firmness, were integrated, and a ripeness quantification and classification model was established using the weighted k-means clustering algorithm, providing an efficient method for rapid field grading. Second, to overcome the difficulty of acquiring in-situ field samples, we employed theWasserstein Generative Adversarial Network with Gradient Penalty (WGAN-GP) to generate synthetic hyperspectral data labeled with ripeness, thereby enhancing the diversity and richness of the training dataset. Finally, we designed the multi-scale attention residual network (MSA-ResNet) ripeness perception modelto fully exploit the interrelationships among multiple indicators. Through feature learning and key band selection, the model achieves ripeness grading using only four key spectral bands. Experimental results demonstrated that the proposed MSA-ResNet model achieved a classification accuracy of 87.10% on the field test set under a single split, with a mean accuracy of 83.87% ± 3.23% across five repeated random splits. This study provides a feasible method for in-situ ripeness detection and offers a reference for ripeness discrimination in harvesting robots.

title: Coupling modeling, design optimization, and experimental research of agrivoltaic systems based on soybean cultivation
abstract: As an effective approach to mitigate land competition between energy and agricultural production, agrivoltaic systems face the core challenge of balancing light demands for photovoltaic power generation and crop growth. In this paper, taking the agrivoltaic system for soybean cultivation as the research object, an optimized design method that integrates multiple sub-models and multi-objective optimization is proposed. A coupled model that includes ground irradiance model, photovoltaic power generation model, and soybean yield model is constructed, and the Kriging model combined with the Non-dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm II (NSGA-II) is applied to conduct multi-objective optimization on photovoltaic tilt angle, mounting height, and row spacing, obtaining a Pareto optimal solution set. A soybean planting experiment lasting over three months verifies the model’s reliability. The results show a trade-off between power generation and soybean yield. During the soybean growing season,the power generation corresponding to the Pareto optimal solution ranges from 364,635 to 364,639 kWh, and the soybean yield ranges from 2,800 to 3,200 kg/ha. The photovoltaic tilt angle (peak at 45°) dominates power generation, row spacing is most critical for yield, and mounting height interacts with the other two parameters. The proposed model and method provide quantitative support for the design of agrivoltaic systems tailored to different regions and objectives.

title: Vision-guided robotic harvesting of Toona sinensis sprouts: Integrating biomechanical calibration with improved YOLO instance segmentation
abstract: Toona sinensis, a Meliaceae tree species yielding tender sprouts valued as “tree vegetables,” faces bottlenecks in large-scale production due to the low efficiency and high labor intensity of manual harvesting. Furthermore, the extremely short harvesting window for tender sprouts often coincides with spring rainfall, creating an urgent need for automated systems that can operate in adverse weather conditions. This study develops an automated harvesting robot that integrates an improved YOLO vision algorithm with the physical and mechanical properties of branches and sprouts. Key physical and mechanical parameters of Toona sinensis branches and sprouts, including size, density, and moisture content, were first measured to provide a data foundation for harvester design and finite element analysis. A geometric model was constructed in SolidWorks, and transient structural analysis via ANSYS Workbench verified the mechanical reliability of the claw mechanism. For the vision system, TSIS-YOLO, an instance segmentation model based on YOLO11n-seg, was proposed with targeted optimizations for the biological traits of Toona sinensis. The deployed model supports sprout detection and 3D positioning on the robot. Tests on the self-built dataset show TSIS-YOLO achieves an F1(Mask) of 87.4% and mAP0.5(Mask) of 89.1%, outperforming the YOLO11n-seg baseline by 1.8 and 2.3 percentage points, respectively. Laboratory harvesting trials attain a success rate of 83.7%, while outdoor harvesting tests under moderate rain reach 78.2% with stable recognition performance. The proposed robot achieves accurate harvesting of Toona sinensis sprouts under controlled conditions and demonstrates feasible emergency harvesting capacity in outdoor moderate rainy environments, providing technical support for automated harvesting operations.

title: From sky to ground: Enabling autonomous vineyard traversal with UAV-derived navigation maps
abstract: Reliable structural maps are essential for deploying autonomous ground robots in vineyards, yet producing these maps often still depends on manual real-time kinematic (RTK) surveying or teleoperated data collection. This bottleneck slows robotic deployment and can limit the reuse of spatial data within broader digital-vineyard workflows. In this paper, we present an operational aerial-to-ground pipeline that converts overlapping nadir Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) imagery into robot-ready vineyard maps. The pipeline integrates structural detection, metadata-driven geospatial projection, spatial clustering, and occupancy/topological map generation. By extracting features directly from raw overlapping frames, the system bypasses computationally expensive orthomosaic processing, accelerating the map generation timeline. We evaluate robustness across multiple seasons and flight altitudes, reporting map-level performance and robotic deployment feasibility. Using August 39 ft imagery, all five evaluated models produced sub-metre maps; YOLO11 segmentation achieved an RMSE of 0.242 m, while YOLO11 object detection reached a perfect map-level F1-score. A supplementary best-case capability analysis identified a minimum RMSE of 0.207 m using YOLO11 segmentation on March 39 ft imagery. Field trials on a Thorvald robotic platform, over approximately 500 m of autonomous row traversal per generated map, demonstrated reliable navigation, achieving a Mean Distance Between Interventions (MDBI) of up to 161.4 m. Furthermore, UAV data collection was consistently faster than baseline methods, cutting field survey time by up to 94% compared to robotic teleoperation in a 2.4-hectare commercial-vineyard scalability study. These results demonstrate that overlapping UAV imagery provides a practical route to generating vineyard navigation maps that support autonomous deployment under the tested conditions.

title: From frame-wise detection to instance-level tracking: robust crop row perception for autonomous paddy field navigation
abstract: Robust crop row perception is essential for vision-based autonomous navigation in complex paddy fields, where dense planting, intra-class visual similarity, and dynamic distortions introduce severe perceptual noise. Traditional frame-wise detection methodologies treat crop rows as isolated, independent targets across frames, inherently lacking temporal continuity and suffering from frequent reference instability or identity switching. To resolve these challenges, this paper reformulates crop row perception as a structured sequence tracking problem tailored for paddy field environments. An instance-level tracking framework is presented, which explicitly integrates domain-specific physical and visual priors into a temporal state estimation model to compensate for vehicle oscillations and perspective compression. Furthermore, a global sequence alignment strategy is established by introducing an explicit constraint based on relative horizontal ordering, ensuring reliable tracking under severe field noise. Methodologically, this constraint acts on the global assignment permutation rather than on local pairwise distances, preventing inversion pairs between adjacent row trajectories and current detections. Field evaluations indicate that the proposed framework improves identity consistency and navigation stability compared with representative MOT baselines such as DeepSORT and ByteTrack under the tested paddy-field conditions. Utilizing a SegFormer-B3 backbone, the tracking system yields a MOTA of 82.5% and an IDF1 score of 84.6%. Furthermore, field navigation experiments deployed across multiple autonomous agricultural platforms yield highly stable guidance performance, confining the average lateral deviation to less than 4.8 cm. Comparative field trials indicate that the proposed framework improves navigation stability compared with conventional frame-wise methods by mitigating reference-line jitter and control fluctuations under the tested operating conditions.

title: Research on interaction mechanisms and operating parameter optimization of soybean threshing based on the discrete element method
abstract: To address the unclear mechanisms by which operating parameters affect grain breakage and entrainment loss during soybean threshing in combine harvesters, as well as the lack of a unified threshing interaction mechanism model, this study developed an integrated threshing interaction analysis framework combining mechanistic modeling, interaction simulation, and multi-objective optimization. First, mechanistic models for grain breakage rate and entrainment loss rate were established to quantitatively describe the relationship between operating parameters and threshing performance. Subsequently, a soybean plant discrete element model and a threshing interaction simulation model were developed. Statistical methods for grain breakage rate and entrainment loss rate in the discrete element simulation environment were proposed, and the effects of grain collision and material separation behaviors on threshing performance under different operating conditions were investigated. Finally, a Kriging-MOWOA-based threshing performance optimization model was established. The optimal operating parameters were determined using the Pareto optimal solution set combined with the TOPSIS decision-making method and were validated through field experiments. The results demonstrated that the proposed mechanistic model effectively characterized the intrinsic relationship between operating parameters and threshing performance. Feed rate, drum speed, and threshing clearance were identified as the dominant factors affecting grain breakage and entrainment loss. The optimal operating parameters were a feed rate of 3 kg/s, a drum speed of 395.66 r/min, and a threshing clearance of 30 mm. Under the optimal operating conditions, the field-measured grain breakage rate and entrainment loss rate were 0.67% and 0.45%, respectively, representing reductions of 24.72% and 40.79% compared with those obtained under conventional operating parameters. The proposed threshing interaction mechanism model establishes the relationship between operating parameters and threshing performance, providing a theoretical basis and modeling framework for elucidating the formation mechanisms of grain breakage and entrainment loss, numerical simulation of the threshing process, threshing system design, and intelligent optimization and control of soybean threshing systems.

title: Obstacle-avoidance selective harvesting of green asparagus via semantic-point cloud fusion
abstract: The intensive manual labor required for harvesting constitutes a major bottleneck in green asparagus production. While automation offers a promising alternative, its practical implementation is hampered by insufficient spatial localization accuracy and the high fragility of unripe asparagus spears. To address these challenges, this study proposed an obstacle-avoidance harvesting method based on semantic-point cloud fusion. First, an improved YOLOv8-seg model was developed, incorporating the lightweight HGNetv2 backbone, an Efficient Multi-scale Attention (EMA) mechanism, and a redesigned VoV-GSCSPP feature fusion module. The resulting model contained only 1.7 M parameters, occupied 3.7 MB of memory, and required 5.2 G FLOPs, achieving reductions of 43.3 %, 41.3 %, and 56.7 %, respectively, compared to the original model. Second, an obstacle-avoidance map for unripe asparagus was constructed in OctoMap using spatially clustered point clouds fused with semantic labels derived from the detection of unripe plants. This map provided essential environmental constraints for path planning, significantly enhancing both the safety and environmental adaptability of the harvesting operation. Experimental results demonstrated high positioning accuracy, with mean absolute errors of 2.1 mm (X-axis), 1.8 mm (Y-axis), and 2.0 mm (Z-axis), as well as total spatial error of 3.75 mm. The system also achieved a maturity assessment accuracy of 90 %, an overall harvesting success rate of 91 %, and a mean harvesting cycle duration of 19.38 s, thereby substantiating its functional integrity and providing a solid baseline for subsequent engineering refinement.

title: Full-season wheat phenotyping using UAV-based multi-source remote sensing: dynamic time-series modeling and high-throughput trait extraction
abstract: High-throughput and full-season phenotypic characterization of wheat is essential for crop breeding and precision agriculture. However, the automated extraction of plot-level traits from unmanned aerial vehicle(UAV)-based multi-source data remains challenging because of complex field backgrounds, inconsistent spatial representations among data modalities, and temporal variation in canopy structure. This study developed an automated framework for full-season wheat phenotyping using UAV-acquired RGB, multispectral, thermal infrared, and three-dimensional(3D)point cloud data. The framework focused on three key tasks: plot-level wheat segmentation from 3D point clouds, spatial integration between 3D point clouds and two-dimensional(2D)imagery, and dynamic analysis of phenotypic traits across growth stages. A 3D wheat point cloud segmentation model, termed 3D Wheat Point-Transformer(3D Wheat PT), was developed to separate wheat plots from background points under different cultivation patterns. Based on the segmented point clouds, projection and feature-matching strategies were used to generate spatially consistent plot masks for 2D multi-source imagery, enabling integrated trait extraction from both 2D and 3D data. In addition, the WheatMorph software system was developed to support visualization, automated segmentation, and quantitative extraction of wheat phenotypic traits, forming an end-to-end workflow from data input to result output. Phenotypic traits extracted from 15 sampling stages were further used to construct dynamic temporal curves for growth stage identification, cultivar classification, and trait prediction. Experimental results showed that the proposed 3D Wheat PT achieved segmentation accuracies of 94.4%, 91.8%, and 92.5% across three experimental sites and cultivation patterns. The extracted canopy height showed strong agreement with measured values(R2 = 0.943). Using canopy height growth-rate dynamics as input features, the Long Short-Term Memory model achieved the highest prediction accuracy of 76.7% at the jointing stage(127 days after sowing). These results demonstrate that the proposed framework provides an effective and scalable solution for automated multi-source wheat phenotyping and temporal trait analysis throughout the growing season.

title: Accurate prediction of wheat grain protein content via integration of genomic prediction and high-throughput phenotyping in breeding fields
abstract: Grain protein content (GPC) is a critical determinant of baking quality, and its accurate prediction is essential for breeders, decision-makers, and the agricultural industry. Currently, GPC prediction primarily relies on genomics and phenomics. However, the integration of high-throughput phenotypic (HTP) and genotypic data to predict GPC remains underexplored. In this study, a novel approach was proposed, termed phenotypic genomic prediction (PGP), which combines genomic prediction (GP) and phenotypic prediction (PP) using machine learning (ML) to enhance GPC predictive performance. The predictive performance of the PGP method was evaluated using a population of 262 wheat recombinant inbred lines (RILs) under full irrigation (FI) and limited irrigation (LI) conditions. First, the correlations between GPC and 29 traits across four developmental stages including anthesis, early grain-filling, middle grain-filling, and late grain-filling were analyzed in both environments. The results showed that the middle grain-filling stage had the highest correlation under FI conditions, whereas the early grain-filling stage exhibited the strongest correlation under LI conditions. In addition, the correlations under LI conditions were higher than those under FI conditions. Subsequently, eight commonly used ML methods were separately applied to predict GPC using GP and PP datasets. The optimal GP and PP datasets were then selected, combined in pairs to generate nine PGP datasets, and further evaluated using seven ML methods to identify the best performing model. The combination of rrBLUP_GP & RR_PP based on the GB method was identified as the optimal model (FI, 0.60; LI, 0.69). Compared to GP (FI, 0.41; LI, 0.39), PP (FI, 0.43; LI, 0.56) demonstrated superior prediction accuracy. On average, the predictive performance of PGP was 31.10 % and 15.13 % higher than that of GP and PP, respectively. Feature importance analysis of the PGP models under both environmental conditions showed that the relative importance of GP (FI: 54.13 %; LI: 30.41 %) and PP (FI: 45.87 %; LI: 69.59 %) differed across environments, and both contributed positively to the final prediction outcomes. This approach effectively captures the complex relationships between genotypes, HTP, and GPC traits. Overall, the proposed PGP method demonstrates effective GPC prediction capabilities and can be extended to other traits and crops.

title: Video-based fruit detection and tracking: effects of scanning conditions on fruit load estimation
abstract: Automated fruit counting and yield estimation systems are necessary for efficient orchard management. This study presents a computer vision system based on video multi-object-tracking for fruit load estimation in apple orchards and provides a comprehensive analysis of the system performance under diverse scanning conditions. The system integrates fruit detection, tracking, localization within orchard, and fruit load map generation. Experiments were carried out in an experimental apple orchard containing 420 apple trees. Data was collected with two different RGB-D sensors (Azure Kinect DK and ZED 2) at three different scanning distances (125 cm, 175 cm, and 225 cm) on two different dates prior to the harvest. Comparing the two evaluated sensors, Azure Kinect provided more consistent performance across different dates. Results also show that the longer scanning distance improves accuracy due to seeing the full tree view gives better fruit counts than close partial views. Between the two dates, best results were achieved near harvest due to fruit color at this stage, achieving a Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE) of 6.91 % and a determination coefficient (R 2 ) of 0.733 (using ZED2 sensor at 225 cm distance). Finally, a test comparing scanning from one or both sides of the tree row showed that bilateral scanning improved fruit load estimation at the stretch level by incorporating information from both sides of the canopy. The results of this work demonstrate the effectiveness of the video fruit tracking systems as a useful tool for automating fruit load estimation.

title: FlowDelayNet: self-supervised siamese learning for automated flow-delay estimation in yield monitor data
abstract: Yield monitor data are widely used for management zone delineation, prescription map development, and on-farm decision making; however, delay in the data caused by sensor response latency can misassign yield measurements to incorrect locations. Existing correction methods often rely on manual tuning, or handcrafted similarity measures that are sensitive to noise, missing data, and irregular harvesting geometry. This study proposes FlowDelayNet, a self-supervised deep learning framework for estimating field-level flow delay by learning delay-aware spatial representations. FlowDelayNet employs a Siamese convolutional encoder trained to discriminate whether two yield patches have similar or dissimilar delays. A dataset of 632 harvested fields was split at the field level into training (70%), validation (15%), and testing (15%). Yield surfaces were rasterized over candidate delays from −15 to +15 logging intervals, and overlapping patches (24 × 24, stride 12) were extracted. A Gaussian-based spatial smoothness score computed using correlation analysis provided the self-supervised supervisory signal. Model optimization combined contrastive loss on Siamese embeddings with regression loss against the normalized smoothness signal. Compared to hard-argmax selection, a temperature-scaled soft-argmax formulation improves delay estimation by computing the expected delay. Across 95 fields, the mean absolute error was 1.24 delay units, with 64 fields predicted within ±1 delay relative to the Gaussian spatial smoothness reference. Embedding analysis showed a mean anchor–positive distance of 0.25 compared to 0.72 for anchor–negative pairs, with 94.8% of sampled triplets satisfying AP < AN. These results demonstrate that FlowDelayNet provides an automated and robust solution for flow-delay estimation across heterogeneous field conditions.

title: Semantic risk-aware motion planning for apple young-fruit thinning manipulators
abstract: Thinning young apple fruits is a key practice for regulating tree load and improving fruit quality, yet manual thinning is labour-intensive and constrained by narrow operational windows. To address the challenges of dense fruit clusters and the coexistence of rigid and flexible obstacles, this study proposes a Semantic Risk-Aware RRT* (SRA-RRT*) algorithm for autonomous robotic thinning. The method employs YOLOv11-seg for instance segmentation of fruit clusters, using anchor box centres as end-effector targets. A dual-layer risk field is constructed, with rigid structures as hard constraints and flexible canopy elements assigned semantic risk values to enable low-risk traversal. Risk-guided sampling and bidirectional adaptive tree expansion improve search efficiency, and Catmull-Rom splines smooth paths to generate continuous, executable end-effector motion.Simulation results indicate that in four types of 2D grid environments, SRA-RRT* achieves an average planning time of 0.15-0.54 s with 100% success. In two 3D orchard scenarios, average planning times are 0.41 s and 0.64 s, with path lengths of 173.97 m and 173.12 m, both with 100% success. Compared with RRT*, FMT*, BIT*, AIT*, APF-RRT*, and RRT-Connect, planning times are reduced by 24.7-95.1% and path lengths by 1.6-17.1%. Single-cluster continuous thinning simulations achieve 93.33% success, while physical experiments confirm reductions of 18.8-97.0% in planning time, 12.1-20.4% in path length, a planning success rate of 91.67%, and a single-cluster operation time of 28.4 s.These results demonstrate that SRA-RRT* provides a safe, efficient, and smooth motion planning solution for autonomous thinning of young apple fruits.

title: A formal approach to crop modeling: Automatic code generation and grid simulation using finite state automata
abstract: In this paper, we present a methodology for describing crop models that combines agronomic knowledge with formal descriptions typical of computer science. Our aim is to provide crop modeling researchers with a formal methodology, supported by automatic tools, enabling the simulation of biological systems at different scales, from individual plants to entire populations, under heterogeneous growth conditions. To validate our approach, we used the well-known tomato model TOMGRO as a case study, rewriting it in the formal language of Discrete-Time Hybrid Automata (DTHA). We then automatically generated a correct-by-construction software version of the model, scalable to grids of multiple plants, as an executable program simulating plant growth under different microclimatic conditions. We tested the scalability of this approach for increasing grid sizes ranging from 9 to 1600 plants, and reported experimental data on the time required to synthesize and run the simulation program.

title: Pre-symptomatic detection of late blight in potatoes using field spectroscopy and backpropagation neural networks
abstract: Late blight (LB), caused by Phytophthora infestans, remains one of the most destructive diseases in potato (Solanum tuberosum) production. Early detection, before the emergence of visual symptoms, is critical for timely intervention and sustainable disease management. However, previous research has highlighted the challenges of consistent LB detection under variable field conditions, growth stages, and resistance levels. This study investigates the potential of machine learning models, specifically a backpropagation neural network (BPNN), for the early detection of LB across diverse conditions. Spectral data (400–1650 nm) were collected using a handheld spectrometer from two potato cultivars with differing LB resistance levels (low vs. moderate) at two distinct growth stages (establishment vs. vegetative). The BPNN model achieved high accuracy rates (>95%) from the first day post-inoculation, enabling LB prediction up to four days before visual symptom onset. When data were pooled across cultivars and growth stages, a BPNN model trained on time-series data maintained an overall accuracy of 94%, highlighting the importance of temporal data in enhancing detection robustness. Notably, the most informative wavelengths were identified in the short-wave infrared (1100–1650 nm) range. However, the use of the full spectral range proved necessary for reliable detection across varied conditions, as no single wavelength subset consistently provided optimal results. These findings support the integration of BPNN-based spectral tools for precise, pre-symptomatic LB detection, offering a promising pathway for precision agriculture to reduce fungicide application and secure potato yields.

title: Design and field validation of a vision-based graded compaction intensity control system for wheat seeding
abstract: Spatial heterogeneity in surface soil structure makes it difficult for conventional seeder press-wheel devices to match compaction intensity to local seedbed conditions. We developed a vision-perception-driven system that classifies soil surfaces into small-clod regions, medium-clod regions, and large-clod regions and maps these classes to light, moderate, and heavy compaction commands. Surface images acquired ahead of the press wheel were processed using an improved YOLOv11n model incorporating C3k2_CoT, DyHead, and Focaler-DIoU. A regional evaluation index combining clod area and number proportions was then used to generate graded displacement commands for an electric linear actuator. The improved detector achieved a precision of 86.3%, recall of 90.8%, mAP50 of 95.4%, and inference speed of 41.02 FPS. Relative to baseline YOLOv11n, recall and mAP50 increased by 4.9 and 1.1 percentage points, respectively. Across three forward speeds and three soil-region classes, actuator displacement tracking accuracy ranged from 86.11% to 94.44%, with mean absolute errors (MAE) of 0.69–1.14 mm and root mean square errors (RMSE) of 1.04–1.36 mm. Separate fixed-extension field trials showed a nonlinear effect of actuator extension on seeding quality. Within the tested conditions, a forward speed of 1.5 m·s−1 and an actuator extension of 25 mm produced a 100% qualified sowing-depth rate and a 92.73% sowing-depth stability coefficient. These results demonstrate the feasibility of integrating pre-compaction soil-structure perception with graded actuator control under the tested conditions, providing experimental evidence for adaptive compaction regulation in wheat seeding equipment.

title: Path planning for unmanned combined harvester edging operation based on UAV imagery
abstract: To reduce the dependence on manual driving during combine harvester edging operations, this study developed a staged unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV)–combine harvester cooperative framework. In this framework, UAV images were reconstructed into georeferenced orthomosaics and processed offline using an adapted SCDeepLabV3 + model to segment paddy field regions and extract boundary points. The resulting boundary files were transferred to the vehicle mounted industrial computer via a USB storage device for navigation path generation and online tracking control. A boundary-type-dependent fitting strategy was adopted, using iteratively reweighted least squares (IRLS) for straight boundaries and curvature-constrained B-spline fitting for curved boundaries generated smooth navigation paths that conformed to the kinematic constraints of the harvester. The experimental results show that the SCDeepLabV3 + model achieved a mean pixel accuracy (mPA) of 98.74% and a mean intersection over union (mIoU) of 97.59%. The IRLS based fitting method achieved a mean vertical error of 0.0076(6.23 cm) and a mean angular error of 0.511°.For the curved boundaries,the proposed constrained B-spline method achieved a mean Ldev of 13.46 ± 3.32 cm and a mean within curve Standard Deviation(SD) of 13.42 cm. A controlled comparison was conducted using navigation paths generated from the DeepLabV3 + and SCDeepLabV3 + segmentation results. Relative to the manually delineated reference path, the baseline model achieved an Ldev of 18.40 cm and an SD of 28.88 cm, whereas the proposed model reduced these values to 6.50 and 7.78 cm, respectively. During the subsequent field test at a forward speed of 0.75 m/s, the standard deviations of the lateral and heading deviations were 5.36 cm and 2.56°, respectively. The proposed framework facilitates a cooperative system between a UAV and a combine harvester, ensuring that the generated paths meet the requirements for autonomous navigation in the edging operation of the combine harvester.

title: EOL-DQN: An intelligent cutting decision of potato seed tubers based on improved deep reinforcement learning
abstract: Current intelligent seed-tuber cutting decisions mainly rely on preset geometric rules, which suffer from poor adaptability, single decision planning, insufficient multi-objective optimization, and poor dynamic response. There is an urgent need to develop an intelligent seed-tuber cutting decision that can adapt to complex seed-tuber shapes and bud-eye distribution, learn manual cutting experience, and balance bud-eye preservation with uniform tuber quality. Therefore, based on the principle of deep reinforcement learning, a DQN-based intelligent seed-tuber cutting decision was first proposed, which realizes seed-tuber cutting by designing the state space, cutter action space, exploration strategy and reward function. Pre-experiments show that the DQN decision has problems such as frequent collisions with bud-eye areas, disorderly cutting of multi-bud seed tubers, and low cutting qualification rate, leading to low seed-tuber utilization. To address this, this paper further carries out improvements from four aspects: multimodal feature extraction, cutting-direction optimization, reward-function design, and decision-network architecture, and proposes an EOL-DQN seed-tuber cutting decision integrating agronomic seed-cutting requirements. First, a bud-eye protection mechanism was introduced to limit the exploration space of cutter actions and improve the agent’s active obstacle-avoidance ability; second, priority was given to selecting the action set that meets the cutting-direction constraints to cultivate the agent’s awareness of sequential decision-making, and the first-cut workspace was limited to the apical region of the seed tuber; third, a layered mixed reward function was designed with the introduction of tuber-area uniformity rewards to enhance bud-eye allocation capability and reduce the bud-free rate; finally, the decision-network architecture was improved to strengthen the multimodal-feature perception capability for seed-tuber contours and the spatial distribution of bud eyes. Experiments show that the cutting qualification rate (Drate) of the EOL-DQN decision algorithm reaches 90.17 %. Compared with DQN, DDQN, Dueling DQN, PERDQN, Noisy DQN, C51, QR-DQN and Rainbow DQN, the Drate of EOL-DQN is improved by 21.99, 16.02, 19.21, 15.65, 14.77, 22.83, 16.96 and 11.19 percentage points respectively. The single seed-tuber decision time of EOL-DQN is 0.034  s, which satisfies the real-time operation requirements of seed-tuber cutting. Platform cutting experiments demonstrate that EOL-DQN maintains a cutting qualification rate above 90 % for multiple mainstream seed-tuber cultivars, with no significant difference observed among cultivars (F = 0.0498, P > 0.05), and the cut tuber pieces can meet agronomic requirements. The EOL-DQN seed-tuber cutting decision strategy proposed in this paper can provide effective technical support for intelligent potato seed-tuber cutting.

title: Low-cost autonomous unmanned ground vehicle for in-situ phosphorus screening to support zone-based fertilization in maize crops
abstract: Conventional fertilization in Peruvian maize relies on generalized, empirical criteria because laboratory soil analysis incurs high cost and provides low spatial resolution. This study presents the design, implementation, and field validation of a low-cost autonomous unmanned ground vehicle (UGV) for in-situ soil sensing for the cultivation of hard yellow maize (Zea mays L.). The platform combines an auger-assisted mechanism that inserts low-cost electrochemical probes up to depths of 15–20 cm into the soil and completes a measurement cycle within 38 s. The sensor-fusion navigation system combines the Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) data with visual inertial odometry data. Among the soil parameters acquired, phosphorus was the only channel yielding usable agreement with accredited laboratory references (INIA LABSAF, ISO/IEC 17025); nitrogen and potassium channels showed high volatility and systematic underestimation, respectively. Hence, the N and K channels are reported herein only for transparency. Through Random Forest calibration of the P channel, the raw-probe root mean square error (RMSE) was reduced from 54.2 mg/kg to 25.6 mg/kg under repeated cross-validation (a 53% reduction), with the raw signal significantly correlated with the laboratory reference (r=0.414, p=0.017). However, the cross-validated coefficient of determination remained near-zero (R2≈0.01) at the available sample size. Hence, the calibrated probe serves as a qualitative tool, rather than a quantitative one, for relative P screening. The sensor-fusion strategy achieved a mean positioning error of 1.02 m, a 91% reduction compared to GPS-only navigation, corresponding to open-field waypoint navigation rather than canopy-stage inter-row guidance. A metric named the terrain irregularity index (TII) was determined for the interpretable detection of furrows and obstacles, and georeferenced measurements were transmitted in real time over 4G LTE to a platform that visualizes relative P variability to support zone-based fertilization planning. Overall, this study demonstrates that autonomous low-cost soil monitoring is feasible as a complementary, P-oriented screening tool for zone-based fertilization in smallholder maize. In addition, the present limitations for N and K sensing, quantitative calibration at small sample sizes, and full inter-row autonomy are made explicit.

title: Simple but effective unsupervised classification for specified domain images: a case study on fungi images
abstract: High-quality labeled datasets are essential for deep learning. Traditional manual annotation methods are not only costly and inefficient but also pose challenges in specialized domains where expert knowledge is needed. Self-supervised methods, despite leveraging unlabeled data for feature extraction, still require hundreds or thousands of labeled instances to guide the model for effective specialized image classification. Current unsupervised learning methods offer automatic classification without prior annotation but often compromise on accuracy. As a result, efficiently procuring high-quality labeled datasets remains a pressing challenge for specialized domain images devoid of annotated data. Addressing this, an unsupervised classification method with three key ideas is introduced: 1) dual-step feature dimensionality reduction using a pre-trained model and manifold learning, 2) a voting mechanism from multiple clustering algorithms, and 3) post-hoc instead of prior manual annotation. Using fungal image data as an example, the results show that, after rejecting some ambiguous samples, the proposed method outperformed supervised learning methods in classification accuracy, achieving accuracies of 94.1 % and 96.7 % on the public and private datasets, respectively. The proposed unsupervised classification method reduces dependency on pre-annotated datasets, enabling a closed-loop for data classification. The simplicity and ease of use of this method will also bring convenience to researchers in various fields in building datasets, promoting AI applications for images in specialized domains.

title: A non-destructive watermelon sweetness classification via vision transformer with cross-modal knowledge distillation
abstract: The quality of watermelon sweetness is essential to non-destructive classification that can be applied to the agricultural production process, but the current methods usually use expensive or destructive measures like spectrometry. This study presents a novel cross-modal knowledge distillation framework as a proof-of-concept for non-destructive fruit sweetness classification under constrained sample sizes. The framework consists of three main components, namely a pre-trained model of a teacher that processes both image and mineral concentration information, a vision transformer (ViT) that is a student component and takes images only, and a feature alignment network that links their respective intermediate representations. The student model learns the composite loss function that combines the classification loss, feature space alignment loss, and probabilistic distribution matching loss and hence maps the multimoded knowledge of the teacher to a unimodal one. The preliminary results of experiments show that the offered approach is superior to the traditional machine learning and deep learning baselines. The provided framework reaches the rate of 94.5%, which is higher than the unimodal and multimodal baselines. Moreover, the suggested method can be applied to the empirical issue of implementing sweetness prediction in a resource-constrained environment because it needs standard imaging equipment.

title: A reduced-order equivalent nonlinear modeling method for tree-specific vibratory harvesting parameter determination of Camellia oleifera
abstract: Reliable determination of operational parameters for vibratory fruit harvesting requires a model that captures the dynamics of individual trees. To address this problem, this study proposes a topology-aware reduced-order equivalent nonlinear modeling method for vibratory harvesting of Camellia oleifera and uses the resulting nonlinear model to determine tree-specific operational parameters. Sparse local Duffing corrections, consisting of cubic stiffness and amplitude-dependent damping terms, are introduced only for these critical elements, thereby retaining the dominant nonlinear dynamics under harvesting conditions while keeping the model dimension manageable. Among five identification trees from a 15-tree field dataset, 26 of 216 connection elements exhibited pronounced nonlinearity, mainly at distal parts of secondary and higher-order branches. After sparse local Duffing correction, the large-amplitude response reconstruction error decreased from 0.29 to 0.16, corresponding to an average reduction of approximately 45%. Tree-specific parameters obtained from the corrected model produced an average measured detachment rate of 87.4% on five validation trees, with a mean absolute prediction error of 5.2 percentage points; compared with a fixed linear-parameter baseline, the average detachment rate was 13.2 percentage points higher. These results indicate that the proposed reduced-order equivalent nonlinear model provides a computable and interpretable dynamic basis for tree-specific operational-parameter determination in vibratory harvesting of Camellia oleifera.

title: Adaptive feature learning and wavelet preservation for forest canopy mapping from UAV imagery
abstract: Accurate forest canopy cover mapping serves as a fundamental support for forest resource inventory, ecosystem management and carbon sink accounting. The integration of ultra-high-resolution remote sensing imagery and convolutional neural networks has advanced the efficiency of forest canopy extraction. Nevertheless, current approaches still encounter limitations when applied to scenes with complex backgrounds and dense forest conditions, particularly in accurate canopy boundary delineation and fine-grained target discrimination. Such limitations are primarily attributed to insufficient adaptive modeling of canopy geometric and textural characteristics, as well as the loss of critical structural details during downsampling. This work presents GMNet, a dedicated network for forest canopy mapping, which consists of two core modules, namely Gradient Adaptive Dynamic Convolution and Multi-scale Wavelet Range Downsampling. The Gradient Adaptive Dynamic Convolution module adaptively recalibrates convolutional kernel weights based on gradient cues to facilitate effective canopy feature learning in complex scenarios. The Multi-scale Wavelet Range Downsampling module integrates multi-scale wavelet decomposition with distance statistics to preserve essential structural characteristics, especially boundary details, throughout the downsampling procedure. Evaluated on the BAMFORESTS benchmark dataset, GMNet achieves competitive performance against several state-of-the-art remote sensing segmentation models across commonly adopted metrics. The presented model also maintains comparatively stable performance under changing illumination conditions and canopy shadow interference. The proposed approach is capable of supporting reliable canopy extraction in dense forest scenarios with complex illumination and overlapping tree crowns, showing applicability for forest resource assessment and sustainable forest management. The code is available at https://github.com/WangShiK/GMNet.

title: Numerical simulation of water dynamics and wastewater treatment effect in spiral substrate for recirculating aquaculture systems of Apostichopus japonicus
abstract: Optimizing attachment substrates in recirculating aquaculture systems (RAS) for Apostichopus japonicus requires balancing sufficient attachment area with hydrodynamic conditions favorable for waste removal. In this study, a novel integrated attachment substrate was developed for a 6 m diameter circular culture tank, and computational fluid dynamics (CFD) was used to evaluate the effects of uniform spiral spacing and non-uniform spiral configurations on tank hydrodynamics. A major strength of this study is the development and CFD-based evaluation of a spiral attachment substrate that, unlike conventional flat or corrugated substrates, actively directs water flow toward the central outlet. Among the uniform designs, a spiral spacing of 0.45 m produced the strongest bottom flow, with a maximum velocity of 6.93 m/s and a mean velocity of 1.03 m/s. Further optimization showed that the five-turn non-uniform spiral design provided the best overall hydrodynamic performance, generating a bottom maximum velocity of 6.93 m/s, a normalized maximum velocity Vmax/Vinlet of 8.96, and a maximum normalized TKE of 2.49. This configuration also formed continuous spiral and centripetal flow paths toward the central outlet, indicating enhanced potential for bottom waste transport. Validation against the physical model showed a maximum relative deviation below 12.80%, confirming the simulation’s accuracy. Overall, the five-turn non-uniform spiral configuration achieved a favorable balance between attachment space, flow enhancement, and turbulent disturbance and is recommended for the investigated A. japonicus RAS.

title: Damage mechanism and evolution of Korla fragrant pear under quasi-static compressive loading
abstract: Korla fragrant pear is prone to compression injury during mechanized harvesting because of its thin peel and delicate flesh. To quantify ripeness-dependent failure mechanisms and provide design bounds for end-effectors, we developed an experimentally validated finite element–discrete element (FDEM) model with embedded cohesive elements to simulate quasi-static uniaxial compression. The model reproduced the measured force–displacement responses across six ripeness levels (R2 > 0.96). Simulations show that stress/strain localize at the platen–fruit contact interfaces, where cracks initiate and then propagate preferentially along the fruit major axis before lateral spreading triggers global instability. Energy tracking indicates that external work is stored mainly as elastic strain energy at early loading, whereas damage dissipation and fracture-related energy rise before the peak load and shift earlier as ripening progresses. The dominant failure mode transitions from shear-dominated to tension-dominated behavior: the shear contribution decreases from ∼ 75% to ∼ 38%, while the tensile contribution increases from ∼ 25% to ∼ 62%. These results link field variables and energy partitioning to cohesive fracture evolution, enabling ripeness-aware parameter selection for low-damage gripping. These findings provide practical references for setting ripeness-specific gripping force, displacement limits, and compliant contact parameters in low-damage mechanized harvesting.

title: A lightweight restoration-assisted framework for occlusion-robust longan picking stem detection
Analysis and parameter optimisation of an orchard green-manure cutting and incorporation machine based on the discrete element method
abstract: To address the lack of a dedicated green-manure cutting and incorporation implement for hilly and mountainous orchards and the unsatisfactory cutting and incorporation performance of existing machines, this study developed an orchard green-manure cutting and incorporation machine integrating stem cutting and incorporation, soil pulverisation and firming. Using hairy vetch (Vicia villosa) as the target material, kinematic and dynamic analyses were performed on the green-manure cutting device and soil pulverising device. Flexible individual-plant and population models of hairy vetch based on the discrete element method (DEM) were established to simulate the cutting process, and DEM models for stem incorporation and soil pulverisation were also developed. Single-factor and Box-Behnken tests were conducted to evaluate the effects of operating parameters. The results showed that the plant removal rate was affected by ground clearance, cutting device rotational speed, and forward speed; the qualified rate of stem length by cutting device rotational speed and forward speed; the stem incorporation rate by tillage depth and forward speed; and the soil pulverisation rate by soil pulverising device rotational speed and forward speed. Response surface methodology (RSM) was used to identify the optimal parameter combination, comprising a forward speed of 1.1 m·s−1, a cutting device rotational speed of 2100 rpm, a ground clearance of 50 mm, a soil pulverising device rotational speed of 700 rpm, and a tillage depth of 203 mm. Field validation yielded a plant removal rate, a qualified rate of stem length, a stem incorporation rate and a soil pulverisation rate of 94.25 %, 89.64 %, 86.37 %, and 87.50 %, respectively, with relative errors below 5 %, confirming the reliability of the DEM models and the optimised design.

title: Thermal performance of a passive solar heating system for tropical greenhouse heating: Experimental and CFD analysis
abstract: Thermal inversion is a common problem in tropical highland greenhouses, where nocturnal radiative cooling promotes cold air accumulation near the crop canopy and reduces microclimatic stability. This study experimentally and numerically evaluated the thermal performance of a passive solar heating system for nocturnal greenhouse heating under tropical conditions. The system consisted of a solar thermal collector, a photovoltaic-powered recirculation pump, and a radiant floor heating pipe. Experimental measurements, energy balance analysis, computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations, and a techno-economic assessment were conducted to investigate heat-transfer behavior, airflow patterns, and economic feasibility. The passive heating system increased the greenhouse air temperature by 1.11 ± 0.18 °C relative to outdoor conditions and maintained a stable vertical thermal gradient that mitigated nocturnal thermal inversion. Energy balance analysis showed that the heating pipe supplied 69.6% of the total thermal input, whereas the roof accounted for approximately 66% of total thermal losses. The validated CFD model accurately reproduced the experimental thermal behavior (MAE = 0.187 °C) and revealed a buoyancy-driven bicellular airflow pattern associated with vertical thermal stratification inside the greenhouse. The economic analysis demonstrated a competitive levelized cost of energy of 0.15 USD kWh−1 and a positive net present value of 578.65 USD over a 20-year period. Overall, the proposed system represents a technically reliable and economically viable strategy for improving nocturnal greenhouse microclimates under tropical conditions.

title: Unraveling the Effects of Univariate and Multivariate Signal Decomposition Techniques on Daily Reference Evapotranspiration Forecasting
Robust Silique Wall Area Index retrieval in rapeseed: A Context-Driven Multimodal Dual-stream Fusion Network with canopy structural prior
A Q-learning-guided adaptive framework for dynamic agricultural machinery scheduling with rescheduling and stability optimization
abstract: Efficient scheduling of agricultural machinery in cotton harvesting and transportation is critical for improving operational efficiency and reducing production costs under dynamic and uncertain environments. However, existing approaches often rely on static optimization strategies and fixed search mechanisms, which limit their adaptability to real-world disturbances such as task changes and equipment failures. To address these challenges, this study proposes a Q-learning-guided adaptive evolutionary framework for dynamic agricultural machinery scheduling. A multi-objective optimization model is developed to simultaneously minimize makespan and transportation distance. To enhance search efficiency and solution quality, a hybrid population initialization strategy is designed to improve population diversity, while a Q-learning-based local search mechanism is introduced to adaptively select neighborhood operators according to the current search state. Furthermore, two representative dynamic disturbance scenarios, namely farmland cancellation and machinery breakdown, are incorporated into the scheduling process. Corresponding rescheduling strategies are developed to enable rapid and effective response to disruptions. In addition, a rescheduling instability index (RSI) is proposed to quantitatively evaluate the stability of scheduling solutions under dynamic environments. Extensive experiments under both static and dynamic scenarios demonstrate that the proposed method shows competitive performance compared with benchmark algorithms in terms of solution quality, convergence behavior, and robustness under the investigated conditions.

title: A compact mechanism-based vertical structural representation for UAV LiDAR detection of dead trees in citrus orchards
abstract: Timely and reliable detection of dead trees is important for precision orchard management, particularly under disease-driven (e.g., huanglongbing) canopy decline. However, existing orchard remote sensing approaches have focused mainly on spectral responses, whereas the three-dimensional structural signature of tree mortality remains insufficiently characterized. This study formulates dead-tree detection as a vertical structural representation problem using UAV LiDAR and develops a compact mechanism-based feature framework for interpretable mortality mapping. UAV LiDAR data were acquired across three citrus orchard fields at six flight altitudes from 20 to 120 m, with 507 trees labeled as dead (147) or non-dead (360). For each tree, a normalized vertical return profile was constructed by dividing the relative tree height into n equal-height bins (n=20 in this study), and six compact mechanism-based features were derived to characterize return position, upper- and lower-canopy allocation, vertical redistribution, and profile complexity. Dead trees exhibited a consistent downward redistribution of LiDAR returns, characterized by reduced upper-canopy profile retention, increased lower-canopy profile enrichment, and a lower vertical return centroid. These redistribution-related features provided the strongest class separation, with four core single-feature AUC values of 0.987–0.996. In multi-feature classification, the full normalized vertical profile achieved the highest performance, while the compact mechanism-based feature set closely approached it, with AUC values of approximately 0.997–0.999, indicating that key discriminatory information was retained in a low-dimensional, interpretable representation. Leave-one-field-out evaluation supported robust cross-field generalization, with AUC values ranging from 0.993 to 1.000. The mortality-related structural signal remained detectable across all tested flight altitudes, although lower-canopy profile contrast became smoother with increasing flight altitude. These results demonstrate that dead citrus trees can be effectively detected from UAV LiDAR using an interpretable vertical structural representation, providing a robust basis for scalable tree-level mortality monitoring in citrus orchards and potentially other perennial tree crop systems.

title: A study on the energy-optimal operation of recirculating aquaculture system in eel farm
abstract: Aquaculture production is on the rise all over the world. Among them, recirculation aquaculture system (RAS) farms are advantageous in water quality management, but consume a lot of energy. In order to maintain stable productivity, not only water quality management but also strategies to reduce energy load are necessary. In this study, building energy simulation (BES) was conducted to analyze energy consumption in RAS-type eel farms. The BES model was designed considering all conditions of the testbed, and the model was validated based on the water temperature data measured in the testbed. Using the validated BES model, the water temperature change and energy consumption of the RAS eel farm for summer weather conditions were analyzed. The simulation analysis of the heat pump operation schedule, water level inside the water tank, groundwater temperature, and mixing ratio was conducted using the developed and validated BES model. The validation of final model was completed and the RMSE and MAPE of the final model were less than 0.2 °C and 0.5%, respectively. The water level of the water tank should be operated so as not to use an unnecessarily high level in consideration of the breeding standards of the eel farm and the tank capacity. In addition, it was considered desirable to operate the heat pump at night in consideration of solar energy during the day when the outdoor temperature was high enough. When the groundwater temperature was high, increasing the mixing ratio could reduce energy consumption, but reducing the mixing ratio was advantageous when the temperature was low.

title: Direct surface reflectance retrieval from UAV multispectral imagery using onboard upward-looking spectrometer with MLR under variable illuminations
abstract: Lightweight spectral imaging sensors for unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) enable fine-scale assessment of landscapes, ecosystems, and environments. However, variable illumination (e.g. cloud cover, solar position) introduces significant noise into retrieved surface reflectance from UAV spectral imagery, resulting in biased vegetation indices or compromised biophysical inversion. In this study, we developed a reliable and cost-effective approach for surface reflectance retrieval from UAV multispectral imagery by utilizing synchronized ambient solar irradiance measured with an upward-looking spectrometer mounted on a gimbal for drone tilting correction, and by applying cosine response correction to the spectrometer to mitigate angular sensitivity errors. Multiple linear regression (MLR) was conducted on sensitive spectral bands identified via principal component analysis to explore more lightweight and affordable multiband solutions to record downwelling irradiance. Results show that stabilization and fine-calibration of the downwelling optical sensor collectively reduced errors in solar irradiance measurements by up to 79.8 %, and that the proposed 4-Band MLR method achieved a root mean square error (RMSE) of 1.37 % for in-flight reflectance retrieval, outperforming the prevailing empirical line and broad-band light sensor methods by 79.7 % and 59.0 %, respectively. Diurnal validations across environments produced RMSEs of 2.24 % for ground-based and 2.03 % for UAV-based reflectance retrieval. During drastic cloud movement over a large rice field, the approach improved canopy reflectance consistency by 95.0 % and vegetation indices consistency by a range of 83.2 %-96.2 %. The proposed approach can reliably retrieve surface reflectance from UAV multispectral imagery under variable illuminations, advancing UAV-based spectral imaging for next-generation multiscale remote sensing applications.

title: Development and evaluation of a chain-groove lateral seedling feeding device based on modular stepping misalignment for multi-row transplanting of rapeseed bare-root seedlings
abstract: To address high labor demand and low operational efficiency resulting from the lack of automated lateral seedling feeding mechanisms in multi-row rapeseed transplanters, this study developed a chain-groove-type lateral seedling feeding device (CGLSFD). The device mainly consists of seedling troughs (STs), a chain-groove conveying mechanism, and an ST position sensor, with their operation coordinated by a programmable control system. Based on the modular stepping misalignment principle and the spatial relationships among the guide groove, conveyor chains, and STs, three key feeding parameters were determined to maximize effective ST utilization, eliminate redundant feeding stops, and ensure uniform seedling supply: a total ST capacity of 95, six STs between adjacent seedling feeding positions (SFPs), and a feeding step length of 6. Pre-feeding lead time (ta) and post-feeding lead time (tb) were introduced to coordinate the feeding and picking processes. Accordingly, a programmable logic controller (PLC)-based control system was developed to implement the prescribed timing sequence. A simplex lattice mixture design experiment was conducted to optimize the timing parameter allocation. The regression models indicated that the feeding performance reached its optimum when ta, tb, and the constant-velocity duration (tys) were 0.483 s, 0.793 s, and 0.938 s, respectively. Under this optimized configuration, bench verification trials yielded an average feeding success rate of 89.2 % and a feeding synchronization rate of 84.7 %, with relative prediction errors of approximately 2.5 % and 1.7 %, respectively. Finally, the CGLSFD was integrated into a full-scale transplanter for field trials. The average transplanting success rate and transplanting synchronization rate reached 86.0 % and 80.7 %, respectively, indicating effective coordination of the lateral feeding device with the longitudinal picking-conveying and flexible-disc planting mechanisms during continuous field operation. This study provides a valuable theoretical and technical reference for automated lateral multi-row feeding of bare-root seedlings.

title: A physical-context-conditioned multimodal fusion network for estimating maize canopy nitrogen content using multi-source UAV remote sensing data
abstract: Maize canopy nitrogen content (CNC) is a key indicator of crop nitrogen nutritional status. However, under complex field conditions, single-spectral models are susceptible to spectral saturation and environmental heterogeneity, limiting their estimation accuracy and generalization. Many multimodal approaches use concatenation, fixed weighting, or attention across parallel modality streams, but heterogeneous modalities are commonly treated as parallel predictors, failing to leverage observations from heterogeneous modalities to condition spectral representation learning and regulate branch-level contributions. To address this limitation, this study proposes a Physical-Context-Conditioned Multimodal Neural Network (PCCMN) with an asymmetric, two-stage physical-context-conditioned fusion strategy for maize CNC estimation. Rather than treating hyperspectral, LiDAR, and thermal infrared observations as equivalent inputs, PCCMN treats hyperspectral features as the primary information source for CNC estimation, while canopy structure and thermal status are jointly encoded as sample-specific physical context. Instead of being directly concatenated with spectral features, this physical context is used as a query to selectively aggregate nitrogen-sensitive spectral tokens. An adaptive gating mechanism subsequently regulates the relative contributions of the context-conditioned spectral representation and the physical context representation. This study analyzed data from field experiments conducted in two consecutive years, 2024 and 2025. PCCMN consistently outperformed the comparative models, across the three growth stages and both year-specific held-out test sets, with mean R2 values of 0.79–0.85 and RMSE values of 0.17–0.65. Ablation experiments demonstrated that the performance gains arose from the coordinated effects of multimodal complementarity, context-conditioned spectral selection, and adaptive gating-based fusion rather than from simply adding auxiliary modalities. Gating analysis showed stronger weighting toward the context-conditioned spectral representation in the trumpet-stage model and more balanced allocation between the spectral and physical-context representations in the tasseling- and grain-filling-stage models. SHAP analysis further showed that model decisions were primarily associated with stage-dependent spectral responses concentrated in the red-edge region.These results demonstrate that organizing heterogeneous UAV observations according to their functional roles and dynamically regulating their information flow can support more consistent CNC estimation under phenological and interannual variability. PCCMN therefore provides a physical-context-conditioned multimodal framework for field-scale crop nitrogen monitoring.

title: Latent-space feature reconstruction-enhanced semantic segmentation for agricultural field roads under visual degradation
abstract: Visual perception for autonomous agricultural machinery on unstructured inter-field transfer roads is often affected by drastic illumination variations and dust contamination. These degradations reduce the robustness of segmentation models in real-world field-road environments. To address these challenges, we propose LDRSeg, a robust semantic segmentation framework that improves robustness under degradation conditions by reconstructing degraded features in the latent space. First, to expand degraded data under realistic acquisition constraints, a GAN-based degradation synthesis pipeline is constructed to generate multi-type degraded samples while preserving geometry and semantic consistency.
