Then, a feature reconstruction module guided by a pre-trained latent diffusion prior is introduced to perform implicit denoising and distribution bias correction in the intermediate feature stream, and a progressive decoupled training protocol is adopted to learn a robust mapping from degraded features to clean semantics. Experiments on real degraded test sets show that LDRSeg achieves 75.80 % mIoU and 84.41 % mAcc, outperforming the baseline by 3.17 % and 3.04 %, respectively. It also reduces the Relative Corruption Error (RCE) to 4.20 % for mIoU and 2.97 % for mAcc. In heavy-dust scenes, LDRSeg improves mIoU by 5.19 %. Beyond the primary architecture, cross-architecture experiments further show that the proposed module can improve degraded-scene robustness when integrated into the evaluated CNN- and Transformer-based segmentation architectures.

title: PhySinc-Net: A physics-informed interpretable deep learning architecture for non-contact respiratory rate monitoring in dairy goats
abstract: Respiratory rate (RR) is an important indicator of animal health and thermal status, but its non-contact estimation in small ruminants remains challenging because thoracoabdominal motion is weak, quasi-periodic, and susceptible to body-motion artifacts and environmental clutter. Although 77-GHz frequency-modulated continuous-wave (FMCW) radar enables contact-free sensing independently of ambient illumination, respiratory monitoring in dairy goats is complicated by weak radar reflections, spontaneous body movements, and non-stationary interference. Existing deep-learning approaches commonly rely on black-box feature extraction and lack physiological inductive biases, limiting their robustness in separating weak respiratory harmonics from broadband motion noise. To address these limitations, this study proposes PhySinc-Net, a physics-informed and interpretable framework for non-contact RR monitoring in dairy goats. The model integrates a parameterized Sinc-based spectral front-end to constrain feature learning within plausible respiratory frequency bands, a Frequency-Amplitude Attention module to enhance weak periodic components, and multi-scale temporal branches to capture respiratory dynamics across complementary receptive fields. A Time-Reversal Consistency training strategy exploits the invariance of respiratory frequency under temporal reversal, improving resistance to transient and directional motion artifacts without increasing inference cost. PhySinc-Net was developed using 210 raw ADC radar recordings collected from 20 dairy goats under a controlled channel-based setting and was additionally evaluated on two public human respiratory datasets. In the sample-level held-out test set, PhySinc-Net achieved a mean absolute error of 4.58 breaths/min (bpm), a root mean squared error of 5.97 bpm, and an R2 of 0.95, reducing MAE by 7.85 % and RMSE by 14.71 % compared with the strongest CNN + Transformer. The evaluations on the human datasets provided preliminary evidence of transferability across heterogeneous radar respiratory datasets. With 36,421 trainable parameters, PhySinc-Net offers a compact architecture that warrants future evaluation on embedded hardware. Overall, the proposed framework provides a physics-guided solution to short-duration, non-contact RR estimation in dairy goats under controlled channel-based acquisition conditions.

title: Numerical and experimental investigation on the cutting mechanism of rapeseed stalk using abrasive gas jet based on SPH-FEM coupling
abstract: To overcome the limitations of traditional harvesters-including high energy consumption, weed entanglement, repeated wear, and poor adaptability-this study proposes a novel non-contact abrasive gas jet cutting technology for rapeseed stalk. A composite model utilizing coupled Smoothed Particle Hydrodynamics (SPH) and Finite Element Method (FEM) was established, and Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) simulations were performed to analyze the jet flow field. Results show that increasing nozzle throat diameter (from 1 mm to 6 mm) or inlet pressure (from 1 MPa to 20 MPa) significantly raises the maximum particle velocity and reduces the jet scattering angle (from 14.6° to 3.6° and from 8.54° to 3.37°, respectively). The Laval nozzle outperforms conventional designs, achieving a maximum abrasive particle velocity of 411.46 m/s at 20 MPa—24.7% faster than conventional nozzles—with a 0.52° smaller scattering angle. The Laval nozzle has the convergent-divergent geometry which can accelerate fluid to supersonic velocities, creating a high-kinetic-energy, minimal-divergence jet ideal for efficient stalk cutting. The tests confirmed that optimal performance is attained with a Laval nozzle at 3 MPa pressure, 5 mm standoff distance, and 5 mm/s transverse speed, yielding stable cutting with a minimum kerf width of 1.84 mm. Conversely, reducing pressure or increasing distance and speed degraded cut quality, widening the kerf to over 9 mm. The proposed technology offers a promising non-contact, high-efficiency alternative for agricultural stalk cutting, with the Laval nozzle providing superior precision and energy efficiency.

title: Addressing scale Variation and texture confusion in strawberry phenology detection via a lightweight synergistic network
abstract: The visual detection of the full-cycle strawberry phenology is a key technology for the intelligent greenhouse management of strawberries. However, the visual detection of full-cycle strawberry phenology is facing two bottlenecks. One is difficult to perceive multi-scale small objects. The second is the textural confusion of similar phenological stages. The proposed lightweight detection network, called MTPNet, employs multi-scale aggregation, texture enhancement, and dynamic scale supervision. The proposed backbone has a Multi-Scale Aggregated Cross-Stage (MSA-C2f). This module works using multi-branch dilated convolutions and adaptive channel gating. This helps to gain multi-scale context from small to large ripe fruits in a single feature layer. In the neck region, a Texture-Enhanced Grouped Cross-Stage module (TEG-C2f) applies channel grouping with half-convolution operations (CG-HalfConv) for semantic preservation decoupled from enhancing textural differences between similar phenological stages like young and green fruit. The training utilizes a scale-dynamic loss function (SD Loss), which assigns weights to objects based on their scale and classification. As such, this loss function forces the network to concentrate more on small objects and confusable samples. Experiments on the self-built strawberry phenology dataset showed that MTPNet achieved an mAP@0.5 of 95.4 %, an AP_Early of 58.7 % for young fruits, and an AP_Green of 91.6 % for green fruits, with 3.6 M parameters and 7.9G FLOPs. The model achieved a 96.3 % mAP@0.5 score in generalization validation on the winter jujube dataset. Moreover, the immature fruit AP improved by 4.9 points for the baseline and exhibits strong cross-domain transferability.

title: ArchiCrop: Crop model dynamics downscaled to 3D+t plant architecture
abstract: Abstract Evolving agricultural practices and contexts invite to reconsider the way crop and plant models represent agroecosystem processes. Crop models assume spatial homogeneity, which reduces confidence in their predictions for structurally heterogeneous systems, whereas FSPMs’ complexity limits their application to field-scale or large-scale studies. To benefit from strengths of both approaches, we introduce ArchiCrop, a parametric 3D architectural model of cereals that generates plant geometries constrained by crop model dynamics and coordination rules. Inspired by the concept of equifinality, ArchiCrop generates a morphospace of architecturally diverse morphotypes which remain equivalent at crop scale in terms of LAI and height. This multiscale approach enables the comparison of processes computed at different scales on wheat, rice, maize and sorghum. We demonstrate its application evaluating light interception Beer’s formalism in STICS soil-crop model relying on the leaf-resolved radiosity model Caribu for the 3D reference simulations, for a sorghum monocrop. We show that the consideration of the variability of only two plant architectural traits, leaf insertion angle and leaf number, introduces up to 27% of uncertainty in the cumulated absorbed light at the end of the season. A possible outcome from this method is also the definition of metamodels for crop model processes, as exemplified for extinction coefficient of Beer’s law. ArchiCrop can support a range of applications, including crop model uncertainty analysis, model-assisted phenotyping, and ideotype design. Highlights ArchiCrop is the first 3D+t botany-based parametric generative model for cereals. ArchiCrop downscales crop model dynamics to 3D+t architecture canopies efficiently. ArchiCrop compares big leaf versus leaf-resolved light interception. Plant architectures with same leaf area intercept light with up to 27% variability. ArchiCrop helps ideotyping, crop model evaluation and error propagation analysis. Graphical abstract

title: MSO-Det: A multi-level synergistic optimization framework for robust spike object detection in field scenes
abstract: Spike object detection is important for precision agriculture, yet existing methods still struggle with density variation, boundary ambiguity, and cross-domain generalization in real field scenes. To address these issues, MSO-Det is proposed as a multi-level synergistic optimization framework, improving spike detection at the feature encoding, multi-scale fusion, and loss optimization levels. Specifically, Adaptive Scene Wave Block (ASWB) replaces encoder self-attention with scene-adaptive frequency-domain wave propagation, enabling the model to adjust its response from sparse to dense scenes. Multi-Scale Interactive Aggregation (MSIA) performs hypergraph-based multi-scale semantic aggregation, capturing long-range cross-level interactions and domain-invariant structure beyond fixed grid neighborhoods. Uncertainty-Guided Distribution Refinement (UGDR) derives uncertainty from predicted side-distance distributions and uses curriculum-guided weighting to improve boundary refinement without introducing inference-time overhead. On the GWHD benchmark, MSO-Det improves AP from 22.2% to 32.2%, AP@0.75 from 13.1% to 27.8%, and WDA by 9.9 percentage points. It also yields consistent gains across growth stages, density bins, and occlusion levels, and reaches 24.9% AP on the unseen DRPD rice dataset in wheat-to-rice transfer. These results demonstrate that coordinated optimization across representation, fusion, and supervision can substantially improve robustness in field spike detection. The code and models are available at https://github.com/autumn-1010/MSO-Det.

title: GC-3DGS-pheno: geometry-constrained 3d Gaussian splatting for affordable plant point cloud reconstruction and high-precision phenotyping
abstract: Accurate 3D phenotyping is essential for plant morphology research, but existing high-precision methods rely on expensive equipment and complex protocols, limiting accessibility for small-scale research teams. This study proposes GC-3DGS-Pheno, an affordable plant 3D point cloud acquisition and phenotyping method based on geometrically-constrained 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS), using maize as a case study. The pipeline begins with multi-view video capture using smartphones, followed by rapid sparse reconstruction via Fast3R integrated with exposure compensation (EO-Fast3R) to address instability under complex lighting. A multi-level geometric constraint mechanism , termed GC-3DGS, is then introduced during 3DGS optimization, fusing single-view depth and normal constraints with multi-view cross-perspective geometric consistency to improve the geometric consistency of the optimized 3D representation. An adaptive dense sampling (ADS) algorithm is further incorporated to convert the 3DGS representation into a densified point-cloud representation for downstream phenotyping. Finally, Neural Kernel Surface Reconstruction (NKSR) generates high-quality meshes for precise extraction of key phenotypic parameters. Experimental results demonstrate that GC-3DGS significantly improves plant point cloud quality, producing structurally complete reconstructions with minimal noise and sharp organ contours, effectively resolving noise artifacts, voids, and geometric distortions. Leaf meshes exhibit continuous surfaces without layering defects, and RMSE values for both leaf length and width remain below 1.2 cm. The method also demonstrates potential applicability to other crops, including lettuce, strawberry, and soybean, through qualitative reconstruction examples under field environments. This work provides an affordable framework for high-quality crop 3D reconstruction and organ-level phenotyping, offering a practical solution for plant phenotyping studies, particularly in resource-limited research settings.

title: From sensing to modeling: machine learning-driven wearable humidity sensors for plant water status monitoring
abstract: Plant water status is a critical phenotypic trait underlying precision agriculture and crop health assessment. Yet, continuous, in situ, and non-invasive monitoring under field conditions remains challenging due to limitations in sensor adhesion stability, environmental interference, and the complexity of interpreting sensor signals. Flexible wearable humidity sensors that can attach to leaf and stem surfaces provide real-time access to near-surface moisture dynamics and transpiration activity. As these sensors generate high-dimensional, strongly coupled, and nonlinear datasets, machine learning has emerged as a promising tool for extracting features and predicting plant water status. However, practical deployment faces obstacles such as signal drift, environmental noise, and biofouling, while model generalizability and interpretability remain key barriers to widespread adoption. This review first systematically outlines the physiological mechanisms governing plant water regulation and summarizes recent advances in materials and device innovations for wearable humidity sensors. It then critically examines the integration of machine learning in sensor data analysis and modeling. Finally, we propose a unified conceptual framework that bridges plant water regulation, sensor-based perception, and data-driven analysis, highlighting how algorithmic strategies can enhance system robustness and enable multiscale characterization. This framework lays a theoretical foundation for intelligent monitoring and precision regulation under real-world agricultural conditions.

title: Design and evaluation of a hybrid fin-ray finger with inflatable soft pads for apple harvesting under leaf interference
abstract: This paper presents the design, modelling, and experimental validation of a Hybrid Fin-Ray Finger (HFRF) integrating segmented inflatable Dragon Skin 30 silicone membrane pads for adaptive and bruise-free robotic apple harvesting. Harvesting fruits within cluttered canopy environments demands a balance between gentle contact to prevent bruising and sufficient pulling and detachment torque. However, conventional Fin-Ray fingers often exhibit limited torsional resistance, non-uniform force distribution, and reduced contact area, leading to slip and localized pressure concentrations on the fruit surface. To overcome these limitations, we integrate inflatable soft membrane pads into the Fin-Ray structure, increasing the effective finger width and improving surface conformity and pressure distribution. An analytical model is developed to predict membrane deformation and contact angle as a function of internal pressure, and the results are validated through finite element simulations and experimental testing. Pressure-sensitive film experiments demonstrate that Dragon Skin 30 inflation at 30 kPa increased contact area by up to 40% and reduced mean contact pressure by 11% relative to the unpressurised configuration, while EcoFlex 00–30 exhibited volumetric expansion under pressure that reduced conformal contact across the tested range. Performance evaluations were conducted under three standardized leaf interference conditions (0%, 50%, and 100% occlusion) using real Pink Lady apple leaves, with statistical analysis performed using one-way ANOVA and Tukey HSD post-hoc comparisons. At 30 kPa without leaf interference, normal detachment force increased by 148% relative to the no-pad configuration and torsional moment increased by 58% relative to the unpressurised condition, while maintaining performance above the detachment threshold. Under full leaf occlusion, torsional performance collapsed regardless of inflation pressure, identifying full canopy occlusion as the primary limiting factor for torsional resistance. These results confirm that the proposed HFRF provides pressure-adaptive, slip-resistant, and bruise-mitigating grasping performance suitable for robotic apple harvesting in unstructured orchard environments.

title: Use of smartphone images in the evaluation of weed control with glyphosate: A computational approach using Random Forest
abstract: The evaluation of herbicide control efficacy is essential in integrated weed management, and this information is fed back into the database for future crop protection actions. The evaluation of weed control using herbicides is carried out based on on-site visual evaluations, which can be time-consuming and imprecise. In this study, models capable of evaluating the efficacy of Urochloa brizantha control by glyphosate were proposed using computational image analysis with Random Forest. The images were obtained with a smartphone in an area with U. brizantha infestation desiccated by glyphosate. To stratify the control response, glyphosate doses of 0, 144, 288, 576, 864, 1152, and 1440 g a.e. ha −1 were applied. For model estimation, 27 vegetation indices were used as input variables, with the objective of estimating control based on visual evaluation data and on control percentage data determined by the plant mass killed by the action of the herbicide. The model developed with data from visual control scores presented excellent performance, both in training (r 2 of 0.92) and in validation (r 2 of 0.92). The model trained with the percentage of dead plant mass also presented satisfactory performance, with an r 2 of 0.88 for the training sample and 0.90 for the validation sample. The proposed evaluation method presents advantages over the usual methods, due to the ease of obtaining smartphone images and the possibility of inserting the indices and models developed in mobile applications.

title: YOLOv8-MST: a lightweight and efficient real-time detection and counting deep learning algorithm for double-grain peanut seeding
abstract: Double‑seed precision hill‑drop seeding is a critical technique for ensuring effective peanut emergence, where precise seeding quality relies heavily on high‑performance seed metering devices and real‑time operational monitoring. Traditional manual monitoring is inefficient for enclosed, high-speed air-suction duckbill seeders. Conventional photoelectric sensors fail to identify seed number per hill, seed damage, and impurity inclusion, while existing machine vision methods suffer from excessive computational overhead and cannot support high‑precision real‑time monitoring on low‑cost embedded devices. To address these issues, this paper proposed an edge computing-assisted deep learning monitoring method for peanut hill-drop seeding quality and developed an improved YOLOv8s-based detection and counting algorithm (YOLOv8-MST). All data collection and model training were conducted on a test bench at Qingdao University of Technology, Qingdao, China. A total of 11,130 peanut seeding images were collected and partitioned at the video session level to avoid temporal data leakage, yielding 7,769 training, 2,277 validation, and 1,084 test images following a 70%:20%:10% split. Precision, recall, AP, and mAP were adopted as the model evaluation metrics. In the network design, MobileNetV3 was applied as the lightweight backbone for seed feature extraction. The parameter-free SimAM attention mechanism was introduced to enhance feature representation of stacked and damaged seeds, and Focal_GIoU was used for bounding box regression. Furthermore, the Kalman filter combined with the Hungarian algorithm was embedded to optimize object tracking and improve counting accuracy. Experimental results showed that the proposed YOLOv8‑MST achieved a competitive performance with a compact size of 3.88 M parameters, a mAP of 92.9%, and an average inference speed of 15.7 FPS. Compared with the original YOLOv8s, the frame rate was improved by 54.05%. The proposed algorithm accurately identified seeding status and counted qualified holes, achieving promising accuracy and real-time capability in complex scenarios, which satisfied the on-site real-time monitoring requirements of peanut double-seed hill-drop seeding.

title: Fusion of multi-branch attention mechanism and hybrid graph convolutional network for accurate cow behavior recognition
A real-time estimation method for wheeled agricultural machinery slip parameters in paddy fields based on the prediction-residual approach
abstract: In unstructured paddy field environments, factors such as muddy and slippery conditions, terrain undulations, and soil disturbances lead to widespread tire slip in agricultural machinery, severely affecting path tracking accuracy and navigation control performance. To address the high costs, poor environmental adaptability, and large computational overhead of existing slip parameter estimation methods, this study developed a real-time slip parameter estimation method for agricultural machinery in paddy fields based on the prediction-residual approach. This method introduces longitudinal and lateral kinematic scaling factors to construct an extended kinematic model of a wheeled tractor. By establishing a geometric residual expression between the predicted trajectory and the Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS)-observed positions, the slip estimation problem is transformed into a closed-form inversion optimization model. The method was validated through straight-line and curved-path tests on a paved road and in a paddy field. In the complex variable-curvature paddy-field test, it achieved RMSEs of 0.0390 for the longitudinal slip ratio and 0.0860 rad for the lateral sideslip angle. The method showed good robustness and real-time performance, meeting the state perception requirements for agricultural machinery navigation control systems. Furthermore, comparative field tests against the standard extended Kalman filter (EKF) baseline indicated that the proposed method maintained comparable or improved estimation accuracy while exhibiting reduced phase lag and improved transient responsiveness under rapidly varying slip conditions. The method proposed in this study provides a novel approach for designing a highly adaptive slip perception system for autonomous agricultural operations in paddy fields, thereby enhancing the autonomous operation capability of agricultural robots in complex paddy field terrains.

title: Multimodal spatiotemporal perception fusion: An intelligent classification system for fish stress using iterated dilated convolutional graph temporal neural network
Model-based optimization of dynamic photon allocation for maximizing biomass production under a fixed total light integral in vertical farming
abstract: Lighting, a major energy input in vertical farming, has transitioned from passive adaptation to natural sunlight to active engineering. Dynamic lighting control has drawn increasing attention as a means of enhancing productivity under fixed total light input. However, the resulting large space of possible allocation strategies renders systematic examination through traditional experimental approaches alone practically infeasible. This study used a model-based approach to determine the temporal distribution of light intensity and photoperiod across growth phases under a fixed total photon budget. The Van Henten (1994) lettuce growth model was used to stochastically generate 13,132 light schedules by independently varying light intensity and photoperiod across four growth phases, while keeping the total light integral constant. Consistent with the general benefit of late-phase light concentration reported in prior work, the scenarios revealed increasing biomass accumulation as photon allocation shifted toward later phases, with high-performing strategies bringing forward the photoperiod to establish a foundation for light interception, while concentrating light intensity in the final phase to amplify this effect as the canopy expanded. This high-performing schedule was evaluated through a cultivation experiment on a vertical farm, comparing shoot biomass and photosynthetic performance against a static fixed control. Under the tested conditions, shoot dry weight was 16.5% higher under an identical total light input, with no significant change in fresh weight, corresponding to higher light use efficiency. These findings suggest that model-based exploration coupled with targeted experimental evaluation can render complex temporal photon-allocation optimization in controlled environment agriculture more tractable and testable.

title: A gradient-enhanced lightweight network for peanut leaf disease segmentation in complex field scenarios
3D-architectured self-powered thermoelectric plant e-skins for high-precision early-stage water stress detection
Geometric representation-based facial keypoint matching for sheep identification across growth stages
Interpretable machine learning reveals threshold effects of blue mussel (Mytilus edulis) fouling on the hydrodynamic response of the marine aquaculture netting
Occlusion-Robust fish individual identification: a multi-model video recognition framework for complex underwater environments
PineWilt-MultiSeg: Joint spatial–spectral learning enables precise detection of pine wilt disease
abstract: Pine wilt disease (PWD) poses a serious threat to pine forest ecosystems, highlighting the need for timely and accurate identification of affected trees to support targeted removal and epidemic control. UAV remote sensing combined with deep learning has shown considerable potential for individual-tree-level PWD monitoring. However, most existing studies rely on unimodal imagery, which may provide insufficient information for distinguishing diseased trees from complex forest backgrounds. Although RGB imagery captures detailed spatial, textural, and morphological features, multispectral imagery provides additional information on vegetation pigments, canopy water status, and physiological stress. Integrating these complementary information sources may therefore improve detection accuracy and model robustness. Nevertheless, publicly accessible benchmark datasets providing co-registered RGB and multispectral imagery with pixel-level annotations for PWD remain scarce, limiting systematic model development and comparison. To help address this gap, we constructed PineWilt-MultiSeg, a high-resolution multimodal benchmark dataset comprising 3938 spatially aligned pairs of RGB and 10-band multispectral images with pixel-level semantic annotations. The dataset covers pine trees at the middle and late stages of PWD under diverse canopy conditions and forest backgrounds. Five representative semantic segmentation architectures — SegFormer, PSPNet, Twins-PCPVT, DeepLabv3+, and EncNet — were evaluated to establish unimodal RGB and multispectral benchmarks, while the CMX architecture was employed to assess multimodal feature fusion. Experimental results indicate that multimodal fusion provides consistent and measurable performance gains over unimodal RGB and multispectral inputs, with mIoU improvements of 1.75% and 5.95%, respectively, demonstrating the effectiveness of joint spatial–spectral information integration. Additionally, the influence of spatial resolution on detection accuracy was investigated, and the physical spectral characteristics of diseased trees were analyzed, confirming the superiority of multimodal data in jointly leveraging spatial and spectral information. This study provides a solid data foundation and methodological reference for multimodal detection of pine wilt disease. The dataset and models will be made publicly available at: https://github.com/caudjcc/PineWilt-MultiSeg.git

title: Completeness-aware underwater weight estimation of free-swimming sturgeon using binocular 3D reconstruction
abstract: Accurate weight estimation of freely swimming sturgeon supports continuous growth monitoring, precision feeding, and size grading. However, underwater occlusion and image boundary truncation produce numerous partially visible observations that methods requiring complete fish contours cannot readily use. This study proposed a completeness-aware weight estimation framework based on stereo 3D reconstruction and keypoint constraints. It integrates completeness classification, standardized segment delineation, 3D phenotypic feature extraction from visible regions, and segment-specific regression. Six anatomical keypoints at the head, tail, and bilateral pectoral and pelvic fin bases define one complete-fish category and five standardized partial-body segment categories. The framework reconstructs only spatially continuous visible regions, avoids extrapolating missing body regions, and routes each segment to its corresponding regression branch. This expands the range of usable observations for weight estimation by incorporating occluded or partially out-of-frame samples with valid, continuously visible body segments. In the overall comparison across the six segment categories, Extra Trees achieved an MAE of 37.10 g and a MAPE of 9.93 %. The best-performing segment-specific models yielded MAPE values of 6.80 % and 6.95 % for the head–midbody visible and midbody visible categories, respectively. Combining visible 3D surface area with 3D contour perimeter reduced MAE, RMSE, and MAPE by 23.14 %, 21.66 %, and 29.67 %, respectively, compared with using surface area alone. By converting numerous partially visible observations into usable samples with consistent anatomical meaning, this approach provides a methodological basis for non-contact weight estimation of partially visible sturgeon in practical aquaculture settings.

title: Optimization and experiments on root cutting device for Brassica campestris L. ssp. chinensis var. communis based on dynamic sliding cutting and fracture characteristics
abstract: To address the problem of incomplete root cutting during mechanized harvesting of leafy vegetables, this paper proposed an improved cutting method. Based on the plant morphological characteristics of Brassica campestris L. ssp. chinensis var. communis, the optimal cutting position was clearly defined as the region between the lower part of the petiole tillering point of the first effective leaf and the boundary point of the taproot-compressed stem. Kinematic and mechanical models of the cutting knife were established based on dynamic sliding cutting theory and root fracture mechanics. These models reveal that the main factors influencing the dynamic sliding cutting angle include the connecting rod length |BC1|, crank length |AB|, the angular velocity of the crank ω, and forward velocity v0. On this basis, optimized the cutting device with crank-to-connecting rod ratio λ. A kinematic model of the cutting knife mechanism was constructed based on RecurDyn, and single factor experiments were conducted with the missed cutting area as the evaluation index to further narrow the value ranges of the experimental factors. The soil–plant-cutting knife coupling model was established based on EDEM, and objective optimization was performed by combining orthogonal experiments with the response surface methodology. The optimal parameter combination was determined targeting root cutting height of 13–17 mm: ha = 16.5 mm, |AB| = 12.5 cm, |BC1| = 35.9 cm, ω = 17.89 rad/s, and v0 = 0.47 m/s. Field validation experiments demonstrated Pearson correlation coefficients between simulated and measured values of 0.98 (p ≤ 0.05) for the missed cutting model and 0.99669 (p ≤ 0.0001) for the soil–plant-cutting knife interaction model. Relative to standard low speed and high speed configurations, the improved cutting method increased the peak root cutting qualification rates by 0.84% and 1.55%, respectively, thereby confirming both the reliability of the models and the efficacy of the improved methodology.

title: Editorial Board
Multi-task learning based approach for carambola fruits detection and stems segmentation
abstract: Carambola is a nutrient-rich tropical fruit, yet its industrial development is constrained by the harvesting process. To enhance both the efficiency and quality of carambola harvesting, automated harvesting technology are increasingly being adopted in commercial orchards. However, most existing studies treat fruit detection and picking point recognition as two separate tasks. This method of task separation makes it difficult for the harvesting system to effectively integrate multi-dimensional information such as fruit identification data, ripeness data, and picking location data, leading to reduced overall harvesting efficiency. To address this challenge, we propose the multi-task learning model YOLO-MCM, which simultaneously performs Carambola maturity detection and precise stem segmentation within a unified framework. On one hand, YOLO-MCM extends the YOLOv7 network architecture through multi-task learning, preserving the maturity detection branch while adding a stem semantic segmentation branch. On the other hand, the model integrates three key components-deformable convolutions, an efficient multi—scale attention mechanism, and WIoUv3—to enhance detection accuracy. Additionally, we employ weight uncertainty and PCGrad (project conflicting gradients), thus balancing loss weights and conflicting gradients. Using segmentation outputs, a morphology-based picking-point recognition strategy is designed. Experiments on a self-built dataset of 6,782 carambola images show that YOLO-MCM achieves 90.2% mAP50 in detection, 80.3% mIoU in segmentation, and 36.2 fps (frames per second). Comprehensive comparative and ablation studies have confirmed its superiority over traditional methods, and provide a viable solution for practical intelligent acquisition systems.

title: SpecMCR: A multi-channel spectral regression framework with clustering and GAN-based augmentation for accurate grape sugar prediction
abstract: Accurate estimation of grape sugar content is essential for evaluating fruit maturity and wine quality, yet conventional spectral models often struggle with large variations caused by grape cultivars and environmental conditions. To overcome these challenges, we propose SpecMCR, a spectral multi-channel regression framework that combines unsupervised clustering, score-based conditional GAN (SCGAN) augmentation, and channel-wise regression. The clustering module partitions the spectra into three structurally stable channels, effectively reducing intra-class variability. SCGAN further refines these channels by generating high-quality spectra that enhance boundary regions. With these components, SpecMCR achieves an RMSE of 19.70 and an R2 of 0.85 on the test set while the RMSE values of PLS and SVM above 26, it also outperforms deep models including Inception-v1 and ResNet18, which show test RMSE values around 26.78 and 23.48 respectively. The results demonstrate that SpecMCR captures the heterogeneous structure of spectral data more effectively than single-channel and deep learning baselines, offering a robust and automated solution for agricultural spectroscopy.

title: CFFPose: a cow fine-grained feature keypoint detection model that integrates context awareness and background noise suppression
abstract: The physical appearance of dairy cows is directly linked to individual anatomical elements such as udder structure and limb morphology, while indirectly influencing core production performance metrics like milk yield and fertility. Keypoint detection enables detailed scoring of phenotypic traits by describing fine-grained features keypoints. However, commonly used keypoint detection methods and the standard template defining 17 keypoints fail to meet the demand for detecting fine-grained feature keypoints due to factors including cluttered farm environments, irregular texture patterns, and occlusion by capture devices. To address the above problems, we designed a customized 34‑keypoint template to capture the key phenotypic traits of dairy cattle. More importantly, we propose CFFPose –a novel cow fine-grained feature keypoint detection model that uniquely integrates context awareness and background noise suppression. The customized CSP2F layer structure and hybrid global context attention mechanism are designed to strengthen feature associations between long distances and suppress background noise interference. Furthermore, we develop an optimized detection head, DyHead, by innovatively combining hard keypoint mining with dynamic upsampling, which enables adaptive and efficient learning of challenging keypoints subject to occlusion or blurring. Experimental results demonstrate that the CFFPose model achieves a particularly high AP@0.75 of 91.5% and a mean AP of 81.5% on the newly constructed Cow-34 dataset. Compared to widely adopted baselines, CFFPose delivers a 3.5% AP improvement over RTMPose-s and a 2.2% gain against HRFormer-B, while maintaining efficient computational metrics: merely 8.394 M parameters and 1.66 GFLOPs. More importantly, challenging keypoints like hooves achieve a mean confidence of 0.8, enabling reliable phenotype characterization.

title: NFGTN: A node-fusion graph transformer network for non-destructive estimation of glucoraphanin content in broccoli leaves using RGB-D imaging
abstract: Non-destructive estimation of crop biochemical traits is important for quality evaluation, precision cultivation, and nutritional breeding. As a major glucosinolate in broccoli, glucoraphanin (GRA) is an important indicator of nutritional and functional quality, yet its quantification still relies mainly on destructive chemical analysis. To address this limitation, this study proposes a node-fusion graph transformer network (NFGTN) for estimating GRA content in broccoli leaves using paired red–green–blue (RGB) images and aligned depth information, collectively referred to as RGB-D data. The proposed RGB-D framework integrates a visual backbone, offline graph construction, node-level multimodal fusion, and graph propagation with joint local–global readout within a unified regression architecture. Specifically, an offline graph is constructed to establish explicit correspondence between visual patch features and local plant regions, while a node fusion module is designed to adaptively integrate RGB appearance cues with depth-derived geometric descriptors. On this basis, graph propagation, weighted local pooling, and iterative global readout are employed to jointly model local structural dependencies and graph-level contextual information for final prediction. Experimental results under five-fold cross-validation show that the proposed NFGTN achieved the lowest RMSE of 0.1369, the highest R2 of 0.9232, and the highest RPD of 3.8239 among the compared RGB and RGB-D methods, with an MAE of 0.1098. Additional comparisons with hyperspectral models based on mean spectral representations showed that NFGTN achieved competitive sample-level GRA prediction performance under the present experimental setting.

title: A diffusion-guided framework and dataset for identifying and tracking visually similar goats in non-standardized pens
abstract: In precision livestock farming, the high visual similarity among goats and the variability of non-standardized pen environments complicate individual identification and appearance-based identity association in multi-object tracking. To address these challenges, OSFDR-Net, a lightweight OSNet-based identification model incorporating diffusion-guided feature discriminability refinement (FDR), was developed. During training, the FDR branch provides auxiliary supervision to refine intermediate representations and promote identity-related feature learning under background clutter and appearance variation. The branch is removed during inference, thereby avoiding additional inference overhead. A video-based data construction pipeline was also developed, resulting in a goat identification dataset comprising 66,714 images from 103 goats. OSFDR-Net achieved a mean average precision (mAP) of 65.98 % and a Rank-1 accuracy of 90.79 %, improving on the OSNet baseline by 12.23 % and 5.06 %, respectively. When integrated into three representative multi-object tracking frameworks, OSFDR-Net improved identity-related tracking performance. The improvements were particularly evident in Hybrid-SORT, where replacing the default appearance extractor with OSFDR-Net increased IDF1, AssA, and HOTA by 15.77 %, 16.88 %, and 11.59 %, respectively. These results indicate that more discriminative appearance representations can enhance identity association in multi-object tracking of visually similar goats.

title: Harvesting sequence optimization for clustered strawberries using a fruit-level harvesting difficulty score
abstract: Existing fruit-harvesting sequence planning mainly focuses on minimizing manipulator travel distance, while fruit-specific harvesting difficulty is rarely considered in clustered environments. This study proposed a difficulty-aware harvesting-sequence optimization framework integrating fruit-level harvesting difficulty score (HDS) prediction, dynamic HDS updating, and weighted-sum multi-criteria sequence planning. A two-stage convolutional neural network (CNN)-based vision framework was developed to estimate fruit-level HDS, and the harvesting sequence was re-optimized after each virtual fruit removal using genetic-algorithm-based (MOP-GA) and simulated-annealing-based (MOP-SA) solvers. The HDS regression model achieved an MAE of 6.55% and an R2 of 72.39%. In offline experiments, MOP-GA reduced the average HDS per fruit to 0.282, compared with 0.291 for TSP and 0.297 for bottom-up. Indoor robot experiments across nine strawberry-cluster scenes further showed lower HDS values for MOP-GA (0.197) and MOP-SA (0.204) than for TSP (0.235) and bottom-up (0.237), with all four proposed-versus-baseline comparisons remaining significant after Holm correction. MOP-GA also achieved a lower observed failure rate than TSP (19.11% vs. 26.67%), although the overall difference in failure probability among methods was not statistically significant. These results indicated that dynamically incorporating fruit-level harvesting difficulty can improve harvesting-sequence feasibility in clustered environments, while the increased computational cost remained a limitation for real-time deployment.

title: Automated mating monitoring and occlusion-aware identity attribution in breeding chickens using multi-stage deep learning
abstract: Monitoring mating behavior can provide behavioral indicators relevant to reproductive management in poultry breeding. However, traditional manual observation is labor-intensive, subject to observer fatigue, and ill-suited to identifying specific individuals within dense flocks. To address these issues, this study develops a framework that attributes each mating event to persistently and uniquely identified individuals, thereby enabling per-individual and longitudinal mating-frequency analysis rather than flock- or event-level detection alone. Because the hens belong to a single breed, are viewed top-down, and are physically occluded by the rooster during mounting — conditions under which appearance-based re-identification fails — we introduce an occlusion-aware spatiotemporal matching algorithm that infers the occluded hen’s identity from interaction-induced disappearance, combining temporal gap detection, trajectory-based last-position estimation, and spatial validation within a dynamically defined interaction zone. A lightweight wearable vest-tag system, built around an occlusion-robust color–symbol code set, supplies the deterministic identity signal. Within the pipeline, YOLO11 performs rooster localization and tracking, and UniFormer performs spatiotemporal mating recognition. Experimental results from one 2.4 m × 1.2 m pen containing 44 Hy-Line Sonia hens and 4 roosters showed that UniFormer achieved the highest F1-score on each of the three independent test days. When predictions from the three days were pooled, UniFormer achieved an F1-score of 91.2% (95% CI: 88.0%–94.3%) under natural class imbalance (≈1:188), while the identity-matching module correctly identified both individuals in 458 of 487 pair-evaluable events (94.0%), with an overall pair-attribution yield of 91.8% across 499 unique confirmed events after cross-track duplicate removal. The system automatically generates structured mating logs that provide behavioral indicators for early warning and reproductive management.

title: StomataSeg: Semi-supervised instance segmentation for sorghum stomatal components
abstract: Sorghum is a globally important cereal grown widely in water-limited and stress-prone regions. Its strong drought tolerance makes it a priority crop for climate-resilient agriculture. Improving water-use efficiency in sorghum requires precise characterization of stomatal traits, as stomata control of gas exchange, transpiration and photosynthesis have a major influence on crop performance. Automated analysis of sorghum stomata is difficult because the stomata are small (often less than 40 μ m in length in grasses such as sorghum) and vary in shape across genotypes and leaf surfaces. Automated segmentation contributes to high-throughput stomatal phenotyping, yet current methods still face challenges related to nested small structures and annotation bottlenecks. In this paper, we propose a unified semi-supervised instance segmentation framework for multi-class segmentation of three nested sorghum stomatal components. We collect and annotate a sorghum leaf imagery dataset containing 11,060 human-annotated patches, covering the three stomatal components (pore, guard cell and complex area) across multiple genotypes and leaf surfaces. To improve the detection of tiny structures, we split high-resolution microscopy images into overlapping small patches. We then apply a pseudo-labelling strategy with class-specific confidence filtering and expert verification to unannotated images, producing an additional 56,428 pseudo-labelled patches. Patch-based preprocessing increases the top semantic segmentation mIoU from 65.93% to 70.35% and the top instance segmentation AP from 28.30% to 46.10%. Subsequent pseudo-label retraining further increases overall AP from 46.10% to 49.20% for Mask R-CNN with ConvNeXt-V2. These results demonstrate that combining patch-based preprocessing with semi-supervised learning significantly improves the segmentation of fine stomatal structures. The proposed framework supports scalable extraction of stomatal traits and facilitates broader adoption of AI-driven phenotyping in crop science.

title: Agri-CPJ: A training-free explainable framework for agricultural pest diagnosis using Caption-Prompt-Judge and LLM-as-a-Judge
abstract: Crop disease diagnosis from field photographs faces two recurring problems: models that score well on benchmarks frequently hallucinate species names, and when predictions are correct, the reasoning behind them is typically inaccessible to the practitioner. This paper describes Agri-CPJ (Caption-Prompt-Judge), a training-free few-shot framework in which a large vision-language model first generates a structured morphological caption, quality-gated and, when triggered, refined once, before any diagnostic question is answered. Two candidate responses are then generated from complementary viewpoints, and an LLM judge selects the stronger one based on domain-specific criteria. The ablations show that introducing a caption at all, even before any quality refinement, is the single largest contributor to downstream accuracy for both models tested; quality-gated refinement of that caption adds a smaller but systematic further increment. On CDDMBench, the full caption-enhanced pipeline yields +22.7 pp in disease classification and +19.5 points in QA score over no-caption baselines (GPT-5-Nano with GPT-5-mini caption generator), with ablations showing caption introduction accounts for the majority of the gain. Evaluated without modification on AgMMU-MCQs, GPT-5-Nano reached 77.84% and Qwen-VL-Chat reached 64.54%, placing them at or above most open-source models of comparable scale despite the format shift from open-ended to multiple-choice. The structured caption and judge rationale together constitute a readable intermediate record: a practitioner who disagrees with a diagnosis can inspect the specific caption observation the answer was conditioned on, though we make no claim that the judge’s written rationale is a faithful account of the computation that produced its selection. The code and scripts are publicly available.11https://github.com/CPJ-Agricultural/CPJ-Agricultural-Diagnosis.

title: Improved point cloud segmentation algorithms for in situ individual plant phenotyping and weight prediction of Chinese cabbage plants using UAV imagery
abstract: With the advancement of precision agriculture and modern breeding techniques, large-scale, efficient, and in situ acquisition of plant phenotypic data has become a critical challenge in research. Traditional manual measurement methods are inefficient and struggle to meet the demand for high-throughput phenotypic data in modern breeding. Consequently, this study proposes a method based on low-altitude drones and three-dimensional (3D) point cloud analysis to achieve in situ, nondestructive phenotypic extraction and weight prediction for individual Chinese cabbage plants. First, RGB images are captured in the field using unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs). Large-scale 3D point clouds are reconstructed through structure from motion with multiview stereo technology. Subsequently, an enhanced graph convolutional neural network (AW-GNN) is proposed, integrating wavelet convolution, adaptive graph structure learning, and attention mechanisms to improve the accuracy and robustness of point cloud semantic segmentation. Building on this foundation, a morphology-guided watershed clustering algorithm is introduced. High-density segmentation of individual plants can be achieved in crowded environments by integrating two-dimensional canopy height maps with 3D point cloud spatial information. Based on the segmentation results, 3D phenotypic parameters, such as plant height, canopy width, and volume, are extracted. Individual plant weight prediction models are constructed using machine learning methods, including support vector regression (SVR) and random forest. Experimental results demonstrate that AW-GNN achieves an Intersection over Union (IoU) of 91.63% in point cloud semantic segmentation, significantly outperforming existing mainstream models. Morphological watershed clustering effectively mitigates undersegmentation and oversegmentation problems encountered by traditional methods under dense plant conditions. For individual plant weight prediction, the SVR model delivers optimal performance with a validation set R 2 of 0.8691 and root mean square error of 0.2810 kg. This study demonstrates the feasibility of achieving individual plant phenotyping and weight prediction in large-scale in situ scenarios using a UAV platform and improved point cloud segmentation algorithms, thereby providing an effective technical approach for high-throughput plant phenotyping analysis and digital breeding decision-making.

title: SSM-2DGS-based 3D phenotyping for automated quantification and GWAS of strawberry fruit morphology
abstract: Accurate quantification of 3D morphological traits is essential for strawberry breeding and germplasm evaluation, but conventional phenotyping methods are often limited by 2D projection errors, subjective assessment, and laborious post hoc 3D segmentation. To address these limitations, this study developed a portable multi-view imaging platform and a Segment Strawberry Model-assisted 2D Gaussian Splatting (SSM-2DGS) framework for objective and non-destructive phenotyping of strawberry fruit morphology. The proposed framework directly generates scale-calibrated strawberry fruit meshes without requiring post hoc 3D segmentation, enabling the quantification of five morphological traits: longitudinal diameter, transverse diameter, aspect ratio, fruit volume, and fruit shape catogory. SSM-2DGS outperformed SfM-MVS, Instant-NGP, and 3DGS in reconstruction quality, achieving a peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR) of 36.91 dB and a structural similarity index (SSIM) of 0.902, while the extracted traits showed strong agreement with reference measurements, with R2 values of 0.9148, 0.9069, and 0.8701 for transverse diameter, longitudinal diameter, and fruit volume, respectively. Fruit shape classification achieved an overall accuracy of 82.64 %, with reliable performance mainly observed for the dominant fruit shape categories. Using the 3D-derived fruit volume phenotype, which directly reflects fruit size as an important economic trait, genome-wide association analysis(GWAS) identified two genomic regions on chromosome 4 associated with strawberry fruit size, yielding candidate genes FxaC_14g14270, FxaC_15g16210, and FxaC_15g16170 for subsequent functional validation. Overall, this study demonstrates that SSM-2DGS not only supports accurate quantification of strawberry fruit morphological traits, but also provides a reliable phenotypic foundation for functional gene discovery and genomics-assisted breeding.

title: Wake-mediated spray transport and canopy delivery in agricultural UAV spraying: A mechanistic review
abstract: Agricultural UAV spraying is commonly evaluated by relating nominal operating settings directly to deposition, drift, or biological efficacy. This mechanistic review synthesizes 156 studies. Terminal data are abundant, but the transport stages between release and collection are much less frequently observed. Evidence is concentrated on terminal outcomes, whereas the transitions linking rotor-wake state, spray-source state, canopy arrival, interception, and retained dose remain poorly resolved. Peak or mean downwash velocity does not represent the heterogeneous and unsteady rotor wake, and nominal droplet size does not define the released spray. Similar deposition patterns can result from different combinations of aerodynamic redistribution, evaporation, canopy access, interception, and retention. This review therefore treats agricultural UAV spraying as a coupled, partially observed transport process. Source-wake-canopy compatibility is used to assess whether the released spray, operating wake, and receiving canopy remain connected through the delivery chain, while the evidence-coverage framework distinguishes interpretations supported by direct measurement, independent constraint, or stage-matched validation from those that remain unresolved. Evidence is strongest for terminal performance and weakest at the interfaces between source release, wake-mediated transport, canopy arrival, and retention. Complete source specification, spatially and temporally resolved wake and plume measurements, stage-matched model validation, and benchmark configurations are needed to support cross-platform comparison, inverse design, and adaptive control.

title: DOSeg: Domain-knowledge-guided orthogonal subspace learning for camouflaged pest instance segmentation
abstract: Timely perception of crop pests in complex field environments is a prerequisite for early prevention and targeted intervention. Accurate pest instance segmentation delineates pest individuals and pest-occupied areas at the pixel level, providing spatial evidence for incipient infestation detection and targeted control. However, severe camouflage interference arises from the high similarity between pests and host backgrounds in color, texture, and contour, while subtle morphological differences among related species further intensify fine-grained inter-class confusion. To address these challenges, we propose DOSeg, a domain-knowledge-guided orthogonal subspace learning framework for camouflaged pest instance segmentation. Specifically, dual-granularity semantic priors are constructed from fine-grained textual descriptions, preserving target-specific details while introducing category-level exclusion anchors. To alleviate feature entanglement caused by shared cross-class attributes, an Orthogonal Subspace Purification module is designed to explicitly suppress interference directions from non-target classes. Finally, semantic-guided mask generation decomposes prediction into semantic anchoring and mask assembly. Semantic activation maps suppress background responses in advance and improve the robustness of class-aware instance masks without compromising inference efficiency. In addition, we release PestCamouflage, a dedicated public multimodal segmentation dataset for camouflaged pests, with instance-level pixel masks and fine-grained textual annotations. Experiments show that DOSeg achieves 76.9% mAP@50-95, outperforming the compared visual and multimodal baselines. The code and dataset are available at http://doseg.samlab.cn/.

title: Forecasting farmland dew intensity using deep learning models optimized via an improved snow goose algorithm
abstract: Farmland dew occurs frequently and in significant amounts. While dew plays a crucial role in enhancing fertilizer and pesticide utilization while reducing their runoff, excessive dew can hinder flowering and pollination. Prolonged dew retention on leaves also increases the risk of fungal infections in rice plants, such as rice blast disease, which can lead to subsequent yield losses. The timely forecasting of farmland dew intensity for the following day can effectively mitigate the related adverse impacts on agricultural production. This study provides critical insights for preliminary decisions on crop foliar humidity, as well as the optimal concentration and application timing of foliar fertilizers and pesticides. Multiyear (2011–2021) continuous observational data on farmland dew and meteorological factors are used to develop a hybrid deep learning model (improved snow goose algorithm (ISGA)–variational mode decomposition (VMD) –convolutional neural network (CNN) –bidirectional long short-term memory (BiLSTM) –support vector machine (SVM)) for forecasting the dew intensity 12 h in advance (the following morning). The predictive performance of the ISGA-VMD-CNN-BiLSTM-SVM model was compared with that of linear and physical models. The results demonstrate that the deep learning model achieved an R2 of 0.9266, significantly outperforming the linear model (0.3926) and physical model (0.3061). The mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) between the predicted and observed dew intensities was only 7.15%, with the forecast accuracy reaching 95.58%. The proposed hybrid deep learning model yields advanced forecast-style predictions of dew intensity. Compared with conventional linear models, physical models and existing machine learning methods, this model uses fewer types of meteorological input parameters and achieves obviously higher prediction accuracy. This model provides a novel methodological framework for dew forecasting in agricultural management.

title: Decision-focused learning-augmented MPC for climate control in controlled-environment agriculture greenhouses
abstract: Controlled-environment agriculture (CEA) facilities rely on automated systems to regulate climate, but these systems are energy-intensive. Existing learning-based model predictive control (MPC) methods for CEA climate control typically train state-space models with the goal of improving predictive accuracy, whereas the controller ultimately aims to balance energy use and climate regulation. To this end, this paper proposes an online decision-focused learning (DFL)-augmented MPC framework for CEA climate control. It updates the state-space model online using gradients derived from a control performance indicator, thereby directly linking model adaptation to MPC performance. Numerical studies using a tomato greenhouse simulation model show that DFL-augmented MPC can shift a nominal baseline MPC toward lower energy use. This energy-use improvement is achieved through a deliberate and tunable trade-off in climate-regulation performance. For example, during the tested winter month, the fraction of control steps meeting the prescribed CO2 enrichment requirement decreases from 99.7% under baseline MPC to 95.6% under the presented MPC, while the energy-use cost decreases by 8.43%. Compared with the tested robust and stochastic MPC benchmarks, DFL-augmented MPC remains competitive, although it is not uniformly superior across all performance metrics. Overall, the results demonstrate the potential of online DFL to adaptively balance energy use and climate regulation in CEA climate control, with the resulting benefits depending on the selected performance priorities.

title: A physics-informed, behavior-aware digital twin for robust multimodal forecasting of core body temperature in precision livestock farming
abstract: Precision livestock farming requires accurate and timely heat stress prediction to ensure animal welfare and optimize farm management. This study presents a physics-informed digital twin (DT) framework combined with an uncertainty-aware, expert-weighted stacked ensemble for multimodal forecasting of Core Body Temperature (CBT) in dairy cattle. Using the high-frequency, heterogeneous MmCows dataset, the DT integrates an ordinary differential equation (ODE)-based thermoregulation model that simulates metabolic heat production and dissipation, a Gaussian process for capturing cow-specific deviations, a Kalman filter for aligning predictions with real-time sensor data, and a behavioral Markov chain that models activity-state transitions under varying environmental conditions. The DT outputs key physiological indicators, such as predicted CBT, heat stress probability, and behavioral state distributions are fused with raw sensor data and enriched through multi-scale temporal analysis and cross-modal feature engineering to form a comprehensive feature set. The predictive methodology is designed in a three-stage stacked ensemble, where stage 1 trains modality-specific LightGBM ‘expert’ models on distinct feature groups, stage 2 collects their predictions as meta-features, and at stage 3 Optuna-tuned LightGBM meta-model yields the final CBT forecast. Predictive uncertainty is quantified via bootstrapping and validated using Prediction Interval Coverage Probability (PICP). Ablation analysis confirms that incorporating DT-derived features and multimodal fusion substantially enhances performance. The proposed framework achieves a cross-validated R 2 of 0.783, F1 score of 84.25% and PICP of 92.38% for 2-hour ahead forecasting, providing a robust, uncertainty-aware, and physically principled system for early heat stress detection and precision livestock management.

title: A lightweight dual-task transformer framework with geometry-constrained path extraction for autonomous under-canopy navigation in maize fields
abstract: To address the challenges of reliable perception and navigation in under-canopy maize environments, this study proposes a lightweight dual-task perception-to-navigation framework that jointly performs road and obstacle segmentation and generates geometry-constrained navigation lines. Experiments on a self-collected dataset containing 5051 annotated images show that UC-TwinLiteFormer achieves 95.3 % road mIoU and 86.7 % obstacle mIoU with only 1.46 M parameters, demonstrating a favourable balance between segmentation accuracy and computational efficiency. Building upon the segmentation results, the proposed GCP-NLE converts semantic predictions into structured navigation paths under obstacle-free, non-bypassable, and bypassable scenarios. Jetson Nano deployment and closed-loop navigation simulation further demonstrate the effectiveness and practical feasibility of the complete perception-to-navigation pipeline. Overall, the proposed framework provides an efficient and interpretable solution for autonomous under-canopy navigation of agricultural robots. Future work will further validate the system through full-scale field robot experiments and investigate cross-region generalisation under more diverse agricultural environments. The source code is publicly available at https://github.com/ayi192/UC-TwinLiteFormer.

title: CMDBNet: A cross-modal dual-branch network for dual-task monitoring of cotton aphid damage using UAV RGB and multispectral imaging
abstract: Aphids are major pests affecting cotton production, and accurate assessment of aphid damage is essential for precision pest management. Existing UAV-based multispectral imaging approaches generally rely on single-modal information or conventional feature fusion and typically address either qualitative damage classification or quantitative damage estimation as a single task. This study developed a cross-modal dual-branch network (CMDBNet) for simultaneous monitoring of aphid damage severity (ADS) and the percentage of curly-leaf plants (PCLP) using UAV RGB and multispectral images collected during two field seasons from 2024 to 2025. To improve complementary information learning between the two modalities, a cross-modal feature interaction (CMFI) module was introduced to enable intermediate bidirectional information exchange between the RGB and vegetation-index branches. A cross-modal feature fusion (CMFF) module was further designed to integrate modality-specific and cross-modal shared representations while suppressing redundant information before prediction. The two monitoring objectives were jointly optimized within a unified classification–regression framework using task-specific loss functions. Compared with the Dual-ResNet18 baseline, the mean accuracy, F1-score, and Kappa increased by 4.83, 4.66, and 6.35 percentage points, respectively, while the coefficient of determination (R2) and residual predictive deviation (RPD) increased by 0.09 and 0.95. The CMDBNet also achieved higher mean performance than the evaluated single-modal and conventional dual-branch networks, with an accuracy of 86.14 ± 1.27%, an F1-score of 86.12 ± 1.36%, a Kappa coefficient of 81.39 ± 1.81%, an R2 of 0.90 ± 0.01, and an RPD of 3.27 ± 0.16. Feature-space visualization further showed that CMFI and CMFF progressively improved class separability and produced more continuous feature distributions associated with PCLP variation. In the leave-date-out evaluation, the performance of CMDBNet decreased under temporal separation. Independent evaluations showed relatively stable performance under the 2024 field and cultivar shift but moderate transfer under the changed cultivar and pesticide-management conditions in 2025. These results demonstrate the potential of coordinated cross-modal interaction and fusion for simultaneous qualitative and quantitative monitoring of cotton aphid damage.

title: Detecting CO2 microleakage-stressed vegetation based on UAV hyperspectral imagery using a temporal recursive probabilistic model
abstract: Underground CO2 leakage poses potential risks to ecosystem safety and storage stability in carbon sequestration projects. Vegetation stress responses provide an effective basis for indirect leakage monitoring using UAV hyperspectral remote sensing. However, as sparse vegetation cover in early growth and natural senescence exhibit stress-like characteristics, existing methods for detecting CO2 microleakage-stressed vegetation remain susceptible to crop growth-stage variations. To address this issue, a Temporal Recursive Probabilistic Model (TRPM) was proposed for CO2 microleakage-stressed vegetation detection using UAV hyperspectral imagery from a field-scale underground CO2 release experiment. First, multi-scale super-pixel segmentation was performed based on Baseline Slope Index (BLSI), from which temporal features were extracted. Second, vegetation stress was modeled as a temporal deviation from healthy evolution rather than a single-temporal anomaly, and a temporal recursive probabilistic inference framework was introduced to integrate multi-temporal information for updating stress probability maps. Finally, stressed regions were extracted from the stress probability maps through probability thresholding, multi-scale voting fusion, and morphological filtering. Results demonstrated that TRPM achieved the most stable detection performance across different vegetation types, with mean Recall improved by up to 0.27 and mean False Alarm Rate (FAR) reduced by up to 0.52 compared with existing methods. TRPM showed better early-stage detection than existing methods by day 6 after CO2 injection, and reduced FAR by up to 60 % during the wheat senescence stage. TRPM improves the robustness of vegetation stress detection across different crop growth stages and provides a reliable strategy for vegetation-based CO2 leakage monitoring from multi-temporal UAV hyperspectral imagery.

title: Multisource look-ahead prediction for coordinated vibration attenuation and seeding-depth control in high-speed no-till seeding
abstract: During high-speed no-till seeding, spatial variations in surface topography, soil compaction, straw cover, and seeding-unit effective mass disturb seeding-unit dynamics and final seeding-depth formation. Insufficient look-ahead information and the separate regulation of furrow opening, vibration, and soil covering make it difficult to simultaneously maintain dynamic stability and seeding-depth consistency. This study developed an integrated prediction–control framework comprising a low-disturbance online prediction platform (LDOP), a weakly mechanism-guided multi-task multi-kernel support vector regression model (WMG–MTMK–SVR), and a prediction-driven hydraulic coordinated control system (PDHCC). The LDOP surveyed soil compaction, straw-cover ratio, undulation bias, and undulation dispersion before seeding. During subsequent seeding, these stored variables were retrieved by segment index and combined with the current operating speed and effective mass to jointly predict vibration root-mean-square acceleration, kurtosis, crest factor, dominant frequency, and furrow-opening depth deviation. The predictions were converted into displacement and damping-pressure commands for the ground-following hydraulic cylinder and a compensation-displacement command for the soil-covering-wheel hydraulic cylinder. The framework was evaluated using 6,288 segment-level samples, ADAMS–AMESim co-simulation, bench tests, and 300 paired field observations. On the independent test set, WMG–MTMK–SVR achieved R2 values of 0.876–0.905 and RPD values of 2.840–3.253 across the five outputs, while the RMSE of furrow-opening depth deviation was 0.574 mm. Across in-situ, cross-regional, and cross-temporal validations, the five-output R2 values remained within 0.829–0.914. Compared with the conventional system, PDHCC reduced vibration root-mean-square acceleration, kurtosis, and crest factor by 11.15%, 8.44%, and 12.90%, respectively. It also reduced the mean absolute furrow-opening depth deviation from 1.474 to 0.577 mm and the seeding-depth coefficient of variation from 15.82% to 5.55%, while increasing the qualified seeding-depth rate from 88.33% to 97.33%. These results support the effectiveness of multisource look-ahead prediction and dual-cylinder hydraulic coordination under the tested planter configuration and field conditions in Heilongjiang Province.

title: Study on the influence mechanism of rotary tiller forward and reverse operation on tillage layer reconstruction based on DEM
abstract: Rice straw incorporation improves tillage layer structure and promotes straw resource utilization; however, soil particle migration, straw burial layer distribution, and tillage layer reconstruction under rotary tillage modes remain unclear. To clarify these mechanisms, a rotary blade–soil–straw coupled DEM was developed. A flexible hollow rice straw model composed of sphero-cylinder particles connected by two types of Bonding V2 bonds was constructed to represent hollow structure, flexible deformation, and fracture behavior. Parameters were calibrated using three-point bending and uniaxial compression tests, and the model was validated through soil bin tests. Measured straw burial rates under forward and reverse operation were 90.16 % and 86.23 %, whereas simulated values were 83.32 % and 80.30 %, with relative errors of 6.84 % and 5.93 %, respectively. Errors in straw mass distribution across soil layers were within 8 %. Forward operation produced shallow-layer-dominated disturbance, with 74.13 % of straw concentrated in Layer1 and Layer2, favoring rapid incorporation and shallow coverage. Reverse operation enhanced the mobilization, lifting, and overturning of middle- and deep-layer soil particles, increasing the straw proportion in Layer3 and Layer4 to 51.21 % and promoting deeper migration. Subdomain Mixing Index analysis showed that regions with high straw mass proportions had greater soil mixing uniformity. SMI values in high-value regions were 0.665 and 0.715 under forward and reverse operation, compared with 0.260 and 0.387 in low-value regions. Straw burial layer distribution was governed by direct blade action, local soil reconstruction, and particle-flow mixing. These findings support selection of rice straw incorporation modes and optimization of rotary tillage equipment.

title: Improving greenhouse fruit-production control by integrating reinforcement learning into short-horizon model predictive control
abstract: Greenhouse fruit-production control aims to maximize the economic performance (fruit revenue minus operating costs) while operating within system constraints under external weather disturbances. Control methods need to balance the delayed economic benefit of fruit yield with current operating costs. For such problems, model predictive control (MPC) can handle constraints under future weather disturbances, but can become computationally demanding when using sufficiently long prediction horizons for (relatively large) nonlinear greenhouse fruit production models. In contrast, reinforcement learning (RL) can learn control policies before deployment while considering economic performance beyond MPC’s prediction horizon. However, desired indoor climate ranges are typically incorporated through penalty terms, and performance may degrade under unseen weather trajectories. This work proposes trajectory-selection RL–MPC , a framework that incorporates the economic benefit of fruit yield beyond the MPC prediction horizon into a finite-horizon optimization problem with a relatively short horizon (one hour). The framework uses an RL rollout trajectory to define a terminal region constraint and terminal cost. Next, a nonlinear MPC solves a short-horizon optimization problem with these terminal ingredients to find a local optimum. Finally, the framework selects and executes the first input from the trajectory with the better objective value, either from the MPC-predicted or the RL rollout trajectory. The method is applied to GreenLight, a large-scale nonlinear greenhouse tomato production model that exhibits stiff dynamics. The simulation results show that trajectory-selection RL–MPC with a one-hour prediction horizon matches the closed-loop performance of a high-performing guiding policy while improving over standalone MPC with the same horizon. On 25 weather trajectories held out during policy training, trajectory-selection RL–MPC achieved ∼ 52 % higher closed-loop performance than standalone RL and ∼ 80 % higher performance than MPC with the same horizon length.

title: Structural parameter optimization of a dual-shaft straw chopping and spreading machine for field return using CFD-DEM coupling
Multi-site benchmarking of deep reinforcement learning for forecast-informed irrigation decision-making in paddy rice
abstract: Forecast-informed paddy irrigation must balance water saving, drainage reduction, and yield protection, but comparative evidence across climates is limited. We benchmarked Deep Q-Network (DQN), Double Dueling Deep Q-Network (D3QN), Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO), and Rewarded-Region Replay (R3) in one paddy simulation across 15 site-crop combinations in six agroclimatic zones of China. Each policy was trained on synthetic seasons under three random seeds and evaluated on 105 observed site-years against full irrigation (FI), three deterministic forecast-driven rules, a tuned forecast threshold, and a perfect-foresight dynamic programming (DP) reference. The learned policies reduced seasonal irrigation by 12.4%–16.2% relative to FI, versus 5.4%–7.9% for the rules and 4.7% for the tuned forecast threshold, and raised rainfall utilization efficiency from 0.56 to 0.66–0.69; mean simulated potential yield loss was 0.03%–0.13%. The two value-based methods used the least water (350.3 mm for DQN and 350.8 mm for D3QN) and PPO the most (366.2 mm), while the two actor-critic methods incurred the lowest simulated yield loss (0.03% for R3 and 0.04% for PPO); neither the DQN-D3QN nor the PPO-R3 difference was significant in irrigation or simulated yield loss. Water depth and forecast rainfall jointly governed the switch from waiting to irrigating, but at a given depth the actor-critic methods required more forecast rainfall than the value-based methods to keep waiting. Under stochastic multicriteria acceptability analysis of TOPSIS rankings (SMAA-TOPSIS), the leading policy changed with management priorities: DQN led at 9 of the 15 site-crop combinations where irrigation or drainage volume carried the most weight, and PPO and R3 together led at 9 where simulated yield loss did. Perfect-foresight DP reduced irrigation by 30.5% relative to FI, and the learned policies captured 47.8% of that saving, leaving a mean 66.6 mm gap to DP. The benchmark provides a reference protocol for comparing forecast-informed irrigation policies across climates.

title: TMF-net enabled coppicing quality index (CQI) for predicting resprouting capacity of Caragana korshinskii via morphological phenotyping
abstract: The morphology of the coppice surface in Caragana korshinskii is a key phenotypic trait that strongly influences post-coppicing resprouting and regeneration. However, current evaluation of coppicing quality still relies primarily on subjective visual inspection, lacking engineered, quantifiable morphological indicators and quantitative mapping relationships with resprouting responses. This limitation hinders objective assessment and parameter optimization for mechanized coppicing operations.
