To address the challenges of fragmented boundaries, complex textures, and low contrast with the background in complex field environments, this study proposes an asymmetric three-stream feature fusion segmentation network (TMF-Net) for high-precision extraction of the coppice surface region. Based on the segmented regions, three morphological indicators were constructed: roundness (R), tearing degree (T), and smoothness (S), which characterize the geometric regularity, degree of fiber tearing and fragmentation, and surface evenness of the coppice surface, respectively. Using the number of lateral coppice shoots as the response variable, a random forest model was applied to quantify the relative contributions of these morphological indicators to resprouting performance, and a comprehensive coppice surface quality index (CQI) was subsequently developed. Experimental results showed that TMF-Net achieved mean Intersection over Union (mIoU) of 87.02% on an independent test set, demonstrating robust segmentation performance under complex field conditions. Roundness and smoothness were positively correlated with the number of lateral coppice shoots, whereas tearing degree exhibited a negative correlation. The three-level quality classification (“excellent”, “satisfactory”, “unsatisfactory”) based on CQI achieved an accuracy of 88.0% (264/300) across 300 independent samples. This work integrates image segmentation, morphological quantification, and resprouting capacity evaluation for coppice surfaces, providing technical support for rapid quality assessment and operational parameter optimization in mechanized coppicing of Caragana korshinskii.

title: Learning to see more: Super-resolution for spectral, spatial, and temporal extensions in precision agriculture
abstract: Satellites provide broad, multispectral coverage but lack spatial detail; UAS offer high-resolution imagery but at higher costs and restricted coverage. Fusing these datasets is vital for scalable, cost-effective agricultural applications, yet extensive UAS data collection is often impractical. This study presents a super-resolution system to integrate satellite and UAS imagery across spectral, spatial, and temporal domains, improving biomass and nitrogen (N) estimation in winter cover crops — a key component of sustainable agriculture in the Chesapeake Bay region. Our approach uses sensor harmonization to combine UAS RGB bands with Sentinel-2 10 m and 20 m bands, generating 12.5 cm resolution images with high spectral fidelity (PSNR >30 dB). This spectral extension extends UAS-RGB data to the vegetation red-edge and near-infrared regions, improving biomass and N estimation accuracy by 18% and 31%, respectively, over Sentinel-2 baselines. Critically, UAS data collection can be limited to a subset of fields and time points — farmers can then enhance the spectral detail of UAS-RGB imagery and increase spatial resolution up to 80× across the growing season. Our hyper-local spatial and temporal extension models further produce 1 m resolution VNIR bands from Sentinel-2 inputs alone, eliminating the need for UAS flights at unsampled locations and time points while maintaining estimation performance. Together, this scalable, lightweight super-resolution system offers an accessible solution for on-farm applications and regional environmental monitoring.

title: Physiology-guided multi-objective machine learning for robust fructose prediction in Asian pear under interannual climate variability
abstract: Predicting Asian pear fructose concentration under interannual climate variability is challenging because sugar accumulation reflects cumulative interactions among developmental progression, environmental conditions, and prior metabolic state. Using a six-year repeated-measures field dataset from ‘Niitaka’ Asian pear trees, fructose concentration at N days after full bloom (DAFB) was predicted from meteorological and phenological descriptors aligned to each DAFB sampling window and sugar measurements from the preceding sampling point (N − 15 DAFB). We developed a physiology-guided machine learning framework using XGBoost as a fixed regressor and three feature-transformation components: a climate gate that weights precursor-history signals by stage-specific environmental conditions, a Richards growth kernel that constrains developmental trajectories, and lagged sugar features that represent metabolic continuity. Representation parameters were optimized under six-fold leave-one-year-out cross-validation using scalarized single-objective optimization or nondominated sorting genetic algorithm III (NSGA-III), targeting the mean, maximum, and standard deviation of yearwise root mean square error (RMSE). The selected multi-objective model achieved a pooled RMSE of 35.48 mg·g −1 dry weight (DW), compared with 55.53 mg·g −1 DW for the climate–phenology baseline, reducing pooled error by 36.1% and interannual variability by 70.4%. Pareto front analysis revealed an accuracy–robustness trade-off and supported the selection of an operationally balanced solution for reliable fruit-quality prediction.

title: Single-view RGB-D cattle body measurement with visibility-aware 3D pose completion and parametric body reconstruction
abstract: Single-view RGB-D reconstruction provides a practical approach to cattle body measurement. However, a side-view camera observes only one side of the body, and its depth map often contains gaps around the limbs, abdomen, and hindquarter. Completed 3D pose was used to link the partial RGB-D observation with parametric body reconstruction. Body masks and anatomical landmarks were extracted from the RGB image, while valid depth values provided metric observations. The gradient-field pose model GFPose-Cow then estimated the missing 3D landmarks using a visibility-aware graph score network trained with synthetic masking based on lateral-view geometry. The completed pose provided anatomical anchors for PoseScaffold-SMAL fitting together with silhouette, depth, visible-surface, and dorsal-profile constraints. The fitted model was converted to a canonical standing pose for body-trait extraction. Under the synthetic missing-keypoint protocols, GFPose-Cow obtained lower missing-only mean per-joint position error than the fully connected score reference. On 102 real-cattle 3D pose samples inferred from a public multi-view RGB-D dataset, GFPose-Cow achieved an MPJPE of 36.21 mm. Across 25 cattle, the final PoseScaffold-SMAL stage achieved a silhouette intersection-over-union of 0.8982 ± 0.0059 and visible-surface and rendered-depth fitting discrepancies of 38.71 ± 4.00 and 17.63 ± 2.88 mm, respectively. Manual-measurement validation included 102 cattle in the external reference and 25 cattle in the study-specific reference. On the external reference, mean absolute errors ranged from 2.23 to 6.61 cm and mean absolute percentage errors ranged from 2.72% to 5.88% across the reported body traits. These results indicate that completed 3D pose improves single-view RGB-D cattle reconstruction and supports fixed-topology body measurement.

title: SADR-VSS: A Scene-Adaptive Dynamic Routing Visual State Space Block for lightweight agricultural object detection
abstract: Precision agriculture requires accurate and efficient visual perception under complex field conditions. However, agricultural images often suffer from illumination variations, high inter-class similarity, scale diversity, and severe occlusion, making it challenging for lightweight detectors to achieve strong representation capability while maintaining real-time inference efficiency. To address this issue, this paper proposes a Scene-Adaptive Dynamic Routing Visual State Space Block (SADR-VSS) integrated into the YOLO11 framework for lightweight agricultural object detection. The proposed SADR-VSS introduces a multi-cue scene-adaptive routing mechanism that jointly considers global complexity, local variation, edge information, and contrast characteristics to dynamically adjust the contributions of a lightweight convolutional branch and a visual state space model (VSS) branch. By adaptively balancing local texture extraction and long-range dependency modeling according to scene conditions, SADR-VSS improves feature representation capability under heterogeneous agricultural environments while maintaining computational efficiency. Furthermore, comprehensive experiments are conducted to investigate the effects of routing strategies and insertion locations, demonstrating that the proposed deeper-stage integration provides an effective accuracy–efficiency trade-off. Experiments on a self-constructed agricultural dataset containing four crop categories, including maize, industrial hemp, pepper, and tomato, show that SADR-VSS achieves a mAP50-95 of 0.8076 with only 6.39 GFLOPs, improving detection accuracy over the YOLOv11n baseline with comparable computational complexity. In addition, TensorRT optimization on the NVIDIA Jetson Orin NX edge platform enables real-time inference at 77.27 FPS, demonstrating the practical deployment potential of SADR-VSS for intelligent agricultural vision systems.

title: Row-alignment navigation and path tracking for a cotton-field residual-film recovery machine using cotton-stalk sensing and geomagnetic-aided inertial navigation
abstract: Self-propelled residual-film recovery machines in cotton fields rely on non-contact perception that fails in airborne dust. These machines also face irregular cotton rows and sluggish hydraulic rear-wheel steering. This study developed a row-alignment navigation system for a rear-wheel-steering residual-film recovery machine by combining contact-based cotton-stalk sensing with geomagnetic-aided inertial navigation. A sensing unit with crossed contact rods measured the swing angles of the contact rods. These angles were combined with the heading angle from the geomagnetic-aided inertial navigation unit in a geometric model that resolved the lateral deviation between the machine and the cotton rows. Simplifying the four-wheel chassis to a two-wheel model yielded a pure-pursuit steering-angle model and a correction formula for the desired right-rear-wheel angle. Using the measured right-rear-wheel angle as feedback, a closed-loop control model combined fuzzy PID control with hydraulic steering dead-zone compensation. It converted the desired angle into electric steering wheel commands for real-time correction. Field tests from 2 to 10 km/h gave a steady-state mean lateral deviation below 1 cm and heading deviation below 1°. Transient lateral deviation remained within ± 7 cm, and 94.8% of observations between 8 and 10 km/h stayed within ± 5 cm. The system therefore met the required ± 5 cm lateral and ± 2° heading accuracy. The method offers a reference for row-alignment navigation in hard-stalk crops under dusty conditions.

title: Asymmetric semi-supervised domain adaptation framework for multi-sensor alfalfa protein prediction via coupled crop and radiative transfer models
Machine Learning-Assisted design and optimization of Fin Ray Effect flexible grippers for lychee harvesting
abstract: The harvesting end effector plays a crucial role in agricultural robots. However, the initial design and configuration optimization have traditionally lacked intelligent methods. To address this issue, this study proposes an Artificial Intelligence (AI) enhanced design and optimization method to develop a novel Gripping-and-Shearing Separation Type Lychee Harvesting End Effector (GS-STLHEE). A case study designs a flexible gripper and uses numerical models to build training and testing datasets for configuration design and optimization. The nonlinear relationships between these parameters and characteristics are predicted by surrogate models, including Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN), Back-propagation Artificial Neural Networks (BPANN), and Support Vector Machines (SVM). The Bayesian Optimization (BO) technique is then employed to fine-tune the hyperparameters of the AI-learning models. The aforementioned data-driven optimization functions and constraints are integrated with the Non-Dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm II (NSGA-II) to identify Pareto-optimal solutions. Configuration parameters such as supporting beam thickness, incline angle, and spacing distance are optimized, and reaction force and gripper mass are enhanced. The results indicate the CNN model demonstrates superior learning ability, with the advancement of higher prediction accuracy, when handling complicated datasets. The optimization flexible gripper demonstrates larger reaction force and lighter mass, with an improvement rate of around 50 %.

title: Vision-guided row-aligned spraying system for soybean seedlings using an improved YOLO11s-seg model
abstract: Accurate alignment between spray bands and crop rows is a key requirement for canopy-directed band spraying in soybean fields. This study developed a vision-guided row-aligned spraying system intended for the banded application of products for foliar disease management or foliar fertilizers to soybean canopies. The system integrates instance segmentation, crop-row extraction, and lateral row-following control. First, an EC-YOLO11s-seg instance segmentation model was constructed based on YOLO11s-seg. The C3K2_EMBC module, CAFM (Convolution and Attention Fusion Module) attention mechanism, Shape-IoU loss, and EMASlideLoss were introduced. These components improved the model’s ability to learn multi-scale soybean seedling features, complex boundaries, and hard-to-classify samples. Second, a crop-row extraction method was developed based on instance segmentation masks. This method combines Monte Carlo sampling, inverse perspective mapping, DBSCAN (Density-Based Spatial Clustering of Applications with Noise) clustering, and least-squares fitting. It enables stable estimation of the spatial position and direction of soybean crop rows. Finally, the vision recognition algorithm, closed-loop lateral adjustment mechanism, and band spraying device were integrated into an electric self-propelled boom sprayer. Field experiments using clean water were conducted to evaluate row-alignment accuracy. The results showed that EC-YOLO11s-seg achieved P m a s k , R m a s k , and m A P 50 m a s k values of 88.96 %, 89.72 %, and 92.61 %, respectively, on a self-built cross-year soybean seedling field dataset. These values were 5.42, 5.58, and 5.20 percentage points higher than those of the baseline YOLO11s-seg model. The average inference speed was 62.82 FPS, indicating good offline inference efficiency. For crop-row extraction, the mean relative distance error, mean relative endpoint error, and mean angle error were 3.69 %, 5.18 %, and 1.43°, respectively. The mean fitting accuracy for row angle reached 0.9065. These results demonstrate good row localization accuracy and directional consistency. Field row-aligned spraying tests showed that the system maintained good row-following performance at operating speeds of 2–5 km/h. The mean lateral deviation ranged from 8.93 to 23.75 mm. The proportion of samples with a lateral deviation less than 10 % of the row spacing remained above 85.0 %. At 2–4 km/h, this proportion was not lower than 92.5 %. These results indicate that the proposed system has good perception accuracy, row-alignment capability, and operational stability under complex field conditions. It can support banded row-aligned spraying and reduce off-row application of foliar liquids in soybean fields at the seedling stage.

title: Mango-SparseInst: A two-stage framework for instance segmentation and picking point localization in automated mango harvesting
abstract: Automated mango harvesting requires robust visual perception to simultaneously segment occluded fruits and slender main branches, and to localize executable picking points. This study proposes a two-stage framework integrating an enhanced instance segmentation model, Mango-SparseInst, and a Full-Path Energy Activation (FPEA) algorithm. To address geometric heterogeneity and severe occlusion in orchards, Mango-SparseInst incorporates three tailored modules: Deform-CA for adapting to irregular morphologies, SK-Conv for dynamically adjusting receptive fields across contrasting target scales, and Light-BiFPN for balanced multi-scale feature fusion. Evaluated on the Mango-1300 dataset, the model achieved 87.0% AP@[50:95] for fruits and 47.1% for main branches, with an overall mAP@[50:95] of 67.1% and mAP@50 of 91.5%, yielding gains of 4.9 and 9.7 percentage points for the respective categories over the baseline. Operating on the generated masks, FPEA localized optimal picking points by minimizing a multi-factor energy function encoding branch topology and geometric constraints, without requiring additional training. On 171 main-branch instances, FPEA attained an 87.1% success rate, representing an 8.8 percentage-point gain over conventional curvature smoothing. Furthermore, cross-dataset validation on litchi demonstrated the transferability of the localization strategy, while TensorRT FP16 deployment on a Jetson Orin Nano confirmed its feasibility for resource-constrained agricultural platforms. This framework establishes a reliable pixel-to-coordinate pipeline, providing a practical basis for vision-guided harvesting robots.

title: Spatially-aware consensus-based bundling for event-triggered multi-harvester row allocation
abstract: Assigning crop rows to several harvesters requires accounting for row lengths, machine speeds, and changes during the mission. We present an event-triggered allocator that combines consensus-inspired bundling with nearest-row filtering, proximity admission, and speed-aware balancing that also works inside a fragmented radio network. On 100-row fields we compare executed allocations with a centralized fixed-sweep dynamic program, a static speed split, and textbook CBBA. With full connectivity the method is within 6.2% of the dynamic program, and its makespan is within 1% of textbook CBBA while it needs about 3 consensus rounds instead of 36 to 51 and keeps each machine on a contiguous block. After failures, joins, and speed changes, frozen plans leave up to 20% of rows unharvested, whereas the method completes every row. With only local information, heartbeat failure detection, and a 50 m radio range, it recovers no more than 2.2% slower than a base-station coordinator and within 6% of an oracle with global state, without needing the base station. Packet loss of up to 30% changes its completion time by less than 1%, and 1 s of latency per hop by at most 2.3%. Straight-line deadhead is 2.6% to 3.1% of travel, and a 30 m turn allowance per row transition raises nonproductive travel to 14.8%. The results come from simulation with simplified vehicle motion; field validation remains future work.

title: Gas characterization pattern-guided adaptive modeling algorithm: Method and mechanism for non-destructive detection of silage quality using a colorimetric sensor array
Text-to-video multi-moment retrieval via adaptive virtual token alignment for pig behavior analysis in surveillance videos
abstract: Video-based pig behavior analysis is important for animal welfare assessment, abnormal behavior monitoring, and precision livestock management. However, most existing methods rely on predefined behavior categories and produce closed-set recognition results, making it difficult to retrieve concrete behavioral evidence according to flexible farm-management needs. Text-video multi-moment retrieval offers a promising solution by enabling users to query specific behavioral evidence from surveillance videos using natural language, supporting more flexible and fine-grained farm-management workflows. To the best of our knowledge, text-video multi-moment retrieval has not previously been investigated for pig-house surveillance videos. To fill this gap, we construct Pig-MMR, a real-farm, expert-reviewed multi-moment benchmark for pig behavior retrieval, containing 397 videos, 644 query instances, 221 unique queries, and 970 annotated behavior moments. This task faces two main challenges: noisy cross-modal alignment between sparse textual queries and complex pig-house videos, and discontinuous pig behaviors with large temporal-scale variation. To address these challenges, we propose Pig Behavior Description-driven Moment Retrieval (PigBDMR), a text-video multi-moment retrieval framework. Specifically, adaptive cross-attention with learnable virtual tokens is introduced to reduce noisy cross-modal alignment, multi-scale temporal modeling to handle variable-duration behaviors, and a training-stage post-verification module to improve multi-moment retrieval consistency. Experimental results show that PigBDMR achieves 35.64 G-mAP and 50.81 mIoU@1, outperforming the strongest baseline FlashMMR by 3.46 and 5.37 percentage points, respectively. Under the same pre-extracted feature setting, PigBDMR reduces model-level inference time from 20.5 ms to 9.9 ms. These results demonstrate the potential of PigBDMR for efficient text-driven behavioral evidence retrieval in pig-house surveillance videos. The code is available at: https://github.com/Kevinyang2/PigBDMR.

title: Hyperspectral olive maturity estimation model for table olives: A non-invasive proof-of-concept study
abstract: The economic significance of olive cultivation and trade is paramount for Mediterranean countries, yielding a substantial impact on their respective local economies. However, the quality of olives is significantly influenced by the harvest timing, which occurs when they reach optimal size and maturity stage. Conventionally, farmers have relied on empirical observation to determine the optimal harvest date, guided by their accumulated expertise and knowledge. While this approach is well-founded, it lacks the rigor and objectivity offered by data-driven methods. The development of an automatic system for determining olive maturity is a significant concern for the industry. This study proposes an artificial intelligence-based system for estimating the maturity of table olives using a novel technological approach. The method involves the identification of olive maturity stages through field methods that utilize proximal hyperspectral imaging technology. A comprehensive analysis was conducted to elucidate the importance of each spectral band and to assess the model’s performance with a reduced feature space. In this proof-of-concept study, a Hyperspectral Olive Maturity Estimation Model (HOMEM) was developed to estimate olives’ maturity by determining their Maturity Index. The model employed visible and near-infrared spectral signatures acquired through in-field hyperspectral imaging. The present study explores the precision of HOMEM and the impact of normalization with hyperspectral images employing various AI-based models. The proposed HOMEM model attained an R2 value of 93 % in its estimation of the Maturity Index through the utilization of visible and near-infrared wavelengths. The results of this study demonstrate the potential of hyperspectral imaging and machine learning techniques to enhance the assessment of olive quality and reduce reliance on traditional, experience-based methods.

title: A low-stress and accurate method for dead chicken detection in commercial caged poultry houses without supplemental lighting
Research on the strawberry picking point localization algorithm based on dual-stage lightweight networks
Lightweight autonomous construction and application of a knowledge graph for soil acidification constraint management based on LLM agents
abstract: In the red and yellow soil regions of southern China, long-term practices in soil acidification constraint management have revealed several challenges, including fragmented knowledge systems, high technical thresholds, and pronounced regional disparities in technical capacity, which collectively hinder the systematic integration and dissemination of management experience. To address these limitations, this study proposes a lightweight autonomous construction framework for a knowledge graph of soil acidification management based on large language model (LLM) agents. By introducing an "AI associative matrix" and a semantic expansion-retrieval mechanism, the framework enables the system to automatically infer related concepts and relationships from a small set of domain-specific keywords, thereby generating an initial ontology structure and knowledge graph schema for management tasks. In addition, a network protocol-based control strategy is incorporated to semantically parse publicly available governmental reports and monitoring data, facilitating automated processes such as entity recognition and relation extraction. At the system implementation level, a cloud-edge collaborative lightweight architecture is adopted to reduce computational requirements and improve usability. Through an empirical in-situ deployment and lightweight field-level testing conducted directly at the farm sites of Chengmai County, Hainan Province, this framework demonstrated a robust capacity to adapt to users with different technical backgrounds and regions with varying levels of resource input, while providing extensibility for the continuous integration of emerging technologies and updated policy regulations. Overall, this study offers a lightweight, user-friendly, and scalable intelligent approach for cultivated land quality improvement and agricultural ecological management.

title: MPRT-DETR: multi-platform real-time rice panicle detection and counting based on the transformer method and complex field imagery
abstract: Automatic and accurate detection and counting of rice panicles provide an important phenotypic basis for high-throughput rice monitoring and yield-related trait assessment. However, the accuracy and robustness of existing methods are often compromised by the challenges inherent to complex field conditions. These challenges include scale variations across multi-platform imagery (proximal vs. UAV), morphological diversity across cultivars and growth stages, and environmental effects such as uneven illumination and dense canopy occlusion. To overcome these hurdles, we constructed a comprehensive, multi-platform RGB image dataset that captures the period from heading to maturity for multiple cultivars, and encompasses a broad range of phenotypic variations and environmental conditions representative of real-world agricultural settings. In addition, we propose the Multi-Platform Real-Time Rice Panicle Detection and Counting Transformer (MPRT-DETR) for rice panicle detection and counting under complex field conditions. The proposed MPRT-DETR is developed as a task-oriented adaptation of RT-DETR for complex field rice panicle detection and incorporates four coordinated modifications: (1) an FEM that extends an illumination-adaptive enhancement framework by integrating WTConv and training-time label enhancement; (2) a FasterNet-based feature extraction network augmented with EMA; (3) an LBFM that reorganizes multi-scale aggregation through bidirectional feature fusion and lightweight DySample and ADown operators; and (4) a lightweight QEH designed in this study for quantity-aware adaptive query-capacity allocation. Comprehensive evaluations show that, compared with the baseline RT-DETR, MPRT-DETR reduces the parameter count by 22.30 % and GFLOPs by 32.50 %, while mAP50 and mAP50–95 increase by 11.52 and 16.43 percentage points, respectively. For panicle counting, the model achieves a coefficient of determination (R2) of 0.9453, a Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) of 16.2, and a relative Root Mean Square Error (rRMSE) of 14.43 % on the primary test set. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of MPRT-DETR for rice panicle detection and counting under diverse field imaging conditions. Overall, MPRT-DETR provides an efficient approach for image-based rice panicle phenotyping and may serve as an upstream component for future plot-level yield-related trait assessment and breeding applications. Our code and pre-trained models are available at https://github.com/Agricultural-DL/MPRT-DETR.

title: HFSR-net: heterogeneous feature semantic refinement network for UAV-based diseased pine tree detection
abstract: Timely detection of diseased pine trees is crucial for preventing the spread of forest pests and diseases. UAV-based remote sensing enables efficient large-area inspection, but interference from complex forest backgrounds remains a major challenge. In UAV imagery, symptomatic crown regions often share visual characteristics with the forest floor, canopy shadows, and overexposed healthy vegetation, causing semantic interference and false detections. Moreover, visible disease features during early infection occupy only a limited number of pixels and can be attenuated or overwhelmed during deep feature extraction, increasing the risk of missed detections. Existing public datasets also contain limited and unevenly distributed small-scale diseased pine tree instances, restricting effective model training and evaluation, particularly for small targets. To address these issues, we propose a Heterogeneous Feature Semantic Refinement Network (HFSR-Net). First, a Heterogeneous Semantic Rectification (HSR) mechanism integrates fine-grained local textures with long-range context from the broader forest scene and adaptively rectifies feature responses, thereby enhancing feature discriminability and suppressing erroneous responses caused by background interference. Second, a Local Representation Enhancement Block (LREBlock) strengthens shallow local representations, preserves subtle disease features, and improves the representation of diseased pine trees across scales. Third, we construct a Small-Object Diseased Pine (SODP) dataset, in which small-object instances account for 57.1% of all instances and are more evenly distributed across images. Experiments on SODP, two public diseased pine tree detection datasets, and a general remote sensing object detection dataset demonstrate that HFSR-Net effectively suppresses complex background interference and outperforms mainstream methods in detection accuracy and broader applicability.

title: IoT irrigation and multimodal phenotyping with CRITIC-based weighting: a monitoring and evaluation framework for moisture stress assessment in tomato
abstract: Conventional irrigation scheduling for tomato genotype evaluation lacks real-time soil–plant feedback. This study deployed an IoT-enabled automated drip irrigation system combined with multimodal phenotyping to assess genotype-specific water productivity under contrasting irrigation regimes. Four tomato genotypes were evaluated under two irrigation regimes, 100% FC and 50% FC during the Rabi season in subtropical India. The soil moisture sensors coupled with LoRaWAN-controlled solenoid valves enabled threshold-based automated irrigation, while an electromagnetic flow meter quantified water delivered per genotype. Sensor-controlled irrigation achieved 12% water savings over ETc-based scheduling under full irrigation; deficit irrigation reduced seasonal water application by 39% while preserving genotype-dependent productivity. Multimodal phenotyping encompassed thermal infrared imaging for canopy temperature-based stress detection and deep learning-driven RGB imaging for digital biomass estimation, validated against destructive measurements. Under deficit irrigation at fruiting stage the average canopy temperature increased by 1.97°C, digital biomass declined by 23.6%, and significant genotype × irrigation interactions confirmed differential stress resilience. These findings demonstrate the importance of genotype-specific responses in irrigation management under water-limited conditions. A multimodal integrated performance framework (MIPF) using CRiteria Importance Through Intercriteria Correlation (CRITIC)-based data-driven weights integrated thermal, RGB, and physiological traits into a unified genotype ranking index. Under deficit irrigation, cv. Arka Meghali ranked first for stress tolerance across all weighting scenarios, while cv. Arka Vikas recorded the highest water use efficiency (0.0108 kg L⁻1). This context-dependent divergence between superior stress resilience and maximum water use efficiency underscores the need for a multimodal genotype evaluation approach that aligns genotype selection with the target water management objective.

title: Enhancing pesticide-likeness prediction via multimodal deep learning ensemble framework
abstract: Pesticide-likeness prediction is a critical task in agrochemical research and design. However, existing methods are often constrained by negative sample selection bias and overreliance on supervised learning. To address these challenges, we propose RGG, a multimodal deep learning ensemble framework that integrates Recurrent Neural Network (RNN), Graph Convolutional Network (GCN), and Graph Convolutional Attention Network (GCAN) to synergistically capture molecular sequence patterns, topological features, and multimodal correlations. The positive samples were collected from the British Crop Production Council (BCPC) database, whereas the negative samples were selected from the ZINC20 database through Hao’s Rule prescreening and Butina clustering. The framework leverages a voting mechanism to harmonize the predictive strengths of heterogeneous models, thereby balancing classification robustness and generalization capability. Experimental results demonstrate that the RGG model outperformed all individual submodels on the validation sets of the 10-fold cross-validation. This improvement is reflected in a 5.33 % increase in average accuracy, along with gains of 5.05 % in precision and 5.46 % in recall. In independent testing, RGG exhibited potential for prioritizing novel bioactive molecules (AUC = 0.81). RGG generates continuous pesticide-likeness scores for candidate ranking, with a less polarized score distribution than the supervised submodels on the sampled molecules. Additional sensitivity analyses showed that the supervised model was robust to moderate changes in the clustering cutoff and benefited from diversity-oriented negative-sample selection. Furthermore, the framework supports multi-label functional categorization (fungicides, insecticides, herbicides) and enables interpretable predictions through attention mechanisms, highlighting molecular fragments associated with the model predictions. This work proposes a precision-oriented and interpretable methodology for pesticide-likeness prediction, advancing the application of deep learning in agrochemical molecular design. We also developed a web application to facilitate the use of our model: https://rgg.pianlab.team/jobs.

title: GNN-Bézier-RP: A joint path-planning method integrating graph neural networks and Bézier-curve obstacle avoidance for safflower picking with a parallel manipulator
abstract: To address irregular target distributions, local obstacle interference, and insufficient trajectory smoothness in safflower picking path planning, this study proposes a global–local integrated path-planning method for a Delta parallel manipulator. The method couples Graph Neural Network (GNN)-based global picking-order planning with Bézier-curve-based local obstacle-avoidance correction. During global planning, an improved GNN encoder models target–obstacle spatial relationships among mature safflower capitula, obstacle points, and the non-entry region, and a Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) decoder generates the picking visiting sequence. During local correction, cubic Bézier control-point optimization modifies trajectory segments with potential obstacle conflicts, and minimum-jerk smoothing improves motion continuity. Simulation results show that, under the Active Search strategy, the proposed GNN-LSTM model obtained normalized path lengths of 7.507, 11.711, and 15.857 for the 20-, 30-, and 40-point settings, respectively. After local obstacle-avoidance correction, the path-growth cost remained within 0.037–0.078. Laboratory validation further showed that the actual path lengths changed from 751.6 cm, 1178.6 cm, and 1585.9 cm to 784.23 cm, 1202.95 cm, and 1693.0 cm, respectively, while the total execution times decreased from 38.40 s, 54.36 s, and 74.16 s to 30.24 s, 47.52 s, and 58.60 s. The planned trajectory execution success rates were 91.67%, 88.89%, and 87.50%, respectively. These results demonstrate that the coupled GNN–Bézier strategy is effective for safflower picking under the tested simulation and laboratory conditions, improving local obstacle-avoidance feasibility, motion continuity, and trajectory execution efficiency.

title: HFDPNet: An RGB-D sweet pepper detection network for complex greenhouse environments
Reliability-aware RGB-D instance segmentation for field-based 3D phenotyping of maize ears and silks
Temporal 3D point cloud reconstruction of tomato seedlings using L-SuperPoint-LightGlue
abstract: 3D point cloud reconstruction is fundamental to high-throughput phenotypic monitoring of tomato seedlings. However, some existing multi-view plant imaging systems require seedlings to be transferred between separate cultivation and imaging areas for time-series data acquisition. In addition, as a traditional hand-crafted feature algorithm, SIFT exhibits limited responses in weak-texture regions, while FLANN is prone to mismatches in structurally similar plant regions, thereby limiting reconstruction accuracy. Furthermore, the lack of time-series 3D datasets constrains precise phenotypic analysis. To overcome these limitations, we developed a data acquisition platform integrating environmental control, automated irrigation, and multi-view imaging, and constructed a time-series multi-view image dataset for tomato seedlings. We proposed L-SuperPoint, a lightweight feature extraction network with a custom-designed keypoint attention block (LKABlock) that enhances structural feature responses. We combined it with LightGlue to improve matching accuracy. Compared with SIFT and the original SuperPoint, L-SuperPoint improved feature repeatability by 39.6 % and 13.6 %, reduced the mean localization error by 14.3 % and 3.6 %, and increased the nearest-neighbor mean average precision by 22.4 % and 8.1 %, respectively. At thresholds of 1, 3, and 5 pixels, its homography correctness increased by 39.4 %, 29.4 %, and 14.5 % compared with SIFT, and by 12.2 %, 6.0 %, and 4.4 % compared with the original SuperPoint, respectively. For feature matching, L-SuperPoint-LightGlue achieved an average of 825.53 inliers and an inlier ratio of 70.18 %. Compared with SIFT-FLANN and SuperPoint-LightGlue, the number of inliers increased by 46.41 % and 22.62 %, respectively, while the inlier ratio increased by 7.94 and 3.70 percentage points, respectively. Applied to two tomato varieties, reconstructed point clouds averaged 9.26 × 10⁶ and 9.12 × 10⁶ points, mean track lengths were 9.05 and 8.74, and mean reprojection errors were 0.79 and 0.86 pixels. Phenotypic parameters of plant height, canopy projection area, and plant volume were extracted, with plant height yielding a coefficient of determination (R2) of 0.994 and a root mean square error (RMSE) of 0.148 cm. The proposed method effectively overcomes key challenges in seedling 3D reconstruction, offering reliable support for dynamic growth monitoring and automated phenotypic analysis.

title: UAV remote sensing monitoring of tea heat-drought stress in complex tea garden environments
abstract: The monitoring of tea heat–drought stress (THS) via UAV remote sensing involves challenges such as complex plantation environments, strong variations in illumination and shadow, the small scale of the diseased spots, and weak spectral differences between THS spots and healthy areas. To address these issues, this study proposes a UAV remote sensing monitoring method for THS in complex tea plantation environments. A scheme called Multispectral Tea Heat-Drought Stress Detection Network (MS-THSNet) is designed, in which a dual-branch feature extraction backbone is employed to exploit the complementary advantages of different modalities in terms of capturing texture information and spectral characteristics. To further enhance the cross-modal feature integration, a Modality Interaction Transformer Module (MITM) and an Adaptive Multispectral Fusion Network structure (AMF-Net) are introduced. The MITM models the global dependency relationships among different spectral bands through a cross-spectral feature interaction mechanism, enabling complementary enhancement of multispectral features and alleviating the insufficient discriminative representation caused by uneven illumination, shadow, and the weak spectral differences of THS spots. The AMF-Net structure adaptively weights and integrates the fused features to emphasize spot-related characteristics while suppressing interference from complex backgrounds. MS-THSNet also includes a Context-Guided Attention Module (CGAM) to perform cross-channel and cross-spatial contextual attention modeling on the fused features, thereby improving the localization and recognition accuracy of THS spots at different scales. In addition, a lightweight small-object detection head is adopted to enhance the perception of tiny THS spots. Experimental results indicate that the proposed method achieves a precision of 86.4%, a recall of 80.5%, and a mean average precision (mAP) of 87.8%, significantly outperforming other state-of-the-art methods. Compared with mainstream multimodal detection methods, the proposed method has an mAP that is improved by more than 3.5%, with a 7% improvement over the baseline detection network, thus validating its effectiveness for UAV monitoring of THS in complex tea garden environments.

title: RGB–multispectral image registration and generative spectral reconstruction for UAV-based jujube orchard monitoring
Decentralized no-reentry access control for automated feeding in socially ranked livestock groups
abstract: Automated feeding in group-housed livestock must combine individualized ration delivery with reliable control of competition for a shared feeder. We develop and analyze a decentralized feeder-access controller for socially ranked groups in which an animal that enters the feeder is blocked from re-entry until the next session. The controller requires only observable feeder-entry events and does not rely on centralized scheduling, hierarchy estimation, or global state information. We model the feeder as a stochastic multi-agent access-control system with ration, capacity, and conflict constraints. Within the decentralized policy class considered, we show that the no-reentry rule is sufficient to make the desired operating regime absorbing and, under an autonomy requirement for unfed animals, unique. We then study transient performance by simulation as a function of interaction scope, responsiveness, and dominance advantage. Global interaction scope yields systematically faster convergence than local scope, and stronger reactivity and dominance accelerate convergence further. Across the tested range of group sizes, local scope is generally better summarized by concave power-type fits, whereas global scope is markedly flatter. Additional simulations show that removing the no-reentry rule sharply reduces feeder utilization and ration completion while increasing congestion and rank-level inequality. Within the model studied here, these results identify a simple and implementable control law for automated livestock feeders and provide a simulation framework for evaluating feeder-access policies in precision livestock systems, including digital-twin and robotic-farming applications.

title: Dual-channel fluorescence LiDAR system for the nondestructive 3D sensing of plant physiological status
Field validation of a strain-gauge sensing workflow for relative structural-response monitoring in a multi-tunnel greenhouse
abstract: Lightweight greenhouse structures are subjected to combined environmental actions, yet their actual structural behavior under field conditions remains insufficiently documented using synchronized sensor data. This study presents field validation of a strain-gauge monitoring workflow for relative structural response assessment in a full-scale multi-tunnel greenhouse. The monitoring campaign combined 20 Hz strain records with one-minute external climate variables. Because the gauges were not zeroed against a known unloaded reference condition, all strain histories were interpreted as relative variations referenced to the initial monitoring state. The workflow linked each strain record to the final gauge labels shown in the monitoring layout, performed signal-quality screening, synchronized strain and environmental records, and compared the gauges by structural family and position. The five-day validation retained 22 strain-gauge signals from pillar, horizontal-member, vertical-bar, and arch locations. The strongest associations were generally linked to internal temperature and solar radiation rather than to the wind-speed-squared proxy. A nocturnal wind-speed decrease under near-constant internal air temperature was retained as an event-specific illustration of localized vertical-bar response rather than as a general wind-load validation. These results show that strain-gauge monitoring can provide interpretable field evidence from working greenhouse structures if gauge location, baseline definition, and environmental coupling are treated explicitly. The proposed workflow provides a basis for longer-term monitoring campaigns and the future integration of greenhouse sensor data with structural modeling and decision-support tools.

title: Ai-driven autonomous laser-weeding robots for agriculture 5.0: A systematic review of perception, navigation, and closed-loop control systems
A novel grid-based canopy cover index for estimating FAPAR of maize canopy from UAV multispectral images
Assessing tree vigor in orchards using wood segmentation and depth-based flash simulation on side-view RGB images
abstract: Tree vigor is a fundamental trait for orchard management, yet traditional measurements like trunk circumference or biomass weighing are slow, tedious and often lack precision. This study introduces a high-throughput phenotyping method using side-view RGB imaging of leafless trees to estimate wood projected area in orchards. A dataset of 2,802 annotated image patches, covering a variety of species, tree training methods, camera geometries and lighting conditions, was built to train nnU-Net models to segment all foreground wood pixels. The background influence was minimized by simulating a flash effect on the images using depth maps estimated from available deep learning models. Estimation of pruned wood biomass in espalier orchards served as a use case for wood segmentation: difference in the wood projected surface area computed before and after pruning based on segmented images, was linearly correlated with field-measured pruned wood biomass. Results highlight flash simulation’s ability to produce a single model capable of segmenting images acquired under natural and controlled conditions with similar accuracy (F 1 -score ≈ 0.91). Standard RGB and RGB-Depth models generally performed worse, especially under natural light, due to confusion with the background and less efficient use of depth information, respectively. The projected surface area of pruned wood, obtained through segmentation, was then shown to be an accurate proxy for pruned wood biomass for espaliered apple trees (R 2 = 0.92) and, to a lesser extent, peach trees (R 2 = 0.61). This illustrates the value of RGB imaging and wood segmentation for assessing vigor and architectural traits in fruit trees.

title: GTWLSTM-Lag: A maize yield prediction framework integrating spatiotemporal autocorrelation
Study on a real-time seeding flow detection method and device based on the seed flow spiral discretisation mechanism
From visual perception to actionable information for autonomous harvesting robots: A review
abstract: Reliable harvesting requires visual information that remains useful for planning and execution. This review examines four complementary functions of harvesting robot perception: detection and segmentation (D), metric three-dimensional localization (L), pose and task-relevant geometry (P), and environment reconstruction (E). D identifies the target, L locates it in a metric coordinate frame, P supplies the geometry needed for approach and detachment, and E describes the surrounding scene and its spatial context. A complete harvesting process requires these functions to work together, although individual studies may cover only some of them. The review distinguishes complete-system evidence, harvesting-specific module evidence, and adjacent evidence, using reported configurations to show how these functions are combined. An actionability gate assesses target identity, coordinate consistency, task-relevant geometry, scene coverage, uncertainty, information age, and the downstream planning or control consumer. A three-level framework connects module performance with information retained across interfaces and with robot or field deployment. By making the perception-to-action pathway explicit, this review clarifies the visual information required at each decision interface, identifies evidence gaps, and provides an engineering basis for designing and evaluating deployable harvesting-robot systems.

title: Hierarchical deep reinforcement learning for dual-arm robotic pear blossom pollination in dense orchard environments
abstract: Pear blossoms are densely distributed and flower within a relatively short period, imposing stringent efficiency requirements on robotic pollination systems to complete multiple targets within a limited operational window. In unstructured pear orchards, irregular blossom distributions and overlapping reachable workspaces of the two manipulators tightly couple target allocation, workload coordination, shared-workspace conflict avoidance, and continuous motion control, making dual-arm pollination inherently a hierarchical decision-making problem. To address these coupled challenges, this study proposes a hierarchical deep reinforcement learning framework for dual-arm robotic pollination in dense pear blossom environments. At the high level, a Transformer-JointQ scheduler models the interactions between candidate pear blossom targets and dual-arm states and evaluates feasible target combinations through joint state–action values, thereby enabling coordinated target selection for both manipulators under dense-target conditions. At the low level, PCCS-MATD3 dynamically adjusts control preferences while incorporating temporal smoothness and dual-arm coordination constraints into policy optimization, improving motion stability and coordination during continuous execution. Simulation experiments show that Transformer-JointQ achieves task completion rates of 99.5%, 98.5%, and 99.0% for scenarios containing 6, 10, and 15 target pear blossoms, respectively, while maintaining high workload balance; meanwhile, PCCS-MATD3 achieves a 99% task completion rate in low-level evaluations and improves motion smoothness and dual-arm coordination without compromising execution efficiency. Field experiments in a real pear orchard further validate the feasibility of the proposed framework under natural illumination, irregular blossom distributions, occlusions, and environmental disturbances. Overall, the proposed framework provides an effective hierarchical decision-making approach for coordinated autonomous dual-arm pollination in dense pear blossom environments.

title: Real-time in-water fish biomass estimation from stereo bounding-box geometry without dense depth maps
abstract: In biomass estimation of in-water fish, a primary challenge is accurately estimating depth to reconstruct the physical dimensions of detected specimens. Conventional stereo methods struggle in underwater environments due to light reflections, homogeneous backgrounds, and optical artifacts, often failing to produce reliable disparity maps. This study presents StereoGeoBox, a practical alternative that estimates depth solely from the geometric correspondence of stereo bounding boxes detected by YOLO11. This eliminates the need to compute a full dense depth map, and the resulting physical dimensions are used as inputs to an XGBoost model for real-time fish weight estimation. We validate our approach using a newly collected longitudinal dataset of in-water tilapia spanning four growth stages (2, 3, 6, and 15 months) over a 15-month period, captured with both ZED X and FD stereo cameras, with ground-truth width, length, and weight obtained via manual measurement. Extensive experiments demonstrate that StereoGeoBox achieves the lowest or near-lowest MAD and MPAE values for fish length, width, and weight across most evaluated datasets compared with conventional stereo vision and learning-based depth estimation methods, while generating substantially fewer outliers. The method also maintains reasonable estimation accuracy under challenging aquaculture conditions, including illumination variations, oxygen bubbles, and turbidity. On a Jetson Thor platform with an FD camera, StereoGeoBox achieves 25.40 FPS at 28.2 ms latency with just 17.7 MB of GPU memory, demonstrating substantially higher computational efficiency than the evaluated full depth-map approaches. The complete system — integrating underwater stereo vision, edge computing, and a cloud-based monitoring dashboard — enables practical remote monitoring of fish growth, supporting more efficient aquaculture management.

title: Rotary tiller blades for wet cohesive soil: Performance prediction and multi-objective optimisation with SPO–BO–BPNN
Robust trajectory tracking control of autonomous tractors under complex farmland disturbances based on tube MPC and dual-channel ESO compensation
A data-knowledge hybrid-driven method for forest dead fine fuel moisture content prediction
Structure over sound: A free box count out-predicts in-hive acoustics for honey-bee colony strength
abstract: In-hive microphones are widely promoted for non-invasive estimation of honey-bee colony strength (frames of bees), and benchmarks report near-perfect accuracy. Whether that accuracy survives on unseen colonies and apiaries decides deployability. We re-analysed two open multi-sensor datasets, UrBAN (ten urban colonies) and MSPB (53 rural colonies at two apiaries), harmonised to a shared 20-feature acoustic space with in-hive temperature and humidity. Random forests and hierarchical mixed models were evaluated under progressively stricter validation, from random k -fold to leave-one-apiary-out and cross-dataset transfer, with the acoustic, environmental and structural contributions separated by ablation. Most of the reported skill is not acoustic. Under leave-one-apiary-out validation the acoustic features alone reach R 2 = 0.17 , in-hive temperature and humidity alone 0.56, and the beekeeper’s box count alone 0.71; the box count from the previous visit, fixed before the label existed, still reaches 0.42 alone and 0.55 with climate. Adding acoustics never improved accuracy materially under any configuration tested ( Δ R 2 between −0.12 and ＋0.02). The box count’s 90% conformal intervals keep near-nominal empirical coverage across apiaries, while those of the sensor model cover 70% of cases in one transfer direction and 99% in the other. In an exploratory cross-dataset comparison, limited by a 17-assessment audio-matched UrBAN sample, the box count transferred in both directions and the acoustic features in neither. A plausible reason is sensing geometry: the microphone sits in the bottom brood box, which barely varies, while almost all population variation is above it. The box count mixes physical capacity with management decisions. It is therefore a diagnostic baseline and not a measurement instrument, and the finding is that a single bottom-box microphone adds nothing to it, though acoustics retain value for other targets. The conclusion rests on the within-MSPB cross-apiary comparison and is limited to a single bottom-box microphone, the shared feature space and the frames-of-bees target.

title: Dynamic real-time detection of maize ear dehusking clearance rate based on deep learning and multi-object tracking
abstract: Real-time assessment of maize-ear dehusking clearance rate is important for monitoring harvesting quality, but dynamic harvesting conditions can cause missed detections, false positives, and duplicate counting due to background interference, target-scale variation, motion blur, and severe occlusion. This study presents a real-time dehusking-clearance-rate monitoring framework integrating object detection, multi-object tracking, and identity-based duplicate-aware counting. An improved You Only Look Once version 11 nano (YOLOv11n) detector, termed PPSE-YOLO, was constructed by incorporating a Partial Frequency Dynamic Convolution-based C3k2 module (PFD_C3k2), the Pyramid Sparse Transformer (PST), and a Separated and Enhancement Attention Module (SEAMHead). PFD_C3k2 improves frequency- and texture-related feature representation under background interference and motion blur, PST enhances selective multi-scale feature fusion for maize ears with different apparent sizes, and SEAMHead strengthens the representation of visible features under partial occlusion. BoT-SORT maintains target identities across consecutive frames, and the resulting trajectories are converted into unique counting events for continuous dehusking-clearance-rate estimation. PPSE-YOLO achieved a Precision of 92.7%, a Recall of 91.8%, and an mAP@0.5 of 95.5%, representing improvements of 2.4, 0.9, and 1.5 percentage points, respectively, over YOLOv11n. Meanwhile, its computational complexity and parameter count were reduced from 6.3 to 5.1 GFLOPs and from 2.58 to 2.28 M, respectively. BoT-SORT achieved an MOTA of 92.05% and an IDF1 of 89.87%. At the system level, the framework achieved an overall counting consistency of 97.67%, a mean absolute dehusking-clearance-rate estimation error of 2.02 percentage points across 10 test groups, and an average end-to-end processing speed of 34 FPS. These results indicate the feasibility of the framework for real-time maize dehusking monitoring under the tested harvesting conditions.

title: Spatially optimized chlorophyll fluorescence imaging for early detection of soft rot in Napa cabbage
FluxMate: An off-grid, cost-effective and dual-mode automated chamber system to monitor carbon dioxide fluxes in grassland ecosystems
abstract: Measuring greenhouse gas (GHG) fluxes in an ecosystem is essential to assess their contribution to global warming. Automated chamber systems can capture high-frequency data to estimate GHG fluxes. An automated dual-mode stand-alone chamber system was developed to measure carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) fluxes in agricultural ecosystems. The array mode consists of several chambers connected via tubing to a research-grade analyser, whereas the independent chamber mode consists of low-cost sensors inside each chamber. Both modes calculate fluxes, measure environmental conditions, and record images of the vegetation inside the chambers to calculate vegetation indices. The low-cost sensors showed a reliable estimation of CO 2 concentration against a research-grade gas analyser (MAPE < 22.1%, RMSE < 25 ppm, CCC > 0.96) and CO 2 fluxes (CCC = 0.97, R 2 > 0.94, with an average RMSE of 4.04 and MAE of 2.48 kg CO 2 ha hr -1 ). Furthermore, CO 2 fluxes followed diurnal patterns similar to the research-grade analyser, with CO 2 uptake during the daytime and release during nighttime. On average, CO 2 fluxes from the sensors underestimated fluxes by 10.7% compared to the research-grade analyser, with minimal systematic linear deviation from the 1:1 line (C.b > 0.99) and 95% of the error being random. Overall, the independent automated chamber system introduced in this study can measure CO 2 fluxes at a lower cost and with a more flexible approach compared to the research-grade analyser because individual chambers do not need to be connected to an analyser. Independently, low-cost chamber systems could allow scaling up measurements and replications of fluxes in agricultural systems.

title: MCAFNet: A multimodal audio-visual cross-attention fusion network for on-the-branch durian (Durio zibethinus L.) fruit maturity assessment
abstract: Accurate on-the-branch durian maturity assessment is essential for determining appropriate harvest timing, yet conventional experience-based evaluation is operator-dependent, and existing automated approaches have limited applicability in complex orchard environments. This study proposes a Multimodal Cross-Attention Fusion Network (MCAFNet) that integrates fruit images, stem images, and fruit-knocking acoustic signals for in-field durian maturity classification. An improved lightweight detector, SG-YOLO, extracts fruit and stem regions, while Mel spectrogram, mel-frequency cepstral coefficient (MFCC), and Chroma representations are stacked into a three-channel acoustic feature map. A Transformer-based cross-attention module subsequently fuses modality-specific features to exploit complementary maturity information. Under five-fold cross-validation, MCAFNet achieved an accuracy of 86.27 % ± 2.32 % and a macro_F1-score of 85.63 % ± 2.55 %, outperforming all 11 evaluated alternative multimodal fusion methods. Compared with the strongest competing method, FDFR-Net, accuracy and macro_F1-score increased by 2.15 and 2.22 percentage points, respectively. Moreover, integrating extracted fruit and stem regions with acoustic information improved accuracy by 6.07 percentage points and macro_F1-score by 5.48 percentage points relative to a full-image-plus-audio strategy. Ablation analyses indicated that fruit images provided the strongest discriminative information, while stem images and acoustic signals contributed complementary maturity cues. A user-oriented application was also developed to support practical assessment. These findings highlight the potential of region-focused visual-acoustic fusion for on-the-branch durian maturity classification and provide a foundation for intelligent harvesting systems.

title: Active disturbance control system and optimized algorithm for rotational-speed stability using a developed horticulture electric direct-drive rotary tiller
Predicting and mapping stem water potential in walnut orchards using machine learning, geostatistics, and spatial validation
abstract: Midday stem water potential (SWP) is a widely used indicator of orchard water status, but pressure-chamber measurements are labor intensive and spatially sparse. This study evaluated machine-learning and spatial-statistical approaches using repeated measurements from 30 trees at 10 monitoring sites during 2019–2021. Random Forest (RF), XGBoost, Gaussian Process Regression (GPR), Support Vector Regression (SVR), and a stacked ensemble used ETo, vapor pressure deficit (VPD), air temperature, soil temperature, solar radiation, wind speed, Easting, and Northing as predictors. Strict leave-one-site-out (Site-LOSO) validation was the primary test of transfer to an unmonitored site. RF had the highest pooled Site-LOSO point estimate (R 2 = 0.41, RMSE = 0.21 MPa, MAE = 0.16 MPa), followed by the ensemble (R 2 = 0.38, RMSE = 0.22 MPa) and XGBoost (R 2 = 0.37, RMSE = 0.22 MPa). Same-date field-assisted inverse-distance weighting achieved R 2 = 0.39 and RMSE = 0.22 MPa. RF reproduced monitored-network date means well (R 2 = 0.97; RMSE = 0.03 MPa) but not within-date spatial anomalies at withheld sites (R 2 = − 0.12; r = 0.09), and leave-one-year-out transfer was weak. The fitted models were applied over canopy pixels for 11 Ceres acquisition dates in 2020. All model maps were spatially smooth at the native grid, but their spatial patterns and within-map variation differed among algorithms and dates. Residual spatial dependence, heterogeneous tree-level performance, and mixed same-date checks indicate substantial uncertainty in fine-scale spatial transfer. The 0.5-m grid is a model-output support and not an independently validated SWP measurement resolution.

title: IoT-Enabled precision fertigation for Ngoc Linh ginseng house Cultivation: Hydraulic–Electronic Co-Design and Edge–Gateway validation
abstract: Ngoc Linh ginseng (Panax vietnamensis Ha et Grushv.) requires stable root-zone moisture, gentle nutrient delivery, and limited manual disturbance under shaded, humid cultivation. This study developed an Internet of Things (IoT)-enabled precision-fertigation platform integrating low-flow hydraulic delivery, protected electrical actuation, embedded sensing, LoRa Node–Gateway communication, and web supervision. The prototype served five racks, 15 rack–tier zones, 45 trays, and 180 pressure-compensated emitters from a 300-L nutrient tank. A local-practice sizing assumption of 0.6 L plant-equivalent⁻1 day⁻1 produced two 54-L events and a design flow of 216 L h⁻1. Across the validation dataset, mean emitter discharge was 1.21 L h⁻1, the emitter-discharge coefficient of variation (CVq) was 1.45 %, and low-quarter distribution uniformity (DU_lq) was 97.26 %. Electrical conductivity (EC) target deviation averaged 1.67 %, pH target deviation averaged 0.04, mean substrate-moisture gain was 8.5 %, and no oversaturation event was recorded. Packet delivery ratio (PDR) remained 97.42–100.00 %, and remote-control and rule-based fault-response success rates were 99.67–100.00 %. These results establish the engineering feasibility of a low-flow, rack-based, digitally supervised fertigation architecture. They do not establish agronomic efficacy for ginseng growth; longitudinal plant-health and quality trials remain necessary.

title: Selective harvesting apple quality assessment in modern orchards: Fruit surface defect detection and severity analysis
abstract: Apple surface defect detection is critical for maintaining fresh-market quality and minimizing economic losses across the supply chain. In commercial production, defect screening is typically performed at the postharvest stage, which increases labor and processing costs because large volumes of fruit must be transported, managed, and sorted. Selective harvesting provides an opportunity to reduce postharvest sorting burden based on visible quality cues. However, robust defect assessment in orchards remains challenging due to canopy clutter, variable illumination, and partial occlusion. This study proposed an image-based apple quality assessment pipeline for on-tree canopy images that integrates surface defect detection, prompt-guided fruit segmentation, and mask-constrained severity estimation to support selective fruit-level picking decisions. First, a YOLOv9 detector was applied to orchard images to localize and classify visible surface deficiencies, including diseases, insect injury, and sunburn. In parallel, a fruit segmentation module YOLOv8-SAM2 was deployed to produce instance masks of visible fruit surfaces. Defect severity was then quantified as a mask-constrained overlap ratio by intersecting defect predictions with fruit masks. A USDA-inspired selective harvesting strategy provided interpretable picking guidance (Fresh Market, Local Market, Processing, Skip, and Uncertain), while sunburn was considered separately for fresh-market selection. In experiments, YOLOv9t achieved a recall of 64.1 %, mAP50 of 67.5 %, mAP50-95 of 45.5 %, and F1 score of 65.0 % on the test set. The YOLOv8-SAM2 module achieved a mean mask IoU of 0.954 and Dice coefficient of 0.975. Manual validation of 76 defective fruit instances showed an MAE of 3.73 percentage points between estimated and reference visible defect coverage. End-to-end validation using predicted fruit masks resulted in an MAE of 3.89 percentage points and a severity-based recommendation agreement of 64.4 % among 73 successfully segmented fruits. The complete image-analysis workflow required 88.10 ms per image, corresponding to approximately 11.35 FPS on an RTX 4090 GPU. A web-based interface integrated the workflow and provided visual and text-based selective harvesting results. Overall, the proposed framework showed the potential to assess apple quality during harvesting and provide useful information for orchard managers and future robotic selective harvesting systems.

title: Image segmentation of sugarcane plants using u-net architecture and pre-trained deep learning models
abstract: Gap identification in the sugarcane ( Saccharum officinarum spp) is important because the uniformity of germination is highly correlated with yield. Field-scale spatial image segmentation using drone imagery to clearly distinguish sugarcane from other materials in the field facilitates a better understanding of gaps and the reasons behind their occurrence. This research reports on the use of this approach to investigate segmentation of sugarcane imagery using six pre-trained transfer learning models and a proposed U-Net model for this purpose. The pre-trained models selected for this study were VGG19, ResNet50, InceptionV3, InceptionResNetV2, MobileNetV2 and EfficientNetB7. Model performance metrics such as model accuracy, loss function, F1-score, Dice loss, IoU, and Jaccard loss were used to evaluate the models. The dataset used in this study was RGB imagery captured from a drone. Ground-truth data consisted of 317 masked images (full rows of sugarcane, incomplete rows of sugarcane, and no sugarcane) for training and validating the model. The resultant models were used to perform spatial image segmentation on a proof-of-concept area. Of the models evaluated, five achieved high levels of spatial image segmentation for sugarcane. From a resource constraint, the proposed U-Net model, VGG19, and InceptionV3 generated the most suitable models for sugarcane segmentation. VGG19 resulted in the best performance scores with accuracy 0.893 but was not substantially different from the proposed U-Net and InceptionV3 models. When processing time and available resources were taken into account, InceptionV3 was also found to be a suitable alternative. Therefore, we conclude that image segmentation of sugarcane plants using the VGG19 and InceptionV3 architectures is a suitable choice for this type of application. These algorithms enable clear visualization of the emerging sugarcane plants, allowing them to be distinguished from the other in the row and across the field. Ultimately, this will be of benefit for future research that can help sugarcane farmers plan and make prompt decisions about field activities to achieve sustainable sugarcane farming, including future studies to identify the causes of the gaps in sugarcane rows.

title: Editorial Board
A unified modeling framework for tree root characterization and scaling: Method in belowground ecology and evolution
abstract: Conventional ecological modeling and sampling frameworks frequently rely on a binary, isolated fine-root paradigm (e.g., a strict 2-mm diameter threshold) that treats fine roots as functionally homogeneous. This approach obscures the full structural aggregation patterns, emergent network complexity, and multi-scale scaling properties of root systems. To address these limitations, this study developed an irregular cylinder ( IC ) root model within a unified structural architecture framework. Tree root networks were modeled as hierarchical clusters of irregular cylinders governed by stable, long-axis orthographic 2D quadrilateral polygon shape constraints to facilitate systematic sampling, digital image processing, and cross-scale annotation. The framework was evaluated using empirical datasets compiled from Cunninghamia lanceolata across various forest developmental stages. The results demonstrate significant non-linear variations in size scaling ratios and scaling exponents, indicating a highly assembled branching architecture with pronounced structural redundancy rather than taproot dominance. Specifically, fine roots, absorptive roots, and second-order roots exhibited distinct shrinkage effects, with scaling exponents for total length, surface area, and volume decreasing sequentially as trait dimensionality increased. Maximum efficiency of nutrient absorption“ is inconsistent with the classic metabolic scaling model. Crucially, the established six-order diameter size classifier successfully reconciles conflicting traditional, functional, and order-based root definitions, serving as a reliable cross-scale operator. By integrating 3D phenotyping, recursive topological constraints, and functional scaling, this modeling framework provides a reproducible mechanism to bridge static structural traits with dynamic developmental processes. These advancements offer a rigorous foundation for refining belowground resource allocation parameterizations in dynamic terrestrial biosphere models (TBMs) under changing climate scenarios.

title: Explainability-guided transformer-based anomaly screening in agave crops
Registration-assisted adaptive RGB–infrared feature fusion for dairy cow hoof disease detection in rotary milking parlors
Non-contact backfat thickness prediction in finishing pigs via multimodal feature fusion for pig sorting systems
Forecasting drought across Canada using a hybrid machine learning approach: a national perspective for adaptations and early warning systems
abstract: Drought is a major natural hazard in Canada, with significant socio-economic impacts across the country’s diverse climatic and geographic regions. This study proposes a hybrid forecasting framework that combines fast adaptive empirical mode decomposition (FAEMD), an ensemble deep random vector functional link (edRVFL) network, and the energy valley optimizer (EVO) to model nonstationary hydrological time series. Using 74 years (1951–2024) of meteorological data from 24 Canadian meteorological stations, we first identified substantial spatial variability and nonstationary trends in historical drought conditions. The proposed FAEMD-edRVFL-EVO framework was then used to forecast the Standardized Precipitation Evapotranspiration Index (SPEI 12 ) at one-, two-, and three-month lead times and compared against standalone and hybrid implementations of extreme gradient boosting, random forest, and k -nearest neighbor algorithms. FAEMD-edRVFL-EVO consistently achieved the best performance, with median correlation coefficients of 0.999, 0.980, and 0.906 for one-, two-, and three-month forecasts, respectively. Performance remained strong in climatically complex regions, particularly in Western and Northern Canada. By effectively isolating nonstationary signals, this applied study demonstrates that the integrated pipeline provides a scalable, accurate, and computationally efficient practical solution for large-scale drought forecasting and early warning under increasing climatic uncertainty.

title: A robotic lotus pod picking method integrating key point detection and active viewpoint adjustment: experimental validation under controlled laboratory conditions
PRIM3: pod reconstruction and instance matching in 3D for lima bean pod counting and yield assessment
Estimating and Forecasting Grapevine Phenology using Deep Learning and Mechanistic models: A comparative study
abstract: Accurate monitoring of key phenological stages, such as bud-break, blooming, veraison, and berries ripe, is essential for optimizing vineyard management, especially in the context of climate change. Grapevine phenology, primarily driven by temperature, has been extensively studied with the most common prediction methods based on the growing-degree-days (GDD) approach. In this paper we propose and compare two novel methodologies, respectively based on a mechanistic and a deep learning approach, to detect and forecast key phenological stages. The mechanistic model simulates the effects of both air temperature and water availability on the major plant metabolic processes that drive the annual phenological cycle (vegetative and reproductive growth, and sugar accumulation in the berry), whereas the deep learning model, based on a Recurrent Neural Network, infers directly the phenological cycle taking as input the time series of the daily weather station measurements. Using seven years of phenological data collected from five grape varieties (‘Aglianico’, ‘Greco’ ‘Syrah’, ‘Touriga Franca’, and ‘Touriga Nacional’) across four Mediterranean sites in Italy, Spain, and Portugal, we evaluate the performance of these models against traditional GDD-based methods. Cross-validation results show that while the mechanistic model excels at predicting bud-break, with a Mean Absolute Error (MAE) of 4.9 days compared to 5.7 and 5.6 days of the GDD-based and the deep learning model, respectively, the deep learning model is an all-around optimal methodology in terms of predicting accuracy across different stages, resulting in an overall MAE slightly under 5 days, with an average error reduction of 0.6 to 1.6 days respect to the two GDD-based models tested. Furthermore, we illustrate how these models can leverage sub-seasonal weather forecasts to predict phenological events in advance, offering practical tools for vineyard managers. This was particularly true for the deep learning model, that was able to predict grapevine phenological stages two weeks in advance with an average error lower than 6 days. These findings highlight the potential of these novel approaches for automating phenology monitoring and improving decision-making in viticulture under changing climate conditions.

title: GAN-diffusion hybrids for image generation in smart agriculture: A systematic review
Linking video tracks and RFID identification to monitor individual broilers in group housing
abstract: Monitoring an individual broiler’s movement, interactions, and environment using video and RFID allows breeders to identify novel or indicator traits of their health, welfare, and performance, potentially improving the effectiveness of selection. However, video monitoring and identifying multiple, similar-looking, group-housed broilers is difficult. This study developed and investigated a data-fusion approach integrating video tracking with RFID identification to reconstruct individual broiler trajectories in group housing. Thirty-nine RFID-tagged broilers were recorded in a pen with thirty subfloor RFID antennas and a video camera at 18 days of age. Tracking was achieved with a YOLOv7-tiny model and a modified version of SORT. Tracks were linked to RFID-tags either through a direct approach or through the developed two-step approach consisting of location estimation through a Hidden Markov Model (HMM), with or without incorporating additional video information, and trajectory reconstruction using a greedy algorithm. Four antenna configurations were assessed: full-grid (#30), two-lines (#12), cross-pattern (#10), and two-antenna (#2). In all antenna configurations, the developed approach outperformed the direct approach, with lower average positions errors and less missing positions when evaluated against ground-truth positions [mean (SD)]: 0.021(0.10) vs. 0.48(0.54), 0.14(0.30) vs. 0.71(0.61), 0.30(0.45) vs. 0.69(0.50) and 0.85(0.59) vs. 1.03(0.60) m, respectively. The developed sensor data-fusion approach provides individual trajectories of group-housed broilers for subsequent locomotion phenotyping (such as distance walked, speed, and acceleration) by combining the spatial precision of video with the identification reliability of RFID.
