title: Hyperspectral retrieval of leaf chemistry is divergent for mass- or area-based carbon and nitrogen contents
Exploring the application potential of linear-scale dielectric sensing systems in substrate moisture monitoring
A short-horizon multi-step environmental response prediction model for pig house digital twins
abstract: Pig-house digital twins require environmental response models that can continuously advance indoor states under specified equipment operation and outdoor conditions. This study combined minute-scale operating analysis, multi-scale temporal representation, and rollout training to improve recursive environmental prediction. One-minute records from 16 pig-house units between January and early September 2026 yielded 335,041 valid prediction origins for temperature, relative humidity, and CO2 at two monitoring locations. Across three operating periods, environmental fluctuations were greater on average in equipment-transition windows than in stable-background windows, supporting the retention of minute-scale information. A dual-stream model separately encoded high- and low-frequency histories and combined them with current-state and weather context to predict six indoor variables. During recursive prediction, model outputs updated the indoor state, while recorded equipment states and measured outdoor conditions supplied the operating and boundary conditions. The model was trained with a trajectory-level loss over 15 recursive one-minute steps. In the temporal-representation comparison, separate encoding with concatenation reduced physical-scale-normalized root mean square error (PNRMSE) by 13.7 % relative to the high-frequency-only baseline. With this architecture fixed, uniformly weighted 15-step training reduced overall test PNRMSE from 0.3851 under single-step training to 0.2996. All four multi-step training schemes also produced lower whole-trajectory error than single-step training in each of three historical 24-h replays. These results support combining multi-scale histories with trajectory-level training to improve recursive environmental prediction and provide a methodological basis for the environmental-response component of pig-house digital twins.

Giving the greenhouse a brain: How artificial intelligence is transforming controlled environment agriculture
abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is redefining how we design, manage, and sustain Controlled Environment Agriculture (CEA). Traditionally, greenhouses relied on rule-based control systems that operated through predefined thresholds for temperature, humidity, and light. Today, advances in computer vision, machine learning, and robotics are transforming these facilities into intelligent ecosystems capable of perceiving, reasoning, and adapting in real time. This perspective review explores the emerging paradigm of the “greenhouse with a brain,” where data-driven perception and decision-making integrate seamlessly with sensing and actuation networks. Unlike technology-specific reviews that primarily examine individual components of greenhouse automation, this article integrates advances across sensing, artificial intelligence, robotics, modeling, and control within a system-level cognitive framework. We discuss recent progress in visual plant phenotyping, predictive climate control, knowledge-enhanced reinforcement learning, and multimodal data fusion that enable closed-loop intelligence for crop monitoring and management. Beyond technical advances, we emphasize the shift toward self-learning and explainable AI systems that can autonomously optimize productivity, resource efficiency, and environmental sustainability. By synthesizing developments across AI, robotics, and plant science, this article envisions next-generation cognitive greenhouses. In these autonomous yet transparent systems, humans, machines, and biological processes collaborate as partners to achieve resilient and sustainable food production in a changing “world”.

title: Pre-symptomatic crop intelligence: a closed-loop framework for anticipatory, confidence-aware decision-making in site-specific crop protection
abstract: Abstract Purpose Symptom-triggered crop protection acts only after damage is committed, and the intervention window has narrowed. This review reframes pre-symptomatic sensing from a detection problem into a closed decision loop, establishing the physiological lead time of a signal, set against its detection confidence and the latency of the response it can trigger, as the organizing principle for anticipatory, site-specific decision-making. Methods A systematic-narrative synthesis was conducted across major bibliographic databases through June 2026. Studies reporting pre-symptomatic capability under field or realistic conditions were retained and coded onto a coupled lead-time × confidence × actionability framework spanning sensing, inference, and actuation. Results Optical modalities were found to dominate the evidence base, while electrophysiological and volatile signals extended achievable lead time. Single modalities were insufficient to separate biotic from abiotic stress, motivating heterogeneous fusion. Edge inference and temporal onset forecasting remained immature, detection confidence was rarely quantified, and the sensing-to-actuation loop was seldom closed. Reported performance degraded sharply from laboratory to field, particularly in perennial and smallholder systems. Conclusions A unifying Pre-Symptomatic Crop Intelligence framework is proposed, governed by the principle that system value is bounded by the weakest of lead time, detection confidence, and response latency; priorities identified include lead-time-labeled benchmarks, uncertainty-aware inference, field-robust fusion, and economic evaluation for perennial crops.

title: Numerical prediction of traction-angle-dependent detachment pathway competition in Rosa sterilis S.D. Shi fruit using a dual-interface cohesive-zone finite-element model
abstract: Mechanical harvesting of Rosa sterilis S.D. Shi fruit may cause separation at either the branch–peduncle or peduncle–fruit junction, yet modelling only one interface prescribes the potential failure site in advance. We developed a dual-interface cohesive-zone finite-element model representing the branch-side separation interface (BSSI) with solid cohesive elements and the fruit-side separation interface (FSSI) with surface-based cohesive contact. Morphological observations, material tests and interface separation experiments informed model construction and parameterisation. Complete-system simulations were compared with vertical and horizontal traction experiments (n = 3 per direction). Simulated peak forces were 10.053 and 6.307 N, differing from the experimental means by 3.17 % and 6.04 %, respectively. Whole-curve normalized root-mean-square errors were 13.7 % and 4.51 %, and the predicted BSSI and FSSI detachment sites agreed with the corresponding endpoint observations. An area-weighted dual-interface damage competition criterion classified nine intermediate-angle coordinated-loading simulations at 8 mm/s. All nine cases were FSSI-dominated under the nominal settings, while event-associated picking-force peaks ranged from 9.86 to 18.46 N. For 45°-a, local BSSI damage initiated before FSSI damage, but FSSI reached global failure first, showing that initiation order alone did not determine the detachment pathway. Restricted single-interface comparisons further showed that excluding one potential route changed the force response and prevented assessment of concurrent damage at both junctions. The dual-interface framework thus relates the predicted separation site to the evolution and sequence of competing interface failures under specified loading conditions.

title: Sqrt-error-weighted grade model for weakly supervised weed segmentation of UAV imagery
abstract: Accurate and efficient weed segmentation is crucial for precision agriculture and automated field management. This study presents a novel weakly supervised framework for multi-type weed segmentation by introducing a new severity grading task and leveraging class activation map (CAM). To reduce reliance on pixel-level annotations, we constructed WeedGrade5k, a UAV image dataset with 5254 samples labeled using image-level severity grades for broadleaf (BL) and grass weeds (GW). To better model the ordinal nature of grade levels, we propose the Sqrt-Error-Weighted (SEW) loss and introduce Accuracy over Error (AoE), a metric that jointly reflects classification accuracy and regression deviation. The SEW-based grade model achieves a 4.8 % improvement in mean accuracy (mAcc) and a 7.6 % gain in AoE over standard baselines. Furthermore, leveraging the grade models and CAM, we train a unified multi-type weed segmentation network using weak supervision. On the manually annotated WeedSeg dataset, our method improves mean Intersection-over-Union (mIoU) by 8.8 %, reaching 56.0 %. Our method is further applied to multi-temporal field UAV orthomosaics to map weed dynamics under varying management regimes. Overall, this framework provides an annotation-efficient route from image-level weed severity grades to fine-grained segmentation, showing practical potential for field-scale weed monitoring in precision agriculture.

title: Mechanical interaction between sweet corn radicles and soil: CT imaging and discrete element modeling
abstract: The growth behavior of radicle (the seed’s first root) in soil is fundamental to understanding radicle-soil mechanical interactions during crop emergence. In this study, X-ray computed tomography (CT) and discrete element modeling (DEM) were integrated to investigate the three-dimensional growth trajectory and mechanical response of sweet corn radicles in soil. CT scanning was used to reconstruct a radicle-soil composite structure, from which a cylindrical sample of radicle-soil complex (66.63 mm in diameter and 48.55 mm in height) was digitally segmented and modeled. The scanned and reconstructed radicle geometry was integrated into a DEM model, and experimentally measured growth rates were applied to simulate dynamic radicle elongation in soil. The results show that the internal forces of soil particle bonds evolve significantly during radicle growth. The normal bond force rapidly increases during the initial stage and stabilizes around 1.8 × 10−3–2.2 × 10−3 N, while the tangential force gradually increases and stabilizes at 1.2 × 10−2–1.4 × 10−2 N, indicating an increasing contribution of tangential resistance during radicle advancement. The required energy, defined as the cumulative mechanical work required for the radicle to overcome soil resistance, increases rapidly during the initial penetration stage and stabilizes at approximately 1.0 × 10−2 J as the radicle-soil system approaches a new mechanical equilibrium. Furthermore, force distribution differs significantly between different regions of the radicle, with the root cap bearing the dominant mechanical load. The proposed CT-DEM integrated approach quantitatively characterizes the geometric evolution and mechanical response of radicle growth under controlled conditions. This study provides a robust basis for understanding radicle-soil interactions and the mechanical constraints governing crop emergence.

title: Forecasting future individual-tree growth using explainable machine learning across northern Chinese larch forests
abstract: Accurately forecasting tree growth under climate change is essential for adaptive forest management, yet the ability of machine-learning models to predict future growth beyond the calibration period remains poorly evaluated. Using 615 trees and 1,230 increment cores collected from six Larix gmelinii var. principis-rupprechtii forests across northern China, we reconstructed annual basal area increment (BAI) series and developed a tree-level dataset spanning 2000–2023. Tree age, previous-year diameter at breast height (DBH), competition index (CI), and multi-temporal climatic variables were integrated into Random Forest (RF) and Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) models and compared with a linear mixed-effects model (LMM). Both machine-learning models substantially outperformed the LMM, achieving cross-validation R2 values of 0.45–0.74 and successfully reproducing interannual growth variability. Temporal extrapolation reduced predictive performance relative to conventional cross-validation, but both models retained robust forecasting skill under unseen future conditions. Variable-importance and SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analyses revealed that previous-year DBH, tree age, and competition intensity were the most influential predictors of BAI, whereas climatic effects were region-specific, nonlinear, and frequently lagged. Future projections under Coupled Model Intercomparison Project Phase 6 (CMIP6) SSP126, SSP245, and SSP585 scenarios indicated generally stable growth during 2024–2028, with differences among sites exceeding differences among climate scenarios. Our results demonstrate that explainable machine learning can provide robust near-term forecasts of individual-tree growth beyond the calibration period and highlight temporal extrapolation as a critical component of ecological forecasting.

title: Multi-view projection estimation of rice flag leaf inclination angle based on skeleton topology constraints and temporal tracking
abstract: Rice flag leaf inclination angle is vital for characterizing plant compactness and light utilization. To overcome the high costs of 3D reconstruction and the inaccuracies of conventional 2D methods, this paper proposes an automated detection framework using multi-view sequences and spatiotemporal constraints. The method utilizes an RGB camera and turntable to acquire full-circumference images, employing U2-Net and skeleton thinning to extract “leaf tip-leaf base” topology. To handle complex canopy occlusion and noise interference: First, a temporal consistency tracking model is established using a Kalman Filter combined with consistency-gated association and interpolation completion strategies, significantly enhancing the stability of flag leaf tracking. Subsequently, a spatial geometric constraint mechanism is constructed by introducing “Skeleton Snapping” (Snap) and “Branch Backtracking” (Branch-BFS) strategies to precisely locate the leaf base while eliminating tracking drift of the leaf tip in free space, ensuring the physical authenticity of morphological features. Finally, a multi-view projection constraint model is utilized to invert the acquired continuous and smooth sequence of 2D angles projected from the 3D leaf onto the current camera imaging plane into the true 3D leaf inclination angle. The results showed excellent robustness across booting, heading, and grain-filling stages. Automated detections were highly consistent with manual measurements, achieving a MAE < 2° and R2 ≥ 0.97. Among the configurations tested in this study, the 20-view configuration provided a favorable balance between accuracy and efficiency, with an average processing time of 1.85 s per plant. This study provides a low-cost, high-precision tool for high-throughput rice phenotyping and ideal plant type breeding without expensive 3D hardware.

title: Boundary-Aware and Structure-Guided semantic segmentation of green orchard fruits with hierarchical Coarse-to-Fine refinement
abstract: Accurate semantic segmentation of green orchard fruits in natural scenes remains challenging because of fruit–background similarity, illumination variation, occlusion, and morphological variation. To address these challenges, an efficient encoder–decoder framework, named HAG-Net, is proposed. HAG-Net combines Dual Focus Attention for boundary- and texture-sensitive representation, Wavelet-Enhanced Content Attention for global structural modeling, and Feature Interaction Fuzziness Elimination for hierarchical coarse-to-fine boundary refinement. Experiments on the self-collected Guava and Green Lemon datasets showed that HAG-Net achieved mIoU values of 95.06 % and 92.80 %, respectively, outperforming nine representative classical and recent segmentation models, including DeepLabv3+, Mask2Former, SegNeXt, and MambaVision. The model required 3.028 GFLOPs and contained 12.285 M parameters. Ablation studies confirmed the contributions of the proposed modules, while fine-tuning experiments showed that the model could be adapted from guava to green lemon segmentation using only 25 % of the target-domain data, with performance approaching that obtained using the complete dataset. These results indicate that HAG-Net provides an effective and computationally efficient approach to green orchard fruit segmentation and may reduce annotation requirements when adapting to new fruit categories. The method may provide visual perception support for orchard monitoring and robotic harvesting.

title: Species-Conditioned hierarchical decoding and cross-attention for uncertainty-aware veterinary skin disease recognition
abstract: Veterinary dermatology is facing two diagnostic challenges. First, many conditions show overlapping visual signs such as alopecia, erythema, crusting, scaling, nodules, and plaques, making image-based recognition difficult. Second, the same visual pattern may correspond to different diseases in cats, cattle, and dogs, which makes flat disease classification unreliable when host species is ignored. While deep learning has advanced animal health monitoring, existing systems are often limited to single species or binary detection tasks. To address this, we propose a species-conditioned deep learning framework designed to analyze standard RGB images across diverse hosts. Our approach introduces a novel architecture featuring: (1) an EfficientNetV2-S backbone for feature extraction; (2) a dedicated pathway for host-species representation; (3) disease-token construction with species-conditioned spatial-token modulation; and (4) species-gated cross-attention for disease classification. Furthermore, we incorporate uncertainty-aware analysis via MC-Dropout, conformal prediction, and Grad-CAM to ensure decision reliability. Evaluated on an internal dataset of 16,942 images (21 categories), the proposed Unified SGCA model achieved 97.5 % disease accuracy and 98.0 % macro-F1 on the internal test set, while SGCA Cross-Attention achieved 96.9 % accuracy and 97.4 % macro-F1. Crucially, on a heterogeneous external cohort of 1,351 internet-derived images characterized by varying quality and background complexity, the model maintained robust performance with a top-3 accuracy of 93.0 % for Unified SGCA and 88.8 % for SGCA Cross-Attention. This framework offers a scalable solution for veterinary decision support, farmer education, and zoonotic disease surveillance.

title: Early electrophysiological responses and photosynthetic changes of tomato under continuous water-supply deviation using leaf electrical signals
From multi-fruit collisions to tissue damage: cross-scale dynamics and prediction of damage patterns during mechanized apple packing
abstract: During mechanized apple packing, fruits undergo successive multi-body collisions and load transfer. Existing studies generally investigate fruit-group dynamics and tissue damage in individual fruits separately, making it difficult to establish a direct link between practical packing conditions and internal fruit damage. To address this limitation, this study proposes a cross-scale damage prediction framework for fresh-market apples during packing, establishing a continuous mapping from packing conditions to collective collisions, tissue stress, and ultimately damage patterns. Fuji apples were used as the study material. Apple models were developed based on reverse engineering and experimentally determined material properties, with the measured minimum pulp yield strength of 0.27 MPa adopted as the threshold for irreversible damage initiation. Multi-body dynamics (MBD) simulations were employed to characterize fruit trajectories, collision behavior, and energy-transfer patterns during packing. Key collision parameters extracted from the MBD simulations were subsequently introduced into finite element method (FEM) models to resolve tissue-scale stress propagation and damage evolution. Building on this framework, a two-stage decoupled GFI-LightMLP surrogate model was developed to enable rapid prediction from packing conditions to mechanical responses and, subsequently, damage volume. The results showed that collision velocity was the dominant factor governing tissue damage. As the collision velocity increased from 1410 to 2450 mm s−1, the maximum equivalent stress increased from 0.27639 to 0.42368 MPa, while the damage volume increased from 2.17 × 103 to 2.74 × 104 mm3. Crate stiffness substantially affected impact-energy dissipation; compared with wooden crates, polypropylene crates reduced the damage volume by approximately 28.5 %. In addition, apples in the bottom layer exhibited a pronounced load-accumulation effect during multilayer packing, indicating that attenuation of macroscopic fruit motion and localized tissue damage can occur simultaneously. On the test set, the surrogate models achieved coefficients of determination above 0.96 for both equivalent stress and damage volume, while validation-set R2 values reached 0.9842 and 0.9415, respectively, demonstrating robust predictive performance. Physical experiments further confirmed that the predicted damage volumes followed the same trend as the experimentally measured values, with relative errors ranging from 3.57 to 19.15 %. Overall, the proposed framework links macroscopic fruit dynamics with tissue-scale damage during apple packing. It further enables rapid damage assessment without repeated computationally intensive simulations. The framework provides a theoretical basis for compliant design of mechanized packing equipment, screening of operating conditions, and optimization of low-damage packing parameters.

title: Real-time semantic segmentation of orchard LiDAR point clouds with a spherical-image convolutional neural network
abstract: Real-time semantic segmentation is essential for intelligent orchard operations. Conventional light detection and ranging (LiDAR) point cloud segmentation methods suffer from limited generalizability and weak adaptability to complex orchard scenarios. Specifically, the widely adopted PointNet++ cannot deliver satisfactory segmentation accuracy when processing multibeam LiDAR data collected from orchards. To address these challenges, this study constructs a nine-class orchard point cloud segmentation dataset and proposes a real-time segmentation framework built upon spherical-image convolutional neural networks. The framework leverages LiDAR-adaptive spherical projection to transform unordered three-dimensional (3D) point clouds into structured multimodal spherical images, thereby enabling dimensionality reduction while retaining geometric and reflectance features. Given the angular anisotropy of LiDAR and the abundance of cylindrical objects in orchard environments, a lightweight, asymmetric Darknet26-AS encoder is devised to establish a favorable balance between segmentation accuracy and inference efficiency. Further, a Gaussian distance–weighted voting strategy is incorporated to refine boundaries within the image domain, with spherical backprojection completing the full 3D segmentation pipeline. Experimental results demonstrated that the proposed method attained a mean intersection over union (mIoU) of 89.9% across the nine orchard classes, thereby surpassing PointNet++ by 15.9 percentage points (pp). Compared to state-of-the-art models, including PointTransformer v3 and SphereFormer, the proposed method achieved competitive accuracy, with the overall mIoU gap smaller than 1.2 pp. Meanwhile, it exhibited drastically reduced computational overhead: its parameter count was merely 1/12 and 1/8.5 those of the two counterparts, respectively, while its inference latency was approximately 1/7.4 and 1/4, respectively.

title: Lightweight two-stage framework for multi-cow behavior recognition based on edge devices
abstract: Accurate behavior recognition of dairy cows is important for automated monitoring in precision livestock farming. To enable efficient monitoring on resource-constrained edge devices, this study develops an integrated lightweight two-stage framework that combines cow detection, multi-object tracking, and spatiotemporal behavior recognition within a unified edge-inference pipeline. In the first stage, an improved YOLOv11n detector integrates lightweight feature extraction, multi-scale feature fusion, and a lightweight decoupled detection head to improve cow localization while reducing computational overhead. With TensorRT acceleration, the detector achieves an mAP@50 of 97.6 %, an mAP@50:95 of 71.8 %, and an inference speed of 34.5 FPS. In the second stage, X3D-S performs spatiotemporal recognition of five target dairy cow behaviors, achieving a standalone Top-1 accuracy of 85.8 % and a Macro-F1 of 85.9 %. The complete pipeline, consisting of the improved YOLOv11n detector, ByteTrack-based multi-object tracking, and X3D-S recognition, is deployed on the NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano edge platform. Under the evaluated barn conditions, the complete pipeline achieves an end-to-end behavior recognition accuracy of 82.4 %, with an effective processing rate of approximately 15.6 behavior-recognition updates/s and an average active Jetson power draw of approximately 7.2 W during continuous inference. These results indicate the feasibility of integrating cow detection, identity tracking, and temporal behavior recognition within a lightweight edge-deployable framework for automated dairy cow behavior monitoring.

title: Pedestrian detection in occluded maize harvesting environments based on thermal infrared imaging
Development and application of a low-cost sampler with in situ detection for leaf pathogenic bacteria
abstract: Early detection of bacterial pathogens is critical for preventing diseases in protected cultivation, but current monitoring methods are often costly, slow, or lack sensitivity. This limitation hinder timely disease warning. This study developed a low-cost three-dimensional (3D)-printed leaf pathogen sampler powered by a handheld vacuum cleaner for non-destructive in situ collection of bacteria from leaf surfaces. Cucumber angular leaf spot caused by Pseudomonas amygdali pv. lachrymans was used to evaluate the system. The sampler used airflow to remove and enrich pathogens from multiple leaves into a single sampling tube, and centrifugation increased detectable bacteria by 1.85 to 7.02 times. Pal release from infected leaves showed a bimodal pattern with peaks at 15:00 and 24:00, indicating optimal sampling times. An on-site recombinase polymerase amplification (RPA) assay combined with lateral flow strips and smartphone readout achieved a detection limit of 200 colony-forming units (CFU)·mL−1, which enable rapid visual qualitative identification. In this trial, detection was achieved four days before symptoms appeared, which suggests a potential early-warning window of at least three days under similar conditions. This system can provide a practical, scalable solution for early warning and precise management of bacterial diseases in protected cultivation and can be adapted to other plant pathogens, improving monitoring efficiency and reducing operational complexity.
